Ever hath God existed, holding all Names in His right hand, and all Attributes in His grasp. All that are in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them sing praise to Him. No God is there but Him, the Almighty, the Best-Beloved.
This is a Sign besides which all else is assigned the character of “creation.” Whoever readeth the prayer “Glorified be He Who is the Living, and dieth not” up to the end – or shall do so hereafter – will become illumined in the sea of the appearance of this Sign in his own heart. For at the beginning of each Revelation this prayer is alone, and the manifestations thereof are rarer than the philosopher’s stone; whereas at the end of each Revelation they are more glorious than every glorious one, and more exalted than every exalted one. Thus, for example, wert thou to say “Glorified is He who judgeth, and is not judged” – at the end of each Revelation the manifestations thereof attain in the hearts of those who glorify God an exaltation such that they are able to pronounce judgment upon all, while the mere thought of pronouncing judgment upon them doth not occur to anyone; notwithstanding that at the beginning of each Revelation the mere thought that they might be possessed of such capacity doth not occur to a soul.
Nay, consider, for example, the pronouncement “Glorified be He Who speaketh truly, and Whose word is not to be approved as true” – at the end of the Revelation the Manifestation thereof attaineth an exaltation such that no one, considering the sublimity of His glory, eminence and majesty, regardeth himself as worthy to approve His words as true, whereas He approveth as true the words of whomsoever He willeth; while the latter take it is as a source of boundless glory and distinction to themselves that they should have been made the object of such approval: yet at the beginning of the Revelation He is “rarer than the philosopher’s stone” to the degree even that no one accepteth His words as true; whereas every truth becometh true solely in virtue of His approval.
Such likewise is the case with all the Names and Attributes, for in each Name and Attribute naught is seen but Him. Nay, the one in whom this Name and Attribute are manifested regardeth himself, in comparison with Him, as entirely non-existent. Consider, for example, who today, in the Dispensation of the Qur’an, might be thought possessed of a heart worthy to be robed in the name of “Knowing, Who is not known:” yet how evanescent doth he still account and see himself in comparison with the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him! In such wise regard thou the manifestations of the Names and Attributes. Yet this is a mighty ocean, wherein the servant, if but the thought occur to him of gazing upon the Sign itself, will drown: and how many are the voyagers upon this ocean who have drowned – and shall yet do so – on account of gazing upon other than the One manifest therein!
How indeed could the case be otherwise when it is evident that the manifestations of the “Living” are susceptible of death? – while similar susceptibilities exist in the case of all the Likenesses and Attributes: yet since naught is seen in these mirrors but He Who liveth from eternity even unto eternity, these manifestations accordingly live in virtue of that Life. So likewise in the case of “Sovereign, with no sovereign save Himself,” and of “Knowing, with none knowing except Himself;” so likewise in the case of “Powerful, with none powerful but Himself;” and so likewise in the case of “Truthful, when there was none truthful besides Himself:” even as the Names of God have neither beginning nor end; nor hath there ever been, or ever shall be, any limit to their number.
In the inner reality of each thing there hath ever been, and ever shall be, a sign from God, in virtue whereof it is able to confess His Unity: which sign within it cometh from the Will, wherein is seen naught but God; while in the Will Itself this sign is none other but Its own Self, Which is the Mirror of God, the Which hath never guided, nor ever shall guide, but unto God, glorified and exalted be He. This is a sign wherein, in all things, naught is seen but God: for the worshipper, at the time when he turneth unto God, seeth not the Divine creation; whereas at the time of remembering that which hath been created through the agency of God, he seeth creation: for he knoweth that this creation hath been, and is, the handiwork of God, and that all besides Him is His creation.
At all events, behold thou how today in the Bayan anyone who confesseth the Unity of God doth so in virtue of the instruction of the Point of the Bayan, from which Dawning-Place of Glory the Confession of the Unity of God shone forth; yet it guided not, at the time of its effulgence, but unto God. (Neither is it in the station in which this effulgence occurred that it guideth not but unto God: nay rather, the aspect of it associated with creation attesteth its servitude unto the Lord, even as that aspect which, in All Things, is associated with their own self attesteth its servitude unto the Lord.) All Things have been created from the ghost of its image: and just as it hath two signs – a sign related to the Truth, and a sign related to creation, in virtue of which latter it worshippeth the Lord, and boweth down before Him – so likewise each and every thing worshippeth its Best-Beloved in virtue of a sign bespeaking its character of “creation;” yet this sign hath not been realized, nor ever shall it be, save in virtue of a sign within that thing from God, which guideth unto Him, not unto aught else: for how might it be supposed to guide unto the sign itself, when this latter is His creation?
Nay, none endued with understanding hath ever looked, or ever shall look, but unto God alone, than Whom naught else is seen in all the Names of the hearts: for should the case be otherwise, God’s servants would be precluded the possibility of worship; whereas naught hath been created but for the sake of worshipping Him: even as He hath sent down in the Qur’an, “I have created not the Jinn and men but to the end that they should worship Me.”
Just as in these Names naught is seen but God, so too in the mirrors of these Names, which are the hearts of them that recognize the Unity of God, naught is seen but Him. Wherefore if someone, when considering a Name, look upon aught else except God, he is at that moment shut out as by a veil, and hath drowned in the sea of imperception. Even as is the case with one who gazeth upon a mirror, for at the time when he doth so, he seeth naught therein but his own image, nor attendeth to the mirror itself: inasmuch as in the mirror it is the mirror that is seen, not the image of the observer. Nay, the image that appeareth of him in the mirror resideth in the image itself – which subsisteth in him as its revealer – and not in the mirror itself. For were it to inhere in the mirror itself, it must needs be witnessed ere the appearance of its own revealer.
Regard thou in like manner the mirrors of the Letters of the Living. Were the Name “Living” to inhere in each of their respective mirrors, it must needs be witnessed ere yet it had been revealed to them; whereas it is only after the revelation thereof by its Revealer that it is witnessed: and in such wise that methinks naught can be discerned in these manifestations of the “Living” but He Himself; even as there is naught, in the mirror whereon thou gazest, save thine own image, not the essence of the mirror. This image resideth in the image itself, not in the mirror itself; for were it to reside in the mirror, the Letters of the Living must needs – ere yet the image of the Possessor of the image had appeared in them – bespeak their affiliation to the designation “Living.” If, perchance, the image already existed in the mirror, this was from a previous revelation: it is not that there is aught in the mirror itself which had lain concealed therein.
This is an ocean wherein all the most discerning observers have drowned, taking the image to reside in the mirror itself. Nay, the throne of the image is none other but its own self; while its appearance is through the agency of the Possessor of the image and the mirror itself. In such wise regard thou all the Names and Attributes, seeing therein none save God alone; nor look upon them in their character of “Names,” or “Signs,” or “Attributes,” whence thou wilt be shut out as by a veil from the true intention.
It is on account of the very straitness of this Path that in the Qur’an the doors of Names have not been opened; nor have the manifestations of the previous Vahid offered any explanation thereof; or if somewhere they have done so, this hath been in the manner of the following utterance of the Prince of Martyrs – may the peace of God be upon him:

“O my God! Thou hast commanded me to return unto the traces: cause me then to return thereunto, in the raiment of lights, and through the guidance of discriminating insight, that I may return unto Thee therefrom, even as I came unto Thee therefrom, with mine inner being preserved from gazing upon them, and mine endeavour raised up above relying upon them. Thou, verily, art powerful over All Things.”

Today too all are relieved of voyaging upon this ocean; inasmuch as they are unable, whilst knowing of the existence of the mirror, not to gaze thereon. Wherefore all have been relieved of this prescription, save whoever is capable of seeing in the Name none but God, and will not commingle the sea of creation with the sea of Truth, nor the sea of Truth with the sea of creation, inasmuch as he seeth in the sea of Truth naught but God; and if once he seeth the aspect of “Reality” – which is its character of “Sign” – he entereth into the sea of creation, and no longer remaineth at the loftiest height of Truth. Nay the Name “Truth” is applied thereto only when naught is seen in it but God.
The Lord hath deposited these two signs in the human temple – nay, in each and every thing – so that, in virtue of the first sign, the one in question may recognize Him; confess His Unity; regard no one as possessed of independence save Him; and regard all else but Him as His creation; while, in virtue of the sign pertaining to his own self, he may worship the Lord; bow down before Him; and turn unto Him in detachment from the love of all else but Him: whence, should anyone turn unto God in such a manner, he shall attain ever unto whatsoever grace is possible for the inhabitants of the realm of being.
In truth, however, the servant seeth within himself naught but his own servitude; while these two stations may not properly be assigned to any other than the Point of Truth, for none but He is able to speak on the part of God: nay rather, all things – that is, aught to which the term “thing” applieth – are worthy only that they should travel upon the sea of servitude, inasmuch as they have never been, nor ever shall be, capable of aught else but this. For the Lord hath granted not such permission but unto the Will; while the servant for his part is not able to arrive at the furthest limit.
After the setting of this Sun, none but He Whom God shall make manifest shall be capable of this manner of revelation of the Divine effulgence: nay, His is the station of pure revelation – a revelation in virtue whereof all the signs which guide unto God are made manifest in the hearts of all. Should a soul mount upwards, and enter into the sea of his heart, then would he behold the majesty of God, besides Whom all else have ever been, and ever shall be, His creation. Yet this same soul still worshippeth God, and turneth unto Him in detachment from all else but Him. In like manner, the Sea of the Will Itself, which is the world of pure revelation, and from the ghost of the shadows of Whose Verses all hearts are created, hath still, to the furthest extent possible, travelled in the realm of servitude, asserting with respect to His station of servitude “Verily, I am lowlier than the lowliest atom;” notwithstanding that the assertion “Verily, I am God, no God is there but Me” hath ever shone forth – as it shall ever shine forth – from the Sea of the appearance of His reality, which is the Mirror of God – the Which cannot indeed be characterized as “His reality:” nay rather, it is the Reality of God, while His own reality hath ever been, and ever shall be, God’s creation.
This is a Path than which there hath never been, nor ever shall be, a straiter in the knowledge of God. At the time of gazing upon the Lord in the light of that sign, all whereby God hath depicted His own Self is evoked; while at the time of gazing rather upon this sign, all whereby His creation hath been depicted is evoked.
Ever hath God been God, and all else besides Him His creation. Never hath there been betwixt God and His creation a third; nay, the “third,” verily, is naught but His creation. No God is there but Him. We all, verily, worship Him.


Gate Two of the Fourth Unity
explaining that all that reverteth unto the Point reverteth unto God, while all that reverteth not thereunto reverteth not unto God; and that all that reverteth unto God reverteth thereunto, while all that reverteth not unto God reverteth not thereunto.
The substance of this gate is that the Eternal Essence hath never been, nor ever shall be, of a nature that can be either apprehended, described, qualified or seen. Whatsoever cometh down from Him is from the Word of the Will; and whatsoever reverteth unto Him reverteth likewise unto the selfsame Source. Thus it is that in each Dispensation, this Will hath particular expressions and manifestations, which the learned of that Revelation have apprehended, and continue to apprehend.
Today, for example, whatever occurreth in the way of the exaltation of the Bayan is “For God,” and shall be regarded as for Him; but only up to the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest, when, if anyone perform an action for other than Him, it shall not revert unto the Lord, although the one in question be a wayfarer in the highest reaches of the recognition of the Unity of God. Even as the believers in the Book of Alif (Evangel) – who likewise recognized the Unity of God – were availed naught, after the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – by the exaltation of their knowledge: save only those of them who entered the fold of the Furqan.
In like manner, whatever eminence the believers in the Qur’an may have attained in every praiseworthy attribute; essence of hidden knowledge; and ascendancy of praiseworthy truth – yet, so they have come not within the fold of the Bayan, it hath been rendered vain, and hath availed them naught. Such too shall be the case with the people of the Bayan at the time of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest: no action of theirs shall revert unto God – though it be the very Word “There is no God but God” – unless it be coupled with belief in Him; whereas before His advent, whatsoever occurreth in the Bayan is performed “For God,” and reverteth unto Him.
It is not that it reverteth unto the Eternal Essence: nay, by reverting unto Him Whom God shall make manifest it reverteth unto Him. By the expression “reverteth unto Him” is intended a relation similar to that evident in the designation of the Ka’bih as “His House;” which edifice, in virtue of its exaltation and sublimity, He hath related unto Himself. Nor is aught else possible in the realm of being. For the Eternal Essence cannot be conjoined with any thing; whereas the beginning of the creation of each thing is the attachment thereto of the Will, while the end of its return is its reverting unto Him.
Should anyone, ere He Whom God shall make manifest ordain the exaltation of the Bayan – be it by no more than the ninth of the ninth of the tenth of the tenth of a minute – take up from the ground a grain of millet seed with the aim of bringing it within his own garden, and of redeeming it from the eventuality that the fruit of its existence should be rendered vain – this conformably with the behest of the Possessor of the Seven Letters – he shall have acted “For God,” and be granted the reward of All Things. If, however, this action be performed at the time of Revelation, or of the command of exaltation, then must he perform it for the sake of Him, and by the leave of Him, should His good pleasure reside in such a matter; for otherwise His good pleasure is Paradise, in whatsoever He ordaineth, or shall ordain, and in whatsoever He doeth, or shall do.
This is the secret of the whole of existence, and the mystery of each fire and light: that if someone but lay hold upon this Handle of Truth, he shall under no condition repose beneath the shadow of the Fire, but enjoy rather the shelter of the shadows of Paradise. Otherwise, in whatever religion thou lookest, the members thereof assert “We perform our works for God.” In the Qur’an, for example, whatever befell them who were the mirrors of “For God,” the perpetrators thereof asserted “We do this for God” – whereas they did it against God. So likewise in the Bayan, whatever sorrow befell the believers therein at the hands of the Letters of the Furqan, they inflicted it not without asserting – what they professed to be their only object – “We do this for God” – whereas they did it against God.
I swear by the Truth of Him Whom God shall make manifest, that there is no more grievous a circumstance in the knowledge of the Lord than this, that no soul shall inflict upon Him, or upon His believers, any sorrow save with the object of acting “For God,” and whilst asserting “We do this for God” – which if he do, he hath spoken, and speaketh, falsely, even as he hath acted, and acteth, against God.
O people of the Bayan! Have mercy upon yourselves; judge in the light of your own reason; admit the Truth; and remain not, on account of veiled matters, shut out as by a veil: for the proof of God at the time of Revelation is perfect before All Things. Behold, for example, how many are now believers in the Qur’an – yet at the time of its revelation, and for a period of seven years, there was but one believer therein; whereas the proof was the same then as it is now and hath ever been. This came about because the people of that age did not employ their reason. In the Bayan too, up to the Day of Resurrection, whosoever entereth therein shall do so in virtue of that first proof.
As for those servants who, at the beginning of the Revelation, remained shut out as by a veil, this came about because they did not employ their reason; for otherwise the proof of God at the time of Revelation is perfect before each atom: whence if, at the time of the revelation of the Bayan, all the believers in the Qur’an – nay, anyone whatsoever – had wished to believe, therein the proof of God was perfect and complete before them. For the Lord reasoneth with everyone as He did with the first to believe; and the same proof whereby he believed existeth with respect to all: why then have they remained shut out as by a veil? By this same proof shall He torment them until such time as they enter within the fold of faith. Take, then, good heed, O ye endued with insight, all of you, without exception!


Gate Three of the Fourth Unity: On this, that alteration (bada’) is God’s, and it is true
The substance of this gate is this, that no form of the worship of God can rival the worship that is based upon the faith in divine alteration, inasmuch as the belief in alteration is the acknowledgement of the unconstrained power of God to whatsoever He willeth. Should one who adoreth Him in the most exalted way imaginable in the realm of creation, happen to acknowledge the truth of the alteration, this very act of worship, his acknowledgement, would be reckoned far mightier than his exalted worship. For were He to desire to make him enter the fire, He would be assuredly potent to do so, and no one would be able to say why or wherefore regarding His action, inasmuch as He is just in His Decree. Conversely, should one who rebeleth against Him, in the most grievous way imaginable in the realm of creation, fail to fix his gaze upon His alteration, this very transgression is far more grievous in His sight than all that is committed by him. And were God to desire to make him enter the paradise, who would have the right to say why or wherefore concerning His action, inasmuch as He is all-praised in His Decree?
However, God’s alteration is immeseaurably exalted above any association with the alteration of His creatures. For the creature’s alteration is due to their powerlessness, whereas God’s alteration is out of supreme power. Therefore, in each Revelation of the Will, His alteration is manifest. For notwithstanding the fact that in the past Dispensation He hath decreed faith and paradise for the its believers, in the New Revelation He subjecteth all to the decree of alteration, and judgeth them to be non-believers, to reveal His absolute might. Otherwise, His court of glory transcendeth the difference between the Qur’an and the Bayan, the laws of the Furqan and the laws of the Bayan. Rather, this alteration is solely due to the supreme height of His power, and the uttermost sublimity of His sovereignty, that all may know that they have always been, and will continue forever to be, in the grasp of the might and power of their Lord, that naught they possess except by His leave (Permission).
But this divine alteration is naught but the alteration of the Will, inasmuch as the Essence of the Eternity hath always been, and will continue forever to be, unchanged. Manifestation and concealment are the attributes of the Will, and firstness and lastness are the schemes of His Wish. Should He be praised as First, His firstness would be His very lastness, and His manifestation, the very concealment.
Be veiled not, O beholder of the Bayan, by the use of these words, that the name first is used at one time in relation to the Unseen Essence, at another in relation to the Primal Utterance, sometimes in relation to the First Creature, and at yet another in relation to the first fire. For the firstness that is mentioned at the station of the Will is the First Creature that is mentioned at the level of the Eternal Essence. Likewise, compared to the firstness of the Will, the firstness that is mentioned with regard to the creatures resembleth the shadow of the sun in the mirror. In like manner, reference to the first in fire, refereth to the firstness in the creation of perishing, and not that of enduring subsistence. Therefore, beware not to be veiled by the manifestations of the names, inasmuch as nothing, with all that is attributed thereto, will ever surpass beyond its own limit.
After thou hast understood the alteration of the Eternal essence as the alteration of the Will, and His Confirmation as the Confirmation of the Will, thou must gaze upon the evident alterations in each Revelation, which hath ever been, and will continue forever to be, billowing like an infinite fathomless ocean. Thus, all who are present in this Revelation have witnessed such manifestations in the ocean of the Will, even as it was manifest in the Furqan by the name abrogation.
As to that which is mentioned in certain traditions that once a thing reacheth the stage of the Decree there will be no alteration for it, it meaneth that if faith attain the fourth stage, which is the pillar of magnification (takbir), there would be no alteration in that which is decreed, solely as a token of grace from God. But as it regardeth the divine justice, alteration hath always been, and will continue forever to be, true of all things, and will never part from anything at anytime, except by the will of God. For God is verily potent over all things.
And by the stage of Decree, in the pillar of magnification, is intended the ascension of the Will, Who from the shining forth out of the pillar of glorification, till His setting in the pillar of dust, is completed within His own self. For example, during the life of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, the very act of ordaining and manifesting of alteration, remaineth the very truth, till the time of His ascension, yet, thereafter, that which is made lawful by Him remaineth lawful till the Day of Resurrection, namely His Next Revelation in His Resurrection, while that which is forbidden by Him remaineth forbidden till His Next Revelation in His Resurrection. Thus, after Him, His Witnesses have remained submerged in the ocean of His Decrees, and had there been exceptions, it would have been in cases where They would have been certain of the good pleasure of God. Thus had anything been mentioned by Them, it would have been exactly the very alteration of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him. But in fact no such thing hath ever happened, rather, They have never transgressed the laws of the Book of God even to the degree of a mustard seed.
However, after His setting, His concealed gifts of guidance are present with the faithful, but no one is illumined by them inasmuch as no one recogniseth Him. But in His days of concealment, He enjoineth naught but that which He hath commanded during the Days of His manifestation.
This was the meaning of God’s alteration, glorified and exalted be Him, that the servant should never abide upon the seat of hope (raja’), even if he hath ascended to the utmost height possible in the world of contingency, inasmuch as fixing his gaze upon the divine alteration exceleth all his ascent. Likewise, should he descendth to the abyss of abasement, he should not be established upon the seat of fear (khauf), rather, he must gaze upon the God’s alteration, inasmuch as failure to do so is more grievous than the abyss in which he hath descended.
However, the revelation of this alteration is solely from the repository of the Will, and naught besides Him, as it hath become manifest in the Bayan. Should the Bayan mention for anything the decree of paradise, it would remain its due destiny till the Day of Resurrection, and should it pronounce non-paradise for anything, it would remain perished in the fire of His justice till the Day of Resurrection. Then at the time of Resurrection, should the very tree of fire attain faith, he would turn into the tree of paradise, and should the tree of paradise be veiled, he would turn into the tree of fire, as those who have been present in this Cycle hath witnessed this truth.
In each Revelation strive your utmost exertion to be blessed with a good mention of God in His Book until the next Revelation, inasmuch as attaining this, is far more excellent than spending thousands and thousands on the lofty seats (maqa’id-i-murtafi’ih) to perpetuate one’s name for the future. Who knoweth, these seats may perish, and there would not remain any name for him, if it is done for the non-truth, otherwise his reward hath always been, and will continue to be, with God. For God verily will reward the doer of good.


Gate Four of the Fourth Unity: Explaining that every male is a bond slave belonging unto Him
The substance of this gate is that the spirits of all things revert unto the human temple; while the Paradise of all things consisteth in the Paradise of man: the similitude whereof is this, that if a believer own a peerless diamond, the glory of that diamond consisteth in the glory which, in virtue thereof, accrueth to the believer. In like manner, all things, and man’s own temple, revert unto the Names and Attributes of God: if his heart guideth unto God, he shall be accounted in the sight of God as under the shadow of “His are the Goodly Names;” while if it reflect rather one of His Attributes, he shall be accounted as among His Attributes. This is the exalted meaning of the Tradition “There is naught but God, and His Names and Attributes.”
Man’s temple cannot, however, be identified with the Names and Attributes of God unless, on the advent of each Revelation, he entereth beneath the shadow thereof; for otherwise his ability to be identified even with belief itself is forfeited – with how much greater reason, then, must his ability to be identified with the Names and Attributes of God be lost? The gaze of the Lord is fixed upon this, not upon outward matters. In this day, for example, it is observable that every goodly attribute is found among the Letters of the Alif (Evangel): but these attributes are today accounted as pertaining rather to the Fire. If today in the Bayan a soul believe in God and His Verses, although he sit upon the earth, yet it is he who is seated upon a throne of glory; whereas if other than he be established upon a seat of the utmost glory, he is nevertheless, in the sight of God, and of those endowed with understanding, in a situation of the utmost abasement.
On the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, it is fitting that upon the heart of every believing man, who believeth in Him, the sun of Him Who is the Object of all Names should dawn, and the ability to exemplify the Names of God be realized within His inner self. Every believing soul in the Bayan hath been, and is, His bond slave; even as the possessors of temples in the Qur’an were, and are, the bond slaves of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him. Remoteness be the portion of that bond slave who visiteth upon his Master aught but what is the prerequisite of servitude! Now look thou, and be sorrowed, observing how unreservedly these bond slaves have placed upon their necks the collar of servitude, priding themselves thereon; and yet how tyrannically they behave towards their Master on His appearance in a nobler guise in His after life! The matter hath reached the pass that He now dwelleth in a mountain. All, in virtue of belief in Him, are believers; yet they have not consented even that He should be called by His own Name “Believer:” for had they consented thereto, things would not have fallen out as they have.
Thus it is that all are immersed in the ocean of imperception; that the suns in the mirrors move by His light, yet are shut out as by a veil from Him; and that the fishes of the sea live by the water, yet question its existence. Today, all the believers in the Qur’an await the appearance of the Qa’im of the House of Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – humbly and fervently beseeching that His advent may be hastened, and taking pride on beholding Him in their dreams; while by their own hand they have sent Him into captivity, and made Him to dwell in a mountain. This is the meaning of the Tradition “In Him is a sign of Joseph: He is bought and sold.”
O people of the Bayan! Seek refuge in your Best-Beloved from the eventuality that ye should inflict upon Him – even whilst bearing the collar of servitude unto Him upon your necks – that which ye would not inflict upon your own selves, who are but His bond slaves. It is not that ye have not heard of the Revelation of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – aforetime, and how, on His advent, those who awaited His appearance were shut out from Him as by a veil; so that for a period of no less than seven years – or, according to another account, nine years – there befell Him that which befell Him: yet still it hath availed you naught; for had it done so, things would not have fallen out in this Revelation as they have.
Stand ye abashed before your Best-Beloved, and forbear ye, on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, to behave in such a manner! Should ye make it a rule among yourselves not to wish for any soul that which ye would not wish for yourselves – from kings at the highest level, down to cultivators at the humblest – God willing, no sorrow shall visit Him. For the suns in the mirrors know not the Sun, save by the ghostly image thereof in their own selves. Thus it is that they perceive Him to be one like unto themselves; whereas all subsist through Him; while it is through the effect of His bounty that the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them have been created: even as someone other than the Letters of the Bayan hath said:

“Of His bounty are the earth and its counterpart * Of His sciences those of the Tablet and Pen.”

The word “of” is here used in the partitive sense: nay, aught to which the term “thing” may be applied is but a sprinkling from the ocean of His bounty, and a dewdrop from the sea of His munificence. Appreciate ye His worth at the time of Revelation, and consent not – as ye do today – night and day to lament for Him in your own honourable situations, even while He Himself dwelleth in a mountain; and sorrow visiteth Him, while ye have all – through His grace and bounty – been exempted from sorrow.
Watch, then, O ye endued with insight; then wait ye!


Gate Five of the Fourth Unity: Explaining that all the possessors of circles are wondrous signs belonging unto Him
The substance of this gate is that the explanation of this Chapter too is similar to that of the preceding: in consideration of the exaltation of that which is related unto Him, reference hath not here been made to “maidservants;” and He is better entitled to His possessions than All Things. Should He wish for Himself any soul, none would be able to ask Him why or wherefore, be it the most exalted of creation, or the most abased thereof. However it may be, He ordaineth what He willeth; neither is He to be asked concerning aught that He ordaineth, while all else are to be asked concerning all that He hath ordained.
The fruit of this Chapter is that if a master grant not permission to his bond slaves, it is forbidden them to wed; and in like manner if, at the time of Revelation, He forbid a soul one of the wondrous signs of in His possession, the sign in question would become unlawful to him: even as He hath in fact forbidden these wondrous signs to all who have not believed in Him, making such a union the gravest of offences: to the end that no one, on the Day of His appearance, should venture to deny Him; or else, if he become not a believer, that he should at least lapse into silence. How like it is that a man, hearing word of His appearance, may not at once believe in Him, yet still come nigh unto one of His wondrous signs: notwithstanding that, from the moment when the mere thought of other than belief occurred to him, such signs have been forbidden him; neither shall they become lawful to him again except at such time as he becometh a believer.
Have a care, O people of the Bayan! For the Divine Manifestation shall appear in whatever manner God willeth; neither, in regard to Him, let the thought of other than belief so much as cross your minds: for His Verses (Signs) are a proof unto all. Were ye to ponder for a moment, ye would at once accept their truth: for there is no difference in terms of inimitability between the whole Qur’an and the Surih of Tawhid; even as there is no difference between belief in the Last whose heart guided unto God, and belief in the First whose heart guided unto Him. Reflect ye ever upon the appearance of the Point of the Bayan. Perchance on that Day ye shall not cause yourselves to be shut out as by a veil from your Best-Beloved. Had ye reflected upon the appearance of the Point of the Qur’an, ye would today have conceived the nature of the Cause of God.
This matter hath not been enjoined but to the end that ye should exert your utmost diligence and effort: not that ye should exert yourselves in every area of religion, yet remain shut out as by a veil from the One by Whom the truth of religion is established. Even as, in the Dispensation of the Qur’an, the mujtahids observed its every aspect with the utmost precision and endeavour; yet, under the claim of “exerting endeavour” and “exercising caution,” they pronounced judgment against the One by Whom the truth of religion is established, and by Whose word its foundation is secured.
If the mujtahids of the Qur’an have carried precaution to such lengths, what will be the case with the Bayan? Yet, the sanction of death hath been forbidden in the Bayan more strictly than aught else: yea, naught hath been made the subject of so binding a prohibition: to the extent even that if the mere thought of slaying a soul enter a person’s heart, he thereby departeth from the religion of God, and shall be tormented for as long as the Lord willeth; while whatever had formerly been permitted him in the Bayan shall become unlawful to him: nay, even his own self shall become unlawful to him.
The Lord hath not granted anyone in the Bayan permission to decree the death of another, in any condition, or in any circumstance, or in any instance. Should there appear amongst them a dissenter in scientific matters, it hath never been, nor ever shall be, the part of anyone to resort to such a measure: nay rather, it is for God to decide and resolve the issue. At what low level must ye be situated, O preposterous creation, for decreeing the death of someone, knowing not that it is from the blessing of that same person that ye have bestowed upon yourselves the name of “Islam”? Picture to yourselves the wrongs that were inflicted upon the members of the Holy Family aforetime: those who wrought these deeds acted ostensibly in the name of Islam: yet they acted against the very shaper of the self of Islam, without belief in whom there can be no Islam.
From the day of the setting of the Sun of Truth, it shall never at any time be permitted for any of the believers in the Bayan to decree the death of another; and should anyone do so, he hath never been, and never shall be, of the Bayan, nor shall there be a greater wrongdoing on his part than this. For the Lord in the Qur’an hath sent down “whoso slayeth a soul … shall be as though he had slain all people.” Such, however, is the case if the soul slain be one among the believers: how then must stand the case if this soul should, like the Ka’bih, have been related unto God, and been called the Self of God?
Yet notwithstanding all the attention that hath been devoted to this matter in the Book of God, still, for all those who, from the beginning of Islam until this day, have regarded themselves as related unto the Qur’an, it hath been to no effect. Nor is there for them a more grievous torment than this, that they should trespass against the One Who is the Object of their adoration, even whilst bowing down before Him. The Lord hath made binding upon His own Sacred Essence not to forgive anyone into whose heart entereth the mere thought of slaying one of the believers in the Bayan: how then must stand the case with anyone who issueth such a decree, or – God forbid – carrieth it into effect?
Whatever king remembereth the calamity of the First and the Last; relieveth the believers in the Bayan of that which befell the First and the Last and those who were between them; and, for the sake of that which befell the First Letters, inflicteth no harm upon any who is possessed of a soul – it behoveth the Lord to bless that which He hath bestowed upon him, and to double that which He hath written down for him. And should his days extend to the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, it is incumbent upon him to arise to aid the One by whom the truth of religion is established; to request of Him the alleviation of whatever works had been hard for them; to beseech of Him sovereignty until the Day of Resurrection (for He bestoweth upon each thing its due; and, if He grant him his boon, none hath the right, by the decree of the Lord, to wrest it from him, for he is better entitled thereto than he: even as, in the case of all the other laws, none hath the right to breach whatever hath been commanded of God); nor to be shut out from the Best-Beloved of all by any thing, inasmuch as all that he possesseth had come from Him, ere yet He had appeared; and to champion His Cause.
Should He command him to wage a holy war, let him, in the height of glory, become a martyr in His path, for the name thereof shall be set down in the scroll of them that are nigh unto Him; otherwise, he shall go from this world, nor any mention shall remain of him.
It is not that during the days of ease, he should commemorate the sufferings of the True One (even as hath been the custom of all the believers in the Qur’an, both high and low, in holding observances to commemorate the sufferings of their Apostle, and of the Viceregents of their Apostle, and to remember that which befell their partisans); yet still, at the time of the appearance of the very One Whose sufferings he had been lamenting, and for the sake of the Viceregents of Whose religion he had been uttering ardent and tearful plaints, he should join the number of those seated rulers who visited wrong upon Him; of those learned divines who pronounced judgment against Him; and of the rest of those who, in a veil of imperception, were veiled from recognizing Him.
I have made mention of that which took place aforetime that haply no king may henceforth perpetrate any action that would result in his abiding eternally in the Fire. The reason why this matter hath been so greatly stressed in the Bayan is that none should become a cause of sadness unto another: haply, He who is the Absolute Possessor of Command and creation may not be saddened by the ghostly images in the mirrors – ghostly images, that is, if they be turned towards Him: for otherwise, how can pure non-entities who, from the beginning to the end of their lives, with the utmost precaution and endeavour worship God, and perform their works for His sake; yet who, at the time of the appearance of the Manifestation of God, are completely lifeless – how can such be profited by their works? Nay, in the sight of God they are unworthy even of the designation “non-entity” – which denoteth the very essence of non-existence.
None can pronounce sentence save Him Whom God shall make manifest: and He is that Goodly Tree Who is made manifest with Verses and Signs for the sake of the good pleasure of the Lord, and the renewal of His religion; to judge with righteousness among the people of the Bayan, and to judge with justice any soul who hath not come within its fold – if any such remain unto that day: for otherwise, how could the kings of the Bayan consent to drink water while there was yet on earth one who did not believe in the Lord and His religion? To resort to such measures, however, is not permitted save to those who are endowed with sovereignty in the religion of the Bayan; nor is it permitted them to do so against those who are related to the religion of the Bayan, in any circumstance, or in any condition, or in any instance: save on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, and against other than the believers in Him and in the Bayan; in which case, permission is granted them to conquer the countries, so that they may cause all to enter beneath the shadow of belief in the Lord and His religion.
Let them not inflict so much as an atom of sorrow upon those who are related to the Bayan. Even, in the conquest of other lands, He hath not approved resort to such a measure against their peoples: nay rather, so far as circumstances allow, let them seek by other means to cause them to enter within the religion of the Lord. Ever, in the eyes of the unperceiving people, hath the gear of this world been dearly cherished: who knoweth but that through the expropriation thereof they may be caused to enter into the religion of God. This law, however, is with respect to other than the people of the Bayan, not they: save on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, when the command of God is the Command which shineth forth from the Court of His Holiness.
Howsoever the command of God be exalted by Him, it is for all to bring it forth from latent potentiality within themselves into manifest existence in the world of being – each in accordance with what he is able to arrange and destine: howbeit, the servant hath never been able to arrange, or to destine, aught save by the leave of God. He, verily, is the best of arrangers and the best of destiners; the best of the exalted, and the best of the peerless. Naught escapeth His knowledge, whether in the heavens, or in the earth, or in whatsoever is between them. Naught can frustrate His purpose, whether in the Kingdom of Command, or of creation, or aught other than these twain. He createth whatsoever He willeth through His Command. He, verily, is powerful over All Things.


Gate Six of the Fourth Unity: On this, that He verily shall not be asked of His doing, while all besides Him shall be questioned of all things
The substance of this gate is this, that there hath never been, nor there will ever be, any revelation or concealment for the Eternal Essence, while none besides Him hath ever had, nor will ever have, any revelation or concealment either. None is permitted in His sublime Court, so that He may be even praised as “He shall not be questioned”, and He is sanctified above any action, to be associated with His Essence, so that He may be praised by “He doeth,” or “He ordaineth”!
Nay, rather, He created the Primal Will, even as He created all things through the Will, while fashioning the Will by Itself. Likewise, He hath related all things unto the Will, and the Will unto Himself, on account of the sublimity and glory of the Will, even as He hath called Ka’bih His own House, whereas all places are equal before Him. Therefore, the distinction of Mecca is due to the sublimity and glory of the attribution unto Him. In the like manner, He hath made the Will the manifestation of “He shall not be questioned”, for in His knowledge there is nothing more exalted than the Will to be worthy of such bestowal. The same is true of “He shall not be forced”, “He shall not be referred unto”, and the like.
Thus He hath destined the Will to be the Manifestation of “He doeth what He willeth, and ordaineth what He wisheth,” inasmuch as His Essence (the Essence of the Will) is the same as His Will, and He hath never willed, nor will ever will, aught but that which is willed by God. And that which is willed by God will never be manifested except through that which is willed by the Will, even as that which is wished by God will never shine forth except through that which is wished by the Will. And none besides the Will can be worthy of such bestowal inasmuch as all are created through Him (the Will). Should God single out two beings as His Will, then the Manifestation of Unity would never be revealed in the world of creation, and the order of the kingdoms of the heavens, of the earth, and of that which lieth between them, would come to naught.
Rather, from the beginning that hath no beginning till the end that hath no end, there hath always been, and will continue forever to be, one single Will, Who shineth forth in each Dispensation by a specific Revelation, becoming the Manifestation of “He shall not be asked of His doing, and He doeth what he willeth.” As to the Letters of the Living, naught will be seen in Them except His Will, even as in the letters multiplied out of the Letters of the Unity, naught should be seen except His Will. Should the heart of a believer conceive of that which is other than the object of His Will, he would not be reckoned, for that very moment, as an inmate of the paradise of that Revelation, and he would be numbered as one who hath rebelled against Him.
For the utmost glory of the mirrors is this, that naught would be seen in them except the Sun, and if that which is seen is the mirror itself, then it would never be worthy to be mentioned before the Sun of Truth. But if the Sun is witnessed therein, then the movement of the Sun would be its movement, inasmuch as it hath possessed, and will continue to possess, no essence but His essence, no praise, except His praise, no action, save His action, and no turning but His turning.
In the Revelation of the Furqan, Muhammad, the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, was the Primal Will, and the Letters of the Living of that Sun of Truth were the very Will of Him, submerged in His Will, inasmuch as They have always been, and will continue forever to be, revolving around His Command, and they willed that which was willed by Him. In like manner, until today, of all the letters multiplied from the Qur’anic Unity (19), those who have attained any nearness, have attained it on account of submerging their will in that of Muhammad, blessings of God rest upon Him, otherwise, they are not worthy of mention.
Thus all the grievous acts of hate which was committed within the Islamic Dispensation, were done by the actors who imagined that they are following His will, otherwise, they would have not even possessed the power and strength of a fly. The same had been true during the Dispensation preceding Muhammad, blessings of God rest upon Him, and the same is true in the Revelation of the Bayan when the Sun of Truth shineth forth in the name of gatehood, until the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest. For all that will happen will be done through His will, and should anything be performed against His good pleasure, it would be done out of the thought that it conformeth with His will, otherwise in this Revelation, nothing would have any power without it.
This is the meaning of “there is no strength nor power except in God, the Exalted, the Mighty.” Had that not been true , no Absolute Truth would have been grieved in any Revelation, inasmuch as at the end of each dispensation, the people of that Revelation seek utmost resemblance with the will of the Manifestation, that they may will naught but that which is willed by Him. Then it is not possible that they recognise their Beloved, and yet to desire aught but His love and the object thereof.
Shouldst thou desire to wintness this with the eyes of the truth, behold that if one cut off from himself the allegiance of faith, he would be severed from power over his own self, how much less to pronounce judgement of severance against anyone else, be it in the realm of the revelation or that of the creation. For example, a Muslim who negateth Islam from himself, he would be powerless to pronounce the decree of the law of Islam against himself, how much less against others. Likewise, at that moment of severance, he must be standing upon a particular religious path, even if it returneth to a distant religion of Adam. Then whatever judgement he may pronounce, it returneth unto the law of Adam, and since at the time of Adam, He was the Manifestation of the Will, then even this very judgement is pronounced by virtue of the power of God. For God hath negated any power or strength for aught but Himself. This is an insight for anyone who desireth to flee form all but God, and to recognise the truth in the realm of the revelation.
The same is true in the realm of the creation. Should one desire to comprehend it truly, he should witness that if he is not within the Bayan, he would be utterly devoid of any strength and power, inasmuch as the essence of all men are brought in the Bayan, therefore, there remaineth no strength nor power in anything besides the Bayan, to constitute an exception. For in truth, there remaineth no strength and no power, which is in God, in the community of Jesus, otherwise, there should be amongst them some who would be judged as true, whereas it is not. The same is true with regard to Islam after the Revelation of the Bayan, and in regard to the Bayan after the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, inasmuch as in that day all strength and power is in God, which will only be revealed out of that Truth Who is the Manifestation of the Will. Therefore, there would be left no more strength or power in truth, for the people of the Bayan, save by abiding beneath His shadow.
Likewise, comprehend that in all the endless Revelations of God, whatever strength and power that may have ever existed in falsehood, it hath been solely due to its relation to truth, even as today, they do the evil things they do with the illusion of that same relation, otherwise in each Revelation, there is no strength nor power except in God, namely, in that which is revealed from Him. Shouldst thou behold with the eyes of the heart, thou wouldst witness that all strength and power belongeth to Him Whom God shall make manifest, in God, glorified and exalted be Him, and that this Revelation is by His grace and assistance, just as all Revelations from Adam till today have been by grace and assistance of this Revelation.
Gaze not upon the places and limits, inasmuch as the Will is the supreme Sign of God, and from time immemorial it hath referred unto God. Had not the First Adam been assisted by This Manifestation of the Will, He would not have attained faith beneath the shadow of This Faith, even as all Prophets are faithful in each Revelation. Likewise, were This Revelation to be unassisted by the grace of Him Whom God shall make manifest, how could They return, in the Day of Revelation, unto Him, and be wholly detached from aught but Him? For should there be thousands and thousands of Revelations afterwards, nay rather, indefinitely, limitless in their range, with no end for them, by them, of them, in them, and towards them, all would be assisted by the grace of the Last Manifestation of divine Revelation, Who is exactly the very First Adam, Who hath no beginning in the world of creation.
This is the hidden mystery of the truth. Should one swim in this sea, he would behold that there is no strength nor power except in God. Then he seeth both ideas of God’s absolute determinism (jabr) and human absolute freedom (tafvid) as barred from truth, treading the path that is wider than the distance between the heavens and the earth. He recogniseth in each age, the Manifestation of “He doeth what He willeth, and He ordaineth what He wisheth”, and acknowledgeth Him upon His declaration. And he weepeth throughout the times of Concealment, till the Day of His Next Revelation, inasmuch as therein true recognition is inaccessible to all. Thus he boweth down before the Manifestation of “He shall not be asked of His doing, while all are questioned at His behest” upon His declaration. He shall not be veiled from Him, and will not be separated from Him even to the extent of the separation between the Letters B and E. For he can see that whatsoever that is manifest in each Revelation is manifested by His word, and fixeth his gaze upon the Essence of the Cause, and not on the multiplied tokens of each Revelation.
For in the sight of such wayfarer, the utmost paradise of union, which naught can be imagined to surpass it in the world of creation, is the new Revelation, while he can directly behold all past Revelations within that Revelation. For example, if one had fixed his gaze upon the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, he would have been able to witness all the Prophets in that same gaze, and he would have observed all the next Revelations in His Revelation, to the degree possible therein.
Such a person is worthy to recognise Him Whom God shall make manifest, and to say unto Him, when turning towards God, ‘O my God! Thou art the First, and there hath been naught before Thee,’ for all past Revelations have ended in the Bayan, and all that is in the Bayan endeth in Him Whom God shall make manifest. Then where there could be any truth before Him worth mentioning? Indeed, had there been any truth other than His truth, the faithful of the past religions would have not been judged as non-believers.
‘And Thou art the Last, and naught existeth besides Thee,’ for in His Revelation, all His subsequent Revelations, are Him and naught but Him, ‘And Thou art manifest in sovereignty, and naught is above Thee,’ for each Manifestation is manifest in His age through Him, and not through His non-believers, inasmuch as had there been any one manifest besides Him, he should have been judged as surpassing Him, whereas he is not even reckoned as a faithful, how much less His superior,
‘And Thou art the hidden, and none existeth besides Thee,’ for had there been anyone hidden besides Him, he should have been the essence and the possessor of a thing, whereas in the day of His Revelation any essence or possessor of anything is a mere nothing, save through Him, even as every possessor of anything cometh to naught in the new Revelation, unless he entereth that Revelation, Who is the Manifestation of God,
‘Thou verily art potent over all things.’ For there existeth no manifestation of power besides Him, inasmuch as had there been any, there should have remained a sovereignty form a sovereign, whereas in each Revelation, all previous manifestations turn into abject nothingness if they fail to enter therein.
Therefore, the true mystic knowers of God, attain the ultimate delightful joy of their existence upon the Revelation of the Sun of Truth, while they weep from His setting till the next dawning, on account of His concealment, with the utmost suffering unrivalled by any other pain. For all suffering are under the shadow of this supreme vexation. Behold the separation of infant from milk. He suffereth so much inasmuch as the milk preserveth his physical being, then how much more one should suffer if he would be veiled from that which preserveth his very heart? All the phenomenal types of love visible amongst the people are due to the shadow of love that is manifested in the soul. See how the separation from it so effectively causeth vexation amongst all the tokens of the kingdom of the Sovereign Lord of existence. Yet, the love pertaining to the soul is not even worth mentioning compared to the love pertaining to the spirit, just as the love pertaining to the spirit is not even comparable with the love pertaining to the heart!
By The sanctified Essence of God! All are wandering perplexedly in the world of nature. Should they ascend above it and enter the world of essential body, they would not be able to stand an infinitesimal part of a moment of separation from the Manifestations of magnification, nay, rather they always unpack the saddle (rahl) of their journey of annihilation at the Last Resting Place (qabr-i-akhir). In the like manner, should they enter the world of love pertaining to the soul, they would retreat in the vicinity of the Manifestations of the celebration of divine unity, and were they to advance from there, they would turn into the inmates of Manifestations of praise. Should they ascend therefrom, they would seclude themselves in the love of the manifestations of glorification, and were they to ascend therefrom, they would fix their gaze upon the Manifest in these Manifestations, and bow down in adoration before God.
For all love that is preceded by faith, turneth into paradisical love, otherwise, it is to be seen naught but the love of the thing in fire. How pure and essential is this Essence, and how detached and transcendent is this Detached reality, and how indivisibly pure is this pure Simplicity, and how delightfully pure is this Essence of unity (kafur), that all delightful joys are created beneath the shadow of His sovereignty, and receive existence out of the relation with Him. For all true delight and joy is in submitting to His good pleasure, even as the man partaketh, when he knoweth that this is His good pleasure, of the cup of affliction, as if he is quaffing from the cup of the pure wine in the heaven. Then how much more he would rejoice if he partaketh of His love, besides which all love is utter nothingness!
Thus, in the time of each Revelation, the explorer inmate of this paradise is wholly surrendered to that glorious Countenance, while from the time of His setting till His rising, he is beset with the sorrow of separation. But before him, and before all who are endued with knowledge, his grief on account of the remoteness from Him, is far more delightful than any pleasure experienced by others.
How can the pen stream forth concerning the lifting of the veils, where all are drowned in the sea of veils, and they have not yet ascended from the world of transitory and accidental body, which turneth to dust after the death? Then how much less they ascend from the essential body, and even less from the stations ordained by God to be above it. Therefore, those who partake of such substantive glorious delight are scarcer than the philosopher’s stone. Nay, rather, none can be found except those who only delight in things whose pleasure is limited to the duration of their life, should they possess them, otherwise, it is not destined that all would even always attain the object of their transitory pleasure.
The fruits of all the Bayan is this that ye recognise the Point of Truth upon His Revelation, for ye shall behold all good beneath the shadow of such recognition, and that ye will not be veiled from Him, for then ye be deprived of all good. At least, Traverse ye in the world of the essential body, that haply ye may be able to befittingly attain His presence in at least one morn. Otherwise, in the realm of the transitory and accidental body, day and night all have been, and will continue to be, with Him, inasmuch as He is concealed within His own Throne amongst these creatures. And that same place is the sublime paradise, and the supreme heaven, even as it hath been before His Revelation, and will continue to be after His Revelation, as well as after His setting, in whatever exalted throne that is destined by God for Him.
All the people of the Bayan are like the fishes who live in the water of His commands, by His grace, and see naught but Him, nay, rather see their own lives through Him, and yet they are veiled from Him.
In reciting each command, gaze ye upon its fruit, that in each Revelation ye may not be shut out as by a veil from Him, inasmuch as this is the fruit of all knowledge and of all deeds, should one but behold. Well is it with Him who is mentioned by God, for verily when he is so mentioned, all things shall mention him, for God remembereth the best. He is the Manifestation of the Will, Who is in this Revelation the Point of the Bayan, and in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, none but Himself, Who is exactly This very Soul in the Resurrected Revelation, Who shall be manifested to a higher degree of excellence.
Should one be mentioned by Him, it is he who is mentioned by God, and none but him. Wander not aimlessly in your vain imaginings, for ye will not find anything. For verily the Cause of God shall be revealed from His treasuries, and He is the Lord of the treasuries of the Cause of God, aforetimes and hereafter. Will ye not be thankful?


Gate Seven of the Fourth Unity: Explaining that the beginning is from God through Him, and the return is through Him unto God
The substance of this gate is that all else but God is His creation, and that the beginning of all things is from God through His command, and the return of All Things is to God through His command.
Consider thou the Daily Prayer, which began from the command of God, through His Apostle – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and the return whereof is unto God, through the command of the Point of the Bayan. In like manner, on the advent of Him Whom God shall make manifest, apply ye this same principle to all the laws of the Bayan, for He is not other than the Point of the Bayan, that there should be occasion to speak of a return to other than God, or a beginning to other than Him. Nay, wherever any beginning can be conceived of, it is to God; and wherever any return can be conceived of, it is to God: howbeit the realization of this beginning and return is through the Manifestation of God of the age in question, so that whatever prayers have been offered up in Islam all circle around the command “Perform ye prayer,” which was uttered by the tongue of the Will.
The same is true likewise in the return: should all these believers, at His bidding, alter the manner of performance of the Daily Prayer, this cometh not but from God; although, in the eyes of those endued with understanding, the beginning is the same as the return, and the return the same as the beginning.
It is not, however, that ye should regard this matter as valid in the realm of theory, yet remain shut out as by a veil from reaping the fruit thereof: inasmuch as this matter hath been addressed on countless occasions in the books of the later writers – yet no one hath reaped the fruit thereof: which is this, that if in this day someone looketh upon the Point of the Bayan and His commandments, he should see naught therein but the beginning, which is the Point of the Furqan and His commandments; even as he should see in Him Whom God shall make manifest none other but the Point of the Bayan. Then would the fruit of this knowledge become apparent in him; otherwise, what would it avail him to have uttered sounding phrases to this effect, but to have remained shut out as by a veil from the fruit thereof? Sufficient in the eyes of those endued with understanding are this admonition and explanation, should they ponder thereon in the light of reason.
God beginneth All Things, then returneth them. Verily, unto God shall all return: that is, unto the command of Him Whom God shall make manifest. Blessed is he who attaineth unto Him; for He, verily, is the Almighty, the Best-Beloved.


Gate Eight of the Fourth Unity
explaining that by His Verses He createth the essence of All Things; sustaineth them; causeth them to die; and quickeneth them to life.
The substance of this gate is that all things revert constructively to man’s temple, the which was created from four signs: the sign of creation, which is his heart, and the sign of sustenance, which is his spirit; the sign of death, which is his soul, and the sign of life, which is his body: all of which are regarded as deriving from the nineteen Gates of Paradise: inasmuch as whatever instances of creation, sustenance, death or life occur are in virtue of the appearance of these manifestations. Such too is the case with the nineteen Gates of the Fire who stand opposed to them: for here too, whatever instances of these modalities occur are performed “in God” through them: inasmuch as these souls had formerly been numbered with those whose actions were performed “in God,” notwithstanding that they have since departed therefrom. Thus it is that they are now judged “Second,” since they have not become conjoined to the Possessor of the Seven Letters; for otherwise they were the “First” who were conjoined to the mention of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him.
For example, should one of the people of the Bayan bestow a rose petal upon a believer, this is naught but the doing of the Letters of the Vahid, for the bestower is among the number of those who have proliferated therefrom; nor hath he performed this act but for the sake of obedience unto them; neither in this act is aught to be seen but the doing of God. Thus it is that if in the East or the West one of the people of the Bayan revealeth unto another some aspect of creation, sustenance, death or life, it is in reality the Lord Himself who hath performed this act, while he, at the moment of its enactment, is the revealer thereof; nor is aught seen in him but that First Vahid, wherein naught is seen but God. Thus it is that none but God createth aught; nor any but He sustaineth aught; nor any but He causeth aught to die; nor any but He quickeneth aught to life.
In like manner, if in the East one of the Letters of the Fire revealeth some aspect of these modalities unto another, such an act is performed “in God,” but not “for God;” neither doth it return “unto God,” nor can it be described as proceeding “from God:” for at the moment of its enactment he beheld other than God: and to behold other than God cometh not about save by beholding aught else but the Point of the Bayan; even as the meeting with God cannot be realized save by gazing upon Him.
Whatsoever is brought into being in the Bayan through these four modalities is in virtue of the Verses and Words that have been sent down in the Bayan. Consider thou the past: Had the Verse of Pilgrimage not been revealed, how would all the various circumstances relating to creation, sustenance, death and life that are attendant upon the performance of pilgrimage have come to pass? So likewise regard thou all the laws, nor see aught else but God, inasmuch as there hath never been, nor ever shall be, one who createth, or sustaineth, or causeth to die, or quickeneth to life, but Him.
Remain thou not, in any Revelation, shut out from the Point as by as veil: for shouldst thou be shut out for even the twinkling of an eye, thou shalt not be numbered with those who make manifest the doings of God Himself: even as today, if a believer in the Qur’an become a manifestation of sustenance, although he is a sustainer “in God,” yet because he hath not recognized Him, and hath remained shut out as by a veil from His Revelation, he returneth not unto God, that his action should be accounted worthy to be subsumed under the shadow of the actions of those who manifest His own doings.
Today, for example, should a believer in the Bayan bestow upon another a cup of water, this, in the eyes of whoever hath recognized God, would be sweeter than that someone who was not a believer in the Bayan should serve up, in the most loving manner possible, all the delicacies of the earth: inasmuch as the offering of this cup of water is subsumed under the shadow of the actions of those who manifest the doings of God Himself; whereas that action, although it was performed “in God,” is not today possessed of any consequence, nor doth the Lord attribute it to them who make manifest His own doings: inasmuch as the particular manifestations wherein the author of this action believeth have, in this Dispensation, been lifted up, and have arrived at their own abodes – yet still he hath not realized this: how then could his action be regarded as subsumed under the shadow of the actions of those who exemplify the doings of the True One? Glorified, immensely glorified, is God above any such conception.
Should anyone attain the bounty of exemplifying a single aspect of the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, it would be better for him than to exemplify every aspect of the Bayan – after His appearance, not before: for in that act, the doing of God is manifest; whereas in the case of all that went before, although it is performed ‘in God,’ yet is it unworthy to be attributed to God; unless, that is, He Himself should become an aspect of the Bayan, when the performer of the act would indeed be worthy to be numbered with those who make manifest the doings of God. For how like it is that the Letters of the Living in that Revelation should be made manifest, and the people still be cleaving unto the present Letters of the Living, and bowing down before them in their resting-places, even as is witnessed in this day. Although these Letters of the Living are identically the same as those, yet, on the advent of the Revelation, they are deprived of their former consideration, while the “doing of God” is revealed in those manifestations who are apparent. Thus it is that judgment is passed against them.
Wait, then, O ye endued with insight: verily, We too are waiting!


Gate Nine of the Fourth Unity
concerning this, that whatever king is raised up in the Bayan should by all means leave a record of his name, and that which God hath destined for him from His presence, up to the Day when God shall assuredly make manifest the Point of the Bayan, that He may recompense each soul according to his works: He, verily, is swift in reckoning; and He, verily, is the All-Possessing, the Most High.
The substance of this gate is that from the time of the descent of the Point of the Bayan until the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, whatever king hath the honour to be raised up in the Bayan, and who, in the path of the love of the Point of Truth, showeth forth all that he is capable of in the way of exalting His word and of blazoning His mention – it shall befit him to set all this down, with matchless eloquence and incomparable lucidity, in a written chronicle; up to the day of the return of the Point, so that He may reward him with the finest of recompenses.
What higher recompense can there be than this, that the Person Whose citation is the citation of God Himself in respect of all things – that He of all people should commend him, and express satisfaction with him? Sufficient honour must this be unto him, in his own eyes, and in the eyes of aught whatsoever, inasmuch as he is thereby constituted the beginning of the proliferation of the First Vahid by way of Power.
If, from the time of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – until today anyone had kept such records, it would have been possible to ascertain what exploits had been performed: yet, one who acted letter by letter according to His religion hath not been heard of. In the Bayan, however, whosoever is raised up shall be made manifest with the panoply of Divine power and everlasting ascendancy; and, in virtue of conquering all the countries, shall become rich enough to dispense with levying so much as a grain of mustard seed from any believing soul.
God enricheth whomsoever He willeth through His grace: He, verily, is the Most Gracious, the All-Bountiful.


Gate Ten of the Fourth Unity
concerning this, that it is not permitted to provide instruction in books other than the Bayan, unless they have been composed therein, and in subjects related to the understanding of the Word of God; and as for the contrived sciences of logic and juridical principles, and others such as these, permission hath not been granted any of the believers to occupy themselves therewith.
The substance of this gate is that the Lord of the world hath made manifest the Point of the Bayan in this Revelation in modes innumerable: whence on the one hand the affirmation “Verily, I am God, no God is there but Me” – representing the most exalted level of guidance unto the Lord – and on the other the affirmation “Verily, I am lowlier than the lowliest atom,” have both proceeded from His tongue. In each respect, the Bayan hath been revealed from Him in ways innumerable: whether in the mode of Verses; or that of Prayer; or that of Commentaries; or that of Philosophical Sciences; or that of Persian Responses: so that no one should stand in need of another.
Permission hath not been granted for instruction to be given in other than His traces. Permission hath however been granted if someone compose a work in some science, when such hath been designated by the Name of God – signifying belief in Him: instruction may legitimately be given therein if it be headed with the words of the Point: for otherwise how should it guide unto the Tree of Truth, if in this “mention” no mention hath been made of Him Who caused this mention to be mentioned therein?
It hath been forbidden to compose works on subjects that neither “fatten nor appease the hunger,” such as juridical principles; logic; rules of jurisprudence and philosophy; the knowledge of disused languages, and the like. As for that which hath been elaborated in the fields of grammar and syntax, such measure of instruction as will enable the student to recognize subject and object, and the various subsidiary matters related to these twain, shall be sufficient: for beyond this, God shall not forgive the servant if he occupy himself withal. Notwithstanding, in this Dispensation most of the people have, in virtue of the Persian Words, become independent of aught else.
Should anyone wish to understand the Bayan, he may take therefrom so much as shall suffice to satisfy his need, no more than this; and from the Bayan itself, not from another source. This is the straight path for those who are undergoing instruction and education: up to the Day when the Tree of Truth shall be made manifest, whereupon the Book of Truth shall speak forth, and recourse unto the Silent Book shall be accounted a mark of being shut out as by a veil from the Speaking Book, the Which is a Book that is exalted and sanctified above the scientific and practical expressions of the people.
Even as in this present Revelation of the Point, anyone who came into His presence hath seen that He was destitute of the sciences of syntax, grammar, logic, jurisprudence and juridical principles, and all their subordinate branches. For the object of all these is to understand the purpose of God in that which He hath uttered: what need, therefore, hath One Whose purpose is the purpose of God, and Whose utterance is the utterance of God, for any such matters? – considering that the Lord hath bestowed upon Him an ability, and a power of utterance, such that in two nights and days – should no interruption occur – a dexterous scribe, writing with the utmost rapidity, could take down from that Mine of utterance the equivalent of the whole Qur’an: utterance of a nature that, were all the learned people on earth to combine together, they would be unable to understand a single Verse thereof, how much less to produce its like, or to speak in such a fashion, or to understand its deeper import. Such is the favour of God in respect of whomsoever He willeth, howsoever He willeth, with whatsoever He willeth, and for whatsoever He willeth; He, verily, is the All-Powerful, the All-Knowing.
Suffer not such matters to shut you out as by a veil from your Best-Beloved on His appearance: for in the Qur’an aforetime the Lord sent down admonitions of a like tenor, all the fruits whereof are in this Verse:

“It is God Who created seven heavens, and of the earth their like: the Command cometh down betwixt them, that ye may know that God hath power over All Things, and that the knowledge of God hath encompassed all things.”

Yet when the time arrived to garner the fruit thereof, all wished to demonstrate the impotence of Him Who is the Manifestation of Power, and the ignorance of Him Who is the Manifestation of Knowledge: whereas they had all been called into existence for no other purpose than to confess His power and His knowledge.
Should anyone, on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest – Who is the Manifestation of the power and the knowledge of God – become, in virtue of the Verses which the Lord sendeth down upon Him, assured of His truth, he shall have attained the fruit of the Bayan; otherwise, how numerous are those who have read the Qur’an, yet remained shut out as by a veil from its fruit, which is to confess the power and the knowledge of Him Who is the Manifestation of this Verse, Who is the Qa’im of the House of Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him. For conceive thou the likeness of His Holiness as that of this Verse: just as in this Verse naught is seen but the power of God, and His knowledge, so too in Him naught is seen but the power of God, and His knowledge. All have been created to this end, yet today have remained shut out as by a veil from carrying it into effect, inasmuch as they have not had regard for Him Who is the Manifestation of His knowledge and power.
His knowledge is not but in Himself, through His own Self; and in His creation, through His own creation; while His power over aught is not but in Himself, through His own Godhead; and in His creation, through His own Lordship. This is the essence of every essence, wherefrom all are shut out as by a veil.
