The fruit of this Chapter is that thou shouldst look to the Source of the law, so that if thou live in the Day of His appearance, thou wouldst not, through this same law of His, be shut out as by a veil from Him: even as today, thou seest that in the shadow of each one of the laws of the Qur’an an illimitable number of souls are, through the blessing thereof, pronouncing judgment: whereas on the Day of Revelation, all, when confronted by His word, become as naught, if they return not unto His word; otherwise, they shall receive whatever gracious outpouring is possible in the world of being. And how perplexing is the matter for the one who is shut out as by a veil from the Source! And how easy is the matter for the one who returneth unto the Source!
Blessed are the God-fearing in virtue of the excellence of a mighty Day!


Gate Thirteen of the Sixth Unity
concerning this, that it is not permissible for the doors of the House of the Point to exceed ninety-five, or for those of the Houses of the Letters to exceed five.
The substance of this gate is that since at Night mankind have recovered from the stupefaction of the Day of Resurrection, and wish to seek to draw nigh unto the Lord through the First Vahid (notwithstanding that were that same day to be the day of the beginning, all would be reduced to naught; yet, because there is no testing in operation, all outwardly claim to commune with their Best-Beloved, and to enjoy His good pleasure), for this reason it hath been enjoined that they may, if they be able, enter into the resting-places of the Letters of the Vahid: for these are lands than which there exist none more exalted in Paradise.
Permission hath not been granted for the House of the Point to have more than ninety-five doors: this as a token that He is the Mirror of “For God” (“Lillah”), aforetime and hereafter, wherein the Sun of Truth hath been, and shall be, manifest; nor, in the case of the Letters of the Living, hath permission been granted for the doors to exceed five: this as a token, in an all-embracing manner, of His “Dominion” (“Mulk”). This is the intention of what the Lord hath attributed unto Himself, not those worldly matters wherein all take pride. Whosoever assimilateth himself unto their likeness deserveth, at his own level, that this designation should be applied in the secondary sense unto him, until the matter endeth in the furthest limit of existence.
The fruit thereof is this, that if, on the Day of Resurrection – by which is intended the appearance of the Point, and the raising up of these Letters, as well as of the rest of the guides, be they of the rank of prophet, saint, witness or believer – if those servants who enter these resting-places were sincere in their belief aforetime, then on that Day too their sincerity shall become apparent in the sight of God, and of His Names.
Consider thou, for example, the Revelation of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him. For a protracted period no one even believed in Him, so as to resolve to visit Him: whereas now, as thou beholdest, each year seventy thousand souls undertake this visitation. Today however, when all have been tested, it is evident that things are once more as they were at the beginning, when no one went to visit Him: for those whom thou now beholdest to undertake this visitation, do so only because it hath become a source of pride and glory. Thus it is that the works of all become of a sudden as scattered dust, inasmuch as they are not undertaken on the basis of discerning insight: else how is it that today – when that selfsame proof whereby at the beginning of Islam the truth of the station of the Apostle was vindicated, hath been made manifest on the part of God – all are shut out therefrom as by a veil?
Consider thou likewise how it was with Qur’an: at the time when it was sent down in the midst of a people distinguished for their eloquence, what things they said! – yet afterwards all the believers, upon learning of these expressions, asked wonderingly “Is it possible that anyone could hearken unto the Word of God, and yet express himself in such a fashion?” All made show of their belief, producing adorned copies of the Qur’an to the value (Baha’) of a thousand; yet the very ones who spake in this wise were tested: for the essence of Islam is found in these Five Provinces: and from the day of the first appearance of the Verses of God until today, would anyone – should he wish to do so – be able to reckon the number of true believers who have lived here?
Yet these same souls, had they existed in that day, would have spoken even as they spake: for indeed if they lived not in that day, they live in this, and behold that the Verses of God, like unto an ocean, are being revealed from the Source of bounty: yet still they speak of “insanity;” whereas if, at infinite removes, they understand His former utterance, they parade themselves as mujtahids before all. Such is the level of the people.
I have taken as an example the Point and His traces, so that thou mayest understand how the matter standeth with respect to the Letters of the Living. Today, as thou beholdest, millions upon millions commemorate the martyrdom of the Fifth Letter. For what reason was he aforetime the Fifth Letter, other than the utterance of the Apostle of God? – yet this designation was not even revealed in the Qur’an, in the mode of Verses (and even if it was, it is not today in the hands of the people). How then is it that not one person can pass over the Sirat, notwithstanding that millions upon millions do whatever they do in His Name? Thus it is that all becometh as scattered dust: so that on whatever day the circumstances of that day of martyrdom were to repeat themselves, thou wouldst see what thou hast heard of on that day. Nay, the Dispensation hath progressed: and just as the degrees of Paradise have become yet more exalted, so also in the opposing domain the degrees of degradation have descended downwards.
Thus it is that at Night there is no testing, whence all the people’s clamorous protestations “’Tis I, ’Tis I!” reach up to the Throne; whereas when the Day of Resurrection arriveth, it is these who perish in the first of its stupefying convulsions, ere ever the second arrive. Nor is the stupefaction of the Day of Resurrection an imaginary occurrence. If, for example, those same Letters who took the Message from the Source at the beginning of the Revelation delivered this unto anyone, and he did not at once accept its truth, he perished in the stupefying convulsion of the Day of Resurrection: for these Letters wished to convince the people, by the selfsame proof whereby their own religion had been established, of the truth of the Revealer of the Verses; yet, notwithstanding all this grace and mercy the Latter showed them, through representing Himself in the station – not of the Point – but of the last of the Gates, that perchance they might be delivered from stupefaction, and be able to support the throes of the convulsion (notwithstanding that, in the eyes of the followers of the Truth, the last is none other than the first manifestation), still it availed the people naught.
Such is the level of the visitants: today one thousand two hundred and seventy years have passed since the inception of Muhammad’s Prophetic Mission, yet no one hath, in a true sense, undertaken that visitation consisting in the meeting with God – a meeting which, as is explicitly stated in the third Verse from the beginning of the Surih of Ra’d, is the very reason why all were created: for to meet with the Eternal Essence is not possible in the world of being: whence by the expression “meeting with God” in the Qur’an is intended the meeting with the Tree of Truth, in Whose utterance naught is to be seen but the Verses of the Qur’an: which description, in the primary sense, is reserved to Him, inasmuch as none but He can produce the Verses of God in this fashion, from the Source of Command – not even the Letters of the Living; all the Names and Likenesses; and whosoever is at the level of creation, of the rank and file of the believers.
A matter that hath been treated in the Qur’an as so superlatively important – to the degree even that it hath been represented as the reason for the creation of All Things – behold, not one person adverteth thereto! Whereas in the case of the graves of the dead, which only at many removes go back to the utterance of the Source – night and day, millions upon millions enter and leave them! Thus it is that all people have acted – as they continue to act – in an insensate manner: for if one were to be governed by sense in his actions, he would not travel abroad to acquire a Tradition – the Vicegerency of whose author is established by the word of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon him – while the Prophethood of the Latter is in virtue of the proof He holdeth – and night and day circle about it, in order that he might qualify himself to act the part of mujtahid, while remaining shut out as by a veil from the very Source wherein all things culminate, and wherefrom they are raised forth anew.
Shouldst thou record, up to the end of this Revelation, that which befalleth the Letters of the Vahid at the hands of the people, then shalt thou know how many, among those who profess to love those Letters, and who visit them, are sincere in their devotion, and how many are otherwise: inasmuch as all are motivated, in the works they perform, by the fanciful imaginations of their own selves, whence these works are not performed for God. Although in their own conceit they perform their works “for God,” yet in the sight of God “for other than God” is the designation which applieth in their case.
No commandment hath been given with respect to these designated shrines: perchance, on the day when their occupants are raised up – a resurrection referred to as the “return” – if thou wert sincere in thy professions, thou wilt be faithful unto them. What expenses thou bearest in order to visit their bodies; whereas today, which is the Day of Resurrection, when thou canst attain the meeting of their living persons, thou dost not do so: and even shouldst thou wish to do so, it becometh in thine eyes a matter as weighty as Mount Uhud, whereby thou wishest to oblige the object of thy visitation; notwithstanding that thou wouldst have borne all the exertion of travelling unto his tomb, and, having secured that honour, wouldst, after thy return home, have vaunted thyself on this account over all: in which, hadst thou been truly sincere, thou must needs have exhibited in this wise thy sincerity during the life of the object of thy visitation.
Howbeit in the Darkest Night, do whatsoever thou art able: but see that thou garner the fruit, so that on the Day of Resurrection thou renderest not vain what thou hast done. If in the Bayan anyone should visit these graves of the Vahid, yet on the Day of Resurrection attain not the honour of visiting them in person, then whatsoever he hath done will be rendered vain. Regard thou such to be the case likewise in the Qur’an; derive for thyself the lesson thereof; nor be shut out from the Source.
Neither act thou on the basis of having companions and fellows in thine actions, but rather act by thyself, for God, even though thou hast no peer: as was the case at the beginning of Islam, when for seven years none but the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him – really and truly believed in the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him: while those who believed in Him thereafter, had they done so sincerely, would not, on the day of the ascension of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – have departed out of the fold of belief, so that there remained no more than three of His companions.
Look thou ever to the essence of the matter, in respect whereof religion becometh religion, inasmuch as the believers on that day in Medina were observing all the laws of the Qur’an: yet the verdict of belief was reserved for these three, who had regard for that whereby the truth of religion is established: for had they not regarded the matter in this light, they would not have been observing the laws of the Qur’an: even as all, at that time, who regarded not the matter in this light were observing them, yet a judgment of other than belief was passed in their regard, and their observance availed them naught.
This is the essence of knowledge and action, and the essence of the visitation to the Point and the Letters of the Living in the succeeding Resurrection, shouldst thou be able to apprehend it. Yea, thou shalt perform the act of visitation during the Night: but on the day when the fruit is garnered, thou shalt esteem thyself a “divine,” with a hundred students seated neatly in thy class; and shalt behold the Letters of the Living to be on their own, nay unknown: and so it is that art not able, on that day, to make visitation, and dost render vain whatsoever it is that thou hast done, without thy noticing it. For thy religion was founded upon the love of Him aforetime; while today thou allowest matters subsidiary to the root to shut thee out as by a veil from Him.
Yet shouldst thou reflect, thou hast on that day no excuse in the sight of God: inasmuch as that same proof whereby formerly the Letters of the Vahid were constituted such existeth also today: the which is the same proof that existed formerly in the Qur’an: but since thou hast not acted on the basis of discerning insight, thou art obliterated, yet heedest it not: and thou shalt be caused to expire, and shalt enter into the Fire, ere ever the thought come into thine heart that the Resurrection hath been set on foot; the Letters of the Vahid have returned; and the Divine decrees with respect to all creation have issued from the Point: yet because thou wast deluded by thy position, thou didst remain shut out as by a veil from all.
Wherefore, do thou put thy whole trust in God, lest thou be shut out as by a veil from the Source of Command: for when once the connection with the Source hath been established, all matters subsidiary thereto shall be established: otherwise all shall be rendered vain. There is no doubt that the difference between a man and an animal resideth in the essence of knowledge, the which becometh not evident save through the ability to speak or write. Shouldst thou reflect upon this knowledge, thou wouldst perceive that it compriseth innumerable degrees – not one of which is fruitful, save only the knowledge of God. Today, for example, among other than the Shi’ih, how many a knowledgeable expert is there in every art! – whereas thou, who art one of those that have submitted unto the Truth, would not adjudge them believers: with how much less reason, then, would He Who is the All-Seeing, the Subtile, adjudge them so?
Nor consider thou the knowledge of God to be an imaginary matter. Nay, such knowledge consisteth in the knowledge of the Manifestation of God, in each Revelation, Who holdeth in His hand the proof; for otherwise there is no one who doth not “believe in God:” nay, all the other-than-true peoples that there are from the Day of Adam until today – all believe in God, and in their own Apostle, in whatever age He was sent: yet because, in the succeeding Revelation, they entered not within its fold, they were rendered vain: for had the essence of knowledge resided in them, assuredly they would not have been shut out as by a veil from recognizing the Revelation of God.
This is the intention of the noble Verse “O my Lord! Why hast thou raised me up blind, when I had before been sighted?” – for today thou mayest hear one who saith “I was aforetime a believer (inasmuch as the intention is not an outward sightedness, but one of faith), and how is it that I have now been raised up blind?” The reply is as hath been sent down: “Thus it is: Our Verses came unto thee, and thou didst forget them: and thus thou thyself art today forgotten.” – in other words, when those same Letters of the Vahid in whom thou wast formerly a believer – under the names whereby they are known to thee – came unto thee with the Verses whereby thine own religion was established, thou didst ignore them, and wast shut out as by a veil from recognizing the Truth, and thus it is that thou hast been rendered blind: by which is not intended an outward blindness: for all, as thou observest, enjoy the use of this outward eye: nay, all share even with animals this external faculty of vision: nay, the intention is rather the eye of the heart, wherewith one may behold, and recognize, one’s Best-Beloved.
Today it is hard for thee to recognize the Point of the Bayan: but consider the Point of the Furqan. There is no doubt that the people of Jesus – peace be upon Him – were all awaiting the appearance of the promised Ahmad – may the blessings of God be upon Him and his Family – even as thou wert awaiting that of the last of the Imams – peace be upon them (shouldst thou represent that all were not awaiting it, amongst the Muslims too not all have assurance on this head: nevertheless, in that case “all” were awaiting the event, and in this case too “all” await it) – yet, after His appearance, no one recognized Him.
This is because the eye of their heart saw not, that they might recognize their Best-Beloved: for otherwise, had they recognized Him, never would they have deviated from the word of Jesus – peace be upon Him. Nay more, one thousand two hundred and seventy years have passed since the inception of the Prophetic Mission of the promised Ahmad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and still the eye of their heart is blind, and they see not; whereas their outward eye perceiveth all things: nay, in perspicuity of vision, they are able to descry through a telescope the countries of the earth upon the surface of the moon, and to count their number.
Shouldst thou look with a scrutinizing gaze, thou wouldst behold that in the one thousand two hundred and seventieth year from the inception of Muhammad’s Prophetic Mission – a year which marked the beginning of the appearance of the True One – the earth had become filled with iniquity and oppression, ranging from the earth of the wisdom of the hearts at one extreme, until the matter endeth with this physical earth of the body. At the beginning of the Revelation, the essence of faith resided in those souls who bestirred themselves to go in quest of the True One: and since the eye of their heart was open, they recognized the True One. For in that land, no one recognized the True One until after His appearance: but since these souls had within them the eye of God – and it is not possible to apprehend Reality save with His eye – they were accordingly able to discern the appearance of their Best-Beloved; and, by reason of His Verses, to make certain of His truth (albeit they knew not that this is the same Holy Personage Who had been promised unto them, inasmuch as it is not possible to recognize Him but with His own eye, which eye had not as yet been created within them – not outwardly, that is, for inwardly it had been). Thus it is that one embraceth the Truth, and seeth; while one is blind, and deviateth therefrom, and seeth not.
Regard thou such to be the case likewise from the appearance of the Point of the Furqan up to the furthest limit of the degrees of faith. How can it be that one should offer up his life on the plains of Karbila, and another perpetrate what thou hast heard of? – this is because one seeth; while another seeth not, conceiving nevertheless that the act he committeth is for God, even while it is perpetrated against God: whereas were he but to know that he was acting against the True One, he would consent that death should overtake him rather than that such a matter should be committed on his part.
Degree by degree, do thou travel through the ranks of the Revelation, until thy journey endeth with the final appearance of the Shi’ih: and indeed thou hast seen how the companions of the Siyyid – peace be upon him – turned unto the Truth, while other than they adhered to that which formerly they had embraced. This is that same Secret of Unity aforetime, which ended in the furthest limit of the Revelation, when those that turned not unto the Truth were negated in Negation; while those who, because the eye of their heart was open, turned towards it, were affirmed in Affirmation.
Nor indeed was it the case that the eye of the heart of all of them was open: for had this been so, none of them, after his ascension, would have deviated from his intention, inasmuch as he had trained them all for naught but the dawning of the Sun of Truth, and to make themselves ready against the “meeting with God” on the Day of Resurrection: yet everything came back, at the furthest limit of existence – when the Provinces of Islam, and the rest of the countries, had become filled with believers – unto that same First Vahid; notwithstanding that all these people – at whatever level they were lying – conceived the Truth to be with them: whereas of all these illimitable numbers, it was only those Letters of the Vahid who – faithful to their pristine and true nature – set out in quest of the Truth. This notwithstanding, all, out of the excess of their endeavour and piety, had arrived at the highest degree of conviction: and for one thousand two hundred and seventy years the heavens had revolved around them.
All these revelations are to the end that, in the Dispensation of the Bayan, thou shouldst look with discerning insight: perchance on the Day of the appearance of the True One – Who is the fruit of the Bayan – thou shalt be able to recognize Him with the eye of God; and be able, with the eye of the Vahid, to be guided by their guidance; and, with the eyes of them that guide unto God, to perceive the manifestations of His Names and Likenesses. For the likeness of the Day of Resurrection in relation to the Night is that of the planting of a tree, the time for the garnering of whose fruit is the Day of Resurrection, for ere then it hath not as yet arrived at the stage of maturity.
For example, in the Revelation of His Holiness Jesus – peace be upon Him –the tree of the Evangel, after it had been planted, attained not perfection until the beginning of the Prophetic Mission of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him: whence had this occurred but one day sooner, that day would have been the first day of His Mission – a day which would then have fallen upon the twenty-sixth, rather than the twenty-seventh, of Rajab. Whatever trees in the Evangel bore fruit did so during the twenty-three years of His Mission, when Divine Revelation was being vouchsafed; the decrees of God were being passed; and the actual decrees – meaning those delivered on the part of God – were being revealed.
After the planting of the Tree of the Qur’an, it arrived at its perfection in one thousand two hundred and seventy: whence had its arrival at maturity occurred at two hours after sunset on the fifth of Jamadiyu’l-Avval, the revelation thereof would not have occurred even five minutes later. For ever, upon the height of His Throne, the Tree of Truth is watchful, and looketh upon the tree that He hath planted in the hearts, spirits, souls, and bodies of His creatures. So soon as He observeth that, from a particular tree, a fruit of the recognition of the Unity of God may be garnered, this marketh the beginning of the Revelation, and, from behind the veils of “I was a hidden treasure,” He sendeth down the love of “I wished to be made known,” so that creation may thereby be “called into being:” to the end that the fruit thereof, which is the knowledge of Him, may be garnered in the succeeding Resurrection: inasmuch as the beginning of religion is the knowledge of God: and since the knowledge of God cannot be made manifest save in virtue of that by which God hath described His own Self, through the tongue of His Apostle, thus it is that such knowledge is dependent upon the knowledge of the One made manifest in the Revelation: and this same principle holdeth true likewise through all the ranks of creation, until the matter endeth in the furthest reaches of existence.
Whatever be the fruits of the Tree of the Qur’an, these must appear ere the ascension of the Tree of the Bayan: otherwise is it evident that the tree in question had no fruit within it, else would this have become apparent: for the gleaners of this Paradise are the angels who extol the glory of God: they gaze upon the whole of creation, and, if they behold upon a tree a fruit of the love of their Best-Beloved, they garner it: which act of garnering is the guidance thereof through the knowledge of the Desired One, and naught else. In like manner, on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, whoever among the people of the Bayan believe in Him, and in His Letters of the Living, these same are the fruits of the Bayan; whereas He consenteth not that any of them should be described as a tree without fruit; albeit, if such hath been decreed in the knowledge of God, then meet thereto is that which is seemly in His sight.
Yet, may all be granted refuge in the Sun of Truth, to take refuge in Whom shall avail them, inasmuch as to do so is identical to taking refuge in the Lord; else how many servants there are who have taken refuge in the Lord; yet because they have not recognized His guides, it is as though they have not sought refuge in God: forasmuch as all repeat the Word “I seek refuge in God” – even that very person in whose regard it was revealed, inasmuch as at the beginning of Islam he too was wont to repeat this Word: yet since he sought not refuge in the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him – to do which is identical to seeking refuge in God – he was not granted refuge from the fire of other than recognition; for otherwise every people whom thou beholdest repeat this Word, each in their own tongue: whereas their true predicament is apparent.
On the advent of each Manifestation, to take refuge in God is to take refuge in Him; while with the onset of each Concealment, it is to take refuge in the laws of that Revelation: up to the appearance of the subsequent refulgence, when neither the Former Manifestation, nor His laws, shall suffice to grant one refuge, but only the Latter Manifestation, and the laws revealed by Him. Be thou ever watchful of the beginning of the Revelation, for shouldst thou tarry for so much as the ninth of the ninth of the tenth of the tenth of the ninth of a second, thou shalt be accounted a “new believer” in the eyes of that embodiment of the Truth: even as today thou art wont so to characterize those servants who, having not previously been Muslims, enter the fold of Islam.
Such was the fruit of making visitation to the Letters of the Vahid, in the succeeding Resurrection, if thou canst apprehend it; and in this present Resurrection which precedeth it, if thou wert sincere in thy belief and devotion. God reserveth His mercy for whomsoever He willeth; and the grace of God is infinite.


Gate Fourteen of the Sixth Unity: Concerning the ordinance of God in respect of the time of the sun’s transition
The substance of this gate is that among the days the Lord of the world hath related one day unto Himself, naming it the “Day of God:” and hath pledged Himself that whosoever recognizeth the right and sanctity of this day, and observeth that which the Lord hath decreed therein, He shall reward with a whole year’s recompense. To expend one mithqal of gold on this day is equivalent to spending three hundred and sixty-one mithqals in the way of the Lord; and in this wise also do thou apply the command of God unto all pious works and enterprises.
This is a day whereon the sun travelleth from the sign of Pisces into that of Aries; and at whatever time this transition occurreth – whether by night or by day – it is fitting that an array of delicacies should be offered, no fewer than the number Vahid, nor more than Mustaghath; and in this period each person hath been, and is, permitted of God to serve up whatsoever he is capable of providing: inasmuch as on other than this day, permission hath not been granted in the Bayan for the enjoyment of numerous delicacies and bounties at one (Vahid) time, in order that each nutriment may confer its full benefit upon the one partaking of it. In like manner it is preferable, when extending hospitality, for the fare offered to be limited to a single bounty – but the finest thereof. Likewise in their regular evening and morning repasts, let the believers enjoy a single bounty, in a single sitting, establishing that the delicacies and bounties should diversify only as the meals multiply, the which proceeding is nearer unto piety in the sight of God.
Permission hath been granted them to recite at night, to the number of the whole year, this Verse: “God testifieth that there is no God but Him, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting;” and in the day the Verse “God testifieth that there is no God but Him, the Almighty, the Best-Beloved;” or alternatively the Verse “God testifieth …” wherein is the mention of “power,” the which is better for the reciters in the sight of God.
This day is the Day of the Point; while the eighteen days thereafter are the days of the Letters of the Living, which are nobler than the days of the following eighteen months, each day of which is related unto one of the laws of All Things; while the embodiments of all these laws in the world of being are the guides unto the Unity of the True One: which designation (since, according to outward appearances, there is in this Dispensation no mention of “prophet” or “viceregent”) applieth to the rank and file of the believers: except, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, when the Tree of Truth shall designate anyone by whatever name He wisheth: for apart from Him, no one recognizeth a person’s true station, that he should presume to judge it in this manner.
During the first Vahid, fasting is not permitted: nay rather, it is incumbent, through the Gates of the Vahid, to gain admittance into Paradise.
All these manifestations are to the end that on the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest – for it is He to Whom this first day belongeth, while His own likeness is that of the sun in the daytime – one should be guided through Him: not that it should befall as in the present Revelation, when a day such as this hath passed, while the One for Whom this day was created was in a state of sorrow: whereas it was precisely in virtue of its relation unto Him that this day was raised to honour.
Every thing on the Day of Resurrection appeareth in the form of a human temple: even the minutes and the hours; the night and the day; the days, months and years; and categories above and beyond these, until the matter endeth with the dawning-places of everlasting signs, and the revelations of the Ancient of Days, whereupon they become too glorious to be accounted subject to the limitations of God’s creation.
Ever hath God been the Knower, the Ancient; and ever hath God been the Ordainer, the Powerful.


Gate Fifteen of the Sixth Unity
concerning this, that God hath commanded you to rise up from your seats if ye hear the name of Him Whom God shall make manifest mentioned hereafter by the title “Qa’im;” and the decree that, as far as possible, none who cause Him sorrow should be left upon the surface of the earth.
The substance of this gate is that the Lord of the world hath granted all permission that, on hearing Him Whom God shall make manifest mentioned by this name, each one may rise up from his place, and then resume his seat, as a token of respect to Him on the part of the Book of God, and as a mark of honour to Him on the part of the Primal Point: perchance on the Day of Revelation none shall make a show of exaltation in His presence: inasmuch as all the works that are performed during the period when He is concealed from sight are for the day when He shall be visibly manifest.
Thus, were a person throughout his whole life to rise up whenever he heard this name mentioned; yet to hear, one hour ere he was caused to expire, that He had been made manifest (or were an Epistle to arrive from Him importing “It is I;” or were He Himself to come before him, announcing “It is I,” and making good His proof through the Verses whereby his own religion is established), and not at once to submit thereto on the part of the Qur’an, and to bow down before Him on the part of the Revealer of the Bayan, all the works he had performed during the period of His concealment would be rendered vain, as though he had done naught; whereas in the reverse case, his works would avail him: and, should He so wish it, He would pardon him if, during the days of His concealment, He had witnessed from him any other-than-loving act: notwithstanding that the lover can never deviate from the good pleasure of his Best-Beloved.
Do ye attend most carefully to this matter, and take heed (for it is inevitable that ye shall meet Him) lest ye show this degree of deference – and perform your works – for His name, while for the Bearer of this name ye do not what ye were performing for His mere appellation (albeit, did ye know it to be Him, ye would perform your works for Him; yet ye confuse the matter in your own eyes). Even as, in the Revelation of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – though all awaited His advent, yet, at the time of His appearance, thou hast heard how they bore themselves towards Him; whereas if they had but seen him in a dream, they prided themselves inordinately thereupon.
Likewise, in the Revelation of the Point of the Bayan, though all rose up at the mention of His name; night and day humbly and fervently entreated that His advent might be hastened; and, if they did but see Him in a dream, prided themselves inordinately thereupon; yet now that He hath been made manifest with the mightiest proof whereby their own religion is established, and those awaiting His advent are beyond all reckoning, all, after hearing His Verses, are sitting tranquilly in their homes, while He is at present consigned to solitude in this mountain of Mah-Ku.
Be a little watchful of yourselves, O people of the Bayan, that things fall not out again in this fashion: that ye should weep for Him each night and day, and stand up at the mention of His name; whereas now, which is the day whereon the fruit is garnered, and when, after having stood up at the mention of His name, ye have a means of attaining the presence of the Bearer of the name, ye be shut out in this manner as by a veil. Call ye to mind the behaviour of those who awaited the advent of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and what befell Him at their hands. Nor claim that they were not religious. Today, thou claimest that they were not religious; whereas on that day, amongst themselves, they conceived themselves to be acting at the highest level of their own code of virtue and religion; nor did they surmise that they might be other than true believers: even as today thou observest that all are acting at the highest level of their own code of virtue and religion; neither do they let the thought that they might be other than true believers so much as cross their mind.
Thou shalt come to hear of that which befell the Point of the Bayan, inasmuch as it hath been enjoined that all should write down and record the events of the Resurrection: perchance, in the succeeding Resurrection, they may be guided thereby: and thou shalt live to see the advent of Him Whom God shall make manifest.
Should ye make it a rule, O people of the Bayan, one and all, not to wish for any soul that which ye would not wish for yourselves – neither to represent falsehood as truth, or the reverse (for He is the purest essence of Truth, under Whose shadow if ye shelter not, ye shall be rendered vain in your religion) – perchance no sorrow may befall Him, and all the works ye have performed from the day of the appearance of the Point of the Bayan until that day may not in consequence be rendered vain.
Put your whole trust in the Lord that ye depart not from this thread: haply, since ye recognize Him not, ye may not bring sorrow upon your Desired One during the days of His Concealment: neither do so during the days of His Manifestation, when He shall make Himself known unto all in virtue of His Verses and His Words; yet, because ye are not all convinced thereby – so that ye might recognize Him – thus it is that ye are shut out from Him as by a veil; notwithstanding that no one hath any excuse for not making certain of His truth, after hearkening unto the Verses – Verses which are the Sirat whereby all enter into Paradise, while those who are wrapped in veils enter thereby into the Fire. Nor hath any greater Paradise been created than this: nay, it is too great to be described by the term “Paradise,” or by any description of a paradisiacal state, inasmuch as the creation of Paradise is realized through His command.
Shouldst thou wish to behold the beginning of Paradise, look thou at the beginning of the religion of Islam, when whoever entered therein was within the bounds of Paradise; otherwise was he in the Fire. Thereafter, degree by degree, Paradise diversified, until – as, one by one, it included the members of the Holy Family – behold how, on their successive appearance, the companions of each were the companions of Ridvan, and of Paradise, while other than they were in the Fire; and so the process continued until it ended in the last of the Gates, when the line of specific appointment was severed. Whosoever abided by the Divine intention, and that of the members of the Holy Family, was in Paradise; while whosoever deviated therefrom by so much as a barley seed was in the Fire. Behold thou finally the creation of Paradise in the appearance of the Name of the hidden of the hidden, and pronounce a sentence of other than Paradise upon whosoever recognized him not, and acknowledged not his due.
Thereafter, regard thou the beginning of Paradise as residing in the Bayan: and, until the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, do thou recognize those who follow it from those who deviate therefrom, and behold with thine outward eye the reality of Paradise and of the Fire, inasmuch as this is the intention of the references that have been sent down in the Qur’an concerning Paradise and the Fire. And seek thou refuge under all conditions from the fire of other than belief, for this condition shall become a cause of fire in the world to come; and so likewise in the case of faith, for this condition shall become a cause hereafter of the Most Great Ridvan, wherein hath been created that which is beloved unto the servant; and wherein hath been created no sorrow, or aught the knowledge whereof is not beloved unto the servant. God createth whatsoever He willeth through His command; He, verily, is powerful over all things.


Gate Sixteen of the Sixth Unity
concerning this, that no one is permitted to travel, unless he wish to visit the House of God, or the House of the Point, once he have means to do so; or he wish to engage in commerce; or he wish to visit the Letters of the Living, provided that he have means to do so, and that the journey be undertaken in a spirit of joy and radiance; or he wish to render someone assistance in the path of God; while should anyone compel another to undertake a journey; or enter his house without his permission; or wish to bring him out of his house without his permission, his wife shall be unlawful unto him for nineteen months; and should anyone transgress this law, and abide not thereby, it is incumbent upon the witnesses of the Bayan to take from him ninety-five mithqals of gold, which are not returnable; and should anyone wish to coerce another in this manner, it is the duty of whoever knoweth, or cometh to learn, thereof to attend and prevent him: and should he know thereof, yet not attend, then his wife shall be unlawful unto him for nineteen days: nor shall she be lawful to him after the expiry of these nineteen days until he make payment of nineteen mithqals of gold, if he be able, or else of silver: or, if he be unable to make payment of silver, then let him seek forgiveness of God nineteen times until he find means to do so: and let him make payment unto the witnesses of the Bayan, so that they may expend it upon those who sound the adhan at the tops of their voices, and thereafter upon the poor and needy among the people of this religion and of the Book, each as his circumstances dictate; nor should anyone undertake a journey save for the essential purposes of pilgrimage, or attaining the presence of the Point, unless he wish to make a visitation, or to engage in commerce, in which case it behoveth him not to prolong the days of his journey: and should he wish to prolong them, then it is incumbent upon him to take along with him his dependents, of those whose beings have been created from his essence: or else not to prolong his journey above eight and thirty months, save in the case of one who tradeth overseas, when he hath permission for five and ninety months: nor is he permitted aught beyond this: and should anyone exceed either limit, it is incumbent upon him, if he be able, to make payment of two hundred and two mithqals of gold, or else of two hundred and two mithqals of silver.
The substance of this gate is that permission hath been granted one to travel unto the House, and the resting-place of the Point, should he have means to do so; and to visit the resting-places of the Living; to engage in commerce; and to lend someone assistance, should he so wish; while for other than these visits permission hath not been granted. If, on a trading journey, he be accompanied by those who have been created from him, no objection can be raised against him; otherwise, permission hath not been granted for a longer absence than two years, in the case of a land journey (unless the journey itself consume this amount of time, in which case God hath granted him permission to tarry longer); while, in the case of a sea journey, permission hath not been granted for a longer absence than five years. The period in question is reckoned from the day of departure out of the house, until the return thereinto; and should he exceed this limit, then, if he is able, a payment of two hundred and two mithqals of gold, or else of silver, is to be rendered, in the manner that hath been ordained, the which is among the penalties fixed by God.
The fruit of this law is this, that on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, one should – at the very moment of hearing thereof – set out to attain His presence, and regard such a journey as taking precedence over that which hath been set forth in this Chapter: inasmuch as the whole of the Bayan is His: while if this, which is but one among the Chapters of the Revelation of His former religion, be not renewed in His Latter Manifestation, a sentence of belief shall not be warranted.
Travel is not permitted unless one have the necessary means, and it be undertaken in a spirit of joy and radiance: except on the appearance of the Day of Resurrection, when it becometh obligatory, even on one’s sandalled feet: inasmuch as it was for this that one was called into being: how then could a person consent to be separated from that which is the fruit of existence, should he have regard for the creation of his own being?
It hath been commanded, in the case of one who entereth the house of another without his permission; or compelleth him, by so much as a single footstep, to undertake a journey; or bringeth him out of his house without his permission, that for nineteen months marital union shall be unlawful unto him. Should anyone transgress this law, it is the duty of the witnesses of the Bayan to decree in his regard the sum of ninety-five mithqals of gold as a penalty for his transgression. It is moreover incumbent upon whoever learneth of an instance of someone exercising such coercion over another to prevent him: and should he neglect to do so, for nineteen days marital union shall be unlawful unto him: after the expiry of which he shall be required to make payment of nineteen mithqals of gold, if he be able, or else of silver: otherwise, let him seek forgiveness nineteen times, whereupon marital union shall again be lawful unto him: then, when he hath found means to defray the sum, either in silver or in gold, it is incumbent upon him to pay it unto the witnesses of the Bayan, who should expend it upon the needy: upon themselves, should they regard themselves as entitled to do so; or else upon those who sound the adhan, and upon the needy amongst the believers – at whatsoever level of belief the beneficiary be situated, he is to be praised.
The fruit of this is that perchance in the Bayan naught wrongful may be inflicted upon any soul: perchance such demeanour may become habitual to all so that, on the Day of His appearance, no sorrow shall befall the Desired One: for were it not for Him, no one would have become subject to any ruling whatsoever – that is, in virtue of their own entitlement: nay, it is out of the ocean of His bounty that all are now included among the number of those who are subject to the law: for otherwise most people are at the level of sheer indifference, inasmuch as they accept not, after it hath been offered unto them, the responsibility of submitting unto the Command of God. The Lord, however, hath under all conditions been rich enough to dispense with His creation; and He hath loved – as He now loveth – that all, with the utmost degree of love, should ascend through His Paradises, so that no soul should inflict upon another so much as a breath of sorrow; and that all may subsist in the cradle of His safety and security until the Day of Resurrection, which is the first day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest.
The Lord of the world hath raised up no Prophet, and sent down no Book, but that He hath covenanted with all concerning belief in the succeeding Manifestation and Book: inasmuch as there is no interruption or limit to the outpouring of His grace.
When travelling, it hath been, and is, forbidden that the stages of the journey should be prolonged: and however much these stages are rendered nearer and lighter, it is more beloved in the sight of God. Should a stage that can be travelled in a single day be travelled instead in two, it behoveth God to double the traveller’s provision. If in the course of a particular stage an animal experience hardship, it will invoke the vengeance of the Lord upon its owner. At all events, regard must be had for each animal’s capacity, so that after its owner hath entered within the fold of the Bayan, he charge it not but with a lighter load than it can bear, inasmuch as the profit he deriveth therefrom shall avail him naught. When travelling, consideration must, under all conditions, be had for the state of the weakest party; and whatsoever is productive of difficulty and hardship hath been, and is, forbidden: as indeed is all but what is conducive to joy and radiance on the way, according to the measures that have been destined on the part of God.
It hath ever been, and is, desirable that consideration be had for pedestrians under all conditions: and should one soul, in the way of the good pleasure of the True One, carry another upon his steed by so much as a single pace, the reward of a whole pilgrimage shall be inscribed in the book of his life’s work: and what bounty could be greater than this, should a person be favoured withal in the way of the Lord?
Whensoever all contrive to pass a journey in a spirit of joy and radiance, it shall become a part of Ridvan. That which was formerly ordained in this regard was on account of the veiled condition of all, who, on account of particularistic considerations of profit, would inflict weariness both upon themselves and upon others: for otherwise, had their journeys been undertaken in a spirit of joy and radiance, no such ordinance would have been given. The travels of the Arabs in this day bear witness unto the reason for the ordinance which was formerly given. Thus, degree by degree, the Dispensation shall progress until all are able to travel no more than a single farsakh in a single stage.
God preserveth whomsoever He willeth on the ways of travel, through His leave; He, verily, is the Preserver of all things.


Gate Seventeen of the Sixth Unity
concerning this, that what cometh out of a mouse is pure, and that there is no need for squeamishness in this regard; and so likewise in the case of the animal which flieth by night, and is named the “ababil.”
The substance of this gate is that, as touching the constraint all the believers had been under on account of what cometh out of a mouse, or that which flieth by night, or the like thereof – the need for such squeamishness hath been removed. Howbeit, for the sake of refinement and cleanliness, fastidiousness in this regard hath been, and is, beloved. These matters do not detract from a state of purity. Do thou under all conditions have regard for that whereby the pure is purified, so that thou mayest not be shut out as by a veil from the Source: lest, on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, thou shouldst speak of “impurity,” for He is more exalted than this: nay, it is His word that purifieth.
Under all circumstances He hath subsisted, and shall subsist, in habitations pure and purified: and, from the day which hath had no beginning until the end that shall have no end, He hath dwelt, and shall dwell, in the heaven of purity and the earth of refinement. Nor is aught capable of altering Him; while His fathers even unto Adam, and likewise His mothers, were the choicest of creation, and the repositories of pureness and purity. Blessed is he who cometh into His presence on the Day of Resurrection in a state of purity derived from Him: for this, verily, is a surpassing bounty.


Gate Eighteen of the Sixth Unity
concerning this, that no one is permitted to look upon the epistle of another, save in the case of merchants, if they permit each other to do so, or be aware of each other’s consent in this regard.
The substance of this gate is that no one, under any circumstances, hath been granted permission to look upon the epistle of another, whether sealed or open; whether a scientific treatise, a statement of account, or such epistles as people customarily write to one another: unless at whatever time he knoweth that he hath the other party’s consent in this regard; or the latter grant him permission; at which time it shall become permitted him to do so.
The taking of such a liberty hath not been forbidden but to the end that all may become arrayed in the mantle of bashful modesty so that, should they live to see the Day of Resurrection, they may not behave towards the Tree of the Desired One otherwise than is the way of bashful modesty. God, verily, protecteth such of His servants as He willeth from that which he loveth not; He, verily, is the Protector of all things.


Gate Nineteen of the Sixth Unity
On this, that it is incumbent upon all to reply when they are written to, and answer when they are questioned, and to heed all that is derived thereof.
The substance of this gate is this, that it is enjoined in this Revelation that should anyone receive a letter from any other, it would be his duty to write him back, by his own hand or that of another on his behalf, and delay or separation is not approved. In like manner, should one ask a question, it would be incumbent upon the addressee to give a guiding answer, that haply in the Day of the Revelation of God no one may be shut out as by a veil from Him. Thus when he revealeth, from God, “Am I not your Lord?” all would answer “Yea.” For the duty to reply is enjoined for this purpose, but its influence will extend till the last atom (dharr) of existence.
The same is true with regard to writing, inasmuch as there is no doubt that in the Day of Resurrection, His Books will be sent down unto all the people. Be warned lest anyone fail to answer the call of his Beloved, on account of his being wrapped up in veils. For it is by answering Him that man’s inmost reality would be created in the dharr of hearts, through acknowledging of the oneness of God, and in the dharr of spirits through witnessing unto prophethood, and in the dharr of souls through testifying unto viceregency, and in the dharr of bodies through confessing unto gatehood.
In each Revelation those who answer are distinguished from those who remain silent, otherwise, all answer in regard to the previous Dispensation. For example, can anyone be found today in the world of Islam, who would not utter the two declarative words of faith, and would not acknowledge that which is derived thereof, like viceregency and the laws of the Qur’an? Nay, this is unthinkable. But it is in the Next Revelation that the sincere men of truth would be distinguished from the insincere men of untruth, by virtue of their answer to the call of God.
That is a man endued with vision, who answereth the call of God in all worlds and all stations, should it be through writing, through utterance, or through action, which is the most mighty means of reply. And it is by virtue of the blessings of the answering of such soul, that all are enjoined to answer each other, to such a degree that if an infant cry out, it would be incumbent to answer him with any means possible. Likewise, should one’s condition silently call upon others, it would be the duty of the men of discernment to answer his call. In like manner should one’s seat of habitation call for answer, or any other manifestation discernible to men of vision, it would be binding upon them to reply, that at no time, no one may witness that which would cause him grief.
This command is binding that haply in the Day of Resurrection, when the eyes of hearts recognise not their own Beloved and Desired One, save those desired by God, they would not, unknowingly, inflict Him with grief, so that all of a sudden that which vindicateth religion would be raised, and yet they would be veiled by clinging to the secondary derivatives thereof. For in each Revelation, this is the veil that shuteth out those who are veiled. But God guideth whomsoever He willeth by His grace, for verily He encompasseth all things.

title: BB00001: Bayan-i-Farsi (Persian Bayan)
section: The Seventh Unity
text:
The Seventh Unity

Gate One of the Seventh Unity
concerning the renewal of books, should two hundred and two years have passed over them, and the washing clean of that which was written aforetime, or the bestowal thereof upon another.
The substance of this gate is that in each Revelation the Lord loveth All Things to be renewed: for which reason He hath commanded each person, once every two hundred and two years, to renew the books in his possession, either by immersing them in fresh water, or by bestowing them upon another: perchance no servant’s eye may fall upon any letter that he would view with abhorrence: perchance, on the Day of Resurrection, the Tree of Truth may behold the outward aspect of no letter to be in an unlovely form: perchance its spirit also, under the shadow thereof, may not prove to be unlovely: inasmuch as seventy thousand angels are charged with protecting each letter that is written; and this is the case also at the time of its washing clean, when they are instrumental in preserving it.
Wert thou today to look on earth, thou wouldst see how many souls are preserving a single letter of the Qur’an – souls whose number cannot be reckoned. The angels love to look upon each letter that is written in a lovely form: nay, do thou behold the same to be true of every object, and so too the reverse. Produce thou naught in the Bayan save at the height of artistry and perfection: perchance, on the Day of Resurrection, if the gaze of thy Best-Beloved fall upon it, He may behold naught unlovely in His creation: for the gaze of all the angels is in the shadow of His gaze. How few are the objects which, on the Day of Resurrection, shall be worthy of the gaze of the Tree of Truth!
Nay, if there be aught on earth which is peerless in its kind, that is an object which hath become worthy of the Sign of “There is naught like unto Him.” All shall renew their Bayans: yet let them be watchful, upon the appearance of the Tree of Truth – from whatsoever land He may shine forth – that on the Day of Revelation they derive from Him alike their sustenance and their delight: for what went before was but an expedient for the sake of that Revelation, and but a sign for the sake of attainment unto that Desired One.
There is no one who, whilst believing in the Bayan, writeth a single word thereof in the finest script but that it becometh incumbent in the sight of God for him to receive whatsoever is beloved unto him. The degrees of the scripts are those of the name “Vahid:” the first is the “Abha” script, and the last the “A’la,” while those which lie between them are according to the degrees of the recitation. Methinks even now I can discern that, in the Revelation, there shall be persons of discriminating talent who write in nineteen sweet styles of handwriting: yet the perfection in one of them is too eminent to admit of comparison; while the aspiration of all towards perfection is the very acme of perfection when once it is conjoined with the good pleasure of Him Who hath been from eternity the Best-Beloved of mankind, and from everlasting the Goal of their desire.
Otherwise, it is today observable that in Islam innumerable books have been written in the finest script; whereas those traces which affirm the Truth and negate the reverse – and if, when confronted with whose very first letter, all former Books confess not belief, their very essence shall not be accepted of them, how much less the beauty of their script – these traces have been left like unto a “disused well and lofty mansion;” and notwithstanding that their beauty, in the eyes of those endued with understanding, is comelier than the beauty denoted by the word “beauty,” it hath yet to be heard that copies of the Book Qayyumu’l-Asma’ have been transcribed to the number even of “Qayyum” – which is the number of the name of “Yusif,” peace be upon him – in the manner it deserveth. Yet, from the beginning of the Revelation until today, how many books have been transcribed! – not one of which, without belief therein, can be of profit.
At the time of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, all shall be shut out from Him in this manner as by a veil, save him whom God willeth. Do thou be perfectly vigilant lest, after His appearance, aught be written but the traces of that Sun of Truth, inasmuch as to write a single letter thereof is of greater consequence than to write the whole of the Bayan, and whatsoever hath been composed under its shadow. Consider thou the beginning of the Qur’an, when if, on the Day of the appearance of the Apostle of God, anyone were to write a single letter thereof, he would be adjudged a believer, provided that he believed therein; whereas if he were to write the whole of the Evangel, and whatsoever had been composed in the religion of Jesus – peace be upon him – under the shadow of the Evangel, it would avail him naught. This is the essence of knowledge, shouldst thou be able to apprehend it; and apprehend it thou shalt.
Be thou perspicacious, lest thou be shut out as by a veil: for naught in that Revelation is more beloved than that thou shouldst present unto Him His traces in the finest script: nay, it hath been enjoined upon all that whatsoever shineth forth from that Source of bounty should be in the possession of all the believers in the Bayan, forasmuch as that is the Bayan of that day: and let whoever is able, in the most exalted manner conceivable in the Bayan, produce a transcription of these traces, and present it unto that Sun of Truth, inasmuch as all have been, and are, held to account for this.
How goodly a craft is printing, for the sake of the exaltation of His words, and the diffusion of His traces, should one be able on the Day of Revelation to lend assistance to the religion of God in this manner! Whereas, if it be as today, each person shall, in the comfort of his own home, be shut out as by a veil. God chargeth no soul with aught unless he first be able to discharge it; put your whole trust and confidence in God: then, on the Day of Resurrection, believe with certainty in the Verses of God.


Gate Two of the Seventh Unity
On the motive of action, inasmuch as it behoveth everyone to engage in no action, unless he uttereth these words:

“Verily, I assuredly arise or sit for God, the Lord of the heavens and earth, the Lord of all that is seen and all that is unseen, the Lord of all worlds.”

And should he recite it in his heart, that would also be rewarded.
The substance of this gate is this, that no behaviour turneth into a real action, unless it is performed for the sake of God. It is for this reason that it is enjoined upon all actors to utter this word at the time of their action:

“Verily I do this for God. The Lord of the heavens and earth, the Lord of all that is seen and all that is unseen, the Lord of all worlds.”

Should he recite it in his heart, it would be rewarded as well.
However, no act will become for God, unless the actor recogniseth the Tree of Truth, inasmuch as the above verse is one verse amongst His verses, and be warned lest in the Day of Resurrection ye be veiled from Him by His verse that is manifested in your soul. Even as in the Dispensation of the Qur’an, he who acted for the sake of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, and that of His Letters of the Living, he hath acted for the sake of God. And it is not appropriate that anyone doeth anything for anyone, unless he doeth it for God, and it will not be for God, unless it is for the sake of the Revelation of that time.
Thus today all who act in conformity with the Gospel, act to attain the good pleasure of God by the command of Jesus, and although before the Day of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, such acts were for God, but at the very moment of the Revelation they turned into acts for one who is other than God. Nay, rather in that Revelation he must have acted for the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, inasmuch as it is only then that acting for God is realised.
In like manner, the people who are now acting in accordance with the Bayan, and recite this verse, should they, in the day of the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, act for Him, they would act for God, otherwise their actions would come to naught, as if they have not done anything. This is the case in regard to the root pillars of religion, discern thou thyself, the requirements of the acts related to the derivative branches thereof.
Likewise comprehend the appropriate modes of action pertaining to this world, which must turn into acts for God. For example, thou partakest of food, and thou desirest to do so for the sake of God, whereas thou art shut out as by a veil from the very Tree that pointeth unto God, not heeding the truth that this verse that is manifested in thy soul hath shone forth from that Tree, and thus it returneth unto Him in His next Revelation. There are even times, that thou barrest Him from that which thou doest in thy being for Him! Regard thou all other modes of thy deeds in the world. Thou claimest they are for God, whereas thou art veiled from Him.
Gaze in like manner, upon the modes of action in religion, till it reacheth the essence of the declarative word which testifieth unto divine unity. For in the Day of the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, shouldst thou act for Him, thou would act for God, whether it be the act of declaring “There is none other God but God,” or just drinking water. Otherwise, shouldst thou fail to act for Him Whom God shall make manifest, then by uttering “there is none other God but God” thou wouldst enter the fire, and by drinking water, thou wouldst drink of the non-paradise drink.
It is for this indivisible essential principle, that at the time of the Revelation of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, it was decreed that the followers of all other religions act for the one other than God, even though they all have believed in the past Book of God and His past Messenger, and even though today they continue to believe therein, as all can see. The secret of this mystery is this, that from the Day of Adam, the One Who was followed by the faithful was none other than the Apostle of God, and all the Revealed books naught but the very Qur’an that is sent down unto Him. This meaneth that in truth they have been veiled from the previous Revelation and His Book, inasmuch as they have failed to recognise that He is the same past Manifestation Who is manifested in the Next Revelation.
Likewise, at this time shouldst thou act for God in the Bayan, and refuse to make thy acts against the Letters of the Unity, and behold all dependent upon the Primal Letters, nay, rather, witness in Them naught but the manifestation of His Revelation, then thou wouldst be reckoned during the darksome Night as one who acteth for God. However, at the time of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, wert thou to perform thy deeds for the sake of the Point of the Bayan, they would be regarded as performed for one other than God, inasmuch as on that Day the Point of the Bayan is none other than Him Whom God shall make manifest. Likewise, His Letters of the Living are exactly His Letters of the Living, for Whom thou hast been acting. Then how is it that when They appear, thou failest to act for Them?
It is for this reason that at the beginning of every Dispensation a vast multitude, who fondly imagine that their deeds are for God, become drowned and ungodly, and perceive this not, except such as He guideth at His behest.
It is better for a man to guide a soul than to possess all that lies between East and West. Likewise better is guidance for him who is guided than all the things that exist on earth, for by reason of this guidance he will, after his death, gain admittance into Paradise, whereas by reason of the things of the world below, he will, after his death, receive his deserts. Hence God desireth that all men should be guided aright through the potency of the Words of Him Whom God shall make manifest. However, such as are conceited will not suffer themselves to be guided. They will be debarred from the Truth, some by reason of their learning, others on account of their glory and power, and still others due to reasons of their own, none of which shall be of any avail at the hour of death.
Take thou good heed that ye may all, under the leadership of Him Who is the Source of Divine Guidance, be enabled to direct thy steps aright upon the Bridge, which is sharper than the sword and finer than a hair, so that perchance the things which from the beginning of thy life till the end thou hast performed for the love of God, may not, all at once and unrealized by thyself, be turned to acts not acceptable in the sight of God. Verily God guideth whom He will into the path of absolute certitude.


Gate Three of the Seventh Unity: On this, that repaying debt is an obligation which should not be delayed
The substance of this gate is this, that extending loan to the faithful hath always been, and will continue to be, beloved before God. Likewise is the repayment of the loan, which is incumbent upon all. Indeed, should it be in one’s power to repay his debt, the act of repayment would be more beloved in the sight of God than any other thing, And delay therein is not permitted.
The fruit of this law is this, that the divine words of glorification, celebration of praise, sanctification, exaltation of unity, magnification, and all other parts of religion are tokens that are bestowed as a loan by the Supreme Truth unto His created beings. Therefore upon His Revelation, it is the duty of all to return them unto Him, from the lofty word of the declaration of divine unity till the last token of limitation. Were one to repay at once, upon the Revelation, his debt, naught would be reduced from him, unless he would behold better thereof in the universes and in souls.
How remote is a man who refuseth to repay the right of another! Then how much more it must be with regard to the right of God, when a servant come to believe in Him, and yet in the due Day of Return, despite his claim of faith, he would fail to recognise the Revealer of religion and the Bestower thereof! This is the contemptible condition of the creatures, couldst thou but behold it with the eyes of certitude. God judgeth in truth, and He verily is the best separator.


Gate Four of the Seventh Unity: Concerning consecration
The substance of this gate is that permission hath been granted for the servant each year to consecrate himself: the beginning whereof is at nightfall on the first eve of the Vahid, until, at sunset on the day of Vahid, it cometh to an end; nor hath there been, or is there, any scope therein for diminution or augmentation. The intention thereof is that one should take delight in but one of the Names of God; nor, if another Name occur to him, hath permission been granted for it; albeit if, through forgetfulness, he turn his attention to another Name, there is no harm in this: perchance, on the Day of Resurrection one may, through the blessing of this observance, be able to believe in Him Who is the embodiment of the Name “Vahid,” nor be veiled from accepting His guidance.
Methinks even now I can discern that the Tree of Truth – Who is the Source of all Names and Attributes – hath been made manifest: yet the dwellers on the sea of consecration are veiled by their own consecration (inasmuch as the object of this exercise is to attain unto Him: while such an one hath allowed this same exercise rather to shut Him out from Him as by a veil: even as the revelation of the Furqan, and the religion of Islam – the root whereof is the knowledge of God, which then diversifieth until the matter endeth in the last question of juridical branches – were sent down for the sake of the recognition of the Sun of Truth, at the time of His dawning: yet behold how each soul hath allowed himself to become veiled by one of these matters, even as thou observest in this day), and have been held back from recognizing the Desired One – Who is the fruit of all – yet advert not to their omission.
Howbeit, even at the time of their inadvertency the proof of God hath been, and is, complete before all: for were they to reflect a while, they would see that, by the selfsame proof in virtue of which they have come to be adjudged Muslims, it would be possible in all cases to accept the Truth.
As for the circumstance that, as thou beholdest, from the beginning of their lives until the end thereof, they observe the precepts of their faith, entertaining not a thought that they might be other than true believers – this is because they are not tested, and the Proof is not apparent in their midst: otherwise, that very soul who is so self-assured in his belief would repeat those same words which, at the beginning of Islam, were uttered concerning the appearance of the Sun of Truth: even as, on the attainment to maturity and perfection of that faith, when the Desired One was made manifest, the people uttered those same words about which they had asked wonderingly, “Is it possible that anyone could hearken unto the Verses of God, and yet express himself in such a fashion?
Thus it is that those who act on the basis of discerning insight in each matter are few; while most, since they are reared in this religion, declare themselves believers therein: yet God alone knoweth in which soul is true consecration, and in which soul true insight. God consecrateth those who believe in Him and His Verses so as to detach them from the mention of aught else but Him. He, verily, is the Almighty, the Inaccessible.


Gate Five of the Seventh Unity
concerning this, that on the Day of the appearance of the Tree, it shall not be permitted unto anyone to believe in the religion wherein he had believed ere His appearance: and should he hear thereof, let him come into His presence in order that He may charge him with what He willeth: and let him, ere coming into His presence, continue acting as he had been doing until then: howbeit, at the time when he cometh into His presence, all religion shall be cut off from him, save that which He charge him withal.
The substance of this gate is that that which is the cause of salvation is the knowledge of the Manifestation, while the same is true likewise in reverse; and the religion of the Lord, on the advent of each Revelation, consisteth in the commands which are promulgated on His behalf in that same Revelation.
Consider thou that, from the time of Adam until that of the Seal of the Prophets, had the believers in the preceding Revelation believed in that succeeding, they would have been adjudged believers; otherwise, whatsoever they had previously possessed would be reduced to naught. In like manner, on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, the whole of religion shall consist in the observance of His laws, inasmuch as the good pleasure of the Lord – exalted and glorified be He – cannot be made manifest save in virtue of His good pleasure: while after He hath been made manifest, to stand upon what was aforetime is a course that can yield no fruit.
Be thou scrupulous in the matter of thy religion: perchance on the Day of Resurrection thou mayest be able to obtain deliverance from the terror of that day: for this is a day whereon the Proof of the Lord shall be manifest before His people.
Make haste, therefore, at the very time of His appearance: neither before that, nor yet after this, if it be your desire to prosper.


Gate Six of the Seventh Unity
concerning the impermissibility of taking up the implements and tools of battle except at time of need, and on the occasion of a holy war, except in the case of those engaged in their manufacture.
The substance of this gate is that such implements as would cause one soul to be afeared of another are not beloved in the sight of God, save only on the day when permission is granted for them, or in the case of those servants who are occupied with their manufacture. Likewise, such attire as would inspire fear in another shall not enter into Paradise.
It is befitting that the servant should be watchful lest aught emanate from him that might inspire fear in another: haply, on the Day of Resurrection, all may appear in temples exemplifying humanity and the modes worthy of the human station: perchance the eye of the Sun of Truth may behold in naught that which would meet with His displeasure. For thou knowest not but that thou shalt be shut out as by a veil from Him Who is the essence of thine own existence: and how like it is that thou shouldst consent for Him to consort with others not of His own degree; even though there hath never been, nor ever shall be, a greater fire than His being thus shut out as by a veil.
Regard thou the Soul Whose utterance none is capable of understanding save them that are well grounded in knowledge, who are the Imams of Guidance: He hath become resident in a mountain whose inhabitants are unable to speak a single word of the language of Paradise – which is the Arabic tongue – how much less to understand it. Consider thou how it fareth with Him Who is the very essence of existence! I swear by the Sacred Essence of God that were a person properly to apprehend the matter, he would at once be dumbfounded by its enormity: and were all to learn thereof, this would in itself constitute the severest laying hold upon them by God: that for the Person in Whom in all respects they believe, and turn unto; and from Whom is the beginning of all, through His command, and unto Whom is the end of all, through His command – that things should fall out for Him in this fashion! – howbeit the believing souls can appraise the measure of this laying hold upon men upon the part of the True One: that for Him, to attain Whose presence all were created, things should fall out in such wise that He is now resident in a place not one of whose inhabitants is possessed of an understanding heart, that he might behold Him with His own eye, save only such as God willeth.
For this reason hath it been forbidden in the Bayan for anyone to consort with others than his like; while it behoveth all to respect the forms and usages that are evident amongst all: the divines amongst their kind; the rulers amongst their kind; the merchants amongst their kind; and the rest of the tradespeople within the limits of their respective kinds: so that no soul may see other than his own like: inasmuch as it is not befitting for the Sun of Truth to be perceived by any save those eyes which see naught else but God: how, then, would it be possible for the eyes of all creation to perceive Him?
Do ye exercise the utmost vigilance (for ye shall live to see the Day of Resurrection) lest aught should befall Him Who is the very essence of existence such as would be unworthy of mention in His Court. He Who heareth from the tongue of the inmost essences of All Things the refrain “Praised be God!” – whereby glory and sanctity are rendered unto the Lord – nay, aught else becometh in His Holy Court an aspect of Negation – how should such a person be deemed worthy to hearken unto any other than a loving word, or to set eyes upon any other than a glorious dwelling?
It is not that on that Day thou shalt not hear, or know, of His appearance: nay, conceive thou that Resurrection to be like unto this, when, although thou knewest not the reality of the matter, yet thou heardest tell of the outward aspect of events: how those who had disciplined themselves, and cast underfoot all that is on earth, arrived, through His grace, at the knowledge of who He was. Can such a Soul, forsooth, Who hath elicited such a response, be deemed worthy to dwell in a mountain such as this? This is as touching the outward aspect of affairs: for otherwise, wert thou to look at the reality of the matter, then night and day it is none other than He Who is mentioned by thee, in the most exalted chamber of thine heart: while all that thou doest, thou performest through Him, and for Him; and yet thou art veiled in this manner from recognizing Him.
Refrain ye then, for fear of God, your All-Merciful Lord, from aught whereby men’s souls may be sorrowed, O ye servants of God, all of you, without exception!


Gate Seven of the Seventh Unity
concerning this, that it behoveth whosoever liveth until the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest, to beseech Him, of His grace, to honour him – should He so wish it, and favour him withal – by gracing his residence with the dust of His sandals.
