The substance of this gate is that just as the inner essences of the whole of existence are, in comparison with the Sun of Existence, like unto a ghostly shadow in a mirror, so likewise regard thou the limitations of all things: and know that no soul, in the sight of God, and in the sight of those endowed with understanding, hath ever been, or ever shall be, more glorious than the Tree of Truth: wherefore, since He is made manifest in the guise of pure Lordship, and all – for that they behold not the reality – are unable to bow down before Him, it hath been commanded that on the Day of Resurrection – which is the Day of His appearance – all should beseech Him, of His grace, to bestow upon them what shall conduce to their own glory: perchance all may not be deprived of attaining the fruit of existence, which is to meet with Him: for save by this means, they have no way to realize this object.
It is not that thou shouldst see in this matter any form of a conjunction: for wert thou to obtain in this glorious manner as the fruit of thine existence all else but God – whatsoever had been created in the past, and whatsoever might be created in the future – assuredly it would not bear comparison with so much as the ninth of the ninth of the tenth of the tenth of a moment in His presence: inasmuch as the substance of all – in respect whereof they are entitled to the designation “thing” – is from Him: how then should it be possible to make mention of His mention as “conjoined” with the mention of aught else but Him? Regard thou this Secret of Reality as applying similarly to all matters, so that thou mayest not be shut out as by a veil from the Source of all good.
Notwithstanding that this Cause is more glorious than aught, yet were that embodiment of invincible power to be made manifest, who would be able to apprehend His glory? Nay, ye are unable even to apprehend the glory of those servants who, for the sake of arraying themselves in borrowed splendour, put on the robe of glory – how then should ye be able to apprehend the nature of such glory with respect to Him?
This is to the end that, should He appear in other than this guise, haply no soul may be shut out as by a veil from the fruit of his existence. God favoureth whomsoever He willeth among His servants; He, verily, is possessed of grace abounding.


Gate Eight of the Seventh Unity
concerning this, that it is incumbent upon each person to write out, from the beginning of one month to the beginning of another, a Vahid of Vahids of whatsoever he loveth of the Names of God, such as “Allah-u-Akbar” (“God is Most Great”), or “A’zam” (“Most Mighty”), or “Azhar” (“Most Manifest”), or the like thereof: and he hath been permitted to make calculation from the beginning of his life until the end thereof, and then to write out whatever had escaped him; and should the principal die, it behoveth his heirs to write out for him in this manner the equivalent of whatever had passed over him of his life.
The substance of this gate is that each soul hath been commanded each month to fill in a Vahid of Vahids, the calculation whereof is from the moment of his conception up to the time when he is caused to die: if the which escape him, it devolveth upon his heirs.
The fruit thereof is that haply, on the Day of the appearance of the Tree of Truth, one may multiply the believers in Him: for the inner essences of the hearts are sustained by God through these names: and so only one make mention of the source of a thing’s sustenance, this conduceth to its arriving little by little at the level of the body, whence it becometh a cause of his entering within the Vahid of the Resurrection.
In this present Dispensation, the fruit thereof is that perchance the First Vahid may be multiplied to the degree that the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them shall become filled therewith, to the end that on the Day of Revelation all may see in that Vahid naught but this Vahid, in a nobler guise, so that the foot of no one may slip upon the Sirat: for had this Vahid, at the time of Revelation, been seen to be the Vahid of the Qur’an, not one of the Muslims would have deviated from the Sirat.
The whole of this Vahid, in its multitudinous degrees, culminateth in the First Vahid. Do thou conceive the entire world as the Vahid of the Vahid, and set as the source of sustenance of each lower degree the degree above it, until, step by step, they arrive at a single Vahid – which is that same First Vahid whose members all are charged to recognize. Nor see thou in that Vahid aught but the innumerate Vahid, Who is the First Letter, so that thou mayest not see in the mirrors aught but the image of the Sun alone. This is the essence of the Unity of God, and the mystery of His Abstraction.
Methinks I see that the mystery of the Vahid shall exercise a pervasive influence, until it permeateth all things – whence even the number of pens in a pen-case would be the number Vahid: while among them the manifestation of the Point would have the value (Baha’) of them all: so that if someone were to apply this principle, yet not assign to the First Vahid the value (Baha’) of them all, he would not have recognized the First Vahid, nor, in its own particular station, rendered unto it its due. For example, if the value (Baha’) of the one pen be nineteen mithqals of silver, the value (Baha’) of the eighteen pens must be eighteen mithqals, while he should set the value (Baha’) of that one pen at the value (Baha’) of the whole Vahid, inasmuch as all are sustained thereby.
Thus it is that the resurrection of the one involveth the resurrection of all; the gathering up thereof involveth the gathering up of all; the presentation thereof before God involveth the presentation before God of all; and the requital thereof involveth the requital of all. Even as thou beholdest today in Islam: whatsoever there is, the sustenance thereof in spiritual matters is through the name of Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and of His manifestations, and the Gates of Guidance; while in worldly matters likewise all derive their sustenance from them.
Thus it is that all the multitudinous numbers subsist in virtue of this Vahid: while this Vahid subsisteth in virtue of the First Vahid, Who is innumerate: while He subsisteth by Himself, through God – exalted and glorified be He. After the rank of First Vahid, the rank of Vahid compriseth innumerable degrees, which none but God can reckon.
God createth whatsoever He willeth, and multiplieth the First Vahid howsoever He willeth, through His command; He, verily, is powerful over all things.


Gate Nine of the Seventh Unity
concerning this, that it is incumbent upon every king who is raised up in this religion to build for himself a house with ninety-five doors, and a house with ninety doors.
The substance of this gate is that it befitteth whatever king is raised up in the Bayan to build, and establish as his place of residence, two houses in the name of Him Whom God shall make manifest, the number of whose doors should not, in the first case, exceed ninety-five, and, in the second, ninety: so that, the Secret of Reality having permeated even to the level of the mineral, the tongue of the reality thereof – which is its outward form – should proclaim that “for God” is the “dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them:” perchance, on the Day of His appearance, his own testimony with respect to Him may not fall short of that of the clay, and he may not deny him the possession of that which is His.
For there is no doubt that death shall overtake all: and should such a king depart while in a state of belief, and engaged in lending triumphant assistance to Him, he shall leave behind him a goodly name, which shall live on until the Day of Resurrection (notwithstanding that one who, on the appearance of the Manifestation of Truth, hath acted according to his own religion, hath not been heard of till this day, or else such would have been cited): for otherwise, from the Day of Adam until the revelation of the Bayan, whatever kings there have been, in every people, have done whatever they have done in the name of the One made manifest in that people on the part of God: albeit hereafter, in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, let the dwellers of his age obtain the source of their own glory, so that until the Day of Resurrection their names may be mentioned favourably in the sight of God: otherwise, they shall depart, even as all, from Adam until this day, have taken their departure: nor hath anyone yet been found who, on the Day of Resurrection, is worthy to be cited as an example.
For otherwise every king, among his people, hath performed his works “for God” according to his own lights: but to what avail if, on the Day of the appearance of the Tree of Truth – among the leaves of the tree of Whose love are the Verses of God – he should remain shut out from recognizing Him as by a veil? – even as, in the age of the revelation of the Bayan, his detachment had reached the point that, conceiving the truth to be in the possession of a certain person, he committed unto him all his affairs; while the Person in Whose name all that are on earth, and he himself, do whatever they do, he hath, as is evident, made to dwell in the Mountain of Mah-Ku. The fruit of this law is that haply on the Day of the appearance of the Tree of Truth, the like of these houses shall have multiplied, so that perchance they may serve Him also for a dwelling.
It is not that when first the Manifestation appeareth His proof is not complete: nay, the proof which the Lord hath bestowed upon the Point of the Bayan is such as hath never till this day appeared at the hand of any that were before Him: to wit, that someone should write even in his own epistles the Verses of God, which being dispatched, His proof is, by a single Verse thereof, made perfect before those upon whom they are sent down; and to reveal responses for whomsoever He wisheth in the language of the Verses, on the part of God. For in the Revelation of the Furqan – which was the jewel of the preceding Revelations – none was addressed but the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him; nor did His Holiness send down upon anyone a single Verse in writing: nay, if He sent aught down, it was in the customary language of the Arabs of that age. Yet, notwithstanding the appearance of this kind of proof, and the completeness of the Divine bounty, behold thou what hath come to pass!
Yet this is that same utterance, in virtue of a single Verse whereof all the believers become occupied with some matter: which Verse, were all that are on earth to become so occupied, would be able to support them; nay, if the Resurrection were never to be set on foot, and all were to perform this matter interminably, would still be equal to the load. Howbeit, it descendeth upon hearts that are not regardful of the secret of existence, and the essence of the proof at the beginning of the Manifestation; and which advert not thereto, nor on the instant bow down before God: whereas this is that same utterance concerning which was revealed aforetime, “Were We to send down this Qur’an upon a mountain, thou wouldst see it humble itself, and cleave asunder, for fear of God;” whereafter reference was sent down to those who hear the Verses, yet bow not down: as is stated in the noble Verse: “And if they hear the Verses of God, they bow not down.”
This notwithstanding, they entertain not a thought that they might be other than believers: whereas their hearts are judged not in the sight of God to be in the same case even as a mountain what time it humbleth itself: not to mention that there is no doubt that the Verses sent down in the Latter Revelation are greater than those sent down in the Former to an extent for which, by which, from which, to which, there is no limit.
If all the believers in the Bayan, when hearkening unto a single Verse, bow down and say “Yea” – nor the thought of “Nay” so much as enter into their heart – they shall be worthy to call themselves believers therein: for the same is a Verse which proclaimeth “Am I not your Lord” unto all, and all works are for the sake of His good pleasure. That is the time of the garnering of the fruit and the testing of the truthful.
I swear by the Lord Who hath been, and is, single and alone, and hath no partner, that were there someone in the East who in the tablet of his memory was able to summon before his eyes the whole of the Bayan, and who had arrived at the highest level of virtue and piety possible in the world of being: and were the epistle of that Sun of Truth to descend upon him, in the mode of Verses, such as to demonstrate unto him his incapacity, in his own estimation, then, should he tarry for so much as the twinkling of an eye, within himself, and not confess alike with his heart and his tongue,

“This is from God, no doubt is there about it: we, all, verily, believe with certainty in God and His Verses,”

he would not be adjudged in the sight of God to be possessed of so much as a grain of mustard seed of belief; nor would the Bayan which he had memorized, and whose provisions he was putting into effect, confer upon him the merest barley seed of profit; neither would he have had within him any innate disposition to confess the Unity of God, forasmuch as he recognized not the utterance of his Best-Beloved.
For had his heart been a mountain, it must needs have cleft asunder for fear of God: whereas this predicament applieth to a degree precedent upon His own, which is that of the Qur’an: how then must stand the case with His own Verses? – nay, in the eyes of the Revealer thereof such a soul would assuredly be regarded as yet remoter than a mountain, albeit in his own estimation he saw none to equal him for piety, inasmuch as he had “memorized the Bayan:” whereas it is not to be imagined that anyone should be found who was capable of committing to memory the whole of the Bayan, or of abiding by its every precept: nay, the above example hath been cited merely by way of an impossible conjecture, so that all people may know their own limit at the time of His appearance, nor put themselves in a yet harder predicament than a mountain.
In their own conceit it is as though, whenever they hear the mention of their Best-Beloved, an ocean of tenderness surgeth within them: yet in a case where one must needs submit, and when the affirmative nature of his own essence – as one who respondeth to the Call – is brought into being, he becometh “as though he had heard naught.”
O people of the Bayan! Be watchful of yourselves, for there is no escape for any of you on the Day of Resurrection. He shall arise suddenly, and pass sentence upon whatsoever He willeth: He shall, if He so wish it, make the most abased of creatures the most exalted, and the most exalted of creatures the most abased: even as He hath done so in the Bayan, shouldst thou advert unto the matter. Nor, apart from Him, hath anyone the power to accomplish such a feat. Whatsoever He enacteth, the same shall come to pass: it is not that it shall not come to pass. For example, the moment that the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – wished to appoint as His Vicegerent the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him – this appointment – notwithstanding all the people could do to oppose it – was established.
Now too, whatsoever He wisheth to command shall inevitably be established: for this is that same Command whereby the religion preceding His was established, and whereby that succeeding His also shall be established. None but God hath ever been, or ever shall be, possessed of the real command: and all shall abide by His command, provided that they act according thereto: otherwise the case is not amenable to judgment. God exalteth whomsoever He willeth among His servants; He, verily, is powerful over all things.


Gate Ten of the Seventh Unity
Do ye protect each soul with a temple of the Name of “Mustaghath” at the time of his birth; nor doth it behove anyone to omit this.
The substance of this gate is that among the Names of God the number of no Name is equal to that of the Name of “Mustaghath,” which is the highest fruit among the Names, having arrived at the final limit of manifestation. Naught is manifest therein but the First Vahid; nor, in the First Vahid, is there aught beside the First Vahid: Who in the Qur’an is the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and in the Bayan the Possessor of the Seven Letters; while prior to the Qur’an He was Jesus – peace be upon Him – and subsequent to the Bayan He Whom God shall make manifest. The thrones in the Revelations appear in different guises: for otherwise the One that is stablished upon the thrones – Who is stripped of the bounds of limitations – is none other but the Primal Will, Which the thrones can never alter.
Considering that no Name hath a higher numerical value than the Name of “Mustaghath,” at the level of the Names: and shouldst thou cast the numbers, Vahid after Vahid, upon the number of “Allahumma,” the number of the Name “Ahad” would fall short: while shouldst thou compute the value of the Name “Mustaghath” with the addition of “Alif” and “Lam,” the number of the Name “Hayy” would come out in excess; and whereas on the Day of Resurrection the embodiment thereof shall have been made manifest, Who guideth unto God: for this reason hath it been commanded that from the moment of conception, each temple should be protected with a temple containing the number of the Name of “Mustaghath:” for from the beginning of the Revelation until the Revelation following, God alone knoweth how much time shall elapse; yet, if God willeth, it shall not exceed the number of “Mustaghath.”
In the Dispensation of the Qur’an, the beginning and the return thereof were within the Name of “Aghfar,” less the number of the Name “Huva.” In the Bayan, God alone knoweth to what limit this period shall extend: inasmuch as there is no standard in this (for the interval betwixt the Evangel and the Furqan reached not even to a thousand): for the Tree of Truth is under all conditions watchful of His creatures: and whensoever He perceiveth a preparedness for the Revelation in the mirrors of the hearts of those who extol His glory, He maketh Himself known unto all, by the leave of God – exalted and glorified be He: inasmuch as He hath never had, nor ever shall have, any motion or stillness of His own, save only through God – exalted and glorified be He.
The fruit thereof is that since all the Names are circling around the Name of God, and the perfection of all Names consisteth in arrival at this Name, perchance all the souls in the Bayan may arrive at whatsoever is possible of attainment, so that, at the time of the appearance of the Manifestation of Truth, they may be able to recognize the Sun of Truth, and to circle around Him. Let them be watchful lest they transgress beyond this number: for should anyone arrive at this number in the Bayan, and hear that the Tree of Truth hath been made manifest, it behoveth him to return unto Him, even though he may not be certain of the matter: perchance he may obtain deliverance from the Fire, through this bounty: nor hath there ever been, or ever shall be, a greater bounty in the Bayan than this, should they appreciate its value, and save themselves from the fire of Him Whom God shall make manifest, and dwell beneath the shadow of His light.
Inasmuch as His appearance is the beginning of the creation of all beings in the Primordial Gathering of the Hearts, after the completion of the Primordial Gathering of the Bodies, ere His appearance: and so only two thousand and one Names be written in a temple, it is sufficient to afford protection: haply by this means one may not remain shut out as by a veil from recognizing the One Who is manifest in the Names; and see none but God, nor witness aught save in the good pleasure of His Best-Beloved.
Do ye then shield yourselves with the protection of being for God, your Lord, and thereafter with that of His Goodly Names, every one of them: for His, verily, are the creation and the Command in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them. No God is there but Him, the Almighty, the Best-Beloved.


Gate Eleven of the Seventh Unity: Concerning the impermissibility of mounting pulpits, and the command to be seated upon chairs
The substance of this gate is that it hath been forbidden to mount pulpits, and commanded to be seated upon thrones, or upon a couch or chair, so that none may depart from the bounds of dignity. In a meeting-place, where an assembly is gathered, let a chair be placed upon a dais, in order that all those present may be able to hear the words of the True One.
The fruit thereof is that perchance on the Day of the appearance of the True One, one may, when acquiring knowledge, have the honour to do so from that Source of knowledge. How very great is this matter! – inasmuch as His knowledge is none other but His own Self: and, apart from them that are well grounded in knowledge – who are the Imams of Guidance – none else are able to understand His utterance: how then could all elect to acquire their knowledge in this manner? Nay whatsoever knowledge is entitled to the designation “thing” hath been created for the sake of understanding His utterance; while that which is with Him is naught but the jewel of existence.
This very utterance that thou beholdest is innovated at its own level, by its own self: for otherwise the station of His essence is too glorious to be spoken of as conjoined with letters. No greater delight hath been created in the world of being than that one should hearken unto His Verses, and understand their intention; nor ask why or wherefore with respect to His Words; neither compare them with the utterance of anyone but Him. Just as His Being is the Manifestation of Godhead and Lordship before All Things, so too His Utterance is the Manifestation of Godhead and Lordship before all utterances: whence if it were a human being endowed with utterance, it would assuredly proclaim “Verily, I am God, no God is there but Me; and, verily, all else besides Me are My creation: wherefore, all ye letters, Me alone do ye fear!” – as indeed, with the tongue of its essence, it doth proclaim what He proclaimed, and all things hear it: for were this not the case, how, on the advent of each new Revelation, could it be incumbent upon all the Heavenly Books aforetime to believe therein, even as it is incumbent upon the souls who believe in those Books to believe in the new Manifestation?
Thus it is that, through one single Verse, His proof is made complete before all that are on earth, to each who is endowed with utterance in his own tongue: whence if there were today one of the people of Adam, one single Verse would be presented unto him – even as it is presented unto the first to believe in the Bayan – and he would be informed that all that are on earth were powerless to produce its like: if, then, upon the instant he proclaimed it to be true, he would have proclaimed the truth of God, inasmuch as there is none more truthful in His word than He; whereas if – God forbid – he hesitated, and made not certain that this was the utterance of the Lord, it would behove him to present it unto all that are on earth: and so soon as he observed the incapacity of all – the which he doth in fact observe – he must needs return, and proclaim the truthfulness of the Lord in respect of His word; while from the time of hearkening thereto until he arriveth at a state of conviction, he is in the fire of his own unperceiving state.
As for the circumstance that all exclaim “O Thou Who art the most truthful of the truthful!” – if at the time of Revelation they confess the truth of the Tree of Truth, and, at the time of reciting His Verses, hesitate not to pronounce them true, then shall they have uttered “O Thou Who art the most truthful of the truthful!”; otherwise, their deed shall have belied their utterance: inasmuch as this name is but a name among His Names, and a light among His Lights, which guideth unto Him in respect of truthfulness (how, then, could it be possible for His essence to be characterized by such a description?): for whatsoever truthfulness might be conceived of in the world of being is truthful only in virtue of His truthfulness: while He, at the top of His voice, is calling unto the whole of creation: “Ye all exclaim ‘O Thou Who art the most truthful of the truthful!’ – why then do ye hesitate to pronounce the truth of that which is being sent down?” Thus it is that the whole world is of a sudden marked out by the Pen of God with a circle as of no account, save him whom God willeth to exempt, while all remain oblivious of their plight.
Should they claim “We have not heard the Verses” – yet heard them they have. And should they claim “Those servants who are truthful have become so otherwise than through following the Qur’an” – this is assuredly not the case. And should they claim “This Verse is not a Verse of God, and all are not powerless to produce its like” – where then is the one who hath shown himself able to do so, by way of innate ability? – whereas these Verses, like unto an ocean, are being sent down from that Ocean of Bounty.
Thus it is that that, all through believing in Him, and accepting His words as true, become “truthful:” yet deny Him that name which He Himself hath bestowed upon one of the manifestations of His Cause, in exemplification of the truthfulness of His own Self: for had they not done so, no Manifestation, at the time of His appearance, would have been charged with falsehood. Thus it is that all, in virtue of His Name, are “truthful:” yet deny this designation to its true Bearer, without perceiving what they do. To illustrate this matter: should someone pronounce the sun in the mirror to be “true” in its radiance, at its own level, yet say not the same of the sun in heaven, how veiled would he be! – as also in the case of the monks at the time of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – who were in this same predicament: inasmuch as the people pronounced them “truthful” in virtue of their following the religion of Jesus – peace be upon Him: yet said not the same of the Sun of Truth – around Whose seal all religions circle – wishing rather to condition their acceptance of the truth of the sun in heaven upon that of its ghostly shadow in the mirror – assuming this latter to have been “true:” whereas, were the mere thought to occur to any such that the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – might be other than true, the spectral likeness of the sun within them would at that very moment be removed.
Regard thou such to be the case likewise in the Revelation of the Bayan; and likewise in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, be thou scrupulous not to condition thy recognition of Him upon that of the people of the Bayan (for to do so would be to act in the manner illustrated): but rather to recognize Him by His own Self. This is the meaning of the saying “Know ye God through God:” and do thou apply this same standard in all subsidiary cases: thus: “Recognize ye God through God;” “Love ye God through God;” “Obey ye God through God;” and “Follow ye God through God:” and behold thou in the same wise all Names and Likenesses on that Day. Observe thou how delicate is the matter! – for if, at the time of the appearance of the Tree of the Bayan, all that were on earth had been believers in the Qur’an; yet, on encountering the first of His Verses, all had not recognized Him as true: assuredly all would have become in the sight of God untruthful, while He alone would have been truthful.
Observe thou how subtle is the matter! Today thou wishest to condition thy recognition of Him on that of persons, the beginning of whose knowledge is the ability to understand the words of those servants who have believed in Him. Thus it is that thou hast not recognized thy Best-Beloved, but hast travelled rather in the Night. Otherwise, shouldst thou recognize the entire world, if He say “Nay,” then thou too wouldst say “Nay;” and if He say “Yea,” then thou too wouldst say “Yea:” inasmuch as that which thou hadst formerly understood to be true became so in virtue of following His word. Thus it is that on the advent of each Revelation, the people of that Revelation allow those learned therein to shut them out as by a veil: heedless the while that behind the matter, through a single utterance on His part of “Nay,” all these become untruthful.
Be thou watchful of the appearance of the True One, lest on the Day of His appearance thou shouldst condition thine acceptance of His truth upon that of the people of the Bayan: for all their acclamations shall be rendered, through a single utterance on His part of “Yea,” unqualified approval, and through a single utterance on His part of “Nay,” the reverse. Consider thou in the Qur’an that if the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – had uttered a single word attesting the truth of a certain group of people, all today would assuredly attest their truth, in virtue of the attestation of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and in the reverse case attest the reverse, irrespective of whether or not the people in question were actually truthful: for the criterion is the testimony of the True One, not the testimony of the people; and His approval, not that of the people.
For example, all those unto whom the promise had been given of Ahmad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – when they confessed not the truth of the Apostle of God, became, through His word, untruthful: whereas in their own age there is no doubt that among them were those who were truthful, who deviated not from the religion of Jesus – peace be upon Him; notwithstanding that, in the sight of God, they were not truthful: for had they been truthful, they would have believed in the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him.
Regard thou such to be the case likewise on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, when all shall be untruthful save only those servants who accept His truth, whether the one in question be the most exalted of the dwellers on earth, or whether the reverse: inasmuch as the acceptance of the True One is through His word, and all become truthful through following it. There is no doubt that on the advent of each Revelation, the Lord testeth His creatures by means of that whereby their own religion had been established, and whereby any one of them had sought to draw nigh unto the Lord. God guideth whomsoever He willeth unto a path of certain truth.


Gate Twelve of the Seventh Unity: Concerning this, that it behoveth no one who performeth his works for God to associate aught with Him in his worship
The substance of this gate is that, whereas on each appearance of the Manifestation of Truth, anyone who performeth his actions for Him performeth them for God; while anyone who performeth his actions for God performeth them for Him: on the Day of Resurrection – which Resurrection is none other but His appearance, and the appearance of His Letters of the Living, and all the believers in Him – no one hath been granted permission, should he perform any work for Him, to lay hold upon His practice in any matter, ranging from a priceless pearl at one extreme to the merest atom at the other: inasmuch as his very existence hath been created for Him – with how much greater reason, then, must this be the case with whatsoever is subordinate to His existence? Notwithstanding, He hath ever been, and ever shall be, more glorious than this: and indeed there is no mention in the Furqan or the Bayan of the “practice” of the Manifestation of Truth – yet such is the limit of the people, and the fruit of their existence on the Day of the Return.
Otherwise, there is no doubt that on the Day of Resurrection no one recognizeth the Tree of Truth, ere He reveal Himself, so as to be able to put this matter into effect; while after His Revelation differences arise to a degree that it would still not be practicable to obey such a command, save in the case of those who recognize Him for who He is: unless, in His Revelation, all should so progress that no differences would occur over the question whether He was to be accounted a believer or nay: at which time the fruit of the Bayan would be fully realized in their regard. Yet even then, how many different ways might it be possible to enumerate in which – with respect to only a few areas of comportment – the actions of a single person could be emulated!
This is for no other purpose than that all should know their proper station: for otherwise, He is a Reality Who hath in His kingdom thousands upon thousands of manifestations of wealth and self-sufficiency: howbeit, since a whiff of other than Divine Unity wafteth in these actions, for this reason have they been forbidden.
God bestoweth His grace upon whomsoever He willeth among His servants; He, verily, is the All-Encompassing, the All-Knowing.


Gate Thirteen of the Seventh Unity
concerning this, that God hath enjoined upon all His servants to acquire from Him Whom God shall make manifest during the days of His manifestation nineteen Verses in His own script.
The substance of this gate is that naught hath ever been, or ever will be, of greater moment in the eyes of the Lord than His Verses: should the which be conjoined with the script of the Tree of Truth, in respect of Whom the Name of God is mentioned (for as thou sayest the “Verses of God,” in His case too thou sayest the “Manifestation of God”), then are they more precious, in the sight of God, and in the sight of those endowed with understanding, than any precious thing: whence it hath been enjoined upon all the people of the Bayan to acquire a single page thereof – comprising nineteen Verses – in His own script.
No recompense on the Day of Resurrection can be compared therewith: for were a person to possess the whole earth, and to renounce it for the sake of obtaining such a Tablet, the value (Baha’) thereof would still be greater, in the sight of God, and in the sight of those endowed with understanding, than that which he had expended: for this is a charter of deliverance from God unto that soul; whereas if – God forbid – he be other than a believer, it is his charter of the Fire until the following Resurrection: even as whatever, in this Revelation, came to the believers was the highest fruit of their existence, upon which they pride themselves in Paradise; whereas aught that came down upon other than the believers is a proof from God unto the one concerned, whereby he is caused to dwell eternally in the Fire, unless God will it otherwise: and such is the case whether this document be composed in His own script, or whether it comprise His traces.
Were it possible in that Revelation for This to become other than That, assuredly the Former would have been the preserver of all the Latter’s traces, in the finest script beyond which none finer could be conceived of in the world of being: yet, since such is not possible, others shall obtain this bounty. Should a person write a single Verse of His, it would be better for him than to write the whole of the Bayan, and all the books that had been composed in the Bayan: inasmuch as all these shall be lifted up, while that shall remain until the following Revelation. If in that Revelation anyone should write a single Word of that Revelation while believing therein, his reward for doing so would be greater than that he should write all the traces of the previous Reality, and whatsoever had been composed beneath their shadow. In the light of such an understanding do thou ascend from Revelation unto Revelation, knowing that there shall be no end to thine ascent, in the knowledge of God, even as there was no beginning to this process.
Methinks I see that the Epistles of that Sun of Truth shall be sent down upon the believers in Him, who shall receive the bearer thereof with greater honour than that wherewith a lover would receive his loved one, and shall stand up for him – these are the pillars of religion and the witnesses of certitude!: far otherwise than what thou observest from the believers in the Qur’an in this Revelation, who, though they stand up in the presence of the Qur’an, have remained shut out as by a veil from the Tree of Truth, Who is the Revealer thereof, as indeed is customary among other than the Shi’ihs to behave in just this fashion. Yea, this action is intended to pay honour to the Book, to the end that the honour of its Revealer should be exalted.
The essence of knowledge in the eyes of those apprised thereof is evident: to wit, that should anyone attain the Revelation – whereof these are but the subsidiary aspects – he shall attain thereby unto all good: even as, at the beginning of Islam, had anyone written the Surih of Tawhid from the Book of God, this would have been better for him than to write the Evangel, and all the books that had been composed beneath its shadow. Apply thou this same principle from the time of Revelation up to the appearance of the Point of Truth: perchance thou mayest not be shut out as by a veil from the Desired One. Do ye then acquire the finest thing that God hath created, should God allow this: then yield Him thanks.
And know thou that this law is but a token of the exaltation of His bounty: for otherwise, no one is entitled in his own right to His bestowal. All are charged to beseech His bounty; while He is charged only with whatsoever may be the good pleasure of God’s Will. He bestoweth His bounty upon whomsoever He willeth, and withholdeth it from whomsoever He willeth: howbeit God bestoweth it upon all people without exception, so only they believe with certainty in God and in His Verses.


Gate Fourteen of the Seventh Unity
concerning the impermissibility of seeking forgiveness except from God, in the Manifestation of His own Self, at the time of His appearance: otherwise, do ye seek forgiveness of God privately within yourselves.
The substance of this gate is that permission hath not been granted for anyone to seek forgiveness from another during the Night; while on the Day of Resurrection it is permitted to seek forgiveness from Him Whom God shall make manifest, or from whomsoever He may designate: otherwise, forgiveness must under all conditions be sought from God, betwixt oneself and Him: for indeed were a servant to beseech forgiveness of God by whatsoever means are possible in the world of being, still it would be no more than what was justly due from him, in view of the just deserving of his own inner essence – how much more of those matters which are subordinate thereto.
It is not that thou shouldst seek forgiveness even while being shut out as by a veil from the One from Whom thou art seeking forgiveness from Him: for seeking forgiveness from God cannot be realized save through seeking forgiveness from the Manifestation of His Cause, Who is the Tree of Truth; and likewise from His Letters of the Living on the Day of His appearance: for otherwise, wert thou to beseech forgiveness to the number of “All Things,” it would avail thee naught: as indeed thou dost so night and day, whilst oppressing the very Person, to seek forgiveness from Whom is to seek forgiveness from the Lord: for in this world of being the people have no way unto God save through the Gates of the Vahid, which culminate in the innumerate Vahid, Who is the One Who bringeth into being all the illimitable numbers aforetime and hereafter.
In like manner, among the Letters of the Vahid, it is not befitting that the Letter “Sin” should seek forgiveness but from the “Ba’;” nor likewise that the “Mim” should seek forgiveness but from the “Sin;” and so on, Letter by Letter, until the First Vahid is complete, whereafter it would be impossible to estimate the extent of its proliferation: for which reason, the command to seek forgiveness in such a manner is cut off, nor cometh back into operation save on the appearance of the Resurrection.
Howbeit, whichever soul seeketh forgiveness betwixt himself and God; nor transgresseth the bounds fixed in the Bayan, the Lord shall accept his plea for forgiveness: up to the time of the Revelation, when no plea for forgiveness shall be accepted unless addressed unto the One made manifest in the Revelation. Conceive thou such to be the case likewise with respect to all acts and conditions: and appreciate the greatness of the Day of Revelation, around which all circleth; and beseech forgiveness of God at every moment, and before each moment, and after each moment.
Gate Fifteen of the Seventh Vahid,
concerning the obligation to bow down at the gate of a city wherein riseth the Divine Point, as a mark of honour thereto on the part of God: He, verily, is the Almighty, the Best-Beloved.
The substance of this gate is that since all souls, having been created out of the shadow of the Verses of Godhead and Lordship, are travelling ever in a course of exaltation and sublimity, but because they have not a seeing eye, that they should recognize their Best-Beloved, are shut out as by a veil from submitting themselves unto Him (notwithstanding that from the beginning of their lives until the end thereof they had, in respect of His former laws, been bowing down in their religion before God, and worshipping Him; and submitting themselves unto that Reality; and humbling themselves before that Essence: yet because, at whatsoever time He appeareth, all look to themselves, they remain shut out as by a veil from Him: for they behold Him to be in the form of a human temple like unto themselves – whereas glorified be God above any such conjunction!: inasmuch as the likeness of His Temple is that of the sun in heaven, the rays whereof are His Verses; while the likeness of all the believers – provided that they believe – is that of a mirror wherein the image of the sun becometh apparent, and whose brightness is in corresponding measure): for this reason hath it been commanded that all should prostrate themselves at the gate of the city from which He ariseth; and so too with respect to that land which becometh the place of His appearance: whence, for example, taking the place of arising to be the city of “Fa’,” and the place of appearance the well-known citadel, it is incumbent upon all souls, at the moment of entering into that city, and into that land, to prostrate themselves.
Howbeit, at the time of Revelation, the former command is cut off; while matters are on that day decreed by leave of the One made manifest in that Revelation. Although there is naught but it deriveth whatsoever it owneth and oweth from the Tree of Truth, yet, on the appearance of each new Manifestation, its obedience unto Him in His Former Revelation is made apparent – not at the time of the Revelation. For example, on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, the submissiveness of the people unto Him in the Point of the Bayan shall be made apparent: inasmuch as the beginning of the Revelation is the stage of seed of the Revelation (although the seminal state of the Latter Revelation is more powerful than the mature state of the Former, yet since all are unable to appraise the matter, it is accordingly expressed in this fashion).
Otherwise, wheresoever thou lookest, there is no soul that is not in some way obedient unto his Creator: which obedience is none other than his submission unto the Tree of Truth, even though, having been shut out as by a veil from Him, his obedience become in the Latter Revelation the image of disobedience. For example, all those who performed their works in the Evangel were submissive through the word of Jesus – peace be upon Him – unto the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – in His Former Manifestation: which Former Manifestation, in comparison with the Latter, is unworthy of acceptance; and in like manner, all those today who, in the Qur’an, perform their works for God, are, in all that they do, submissive and lowly unto the Point of the Bayan: howbeit, since they recognize not the Sun of Truth, it is for this reason that they have remained shut out as by a veil from belief in Him.
It is not that He wisheth all to become believers in Him: rather, the salvation of all consisteth in belief in Him, while He in Himself is independent of believing in aught besides Himself: even as, if all had believed in the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – they would but have secured their own salvation; for otherwise that Tree, by Himself, hath ever been, and ever shall be, in Paradise.
O people of the Bayan! Should ye believe in Him Whom God shall make manifest, to your own behoof shall ye do so: for otherwise, He hath ever been, and ever shall be, independent of all things. For example, if an illimitable number of mirrors were to be placed before the sun, they would not the less reflect its image, and tell of its appearance: whereas the sun in itself is independent of the very existence of the mirrors, and of the image of the sun that is imprinted upon their surface. Such is the limit of the world of being in comparison with the revelation of the Ancient of Days.
Be a little watchful of yourselves, that ye make your beings, your selves, your very entities, as mirrors in the love of the Unity: perchance on the Day of the appearance of the Manifestation of Truth, the image of the First Unity may become imprinted upon their surface: and neither the Second Unity – nor any of the infinite succession of Unitys – may shut thee therefrom out as by a veil: for such an outcome is the Signal Bounty and Sublime Attainment, shouldst thou appreciate its value; otherwise shall ye have rendered vain the fruits of your own existence, even by your own hands.
Today each year seventy thousand souls go on pilgrimage to the House of God, which observance was instituted by the command of the Apostle of God: yet the Author of this command – that is, His Holiness – was for seven years secluded in the Mountain of Mecca: notwithstanding that the Author of the command is more powerful than the command itself. Thus it is that all these people who now go on pilgrimage act not on the basis of discerning insight: for were this not the case, they would, when He returned in His Latter Manifestation – which is more powerful than His Former Manifestation – have been graciously favoured with obedience unto His Command; whereas thou beholdest how things have fallen out: how, in virtue of His former Command, they are adjudged believers in His faith, and night and day bow down unto God through Him; yet hath His dwelling-place been established in a mountain: notwithstanding that the boast of all is on their belief in Him: even as thou beholdest that today all pride themselves on believing in Him in His Former Manifestation; while in His Latter Manifestation – when adherence to the former faith is adjudged to be for other than God – they have allowed this very adherence on their part to shut them out as by a veil from Him: even as the belief of the believers in the Evangel was adjudged, at the time of the appearance of the Apostle of God, to be other than belief. In like manner, on the advent of each new Revelation, regard thou such to be the case with the preceding Revelation.
Know thou that on the advent of each new Manifestation, the ways of His own Former Manifestations, in an infinite procession before Him, derive precisely from Himself: so that, for example, in the case of that Revelation wherein the Manifestation thereof appeared in the guise of a tailor, in this Revelation the essence thereof is made apparent, even though by a single degree: and regard thou all such instances to be in a similar case: nor allow thyself to be shut out as by a veil, in order that thou mayest attain the fruit of thine own existence, and exist for ever in the Paradise of His bounty. This is a token of God’s grace unto you: haply ye may bow down before Him.
It is not that, as is today the custom, ye should bow down at a distance of two farsakhs from Najaf – or perform the same obeisance at sea, where this is possible at many farsakhs’ distance – so as to pay your respects unto His Sanctified Dome (whereas there was no command in this respect in the religion of Islam) – but that, at the time of Revelation, one should all at once not bow down before Him: should ye forbear the which proceeding – nor any wrong befall Him – He shall rest contented.
Thus it is that on the Day of Revelation all are tested: and should they employ their reason, and accept the truth of the Manifestation of God in the light of their own understanding, all shall obtain salvation: yet since they do not so, the proof is made complete before them, while they themselves persist in their veiled condition. God guideth whomsoever He willeth unto a path of certain truth.


Gate Sixteen of the Seventh Unity
concerning this, that God hath enjoined upon every king who is raised up in the religion of the Bayan not to leave anyone upon his territory who hath not believed in this religion; enjoining in such wise also upon all people without exception, save in the case of those who, like the Letters of the Evangel, are engaged in a general trade from which all people stand to benefit.
The substance of this gate is that it hath been, and is, established on the part of God that no potentate should leave in his territory any but believers in the Bayan; or, on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, any but believers in Him. The fruit thereof is that on the Day of Resurrection the Tree of Truth may not behold in the land wherein He is made manifest other than believers in Himself: and that in the earth of Paradise there should be no fiery soul. To bring forth the people of the Bayan out of the bounds of Paradise hath been, and is, contrary to the good pleasure of God.
Be ye watchful that, in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, things fall not out for the believers in Him as they have in this present Revelation: when for the Letters of the Living – notwithstanding that one and all, in virtue of their former traces, made show of their own knowledge; and although the very root of their religion was established in virtue of their love for them – they accepted not that which they accepted for others. Observe thou in what a veiled condition all are raised up, and, by contrast, with what penetrating vision the Letters of the Living are endowed!
Be thou watchful that things fall not out for any soul in such a fashion, for naught hath been made the subject of a more binding interdiction: perchance on the Day of Resurrection, through following this law, thou mayest obtain deliverance: nor occasion any sadness unto those Letters of the Vahid through whom thou hast established the very root of thy religion. For thou recognizest them not: yet even at the time when thou recognizest them not, they have with them the unmistakable signs of who they are, that thou mayest make certain of their truth: for shouldst thou be possessed of an understanding heart, then merely by hearing the Verses uttered from their lips, thou wouldst know that it is the beginning of the gathering together of the Resurrection; and that these from whom thou hearest the Verses are the Letters of the Name “Vahid” – or other than they – who are communicating the Cause of God unto all.
Exemption hath been granted unto the Letters of the Book of Alif (Evangel), or unto any community like these from whom the believers stand to benefit through trading with them: whereupon such commerce hath been permitted; otherwise hath it been made subject to a most binding interdiction: perchance on the Day of Resurrection the Tree of Truth may behold not in the land of belief other than believers in Himself. If in the dominion of a believing monarch there be one such soul, then to that degree is he in the Fire: save only in the case of the one unto whom permission hath been granted, if he be engaged in a general trade; for otherwise such hath been, and is, forbidden: especially if it be under undignified circumstances, in which case permission is absolutely refused. Lay not then aside the fear of God in respect of this ordinance; then fear Me!
It hath not been, nor is it, lawful for anyone to be in the company of such a soul: inasmuch as such a one is not adjudged to be a believer: whereas the prerequisite of sitting with another is purity of faith, not other than this. Fear ye then God with all due reverence, O people, all of you without exception!


Gate Seventeen of the Seventh Unity
concerning the recitation on Friday of the following Verse before the Sun:

“The Glory of God (Baha’u’llah) be upon thy beauteous countenance, O thou rising sun! Bear thou witness, then, unto that which God hath testified of His own Self, ‘There is no God but Him, the Almighty, the Best-Beloved’.”

Know thou that the Lord of the world hath created Friday for the sake of purity and refinement, and of the servant’s repose from whatever toils he had been bearing throughout the preceding six days of the week. Any work performed on the eve or day of Friday shall be rewarded with a whole week’s recompense.
Considering that the spirit of each thing attacheth to man, and that the testimony of each thing is accordingly that of man himself, for this reason hath it been commanded that on Friday, the believers, standing opposite the sun, should call upon it to recite, by way of testimony, a Verse importing its confession of the Unity of God, and its belief in the Point of the Bayan, and in whatsoever hath been sent down therein: perchance, on the Day of Resurrection, one may speak in such a fashion before the Sun of Truth, and testify to the Unity of the Lord in His presence, and to the truth of whosoever followeth Him: the which is the fruit of this law, should anyone be able to attain it.
Otherwise there is no doubt that after the appearance of the command, everyone shall repeat this Verse each Friday: howbeit, on the Day of Resurrection he shall be blotted out if he utter it not before God: and it is incumbent upon all to recite this same Word on the Day of Revelation before Him Whom God shall make manifest – upon each Friday, whoever happeneth to be in His presence, until such time as He granteth leave for whatsoever may be His own good pleasure in that Revelation.
He doeth what He willeth and ordaineth what He pleaseth; He is not to be asked of His doings, while all else are to be questioned concerning all things.


Gate Eighteen of the Seventh Unity
concerning this, that should anyone deliberately cause sadness to another, it behoveth him to make payment of nineteen mithqals of gold, if he be able, or else of silver: otherwise, let him beseech forgiveness of God nineteen times: unless he beg pardon, and be pardoned, whereupon he shall be liable to naught; and should anyone confine another, he shall be forbidden that which had previously been lawful unto him, for so long as he persisteth in this course; all his works shall be frustrated; and he shall not be numbered among the believers: and should he revert unto that which is forbidden unto him, it behoveth him each month to make payment of nineteen mithqals of gold: while any child that is conceived during such a period is not deemed to be within the Bayan.
The substance of this gate is that the Lord of the world, out of the abundance of His grace and bounty, hath forbidden that any of His servants should cause sadness to another, for the sake of that same Tree of Truth, that perchance no sorrow may befall Him during the day of His concealment, when none recognizeth Him. Should anyone transgress the bounds (hudud) which God hath fixed, the penalty of “hadd” shall be pronounced upon him: should he transgress which, the sentence of belief shall not be applicable in his regard; howbeit he is excused in case he be pardoned, whereupon the hadd shall be lifted from him.
A fine hath been ordained of gold or silver to the number Vahid, should he remain shut out as by a veil from observance of the bound (hadd) fixed by God; which if he be unable to pay, let him beseech forgiveness from the Lord of the world to the number Vahid, and beg pardon of the one unto whom he hath occasioned sadness. For the heart of the believer is the place of the revelation of God: which if sorrow visit, it would be as though it had visited the Letters of the Living; while if sorrow visit the Letters of the Living, it would be as though it had visited the Tree of Truth; while if it visit Him, it would be as though it had visited the Lord – exalted and glorified be He.
It is for this reason that no act of piety in the Bayan is nearer unto God than bringing joy into the hearts of the believers; nor likewise is any action more remote from godliness than causing sorrow to befall them: and this is doubly true in the case of the possessors of circles, whether in respect of joy or sorrow. Man must under all conditions be watchful that, if he bring not joy unto another, at least he cast not another into sorrow.
Should anyone, to the least degree that can be mentioned, subject another to restraint, he shall be liable to the penalties (hudud) of God: inasmuch as no action hath been comparable thereto in the eyes of the Lord, nor is it now, in respect of the extremity of its remoteness from Him: nor hath the perpetrator of such an action been, or is he now, accounted a believer; and should anyone draw nigh thereunto, those with whom he enjoyeth marital union shall become unlawful unto him: and, for so long as he continueth to detain that person, not one of his marital consorts shall be judged lawful unto him: while all his works shall be frustrated, even should he be acting at the most exalted level of godliness and piety; and should he revert unto that which hath been forbidden him, he shall be liable – pursuant to the penalties (hudud) of God – each month to make payment of the number Vahid in gold: and if a manifestation of life be subsequently conceived, it shall not be judged to have been conceived in the Bayan.
At all events, be ye watchful that night and day ye bow not down before God, at the very time that ye are subjecting another person to restraint: which if ye do, all your works shall be brought to naught, even while ye yourselves remain oblivious of your plight. Fear ye then God with all due reverence, whence haply ye may prosper.
The fruit thereof is that the people of the Bayan should be trained in this manner, so that haply, on the Day of the appearance of the Manifestation of Truth, they may cause no sorrow to befall Him, nor comport themselves towards Him according as is their present custom. Inasmuch as the servant, from the beginning of his life until the end thereof, is adjudged a believer in His Faith, and performeth his works for the sake of meeting Him: yet it may chance that He appeareth, and such a soul occasioneth Him sorrow, or subjecteth Him to restraint: notwithstanding that to outward appearance he is the most exalted of mankind, and more plentifully provided with the means of guidance than anyone on earth: and that he is caused to yield up his soul without ever knowing of the Revelation: whereas night and day he had, in his yearning for Him, been immersed in sorrow, and ardently entreating that His advent might be hastened.
Had those invested with authority aforetime changed their practice after hearing of the episode of Musa Bin Ja’far – peace be upon them both – perchance the Tree of Truth also, on the Day of His appearance, would not – since there was no prevailing custom of subjecting others to such treatment – have suffered a similar fate. Yet how many edifices have they reared, each monarch during his own reign – from which, however, he derived not the slightest benefit on the Day of Resurrection: whereas had he adopted an innovation of this sort, perchance it would have availed to spare someone the need of experiencing sorrow. These same matters which may appear exceedingly trivial become in their own station greater than all that is on earth, and the expenditure of the same: albeit there is no doubt that those invested with authority in the Bayan shall take measures to prevent such instances of sorrow as befell the Tree: perchance on the Day of the appearance of the True One, no such instances shall befall on His return.
Yet fear ye the return itself, inasmuch as ye are all deluded by the spectral likeness of your own beings: howbeit, shouldst thou make it a rule not to cause sorrow to another, perchance thou mayest but have drawn a veil over thine own self, and veiled it from believing in the Lord; yet if – God forbid – any sorrow should befall the Tree of Truth, it would be a matter of greater consequence than the sorrow of All Things that could be mentioned in the world of being; and so likewise with respect to other matters, ranging from a priceless pearl at one extreme to the merest atom at the other: for all things acquire through Him their capacity even to be termed a “thing” – while He is too glorious to be conjoined to any thing.
The same principle holdeth true also of the Letters of the Living, the nearest taking precedence over the nearer; then, after the First Vahid, of the Second Vahid; and so on until the end that hath no end: inasmuch as one of the numbers of the Vahid cometh hindmost, becoming foremost in the Second Vahid. For example, if the lowliest of people on the Day of Revelation believe in the True One, he shall become more exalted than the exalted one who hath not believed in Him. Thus it is that in each Revelation the exalted becometh abased, and the abased becometh exalted; and conversely, the exalted becometh yet more exalted, and the abased yet more abased, should he confess not the truth of the True One. God aideth whomsoever He willeth among His servants to accept His Cause; He, verily, hath knowledge of All Things.


Gate Nineteen of the Seventh Unity: Concerning prayer
The substance of this gate is that the first prayer to be laid down was the noonday prayer: while the whole thereof was fixed at the number Vahid, so that each rak’ah might be a gate of Paradise in obedience to the True One, wherein one might see none but the one manifest in that letter, nor in the whole see aught but the innumerate Vahid: to the end that it might be a sign of submission and lowliness upon the necks of all, for the sake of Him Whom God shall make manifest: so that should someone outwardly disdain to render Him obedience, yet in his inner essence he is still worshipping God through Him.
No act, after the recognition of God, hath been, or is, superior to prayer; while the prayer of each person is according to the limit of his own existence: for example, the prayer of the Point in relation to the prayers of the Living (Hayy) is in the same case as the Point in relation to the Letters of the Living (Hayy): and so likewise the prayers of the Living (Hayy) in relation to the Letters of the Second Vahid: and so likewise the prayers of the Second in relation to the Letters of the Third: and so on, until the matter endeth with the last person in existence. Thus, for example, the Tree of Truth, ere He reveal Himself, performeth the Daily Prayer; while the last person in existence likewise performeth – according to these outward forms – the Daily Prayer: yet the prayers of all people, in comparison with a single rak’ah of the prayers of His Letters of the Living, are as naught: what then must be their predicament when brought into comparison with Him? Regard thou such to be the case likewise with respect to all actions.
A single utterance by Him Whom God shall make manifest of the Word “There is no God but God” cannot be conjoined with the utterance by All Things of the confession of the Unity of God, whether aforetime or hereafter, whether secretly or openly: inasmuch as the confession He uttereth is that which God hath testified of His own Self; while whatsoever confessions are uttered by others – to wit, by the Letters of the Living, and all the numbers proliferating from the First Vahid – are uttered through Him.
Shouldst thou be unable to conceive the matter in this case, consider how it standeth with the Point of the Furqan. The prayer of anyone other than the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – from the noblest of men, who was the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him – down to the last person in existence – was created through His command: how then could it bear comparison with His prayer? Thus it is that each thing moveth about itself; nor can it exceed the compass of its own beginning. Howbeit, within the prayer created through His command, the prayers of All Things cannot bear comparison with a single rak’ah of the prayer of the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him; and the same principle holdeth true likewise of all degrees, the nearest taking precedence over the nearer, until the matter endeth with the First Vahid.
The value (Baha’) of all is comprised within His prayer: even as, wert thou to abstract the value (Baha’) of a diversifying proliferation of objects, until it arrived at a single jewel, this would comprise the rest – in respect of value (Baha’), that is, not of inmost essence. By the same token, the prayer of the Commander of the Faithful compriseth all prayer, in respect of value (Baha’), not of reality; and regard thou such to be the case likewise in respect of all matters.
That same prayer at which, when first it was laid down, the Arabs clapped their hands – see only how much discussion now taketh place amongst the learned merely over the place where it should be performed!: to the degree that with respect to a single question in this area, concerning the branches of the law, the accomplished of the divines have composed a thousand verses. Yet allow not these matters to shut thee out as by a veil from the Source. Even as today all the believers in the Qur’an night and day perform seventeen obligatory rak’ahs of prayer, performing in each rak’ah two obligatory prostrations unto God: yet remain the while shut out as by a veil from the very Shaper of the self of prayer, inflicting upon Him that which they inflict: notwithstanding that on the day when the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – laid down the Daily Prayer, it was intended but as a cord of submission and lowliness that should be upon the people’s necks against the Day of His return.
Yet, considering that worship is not acceptable unless conjoined with the confession of the Unity of God, at the level of worship, hear only what befell Him!: all, at the level of worship, are directing themselves, through Him, unto God, while He Himself they have deprived even of the outward forms of prayer; notwithstanding that whosoever of those who night and day are occupied with prayer turned not unto God, a sentence of other than truth was revealed in his regard – what then must be the case with his prayers, which are but one among numerous subsidiary aspects of his faith?
Know thou that upon the advent of each new Revelation, the Twin Confessions – which form the beginning of religion – are renewed: whence for example, if, on the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – anyone had said “There is no God but God, and Jesus – peace be upon Him – is the Spirit of God,” he would not have been adjudged a Muslim: save only if had said “There is no God but God,” conjoining this with “Muhammad is the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him.” In like manner, on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, the words “There is no God but God” shall be accepted when conjoined with a testimony unto Him: which attestations are the same identical “There is no God but God” and testimony unto the Point of the Bayan. Howbeit, on that Day they shall not be accepted save when framed in the terms of that Revelation; even as, in the Revelation of the Furqan, they were not accepted unless converted into the Arabic tongue, and into an acknowledgement of the Prophethood of Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him.
Considering that such is the predicament even of the essence of religion, how then must stand the case with that which is merely subordinate thereto? Today thou beholdest how each soul, through preoccupation with a particular observance, hath remained shut out as by a veil from the One Who is the very Shaper of the self thereof: whereas had all but fixed their gaze upon the essence of the proof, and the beginning of existence, then assuredly, swifter than the twinkling of an eye, they would have passed over the Sirat, nor allowed preoccupation with these matters to shut them out as by a veil from Him.
Neither indeed, after the setting of the Sun, allow these matters to shut thee out from Him as by a veil: for wert thou to deviate in this respect by so much as a barley seed, the witnesses of the Bayan would decree the abasement of thy faith: but cast thy gaze too ever upon the Source, in relation to Whom all these other matters are but as a ring upon thine hand, which thou turnest in whatsoever manner thou wishest.
Yea, a person can be considered to have prayed in proper fashion what time he believeth with certainty in the Letters of the Vahid; perceiveth glory to reside in the Command of God, not in the thing itself; becometh not shut out as by a veil by looking at that thing, and contesting ‘Were it not worthy the honour, never would it have been made the subject of His command;’ and, when offering prayer, purposeth it to be for God, single and alone – bearing in mind this point, that should the Day of Resurrection befall, he would be submissive before but one of the Letters of the First Vahid: under such circumstances can he be deemed to have prayed in proper fashion, should he be tested – and approve his truthfulness – on the Day of Resurrection; otherwise, during the Night, his prayer shall be accepted of him so only he view it in this light.
It behoveth the worshipper, at the time of prayer, to see none but the Adored One; nor to look but towards the Lord, single and alone, Who hath no partner: for should he, when worshipping, bring before his gaze a Name or Attribute, he would be shut out as by a veil from the Object of his devotion; nor would his worship be accepted. It behoveth him to direct himself unto the Most Sacred Essence of God, Who hath ever been, and ever shall be, characterized by the assertion “He begetteth not; nor is He begotten;” and apart from Whom All Things else are His creation; while He, in His inmost reality, cannot be recognized; nor, in the sanctified glory of His being, is it in the power of words to describe Him. Naught is entitled to worship and adoration but His Essence.
Yet in all these matters, be watchful lest ye depart from the Gates of Guidance, inasmuch as in each rak’ah one of the Gates of Paradise is opened: by which is meant the knowledge of the Letters of the Vahid on the Day of their appearance. This Paradise is too glorious to contain within it outward forms. Nay, that Paradise which containeth within it outward forms – such as silken garments and golden vessels; fresh meat and pure beverage; maidens like unto lustrous rubies; and such descriptions as have been furnished – the custodians thereof are other than that Vahid, yet derive nevertheless their sustenance from that same First Vahid. It is not, however, that thou shouldst allow them to shut thee out as by veil from recognizing that First Vahid: for in that Court there is naught but pure love and revelation – conditions which have not as yet attained the stage of outward, gem-like forms, but whose appearance, whensoever this occurreth, shall be in virtue of the sustenance of that Vahid, and of naught else.
For example, if today, in a holy resting-place, forty thousand crystal lanterns be illumined – which is a type of the purity of Paradise – bethink thee that the warrant for this is that Tradition according to which it is was asserted aforetime that there is no extravagance in respect of lanterns. Thus it is that the custodians of these finite matters are all sustained by that First Vahid even though, at the beginning of Islam, there was in His habitation but a single lighted lamp. Regard thou such to be the case likewise with all the Revelations: perchance on the Day of Resurrection thou mayest not remain shut out as by a veil from recognizing the First Vahid: nay, even though He be provided with the means of illumination (notwithstanding that to speak fitly, whatsoever in the way of lamps is possible in the world of being – fitting would it be for them to be illumined in His presence) – yet the custodians of all these outward forms are from the proliferation of the Vahid – each in his own particular station – not the First Vahid as such.
Look thou upon the outward aspect of the world, and reason accordingly with respect to works. Conceive thou all people as a proliferation of Vahids, which mount up, Vahid after Vahid, until they culminate in the First Vahid, Who is the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and His Letters of the Living: and observe thou how – at whatsoever level of the proliferation that Vahid may be situated – all subsisteth through Him. In like manner, the prayers of all people exceed not their proper bounds: all prayers, in themselves, bow down before the prayers of the Letters of the Living; all the prayers of the Letters of the Living, in themselves, bow down before the prayer of the Point; while His prayer boweth down before the Lord, single and alone.
I have taken the instance of prayer as an example, in order that thou mayest regard the human realities to be in a similar case: for works are in identically the same case as the realities of those who perform them. Although the prayer of the last person in existence is identically similar to the prayer of the First Person in existence, yet, just as the reality of the last person in existence cannot be mentioned in comparison with that of the First Person in existence, save only at his own level – which is that of the furthest limit of existence – regard thou such to be the case also with all works.
In the first three rak’ahs at the beginning of the prayer, confess thou the unity of the Essence; in the following four rak’ahs confess thou the unity of the Attributes; in the following six rak’ahs confess thou the unity of the Actions; and in the following six rak’ahs confess thou the unity of worship: nor, in all of them see aught but God, single and alone, Who hath no partner. Regard thou likewise the whole proliferation of the Vahid to be even as the First Vahid: whence if someone at the furthest limit of existence should engage in worship; or prior to this confess the Unity of God in respect of the unity of His Action; or prior to this confess the Unity of God in respect of the unity of His Attributes; or prior to this confess the Unity of God in respect of the unity of His Essence – none of these acts of worship are aught but what hath shone forth refulgent in the First Vahid.
Nor see thou any source of creation save God; nor any source of sustenance save God; nor any source of death save God: inasmuch as in all the mirrors there is naught refulgent but one single Sun: and that is the Reality of the Primal Will, Which, in Itself, guideth unto God. Whatsoever all do – each in his respective mirror – they do through It: while Its own works It performeth through God – exalted and glorified be He.
Shouldst thou view matters in this light, thou wouldst perceive with the eye of certainty that the very substance of all things – in respect of which they are entitled to the designation “thing” – existeth in virtue of the Will made manifest in the world. It is not that the essence of the Will is made manifest in its very essence: nay rather, in each Revelation whatsoever is at that time possible in the realm of being, is made manifest in virtue of Its appearance. This is the meaning of “Are ye the sowers thereof, or are We the sowers?” In citing this Verse, I have taken as an example but the lowliest instance, in order that thou mayest thyself infer how the case standeth with the most exalted.
Do thou behold all these matters as plainly as thou beholdest the palm of thine own hand; nor pass them off as merely theoretical considerations: perchance on the Day of Resurrection thou shalt be able to garner the fruit; for otherwise, millions upon millions of doctors have written thousands upon thousands of books on theology: yet, had they considered Whose praise they were writing; and where it was tending; and from whence it had shone forth; and under the shade of which Manifestation it would come to rest – assuredly it would have availed them on the Day of Resurrection. Thus it is that on the Day of Resurrection, all speculative sciences – if they become visible reality – shall bear fruit; otherwise shall they remain imaginations in the heart of their exponent.
Turn thou not in worship but towards the Invisible and Eternal Essence, Who alone is entitled to be adored and worshipped. Only on condition, however, that thy turning unto Him be conjoined with an acknowledgement on thy part of that to which the Letters of the Vahid adhere – in respect of His knowledge and good pleasure – shall it gain admittance into the City of Divine Unity, without thy seeing another than God. Should anyone, at the time of worship, fix his gaze upon a particular Name, he shall not have worshipped God, and shall have remained shut out as by a veil from recognizing His purpose – exalted and glorified be He. Nay, all Names guide but unto the truth that there is no God but Him, nor any object of adoration besides Himself. Whatsoever is endowed with substance – to the degree of meriting the designation “thing” – is His creation; while He – not His creation – is entitled to be worshipped and adored.
Worhship thou God in such wise that if thy worship lead thee to the fire, no alteration in thine adoration would be produced, and so likewise if thy recompense should be paradise. Thus and thus alone should be the worship which befitteth the one True God. Shouldst thou worship Him because of fear, this would be unseemly in the sanctified Court of His presence, and could not be regarded as an act by thee dedicated to the Oneness of His Being. Or if thy gaze should be on paradise, and thou shouldst worship Him while cherishing such a hope, thou wouldst make God’s creation a partner with Him, notwithstanding the fact that paradise is desired by men.
Fire and paradise both bow down and prostrate themselves before God. That which is worthy of His Essence is to worship Him for His sake, without fear of fire, or hope of paradise.
Although when true worship is offered, the worshipper is delivered from the fire, and entereth the paradise of God’s good-pleasure, yet such should not be the motive of his act. However, God’s favour and grace ever flow in accordance with the exigencies of His inscrutable wisdom.
