The substance of this gate is that since the confession of the Unity of God attaineth in the letter “Dhal” the utmost limit of its ascension (the secret whereof is that if the term “Allahumma” [“O my God”] pass seven times over the letters of the third degree of the confession of the Unity of God [“There is no God but God”], the fifth degree will become apparent [“There is no God but Him in Whom …”]) – permission hath accordingly been granted for one to recite, if he be able, each day and night seven hundred Verses of the Bayan; or, if he be unable, to repeat seven hundred times “Allah-u-Azhar” (“God is Most Manifest”). The fruit thereof is that should the Day of Judgment arrive, he would believe in Him Whom God shall make manifest, so that his inner being might become worthy to guide unto the letter “Dhal,” and to be numbered with that number, should he fall without the bounds of numbers, and see naught but the innumerate Vahid.
It is not that this is any easy matter. Yea, it is easier than aught, shouldst thou but believe: yet since that is a mighty Day, it is exceeding hard for thee to be able to make one of the believers (inasmuch as the believers on that day are the denizens of Paradise; whilst other than the believers are the denizens of the Fire: and be thou certain that Paradise is the recognition of Him Whom God shall make manifest, and obedience unto Him; while the Fire is the very existence of him who bowed not down before Him, and the enjoyment of his good pleasure): for on that Day thou imaginest that thou art among the denizens of Paradise, and a believer in Him; yet art thou shut out as by a veil, and in the root of the Fire hast thine abode, whilst thou thyself art heedless of thy plight.
Conceive thou His appearance to be as that of the Point of the Furqan: how many the Letters of the Evangel who awaited His advent! – yet for five years after His appearance the denizens of Paradise numbered none but the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him – and whoever in that day believed in his Holiness in secret: and all were denizens of the Fire, imagining the while that they were denizens of Paradise.
Regard thou such to be the case likewise in the present Revelation: until today, He hath, through the dispositions of Divine providence, bestirred the very gems of creation to go in quest of the Truth, until three hundred and thirteen people – accounted the “nobles” of their age – were gathered in the Land of Sad, which is to outward appearance the greatest of lands, and in every corner of whose madrasihs there are innumerable servants who are famed alike for their learning and for their endeavour: yet when the time came for the gathering of these gems, it was the wheat-sifter thereof who donned the robe of “nobility.” This is the mystery of the reported utterance of the members of the Holy Family – peace be upon them – concerning the Revelation: “The most abased among the people shall become the most exalted among the people, and the most exalted among the people shall become the most abased among the people.”
Behold thou likewise the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest: persons to whom the very idea of incurring the displeasure of God never entereth their hearts, and whom all look to as models upon which to fashion their own behaviour, in respect of piety – who knoweth but that they may become the root of the Fire, if they believe not in Him; whereas those servants whom no one so much as suspecteth to be possessed of consequence – who knoweth but that, through attaining the honour of belief in Him, they may don the robe of Vicegerency at the hands of Him Who is the Source of Bounty: inasmuch as through His word is created whatsoever is created in religion, ranging from the loftiest expressions of existence on the one hand down to the furthest limits thereof on the other. In the Revelation of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – for example, his Viceregents were by His word constituted such. Behold thou the enormity of the matter! He Who hath it in his gift to bestow the bounty of the robe of Vicegerency – His creatures refuse Him even the name “believer,” which is valid of the very lowliest among His creatures.
I swear by the Sacred Eternal Essence! Were all the people of the Bayan to believe in that Sun of Truth even as the First to believe in Him shall do so, assuredly He would array each one in the robe of His own Name, so that in his inner being naught would be seen but Him: and should his name be “’Azim” (“Mighty”), He would make it “A’zam” (“Most Mighty”); relate it unto His own Self; and send down in an Epistle, “God, no God is there but Him, the Most Mighty, the Most Mighty.” Behold thou the enormity of the matter! He, the ocean of Whose bounty is such as to bring forth absolute non-existence from the arena of extinction into the sacred court of immortality, so that in the inmost essence of its heart naught may be seen but His own Name (if in that which is manifested in its will naught be seen but the Will of Him that manifested it) – He, the Fountain-Head of eternal grace and everlasting beneficence, Whose bounty is even such as this, pleaseth nevertheless that whomsoever He willeth should don the robe of extinction, if He seeth that, whilst worshipping Him, he is yet shut out from Him as by a veil, inasmuch as He is veiled from recognizing the Vehicle of His Revelation.
The Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – for example, beheld that all the believers in the Evangel were worshipping God, and believing in that which He had sent down; yet when He saw that they were shut out as by a veil from His own Self – to be shut out from which is to be shut out from the Lord – for this reason He adjudged them to be for other than God. Regard thou such to be the case likewise with the Point of the Bayan; and such likewise in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest: for were all on that Day to have regard for the beginning of the proof, and the essence of reality, there would remain not one of the people of the Bayan who did not confess His truth: even as, in the Revelation of the Point of the Furqan, had all been persuaded of the truth of the Qur’an aforetime, assuredly there would have remained not one of them who, on hearkening to the Verses of God, had not – swifter than the twinkling of an eye – passed over the Sirat.
It is not, O people of the Bayan, that ye would oblige Him by believing in Him: nay, should ye believe not in Him, ye would but condemn yourselves to become for other than God. Rather, do ye make it your endeavour to believe in Him, so that ye may become for God, and be converted from fire into light; for otherwise He is rich enough to dispense with all besides Himself. Even as today, should all that are on earth believe in the Bayan, to their own behoof would they obtain deliverance from the Fire, and enter into Paradise: obtain deliverance from the designation “For other than God” (which is more grievous than any fire), and enter into the Paradise of “For God” (which is mightier than any Paradise): and obtain deliverance from the designation “Kaf,” and enter beneath the shadow of belief; for otherwise the Point of Truth hath ever been, and ever shall be, rich enough to dispense with All Things; while all have been poor enough still to be in need of Him, in virtue of the mere existence of their own essence: so that if, on the Day of the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – all that are on earth had believed in Him, to their own behoof would they have obtained deliverance from the Fire; yet now that they have not done so, to their own detriment have they been caused to dwell eternally therein.
In each Revelation, do ye make it your endeavour to deliver yourselves from the fire of the preceding Revelation; for otherwise, the One made manifest in the Revelation is completely independent of all else besides Himself. Naught is there which, in its own inner essence, doth not bow down before God – exalted and glorified be He – even though the thing itself be wrapped in veils, and, on the Day of His Revelation, become not a believer: for were the veil to be lifted from its eyes, it would indeed be counted a believer in His Cause, even as it is a believer in His own previous Revelation.
O people of the Bayan! Repeat not the actions of the people of the Qur’an, who bowed down before God, yet inflicted upon His Manifestation that which they ought never to have inflicted. Thus it is that all works are rendered of a sudden for other than God, while their author remaineth oblivious to his plight: even as all peoples have remained wrapped in similar veils. It is fitting, on the advent of each Revelation, that all should believe therein, inasmuch as all subsist in virtue of that Revelation.
Recite ye then the Bayan in a sorrowful accent throughout the watches of the night and the hours of the day: perchance ye may be stirred with a rapture born of the Name of God; then moved with sorrow for the sake of them who are His Names.


Gate Fifteen of the Eighth Unity
concerning this, that it behoveth everyone to marry, so as to leave behind him one who shall confess the Unity of God, his Lord, and he must needs strive to accomplish this; and should there appear from either party that which would preclude them therefrom, it is permitted unto each, with the consent of the other, to bring about the appearance of such fruit; nor is marriage permitted with one who entereth not within the fold of the religion; and should one be already conjoined in wedlock with another, it is incumbent upon him to separate, if he witness from his consort other than belief in the Bayan; nor is aught lawful unto him or unto her before returning within the fold of the Bayan; howbeit, ere the Cause of God be exalted in the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest, such unions are permitted unto the believing men and women, that haply they may return unto God.
The substance of this gate is that in this world, the greatest fruit which the Lord – after belief in Him, the Letters of the Vahid, and whatsoever He hath sent down in the Bayan –hath bestowed, is to garner a fruit from one’s existence, so that, after his death, the one whom he hath left behind him may remember him with kindness. This, in the Bayan, hath been made the subject of a most binding injunction: to the degree even that permission hath been granted, if some obstacle to the fulfilment of this purpose be witnessed from either party, for the one, with the permission of the other, to choose another consort, in order that a fruit may be forthcoming from his existence: perchance it may become a leaf of Paradise, should it believe in Him Whom God shall make manifest; for otherwise, it shall become a leaf of the Fire, such that it would have been better for it never to have been brought into being, while its non-existence would be better than its existence.
Marriage is not permitted save with one who, in each Revelation, hath believed in the One made manifest in that Revelation. Should only one of the married couple choose to become a believer, marital union is not permitted the believer; while the rights of the non-believing party are forfeit. For the Possessor of All Things is the Lord – exalted and glorified be He – and He hath not granted permission for non-believers to be possessed of aught. Whatsoever thou beholdest in the hands of other than believers is without right: whence were this “right” to be an earthly potentate, it would deprive them of their very breaths – if they believed not – with how much greater reason of their property.
Ere the exaltation of the Word of God, however, which is the beginning of the Revelation, permission hath been granted for such unions, so that the believing souls may be protected. Howbeit, at the time of exaltation no such permission hath been granted: nay, a leaf of Paradise cannot become the consort of a leaf of the Fire, inasmuch as the inner essence of the one deriveth sustenance from Negation, while the inner essence of the other deriveth sustenance from Affirmation: the one is pure non-existence, while the other is pure existence, through the command of God.
It befitteth all the souls who shine effulgent in the Bayan to garner for themselves a fruit from their existence, so that the degrees of the numbers may proliferate, until they enter into the sea of infinity: for at the beginning of each Revelation the numbers are finite: then, stage by stage, they multiply, culminating finally in an endless proliferation. Consider thou how it was one thousand two hundred and seventy years ago, when Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – together with the Commander of the Faithful, were the sole believers in the Qur’an: whereas now, if thou lookest, canst thou estimate their number? Thus it is that the “Alif” progresseth to an illimitable extent: nor hath there ever been, or is there, any limit to its ascent.
Regard thou likewise the beginning of the Revelation of the Bayan. For forty days, none but the Letter “Sin” believed in the “Ba’:” then, little by little, the temples of the letters of the “Basmalah” donned the robe of belief, until the First Vahid was complete: and thereafter, behold how greatly this Vahid hath proliferated until today! I swear by the Sacred Eternal Essence, that if, at the beginning of the Revelation, the means thereof had become apparent, there would today be none on earth who were not believers: inasmuch as Reality is the Fire of God, should all enter beneath Whose shadow they would, in the Fire of His Love, render glory, thanks, unity and grandeur unto God, without aught being either taken away from His Dominion, or added thereunto. For unto God belongeth all that is in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them, whether it appear that the Manifestation of Reality, to appearance, make this apparent, or whether all, in His Name, make it apparent. Stage by stage, thou shalt behold the evolution of this process, until, from the limited to the unlimited, and from the finite to the infinite, thou shalt witness the creation of the wondrous Paradise.
Put then your whole trust and confidence in God; then be patient in His days.


Gate Sixteen of the Eighth Unity
concerning this, that it hath been prescribed unto each person, of all that he acquireth worth one hundred mithqals of gold, of the value (Baha’) of all things, to make payment of nineteen mithqals, and to keep one mithqal for God: let him, should the Sun be risen, remit these unto Him, that He may divide them among the Letters of the Vahid, for each one (Vahid) a mithqal, if He so wish – otherwise, the matter is in His hand; He is not to be asked of His doings, while they are to be asked of theirs: and should the Sun be veiled, and the Letters of the Vahid have offspring, let him render these unto them: otherwise, let them be expended on marriages between the believers, even if the servant expend them on the marriage of his own son or daughter: and let the Mithqal of the Fire be preserved for Him Whom God shall make manifest, or expended on the Bayan, whence one may himself recite it, preserving it as he would his very eyes, so that it may be restored unto its Owner.
The substance of this gate is that once the value (Baha’) of aught hath reached one hundred mithqals of gold, it behoveth the possessor thereof, if the Tree of Truth be manifest, to render, obediently to the Lord’s command, nineteen mithqals unto the Letters of the Vahid, and to keep one mithqal for the Fire: while if the Night be risen, all may deliver them unto the offspring of these Letters: should the which be absent, they may conjoin therewith the believers in wedlock, preserving the Mithqal of the Fire, that it may be returned unto Him Whom God shall make manifest. On His appearance, the rulings relative to conjoining in wedlock, and bestowing upon the offspring, are cut off, except by His leave.
The fruit thereof is that if, on that Day, He should issue some command, it behoveth all to obey it with the same degree of obedience as they are accustomed to show forth on that day. Consider how today the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – is obeyed in His every command: the obedience owed to the Tree of Truth in every Revelation is in this same wise: nay, in the eyes of those who recognize Him, this duty of obedience is yet more compelling on the Day of Revelation than amidst the veils of Night, inasmuch as that is the Day of the meeting with God, which no one shall again be able to attain until the following Resurrection.
It is fitting, after each prayer, for the servant to beseech the Lord’s mercy and forgiveness for his parents: which if he do, a call shall reach him from the presence of God “For thee are two thousand and one-fold the like of that which thou hast entreated for thy parents.” Blessed is he who remembereth his parents in virtue of the remembrance of his Lord. Verily, there is no God but Him, the Almighty, the Best-Beloved.


Gate Seventeen of the Eighth Unity
concerning this, that if silver and gold attain, by the measure wherewith ye weigh them, six thousand and five mithqals, five and ninety mithqals are for the Point: God shall take these of you, and all shall be asked thereof: and ye shall return them unto Him Whom God shall make manifest, and preserve them as ye would your very eyes.
The substance of this gate is that since there is no glory save in obedience unto the Lord (even as, in each Revelation, that upon which the believers therein boast themselves, one over the other, is obedience unto the Lord, not other matters: inasmuch as other matters – notwithstanding that they are not such as can be judged “true” – have ever been, and are, in the possession of the followers of every Revelation: and shouldst thou wish to behold this circumstance, look thou to the end of each Revelation, when it may chance that there is one who, from the beginning of his life to the end thereof, never remaineth without having performed ablutions, which is a recommended state, so that he may make it his boast “Never have I gazed upon the heavens without having performed ablutions” – yea, this is a glory if it be conjoined with that whereby the truth of religion is established, which is the knowledge of God, and the knowledge of Him Who is charged to manifest His Cause on His behalf: for otherwise the inner realities shall be converted from a luminous into a fiery state – with how much greater reason, then, must this be true of works?).
And know thou that after the number of gold and silver attain the number of all the letters, plus the Hidden Ten, six thousand and five is obtained; and shouldst thou cause the six thousand to descend downwards it would arrive at six, whereupon a reference would be signalled to the first letter, which is “Ba’” – for this reason hath it been decreed that after these twain have reached this limit, ninety-five mithqals should be taken of each of them for God. On the appearance of the Point – whether in His Former or in His Latter Manifestation – these should be disposed of by His leave; while in the period betwixt the Twain, they should be distributed among nineteen obedient souls, whom He shall designate – unto each the number “Ha’” – details whereof shall be mentioned in their own places. This law it is which shall remain even until the Day of Resurrection; which the believers shall abide by; and which hath been, and is, greater than any commerce, forasmuch as there shall be therein no alteration or change until the following Resurrection.
Now observe thou the bounty of the Point of the Bayan: had He, after this limit had been reached, decreed payment of the equivalent thereof, wouldst thou have been able to ask why or wherefore, wert thou possessed thereof, and among the denizens of Paradise who were obedient to God? Then wouldst thou behold the degree of bounty which, in a single law, had been vouchsafed unto thee, and all creatures: for were all that are on earth to become believers, and wish to enter into Paradise through obedience to the Divine precepts, see only how many laws would have become incumbent upon all! Yet behold by contrast the degree of bounty which hath actually been vouchsafed.
Thus it is that whatsoever there is, proceedeth from the Source – though all are heedless of the matter. For example, if the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – had decreed “Perform thou pilgrimage once a year, if thou hast means to do so,” what believer who was possessed of sufficient means would have been able to deviate from His command? Nay, he would have sought, through obedience, to draw nigh unto the Lord; while amongst God’s creatures he would have boasted himself upon the evidence he had afforded of his obedience. Regard thou all the laws in this same light, perceiving how all men are held within His grasp.
Should He wish to enrich someone, He would enrich him until the Day of Resurrection – and do so in justice, not in other than justice. Likewise, should He wish to elevate someone to the dignity of kingship, He would crown him king until the Day of Resurrection. And likewise, should He wish to ennoble someone, He would ennoble him until the Day of Resurrection. The proof thereof is that if the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – had decreed “It is incumbent upon all to confer riches upon the offspring of such-and-such a believing person, and this is a precept of the faith” – consider what riches would until this day have been heaped upon them, whence “riches” might be truly realized.
Had He decreed “The offspring of such-and-such a person must be sovereigns on my behalf,” would the believers have been able to deviate from His command? – nay, this entitlement would have been theirs until the Day of Resurrection. And had He decreed “The offspring of this believer must be honoured until the Day of Resurrection,” behold the glory which until this day would have accrued to them. Whereas in fact, as thou seest, He commanded only “… to God, as a duty upon the people, is owed a pilgrimage unto the House” – in consequence whereof each year seventy thousand people travel from their homes, and circle about the clay. Even such is the exaltation of the Command of God, and its independence of all else but Him.
In like manner, should He will the reverse, as by willing to reduce someone to poverty, the one in question would become impoverished until the Day of Resurrection. Observe thou that He hath sent down a single unloving mention of Abu Lahab: and today, shouldst thou travel throughout both the East and the West, thou wouldst behold that his name no longer existeth, to the degree that his memory is not preserved by so much as a single name, even should it be in the chain of followers of other than the truth. What “poverty” can exceed this, that not so much should remain of one as the very mention of one’s name? Regard thou other matters in this same light, perceiving that the true command is that which endureth from Resurrection unto Resurrection.
Observe thou the remoteness of the people: the manifestations of governance, in the conceit of a month of kingship, are willing to cast themselves out into the shade of obedience (albeit, shouldst thou examine the object of their obedience, thou wouldst see that it is still established in the name of the Truth, inasmuch as they claim that it is derived from “Islam” – this pretended object of their obedience – whereas really, in the sight of God and of those endowed with understanding, it is adjudged to be for other than God) – observe thou the remoteness of such a one: he is shut out as by a veil from recognizing the Source of a command that endureth from Resurrection unto Resurrection; yet, in the conceit of a single day’s delight – even should it be for other than God – how gladly would he offer up his very soul.
This resulteth from naught but his lack of insight, and his lack of apprehension: for otherwise, how could a perspicacious person, and a punctilious believer, pass up a period lasting from Resurrection to Resurrection when he would be in Paradise, and take instead a single day when he would be in the Fire – a Fire equal in its intensity to the remoteness of that day – and, until God pleased to deliver him therefrom, to be adjudged for other than God, and deserving of the Fire?
Know thou that the means whereby God delivereth the people of the Fire from the Fire is this, that He calleth them unto Himself: whereupon, should they turn unto Him, they shall be delivered from the Fire; otherwise shall they remain therein. Yet, because the Call of God cannot be realized save in virtue of the call raised by the Bearer of His Revelation; and likewise the response to the Lord cannot be realized save in virtue of the response to Him – it is for this reason that when, in each Revelation, the followers of the previous Revelation respond not unto the Call of God, as raised by the Bearer of the following Revelation, and by the various manifestations who summon all mankind unto Him, and lead the way unto Him – that is, the Letters of the Living, and every Vahid that guideth unto the First Vahid – they obtain not deliverance from the Fire.
For example, if at the time of the revelation of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – all that are on earth had responded to His call, and complied with His commands, all, having obtained deliverance from the Fire, would have entered into Paradise: for that which is destined in the world to come – in respect of the Fire and Paradise – circleth about the doom of this present world: for which reason, in the religion of Islam, the believers have been commanded to resort to coercion, that perchance they may compel the people of the Fire to enter into Paradise; while they have been commanded to show forth the intensest love among themselves, that haply they may don the robe of the denizens of Paradise. Should anyone in the Bayan, through coercion, cause all that are on earth to enter within the fold of the Bayan, he would, having delivered all from the Fire, have caused them to enter into Paradise – the which would be a bounty that had been vouchsafed in their behalf.
I swear by the Sacred Divine Essence that if, in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, all obey Him, not a single person shall remain in the Fire, but all shall enter into Paradise: and all that is on earth shall become a part of Ridvan. Howbeit my sorrow is on account of them that believe in Him, not of other than they: for during the Darkest Night they shall suppliantly and ardently implore that His advent may be hastened; ostentatiously transact in His Name their spiritual and worldly affairs; and night and day be tearful and suppliant in anticipation of His advent; yet at the time when He maketh Himself known unto His creatures – which is the Most Mighty Paradise, beyond which no Paradise can be imagined (inasmuch as the beginning of religion is the knowledge of God; while the knowledge of God cannot be imagined save in virtue of the knowledge of Him) – those servants who, in virtue of the sign deposited temporarily in their souls from His own Former Manifestation, had been performing their works for God, shall rise up and bear the burden of that which beseemeth not.
Should the mere thought occur to their hearts that He might be other than true, this would be more grievous in the eyes of God than any sin, and blot out on the instant all their works, as though they had never been: even as, in the Revelation of the Point of the Furqan – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – thou hast heard how all the believers in the Evangel were awaiting the promised Ahmad, and what things, during the twenty-three years of His Revelation, befell that Sun of Truth, until at last He cried out “No Prophet of God hath suffered such harm as I have suffered” – and this notwithstanding that all were suppliantly and ardently awaiting His appearance, so that, by the word of Jesus, they might perform their works for His sake.
Yet, praise be to God that thou wast not in that day: howbeit, thou art in the Revelation of the Point of the Bayan, when all the believers in the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – are awaiting the appearance of the promised Mahdi, inasmuch as this Tradition is from the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and both the high and lowly are at one in their acceptance of it; nor is there any doubt that the essence of faith was confined to the Shi’ihs; while the provinces of Islam are these same Five Provinces which are apparent, the dwellers whereof term themselves Shi’ihs, and outwardly denominate the Land of Fars the “Home of Learning” – yet, although the Tree of Truth hath risen, none of their dwellers have recognized Him; and even after “recognizing” Him, the degree of their remoteness is apparent – the which is sufficient abasement unto them. This notwithstanding, night and day they cry out “Make haste, make haste!”
Regard thou such to be the case also in the Bayan, and be not deceived if all assert “We believe in Him” – inasmuch as this is that same “all” which existed when first the Point of the Bayan was made manifest; and the same identically which existed when first the Point of the Furqan was made manifest: this notwithstanding that the Point of the Bayan hath been made manifest in such a manner that no child can deny Him: yet, notwithstanding that all asserted – and held it for certain – that the Qur’an was the Book of God: whence the Prophethood of the Prophet; the Vicegerency of the Vicegerent; the character of the Gates as “Proofs” – and thereto all the laws of the faith of Islam – were established upon this basis; and although all cited it as the greatest miracle of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and were certain – nay, held it as incontestable – that none but God could reveal its like (and indeed, throughout the course of one thousand two hundred and seventy years no one had produced so much as a single Verse comparable thereto) – despite all this, the moment that such a Proof was made manifest, and, like unto an ocean, sent down without pause Verses from the ocean of His bounty, all, who were thus obligated to make certain that it was from God, and that – according alike to the text of the Qur’an and their own belief – it could not possibly emanate from another than God – nevertheless maintained that it was from other than He, and proceeded to inflict that which they inflicted.
O people of the Bayan! Inflict not that which the people of the Qur’an have inflicted, all performing whatsoever ye do in His Name, yet remaining shut out as by a veil from Him. Should ye remain shut out as by a veil from Him, ye would but have inflicted a wrong upon your own selves, so ye inflict not sorrow upon Him; yet if – God forbid – aught unjust be inflicted upon Him, then would ye have inflicted it upon God – notwithstanding that night and day ye bow down before Him, and from the beginning of your lives until the end thereof ye wish by your actions to win His good pleasure.
It is on account of the enormity of the Cause that ye are unable to sustain it, not its slightness: for of a sudden ye see that One Whom ye have known (and how like it is that ye may be His father or mother, or among His relatives) is made manifest, and soundeth the proclamation “Verily, I am God, no God is there but Me:” whence ye all, of a sudden, are dumbfounded and bewildered by the sheer incomparable exaltation of that Sun of Truth, and unapproachable sublimity of that Countenance of Lordship. Yet if ye remove not your gaze from the essence of the proof, which is the Verses of God, nor say that which was said formerly of the Qur’an, or that which was said latterly of the Bayan, then haply, if ye believe not, ye shall at least not have pronounced judgment against God; otherwise, the consequences thereof shall be borne by you alone.
Should anyone pronounce judgment against God, at what low level must he be situated? Nay, I swear by the Sacred Divine Essence that those servants who pronounce judgment against Him are in a yet more grievous plight than those souls who in this Revelation pronounced sentence against Him. How remote do those persons who made mention of their own existence before the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – now appear in thine estimation! – yet thou too, if thou believe not, shalt be in the selfsame plight in the eyes of those who come hereafter. Today indeed there are persons who view matters on the basis of discerning insight; and likewise, in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, the believers in Him shall, on the basis of discerning insight, view those who are shut out as by a veil as in a remoter case than those who are shut out as by a veil in this present Revelation.
Dost thou forsooth today make any mention of the notables of Mecca and Medina – or know their very names? So shall it be for those who come hereafter in relation to this Revelation; and so too in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, when, even if some mention of falsehood should remain, it shall be on account of the mention made of it by the True One, not because it, in itself, is worthy of mention: as in the case of the name which was sent down in the Qur’an. Come a little to thy senses, and remove not thy gaze from the essence of the proof: perchance on that Day thou mayest obtain salvation; for otherwise the burdened in each Revelation shall unwittingly bear the burden of their works, under the apprehension of performing them for God.
Fear ye then God as it is meet that he be feared; then make certain of His Cause.


Gate Eighteen of the Eighth Unity: On the fast. Make ye mention of God during the nineteen days, at the end of each year, when ye are fasting
The substance of this gate is this, that before fasting thou must comprehend God’s purpose thereof, that what is the fruit of the fast. Hast thou been present at the time of the Revelation of the Qur’an, and asked the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, of the reason for the command of fasting, He would assuredly have granted thee the same answer that is given here: the purpose of fasting is to fast from anyone who is not for God.
For example, at the time of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, if thou loved not anyone who loveth Him not, and wert not for anyone who is not for God, and then fasted in that condition, the reward of fast would assuredly have been granted unto thee. Likewise, extend this same principle, letter by letter, to the Letters of the Unity of the Qur’an, till it endeth in the Last Letter Who embraceth the Manifestations of the entire Unity, so that had thou fasted from other than Him, thou assuredly wouldst have been fasting in that day for God.
In like manner gaze upon the Revelation of the Point of the Bayan. Shouldst thou hear of this Revelation, and attribute non-truth unto it in thy heart, the root pillar of thy Faith would be removed at once, how much more it must bring to naught thy fasting, which is one of the derivative branches of thy Faith. For when thou heard of the Revelation, God’s testimony was complete for thee, inasmuch as the one who proclaimed it to thee, hath adduced verses as the proof, and thus, thy veiling from Him hath been thy refusal to answer the call of God in the fourth dharr.
For at that time, He revealed Himself by that title, and described Himself as the revelation of one of the Gates. It is for that reason that the first dharr was manifest in the fourth dharr, inasmuch as in that very fourth dahrr, He revealed the supreme word “Verily I, Myself, am God, none other God is there but Me.” Should there be a man of discernment in the world, he would be able to tread the path and attain certitude that the Last is exactly the First, and the Seen is the very Hidden, but only in the rank of the First and not in that of the Second. For the Names of each rank conformeth to its own rank and would not surpass its limit. For example, behold the kingdom of the firstness: from the First of Existence till the Last of existence are mentioned therein. But the firstness that is mentioned with regard to the First Himself, can never be compared with the firstness that is mentioned in regard to the Last of Existence. In like manner comprehend all the ranks of Names and examples, and judge accordingly.
Wert thou to fast in this Revelation, thou must fast from the love of the one other than the First letter, inasmuch as naught is seen in all the Letters but that Single Letter. Inasmuch as obedience is solely decreed unto the First Unity, and not unto the multiplied numbers, therefore, regard as fasting those who are for Them, and reckon those who are for other than Them, as non-fasting. Likewise, witness in Their Countenances the gates of the paradise, and behold in the nineteen who dwell in shadow, the gates of fire, inasmuch as fast is indeed fasting from them.
For example, in the Day of the appearance of the Commander of the faithful, peace be upon Him, all were fasting, yet only those were judged as fasting who were abiding in His love, and were fasting from His non-love. In each Revelation, all the people of that Dispensation perform the laws of that Revelation, but upon the inception of the Next revelation, the efficacy pertaining to the root pillar of the previous religion is removed, how much more cometh to naught the derivative branches thereof.
By saying that upon the inception of the New Revelation the previous laws are removed, it is intended that the previous religion is now manifested through the New Revelation, otherwise in truth it is not removed. Thus in this Revelation, only those who were abiding in the love of the Second, have fasted during the month of God. Otherwise, all in their own limitations obey the law, but of no avail. Had all the faithful in the Qur’an, failed to fast and yet the calamity which is afflicted upon Him had not, it would have been far more beloved in the sight of God than all their fastings and the disgrace that happened. For had His martyrdom not happened, the root beginning of their faith would not have been judged as removed, but now even though they perform the laws of the religion, it is decreed as removed.
When fasting, it behoveth the one doing so, to take heed lest he would be veiled from the good pleasure of God, so that should during his fast, the Tree of Truth shine forth, and command non-performance thereof, he would obey unhesitatingly. For this fasting that he now performeth is solely due to His command in His previous Revelation. In like manner regard all the deeds. Guard thyself from drinking, eating, intercourse, contention, even in words, and injustice, even to the extent of a carat, and pronouncing judgement against God. Be especially careful with regard to the last three prohibitions, inasmuch as from the inception of the Revelation till the beginning of the Next Revelation, whoever pronounceth judgement against the Point, he hath pronounced judgement against God, which rendereth his fasting naught.
The same is true with regard to the Day of the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, inasmuch as there is no doubt that at that glorious time all the people of the Bayan will be fasting, but should they pronounce judgement against Him, the root beginning of their religion would assuredly come to naught, how much more it will be in regard to one of its token laws.
Be watchful from the sunrise till the sunset, and fix thy gaze upon the name of the Unity (19). No faithful, male or female, is required to fast before reaching the age 11(the number of the name He, Huva), except till the time that sun reacheth its zenith. And should they fast beyond that time, they would not be reckoned as fasting. After the age 11, it is required till the age 42 (the number of the age yea, bala), and beyond that there would be no fasting.
Behold each of the parts of the ordinances of God. Had all on earth combined together, they would have been unable to decree, in truth, in an infinitesimal part (a ninth of the ninth of the tenth of the tenth) of a moment, anything other than it. But witness now how the ocean of divine bounty is billowing for His servants, without their desert. For had it been due to their own worth, they would assuredly have remained in their past veils. For the source of recognition is His grace, so that had He refused to make Himself known, they would have continued to perform the past deeds till the Next Resurrection.
Fast ye for God, your Lord, that haply in the Day of Resurrection, ye would be far from those who fail to recognise Him Whom God shall make manifest.


Gate Nineteen of the Eighth Unity
If the Name of the Tree be mentioned, pronounce ye blessings upon Him: and if the Letters of the Living be mentioned, pronounce ye salutations upon them; and make ye mention of God by the Name of Muhammad, and the manifestations of His Cause, on each eve and day of Friday, two hundred and two times: then make mention of God therein four thousand times, saying “Ya Allah!” (“O God!”).
The substance of this gate is that whensoever He Whom God shall make manifest is mentioned, send ye blessings upon Him; and whensoever His Letters of the Living are mentioned, invoke ye Glory (Baha’) upon them; and employ ye the same blessings and salutations in the case of that which hath already been made manifest as in the case of that which shall be made manifest. On each eve and day of Friday, appreciate ye their worth, for this is a night and day whereon the recompense of works is doubled: and make ye mention of Him Whom God shall make manifest, and His Letters of the Living, two hundred and two times; and call ye upon God in a spirit of consecration to the number of four “Ghayns.”
It is not that ye should prostrate yourselves, and call upon God, while remaining shut out as by a veil from recognizing the very Person Whose remembrance is the remembrance of God, even as the remembrance of God is His remembrance; and whose recognition is the recognition of the Lord, even as the recognition of the Lord is His recognition. Consider thou the Revelation of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him, and how many an eve and day of Friday passed over that Sun of Truth while the believers in the Evangel were all calling upon God in their own tongue – yet did this remembrance on their part avail them aught?
Regard thou such to be the case likewise in the Revelation of the Point of the Bayan. Some there are among God’s servants who each eve till dawn are occupied with the remembrance of God: yet the Sun of Truth hath well nigh mounted to its zenith, in the heaven of Revelation, and still these people have not stirred beyond their prayer-mats! Should the wondrous Verses be recited to one amongst them, he would make reply, “Withhold me not from the remembrance of God!” O thou veiled one! Wouldst thou forsooth make mention of God? – why then art thou shut out as by a veil from the One Who revealed the effulgence of this remembrance within thee? – for had He not sent down aforetime “Make ye then mention of God,” how wouldst thou have known to make mention of Him, and by what means wouldst thou have gone about this?
Know thou that if thou makest mention of Him Whom God shall make manifest, then shalt thou have made mention of God. By the same token, shouldst thou hearken unto the Verses of the Bayan, and accept them to be true, then shall the Verses of God be of benefit unto thee – for otherwise, how shall they avail thee? Nay, do thou make the whole of thy life, from the beginning thereof until the end thereof, a single prostration, and pass it all in the remembrance of God: yet believe not in the One made manifest in the Revelation wherein thou livest – and see what benefit it shall do thee! Yet, shouldst thou recognize Him, and know His due; and should He say “I have accepted thine whole life as dedicated to My remembrance,” then assuredly thou wouldst have remembered Him to the utmost limit of remembrance: for thou performest thy works to the end that God should accept them: while the acceptance of the Lord is not made apparent save by the acceptance of the One made manifest in the Revelation.
For example, if the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – accepted some matter, it was God Who accepted it; otherwise it remained but a mere figment of the imagination of the one who wrought it, and returned not unto God. Likewise, should the Point of the Bayan accept some action, it is God Who hath accepted it, inasmuch as the contingent world hath no way unto the Eternal Essence: save only that whatsoever cometh down, must descend from the One made manifest in the Revelation; while whatsoever riseth up, must ascend to the One made manifest in the Revelation.
Praise be to God that not a single rational person hath been seen in whose regard He might make mention of acceptance! Yet all, from the beginning of their lives to the end thereof, perform their works with the utmost diligence and endeavour: and wert thou to ask one amongst them “Wherefore performest thou these works?” he would make reply, “That haply they may prove acceptable unto God.” O thou insensate creature! The acceptance of God is not made apparent save by the acceptance of His Proof. Hast thou a Word from His Proof wherein He hath stated “I have accepted thy works”? Thus it is that all insensately perform their works, whilst shut out from the fruit thereof as by a veil. Yea, a person shall truly have performed his works in the Bayan if, on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, he hath a deed from Him signifying acceptance of his works: he it is of whom it may fitly be said that he hath performed his works for God, and that God hath accepted them; yet otherwise, to what avail? – for all who are on earth perform their works according to the precepts of their faith.
Yet look thou unto that Source whence the acceptance of the Lord is made apparent. Methinks in the Revelation of the Apostle of God there was not a single discerning person – apart from those who had truly recognized His station – to request of Him the acceptance of their works, for had any such instance occurred, mention would have been made of it in the Qur’an, in the language of Revelation: inasmuch as it is not possible for the acceptance of the Lord to be signified in the language of men (were it indeed to be signified in the language of the Apostle of God Himself – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – it would then be His acceptance, not the acceptance of the Lord).
That Source whence, like unto an ocean, the Verses of God are shining forth, this people have concealed in a mountain, whilst night and day they perform their works “for God:” bethink thee – hath the merest soupçon of a savour of sensibility wafted over them? – whereas the fruit of all their actions is that they should prove acceptable to God: while the acceptance of God cannot be made apparent save in the language of the Verses, which convey the incapacity of all else but Him, even as today the Qur’an conveyeth the incapacity of the whole of existence.
Now, do what thou wilt – yet see whether a single straw of a mention of acceptance shall be made in its regard. Thus it is that ye move in the darknesses of the Night, nor see any fruit from your endeavours. From the beginning of your lives until the end thereof ye perform your works for God: then of a sudden ye perform them not for that Manifestation unto whom all work returneth: whereas, did ye but perform your works for Him, ye would not, on the Day of Resurrection, be afflicted in this fashion.
Observe thou how mighty is the Cause, and how veiled are all mankind! I swear by the Sacred Essence of God that the whole mention of God, and performance of works for Him, is the mention of Him Whom God shall make manifest, and the performance of works for Him. Deceive not yourselves by the assertion “We perform our works for God” – nay, ye perform them for other than Him: for if ye be truly performing them for God, then shall ye perform them for Him Whom God shall make manifest, and make mention of Him; for otherwise, even the dwellers of this mountain – who know naught – repeat night and day “There is no God but God” – yet what profit doth it yield them?
Come a little to your senses, lest ye be shut out from the Source of Command as by a veil: for all your worldly actions revert, even in your own estimation, unto your spiritual estate: while the fruit of all your spiritual actions is the acceptance of the Lord; and the Lord’s acceptance cannot be made apparent save by the acceptance of Him Who hath already been made manifest, or of Him Whom God shall make manifest, from Whom the language of the Verses shall be apparent: for if they be accepted by other than these, then is it not the acceptance of God: inasmuch as the utterance enshrining God’s acceptance is other than the utterance of men; nor is it capable of becoming Two.
Shouldst thou assert “The acceptance of the Gates is the acceptance of the Imams, whilst the acceptance of the Imams is the acceptance of the Apostle of God” – this delegation of acceptance is because that Tree hath accepted in this wise: and similarly, His accounting the sorrow of a believer His own sorrow, and terming his happiness His own happiness – these correlations are because He Himself hath sent down the matter thus, for had it not been for Him, no such fruit would have been forthcoming.
Keep your gaze fixed ever upon the Source of Command, under Whose shadow all things else are made apparent. He is not Two, but One (Vahid); and His One (Vahid) is not numerate but innumerate; while that numerate Vahid hath by His command been constituted such: for were it not for Him, no ordinance would be issued. Do ye then confess the Unity of God, your All-Merciful Lord, in a spirit of consecration; then, by the aid of God, and through the power of Truth, perform ye your works.
