title: BB00001: Bayan-i-Farsi (Persian Bayan)
section: The Ninth Unity
text:
The Ninth Unity

Gate One of the Ninth Unity
concerning this, that the glory of the whole earth is for God, and the peerless of all cities is for God: and whoso of the possessors of the Bayan prayeth in the palaces which are today related unto kings, let him make a charitable donation of one mithqal of silver: unless these should be used as residences for the relatives of the Letters of the Vahid, or the witnesses of the Bayan; and in all seats of glory do ye leave places vacant for souls to the number Vahid, if there be ample space; otherwise the innumerate Vahid shall suffice those obedient to this law; and the place of that which hath been taken from the Point must needs be attached to one of the Twin Holy Sanctuaries, and over that resting-place a building clad in mirrors be constructed, that the people may make mention of God, and pray, therein.
The substance of this gate is that the glory of every land is for God, and returneth on the Day of Revelation unto Him Whom God shall make manifest, or whomsoever He may designate; and so likewise the glory of the cities, and of the palaces that have remained from the kings who were aforetime. Should any of the people of the Bayan pray therein, it behoveth him to make a donation of one mithqal of silver, so that none may reside in them save the witnesses of the Bayan, and the manifestations of the Vahid.
If any honourable assembly – peerless in its kind – be gathered, it is fitting that places to the number Vahid should be left vacant, so that if at that hour He Whom God shall make manifest and His Letters of the Living should make their appearance, no one would be conjoined with the gems that are gathered from the Bayan. Should there be insufficient room in an assembly, permission hath not been granted for space to be left for more than a single person. Likewise is it fitting that in every dwelling a place be left vacant for a single person: inasmuch as one may see that even in the home of Him Whom God shall make manifest, it is evidently the fashion for the members of His own family to deny Him His seat, since they know Him not, to do Him reverence by His own Name. Howbeit He knoweth them all, and laugheth at those servants who observe such respect and veneration towards His Name, yet on the Day of His appearance remain shut out from recognizing Him as by a veil, notwithstanding all their pious intentions.
It hath been commanded that the clay which hath been taken from the Point should fall in one of the Twin Holy Sanctuaries, and a chamber clad in mirrors be raised over it, wherein the believers may perform their prayers: so that it may be a sign unto the people that the Point of the Bayan was but a servant who was created, sustained, born – and His property inherited: and that whatsoever He spake on the part of God was from Him, not from Himself: so that no one may speak extravagantly, attributing to Him a station such as would exceed the limits of servitude. For the progress and ascent of them that travel in the Bayan cannot be compared with those of them that travel in the Qur’an – how much less of all that are on earth: yet all these wayfarers circle around the wayfarers in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest: inasmuch as the Truth is on that Day established through them, not through other than they.
Fear ye then God in respect of all that He hath sent down from His presence: for, verily, the Command of God in relation to the higher is the same as in relation to the lower. O ye servants of God, fear Me!


Gate Two of the Ninth Unity
concerning this, that should anyone have a skill in calligraphy that is without equal during his days, let him write out a thousand Verses for God, and will that these be delivered to the Point, so that God in His mercy may recompense Him on the Day of Resurrection: He, verily, hath knowledge of all things.
The substance of this gate is that if, in the Revelation of the Bayan, there be found a penman without equal in his age, in whatsoever style of penmanship he be proficient – ranging from the “Abha” at the highest level to the “A’la” at the lowest (which are the degrees of the Vahid) – it would be well-pleasing for him to write out on a sheet of paper – this also to be peerless in its kind – one thousand verses, the modes whereof should likewise be of this same description: and will that on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, it be presented unto that Tree of Truth, in order that He may recompense him with those Verses which it is His alone to give, and he may by this means be remembered before his Best-Beloved.
Should anyone be unable to complete a thousand verses at the time of writing, it behoveth the witnesses of the Bayan to deliver unto him the value (Baha’) of the thousand: yet if he be possessed of such competence, then it would be unbefitting for one who performeth a work for God to set a value (Baha’) thereon. Whatsoever he may write of the Five Modes of the Point of the Bayan – whether the Verses, Prayers, Commentaries, Scientific Discourses, or Persian Words – all shall be acceptable.
The fruit thereof is that if, on the Day of Revelation, there be found such a person – or any like him – they would not move their pens save to write the traces of Him Whom God shall make manifest: inasmuch as they have been forbidden to move their pens to write any words save His: haply on that Day one soul at least shall perform a work for God – the which shall be better than all that is written during the Night.
No script in this Revelation hath been more beloved in the eyes of the One made manifest therein than the shikastih script – that is, the living thereof, not the dead: inasmuch as most people write it as they have been schooled to do so – yet is it dead, not living. The comeliness thereof resideth in its quickness: the likeness whereof, in relation to the naskh script, is that of a young man in relation to an old. Howbeit all things within their proper bounds have been, and are, beloved in the eyes of the Lord.
Do ye then school your offspring in the most glorious (Abha) and the most exalted scripts in your possession: perchance by this means ye may, on the Day of Resurrection, have that whereon to pride yourselves in the sight of your Lord.


Gate Three of the Ninth Unity
To God is owed by every king or sovereign who is raised up in this religion the duty of constructing for himself a palace clad in mirrors, wherein to write the Verses of God, having before his eyes the Verse set forth in the following.
The substance of this gate is that the whole of existence hath not been created but for the Day of the appearance of God, the which, in the usage of the Bayan, is termed the Day of Resurrection, which extendeth from the first appearance of the Tree of Truth up to His setting. For example, in the Revelation of the Point of the Furqan, that Day, for which all had been created, was twenty-three years in length. The likeness of those days is that of the sun in relation to the stars; and similarly, the likeness of the people of that Revelation in relation to its Bearer is even such as this.
It is for this reason that in that Revelation, those who truly recognize His station should forbear to give rein to their pens, and be abashed of their own writings, treatises and compositions, and of their own displays and exhibitions: for if a star rise during the daytime, then assuredly these too shall be regarded as enlightening. By the same token, should the most learned doctor of the age of Him Whom God shall make manifest, after His appearance, venture to write a single word, it would be exactly in this wise. Just as the Point is the Sun of Truth, so too His traces – in relation to all other traces – are the Sun of Traces. Thus it is that even should all, up to the furthest limit of existence, become mirrors, reflections would become apparent in each one of them from that Sun of Traces: nay, they are independent of aught else but this. Howbeit, after the setting thereof, permission hath been granted for all, as far as they are able, to ascend beneath its shadow: yet were all the world to combine together, and to soar up in this manner, they would still be unable to arrive at an understanding of a single letter thereof.
It hath been noted in the Bayan in respect of potentates – alike those designated “Mim” and “Sin” – that each should construct for himself an exalted dwelling-place clad in mirrors, wherein should be written before his eyes some mention to the effect that if He Whom God shall make manifest should appear, and he believe in Him, and arise to aid him, then would he become the most exalted of all men; yet in the reverse case the most abased: perchance on that Day he may be watchful of himself lest, for a few fleeting mornings of kingship, he should be shut out as by a veil from attaining the meeting with his Best-Beloved, for the which, from the beginning of his life until the end thereof, he had been – as he still is – performing all his works: nor shall aught avail him but that he should perform them for Him, and arise to aid His faith with that wherein shall lie His good pleasure; for otherwise he shall depart – even as those who were before him have departed – nor any trace shall remain of him other than an unholy memory, and the fact of his having been shut out as by a veil from the Beloved Object for Whom he did whatever acts he performed, and in Whose Name he was honoured in the Bayan.
For if any sorrow befall Him Whom God shall make manifest, then whatever vengeance could be exacted from All Things shall be wrought upon him; whereas if he assist Him, then whatever bounty could be lavished upon all things shall fall to his lot: inasmuch as if he undertake not aught that would cause Him sorrow, no one else shall have a way to do so either: inasmuch as in this age the matter was in this wise, that the divines would have been of no consequence but for his support. God alone knoweth in what manner shall be the training and limitations of the people of that age. Should a divine in that Revelation venture upon the reverse of His good pleasure, it would be as though he had burdened himself with the remoteness of the whole of existence: while every fire which had been created for aught that was not “for God” would be for him: inasmuch as the gaze of all, both high and low, is turned towards the divines living at the time of each Revelation, so that if these be truthful in their belief, none shall deviate from their adherence to the True One: whereas if any sorrow befall the True One, it shall be on account of the deviance of the divines, for all conceive them to be in the right: whereas in the sight of God they have ever been, and are, for other than God.
Thus it is that that fire which reacheth all, cometh first to them, and only after them to others; just as, if they embrace the Truth, the grace of God cometh first to them, and only then to others.
A goodly grade is it, the grade of knowledge! – if it be the knowledge of Him Whom God shall make manifest, and the source of His contentment; otherwise is it the worst of grades in the sight of God, and of All Things: for were one to know no word of knowledge, it would be better for him than to have the knowledge of All Things, yet to have not the knowledge of Him Whom God shall make manifest, by Whose command all things put on the robe of existence, and acquire in consequence that substance in respect whereof they are entitled to the designation “thing:” for at the time when he knoweth not a word, yet still, if he embraceth the Truth – then Blessed is he!: while if he turn aside therefrom, he shall but have cast his own self into the Fire; otherwise, whoever hath followed him in virtue of his knowledge shall be with him in the Fire: while whoever, again in virtue of his knowledge, followeth the True One, shall through his agency enter into Paradise: howbeit, because this following of one soul by another is liable to cause the latter to be shut out from the Truth as by a veil, for this reason would it be more profitable for the former to be devoid, than to be possessed, of knowledge; unless he should consecrate himself unto God, reasoning with himself that perchance, through his knowledge, he may be able to lend assistance to the True One on the Day of His appearance, and someone in consequence be moved to accept His Truth.
Were he so to consecrate himself, then, at the moment when he looked, and beheld in the Verses of God his own incapacity to produce their like, he would at once bow down, confessing:

“These are the Verses of Him Whom God shall make manifest, whereof the promise hath been given unto all. Thanks be to God that on the Day of Resurrection He hath acquainted us with Him, so that we may attain the fruit of our existence, nor remain shut out as by a veil from the meeting with our Maker, for the which we were created; neither have we performed our works for aught else but this. This is a token of God’s grace unto us: He, verily, is the Most Gracious, the All-Bountiful.”

Know thou that, wert thou to make certain of the Truth, then assuredly thou wouldst act in this wise: yet since thou canst not do so, on account of the veils wherein thy soul is swathed, thus it is that thou shalt remain in the Fire, all unwitting of thy plight. If, on the Day of His appearance – other than to believe in Him – thou wert to perform all good, still it would not save thee from the Fire; whereas, if thou wert to believe in the True One, all good would be writ down for thee in the Book of God, and therewith thou wouldst enjoy the delights of Paradise until the following Resurrection. Mark thou well this matter – as well as thou canst mark it – for it is exceeding delicate, even while it is broader than the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them.
For example, had all those who awaited the advent of the One promised by the word of Jesus – peace be upon Him – made certain that the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – was the appearance of Ahmad, not one soul would have deviated from the word of Jesus – peace be upon Him. Likewise, in the Revelation of the Point of the Bayan, were all to make certain that He is none other but that selfsame promised Mahdi, whereof the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – gave tidings, not one of the believers in the Qur’an would deviate from the word of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him. Behold thou likewise this same circumstance obtaining in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest: so that if all make certain that He is none other but the One of Whom, under the title “Him Whom God shall make manifest,” the Point of the Bayan gave tidings, no one shall deviate from the path.
It is not that they shall have any warrant for their lack of certitude in His respect. Should the monks of the Evangel – or the divines of the Furqan after the revelation of the Bayan – have any such warrant, then these too shall have such a warrant. Be thou scrupulous – to the utmost limit of scrupulosity – lest thy very scrupulosity cause thee to be shut out as by a veil from recognizing Him. And do thou recognize Him with His own eye, in order that thou mayest attain the honour of knowing Him.
These words have been mentioned to the end that on that Day all, both high and low, may be watchful of themselves, whence haply they may not enter within the purview of “Evanescence,” nor remain shut out as by a veil from attaining the apex of reunion. Wherefore be ye watchful of God: then guard against incurring His displeasure.


Gate Four of the Ninth Unity
God hath enjoined upon the people to remember Him in their heart. Say! All are questioned thereof.
The substance of this gate is this, that the essence of all knowledge is the knowledge of goodly characters and traits. Man must act in conformity with it, that by virtue of such knowledge of ethics he would neither witness any grief in his soul, nor inflict sorrow upon any other soul. All the reasons for ordaining righteousness, abstinence, and other attributes, return unto this principle. For example, should one be afflicted with poverty, but choose contentment and patience, his self-esteem would remain intact, and he would not be grieved, and therefore when the days of his need hath passed, he would not see any abasement. On the other hand, should he show his poverty he would, at the best, receive assistance from someone which would remove that which is grieving him, but then when he beholdeth himself, the received assistance would never equal the abasement brought about for him. Regard in like manner, all the good traits and attributes in all stations.
The reason why remembering God in heart hath been enjoined in moments of devotion is this, that thou mayest give thy best attention to the remembrance of God, that thy heart may at all times be animated with His Spirit, and not be shut out as by a veil from thy Best Beloved. Let not thy tongue pay lip service in praise of God while thy heart be not attuned to the exalted Summit of Glory, and the Focal Point of communion. Thus if haply thou dost live in the Day of Resurrection, the mirror of thy heart will be set towards Him Who is the Day-Star of Truth; and no sooner will His light shine forth than the splendour thereof shall forthwith be reflected in thy heart.
For He is the Source of all goodness, and unto Him revert all things. But if He appeareth while thou hast turned unto thyself in meditation, this shall not profit thee, unless thou shalt mention His Name by words He hath revealed. For in the forthcoming Revelation it is He Who is the Remembrance of God, whereas the devotions which thou art offering at present have been prescribed by the Point of the Bayan, while He Who will shine resplendent in the Day of Resurrection is the Revelation of the inner reality enshrined in the Point of the Bayan -a Revelation more potent, immeasurably more potent, than the one which hath preceded it.
Shouldst thou mention Him in such manner, in thy heart and by virtue of thy faith in Him, the reward of such remembrance would be 95 times that of thy manifest remembrance. However, in the Day of His Revelation, make mention of the Absolute Truth manifestly, inasmuch as in that Day mentioning Him manifestly is 95 times more excellent than mentioning Him in heart. This is the essence of the remembrance before both he who mentionth and He Who is the Object of remembrance, couldst thou but comprehend. Make then mention of God in your heart with your utmost power.
Take heed and watch the objects attended by thy heart which hath always been, and will continue forever to be, susceptible of infinite degrees. If thou hast been of the true people of vigilance and introspection, thou wouldst know that in the highest degrees of vigilance, the objects of heart would resemble those of the manifest objects of perception, until a stage in which the remembrance of one’s heart would be the same both in sleep or waking.
Shouldst thou attain such an exalted stage, and yet fail to recognise the Sun of Truth, it would not profit thee, but shouldst thou recognise Him, and thou fail to attain such stage, it would profit thee.
Excess in devotional reciting is not approved, be it in heart or in tongue, nay, rather, wert thou to make mention once with exultation and rapture, it would far excel a thousand mentions without them. The precise measure of such balance is known to each person in his own soul.
However, the real purpose is making mention of Him Whom God shall make manifest. Those men living at the time of This Revelation, who have claimed the attainment of vigilance and introspection, they are of no weight whatsoever before God. The binding precepts of God are solely those that have been revealed in the Bayan. Fix not your gaze upon these kinds of names who lack any truth, inasmuch as the people who made such claims were shut out as by a veil from this Revelation. On the other hand, those who had never gazed upon these directions, even had not heard of the word vigilance and introspection, were saved by their recognition.
Take heed then and watch yourselves. And make mention of God in your heart and your manifest expressions, for ye would be tranquillised by the remembrance of God. Claim ye not that which will not profit you before your Lord in the Day of Resurrection, unless ye prostrate before Him Whom God shall make manifest, which is naught but prostrating before God. Fear Me then, O ye people of remembrance!


Gate Five of the Ninth Unity
To God, as a duty upon each soul, are owed nineteen days when he shall serve the Point on His return, and act as He may give leave, should leave He grant him; otherwise is he his own master: and God, verily, is possessed of grace abounding.
The substance of this gate is that aught to which the name “thing” applieth is from God, in virtue of His Will. Howbeit, the Manifestation of the Will hath deposited of His signs within each temple nineteen signs all told, beyond which aught else is the proliferation thereof, whose number cannot be reckoned. For this reason hath it been commanded that on His appearance one should, each day, on behalf of the sign he hath within him, present himself before God, at His behest, in order that the fruit of the very root of his religion may be made apparent in the sight of God – to make no mention of its branches. The first day is for the Point; while the days of the Hayy (Living) are for the Letters of the Living: and from the beginning of the Day of Resurrection until the end thereof, this law is incumbent upon all the believers in the Bayan, both high and low; neither shall it be lifted from them until such time as He may give leave for it to be lifted, at which time – and not before – it shall be lifted.
Howbeit, on the day in question, do thou assuredly exert the utmost effort possible in the world of being. Consider, for example, how worshipful thou art today in relation to but one of the Letters of the Furqan, in the place where he lieth buried: even so shouldst thou comport thyself, on his behalf, towards the Point of Truth. Observe thou how many people today make visitation to the sanctuary of the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him; yet consider how the Commander of the Faithful himself – peace be upon him – in the Revelation of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – stood in relation to His Holiness: nay, whatsoever he possessed of glory and of exaltation – all derived from Him.
Reflect then: how canst thou presume to enter into so hallowed a presence? – when with respect even to those Letters of the Vahid whom thou seest today, all people, both high and low, are circling about their tombs, and expending their substance so that they may be styled a visitant to these shrines. Yet all these displays of grandeur which now surround them are in virtue solely of the command which came from the Source, which is none other but the word of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him.
Reflect then: who can presume to enter into so hallowed a presence? – when if the whole of existence were to be a single soul: and that soul, from the beginning that hath no beginning until the Day of His Revelation, were to prostrate himself, for His sake – even up to the Day of His appearance – still, on the Day of His appearance, should He have regard for his deserving, assuredly He would not grant him permission so much as to lift his head. The Sun of Truth is a reality such that the grandeur of all things, in comparison with Him, is more insignificant than an atom. Yet this notwithstanding, regard thou His words, and behold how He educateth thereby all His creatures, that haply all may in complete detachment devote themselves unto the One Who createth alike Him and All Things; Who sustaineth alike Him and All Things; Who causeth alike Him and all things to die; and Who restoreth alike Him and All Things to life.
Shouldst thou apprehend the knowledge of the hidden of the hidden, and act accordingly, on the basis of certitude, then canst thou be worthy to enter into the presence of Him that lighteneth the light – through His grace, not through thine own deserving; otherwise, shouldst thou enter into His presence, yet not have attained the station betokened by the words “I associate naught as partner with God,” then shalt thou be unable to think one thought according to His actual pleasure – how much less to perform one work (considering that even were all mankind on that Day to perform their wonted works, dost think forsooth that their Best-Beloved would be well pleased with them? – any more than He is today, when thou beholdest how they expend thousands upon thousands in the way of that House which He hath related unto Himself; yet, on the Day of His appearance – through whose each word a House such as this is created – if even one soul ascendeth unto Him it is apparent). Wherefore fear ye God; then be sincere in your actions: for shouldst thou enter into His presence otherwise than as is His desert, assuredly thou shalt be shut out as by a veil from obeying His command.
Shouldst thou desire the glory of knowing him, thou art not forsooth worthy to set foot within the court of His glory. See, “E’en from the Throne’s high parapet they summon thee ‘Soar aloft!’” Nay, regard thou His estate as yet more glorious than this: rather, His word maketh the Throne the Throne; while He Himself is too exalted to be characterized by such a description, or qualified by such a portrayal – and this at a time when thou beholdest a situation so far from glorious that, seemingly, thou couldst witness none more abased: even as thou hast heard, concerning the Last Letter, on the part of his own former manifestation in the Point of the Bayan: in respect of which Letter – who had become the place of His Revelation – hath been sent down: “Glorified is He Who is the Most Exalted, nor is there above Him one His equal; and glorified is He Who is the Most Abased, nor is there beneath Him one His like.” How then can these kinds of outward manifestations be held worthy of mention in His hallowed presence?
The above remarks, however, are as concerning the paths of mystic understanding and the gems of Divine Unity. Notwithstanding, do thou, in the way of whatsoever outward forms are customary in that Revelation, exert thyself to the highest limit that lieth within thy power: which if thou do, He shall accept thine efforts, provided that thou exceed not the limits of these outward forms. Yet shouldst thou look upon Him with a gaze other than that of recognition of His Divine Unity, He shall adjudge thee to be an animal; while shouldst thou – God forbid – ask why or wherefore, it shall be as though thou hadst done so with respect to His own Self: inasmuch as He hath no similitude to which He might be likened: should I say “the Point of the Bayan” – lo, His Revelation is more manifest; and should I say “His subsequent Revelation within His own Self” – lo, that same Revelation is more hidden.
Of what consideration am I, that I should be able to make mention of Him? – when the mightiest exaltation, and the loftiest sublimity, are but His permission unto His creatures to make mention of Him; for otherwise, He would have been sanctified above all mention, and consecrated above all praise: while He – with all that exaltation of grandeur and loftiness, and sublimity of majesty and glory – hath ever been, and ever shall be, with God. Exalted, immensely exalted, therefore be God above any description of Him that can be given.


Gate Six of the Ninth Unity
concerning this, that it behoveth the people to honour the clan from amongst whom the Point of Truth shall come forth, should they believe in Him.
The substance of this gate is this: know thou that there is no land than which there is none more temperate, but that it shall become the place of Revelation; and likewise there are no Names than whom there are none nearer unto God – after the Letters of the Vahid – but that they shall become the companions of the Tree of Truth. Howbeit, should the remotest of God’s creatures believe in Him, then shall he become the nearest thereof: as thou mayest observe, if thou wishest, in the Letters of the Vahid; or, if thou preferrest, in those aforetime. Consider, for example, with respect to the “nearest” in the Furqan, that the criterion was faith – yet if such were forthcoming from a near one, he became nearer still (as was indeed the case with the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him – in the Qur’an). Nay rather, the criterion is nearness of faith, even as thou hast witnessed in the case of the Letters of the Vahid.
Know thou that the Lord gazeth upon His dominions, and if there be a father than whom there is none better, He chooseth the same for Him; and similarly if there be a mother than whom there is none better, the Lord chooseth her for Him. Regard thou such to be the case likewise with respect to all other matters. Forasmuch as there is but one existence, and that Ocean of Bounty. All in virtue of this alone are living; and all in virtue of this alone shall be dead. Should they embrace His truth, then shall they be living; otherwise shall they be dead – whether one be the highest of God’s creatures, or whether the lowliest thereof: inasmuch as His relation unto all things is equal. Howbeit, the Lord hath sent down all His Glory (Baha’) and splendour upon His parents, ere yet they were created; and hath sent down blessings upon them ere the creation of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them – which blessings are those which are sent down upon them from their own Newborn, not another than He.
For the Eternal Essence is exalted above any mention or conjunction: while that which is possible in the world of being is the revelation of the Primal Will – in the Manifestation thereof, not in Its own essence – which Manifestation is the embodiment of the Will, in Whom naught is to be seen but God – glorified and exalted be He – and the Eternal Best-Beloved – glorified and exalted be He. Whoso is for Him is for God; and whoso is not for Him – know thou that he is for other than God. Regard thou the whole of existence, in comparison with that Ocean of Bounty, as but a drop out of the ocean of His bounty: and attain thou unto Him, or yield up thy soul in the love of doing so: for attain unto Him thou shalt, should His Revelation not befall; otherwise shouldst thou, after hearing thereof, delay for so much as the ninth of the ninth of the tenth of the tenth of a second in responding “Yea,” thou shalt not after death attain unto His presence.
Know thou that obedience to Him is naught but obedience to God, while love for Him is naught but love for God. Allow thou not books and words to keep thee back from recognizing Him, on the Day of His appearance, for all are but means of attainment unto Him: and if He be, and all else be not – He shall be, and all shall be beneath His shadow; while if He be not, and all else be, there hath never been, nor ever shall be, aught, and all shall be reduced to utter nothingness. This is the meaning of the following noble Verse, shouldst thou, in fathoming its purport, look upon it with illumined vision:

“Say: God sufficeth All Things above All Things, and naught but God, thy Lord, sufficeth – neither in the heavens nor in the earth nor in whatsoever is between them. He, verily, hath ever been the Knowing, the Sufficing, the Powerful.”

There is no matter for which, if thou recite this Verse to the number of the Name “Qadir” (314), thou shalt not behold an answer from the Source of Command: for the Lord is nearer unto thee than thou art unto thyself; hath power over all things; and hath knowledge – now as aforetime – of all whereunto the designation “thing” attacheth. After thou hast recited it with the tongue of thine outward being, the letters of this Verse have been, and are, in His dominions, where they are instrumental in making manifest the means whereby this answer is vouchsafed on His behalf. Yet look thou not but unto God, than Whom all else is His creation; and God is the All-Possessing, the Most High.


Gate Seven of the Ninth Unity
concerning the prohibitions of the sale of Anghuzih and the leaf of the tree of Zaqqum. Know thou that the root of all prohibitions is the First Letters of Negation; and in like manner, whatsoever cometh under their shadow entereth within the purview of Negation: and know thou that whoso is not for Him Whom God shall make manifest is for other than God; while whoso is for Him is for God. Regard thou such to be the case likewise with the Point of the Bayan; and, one Revelation before Him, in the Qur’an; and, two Revelations before Him, in the Evangel: and if, on the advent of each successive Revelation, the preceding Revelations enter not within its fold, do thou regard them as within the purview of Negation.
It hath been forbidden to make use of tobacco and its likenesses, as well as that which is transported from the direction of Khurasan – which hath an other-than-goodly odour – and its similitudes, in whatsoever forms these may be prepared. Shouldst thou wish to behold the degradation of “the First” and “the Second,” then look thou at these twain, inasmuch as whatsoever is other than goodly reverteth unto those twain; while whatsoever is goodly reverteth unto Muhammad and ’Ali – peace be upon them. The matters related to these have been forbidden on account of those. Seek thou refuge under all conditions in the one Lord – exalted and glorified be He – and in His Names and Likenesses, inasmuch as the likeness of other than a believer is even this.
Know thou that every goodly thing that hath been, and is, in the knowledge of God is beneath the shadow of the Tree of Affirmation, Who is He Whom God shall make manifest; while aught else is beneath the shadow of Negation. Applying this perception to the outside world, behold with thine outward eye its realization in His Revelation: haply thou mayest not remain shut out as by a veil from beholding His beauteous countenance; and mayest bow down for God, for Him; confess the truth of that which He sendeth down on the part of God; and compile His traces in the finest script and the most exquisite craftsmanship: inasmuch as whatever words are sent down on His part are the manifestations of the Eternal Paradise shining forth upon the temples of the hearts of all created things. In each Revelation, do thou garner the first-fruits of the gardens of that Revelation; and, by all means possible in the world of being, do thou assist and obey Him, that perchance thou mayest come out of Negation, and enter into Affirmation – for this is the all-embracing Divine mercy, which attacheth unto all things, and the all-comprehending Celestial bestowal, which hath ever encompassed all things.
Say: God hath forbidden unto you Negation, and whatsoever is related thereunto; and hath enjoined upon you – and upon all things – Affirmation, and whatsoever is related thereunto, that perchance on the Day of Resurrection ye may follow God, then be guided aright by His Command. Say: All bow down before Him.
Know thou that the very existence of Negation would not, in itself, be deemed worthy of mention, were it not for the mention made of it by Affirmation: for were the Tree of Truth, on the Day of Resurrection, to behold none who was not a believer, he would not send down any mention of him. Whatsoever is mentioned – or hath been mentioned – is for the sake of the exaltation of Affirmation, and the evanescence of Negation, not other than this. The aforesaid two substances, for example, have been prohibited for the sake of the preservation of the believing soul, not on their own account. Behold thou likewise in all the degrees of existence the ocean of His bounty; and place thou reliance in thy Lord in every matter, for He is the best of preservers.


Gate Eight of the Ninth Unity: Concerning the prohibition of opium, intoxicants, and drugs absolutely
The substance of this gate is that all the manifestations of other than love have ever been, and ever shall be, aspects of other than truth; while all the manifestations of love have ever been, and ever shall be, aspects of the Truth. It hath been forbidden to make use of intoxicants, and whatsoever is adjudged a drug, absolutely, so that thou mayest purify thyself from whatsoever is accounted “for other than God,” exchanging it, in cases of need, for exquisite delicacies and goodly bounties, which have ever been, and ever shall be, aspects of the Tree of Love.
This rule is valid of the whole as of the part: even as the avoidance of a single non-believing person is as the avoidance of all the non-believers. Howbeit the Lord of the world – exalted and glorified be He – hath under all conditions revealed Himself in such a manner that the whole of existence boweth down before Him; and all are desirous of His love, and ascending up in His obedience; nor is there a single atom but that, in its innermost being, it worshippeth Him, and, in its own tongue, uttereth His praise. Notwithstanding, in this Revelation, aught that is not a manifestation of the Tree of Love hath not been, nor is it, beloved; while aught that is such, hath been, and is, beloved.
Permission hath nevertheless been granted in the Revelation for the practice of certain crafts which are calculated to meet the need of the people thereof for certain of these commodities: and this is to the same degree to which, in every Revelation, the people thereof have been granted permission to show forbearance unto the manifestations of other than truth: whence haply a fruit may be garnered from their existence, through believing in the True One: inasmuch as the capacity to do so existeth in every person, should he not be shut out as by a veil – even by his own self – from doing so.
Seek ye therefore refuge from all that God loveth not, in God, your All-Merciful Lord, if it be your love to prosper.


Gate Nine of the Ninth Unity
concerning the prohibition of congregational prayer, save in the Prayer for the Dead, which do ye perform together, but with the intention of performing it separately.
The substance of this gate is that whereas in congregational prayer it is established that the imam must unfailingly be a Letter of Affirmation; and whereas at the end of each Revelation, all parade themselves as manifestations of Affirmation, not of Negation – yet at the beginning of the Revelation it emergeth that they were after all manifestations of Negation: for this reason hath the practice been forbidden, so that none may be in the position of having worshipped the Lord for other than God. Should someone today have believed in God and His Verses, and in the Tree of Truth and His manifestations, and ere this have prayed behind a person who hath not as yet confessed belief, it is incumbent upon him to repeat them.
This is among those laws that bear upon the reality of the matter as it truly is: inasmuch as the imam was on that day for other than God: for had he not been so, he would not have become so; while the one who performed prayer with him was for God: for had he not been so, he would not today have become a believer. This is one of those Davidic laws that have been decreed with respect to the hidden, not to the manifest: for had it concerned only the manifest, permission would have been granted – yet this permission is the very point at issue, for why then would one have been so imperceptive as to choose for himself an imam who should turn out to be for other than God?
Howbeit, in the Prayer for the Dead permission hath been granted, for this is a question rather of honouring the believer: whence the greater the multitude assembled to perform this prayer for him, the more beloved hath it been, and is it, in the eyes of the Lord. Yet let no one stand before the rest; and let all, in their several ranks – in upright posture – perform the prayer for him, with the intention of doing so separately.
Yet consider – with respect to the congregational form – how many congregational prayers, from the beginning of Islam until the appearance of the Point of the Bayan, have been performed – nay, it would be impossible to estimate their number! Yet, praise be to God that He let no one pray with the Manifestation of His own Self, in His Latter Manifestation, who should turn out to be for other than God – and this notwithstanding that all had been performing prayer in His Name, and praying by His word. Behold thou the level of the people! – that for all their protestations of love, and expectations of “deliverance,” not one of them, after His appearance, should be honoured to perform with Him a single prayer – a prayer such as, in company with even the lowliest of God’s creatures, he performeth five times each night and day – nor be favoured with this bounty until at length the Divine law be lifted from him.
Be thou watchful of the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, lest thou be shut out as by a veil from Him in such a fashion: to wit, that night and day ye pass your time in the hope of His remembrance, and lull your hearts with the thought of the laws promised at the time of His appearance: then all at once He arise, suddenly: until the time arrive for Him to grant leave for the lifting of the previous laws, at which time ye shall all be deprived, and left, one and all, without a portion of the fruit of your existence. Notwithstanding, that Ocean of Bounty is patient: whence if there be in His knowledge but a single soul who, on the Day of Resurrection, shall be faithful unto the Covenant of God, assuredly He shall tarry, until the latter fulfil his pledge.
Yet it may chance that the Day of Resurrection befall, and thou be sunk in slumber; and even after thou be awakened, thou become shut out therefrom as by a veil: as in the case, for example, of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – Who, after He had been made manifest, awoke those servants who were within the fold of the Evangel; yet they awoke not, and remain unto this day immersed in slumber. For it behoved Him but to announce “I am the promised Ahmad” – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him, and to establish His proof by means of those Verses which the Lord had sent down upon Him – not by means of satisfying whatever arbitrary request anyone might wish to make of Him: for were this the criterion, no proof in any Revelation would ever have been denied.
Consider thou the Furqan, of whose truth thou art persuaded, and the degree of blame it layeth upon those servants who requested of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – the various fanciful matters they requested, having the audacity even to ask of Him “… bring forth God and the angels in a host” – than which there could have been no greater transgression on their part – in making such a request – inasmuch as the Lord is sanctified above all such depictions; while whatsoever is possible to His creatures is unworthy even to be mentioned in that sacred court of His, how much less that He should realize it in the world of being.
Yet to this day the waiters still await: and how like it is that the Resurrection of Him Whom God shall make manifest shall be set on foot, and still they shall await, if the Lord raise not up a potentate who shall exercise a compelling sway over His believing people of the Bayan; else shall the grace of the whole of existence be his. Were the means of Revelation otherwise, assuredly the Lord would have revealed them unto His Apostle – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him. Nay, it behoveth the people themselves to become manifestations of the Cause in actual practice; while the Source is charged but with the issuance of the command. For example, it was the part of God to say “… to God, as a duty upon the people, is owed a pilgrimage unto the House;” while the exaltation thereof was realized by the people, through their obedience unto God’s command. Otherwise, in the eyes of the percipient and subtle observer, that same glory which hath inhered ever in the Cause of God is inherent in it still, irrespective of whether all obey His bidding, or whether all omit to do so.
Do ye then pray to God, your All-Merciful Lord, that haply, on the Day of Resurrection, ye may be persuaded of the truth of His Verses.


Gate Ten of the Ninth Unity: On the purification of the earth of the souls
The substance of this gate is this, that everything hath its own kind of purification according to the divine knowledge, and that all would be purified by the remembrance of God, should they recognise Him Whom God shall make manifest. As to the hearts, they would not be purified except through faith in the Three Letters, and the spirits except through faith in the Four Letters, and the souls except through faith in the Six Letters, and the essential bodies except through faith in the last Six Letters.
And all purification lieth in the declarative word of the divine unity, by whose help thou art empowered to purify these Signs of Unity (19) from the hellish signs in Their shadow. In like manner the same word enableth thee to witness affirmation and non-affirmation in all things, that thou would be able to purify them all.
For example, should the handkerchief in thy hand be the least spoiled, its purification would not be realised except through that which is destined in its own level. In like manner behold all things, from the sublime summit of existence till the last level of being, so that thou may not be veiled from the remedy of any affliction.
Know thou that in the Bayan purification is regarded as the most acceptable means for attaining nearness unto God and as the most meritorious of all deeds. Thus purge thou thine ear that thou mayest hear no mention besides God, and purge thine eye that it behold naught except God, and thy conscience that it perceive naught other than God, and thy tongue that it proclaim nothing but God, and thy hand to write naught but the words of God, and thy knowledge that it comprehend naught except God, and thy heart that it entertain no wish save God, and in like manner purge all thine acts and thy pursuits that thou mayest be nurtured in the paradise of pure love, and perchance mayest attain the presence of Him Whom God shall make manifest, adorned with a purity which He highly cherisheth, and be sanctified from whosoever hath turned away from Him and doth not support Him. Thus shalt thou manifest a purity that shall profit thee.
Know thou that every ear which hearkeneth unto His Words with true faith shall be immune from the fire. Thus the believer, through his recognition of Him will appreciate the transcendent character of His heavenly Words, will whole-heartedly choose Him over others, and will refuse to incline his affections towards those who disbelieve in Him. Whatever one gaineth in the life to come is but the fruit of this faith. Indeed any man whose eye gazeth upon His Words with true faith well deserveth Paradise; and one whose conscience beareth witness unto His Words with true faith shall abide in Paradise and attain the presence of God; and one whose tongue giveth utterance to His Words with true faith shall have his abode in Paradise, wherein he will be seized with ecstasy in praise and glorification of God, the Ever-Abiding, Whose revelations of glory never end and the reviving breaths of Whose holiness never fail.
Every hand which setteth down His Words with true faith shall be filled by God, both in this world and in the next, with things that are highly prized; and every breast which committeth His Words to memory, God shall cause, if it were that of a believer, to be filled with His love; and every heart which cherisheth the love of His Words and manifesteth in itself the signs of true faith when His Name is mentioned, and exemplifieth the words, ‘their hearts are thrilled with awe at the mention of God’, that heart will become the object of the glances of divine favour and on the Day of Resurrection will be highly praised by God.
Know thou that the purification of thy soul is not merely this, that thou recitest the words that are revealed by God, inasmuch as the root beginning of thy faith is confirmed by the word “There is none other God but God”, together with mentioning the Manifestations of the First Unity, and that of the Bayan. Yet the words other than the words of the sublime paradise pertaineth to the first letter of negation, who at the time of Revelation, regardeth himself to be one of the purifiers of the earth of the souls. Nay, rather, the meaning of purification of the souls is this, that thou must purge thyself from whatsoever that is for one other than God, and attain unto whatsoever that is for God.
Should the Revelation of the Bayan reach a stage in which there would be no longer any mention of being for the one other than God, then it would be permissible unto thee to recite not the words other than the words of the sublime paradise. Wert thou to desire to traverse throughout all thy life in the sea of pure love and the sublime paradise, thou wouldst possess sufficient provisions for thy journey. For should all the beings tread the path with only this single word “God is the Most Mighty”, they would assuredly reach their destiny, which is naught but Him Whom God shall make manifest, inasmuch as he is the One Who is manifest in the manifestation of this word.
And know thou the negation of each Revelation entereth fire in the Next Revelation and not during the Revelation itself. For example, the negation of Gospel became manifest in the Revelation of the Qur’an, and the negation of the Qur’an in the Dispensation of the Bayan, universally and not empirically. Likewise, the negation of the Bayan will not be manifested except through the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, inasmuch as in that Day all shall claim to be amongst His letters of the affirmation, and wholly clear of those of negation. But ‘well is it when the touchstone of test appeareth,’ inasmuch as at that time all shall be purified in such wise that the heavens, the earth, and that which lieth between them, will all bow down before the majesty of such universal separation. Thou hast witnessed this in the Revelation of the Bayan, and shouldst thou be present in that Day, thou wouldst behold that all the fishes of the ocean of the Bayan owe their lives to that supreme invigorating Water, and yet they would be veiled from Him. Purify ye then your souls with the utmost of your true power.

title: BB00015: Dala’il-i-Sab’ih (The Seven Proofs—Persian)
text:
Part 1: “Praise be to God, besides Whom there…”
In the Name of God, the Most Unique, the Most Unique!
Praise be to God, besides Whom there is no God, the Most Unique, the Most Unique. Verily all glory from God be upon Him Whom God shall make manifest and then upon His faithful ones, forever and ever.
To continue: I have examined the letter you have written. Were one to desire a detailed exposition of proofs establishing this Manifestation, the tablets of creation and possibility could not bear it. Yet the essence of speech and the core of purpose is this: There has never been, nor shall there ever be, any doubt that God has eternally existed in the independence and majesty of His sacred Being, and will forever exist in the inaccessibility and exaltation of His holy Essence. No thing hath known Him as He deserveth to be known, and no thing hath praised Him as He deserveth to be praised. He hath been sanctified above all names and exalted above all similitudes. All things are known through Him, while He is too glorious to be known through aught else. For His creation there hath been no beginning, nor shall there be an end, lest His bounty be interrupted. To the number of all that is possible in the realm of contingent being, He hath sent forth Messengers and revealed Books, and will continue to do so.
If thou sailest upon the sea of names, know that all are known through God, or are attributed to His servants. Everything thou seest hath been created by His Will. How then can it serve as proof of His unity? His existence itself is proof of His oneness, and the existence of all things is proof that they are His creation. This is the proof of wisdom for those who sail upon the sea of truth.
And if thou sailest upon the sea of creation, know that the First Remembrance, which is the Primal Will of God, may be likened unto the sun, which God, exalted be His glory, hath created through His all-pervading power. From a beginning that hath no beginning, He hath made it manifest in every Dispensation through His Will, and unto an end that hath no end, He shall continue to make it manifest through His decree. Know thou that its example is like unto the sun—if it should rise unto infinity, there would still be but one sun, and if it should set unto infinity, there would still be but one sun. It is He Who hath been manifest in all the Messengers, and He Who hath spoken in all the Books.
He hath had no beginning, for through Him doth “the beginning” begin; and He hath had no end, for through Him doth “the end” end. It is He Who in this wondrous Cycle, which is now in its thirteen thousandth year, is known as the Point of the Bayan, and as the First Creation in the days of Adam, and as Noah in his day, and as Abraham in his day, and as Moses in his day, and as Jesus in his day, and as Muhammad the Apostle of God in His day, and the Point of the Bayan in His day, and He Whom God shall make manifest in His day, and He Whom God shall make manifest after Him Whom God shall make manifest in His day, have been known. And this is the mystery of the words of the Apostle of God aforetime: “As for the Prophets, verily I am they,” for the One manifest in all is but a single Sun.
And this is the meaning of the tradition concerning the Proof, wherein al-Sadiq hath said:
He saith not “Let him behold this,” for that which made the Messengers to be Messengers is in Him, and that which made the Books to be Books is from Him. The essence of the matter is that God, exalted be His glory, in His consummate wisdom, hath in the Dispensation of Muhammad, the Apostle of God, ordained the Furqan to be the Proof. This was a bounty not vouchsafed to any people before Muhammad, the Apostle of God—that a verse from the Book of God should serve as proof for all who dwell on earth, demonstrate the powerlessness of all, and establish the power of God.
From the day of the revelation of the Furqan until the day of the manifestation of the Point of the Bayan, one thousand two hundred and seventy years elapsed, during which all were nurtured by this proof until they became ready for the appearance of the Sun of Truth. And whatsoever proof other than this they mention—by their own admission the Most Great Book is greater, and the Greater sufficeth in lieu of the lesser, and mention of aught else beareth no fruit in the sight of the All-Wise, the All-Seeing. This is if I leave thee to what thou hast heard and am forbearing with thee in argument. Otherwise, this is established and manifest—prove aught else! Think not that this sufficeth not in place of all miracles. Nay, by God! It hath sufficed and will suffice in place of all miracles.
Seven conclusive proofs have I taught thee regarding this matter, each of which alone sufficeth as evidence unto the fair-minded.
First, if the verses of the Qur’an were not greater than all the miracles of the Prophets, how were their Books abrogated by it while the Qur’an alone remained? This is a conclusive and compelling proof that this evidence was and is greater than the rod of Moses and similar physical proofs.
Second, in the religion thou now professest, thou hast no escape, according to the decree of the Qur’an, from saying that none but God can reveal a verse. And now that thou beholdest, thou hast no escape from declaring it to be from God, for had it been possible for any created thing, during the course of one thousand two hundred and seventy years someone would have produced a verse. Yet thou hast witnessed the powerlessness of all. Behold how perfect hath been the divine favor unto all the people of the Qur’an, that God, exalted be His glory, hath blocked for them all avenues of doubt, that when they witness verses, no thought of their being from other than God might cross their minds. For He hath revealed that none hath power to bring forth even a single utterance. If one believeth and is certain of this decree, no thought can enter his heart that the verses of the Bayan are from other than God. Indeed, he would not even take up the pen to attempt it, for according to his own faith it is impossible, let alone, God forbid, that he should manifest uncertainty or denial.
I swear by God’s holy Essence, exalted be His glory, that His favor towards the believers in the Qur’an hath been so perfect that had anyone pondered upon the proof of the Qur’an, no thought contrary to faith would have occurred to him upon witnessing a single verse of the Bayan, much less that he should doubt or manifest anything less than certitude. Be fair—what difference is there between the time when thou first knew thyself and became adherent to thy religion through the proof of the Qur’an, and when thou looked upon the Bayan yet did not believe? There is no doubt thou never saw the Prophet and seest no miracle save this Qur’an. If thou entered thy religion unconsciously, why didst thou enter? And if with insight, what is the difference between when thou saw the Qur’an, became convinced of all others’ powerlessness and embraced the religion of God’s Messenger, and when thou looked upon the Bayan yet remained unconvinced? Will there be any proof for thee before God?
God will ask thee: “By what means didst thou enter Islam?” Other than saying “through the Qur’an,” thou hast seen no other proof. By this same means doth God establish His proof against thee—that just as thou embraced His Messenger’s religion upon witnessing His Book, it was incumbent upon thee to embrace the true Faith upon witnessing the Book of the Point of the Bayan, for thou hast not seen the Messenger of God, and yet thou hast become faithful through the Book itself. Even as thou didst behold a verse from the Bayan, by the same proof through which thou didst become faithful to the religion of the Qur’an, it is incumbent upon thee to believe in those verses.
God hath never sent any Messenger whose books published before Him would be proof in themselves. This is unique to the Point of the Bayan, that if He should write a book in the mode of verses to one of the believers in the Qur’an or to others, the proof becometh complete and perfect through the Book itself upon beholding a single verse thereof, if the observer be possessed of insight and understanding. Otherwise, he is not and hath never been worthy of the decree, for in most instances God hath declared that it is for a people who believe and understand, not for the majority of mankind who are as naught.
These are two proofs from the seven proofs whereby I have established that the verses themselves are greater than all the miracles of the Prophets. And secondly, that none but God is capable of revealing a verse. Behold how God doth test mankind! Had He bestowed upon the Point of the Bayan the like of what He bestowed upon Moses, perchance not a single one of the believers in the Qur’an would have remained veiled and they would have believed. Yet now that God hath bestowed what is greater than that—as proven by the religion of all Muslims which is established and demonstrated—how many souls are being tested and cast into trials! This is naught but the result of their failure to ponder and reflect upon their own religion. Otherwise, upon beholding or hearing a single verse, it would prove greater than the miracles of all the Prophets.
The third proof is that the manifestation of power in these verses appears in a manner that endureth, unlike aught else. Think not this is a simple matter; rather this is a creation more magnificent than the creation of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them. Consider the letters of the alphabet which all mankind employ in speech. God, exalted be His glory, hath caused them to appear from an unlettered Person in such wise that all who are on earth are powerless to produce the like thereof naturally. This is naught but the pure manifestation of power and the mere expression of grandeur. Yet since most of mankind dwell in limitation, they perceive not the greatness and majesty of the verses. How often they perceive only limited aspects, and fail to become enlightened by this conclusive proof and demonstrated evidence which shall endure until the Day of Resurrection.
Fourth, the verses themselves and the Book suffice in place of other miracles. Thus for one who believeth in the Qur’an there is no escape save to acknowledge its sufficiency, even as God hath revealed in the Surih of the Spider:
And in the Qur’an, in most instances, those things which they demanded of the Messenger of God according to their own desires were rejected. As the Divine Revelation declareth in the Surih of Bani-Isra’il: “And they say: We shall not believe in thee until thou cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth; or thou have a garden of date palms and vines, and cause rivers to gush forth in their midst abundantly; or thou cause the heaven to fall upon us in fragments, as thou hast claimed; or thou bring God and the angels before us face to face; or thou have a house adorned with gold; or thou ascend up into heaven; and even then we will not believe in thine ascension until thou bring down for us a book that we can read.’ Say: Glory be to my Lord! Am I aught but a mortal messenger?”’
Now judge with fairness. The Arabs spoke thus, and thou desirest something else according to thy fancy. What difference is there between thee and them? If thou wouldst reflect a little, it behooveth the servant to be convinced by that which God hath made a proof unto him, not by that which he desireth. And if it were a matter of desire, no one on earth would remain an unbeliever, for every people would believe when their desires were fulfilled by the Messenger of God. God forbid that thou shouldst make anything a proof according to thy own desire. Rather, take as proof that which God hath made a proof. Thou believest in God for His good-pleasure; how then wouldst thou make something a proof of thy faith which was not and is not His good-pleasure?
As is warned in the Qur’an concerning those servants who believe not in the signs, as God hath revealed in the Surih of Nahl [the bee]: “As to those who believe not in the signs of God, God will not guide them, and they shall have a grievous torment. It is they who forge falsehood that believe not in the signs of God, and it is they who are the liars.” Be thou discerning in every Manifestation, for it is here that most people slip from the path and enter from the paradise of faith into the fire of unfaith. Know thou that whenever a proof is established from God, it sufficeth as evidence, even as God hath revealed in the Qur’an through the tongue of Moses: “We have indeed brought thee a sign from thy Lord: and peace be on him who followeth guidance!” If the proof of Moses and Aaron unto Pharaoh had not been sufficient through a single sign, God would not have revealed it thus. Know then that a single sign sufficeth as proof.

title: BB00015: Dala’il-i-Sab’ih (The Seven Proofs—Persian)
section: Part 2: “And fifthly, God in the Qur’an hath not…”
text:
Part 2: “And fifthly, God in the Qur’an hath not…”
And fifthly, God in the Qur’an hath not adduced any evidence for the reality of the Messenger of God other than verses. As He hath revealed: “Say: ʿIf mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur’an, they could not produce the like thereof, even if they backed up each other.”’ And if these miracles which are now related in books had any significance with God, He would have used them as proof for the reality of the Messenger of God. And even where He hath mentioned them, the divine purpose was not to use them as proof, such as “The Hour draweth nigh and the moon is cleft asunder.” Know ye that God alone knoweth the meaning of His utterances, even as is attested by the blessed verse, “None knoweth its interpretation except God and those firmly grounded in knowledge.”
Sixthly, We speak to thee now through the evidence of reason: If someone today wishes to enter the religion of Islam, is the divine proof complete upon him or not? If thou sayest it is not, how then shall God punish him after death, and why in this life is he judged as a non-Muslim? And if thou sayest the proof is complete, by what means is it so? If through that which thou relatest, he heareth mere words which do not constitute proof for him. And if thou sayest through the Qur’an, this indeed is a sound and evident proof.
Consider now the Revelation of the Bayan: had the people of the Qur’an applied to themselves the same arguments they use against those who differ from their faith, not a single soul would have remained veiled, and all would have attained salvation on the Day of Resurrection. And if a Christian says “I understand not the Qur’an, how then can it be a proof for me?”, this cannot be accepted from him. Similarly, when certain souls say regarding the Bayan “We comprehend not the eloquence of its verses, how can it be proof for us?”, say to such a common person: By what means didst thou embrace the religion of Islam? Thou sawest neither the Prophet nor witnessed any miracle. If thou didst so without understanding, why didst thou do it? And if through the authority of the Qur’an, was it because thou heardst from the learned and assured ones who confessed their inability, or was it that at the mere mention of God’s name thou wert naturally moved to submission and humility—which is one of the greatest signs of love and recognition? The proof that was decisive for thee then, apply it now to thyself regarding the Bayan.
Seventhly, all believe that God hath been and ever shall be All-Knowing and All-Powerful over all things. Therefore, when one claimeth to be His Proof and manifesteth evidence thereof, and the Almighty, despite His power, raiseth up none to refute him, this itself is proof that such a one is from God and that his assertion is pleasing unto Him. For His acquiescence and failure to manifest opposition, despite His ability to do so, prove that the claimant is from Him and acceptable in His sight. And I counsel thee regarding the Bayan to argue in support of each Revelation using the proofs specific to that Revelation, not through other means, for that would be unseemly and improper. For example, when the Messenger of God, peace be upon Him and His family, wished to establish His prophethood, He did so through the verses of God. If thou be a man of valor, then produce thou a verse as well, else resort not to other means of argumentation.
It is not for you to arise in opposition. Consider all the odes that the Arabs composed at the first appearance of the Messenger of God—did they yield any fruit? If they wished to arise in opposition, they should have spoken in the same manner as the verses, not in the form of odes. In every Dispensation, observe this principle, for there has never been and never will be any other path for those possessed of wisdom and understanding. It leads only to regret in the end, for the divine proof endures while that which arises in opposition through other means, being of human origin and not beyond human capacity, perishes. The proof of God remains, and opposing it brings no benefit.
Know that there is no valid means of opposition other than this. If imprisonment were proof of illegitimacy, then the Prophet Joseph was imprisoned among the Prophets, and Musa ibn Ja’far among the successors, yet both were proofs of God. Likewise, other circumstances do not negate authenticity—you have heard the story of Zachariah among the Prophets and the Prince of Martyrs among the successors, yet both were divine proofs. These examples are given that you might gain insight into these matters.
As for your saying that you cannot attain certainty between yourself and God, or else you would believe—know that what you imagine between yourself and God is mere fancy. For five hundred years they were nurtured in the Psalms until they reached perfection. Then when Jesus appeared, only a few who possessed wisdom and insight concerning the Psalms believed, while the rest remained behind. Yet all of them considered themselves right before God. It was not that they wished to oppose truth deliberately—like your own state, where your intention is not to oppose truth but rather you wish to attain certainty so that you might believe.
Consider David’s people to be like yourself—had they been certain that Jesus was the same Prophet of whom David had given tidings, not a single one would have entertained thoughts other than belief, let alone rejected faith. Yet from the day of David’s appearance until the beginning of this Dispensation, two thousand two hundred and seventy years have passed, and still some followers of the Psalms remain in their religion, imagining themselves right before God. Now see how that which they claim between themselves and God is as nothing in the eyes of the Christians, let alone in the sight of the Creator of all. Likewise consider the people of Moses, who were nurtured for a thousand years before David until they reached perfection.
And when that which Moses had promised them regarding the appearance of Jesus was fulfilled after David, only a few possessed of wisdom and insight believed in Jesus. And the rest also made the utmost effort, and between themselves and God they wished to believe in what Moses had said. But they did not attain certainty and remained thus, as they remain until now, still awaiting the Prophet of whom Moses gave tidings. Between themselves and God they consider themselves correct. Now observe how utterly worthless is their claim that between themselves and God they were not certain that Jesus was that Prophet of whom Moses gave tidings—how insignificant this is in the presence of the Creator of all, or His witnesses.
Then consider the people of Christ who were nurtured for five hundred years, like the people of Moses. When they had reached perfection in their religion, God made manifest Muhammad, the Messenger of God (peace be upon Him). This despite the fact that Jesus had taken a covenant from His people regarding belief in Him at His appearance, for this had been the practice of all the Messengers—no Messenger was ever sent except that He took from His people a covenant to believe in the subsequent Messenger. And after the appearance of the Messenger of God, you have heard what befell that Holy Being, Who declared: “No Prophet has been persecuted as I have been persecuted.” Yet all the people of truth at that time, who were the people of Christ, were awaiting His appearance and supplicating night and day for it, and were obeying the monks of their religion, believing these would be the ones to remind the people about the Messenger of God. Yet after He appeared, for seven years, aside from the Commander of the Faithful and a small number, none believed in Him, even though all existence was working for His sake.
Here let Me teach you a mystery of which you have not yet been aware: Observe the deeds of the followers of each Prophet, whose source is from His Word, which in truth belongs to Him. And since He is the Mirror of God, nothing is seen in Him except God. Thus all becomes “for God” if the deed is purely for His sake. And just as the source of all deeds of the followers of each Prophet is from Him, the return of those deeds is also to the subsequent Prophet. In the Day of the appearance of the Messenger of God, all were working for that same Soul, but none perceived the reality, else they would not have turned away from their Beloved.
Observe how they have exalted a mere donkey which Christians imagine belonged to Jesus, and how they ascend to it in crowds, seeking nearness through this act. Yet when one like the Messenger of God appears, for seven years they do not believe in Him. Now behold where the weight of people’s deeds truly lies, when if the people of Christ had attained certainty that this Prophet is indeed the Promised Ahmad, not a single Christian would have remained veiled. From the Messenger of God—and what monks there were who practiced austerities to attain the good pleasure of God! And for Him for Whom they labored, He appeared, yet they believed not in Him, saying “Thou art not He of Whom Jesus gave tidings.”
Think not that they were not cautious in their religion, or that they did not wish to believe in the truth. Rather, their lack of faith and certitude stemmed from their extreme caution in their religion. In their relationship with God, they all considered themselves strivers and righteous ones, such that had they truly been convinced that the Messenger of God was the same Prophet of Whom Jesus had given tidings, they all would have believed in less than the twinkling of an eye. Now observe how the self and the deity they claim, in the sight of even a single follower of God’s Messenger, is as nothing. How much more so in the sight of the Creator of all, His Messenger, the martyrs of His Faith, and the proofs of His Cause! And thus does the matter become confused to all. And yet they all believe they act for God in their relationship with Him. However, no more than seventy Christians believed in God’s Messenger, as recorded in one tradition. The fault lies with their divines, for had they believed, the rest of creation would have believed.
Now observe how the Christian divines became learned in order to save the followers of Jesus, yet they themselves became the cause of preventing people from faith and guidance. Now go and become learned again! All the followers of Jesus obeyed their divines in order to attain salvation on the Day of Resurrection, yet this very following caused them to enter the fire on the Day of the Manifestation of God’s Messenger, as it veiled them from One like unto God’s Messenger. Now go and become a follower! Nay, by God! Neither become learned nor follow without insight, for both perish on the Day of Resurrection. Rather, become learned with insight, and follow God through the true learned one with insight. You see countless learned ones in every religion without insight, and you see countless followers in every religion without insight. Gain some insight, have mercy upon your own soul, turn not away from proof and evidence, and make not proof and evidence subject to your desires. Rather, establish them according to what God has established.
Know that being learned in itself is not noble, nor is being a follower in itself. Rather, that knowledge is noble which accords with God’s good pleasure, and that following is noble which accords with God’s good pleasure. And do not regard it as an imaginary matter, for it is the good-pleasure of His Messenger.
Consider again the followers of Jesus, who all sought the good-pleasure of God, yet not one attained unto the good-pleasure of God’s Messenger, which is identical with God’s good-pleasure, except those servants who believed in Him. From the appearance of Jesus until the appearance of the Point of the Bayan, one thousand seven hundred and seventy years have elapsed, during which all the followers of Jesus have imagined that they were acting for God’s sake in their relationship with Him. Yet those who attained unto God’s good-pleasure were only those seventy persons who, in the time of God’s Messenger, believed in Him. The rest imagine they are acting in God’s good-pleasure while they are acting contrary to it.
And think not that these people act with insight in their religion. Rather, every soul follows whatever religion they were born into. You see rarely does a Christian become Muslim, or a Muslim become Christian—this is nearly impossible. Rather, your nobility lies in having been born into a religion that was true in the sight of God, not because you yourself possessed insight—though you should have possessed it, but since grace was not granted, you did not.
Similarly, consider the Manifestation of God’s Messenger (peace be upon Him)—one thousand two hundred and seventy years passed until the first appearance of the Bayan, during which He made all await the appearance of the Qa’im of the family of Muhammad, as He said:

“If there remained but one day in the world, God would prolong that day until He raises up a man from among my descendants whose name shall be My name”

- to the end of the tradition. And since all the deeds of Islam began from God’s Messenger, it is fitting that they should return to Him. And God made Him manifest with the same proof whereby He made God’s Messenger manifest, such that no believer in the Furqan (Qur’an) could doubt His reality. For it is revealed in the Qur’an that none but God can reveal verses, and for one thousand two hundred and seventy years all the people of the Furqan witnessed that no one came who could produce such verses.
