Verily, Thou art the Inaccessible, the Mighty.
O my God! I behold in existence naught but two trees—the tree of negation and the tree of affirmation. I witness before Thee and before all things that whosoever hath not believed as Thy Beloved believed is of the tree of negation in Thy sight, having no mention, while whosoever hath believed as did Thy Beloved Muhammad—Thy blessings be upon Him and upon His Manifestations—is of the tree of affirmation. Therefore hast Thou exalted it, glorified it, elevated it and magnified it, until it reached the ultimate bounds of Thy grace, when Thou didst bring forth the Tree of the Bayan.
I testify before Thee and before all things that whosoever believeth not as the One of the Seven Letters believed is, in Thy sight, of the tree of negation—he shall perish by Thy command in such wise that his own self shall not remember his self, his essence shall disavow itself, and his ego shall prevail against his ego. And whosoever believeth as the One of the Seven Letters believed is of Thy tree of affirmation, which Thou hast exalted, glorified, beautified, magnified, given sovereignty to and made manifest above all things. There is no end to Thy bounties toward it, nor to Thy generosity in its faith and attributes, until the Day of Resurrection when Thou shalt manifest what Thou dost manifest. Then whosoever believeth not as the Manifestation of Thy Self believeth on that Day is a letter of negation, even though he be among the highest manifestations of affirmation in the Bayan. And whosoever believeth as He believeth is of Thy tree of affirmation, even though he had been of the tree of negation in the Bayan. Thus dost Thou bring forth from the fire whom Thou willest, and cause to enter Paradise whom Thou willest, and bring forth from Paradise whom Thou willest, and cause to enter the fire howsoever Thou willest.
Have mercy then, O my God, through Thy mercy, upon all who have believed in the Bayan, that Thou mayest not cause them to enter the fire of negation, but rather hold them fast by Thy might to enter the paradise of affirmation, for the former is the source of all evil in Thy sight while the latter is the source of all good before Thee. Preserve me, O my God, from that which Thou lovest not, for it is of the tree of negation in Thy sight. Strengthen me, O my God, in that which Thou lovest, for it is of the tree of affirmation before Thee. Forgive, O my God, every male and female who entereth beneath the shade of the tree of Thy love, and judge, O my God, whosoever entereth not, for that is justice for the former and this is grace for the latter. There is no power nor strength except through Thee, and unto Thee do all return.

title: BB00148: Du’a’ ’ala’n-Nafy (prayer of negation)
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy!
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy First-ness, which is exalted above all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Transcendence, which is inaccessible above all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Ever-Turning Grace, which is sanctified above all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Steadfastness, which is supreme above all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Omnipotence, which is dominant above all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Life, which pervadeth all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Creative Power, which endureth above all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thine Eternity, which excelleth above all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Creative Force, which is manifest above all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy All-Mercifulness, which is exalted above all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Cultivating Power, which ruleth above all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Glorified Being, which is adorned above all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Witness, which is established above all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thine Eternality, which is exalted above all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Safeguarding Power, which shineth above all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Purity, which is purifying above all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Outwardness, which is exalted beyond all things, to protect from the Tree of Negation and all that pertaineth unto it, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy transcendent exaltation which is high above all things, to restore from the tree of negation and all that pertaineth thereunto through Thy power whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy self-sufficiency which is independent of all things, to restore from the tree of negation and all that pertaineth thereunto through Thy power whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy singleness which standeth unique above all things, to restore from the tree of negation and all that pertaineth thereunto through Thy power whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy self-subsistence which standeth firm above all things, to restore from the tree of negation and all that pertaineth thereunto through Thy power whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy grandeur which shineth resplendent above all things, to restore from the tree of negation and all that pertaineth thereunto through Thy power whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy subtlety which is exalted above all things, to restore from the tree of negation and all that pertaineth thereunto through Thy power whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy sovereignty which is elevated above all things, to restore from the tree of negation and all that pertaineth thereunto through Thy power whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy radiant attribute which illumineth above all things, to restore from the tree of negation and all that pertaineth thereunto through Thy power whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy providence which transcendeth all things, to restore from the tree of negation and all that pertaineth thereunto through Thy power whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy guidance which is sanctified above all things, to restore from the tree of negation and all that pertaineth thereunto through Thy power whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy divine nature which is exalted above all things, to restore from the tree of negation and all that pertaineth thereunto through Thy power whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy ruby-like essence which shineth resplendent above all things, to restore from the tree of negation and all that pertaineth thereunto through Thy power whatsoever Thou willest. Verily, Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily Thou art the Creator of negation and affirmation, the Sovereign of fire and of light, the King of extinction and of abiding. Thou hast loved to cause this to perish and that to endure; to remove this and to bring forth that; to abase this and to succour that; to humble this and to exalt that; to cast down this and to raise up that; to rend this asunder by every fire, and to bestow favour upon that through every light. How exalted, O my God, is Thy power, and how penetrating, O my Beloved, is Thy will! Thou hast ever been dominant above all contingent beings, manifest above all existences, exalted over all who are in the kingdoms of earth and heaven, inaccessible above all who dwell in the realms of names and attributes, transcendent above all created things, sovereign over those in the dominions of beginning and ending, possessed of mastery over those in the realms of origin and finality. No portion hath he whom Thou hast destroyed and forsaken, upon whom Thou hast sent down Thy vengeance, whom Thou hast seized with Thy might and Thy severity. Verily Thou art the most mighty in might and the most severe in retribution.
Nor hath there been any diminution for him whom Thou hast willed to uplift and to honour, to bestow upon and to exalt, to enrobe with glory and to invest with authority, to manifest and to endow with dominion, to grant ascendancy over whatsoever … of the rebellious. Verily Thou art the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.
O God! Cut away whatever has sprung from the tree of fire and is attributed to it, even if it appears in temples of light, for that does not belong to it but returns to that from which it began. And […] O God, all that You have loved of the Manifestations of affirmation, and cut away from them whatever contains the poisons of fire, and purify us, for it originated from it and returns to it. Take away whatever You have witnessed of the attributes of light in the fire and join it to its tree and […] between it and its people until You cut it away from them and cause us to enter beneath the shade of the tree of affirmation, for these have no light and those have no fire.
O my God! If You witness in these any attributes of light, cut them away and join them to the tree of Your love as befits them. And if You witness in those what You have not loved for them, and it is of the fire, cut it away from them and join it to its tree, for that is not deserving after Your grace upon them and toward them in the Mother Book. Glory be to You! There is no God but You. I have loved none but You, desired none but You, intended none but You. We prostrate to none but Your face, worship none but Your Essence, trust in none but You, hope for none but Your grace, fear none but Your justice, ask from none but Your forgiveness, and rely on none but Your bountiful giving and favor.
O God! Send down at this time, at the dawn of Friday of the month which […] You have attributed to Yourself, upon […] and the people of my love, and those who follow what You have revealed in the Bayan, that which befits the loftiness of Your sanctity and the exaltation of Your elevation, for what befits Your Essence befits none other than You, and what befits others does not befit Your Essence. You are the Self-Sufficient and all else are poor before You.
O God! Send down Your mercy at this time upon all who have believed in You and Your verses, for You are the Best of those who show mercy. And bestow Your blessings, O God, upon the letters […] at all times and before all time and […] and there is no power nor strength except […] the Most High, the Most Great.

title: BB00189: Du’a’ ’ala’n-Nafyi’n-Nafy (prayer for the negation of negation)
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I bear Thee witness—and all things bear Thee witness—that Thou art God: there is none other God but Thee, One, without partner. Thine is the dominion of mulk and malakut; Thine the might of ʿizzat and jabarut; Thine the potency and lahut; Thine the power and the radiant ruby-glory; Thine are the Most Beautiful Names and the similitudes that point to none save Thee. Thou givest life and causest to die, then Thou causest to die and givest life again; and verily Thou art the Living Who dieth not. Within Thy grasp is the kingdom of all things; by Thy command Thou bringest into being whatsoever Thou willest. Thou, in truth, hast ever been powerful over all things.
Hallowed art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Primality—whereby Thou art supreme above all things—that Thou annihilate every identity of alif that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest; for Thou art, in very truth, potent over all things.
O God! I entreat Thee by Thy Loftiness—manifest above all things—that Thou efface every identity of ba’ that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest; verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Omnipotence—transcendent above all things—that Thou blot out every identity of jim that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Ever-abidingness—unassailable above all things—that Thou efface every identity of dal that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Guidance—uplifted above all things—that Thou annihilate every identity of ha’ that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for, verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Guardianship—whereby Thou standest over all things—that Thou… (grant the same) by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Sowing and Nurturing—exalted above all things—that Thou annihilate every identity of za’ that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Life—immutable above all things—that Thou efface every identity of ha’ that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Purity—sublime above all things—that Thou annihilate every identity of ta’ that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Certitude—which pierceth the hearts of Thy loved ones—that Thou efface every identity of ya’ that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Majesty—manifest over all things—that Thou annihilate every identity of kaf that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Subtlety—uplifted above all things—that Thou efface every identity of lam that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Sovereignty—prevailing over all things—that Thou annihilate every identity of mim that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Luminosity—exalted above all things—that Thou efface every identity of nun that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Holiness—sanctified above all things—that Thou annihilate every identity of sin that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Exaltation—high above all things—that Thou efface every identity of ʿayn that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Oneness—solitary above all things—that Thou annihilate every identity of fa’ that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Self-Sufficiency—invincible above all things—that Thou efface every identity of sad that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Strength—over-mastering all things—that Thou annihilate every identity of qaf that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Mercy—enrobing all things—that Thou efface every identity of ra’ that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Witnessing—witness above every thing unto every thing—that Thou annihilate every identity of shin that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy All-Returning grace—august above all things—that Thou efface every identity of ta’ that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Steadfastness—prevalent over all things—that Thou annihilate every identity of tha’ that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Creative Power—manifest above all things—that Thou efface every identity of kha’ that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Fashioning—uplifted above all things—that Thou annihilate every identity of dhal that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Guarantee—unassailable above all things—that Thou efface every identity of dad that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Manifestness—sublime above all things—that Thou annihilate every identity of za’ that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Predominance—prevailing over all things—that Thou efface every identity of ghayn that is ascribed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou wilt; for Thou art powerful over all things.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I ask Thee thus in Negation because, thereafter, naught remaineth to it; for the Names, apart from Thy loved ones, are not void of these letters, and whatsoever is ascribed unto them is not severed therefrom. Therefore do I implore Thee, by Thy power which hath left nothing to him who boweth not down before Thee—for everything is related to these letters—that Thou annihilate, from all who refuse to prostrate themselves before Thee, every identity composed of letters attributed to aught beside Thee.
Manifest then, O my God, the station of this supplication; exalt, O my God, him who calleth upon Thee with this praise; and honour, O my God, whoso annihilateth Negation according to this decree in the very act of effacement. For whoso is unable to efface Negation by aught but these words—this is the most exalted of paths for affirming Thy unity: the negation of negation from the court of Thy holiness, from the seat of Thy might, from the sovereignty of Thy self-subsistence and the kingship of Thy Lordship.
Wherefore will I praise Thee, O my God, unto the furthest… for that Thou hast enabled me thus to exalt Thy unity, to magnify Thy holiness, to proclaim Thy glorification, and to uplift Thy unicity. There is no power nor strength save in Thee; unto Thee is the return. And send Thou Thy blessings upon the Letters of the First (the Letters of the Living) at every moment—before time and after time.

title: BB00144: Du’a’ li’l-Ithbat (prayer of affirmation)
text:

title: BB00192: Du’a’ li-Ithbati’l-ithbat (prayer for the affirmation of affirmation)
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy!
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I bear witness before Thee and all things to that which Thou hast caused me to witness: that there is none other God but Thee, and that the Letters of the Unity are the nearest of Thy names unto Thee in Thy Book. Unto Thee belongeth might and majesty, unto Thee belongeth glory and beauty, unto Thee belongeth power and perfection, unto Thee belongeth strength and dominion, unto Thee belongeth grandeur and independence. Thou hast ever been one God, single, unique, eternal, self-subsisting, ever-abiding, everlasting, self-dependent. Thou hast taken unto Thyself neither consort nor son, and Thou hast had no partner in Thy creation, nor any protector in what Thou hast fashioned. Thou hast exalted Thyself through Thy might above all created things, and hast magnified Thyself through Thy sovereign might above all who dwell in the kingdoms of earth and heaven, and hast elevated Thyself in the pure essence of Thy camphor-like nature above all who inhabit the realms of names and attributes.
I beseech Thee, O my God, at this moment—inasmuch as Thou art powerful over whatsoever Thou pleaseth, and invincible in whatsoever Thou willeth, and exalted above whatsoever Thou hast ordained, and transcendent above whatsoever Thou hast decreed, and sanctified above whatsoever Thou hast executed, and dominant over whatsoever Thou hast established, and triumphant over whatsoever Thou hast sent down—through Thy Divinity which is supreme over all things, to preserve every essence of Alif that is related to the Tree of Affirmation, through Thy power over whatsoever Thou pleaseth. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.

title: BB00268: Letter to Quddus
text:
He addresseth Mulla Muhammad Ali al-Mazandarani, entitled Quddus, and assigneth to each one of the Four Gates a single star, making himself the Manifestation of the name Muhammad, and Mulla Muhammad Ali the Manifestation of the name Ali, and Qurratu’l-ʿAyn the Manifestation of the name Fatima, and Mirza Husayn Ali al-Baha the Manifestation of Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, and so forth. And it is this:
O Muhammad-before-Ali! The number of negation in exile hath been decreed, not for God’s sake. It is binding upon every soul to establish the Alif of affirmation in that wherein ye are, and verily this on that Day is, in God’s sight, the whole matter for those who are certain thereof. Let negation be negated and affirmation be affirmed according to the truth over which ye have power.
Say: Verily religion after religion is the knowledge of God and His unity, and the recognition thereafter of His justice, and following what hath been sent down from His presence, and the negation of limitation from His holy court, for whatsoever is besides Him of all things was created for Him. Say: O My creation, fear ye Me!
And whatsoever God hath created of anything in the Book and what is therein—He intendeth by the first letter of the first verse and what is therein in the mighty Basmalah and what is therein in the first letter—verily there is no God but I, the Lord of the worlds. Verily all that the Qur’an containeth is encompassed in the Surih of Praise, and all that it containeth is encompassed in the Basmalah, and all that the Basmalah containeth is encompassed in the letter Ba, and all that is in the Ba is encompassed in the Point, and I am that Point beneath the Ba.
But the Bab intendeth by this utterance that aforementioned Point, for it is He. Thus were the Babis named according to the Point. The foundation of religion in the beginning is the glorification of God, and in the end the praise of God, and in the outward the unity of God, and in the inward the magnification of God. And verily on that Day, so long as the sun shineth, the whole of religion is “There is no God but God” outwardly and inwardly, first and last, then “Muhammad is the Messenger of God”, then the Imams and the Inheritors are the proofs of God, then the Gates are for the outward magnification. That is a comprehensive word, and verily the measures of the branch revolve around it.
So enter ye into the religion and be ye dominant over the earth and whatsoever is thereon, and purify the lands of negation through the Most Beautiful Names and the Most Exalted Examples and the Prophets and the Truthful Ones and the Martyrs and the Righteous, and give ye greetings unto them from thy Lord—meaning Himself by “the Lord.” And whoso desireth to enter beneath the shadow of affirmation, these are they who shall inherit. And if there be an Ali there, then mention him from thy Lord and say: Verily thou, on the Day of Resurrection, art of the triumphant ones. If thou desirest that We should be present from whence thou knowest not, and that thou shouldst console the people of grief in the (letter Fa), it is more beloved to Me. And We sent the Tablets unto him! God will gather together, by His command, between me and those who have recognized the truth from me. Verily, He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.
And the wonder concerneth the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden. From the night of thy recognition of thy Lord, the number of negation in “There is no God” hath been fulfilled—fifty thousand years—and the days of affirmation have dawned. Until that time, what was befitting in the negation of negation and the affirmation of affirmation had not been mentioned. This is the whole of religion on that day, not that wherein people were rejoicing.
Watch thou Our Great Name and recite the Book of the All-Bountiful, for unto each one are examples of that Temple preserved with God. Recite ye this verse 361 times day and night:

“God beareth witness that there is no God but Him. His are the Creation and the Command. He giveth life and causeth death, then causeth death and giveth life. Verily, He is the Ever-Living Who dieth not. Within His grasp is the kingdom of all things. He createth what He willeth by His command, then by His verses. These are they who are the triumphant.”

Say: God is the Lord, and whatsoever is besides God is servant, and all are worshippers unto Him. He verily hath power over all things. And whosoever believeth in God from where they know and from where they know not. Verily the station of interpretation belongeth to the Prophet, and supplication to the Guardian, and knowledge to the Gates. We have manifested the glory of His exalted remembrance, as none but He can bear it, and after God there was not […] these stations. Then We have attributed to the Manifestations of the Living One and specifically reserved for the verses of God a new discourse in which people believed.
Say what Ali (meaning the Commander of the Faithful) hath said: “His signs are His proof, and His existence His affirmation.” And God is All-Knowing, All-Powerful. Verily I have sent forth temples of 313 companions in number 224. Were but one of these to be with anyone who hath faith, he would prevail over all the worlds. And verily the number of the Gate in the Greater Temples was first adorned and shone forth. He is the Proud, the Beautiful, the Beneficent. He hath subjected therein the ranks of the earth within five divisions of Divine Unity. Hasten ye, for through them shall ye assuredly prevail.
Then it shone forth and arose; then it gave light and resounded; then it irradiated and was uplifted from the court of the camphor-like holiness, the limpid purity, the hiddenness of the Manifestation; from the dawning of the famed Epiphany, the vesture of concealment, the unrolled Remembrance, the public proclamation of the Zealous, the Rememberer, the Remembered; from Him Who dwelleth within and is loosed upon the Mount; from the Summoner unto the veiled Mystery—and from my Lord ʿAli upon the Blessed Tree, its root and its branch and its boughs—“the Proof of God,” the inscribed symbol, the Oft-frequented House, the Luminous Presence and the dispeller of gloom—its fruits and its shades; even as the dove warbleth upon the branches of the Tree of Tuba in Paradise, and as the birds sing upon the leaves of the Lote-Tree beyond which there is no passing, in the shadows of Firdaus.
Know then—and give thanks unto God—that “Zarrin-Taj, Qurratu’l-ʿAyn,” the wearer of the golden crown, is addressed by this Tablet; for thy Book is “sealed,” that is, sealed—for in Persian “khatam” signifieth the seal. Wherefore, laud thy Lord for His favour; He, through His bounty, hath delivered thee for God’s sake from what thou didst fear and dread.
Be thou assured that, as a bridal dowry from the jewels of thy knowledge, the inward meanings of the ordinances and the loci of trials have been disclosed. Be patient, be patient, with the remembrance of the Ocean of Succour and the Fount of Blessing.
They attributed to you certain incidental matters, but their statements were disproven clearly and openly, for Husayn was indeed martyred. Whosoever claims he was not killed has forgotten God’s decree and that which reason has witnessed. There is no vengeance more severe than what he believed and said that Paradise and knowledge suffice as witness. Then indeed the fire and Paradise are created, and in them are servants whose number none knows save God. And before the Day of Resurrection it shall not be manifest to anyone. The return of the Qa’im—may God hasten the manifestation of that Light—suffices. Seek forgiveness from God, for that is the gate of guidance through which all are created.
We revealed in the first year: Say, these are the fruits of the garden of the First Name in the form which you recite in prayer, if you are certain. Then the fruits of the Tree of Oneness, if you bear witness. Then the fruits of the Tree of Divinity, if you are assured. Then the fruits of the Tree of Eternality wherein flow four rivers, and therein you shall find the delights that God has created in those rivers, which God has specially ordained. This is of God’s bounty and mercy that you may be thankful.
We have ordained the fruits of the First Tree for Muhammad, the Messenger of God—this is your Lord’s gift, neither cut off nor forbidden—then for Ali, the true and beloved Imam, then for Fatima, a leaf from the First Tree—thus shall you be gathered together—then for Hasan and Husayn, whom God made Imams from His presence over all the worlds. Say: These are nine letters after the ten, all created according to what God has ordained for them.
Say: The letters of those five are for one; when each is made a gate, you shall not witness the matters about which you say “We are God’s servants.” But you shall not see in the inward the pillar by which the gates of guidance are made manifest, nor in the outward the pillar by which the Imams of religion stand in truth, nor the other pillar by which you are sustained. And by it you bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God from God, before the creation of the heavens and earth and what lies between them, the creation of the worlds. Then in the first pillar by it you bear witness that there is no God but He, that Lord of the worlds.
Whosoever desires God, seeking your Lord’s good pleasure, let him gather all that We revealed in the First in a written book upon the first earth which We ordained for Muhammad—this is of your Lord’s bounty until the day you shall be brought before God—until it reaches the fruits of the Garden of Eternality, for then you shall be upon the earth whereon you were previously to appear. It behooveth none save that he should spend five souls from God’s right in what is written in the Book, all that God has revealed until the number five is expended—this is of God’s bounty and mercy that you may be thankful. Choose from those five pieces five souls to gather all that God has revealed, and attribute it to God until the day all shall be brought before God.
And verily the first earth—We were its writers, thus until your Lord’s remembrance ends—all We were witnesses. So be ye patient until God bringeth His decree; and ye are surely able to do this. This is of the bounty of God and His mercy. The measures of all things have been set forth in the Book for the day when ye shall be brought before God.
Glorified be God! To Him prostrateth whosoever is in the heavens and whosoever is on the earth; we are all prostrate before Him. He it is Who determineth the measures of all things through His mercy. Verily, He is the All-Bountiful, the All-Subtle. His are the hosts of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them. All that are in the heavens and all that are on the earth and whatsoever lieth between them glorify Him, and we, likewise, are workers in His Cause. And verily He is the Truth, the Sure. And unto God belongeth the origination of the heavens and of the earth and of whatsoever lieth between them, and verily He is the Single, the Sublime. That same God is your Lord; His is the creation and the command. Say: All are submissive unto Him.
That which was revealed in the first year is the fruits of the Paradise of the Divine Identity, pertaining to Muhammad (peace be upon Him), and His star pertaineth to the land of Persia, wherein it must be recorded in a book containing the four rivers of divine manifestation.
That which was revealed in the second year is the fruits of the Tree of Divinity, pertaining to Ali (peace be upon Him), and His star pertaineth to the land of Iraq, to be written in a book containing the four stations of creation, sustenance, death and life.
That which was revealed in the third year is the fruits of the Paradise of Oneness, pertaining to Fatima (peace be upon Her), and Her star pertaineth to the land of Azerbaijan, wherein it must be recorded in a book containing the four stations.
That which was revealed in the fourth year is the fruits of the Paradise of Divinity, pertaining to Imam Hassan (peace be upon Him), and His star pertaineth to the land of Khorasan, wherein it hath been recorded in a book containing the four manifestations of unity, prophethood, divine authority, and the Shi’ih Faith.
That which was revealed in the fifth year is the fruits of the Paradise of Eternality, pertaining to Imam Hussein (peace be upon Him), and His star pertaineth to the land of Mazandaran, recorded in a volume containing the four stations.
And verily that which We have sealed on the twenty-first day of that month shall be inscribed beneath the shade of the Tree of Eternality, as a mercy from thy Lord. Verily, He is the Mighty, the Merciful.

title: BB00504
text:
In the name of God, the Supreme Helper
O Lord my God! I beseech Thee by the Alif of the Father, and the Ba of the Revelation, and the Ta of the Oft-Returning, and the Tha of Steadfastness, and the Jim of Generosity, and the Ha of Wisdom, and the Kha of the All-Informed, and the Dal of Perpetuity, and the Dhal of Creation, and the Ra of Lordship, and the Za of the Sower, and the Sin of Splendor, and the Shin of Gratitude, and the Sad of Patience, and the Dad of Conscience, and the Ta of Sinai, and the Za of Manifestation, and the ʿAyn of Knowledge, and the Ghayn of Victory, and the Fa of Success, and the Qaf of Nearness, and the Kaf of Glory, and the Lam of the Standard, and the Mim of Honor, and the Nun of Light, and the Vav of Providence, and the Ha of Identity, and the Lam of Grace, and the Alif of Command, and the Ya of Certitude, to send Thy blessings upon all Thy guides and the thrones of Thy manifestation and the seats of Thy concealment, both of the past and of the future.
O my God! Send forth from Thy presence one who shall seize these infidels, and from Thy side one who shall lay hold upon these immoral ones, and from among Thy servants one who shall subdue these transgressors, and from all Thy creation one who shall overcome these oppressors.
Verily Thou art the most severe in might and in punishment, the most powerful in conquest and in supremacy, the most forceful in assault and in dominion, the most vigorous in seizure and in chastisement. Verily nothing in the heavens or on earth or between them can frustrate Thee, and Thou hast power over all things.

title: BB00624
text:
He is the Most Great
In the Name of God, the Most Great, the Most Great. God—there is none other God but He—the Most Great, the Most Great. Thus hath the Cause been established: the negation of negation and the affirmation of affirmation.

title: BB00317
text:
God testifieth that there is none other God but He, the Mighty, the Well-Beloved. Whoso turneth unto God with all his heart—verily he is the one feared by the peoples of the heavens and the earth, and he is the one drawn nigh among His saints and His trusted ones.
And now: as for the messenger of God unto thee—upon thee be Baha, and upon thee be praise and light—he hath written these words in the station of reason and in the precincts of faith, beholding thy sorrow-laden heart: “O God! Bless and salute!” Then send down all Thy mercy upon those trembling hearts, those grief-stricken spirits, those burning souls—Thy friends, Thy chosen ones, Thy trusted ones—who have cut themselves off, wholly, unto Thee, and have laid down their lives in the path of Thy blood, that Thy unity might be established. Yea, such is Thy wont, from before and after; I find no change, nor alteration, in Thy wont.
It was while I sat, in the corner of resignation, steadfast and patient under what the Sovereign of decree had manifested—carrying into effect the ordinance for the people of fidelity—when suddenly there came unto me, from before, tidings from him who hath migrated unto God: upon him be all praise. From the Point of Splendor there reached me light and radiance, borne upon the steed of thanksgiving and praise unto Him Who is seated upon the throne of bounty. Thus did I deem it incumbent to bind my own self, in every thought, to the fragrant remembrances of a manifest light, and to reckon as the true qiblih that Messenger who hath drawn nigh.
O Beloved of my heart! I have no refuge save submission and contentment: contentment with the decree of God, and surrender unto His command. Verily we are God’s, and unto Him we return. Blessed, then, are they who have ascended unto Him through the attraction of their hearts. I beseech God, of His grace, to join us unto His friends, and to bestow upon us what He hath bestowed upon them in His path. Verily He is the Possessor of mighty bounty.
My supplication was offered, and the service was rendered, that the heart might be soothed by the chanting of the revealed words. And in the end, too, the Tablet of the presence of Fatimih—may the blessings of God rest upon her—hath bestowed upon me solace, saying in effect: “Be not sorrowful at whatever may befall.” Such is that which God hath written for His loved ones from aforetime; they asked it of God their Lord, and they were, thereby, of the joyful.
God willing, whenever the Lord shall ordain, the return will be hastened—for blessed is that return, and it is the very goal of the seeker. And whensoever it be possible, for the quieting of hearts, the treasured Tablets—upon them be the glory of God—shall be conveyed; otherwise, I remain settled in the dwelling of resignation until tidings arrive.
And since, after the appearance of the Gate, the blessed Pen—manifesting from the horizon—hath itself been grieved for the sake of that direction, therefore I have, from the former manifestations, nothing but prayers and devotions, and whatever else hath been brought, these I have forwarded, by the blessed handwriting of the Most Exalted, and, by agreement with Hamid, they have been delivered in service—so that, by that, the bearer of the trusts may be sent to the dwelling of those in grief. If it be profitable, let him return of his own accord; otherwise, send him, with sure handling, as a bearer, if it be feasible and no hindrance arise.
From among the people of the world there may, with effort, be found in such-and-such a city certain copies—bearing a token of “There is none like unto Him.” Do thou follow this: first, send the bearer to thy honored presence; then dispatch him—if need be—for the dwellers of the house and for those souls departed, in the place wherein thou residest.
And I beseech thee: by two words, or by a brief message, describe my condition, and set forth somewhat of my circumstances, that tranquility may return unto my heart, and that I may attain assurance.
O God, Fashioner of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen! Thou judgest between Thy servants concerning that wherein they differ. Praise be to God, the Lord of all worlds.
Keep with thee the glad tidings, O sovereign messenger; then add—if thou wilt—that unto the very end, for the Letters…

title: BB00308: Ziyara for the martyrs, on Thursday night
text:
Visitation for the martyrs, upon them be Glory
In the name of God, the Inaccessible, the Most Holy
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I and all things bear witness that verily Thou art God; there is no God but Thee, alone, without peer. Unto Thee belong the most excellent names in their essence, and unto Thee belong the most exalted attributes in their sovereignty. Thou hast ever existed before all things, and Thou wilt ever remain after all things. I and all things testify that from time immemorial Thy dominion over the realm of creation hath been in Thy grasp, and Thy kingdom over the realm of invention hath been in the right hand of Thy will. None can reckon the beginning of Thy creation, nor its end. Indeed, Thou hast shown me from the wondrous beginning of Thy creation until this time when the first millennium and decade have been completed, and we are now in the third millennium after the decade.
I bear witness that Thou hast been One, not in number, One without resemblance to any other, from the wondrous beginning of Thy creation until now. Thou hast never sent a Messenger, nor revealed a Book, nor supported the people of the religion of God except for Him Whom Thou shalt manifest on the Day of Resurrection through Thy signs. Verily, Thou hast never revealed any decree in any Manifestation except that Thou didst intend to exalt the Manifestation of Thyself in the subsequent Revelation. As Thou hast permitted me in all things, I have desired naught except to aid Him Whom Thou shalt manifest and to exalt the Word of Him Whom Thou shalt raise up.
By Thy might! Had I known of any decree that might occur to anyone’s heart without love for Him and obedience to Him, I would not have revealed that decree, and had I revealed it, I would have abrogated it through an irrevocable decree from Thee and an unalterable ordinance from Thy presence. For all this is for the manifestation of Thy unity, the exaltation of Thy sanctity, the elevation of Thy praise, the glory of Thy countenance, the independence of the sovereignty of Thy Self-Sufficiency, the splendor of the light of Thy Beauty, the majesty of Thy Glory, the beauty of Thy Face, the greatness of Thy Everlasting Might, the radiance of Thy Holy Light, the mercy of Thy All-Merciful Nature, the perfection of Thy Oneness, the grandeur of Thy Sovereign Singleness, the might of Thy Conquering Authority, the power of Thy Sovereign Dominion, the good-pleasure of Thy All-Glorious Sovereignty, the transcendence of Thine Eternity, the dominion of Thy Divine Lordship, the sovereignty of the might of Thy Oneness, and the power of the strength of Thy All-Knowing Sovereignty.
By Thy might! If I knew that anyone on the day of His manifestation would cause Him grief, I would assuredly send down unto him a missive and forbid him therefrom, for no doubter followeth Me in Thy good-pleasure. On that day the Bayan shall appear with supreme elucidation, and verily I behold Thee and all things on that Friday night which Thou hast made glorious, and sought after, and adorned, and magnified, and illumined, and sanctified, and elevated above all else. Then shall I address all things from Thy presence, saying:

“O all things! God hath created naught save for Him Whom He shall make manifest in truth. Therefore watch over yourselves, for not to practice your religion is better than to pass judgment upon God, your Lord.”

This is what God, your Lord, hath counseled you in the Bayan, and before and after, that ye may prosper on the Day of Resurrection. And sufficient art Thou, O my God, as a witness unto what I have made Thee and all things to witness, and at that time Thou didst send down a decisive proof from Thy presence concerning the believers.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I testify that all besides Thee is Thy creation and within Thy grasp, and all things shall confess before Him Who manifesteth Thy Self on the Day of Resurrection that Thou didst create all things for Him, and sustain them for Him, and cause them to die for Him, and give them life for Him, and judge them for Him. I testify that He hath no peer in Thy knowledge, no equal in Thy Book, no likeness in Thy heaven, no partner in Thy earth, and no similitude between them in the kingdom of Thy command and creation. For this is a Lamp which, if Thou cause it to shine, shall illumine all things with its light; a Word which, if Thou send it down, shall set aright the affairs of all things through Thy grace; and a Book which, if Thou unfold it, […], therein shalt Thou find, by His leave, whatsoever Thou desirest of all things. Glorified art Thou, O my God! By it Thou didst rectify the matter of all things even before its manifestation—from the Day of Adam until that moment—and before Adam unto all that Thou hast numbered; and thereafter, until Thou shalt have numbered all.
Do Thou, then, send down at that hour—upon him and upon those who have believed in him on the Day of Resurrection—the truth: from every splendor the most resplendent, from every majesty the most majestic, from every beauty the most beauteous, from every greatness the greatest thereof, from every light the most luminous, from every might the most mighty, from every mercy the most abundant, from every word the most perfect, from every manifestation the most manifest, from every hiddenness the most hidden, from every knowledge the most effectual, from every utterance the most well-pleasing, from every love the most entrancing, from every sovereignty the most enduring, from every exaltation the most exalted, and from every good that, in Thy knowledge, hath no equal.
Fill, then, the pillars of all things with love for him, with his good-pleasure, with awe of him and reverence before him, and with obedience to whatsoever Thou sendest down upon him of the decrees of Thy power. For all bounty is in his hand: if he exalteth a command, then from the day of his appearance until the Resurrection, all abide in ease through his grace; and if he decreeth a matter, all dwell beneath the shade of his obedience.
O God! Preserve him from all sorrow, lest he be concealed from that creation and pass judgement upon them from which they cannot escape, nor can they be veiled from the commands of His dominion. For if He bestows anything, all things receive it, and if He judges anything, all things apprehend it, for in every Manifestation all things bow down before the Manifestation of Thy Self and humble themselves before the Dawning-Place of Thy Being. Therefore, O God, do Thou send down upon him and upon the Letters of the Living and upon all his names and likenesses that which befitteth the loftiness of Thy sanctity and the exaltation of Thy grace. And do Thou send down upon his parents and those who love him that which befitteth the sublimity of Thy bounty and the exaltation of Thy grace and the elevation of Thy generosity and the inaccessibility of Thy wisdom.
And do Thou send down, through the mention of his name with Thee, upon the Point of the Bayan and His Letters of the Living and all His followers, and those who have ascended unto Thee in their love for Him from among the Letters of the Ten, and those who have ascended unto Thee with their hearts and spirits and souls and bodies, that which befitteth the sublimity of Thy bounty and the exaltation of Thy grace.
And do Thou send down, O God, upon those who have not believed in Him, all Thy chastisement and retribution, for Thou art the most severe in punishment and the most terrible in vengeance. And do Thou send down that which Thou sendest down upon those who have not believed in Him upon those who have not recognized Thee in the Point of the Bayan, nor in the Manifestation of Thy Self, nor in the names of Thy might, nor in the examples of Thy holiness, or who have written concerning anyone that which is not befitting at the rising of Thy might and the appearance of Thy glory. Verily, Thou art severe in chastisement and Thou art, over all things, powerful.
And if thou art on such a night at the tomb of the First and the Last or what lieth between them, or anyone who hath ascended unto God on the Day of Resurrection, after completing the prayers of sunset and evening, enter by thy Lord’s leave that most exalted seat and most glorious pavilion. Then say by covenant from thee: “When thou attainest unto the Day of Resurrection, remember this in His presence when God permitteth thee. Verily the glory from God, then from the Letters of the Unity, then from all who have believed in God and His days, be upon you, O ye hearts that glorify, spirits that sanctify, souls that unite, and bodies that magnify!
God hath never ceased to remember you with the loftiness of His remembrance and to send down concerning your station the exaltation of His glory. I testify before God and all things that ye have ascended unto God in your entirety and have attained unto what God hath prepared for you. Verily, all essences glorify, all beings sanctify, all souls unite, and all existences magnify the greatness of your essences’ essence, the loftiness of your beings’ being, the sublimity of your souls’ soul, the growth of your existence’s existence, and the manifestation of your camphor’s camphor. There weep for you whatsoever is in the highest kingdom down to the lowest atom: the heavens in their steadfastness, the sun in its rising, the moon in its fullness, the stars in their rising and setting, the earth in its spreading forth, the sea in its waves, the fish in their courses, the trees in their height, the leaves in their growth, the fruits in their ripening, and whatsoever is in the heaven and the earth in that which remembereth you and what hath befallen you.”
You shall return on the Day of Resurrection and settle in the seats of glory, and you shall look upon those who weep for you and expend in your path what God has ordained for you. This is your recompense, since you have come unto God, your Lord, Who created you, sustained you, caused you to die, gave you life, and raised you from the resting-places of your hearts, and clothed you in the garments of His remembrance, as He wishes, with what He wishes, for what He wishes, for He does what He pleases and is powerful over what He desires.
Will those who turned away from you be remembered then? No, by your essence! If they knew themselves, they would flee from themselves and bear witness against themselves, destroying themselves by their own hands. By God, He will take vengeance upon them and cause their tongues to utter what befits them in their lives, then after their return whence they know not and comprehend not. Thus does God take vengeance on whom He pleases and singles out for His favor whom He wishes. Verily, He is the All-Bountiful, the All-Encompassing, the Most Generous.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Thou seest those hearts, spirits, souls and bodies in the chambers of Thy good-pleasure, the mysteries of Thy gardens, the loftiness of their seats and the inaccessibility of their ascents. Therefore, O my God, do Thou send down upon them that whereby they may soar in the chambers of Thy paradise and dwell in the seats of Thy glory, and hear how Thou didst take vengeance on those who committed against them, without right, that which Thou hadst not permitted to anyone before. And they shall witness, through the manifestations of Thy creation, the breathings of Thy holiness, the revelations of Thy creation, the signs of Thy glory, and the modes of Thy grace, that which shall glorify Thee beyond all that hath glorified Thee or shall glorify Thee, and shall sanctify Thee beyond all that hath sanctified Thee or shall sanctify Thee, and shall unite Thee beyond all that hath united Thee or shall unite Thee, and shall magnify Thee beyond all that hath magnified Thee or shall magnify Thee, and shall exalt Thee above what hath exalted Thee or shall exalt Thee.
For less than this befits not the sublimity of Thy holiness, the exaltation of Thy glory, the elevation of Thy might, the inviolability of Thy sanctity, the radiance of Thy countenance, the invincibility of Thy Lordship, the power of Thine eternity, the majesty of Thy oneness, the beauty of Thy bountifulness, the loftiness of Thine everlastingness, and the permanence of the sovereignty of Thy self-subsistence.
Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee before all things, and glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee after all things, and glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee above all things, and glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee beneath all things. All are Thy servants and within Thy grasp. Thou givest life and causest death, then causest death and givest life, and verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not. Within Thy grasp is the kingdom of all things. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command. Verily, Thou hast power over all things.

title: BB00111: Ziyarat for the first [to believe]
text:
Part 1: “First Visitation, upon Him be the Glory…”
First Visitation, upon Him be the Glory of God, the King of Eternity
In the Name of God, the Most Ancient of the Most Ancient!
Verily I am God! There is no God but Me, the Most Ancient of the Most Ancient! Verily I am God! There is no God but Me, the Most Precedent of the Most Precedent! Verily I am God! There is no God but Me! I have been eternally ancient before and after; all worship Me.
Verily I am God! There is no God but Me! I have been wondrous bounty; all prostrate to Me. Verily I am God! There is no God but Me! I have been the God of all things before and after; all are devoted to Me. Verily I am God! There is no God but Me! I have been the God of all things, and all remember Me.
Verily I am God! There is no God but Me! Mine are all the most beautiful names before and after; all seek proof of Me. Verily I am God! There is no God but Me! Mine are the most exalted similitudes before and after; all abide in My shadow.
Verily I am God! There is no God but Me! None knoweth Me save My own Self, and verily I know all things by their own essence before their existence, and verily I have been All-Knowing, All-Wise. Verily I am God! There is no God but Me! None comprehendeth Me save My own Self, and verily I comprehend all things by My command, and verily I have been All-Powerful, All-Mighty.
Verily I am God! There is no God but Me! I have created all creation, which hath no beginning in My knowledge nor end in My Book. They commence from infinity unto infinity by My command, and all are within My grasp, and all await Me.
Verily I am God! There is no God but Me! I have been a mystic veil. When I desired to make Myself known, I created a pure, pristine essence and said unto it: “Am I not thy Lord?” It replied: “Yea, verily Thou art my Lord and the Lord of all things. Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee! Verily I am the first of them that worship.”
I made it My beloved, and through it I created that creation, and ordained for them from My presence that which they ask of My grace. Then through it I made Myself known by all My names, whereupon all seek proof of Me and abide in My shadow. That creation had no beginning that ye could comprehend before it. I have brought all creation from everything to the First Innovation, whereupon I renewed the creation of all things through its manifestation, and then ye worship Me.
Then I made Myself known to it and revealed unto it the Book and ordained for it from My presence the ways, whereupon all who follow it rejoice in My good-pleasure, and all who follow it not, I make no mention of them. Thus doth God judge amongst the worlds.
Then after the First Innovation I made Myself known in every dispensation by whatever name I manifested, and revealed unto it the Book and ordained for it ways from My presence until this time, all worship Me, until I concluded all My manifestations with Muhammad, My Messenger from before, and revealed unto him the Furqan and ordained for him ways therein, and all seek Me.
And I have adorned the beginning of creation until this time with those whom I have sent and revealed unto them from the Books for the day of My manifestation, that ye might worship Me.
Then I made Myself known on the Day of Resurrection through the Point of the Bayan, whereupon all My servants were veiled save those who recognized Me and were assured of My signs. Then I chose them for Myself and selected for them the most exalted life and raised them unto Me by My command. Verily We have been the Doer thereof. And when I made Myself known unto them, they, ere I gave them leave, sacrificed themselves for Me, inasmuch as they knew Me and were of them that were certain of My signs. These are they who have worshipped Me from the beginning that hath no beginning, and these are My guides in the Book—all seek Me alone.
O My First Name! Upon thee be My glory at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My majesty at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My beauty at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My grandeur at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My light at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My mercy at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My words at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My names at all times, and before all times, and after all times.
Upon thee be My perfection at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My might at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My knowledge at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My power at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My good-pleasure at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My honor at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My sovereignty at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My dominion at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My bounty at all times, and before all times, and after all times. Upon thee be My signs at all times, and before all times, and after all times.
I have created thy essence from Mine own Essence and made thee a sign unto all worlds. I have chosen thee for Myself and made thee a proof unto all worlds. Thou hast borne witness to that which thou hast witnessed in My path. Grieve not to the extent of a mustard seed, for thou art among the immortals in My good-pleasure.
I have made thee a living one who shall not die therein, and all shall present themselves before thee. I have made thee the guardian over all therein, and all shall glorify Me before thee. I have made thee a king therein, and all move by thy command. I have made thee a sovereign therein, and all dwell by thy command.
When thou didst turn to those who worshipped God through thee, all such as glorify God through thee turn unto Me. They prostrate themselves before Me through thee by night and by day. Were they to know thee, they would surely be among the patient ones at thy resting-place. They would not leave thee until, by God’s leave, they receive the recompense of what their hands have wrought in thy path. God will seize them through thy hands by making thee among the powerful ones on earth. For they remember themselves without right by names before them, and there is no vengeance more severe than what their hands have earned. God will show them their own selves and their deeds, and will render them as though none of them had ever been mentioned on earth.
Therefore mention thou all My names there, for verily We have ever been mindful. Look upon them as We have been looking upon thee. Say unto them: O My names! Ye seek to prove Me and ye abide under My shadow. In this your turbidity there is no good-pleasure like unto what ye have earned, and after your death there shall be no good-pleasure like unto how God remembereth you. In the chambers of Paradise ye shall be rewarded according to your hearts’ desires. Grieve not to the extent of a mustard seed, for ye shall be among the mighty ones in the highest Paradise with your Lord. Therein are for you houris like hidden pearls, therein are for you servants who are like hidden pearls. Therein shall ye have all that your souls desire. Ye shall wear naught but the most glorious silk, and shall find before you only such things as have been fashioned therein by God’s leave, all gold-encrusted on the right and on the left. God createth by His command; verily He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.

title: BB00111: Ziyarat for the first [to believe]
section: Part 2: “Ye shall recline upon your couches, reciting what…”
text:
Part 2: “Ye shall recline upon your couches, reciting what…”
Ye shall recline upon your couches, reciting what hath been sent down in the Bayan, and through God, your Lord, shall ye be strengthened. And if ye attain unto the measure of what ye have witnessed, ye shall thereby gain possession of the Most Great Paradise in the sight of God and the Most Exalted Mention in the Book of God. Thus doth the eye of God rest upon whomsoever He willeth of His servants. There is no God but Him, the Protector, the Powerful.
God, your Lord, shall return you to the first life that ye may, by His command, take vengeance on those who have waxed proud against you. Verily, He hath power over all things. Grieve not in your chambers over anything, for therein ye shall have whatsoever ye ask of your Lord’s bounty. Look upon those who recall what hath been decreed for you, how they are blessed in your paradise. And look upon those who know you not, how they perish in their veils.
Say: O My Names! We have indeed revealed Ourselves to you through your own hearts before the creation of the heavens and the earth and all that lieth between them, yea, before the creation of all things. We have made you guides to the First Name, that ye may, on the Day of Resurrection, find rest beneath His shade.
We shall surely manifest Our Self on the Day of Resurrection in truth, and We shall bestow favor upon Our Names by their mention in the Book of God, for We are indeed All-Knowing. We shall return you to the first life in the life to come, and We shall bestow Our favor upon you on the Day of Resurrection as ye seek shelter in the shade of your Lord.
O My creation! If ye seek shelter in the shade of Him Whom We shall manifest on the Day of Resurrection in truth, then ye are indeed My proofs testifying unto Me, and ye are My Names receiving tidings from Me. But if ye deprive yourselves through your veiling from the Manifestation of My Self on the Day of Resurrection, after We have made known to you the paths of your salvation on that Day, that ye might be saved.
Say: All worship Me, and there is naught but prostrateth before Me and is among those who worship. But those who are the companions of Paradise—these are they who know Me and the Seven Letters from My presence, and thereby enter the most exalted Paradise. And those who worship Me but know Me not through the Seven Letters of My Glory—their deeds shall not be raised up unto Me, and We shall render void all that they have earned and all that they earn.
For I desire to be worshipped as I love, not as My creation loveth. My love at that time is that ye worship Me through the Point of the Bayan and believe in what hath been sent down therein, then be certain, then act accordingly. And prepare yourselves for the Day of My Manifestation on the Day of Resurrection that ye may recognize Me.
Say: If ye recognize the Manifestation of My Self on that Day, then ye have recognized Me. Otherwise, how could My creation recognize Me? For I am indeed the Unseen, from Whose grasp escapeth nothing in the heavens or on earth or whatsoever lieth between them.
Verily, I am the Ever-Living Who dieth not. I shall surely give life to all My creation on the Day of Resurrection through their recognition of My Self. This indeed is My favor unto the believers. And We shall cause all My creation to die on the Day of Resurrection through their veiling from the Manifestation of My Self. This indeed is true justice for those who are veiled.
Know then, O My creation! I have created neither heaven with its loftiness, nor earth with its expanse, nor sea with its depths, nor mountain with its height, nor anything with its might, except for Him Whom We shall manifest on the Day of Resurrection through these My verses and My Being. Follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My light; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My mystery; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My command; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My glory; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My name; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth.
This is My hearing; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My sight; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My tongue; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. These are My hands; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My splendor; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My majesty; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My beauty; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My grandeur; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My light; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth.
This is My mercy; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. These are My words; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My perfection; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. These are My names; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My might; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My knowledge; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My power; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My good-pleasure; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My honor; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth.
This is My sovereignty; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My dominion; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My exaltation; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My bounty; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. These are My signs; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My grace; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth. This is My generosity; follow ye Him, for He, verily, is the Certain Truth.
Verily, I shall bestow My blessings upon thee, O Manifestation of My Self on the Day of Resurrection, and upon those who abide beneath thy shadow and who believe in that which hath been sent down unto thee. These are My names from before and after, and these are My guides in the kingdom of Command and Creation and whatsoever lieth between them. All seek thee, and all through thee turn unto Me. And My splendor be upon you at all times, before all time and after all time, from Him Whom We shall make manifest on the Day of Resurrection in truth. We, verily, have power over all things. We, verily, are cognizant of all things. We, verily, are the Lord of all worlds. We, verily, are the Beloved of all worlds. We, verily, are the Goal of all worlds. We, verily, are the God of all things and the God of all worlds.

title: BB00223: Ziyarat for the first [to believe]
text:
The First Visitation Prayer, upon him be the Glory of God
In the Name of God, the Most Luminous, the Most Luminous
The Glory from God be upon His Most Luminous Light and upon those who resemble that Light among His Most Manifest, Most Manifest Guides. I testify that God, glorified be He, has ever been from time immemorial and will ever be as He has been. His are the most beautiful names, from before and after, and the most exalted similitudes in the kingdom of the heavens and earth. There is no God but Him, the Mighty, the Beloved.
God created naught in His Most Exalted Paradise except that He created in relation to it religion, and all its particular aspects are manifestations of the Mighty One in the Divine Garden, and all its joyous aspects are manifestations of Glory in Paradise. Therefore, remember what was ordained in that religion in the days of the appearance of the Eternal Dawn and the Ancient Dayspring. Verily, the greatest of what transpired was first what was ordained for Him, then for the First Living One, then for His guides, as mentioned in the Book.
Therefore, remember what was ordained for that Living One and for the First One to whom God revealed Himself, for that Living Spirit in those Primary Letters. Those Divine Letters have acquired the glory of God, exalted be His glory, and have been clothed in the majesty of God, exalted be His majesty, and have been adorned with the beauty of God, exalted be His beauty, and have been magnified by the grandeur of God, exalted be His grandeur, and have been illumined by the light of God, exalted be His light, and have been elevated by the sovereignty of God, exalted be His sovereignty, and have been exalted by the loftiness of God, exalted be His loftiness, and have been made impregnable by the impregnability of God, exalted be His impregnability, and have been strengthened by the might of God, exalted be His might, and have been raised by the transcendence of God, exalted be His transcendence, and have been endowed with the knowledge of God, exalted be His authority, and have been empowered by the power of God, exalted be His power, and have been blessed with the good-pleasure of God, exalted be His good-pleasure, and have been ennobled by the nobility of God, exalted be His glory, and have been invested with the dominion of God, exalted be His dominion, and have been granted the sovereignty of God, exalted be His sovereignty.
When thou desirest to present thyself before that Unity, begin with the remembrance of God and His praise in such wise that shouldst thou attain unto Him Whom God shall make manifest, exalted be His proof, thou shalt not be veiled by the Most Exalted One from those Most Exalted Letters, for all that is in the heavens and earth and what lies between them shall come before Him on the Day of Resurrection as servants. Thereafter, seek permission at the gates of that House, then enter by God’s leave and say before the Letter Sin or whomsoever thou willest:
The Glory be upon thee, O Essence of God! Then the Majesty be upon thee, O Camphor of God! Then the Beauty be upon thee, O Soul of God! Then the Grandeur be upon thee, O Being of God! Then the Light be upon thee, O Entity of God! Thou hast been raised up and there is none above thee in elevation, then thou hast descended and there is none like thee in humility. How lofty is thy station and how glorious thy rank, wherein God hath honored thee with faith in the Manifestation of His Self before all things and hath created in thee the word of the Covenant before all things. Through thee hath God opened the gates of the Bayan and created the essences of Paradise. There is no right after God like thy right over all who dwell in the kingdom of the heavens and earth and what lies between them.
Thou hast been exalted until thou hast been invested with the mantles of Primal Unity from the Dawning-Place of the Sun of Primality. Therefore, all glorify through thee, all sanctify through thee, all unite through thee, all magnify through thee. Thou wert never abased, as God hath ever been thy strengthener, nor wert thou ever vanquished, as God hath ever been thy victor. May God, exalted be His glory, be pleased with thy good-pleasure and send down His vengeance upon those who are not pleased with the exaltation of thy power. What heart does not grieve for thee, when thou hast glorified God in words both outwardly and inwardly? What soul does not sorrow for thee, when thou hast praised God openly while standing? What being does not mourn for thee, when thou hast unified God manifestly and supremely? What body’s tears do not flow from its eyes upon its cheeks, when thou hast magnified God thy Lord openly and loftily? Thou didst worship God thy Lord after witnessing the veiling of all His creation, and thou didst desire the exaltation of thy Creator’s mention after witnessing all being extinguished therein.
How exalted is thy right over those in the Bayan, and how lofty thy station in that Paradise! None hath believed in God, nor in the Letters of the Seven, except that he acknowledged thy right therein and thy response to thy Lord’s command before all souls in His presence. Thou didst take the maidens of the gardens of unity before any heaven or earth or aught between them was created, and thou didst ascend unto God and dwell with Him when none but thee existed before God in prostration. God hath ever loved those who grieve for thee, and God hath ever loved those who exalt thy mention, and God hath ever loved those who acknowledge thy right, and God hath ever loved those who appear before thee, and God hath ever loved those who invoke blessings upon thee, and God hath ever loved those who take vengeance on such as are veiled from thee and curse those who are proud before thee.
The heavens and the earth and all between them wept at the loftiness of thy affliction, and the kingdom on high unto the lowest atom grieved at the sublimity of thy calamity. Thou didst love God thy Lord with a response resplendent, majestic, beauteous, magnificent, luminous, great, mighty, exalted, sovereign, powerful, well-pleased, noble, loving, manifest, hidden, transcendent, impregnable and unconquerable—a response that filled the highest heavens with the words “there is no God but God,” and the lowest earths with the words “there is no God but God,” and all below them with the words “there is no God but God,” and all above them with the words “there is no God but God,” and all beneath them with the words “there is no God but God.” How glorious art thou as a Gate towering and lofty! How exalted art thou as a Book sublime and impregnable!
How many servants in Islam were strengthened by thy might and entered God’s religion through the grace of thy manifestation before thy throne of glory, yet all became distant from thy presence when thou didst appear before God thy Creator. Nay, by thy glory, all they comprehended of God’s religion before did not equal thy response. Yea, in that Manifestation, while this endureth until the Day of Resurrection, this one, if he entereth not herein, perisheth and hath neither highest station nor mightiest seat. Thou didst attain until thou reached the throne on high and drew nigh, thou didst arrive at the distance of two bow-lengths or closer, when thou didst not comprehend in the latter life greater than what thou didst comprehend in the former life, for thy delivery of thy Lord’s message in those numbered days was greater than what thou hadst delivered before.
Upon thee be from God, exalted be His glory, then from the Point of Reality, then from thyself, then from the Letters who were guided by thy guidance, then from all who enter that religion until the Day of Resurrection, that which befitteth the loftiness of God’s grace in thee and the sublimity of God’s bounty with thee. Then upon thee and upon those martyred in thy path and those who joined thee in the highest pavilion of Paradise that which should descend from God, the One, the Bestower. Verily He is the Single, the Supreme, the Transcendent, the All-Glorious.
