title: BB00248: Ziyarat for the first [to believe]
text:
Visitation for the last [to ascend], upon him be the Glory of God the Manifest
In the name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Upon thee rest the splendor of God, then the peace of all who have believed in Him, both before and after. O Thou Divine Rising Sun, Eternal Manifestation of the Lord, Sacred Countenance of Glory, Impregnable Eternal Word, and Exalted Fruit of Oneness! How lofty is the exaltation of Thy mention, whereunto all manifestations culminate and all signs return. Through Thee shall God be glorified, through Thee shall God be sanctified, through Thee shall God be unified, and through Thee shall God be magnified.
Thou worshippest none but God, my Lord and Thy Lord; Thou unitest with none save Him, my Creator and Thy Creator; Thou sanctifiest none except Him, my Fashioner and Thy Fashioner; and Thou glorifiest none but Him, my Maker and Thy Maker. How exalted is Thy station with God, whereby all created things are severed from Him, and how glorious is Thy elevation in the Book, whereby all existence turneth toward God!
Verily, Thou art the Glorifier in the depths of divinity through Thine inmost heart, and Thou art the Sanctifier in the seas of omnipotence through Thine essential spirit, and Thou art the Unifier in the manifestations of the kingdom and dominion through Thine own self, and Thou art the Magnifier in the heights of holiness and glory through the essence of Thy physical being.
I testify that Thou art pure, purifying, and purified. Nay, God hath sanctified Thee beyond such mention and purified Thee beyond such praise, for all that turneth toward Thee becometh pure, and every fire that draweth nigh unto Thee becometh light. Thou art not abased, for by God, God is Thy Exalter! Thou art not alone, for by God, God is Thy Uplifter!
By Thy right over all created things, than which there exists nothing greater in all creation, and by the manifestation of Thy revelation unto all existence, than which there exists nothing mightier in all invention, from the beginning of Thy primacy that hath no beginning unto the end of Thine ultimacy that hath no end—all circle round Thy Will, prostrate themselves before God through Thy Countenance, worship God through Thy Face, and dwell in the kingdom of the heavens and earth and what lieth between them through Thy decree.
Were the veil to be lifted from the eyes of all who possess spirit, they would surely gather there and weep for Thee until their spirits departed from their bodies. In this, my station, I draw near unto Thee through my turning toward Thee, though none be with me, finding therein my rest and taking pride therein above all things, for all glory belongeth to whoso knoweth Thee, and all fire to whoso is veiled from meeting Thee.
Through Thee have all glorifiers glorified in the heights of their hearts, all essences praised in their realm of might, all realities unified in their sanctified elevation, and all identities magnified in their sublime glory. Thou hast risen, and above Thee there is no elevation. Thou hast brought low the pillars of the heavens and earth and all that lieth between them through the loftiness of Thy ascension and the sublimity of Thy inaccessibility. Then Thou didst draw nigh in such wise that nothing equals Thee or compares with Thee, whereby all are veiled by Thy loftiness in Thy loftiness and Thy transcendence in Thy arrival before God, Thy Lord.
Nay, by Thy glory, when Thou didst ascend to the dust, I shall surely prostrate myself through Thee unto God and take pride in Thy presence and in praising Thee. And when the decree was fulfilled upon Thee, I shall surely magnify Thee and exalt Thy station, for I have witnessed no fruit more inaccessible than Thee in the Book, nor any abstract essence more like Thee in the verses.
Thou hast indeed unified God throughout all manifestations until Thou didst unify in the ultimate manifestation of limitations. God hath ever sent down upon Thee and upon whoso seeketh Thy good-pleasure that which beseemeth the loftiness of His holiness and the sublimity of His bounty.
How exalted is Thy calamity in the Book, how great is Thy tribulation in creation, and how mighty is that which was decreed upon Thee in the kingdoms of earth and heaven! Can any heart remain unmoved at Thy mention, or any soul fail to be rent asunder upon hearing of Thy tribulation? What essence hath borne the manifestations of Thy love, and what eyes have not shed tears before the seat of Thy glory in the face of the decrees of Thy Cause?
By Thy right! My heart is unable to make mention of those who have grown proud against Thee and veiled themselves from meeting Thee, for in all things they worship God through Thee, prostrate themselves before God through Thee, bow down before God through Thee, and humble themselves before God through Thee. A single hair of Thy body is more beloved unto God than the essence of their being, let alone their deeds. They have no mention with God, nor with those who have believed in Him and His verses.
Thus doth God bestow His grace upon Thee with that which draweth nigh all who are brought nigh, and which all the God-fearing desire. God hath created for Thee in Paradise a most glorious pavilion that none can attain unto through what they have comprehended. Blessed art Thou and what Thou hast drunk!
By Thy glory! In Thy Lord’s knowledge there exists no paradise greater than what Thou hast attained in God, glorified be His majesty, nor any fire more intense for those who have veiled themselves from Thee than their veiling themselves from Thy countenance, for what God hath promised in the Hereafter shall be manifested in that life.
I testify before God and all things that Thy beginning and Thine end are for God and in God. God shall exalt Thy station to the highest heights and most sublime sovereignty through that which shall delight Thine eyes on the Day of Resurrection before God. Grieve not, for God shall cause Thee to dwell and descend in the chambers of Thy victory and the heights of Thy life where Thou shalt behold Thy loved ones from among Thy kindred and Thy friends from among those who love Thee in the Most Exalted Paradise and before Thee in the Most Glorious Paradise.
All begin from water and return to clay. How blessed is he who preserves between these the mention of his soul until the Day of Resurrection, even as Thou hast preserved it. This is God’s bounty unto whomsoever He willeth of His creation, and this is God’s generosity unto whomsoever He desireth of His servants.
Upon Thee be the blessings of God and His mercy in Thy return and resting-place, in Thy rising and sitting, Thy repose and ascent, Thy nearness and contentment with Thyself. Thou art the Mirror wherein naught is seen except God, as I have seen naught in Thee save Him.
Thou art the First through Thy Lord’s manifestation, and the Last through Thy Lord’s concealment, the Outward through Thy Lord’s exaltation, and the Inward through Thy Lord’s inaccessibility. Upon Thee and upon them that love Thee and upon those who have attained unto the meeting with Thy Lord in God’s path be that which befitteth the sublimity of His generosity and the excellence of His grace.
Verily He is the All-Compelling, the All-Bountiful. And verily there is no God but Him, the Gracious, the All-Munificent.

title: BB00666: Ziyarat for the first [to believe]
text:
Visitation Tablet for the first [to believe], upon Him be the Glory of God, the King of Eternity
In the Name of God, the Most Glorious, the Most Glorious
Verily, I am God! There is no God but Me, and all else is My creation. Say: O My creation! Worship ye Me alone. Verily, I am God! There is no God but Me. I have been from all eternity, and before and after all things, all seek Me out.
Verily, I am God! There is no God but Me. I was pure and ethereal before and after all things, and all worship Me. There was no beginning to what I have created, nor any end. All within the bounds of their creation, by My command, before and after, make mention of Me.
I made Myself known on the Day of Resurrection through My verses. The first to know Me was He of the Seven Letters [ʿAli Muhammad, the Bab], mighty and glorious; then He of the Eight Letters [Mulla Husayn], powerful and inaccessible; then the Guides of the Most Glorious in God’s Book; then whosoever entereth the Bayan until such time as shall be raised up unto Me from the Manifestation of My Self. All are guides unto Him of the Eight Letters, and all through Him turn unto Me.
This is the Essence I have chosen from among all My servants. O all things! Ye shall make mention of Her. This is the Pure One I have selected for Myself. O all things! Ye shall remember Her. This is the Pristine One I have chosen for Myself. O all things! Ye shall commemorate Her. This is the Ethereal One I have elected for Myself. O all things! Ye shall call Her to mind.
He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden. Through Him do all fulfill their duty unto Me. Were it not for His presence before Me, I would not have made Myself known through any other, and this sufficeth as My testimony unto Myself. Thus have We ever been witnesses.
Through Him was the Bayan revealed, and We were indeed cognizant thereof. After I made Myself known to Him and established Him as the Manifestation of My Self—there is no God but I, and all worship Me—I made Him the Gate of My knowledge for whosoever desireth to believe in Me and in My verses, that all who are created and shall be created might through Him be brought before Me.
From the first day I created Him until the last mention shall be made, I have witnessed naught but the remembrance of My Self—verily, there is no God but I, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting. After I made Myself known to Him, He delivered the messages of His Lord unto all the worlds. He endured in the Cause of God what He witnessed from those who were given the Book aforetime, though all were but as scattered dust within His grasp.
When He saw that all were veiled from the presence of their Lord, though all stood firm by His command and all sought other than Me—they knew Me yet wished not to recognize Me—His Being could not bear to see any upon the earth veiled from the knowledge of their Lord. Thus did He strive against those who through Him had turned unto Me. They knew not God, their Lord, they who fought against Him, else they would not have shown pride toward Him. Had they known Him, they would have prostrated themselves before Him as they prostrate themselves night and day.
Until He was martyred in My path, along with those who were with Him among the guides of His Self, and all returned to that from which they were created by their Lord’s command, and all at that moment rejoice in My knowledge. Before them is whatsoever they desire—therein are maidens fair as hidden pearls, therein are youths like treasured crimson rubies, therein are all manner of noble garments they don with pride, therein is every bounty they desire, say what they will therein, and they do naught but glorify. At all times do they sanctify, at all times do they magnify, at all times do they extol, and at all times do they revere. My wrath hath descended upon those who knew them not, and in the fire shall they abide forever. God will visit His retribution upon them by their own hands and the hands of all the believers together, and they shall take vengeance upon themselves by their own selves, and curse themselves with names from before them from their own midst, yet they perceive not.
It behooveth everyone on earth to seek shelter beneath the shadow of him who hath believed in Me, even though all be veiled. But those who are in Islam, they believe in Him. He it is Who hath appointed for you this religion and hath commanded you therein that ye judge not against Me, for I am a Messenger from the Lord of the worlds. Thus are ye tested in the Day of Resurrection in the manifestation of My Self. He it is Who hath appointed for you your religion that ye may not be veiled from Him on the day of the appearance of the Truth.
And verily I shall send blessings upon thee, O My Splendor, then upon all things, a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. And verily I shall send blessings upon thee, O My Glory, then upon all things, a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. And verily I shall send blessings upon thee, O My Beauty, then upon all things, a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. And verily I shall send blessings upon thee, O My Grandeur, then upon all things, a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. And verily I shall send blessings upon thee, O My Light, then upon all things, and thy light shall not be extinguished in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and what lieth between them until the Day of Resurrection. This is what hath been ordained by God, the Supreme, the Self-Subsisting.
And verily I shall send blessings upon thee and upon all who seek shelter beneath thy shadow, of the first and the last, the manifest and the hidden. These are the gems of the Qur’an which We have sent down therein upon thee, for We were indeed cognizant thereof. Thus have We returned them unto thee even as We began them from thee, for We have power over all things.
O ye who are in Islam! This sufficeth you that ye have slain Him Who ordained your religion for you and then the martyrs of His Cause, and this disgrace shall not leave you until the Day of Resurrection, and in that fire shall ye abide forever, except if ye return unto God, your Lord. Then when what your hands have wrought shall be struck upon your faces, those in Paradise shall be distinguished from those in the fire, and soon shall ye yourselves know—before your death or after your death or in your transformation—and ye shall surely receive from God the recompense of what ye have earned.
Ye were naught on earth but perishing ones; nay, the very letters of annihilation are ashamed to be associated with you, for ye have committed deeds such that annihilation itself disdaineth to mention you. O people of the Bayan! Are ye not ashamed? Slay no one ever, for whoso slayeth a soul, it is as though he hath slain all mankind, and whoso giveth life to a soul, it is as though he hath given life to all mankind.

title: BB00678: Ziyarat for the first [to believe]
text:
Visitation for the First [to believe]
In the Name of God, the Most Glorious, the Most Glorious
Verily the glory rest upon thee, O First Temple! Then majesty be upon thee, then beauty be upon thee, then grandeur be upon thee, then light be upon thee, then mercy be upon thee, then the names be upon thee, then might be upon thee, then knowledge be upon thee, then power be upon thee, then good-pleasure be upon thee, then love be upon thee, then honor be upon thee, then sovereignty be upon thee, then dominion be upon thee, then grace be upon thee, then the verses be upon thee, then the words be upon thee, then the manifestations be upon thee, through that which the knowledge of thy Lord hath encompassed from before and after, and His power extendeth over all things in the kingdoms of Command and Creation and what lieth between them. Verily, He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.
In the Name of God, the Most Exalted, the Most Exalted!
All glory be to thee, O Second Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Beautiful, the Most Beautiful!
All glory be to thee, O Third Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Great, the Most Great!
All glory be to thee, O Fourth Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Luminous, the Most Luminous!
All glory be to thee, O Fifth Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Merciful!
All glory be to thee, O Sixth Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Great, the Most Great!
All glory be to thee, O Seventh Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Mighty, the Most Mighty!
All glory be to thee, O Eighth Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Knowing, the Most Knowing!
All glory be to thee, O Ninth Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Powerful, the Most Powerful!
All glory be to thee, O Tenth Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Pleasing, the Most Pleasing!
All glory be to thee, O Eleventh Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Loving, the Most Loving!
All glory be to thee, O Twelfth Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Noble, the Most Noble!
All glory be to thee, O Thireenth Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Central, the Most Central!
All glory be to thee, O Fourteenth Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Sovereign, the Most Sovereign!
All glory be to thee, O Fifteenth Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Ancient, the Most Ancient!
All glory be to thee, O Sixteenth Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Generous, the Most Generous!
All glory be to thee, O Seventeenth Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Permanent, the Most Permanent!
All glory be unto thee, O Eighteenth Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
In the Name of God, the Most Manifest, the Most Manifest!
All glory be unto thee, O Nineteenth Temple! [Same blessings repeated]
Glorified art Thou, O my God! The proofs of the temples of Thy chosen ones in the Bayan cannot be numbered, nor the like of the circles of Thy handmaidens therein. And verily, as Thou hast taught me and all Thy creation, the First is One, and after that the temples and circles in their most exalted, most impregnable, most holy, and most sovereign states, and what is in them and upon them of the manifestations of Thy names and the revelations of Thine examples, since all things return unto the temple of man. Therefore, O my God, cause all who are in the Bayan whom Thou hast loved to return unto the temple of Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest on the Day of Resurrection, prostrating before Thy face, worshipping Thy Being, devoted to Thy Self, remembering Thy verses, grateful for Thy favors, content with Thy decree, patient in Thy good-pleasure, submissive to Thy Essence, humble before Thy Identity, supplicating the Sovereign of Thy Oneness, exalted through the exaltation of the King of Thy Singleness, lest any temple and its deeds be lost, and that all Thou hast planted may bear fruit to the highest degree possible. Verily, Thou art powerful and mighty over that, and knowing and encompassing all things.

title: BB00153: Ziyarat for the two hidden names
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy!
The splendor of God rest upon you both, O ye two luminous lights, ye two blazing flames, ye two exalted names, ye two impregnable words, ye two celestial fruits, ye two concealed countenances! And upon you be glory, and beauty from your right hand, and grandeur from your left hand, and light before you, and mercy behind you, and might above your heads, and bounty beneath your feet.
God hath never ceased to send down upon you both from every splendor its most splendid, from every glory its most glorious, from every beauty its most beautiful, from every grandeur its most grand, from every light its most luminous, from every mercy its most extensive, from all words their most perfect, from every might its mightiest, from all names their greatest, from every will its most effective, from every knowledge its most penetrating, from every power its most potent, from every utterance its most pleasing, from all questions their most beloved, from every dominion its most enduring, from every sovereignty its most excellent, from every loftiness its most sublime, from every bounty that which hath no equal, and from every good that which hath no parallel.
Ye have ascended unto God, your Lord, even as ye began with God, your Lord. God hath never ceased to gaze upon you and to send down His mercy upon whosoever remembereth you and grieveth for you and weepeth for that which was decreed for you in the path of God.
And verily, upon you and upon whosoever hath ascended unto God, your Lord, be that which befitteth the sublimity of God’s grace and His bounty, and the exaltation of His generosity and munificence. Verily, He is the Mighty, the All-Bountiful.

title: BB00099: Ziyarat for Thursday night (Ziyara jami’a)
text:
Part 1: “Praise be to God, besides Whom there…”
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Praise be to God, besides Whom there is no God, the Living, the Sovereign, the Self-Subsisting. Verily, the Glory from God be upon the First Unity, then upon its numbers, then upon those that resemble those numbers wherein naught is seen save the First Unity. And then, if thou art, on such a Friday night, at one of the seats of the numbers of Unity, or at the dust wherefrom its essence hath ascended unto God from the beginning of the Bayan until the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest, when He giveth permission for its exaltation—then purify thyself from all that thou abhorrest. And when thou hast completed what God hath prescribed for thee of thy prayer, enter that seat in such wise that shouldst thou attain the Day of Resurrection, thou wouldst present thyself before none save God or before what God hath commanded thee.
For verily this shall profit thee in the night. Establish thyself in thy seat there and remember what hath transpired in the Bayan of decree, and let thy tears flow from thine eyes in the paths of glory and exaltation, and whatsoever lieth between them and beneath them. For verily God loveth the tear that floweth in the paths of His love for the exaltation of His Word, and at the moment when thy tears flow from thine eyes, God shall, of His grace, forgive whatsoever thou hast encompassed in knowledge. He, verily, is the All-Bountiful, the All-Subtle.
Then, when thy grief hath subsided, recite this prayer:
Glory be unto Thee, O God, my God! I bear witness at this moment, on this Friday night, and so doth every thing, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone, with no partner. Thine is the kingdom and Thine the praise. Thou givest life and causest death, then causest death and givest life. And verily Thou art the Living Who dieth not, and the King Whose sovereignty passeth not away, and the Just Who wrongeth not, and the Sovereign Who changeth not, and the One from Whose grasp nothing escapeth, whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them. And Thou art, verily, powerful over all things.
Thou didst create me, O my God, in the realm of creation from the beginning that hath no beginning until Thou didst bring me to this hour. I bear witness, and so doth every thing, that Thou hast brought all things into being through me, and I do observe the paths which Thou hast established among Thy creation, whereby all do worship Thee, glorify Thee, sanctify Thee, unite with Thee, and magnify Thee. And all, apart from Thy will, are Thy servants, and apart from Thy good-pleasure are Thy worshippers, save those who prostrate themselves before Thee in the Bayan and worship Thee according to what Thou didst reveal unto me in that Manifestation in most excellent exposition.
I praise Thee for having created me, then the Letters of the Living by Thy power, then all who have believed through Thy might until the Day of Him Whom Thou shalt manifest. We are, verily, Thy servants in truth upon the earth and Thy worshippers in justice thereon. How many faces, O my God, have prostrated themselves before Thy grandeur on this night, and all have fallen short of Thee save those who prostrate themselves before Thee through my Manifestation! And how many hearts have submitted themselves before Thee in this hour, and all have returned unto themselves save those that submitted in that Manifestation, for these return unto Thee! And how many eyes weep from fear and awe of Thee, and all are rejected by Thee save those who fear Thee in the Bayan and stand in awe of Thy justice!
And how many bodies toil in the paths of Thy good-pleasure that Thou mightest accept from them a remembrance, and all are barred from Thy will save those who toil for Thee in the Bayan with joy and fragrance according to what Thou hast ordained of the paths and the exposition! And how many servants strive after Thy countenance on such a night as this and call upon Thee with the clamor of their tongues and the cry of their voices, and verily these are cut off from Thy will save those who commune with Thee through him by whom Thou hast opened a path for creation.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy bounty to manifest One possessed of power and might, and to establish His dominion through Thy power and sovereignty. Do Thou clothe Him with the robe of Thy dominion and might, and array Him in the mantle of Thy glory and munificence, that He may, through Thy hidden mercy, show compassion unto all who dwell on earth, that He may cause all to enter Thy paradise and give all to drink of the water of Thy love. For I grieve over all who dwell on earth, since all were created through Me, yet I behold them in their remoteness from Thee and their estrangement from Me.
I beseech Thee therefore, O my God, on this night, by the power wherewith Thou hast empowered it, by the might wherewith Thou hast endowed it, by the self-subsistence wherewith Thou hast established it, by the sanctity wherewith Thou hast hallowed it, and by the pre-existence wherewith Thou hast preordained it, that Thou send Thy blessings upon the Primal Unity and upon Him Who is Thine alone—there is no God but Thee—in the Bayan, and that Thou raise up in it One Who shall cause all on earth and all things to enter that Most Great, Most Great, Most Great, Most Great, Most Great Paradise, whose breadth is as the breadth of heaven and earth and all that lieth between them, wherein are all things without similitude, equal, peer, companion or likeness. And make all these believers in Him Whom Thou shalt manifest and prostrate themselves before His countenance through what Thou shalt elevate through the signs of Thy power.
By Thy might! Were it possible that a soul should entertain, even for an instant, any thought beneath the measure of its faith, Thou wouldst assuredly seize it and cause it to perish—better for it were this than that Thou shouldst suffer it to remain, to veil itself from God its Lord, to become vain, and to render void the fruit of its existence. For Thou, verily, hast not created the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them save in truth, pure and dedicated unto Thine own Self, apart from any beside Thee—except such as abide within the good-pleasure of Thine own Self and are established beneath the shadow of the ordinances of Thy holiness.
For such a one hath his portion according to the measure of his recognition; and were all who are in the heavens and on the earth and between them to beseech of Thy bounty that Thou wouldst bestow it upon him, Thou wouldst grant it, without that aught should be diminished from Thy sovereignty; for, inasmuch as each possesseth this and that, each is within his own degree. Glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou, O my God! I magnify Thee for what Thou hast created; and how resplendent is Thy generosity toward them whom Thou hast brought into being!
These are, O my God, the seats before Thee which Thou hast raised up through the word of the Point of the Bayan. Verily we—howsoever we be commanded to follow—shall indeed follow this; for we know not the loftiness of what Thou hast ordained for us beyond what Thou hast taught us, nor is it ours to say in the face of Thy decree, “Why didst Thou not call?” For Thou didst choose aforetime clay, and didst ascribe it unto Thyself, and it became Thy House; even so hast Thou chosen a soul, and it became Thy Vicegerent after Thy Messenger. And that which made the House to be a House was but the utterance of Thy Beloved from Thee; and make Thou the Vicegerent to be a Vicegerent by the word of Thy Beloved from Thee—that we should seek proof in none beside him, and find no testimony save him. We behold him, on that Day, before our eyes, as we behold Thy Word in a station whereunto all the worlds are powerless to attain. By this have we believed that he is from Thee, and in this there is no doubt.
And were we to behold this alone in the presence of Him Whom Thou shalt cause to appear, we would prostrate ourselves before him, ere Thou shouldst say “Why?” or “For what?” For we entered into the Bayan only for this; and whoso seeketh proof other than this, his faith shall not be accepted of him, nor shall he have any proof with Thee. For I desired that the Day of Resurrection should be even as this day, O my God, wherein I have planted the Bayan; yet on that Day I behold each one in such a state that he is veiled from the Planting of his own hand, save whomsoever Thou willest of Thy creatures. And I bear Thee witness that on that Day all are liars in their faith, save him who shall have believed in me by that proof in my latter end; and all are veiled from meeting Me, save him who believeth in me by that proof on the day of my return, my exaltation, and my sublimity.
Therefore do Thou protect, O my God, all Thy creatures; for I have planted the Tree of the Furqan, and I found not, at that time, any who would fulfil his covenant therein, or be informed of my purpose, or act purely for Thee unto the day of meeting Thee; nay, all were in far-removed desires and in veils not subtle. Do Thou, then, rend asunder, O my God, all veils between me and them through Thy power; and cause them, O my God, to know my purpose aforetime, by Thy might.

title: BB00099: Ziyarat for Thursday night (Ziyara jami’a)
section: Part 2: “They shall behold the Cause of my Lord…”
text:
Part 2: “They shall behold the Cause of my Lord…”
They shall behold the Cause of my Lord according to the measure thereof within their own selves; and whoso hath veiled himself, the severity of Thy wrath shall be upon his own self. And I bear Thee witness, and all things, that none in the Bayan shall his faith profit him, if he attain the Day of Resurrection, unless he believe in Him Whom Thou shalt cause to appear—though it be in the darkest night. For if he transgress not Thy bounds, he is within Thy paradise and Thy good-pleasure, and within the loftiness of Thy glory and Thy exaltation, and the sublimity of Thy bounty and Thine abiding—yet after that…
Glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou—far be it from me to judge any soul by its “thingness,” for the “thingness” of all things hath been brought into being for that Day; how much more so, then, when He Who shall appear, by His own “thingness,” causeth every thing to appear! Glorified art Thou: there is none other God but Thee. Glorified art Thou! Verily I have been of them that remember Thee.
Then say: Verily the Glory is from God upon you, O gems of glory; then the Majesty is from God upon you, O gems of majesty; then the Beauty is from God upon you, O gems of beauty; then the Grandeur is from God upon you, O gems of grandeur; then the Light is from God upon you, O gems of light; then the Mercy is from God upon you, O gems of mercy; then the Names are from God upon you, O gems of the names; then the Might is from God upon you, O gems of might; then the Will is from God upon you, O gems of will; then the Knowledge is from God upon you, O gems of knowledge; then the Power is from God upon you, O gems of power; then the Good-pleasure is from God upon you, O gems of good-pleasure; then the Love is from God upon you, O gems of love; then the Honour is from God upon you, O gems of honour; then the Sovereignty is from God upon you, O gems of sovereignty; then the Dominion is from God upon you, O gems of dominion; then the Bounty is from God upon you, O gems of bounty—each one of you.
Then most of you—inasmuch as ye have ascended unto God your Lord, and mounted up unto God your King, and been uplifted unto God your Possessor, and been drawn unto God your Sovereign—yours is, of the favour of God, its most excellent; and of the bounty of God, its most bountiful; and of the kindness of God, its most gentle; and of the generosity of God, its most generous; and of the bestowal of God, its most freely bestowed; and of the gift of God, its greatest; and of the beneficence of God, its nearest and its greatest; and of the signs of God, their most perfect; and of the words of God, their most wondrous; and of the manifestations of God, their most manifest; and of the effulgences of God, their most drawing; and of the names of God, their most holy; and of the attributes of God, their most ancient; and of the archetype of God, its most exalted; and of every good that hath no equal, and of every fair deed that hath no likeness, and of every remembrance that hath no peer, and of every glory that hath no companion, and of every loftiness that hath no exemplar.
Ye have, through your power, attained unto that whereat the former and the latter would rejoice; and ye have, through your detachment, possessed that which the manifest and the hidden would seek. All have been created of water and return unto dust; and ye have been created even as they were created, and ye return even as they return. Yet have ye surpassed them by that which ye have surpassed—so that God remembereth you from everlasting to everlasting, and His angels invoke blessings upon you without number and without end—not by reason of your works in His religion, but by reason of your severing yourselves from all else save God your Lord. For how many have wrought as ye have wrought, and have sought the Glory of God as ye have sought it, yet are they, even unto that time, unable to attain the path to that which ye have possessed, nor can they find any proof unto that bounty which God hath opened before you.
This is your honour with God your Lord, inasmuch as, at your threshold, the angels on high, and they that glorify, and the Cherubim, and the sanctified, and they that cry “there is not god but God,” shall descend. Yet all this would not equal that He should ennoble you by what God shall reveal through His primal bounty, and that the Manifestation of the Essence should remember you by His remembrance of you—higher is this than that every thing should remember you; and His presence there is more precious in the sight of God than that every thing should come to be present before you.
It behoveth you to recognize your Dawning-Place on the day of His appearing, apart from what your loved ones have said. It behoveth you to aid your Educator with all the loftiness that is possible within you. It behoveth you to cleave unto your King with the sublimity He meriteth from you in the sight of God. It behoveth you to be drawn by the signs of your Lord when ye hear the call of your Sovereign. It behoveth you to detach yourselves from every possessor of “thingness,” and to deliver your souls unto the Will of every possessor of will; and your souls should love that God and all His creatures should remember you. And if ye attain Him—this is the gift of God within you and upon you, and the Glory of God from Him vouchsafed unto you, until the Day of Resurrection. Then whoso earneth, beyond the measure of a single atom, shall behold it in the presence of his Lord; and whoso falleth short of that beareth witness against his own self before his Lord. Therefore await ye—verily We have been awaiting. And wait ye—verily We have been waiting.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! These are hearts that have ascended unto Thee, and spirits that have mounted up in Thy presence, and souls that have been severed unto Thee, and bodies that have been transformed beneath Thine eyes. And Thou, verily, art the Almighty over the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and the All-Subduing over them that dwell in the dominions of command and creation and whatsoever is beneath them. Do Thou then take vengeance, O my God, for Thy loved ones upon him whom Thou hast testified against, for lack of Thy love and Thy good-pleasure; and send down upon him who hath grieved in the Bayan for Thy sake—or hath borne witness beyond that—of every glory the most glorious, of every majesty the most august, of every beauty the most fair, of every greatness the most mighty, of every light the most luminous, of every mercy the most merciful, of every word the most perfect, of every name the most great, of every might the most puissant, of every will the most effectual, of every knowledge the most penetrating, of every power the most potent, of every utterance wherewith Thou art well-pleased, of every request the dearest unto Thee and the most guarded in Thy presence, of every honour the most honourable, of every sovereignty the most enduring, of every dominion the most splendid, of every loftiness the most sublime, and of every good wherewith Thou art worthy of the Most Exalted Loftiness and the most resplendent sublimity.
Verily Thou art He from Whose knowledge nothing escapeth, whether in the heavens or on the earth or whatsoever lieth between them. Thou shalt surely take vengeance upon him who hath not believed in Thee nor in Thy signs; and Thou shalt cause every favour of Thine to reach him who hath believed in Thee and then in Thy signs. For this cause do the souls of Thy glorifiers in Thy signs and Thy words, from the First One unto whatsoever Thou dost number and wherewith Thou art well-pleased—and beyond that wherewith Thou art well-pleased—cry aloud. Verily Thou art my Protector and the Protector of them that have believed in Thee. In Thee do we put our trust, in the latter life and in this. Verily Thou art sufficient: through Thee have we sought victory, and prevailed, and subdued, and been strengthened, and been protected, and been given dominion, and been exalted. There is no power and no might save through Thee. Thou art, verily, our Lord. Glorified art Thou: there is none other God but Thee. Verily we have submitted ourselves unto Thee.

title: BB00242: Kitabu’l-Huzn
text:
For the Generous One, He is the Most Generous, the Most Bountiful, the Most Kind, the Most Noble, the Most Excellent, the Possessor of Glory and Majesty.
In the Name of God, the Most Generous, the Most Generous. Verily I am God, there is no God but Me, the Most Generous, the Most Generous. God has testified… O Generous One! Clothe thyself and all things in the garment of sorrow from thy Lord for Muhammad, the Messenger of God, and for those who ascended in His shadow. Say: Verily we belong to God, and God originates all things and then causes them to return, and verily we all return unto Him.
And that Essence of Generosity was utterly effaced, and all that has come into being and will come into being through the generosity of the Lord of Glory and Majesty. For God has ever been and ever shall be, and for His Essence there has never been and never shall be a manifestation of His Own Self, since the manifestation of eternity in contingent being is through contingency itself, and in contingency there has never been and never shall be anything greater than His Most Great Will. And this is the Single Point through which in every Dispensation the beloved conditions are created through the acceptance of creation, and the glorious conditions of the Beloved are made manifest to His companions.
The first cycle represents good and paradise, while the second cycle represents that which is other than good and fire. In the estimation of them that are endued with understanding, it is expressed through negation and affirmation, which are the most subtle of elements. And He is the One for Whom there was no beginning in the realm of existence, nor shall there be an end.
And this cycle of Manifestation—which extendeth from the Dispensation of Adam, peace be upon Him, until this day, a span of twelve thousand two hundred and ten solar years—hath, in every age, appeared under a distinct Name. In each Revelation the Manifestations gone before were subjected to denial, and a judgment beneath the Truth was pronounced concerning them; and all were made believers through His own wondrous Revelation, and were rendered expectant through His subsequent appearance. He is, verily, the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden. He was Muhammad, the Messenger of God, in the former age, and today He is the Qa’im of the House of Muhammad, peace be upon Him—whose Revelation is in very truth the Revelation of the Messenger of God, in relation to those that preceded Him.
He blotteth out whatsoever He willeth and establisheth whatsoever He desireth. The Proof, moreover, is the very Proof of the Messenger of God Himself; and in the Qur’an the Almighty, the Exalted, hath not adduced argument save by that Proof alone. Through it the reality of all things is established, the authority of the Trustee made manifest, the love of Moses confirmed, and the ordinances of the Qur’an rendered sovereign. All traditions, should they conflict, are, by the judgment of the masters of tradition, rendered null. He it is in Whose Name all have believed, and unto Whom all have been ascribed; and yet behold, today, how they withhold from that believer—within whose dominion there is no peer—that which is His due.
What fire is fiercer than the fire of those companions who are severed from their true purpose? For their beginning is from Him, their return unto Him, their uprising through Him, and their life sustained for the sake of His good-pleasure; yet they commit against Him that whereof the mere hearing is itself a fire. This is the Fire of Truth for the veiled, and His Light for them that truly know. It hath been rendered into the letters H–M–F–D, and He hath been mounted upon the veil of cloud. Even so is it with every soul whom thou admittest into the ocean of His bounty—He Who was the first Manifestation of the Day of Resurrection and the Lord of the world of return.
All have been created for the meeting with the Face of God; and it is nigh that, in the very reality of truth, the mediation of the Names shall be attained. Yet the mirrors have not recognized their own reflection, and they imagine unity through the effulgent Revelation that preceded Him, which appeared in the Muhammadan Temple—peace be upon Him—whereas that Revelation hath been lifted up, even as, at the advent of the Messenger of God, the dispensation of Moses, the Spirit of God, was lifted up. Had it remained, the judgment beneath faith would not have been established.
The difference is this: that the Sun of Truth, on that Day, arose from a prior Manifestation—inasmuch as from the time of His Mission one hundred and twenty-seven years had elapsed. In this Revelation, likewise, whatsoever hath been ordained shall come to pass; yet His Name is One—that He may arise with that which hath no equal, and may set with that which hath no equal. Nevertheless, each one imagineth that whatsoever he doeth, he doeth for God’s sake; yet before God the contrary thereof shall be made manifest. And today that which God hath borne witness to from all eternity is the very thing whereunto the Divine Will hath testified.
Say: O sanctified ones of the Merciful! Have mercy on yourselves, for three hundred and thirteen persons have outstripped others from their stations, and if there were others, why did they not outstrip? And if it appears later it will be decreed for a later creation. And for all who exist in this Manifestation, God the Mighty and Glorious will grant infinite rewards in Paradise.
And regarding what has been mentioned, this glorious verse of the Qur’an should be recited 298 times, corresponding to the number of the name “the Merciful”: “Who, when affliction befalls them say: We belong to God and to Him do we return.” For which God revealed in the Qur’an the response: “These are they on whom are blessings and mercy from their Lord, and these are the followers of the right course.” And know that the Qur’anic manifestations have been lifted, and the manifestations of the Resurrection are arranged according to the number of all things, and before the one who migrates to God from among them, corresponding to the number of the Name “the Single” minus the number of ʿdal’, through the revival of sea and land.
When the path is other than this, it leads astray, otherwise one becomes adorned with the Name “the Compeller” until God grants you joy, for He is the Generous, the Bountiful. Therefore don them with the garment of grief for the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden. What ails you that on that Day you shall enter the Ridvan? Grieve not in Paradise for you are sanctified therefrom. Aid the Cause in the days of God and place your trust in God, your Lord, the Merciful. For We are all in that Day deprived in the religion of God. In God do we trust; He suffices us, and in God, their Lord, let the believers place their trust.

title: BB00051: Du’a’a’i-Avval li’l-Avval
text:
Part 1: “Glorified art Thou, O my God! I testify…”
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I testify, and all things testify, to that which Thou hast testified concerning Thyself, and all things bear witness thereunto, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone, without peer. Thine is the Kingdom and the Dominion, and Thine the Glory and the Might, and Thine the Power and the Divine Realm, and Thine the Authority and the Sapphire Realm. Thou givest life and causest death, and causest death and givest life, and verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not. Within Thy grasp is the kingdom of all things. Thou createst whatsoever Thou willest, how Thou willest, by Thy command. Thou art, verily, powerful over all things.
Moreover, I bear witness, together with the Primary Letters, the number of the Unity, to that wherewith Thy Being hath glorified itself, Thy Essence hath sanctified itself, Thy Identity hath unified itself, and Thy Self hath magnified itself, and to that which Thou hast ordained for these Divine Manifestations and Eternal Dawning-Places, and that whereby Thou hast revealed Thyself unto all things, when there was none besides Thee possessed of remembrance, neither before nor after, nor any besides Thee possessed of sovereignty in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, nor any besides Thee possessed of might or power in the kingdom of Command and Creation.
For all the evidences of Thy Lordship and the manifestations of Thy power have created the Tree of Unity, making its root the Point, its trunk the Letter Sin, its branches and fruits from its own letters, then its leaves from the manifestations of Thy names and the dawning-places of Thy examples. Thou didst desire to manifest thereby the oneness of Thy Essence, the glorification of Thy Being, the sanctification of Thy Camphor-like Nature, and that which befitteth Thy Pure Reality.
I beseech Thee, O my God, by what Thou hast enumerated upon that Tree of Thy names from the First Letters to the Seven wherein there is no name, and from the first name—Thy name the Eternal of seven letters—and what Thou hast enumerated from the rank of Will to that Most Exalted Book, and what Thou hast enumerated above this until it terminateth at Thy name the Mustaghath, since Thou hast not revealed in the Bayan any number higher than that Name. I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thy might, that Thou cause that Tree to put forth leaves with all Thy names until they are numbered to the extent of what Thy knowledge hath encompassed, for there is no limit to Thy remembrance and no end to what is with Thee.
I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thy names which Thou hast enumerated upon that Tree from the Eternal [abad] to the Mustaghath, wherein naught is seen save Thee, that Thou establish that Tree in the palm of Thy Eternality and the right hand of Thy Oneness, and that Thou cause to descend upon it in every moment from the time when Thou didst plant it in the heaven of Thy Lordship—having made its earth from its water, and its water from its fire, and its fire from its air, and all of it from its parts, and its parts from all of it, and its beginning from its end, and its outer from its inner, and its branch from its root, and its fruits from its branches, and its leaves from what Thou hast caused to grow therein—for this is a Tree that hath glorified itself through Thy glorification of it, sanctified itself through Thy sanctification of it, unified itself through Thy unification of it, and magnified itself through Thy magnification of it—One without number and Exalted beyond mention or hope that names be mentioned therein, for they are from its attributes and its manifestation unto its manifestations, and if there be concealed therein what riseth from it, it is from the foundation of its power.
All things are in the place of Thy manifestation. Glorified art Thou, there is no God but Thee, to the extent possible in creation. This is the Tree of Thy sanctification and glorification, of Thy unity and magnification, and of that which transcendeth all utterance.
Glorified art Thou beyond being described by what is possible or impossible! Rather, this is from what Thou hast specifically bestowed upon me, having made me the root of that Tree and all that returns unto it in its beginning and its end, demonstrating that Thou art [exalted] above its praise and transcendent above its knowledge. Indeed, it is a Tree that hath grown in the soil of its own self, by its own self, from naught but itself. It hath glorified its Lord through the manifestation of its own essence unto itself, by itself, and hath ascended from the beginning of names to the end of attributes through the sublimation of its camphor-like essence and the realization of its pristine nature. Verily, it is exalted above all exaltation through the exaltation of its Revealer, and sanctified above all sanctification through the sanctification of its Nurturer.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Nothing is greater in Thy sight than this Tree, for all aspects of turning unto Thee have sprung from it and return unto it. All who have declared “There is no God but Thee” have only done so through it, and all who have glorified Thee, sanctified Thee, magnified Thee, prostrated before Thee, or extolled Thee have only comprehended aught thereof through it. For hadst Thou not previously manifested Muhammad, Thy Beloved, could anyone have said “There is no God but Thee”? Even so, all things are from Thee, of Thee, with Thee, unto Thee, and there is no power except through Thee.
I testify unto Thee that this Tree’s encompassing power hath embraced all creation and invention, and its knowledge encompasseth all that is in the kingdoms of earth and heaven. It is indeed a garden whose breadth is as the breadth of the heavens and the earth and all that lieth between them. In its smallest particle is seen its supreme exaltation, and in its supreme exaltation is mentioned its power.
I beseech Thee, O God, by this Tree—than which nothing in Thy sight is its equal, nor hath it any likeness, peer, similitude, or companion—to raise it up through all Thy power to true exaltation, and to manifest it through all Thy power above every manifestation and inaccessibility. And since nothing’s reality is manifested except through its opposite, Thou hast created for it a shadow in the dust that it might know itself according to what is within it, and what is in its shadow according to what is upon it.
Thou hast made this Tree the Tree of negation at the time of Thy affirmation, and Thou didst not create it except through its acceptance after the manifestation of Thy proof upon it and the exaltation of Thy Word in the kingdoms of the heavens and earth and what lieth between them, upon it and upon what is on its right and its left and all its directions.
O God! Cast down the Tree of negation and annihilate it as though it had never existed. O God! Raise up the Tree of affirmation and manifest it in such wise that no manifestation or exaltation is possible above it. For that Tree hath ascended to the ultimate heights in the path of Thy love, while this one hath descended to the uttermost depths through what its hands have wrought. It hath descended to a depth none hath preceded it to, and I know of none equal to it. Verily, the Tree of Thy affirmation hath been raised to such a station as is not possible in contingent existence higher than this, such that some of its leaves, branches, fruits, and boughs have been adorned through the shedding of their blood.
Glorified art Thou, O God! Through this Thou hast planted the Tree of Thy sanctification, and through this have grown the leaves of Thy praise. Through this hast Thou established the essences of Thy glorification, and through this have arisen the manifestations of Thy unity. Accept, O my God, through Thy bounty, these sacred drops of blood into the water of the Tree of Thy Unity, for no blood befits Thee save these drops, since they worshipped none but Thee and prostrated before none other than Thee. Indeed, one drop thereof equals not the blood of all that is in the heavens and earth and what lies between them. Even if it were but the blood of a single letter of the One before that Tree, it would suffice to establish unity more than the blood of all upon the earth, for all things were created through it, sustained by it, and are made to die and live through it. By Thy might! A drop thereof equals not the blood of all Thy trustees, chosen ones, loved ones and friends. How exalted, magnificent, pure, lofty and holy it is, returning to its Lord as it began! That Tree stood as firm as mountain upon mountain.
Glorified art Thou! Glorified art Thou! This is Thy power in manifesting Thy proofs—one who has no equal in Thy work, no peer in the kingdom of Thy heaven and earth, no likeness in what Thou hast created. It is among the wondrous innovations of Thy Lordship that any creation would be content with the light of his heart without his Lord’s permission to ascend wholly unto Thee and attribute the blood of his being before Thee. Glorified art Thou! This stems only from the loftiness of Thy grandeur and the exaltation of Thy majesty.
I bear witness, as do those near Thee, that at that time it ascended unto Thee, the Tree of Proof stood with perfect independence, for if all upon earth were to be martyred in the path of Thy love, their blood would not equal nineteen nineteen grains of mustard seed of blood from that Name which Thou hast placed above all Thy names and through which Thou hast magnified all in the kingdom of Thy earth and heaven. Therefore, O God, reward him with the true reward of the Bayan, raise him, O God, to the highest chambers of Paradise, and enable me, O God, to meet him when I return to the primal life, in such exalted glory and sublime majesty that all faces bow before it and all souls present themselves to it.
Make him, O God, and what Thou hast ordained for him a shelter for those who believe in Me and a door for those who seek Me, for Thou art the Powerful over what Thou willest and the Inaccessible in the kingdom of creation. Raise him then, O God, with his branches, leaves and fruits to the highest heights, and send down upon him what befits the loftiness of Thy countenance and the sublimity of Thy grandeur. How great is Thy right and how mighty Thy station, that Thou hast consented that those sacred drops be sacrificed in establishing that inaccessible Tree!
Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. I have nothing except through Thee, from Thee, and unto Thee. There is no power nor strength except through Thee. Thou art the One Who sustains every soul, the Subduer of all things, the Manifest above all things, the Inaccessible above all things, and the Exalted above all things. Nothing can frustrate Thee, neither in the heavens nor on earth, nor can anything escape Thy knowledge in the kingdom of Command or Creation.
Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. Thine is the Creation and the Command, before and after. Thou hast manifested all Thy signs through the raising of the Tree of Sin, and Thou hast destroyed, through what the Tree of Piety has earned, all its letters. This is for one who has understanding or a heart capable of knowing anything, for above that there is no victory in affirming Your unity, nor below this is there abasement for one whom You have forsaken by Your power, that You might annihilate him before Your detachment. For all else are changing conditions, all returning unto that.
But O my God, since You have created in Your kingdom the wondrous manifestations of Your power, no soul can comprehend all Your victory in affirming Your unity and the obliteration of negation before it, after having fulfilled the right of fulfillment, after the days of negation had passed through what its tree had earned, where there was no extinction with You.
Thus was established at the Tree of Your affirmation the tree of the independence of Your singleness, through all being melted in the path of Your love, where there was no affirmation above that in Your knowledge. From You unto You—and You did not annihilate any tree of negation at its extinction as You annihilated this one, nor establish any tree of affirmation as You established this one through those sanctified souls upon the branch of the Tree of Your oneness and the boughs of Your eternality.
I testify with my heart, my spirit, my soul, my body, my hearing, my sight, my blood, my skin, my hair, and all that You have caused me to possess, that there is no God but You, for You have truly annihilated in the Primal Word the manifestations of negation through what their people’s hands have earned, where no extinction in creation is possible above this. And You have established the tree of Your unity, Your sanctification and Your oneness through having witnessed the blood of Your loved ones in the path of Your Cause upon the truth of inaccessibility and affirmation, where there is nothing in creation above that.
Therefore glorified are You, there is no God but You. I see in the letters of “there is no god” only the truth of Your grasp, and in “but You” only the truth of Your grace. I beseech You, O God, by Yourself, to manifest the extinction of negation through what the hearts of the weak among Your servants may comprehend and the souls of the exalted among Your chosen ones may feel, and to elevate the tree of affirmation through what may tranquilize the hearts of Your friends and cool the breasts of Your trusted ones. For all that appears of elevation is the effect of those purified bloods, and all that appears of seizure and vengeance from You upon Your enemies is the recompense of that which their hands have earned.
Therefore manifest, O God, through Your power which nothing can frustrate and Your sovereignty which is exalted above all things, the truth of manifestation in the appearances of Your affirmation and the truth of destruction in what You have made to be the letters of negation with You, through what the sight of every soul may perceive, despite its remoteness and what is in it and upon it. For none sees Your might in Your good-pleasure nor Your grasp in aught else; rather this is for those who seek guidance among the people of thought and those who are endowed with insight among the people of vision.

title: BB00051: Du’a’a’i-Avval li’l-Avval
section: Part 2: “Therefore manifest, O God, what those…”
text:
Part 2: “Therefore manifest, O God, what those…”
Therefore manifest, O God, what those in the regions and valleys may perceive, through the ultimate consciousness of what You have created therein, that the letters of Your affirmation may witness upon the throne of Your sovereignty and the independence of Your grandeur, manifest without being veiled, and that You might give them power over the letters of negation that they may seize them for what their hands have earned and take vengeance upon them for what they have unjustly inflicted in the path of Your Cause. For verily You are the One powerful over that, none besides You, and the One mighty over this, none except You.
Therefore aid, O God, with all Your aid, that through which all souls and spirits may recognize the manifestations of Your affirmation, and forsake, O God, with all Your forsaking, the tree of negation and hatsoever exists therein and thereupon, through what all minds perceive, beyond the selves and spirits of all Thy servants. Verily, Thou art over all things powerful, and there is no might nor strength except through Thee, and verily Thou art the All-Strong, the All-Powerful, the All-Mighty.
Then say, when thou dost encounter the Tree of Sin: Verily, the Most Glorious and Most Splendid Splendor from God, the Lord of the last and the first, be upon thee, O thou to whom He hath manifested Himself through what was manifested in thee, comprising all that is seen and unseen from the highest heights to the primal atom.
Through thee He hath created and sustained, then caused to die and brought to life whatsoever His knowledge hath encompassed. How exalted is thy station next to the Point, and how impregnable thy immunity before God, its Lord!
Thou hast indeed recognized thy Lord with true recognition through thy heart, spirit, soul, body and form, and hast nullified the deeds of those who profess God’s unity with their tongues while negating the Tree of Negation through their utterance.
Thou hast established, through thy acceptance to see thyself as thou hast seen, and what is in thy shadow as thou hast witnessed, the Tree of Affirmation with true affirmation through thy heart, spirit, soul, body and form—not like those who profess God’s unity with their tongues while they neither negate negation nor affirm the letters of affirmation, speaking of that which they comprehend not.
Thou art the one who hath recognized true unity in thy entirety and hast been truthful in thy recognition of God thy Lord, having witnessed the fire in negation where thou didst extinguish it with all thy might, and having witnessed Paradise in affirmation where thou didst establish it with all thy power.
This indeed is better in God’s sight than all who have recognized God’s unity before or will recognize it hereafter, for this is the essence of the Bayan for whoso desireth to recognize thy Lord.
How many servants glorify God while they eliminate not from themselves the manifestations of glorification through which they glorify! That is but a word their tongues pronounce, and they have no way therein save to recognize its Manifestations and glorify them according to their capacity.
When they turn wholly to God while glorifying Him day and night through their words—and how many servants sanctify God and praise Him while they know not the letters of praise nor affirm God, speaking of what they know without true knowledge or exposition—how can this benefit them before God unless they affirm the letters of praise to God not merely through their tongues but through the height of their power?
Perchance God may accept their words when they praise, else all praise Him, glorify Him, recognize His unity and magnify Him according to what God hath ordained, without comprehending aught of what God intended thereby.
So glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no God but God, and God is Most Great, according to what my heart, spirit, soul, body and all that my Lord hath given me have witnessed. I shall surely glorify God as He hath willed, and praise God as He hath desired, and outwardly recognize His unity just as I have recognized [the Embodiment of] the ornament of the Bayan, the essence of the Qur’an, and the Manifestation of the All-Merciful [and the Dayspring of] glory, and I shall surely magnify God by recognizing their Manifestations in the seats of their revelation, just as I have gained God before reciting His verses in what I have loved, believed in, been drawn to, magnified His Cause, and elevated His remembrance.
O my God! Prepare me for what Thou lovest and art pleased with. O my God! Make known to all the Letters of the Bayan the stations of Thy Command, that they may recognize Thy unity in Essence, then Thy unity in Attributes, then Thy unity in Deeds, then Thy unity in Worship, for verily I worship none but Thee and we worship none other than Thee, and I see naught but Thy creation in Thy grasp.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Send down upon that Divine Name, that glorious Manifestation, that eternal Light, that divine Mystery, and that Sign which hath no equal—for I have indeed recognized Thy unity as it hath appeared before Thee, while all others today profess Thy unity with their tongues yet are among the letters of negation in Thy sight and know not.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Send down upon Him and upon the Manifestations of His Self and the Gates of His Glory what Thou hast specially ordained among Thy names for the Manifestation of the Point, the Dayspring of Thyself, before all names through their attendance and prostration before It—those Eight Letters before the Ten—as befitteth the loftiness of Thy power and the exaltation of Thy majesty.
Verily I glorify Thee with my tongue and limbs and all that pertains to my return and abode, ascending thereby to the highest horizon and seeking Thy good-pleasure in that most glorious station. I see no pure glory save in glorifying Thee, though I be cast upon the dust, and I praise Thee likewise, seeing no true exaltation save in praising Thee, even shouldst Thou witness me in such a station.
I shall profess Thy unity likewise, seeing no glory of beauty save in how He Who was content to be the first Tree of Thy affirmation hath recognized Thy unity—if Thou ordainest for me this bounty from Thee; and if not, then what Thou ordainest is best for my return and abode.
I shall magnify Thee likewise, seeing no pure glory save in recognizing Thy grandeur and the exaltation of the Manifestations of Thy eternity, though I witness in but one letter thereof that it possesseth not even a garment to clothe it, after Thou hast created all things for God and through Him.
Glorified art Thou: there is none other God but Thee. This is what I have caused Thee to witness unto through the very essence of my being; and I have glorified Thee with the camphor of mine own selfhood, and sanctified Thee with the quintessence of mine “I-ness,” and confessed Thine oneness in my inmost self and in my outward state. Thus, on that Day, I acquit all who are in the Fire, in that I am, verily, quit of it and of all that are therein; and I testify concerning those who are in Paradise that they abide beneath the shadow of the shades of the Tree of Thy unity. They love me, and I shall assuredly love them in the path of Thy love. I have not appointed love for any lover of God save in the path of Thy oneness; and time hath singled me out unto Thee in this my station, by reason of that which I have spoken in Thy praise—and beyond this there is naught. Thine, therefore, be praise for this; and from Thee … for that. And how can I have power to perform aught of Thy praise, or to manifest any portion of Thy glorification?
Nay, by Thy might! Thy good-pleasure towards me—though I be but this clay—is better than the sovereignty of the world to come and of this world. For when Thou takest me unto Thyself, if I be within Thy good-pleasure Thou wilt sustain me in Thy good-pleasure; and though Thou shouldst destroy me throughout the East and the West of the earth, I would seek refuge from aught save Thy good-pleasure at the moment Thou summonest me unto Thee, in whatsoever state. Nay rather, Thy good-pleasure profiteth me in that hour in which Thou sustainest me thereby, even as it sustaineth me at that time when Thou didst uplift them unto Thee through what Thou didst send down from Thy presence—of the signs of Thy good-pleasure, the manifestations of Thy bounties, and the abodes of Thy favour.
Nay, by Thy might! Were Thou to love me in the manner Thou wiliest that I should love Thee—then if Thou shouldst give me dominion over the East and the West of the earth, I would love that only because of Thy love for me; and if Thou shouldst love that I behold myself in such a state, I would love it for the love wherewith Thou hast caused me to love it. For when the spirit is wholly severed from all else, that which reacheth me from God is Thy good-pleasure and Thy meeting; and that which uplifteth me unto the loftiest height of the chambers of good-pleasure is none other than Thy bounty and Thy gift.
Therefore unto Thee do I entrust the Tree of Thy oneness in me, with me, upon me, before me, after me, above me, beneath me, before my face, and from every direction. However Thou dost cause it to flourish, that is best for it; however Thou dost make it firm, that is glory for it; however Thou dost raise it up, that is a bounty for it from Thy presence. For naught is hidden from Thy knowledge, and all that Thou causest to happen to it is what Thou hast chosen for it.
Unto Thee be praise in the heights of praise, unto Thee be glory in the summit of glory, unto Thee be sovereignty and exaltation, unto Thee be might and invincibility, unto Thee be radiance and joy, unto Thee be awe and detachment, unto Thee be power and grandeur, unto Thee be majesty and splendor, unto Thee be love and good-pleasure, unto Thee be the examples and the names, unto Thee be […] Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee. Thou hast ever been and will ever be. Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee in whatsoever Thou hast created or wilt create by Thy power in all existence.
Therefore raise me up unto Thee at all times through that which causeth my heart to accept Thy remembrance, even if it be but a single remembrance. And cause my heart to dwell in remembrance of the Manifestations of Thy Self, even if it be but a single remembrance. Though I be immersed in the oceans of verses and soar in the heaven of words where there is neither beginning nor end, yet this is but provision for those among Thy near ones who desire to ascend unto Thee, Thy chosen pure ones, Thy sincere servants, and Thy tested servants.
That which satisfieth my heart is that there is no God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thine is the kingdom and Thine is the praise. Thou givest life and causest death, and Thou causest death and givest life. Naught is hidden from Thy knowledge and naught escapeth Thee, neither in the heavens nor on the earth nor between them, and Thou art powerful over all things.
Then say unto him: O Essence of utterance, Camphor of the Qur’an, Countenance of Glory, Sign of the All-Merciful, and Mystery of creation! My heart findeth no rest save through Thee, nor my spirit save through Thee, nor my soul save through Thee, nor my body save through Thee, being certain that naught is hidden from Thy knowledge, no voice is veiled from Thee, and no places nor boundaries of any numbered thing can come between me and Thee. I shall prepare myself to meet Thee again after the first time, for unto God belong the last and the first. He raiseth me up unto Thee again as He willeth, even as He caused me to descend upon Thee in the highest horizon. I love not to part from Thy dust, yet God hath ordained for me what He hath ordained from the station which He hath given me, and for each is a portion from His presence.
Therefore I shall return from Thy presence hoping that Thou wilt permit me and raise me unto Thee better than Thou didst raise me before, and that Thou wilt exchange my station there for my station with Thee, and that Thou wilt grant me to attain Thy presence on the day of Thy return, and that Thou wilt make me among those who have believed in the name of Thy Lord, who have recognized His signs, who have been guided by the light of Thy guidance, and who have been exalted through the exaltation of Thy beloved ones. For this is in Thy hands, as God hath entrusted unto Thee the command of His servants from before and after, and there is no power except in God. All are His servants and all shall return unto Him.
I seek refuge with God, Thy Lord, from being among those who expect not Thy days, who curse not those who love Thee not, who believe not in Thee, and who follow not what Thou hast borne of the Book of God. And should I be of these, then upon me be the curse of God and the curse of all whom God hath created or will create. And if I be not of these, then upon me be the blessings of God and the blessings of all that He hath created, for this is the Most Glorious honor from His presence for those who believe in His signs. Thus doth God cause to flow from the tongues of those who showed pride before Thee the curse of their own souls through their words, which shall testify against them on the Day of Resurrection before Thy Lord, even though on that Day they shall speak without knowing. Thus shall God take vengeance upon the letters of negation and send down His mercy upon the letters of truth from His presence through what He revealeth in the Book by His command, for He hath power over all things.

title: BB00228: Du’a’a’l-Khamis li’l-Avval
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
The Fifth Prayer
Verily, we are God’s and unto Him do we return. Glorified art Thou, O God! Thou art the Lord of destiny and decree, the Sovereign of permission and tribulation, the King of creation and composition, the Beloved of all who are on earth and in heaven, and the Ordainer of all things in accordance with what leadeth to the horizon of contentment. How can I remember Thee, O my God, at this time after having witnessed in Thy path, from among Thy creatures in the world, Thy holy lights, Thy manifestations among the most exalted ones, and Thy appearances at the Dawning-place of remembrance? Exalted, magnificent, transcendent and elevated is that which destiny hath ordained to be executed and creation hath made the ways of contentment to flow in the manifestations of Thy names.
Glorified art Thou, O God! Thou art the Seeker of those holy bloods, the Upraiser of those enchanted spirits, the Attractor of those exalted hearts, and the Fashioner of those unapproachable bodies. Thou hast ever been One God, Single, Unique, Eternal, Self-Subsisting, Ever-Living, All-Compelling. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou wilt ever be as Thou hast been. Thou hast taken no protector and art not joined with anything, and Thou hast no partner in what Thou hast created, nor any guardian in what is Thine. Thou hast ever been alone in bringing things into being, dominant over all in the kingdoms of earth and heaven, transcendent above all things through Thy sovereign decree, and elevated above all things through the authority of Thy command.
Therefore, O God, send down Thy blessings upon those who gather their wealth to be known in the path of the spots which Thou hast chosen above the earth for the manifestations of Thy unity, and upon those who ascend unto them through what Thou hast ordained in them of the exaltedness of their love and the detachment of their beings, and upon the ears that have heard mention of their calamities, and upon the eyes that have shed tears in their exalted visitations, and upon the tongues that have remained silent at the raising of their word, upon the hands that write of what was ordained to pass upon them from their beginning to their end, and upon the hearts that were humbled at the elevation of their remembrance, and upon the faces that fell prostrate before the sublimity of Thy majesty in their regard—for these are Thy chosen ones whom Thou hast selected for the seats of Thy glory, and Thou hast caused Thy paradise to yearn for them in what Thou hast ordained for them of Thy wondrous, sublime, and impregnable handiwork of Thy Lordship.
Is there any heart, O my God, in the depths of the highest heaven that is not humbled at their mention? Are there any spirits in the book of those drawn nigh that do not bow down at their calamity? Are there any souls that are not detached unto them at the raising of their word? Are there any bodies whose eyes have not shed tears upon their cheeks for the afflictions which Thou didst ordain for them? By Thy might! Thou hast not created the like of this; nay, Thou hast created in the fire that which prostrated at the dawning of Thy will and wept over the magnitude of the afflictions of the manifestations of Thy unity. But how can this benefit them in what their hands have wrought?
Such is the sublimity of their affliction and the exaltedness of their calamity that no one with hearing can hear except they grieve, none with sight can witness except tears of Thy mercy flow therefrom, no heart except it testifies to this from the heights of Thy power, no tongue except it sends salutations upon them and curses upon their enemies, none with power save those who record the loftiness of their afflictions, and who send down that which is wrought by the hands of those who worship Thee not, yet who prostrate themselves before Thee by night and by day in ways they know not.
That which their hands have wrought shall profit them not. Therefore, O my God, send down upon them all Thy severity, Thy grasp, Thy might, and Thy vengeance. Seize them with the grasp of One mighty and powerful. Destroy them as Thou didst destroy those of old before them, and shalt destroy those who come after them. Verily, Thou art the Lord of great retribution, of severe chastisement, and of mighty power. Nothing escapeth Thy grasp. Only he who feareth escape for himself hastens in vengeance. Glory be unto Thee! Far be it from my heart to write thus, for Thy power hath ever been and shall ever remain exalted and supreme. Thy forbearance is naught but what Thou hast willed, that Thou mightest multiply upon them that which Thou hast ordained for them of Thy vengeance. Thy Will hath ever been swift in what Thou desirest, and transcendent above all things in its essence, its camphor-like purity, its firstness and lastness, its outwardness and inwardness. Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee.
Therefore, send down upon the Tree of Thy Oneness, upon its root and branch, its twigs and leaves and fruits, that which befitteth the loftiness of Thy bounty and which is worthy of Thy exaltation. Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee. Thou seest at this moment what is seen and unseen, and verily Thou, O my God, art in the Most Exalted Horizon. Sanctified be Thy names, exalted be Thy likenesses, and glorified be the manifestations of Thy light.
Glory be unto Thee, O God! Ordain at this moment for that Tree, for its root what befitteth Thy glory, for its branch what befitteth Thy majesty, and for its twigs, leaves, and fruits what befitteth the beauty of Thy sanctity and the exaltation and inaccessibility of Thy sovereign throne. For Thou art powerful over what Thou willest and mighty over what Thou desirest.
Then turn unto him who is established upon the clay of his existence and settled upon the dust of his paradise, and say: Glory be unto Thee, O God! Verily, Thou art the Lord of Glory, the Possessor of Glory, the Ordainer of Glory, and the Fashioner of Glory. How can I describe Thee, O my God, by Glory?
