Therefore, O God, send down the tokens of Thy might upon the Name of Thy Identity, which Thou hast placed above all Thy names, through which Thou hast caused the Qur’an to ascend, expounded the Bayan, opened the gates of heaven, and brought all things into the presence of Thy Oneness—the Countenance of Thy Lordship, the Sign of Thy Singleness, the Camphor of Thy Self-Subsistence, and the Essence of Thy Grandeur, which Thou hast freed from all similitude and names, and sanctified from all comparison and likeness.
And upon the manifestations of His Self and the gates of His might—the Letters of the Living, whom Thou didst create for the manifestation of the Point before all Thy names, for all else was created for It and through It. I beseech Thee, O God, by what Thou hast created for It before all things—and these are those sanctified names and glorified letters—to send down at this moment upon those who have been martyred in the path of Thy love that which befitteth the loftiness of Thy Countenance and the exaltation of Thy Sovereignty, and to send down Thy blessings upon them from me and from all things, at every moment, before every moment, and after every moment. And send down upon those who love them not all Thy retribution in every condition, before every condition, and after every condition. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things, and there is no might nor power save in Him, the Most High, the Most Great.

title: BB00057: Du’a’a’r-Rabi’ li’l-Avval
text:
Part 1: “The Fourth Prayer…”
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
The Fourth Prayer:
Verily, the least that sufficeth the servant at the thrones of the Letters of the Unity, whether he be present before them or desireth to turn towards them in the station which God hath ordained for him, is that he should purify his body with the utmost refinement and cleanse his garments with the utmost purity, and take a ring upon his right hand. Then let him be seated and say:
Verily all glory most glorious is from God, the Lord of the Hereafter and of the first life, upon thee, O Point of the Bayan, at morn and eventide. And verily all majesty most sublime is from God and from all things upon thee, O Letter Sin, in the kingdom of earth and heaven, then at eve and at dawn. And verily all beauty most beauteous is from God, exalted and glorified be He, and from all things upon thee, O Letter Mim, in the watches of the night and the ends of the day.
And verily all grandeur is entirely from God and from all things upon thee, O Letter Alif, in the kingdom of might, then on the Day of Reckoning. And verily all lights are entirely from God and from all things upon thee, O Letter Lam, at eve and at dawn. And verily all mercy is entirely from God and from all things upon thee, O Letter Lam, at morn and eventide.
And verily all names are entirely from God and from all things upon thee, O Letter Ha, in the kingdom on high unto the lowest atom. And verily all glory is from God, exalted and glorified be He, and from all things upon thee, O Letter Alif, in the kingdom on high unto the lowest atom. And verily all power is from God, exalted and glorified be He, and from all things upon thee, O Letter Lam, in the Hereafter and in the first life.
And verily the most exalted light is from God, exalted and glorified be He, and from all things upon thee, O Letter Alif, in the kingdom on high unto the lowest atom. And verily the essences of knowledge from the Book of God and from all things are upon thee, O Letter Mim, at all times, then in the watches of the night and the ends of the day.
And verily all might is from God and from all things upon thee, O Letter Nun, from the highest peak unto the lowest atom in the kingdoms of the Hereafter and of the first life. And verily all loftiness is from God and from all things upon thee, O Letter ʿAyn, in whatsoever the name of anything is mentioned from the most high unto the lowest atom.
And verily all good-pleasure is from God, glorified and exalted be He, and from all things upon thee, O Letter Alif, in the Hereafter and in the first life. And verily all divine authority is from God, glorified and exalted be He, and from all things upon thee, O Letter Lam, in the kingdom on high and the lowest atom and whatsoever lieth between them unto what the Lord of the Hereafter and of the first life doth reckon.
And verily all love is from God, glorified and exalted be He, and from all things upon thee, O Letter Alif, at morning light then at the hour when the sun doth shine in the highest horizon. And verily all sovereignty is entirely from God, glorified and exalted be He, and from all things upon thee, O Letter Qaf, in the Hereafter and in the first life. And verily all dominion is from God, glorified and exalted be He, and from all things upon thee, O Letter Sin, in the kingdom on high, until it reacheth unto the lowliest atom, then in the hereafter and the former times.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Thou art the Lord of the heavens and of the earth and of whatsoever is between them, their Inspirer, their Ordainer, their Fashioner, their Creator, their Originator, and their Generator.
I testify, and all things testify, that there is none other God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thou wert One God, Single, Self-Subsisting, Ever-Living, Self-Sufficient, Eternal, Ever-Dependent. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast no partner in sovereignty, nor any protector to act save by Thy leave.
I shall glorify Thee, praise Thee, proclaim Thy unity, magnify Thee, extol Thee, sanctify Thee, exalt Thee, and elevate Thee, and I shall testify before Thee as I hope to testify on the Day of Resurrection before the Point, the Manifestation of Thy Divinity, that there is none other God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thine is the sovereignty and Thine the praise. Thou givest life and causest death, then causest death and givest life, and verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not. Within Thy grasp is the kingdom of all things. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command, and Thou art powerful over all things.
And whatsoever is beneath Thee among all things by which the name of a thing created for Thee is mentioned, Thou hast created it from nothing by Thy command and established it from nothing by Thy sovereignty. Then Thou didst present Thy unity unto all things, and the first to accept it Thou didst make its essence Thy Paradise, wherein Thou didst create from the wonders of the arts of Thy Lordship that which attracteth all souls and spirits through Thy love.
And Thou didst make that essence a holy, transcendent, lofty, inaccessible, and mighty tree possessed of branches, leaves, and fruits which none save Thee hath encompassed in knowledge. Send down upon it, O my God, that which will elevate it morn and eve, will clothe it night and day, will strengthen it throughout the watches of the night and the hours of the day, will magnify it at dusk and dawn, and will sanctify it in the Kingdom on high unto the lowliest atom until the matter endeth with Thee on the Day of Reckoning, for that tree hath prostrated itself before Thee, hath submitted, hath shown humility, hath yielded, and hath surrendered to that which Thou hast sent down upon it.
Send down upon it, O my God, every good thing which Thy knowledge hath encompassed, and magnify it, O my God, through Thy might and glory and power and strength and sovereignty and supremacy over all things, from that which Thou lovest not for it and which grieveth its soul. Verily, Thou art powerful and mighty over all that.
Cause to grow, O my God, its branches and leaves and fruits in every less than nineteen nineteen ten moment with the growth of a thousand years, and raise it unto what is possible in the kingdom of Thy power and might, that Thou mayest crown unto Thyself a simple essence and a treasured [jewel] and a pure, pristine, beloved entity and a camphorated, hidden being, for verily Thou art the One with power over whatsoever Thou willest, and the Most Exalted in the dominion of creation, and the Most High in the sovereignty of destiny, and the Most Inaccessible in the sublimity of might of creation, and the Most Holy in the kingdom of earth and heaven.
All faces have prostrated themselves before the exaltation of Thy countenance and all matters have submitted at the dawning of Thy Will. Thou hast ever done what Thou willest and decreed what Thou desirest. Thou art not asked about what Thou doest for there existeth no god besides Thee to question Thee, and Thou shalt ask all things about all that they do, for verily Thou art the God of all things.
I testify by my prostration before Thee that my heart shall find repose with Thee, for this is the Most Exalted, the Most High, above all loftiness and glory. Through my acknowledgment of Thy oneness and my abasement before Thy Countenance, my being shall be soothed, for this is the highest ascendancy above all ascendancy and exaltation. Though another might possess the earth and all that is therein, by Thy glory, my soul findeth no rest save in Thee and in faith in what Thou dost reveal, for the one who possesseth the earth is veiled from Thy Countenance. By Thy glory, I seek Thy protection from this, and this is naught but through the excellence of Thy grace, whereby I have become detached from all that passions desire, that nothing may veil me from the Dayspring of Thy good-pleasure. Praise be unto Thee, O my God, for what Thou hast bestowed upon me of the clear signs, which those in the kingdom of earth and heaven are powerless to comprehend, and a single letter thereof is dearer to my heart than the dominion of the hereafter and this world, for such dominion, when its possessor dieth, is cut off from him, while these verses endure unto the Day [of Resurrection].
All praise be unto Thee for the sublimity of joy before Thy Countenance and the excellence of detachment before Thy Face. Thine is the most exalted praise and the most resplendent glory, above all praise and glory, for having made me the mirror of Thyself and distinguished me with that which Thy Being uttereth, and none but Thee can do this, for this is befitting of Him Who is the God of all things, their Lord, the Creator of all things and their Ordainer.
For, verily, all—whether of the exalted or of the lowly—shall, on that Day, say:
For that which is sent down from Thy presence hath no peer, that any of Thy servants might venture to aspire unto companionship with it—neither the Letters of the Living, nor Thy Names, nor Thine archetypes, nor Thy Prophets, nor Thy Messengers, nor Thine angels, nor those of Thy servants who draw nigh, nor the chosen among Thy saints, nor the human companions of Thine elect, nor the lofty among Thy trusted ones. Nay, all, in the stations of their existence, shall glorify Thee, assuredly convinced of the impotence of their hearts to comprehend Thy verses. And how could it be otherwise, when the bringing forth of them…?
Send down, then, O my God, upon the Tree which hath turned unto Thee with its whole being, and hath prostrated itself before Thee in its inmost reality, and hath submitted unto Thee in its very selfhood; which hath delivered Thy messages in all that is within it and upon it; which hath feared Thy justice and feared none beside Thee; and hath hoped for Thy bounty and hoped in none save Thee—send down upon it of Thy blessings, the most mighty thereof, the nearest thereto, the most unassailable, the most holy, and the most exalted. For that Tree is Thy Most Great Paradise for him that believeth in Thee in this world and in the world to come; therein are things seen and things unseen, and whatsoever souls and spirits desire, until the Cause returneth unto Thee on the Day of Return.
Then, when the oneness of the Point was set forth before all things, that Tree turned toward Thee, and Thou didst make it Thy Most Great Paradise for those who are in the heavens on high and the earth below, in this world and in the next. And another soul turned away, after all Thy signs had been presented to it; and it waxed arrogant, without seeing and without understanding. Therefore hast Thou made it the Tree of Fire, within its shadow; and Thou didst create its branches, its leaves, and its fruits from its own self; and Thou didst make it evanescent, non-existent, withered, unremembered—save that when it is mentioned it is joined to that which it hath earned for itself. And Thou didst render all that is within it and upon it—of fire—unto fire; and Thou didst make it lawful for him who hath not believed in Thee nor in Thy signs, and didst forbid it to the Tree that hath turned unto Thee, and to all its branches, and leaves, and fruits. And upon it there came down every name which Thou lovest not.
I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thyself, to send down upon the Tree of Thy love that which befitteth the loftiness of Thy sovereignty, and to send down upon the tree which prostrated not before the manifestation of Thy oneness all Thy chastisement and destruction which Thou hast made lawful for it. Even though Thou didst not wish to create the Tree of Fire when Thou didst not send down in the numbered nights and treasured hours anything less than the letters of the most exalted ones in Thy paradise, and Thou didst desire that there be nothing upon the earth save the Tree of Thy love, that all souls and what they possess might seek shelter in its shade.
But those who have been enriched by its dominion from the goods of this world from the Tree of Fire, when they gained through the rights of the essences of Thy verses and the gems of Thy words that which no heart can encompass in knowledge nor any ear can hear mention thereof. Therefore hast Thou created that Tree to annihilate it and destroy it and seize it and send down upon it what it deserveth of Thy vengeance and Thy might, even though Thy mercy hath encompassed all atoms.

title: BB00057: Du’a’a’r-Rabi’ li’l-Avval
text: “The Qur’an is but a book of earlier times beside Thy Book.”

title: BB00057: Du’a’a’r-Rabi’ li’l-Avval
section: Part 2: “For by Thy glory, even unto the uttermost…”
text:
Part 2: “For by Thy glory, even unto the uttermost…”
For by Thy glory, even unto the uttermost limit, I cannot bear to see an ant grieve in Thy path—how much less when Thy mercy, which hath encompassed all things, is too holy to see a soul grieve in the path of Thy love or that the knowledge of any of Thy loved ones be associated with that which Thou lovest not. Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. How great is Thy grace and bounty! Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. How vast is Thy generosity and beneficence! How boundless is Thy gift and favor! How exalted is Thy tenderness and grace! How ancient is Thy radiance and bounty! Glorified art Thou! Glorified art Thou!
All who are attributed unto Thee pour forth the portion of their existence, whether after an hour or after their ascension from one station to another, or nearer than this or further, for nothing escapeth Thy knowledge in the heavens or on earth or between them, and nothing in the kingdom of command or creation or below them can frustrate Thee. Thou shalt surely reward every soul that hath believed in the Point and then in Its letters after It, and hath loved the leaves of that Tree, then its branches and its leaves, with a true reward from Thy presence. Verily Thou art powerful and mighty over that.
And Thou shalt surely destroy those who prostrate not before Thee nor believe in It, and Thou shalt seize them with true seizure through Thy power and might and the extension of Thy Lordship’s dominion. Verily Thou art powerful, omnipotent and mighty over that which none other than Thee can do. Thou art unique in making lawful what Thou willest and making unlawful what Thou willest. None can reverse Thy Will nor alter Thy Purpose.
O my God! Thou art indeed independent of the essences of creation, how much more their deeds. Nay, all religions and faiths are from Thee, like a pomegranate given to a child to occupy him. Glory be unto Thee, glory be unto Thee! Thy independence from all things is indubitable, and the dependence of all things upon Thee is indubitable.
Were Thou to impose upon Thy servants any decree, who could say “why” or “wherefore”? And were Thou to lay upon them what would weigh heavy on their beings, who could say “why” or “wherefore”? And were Thou to prescribe for them what their hearts would accept, who could say “why” or “wherefore”? But since Thy way hath ever been loving-kindness and beneficence, and Thy custom bounty and grace, Thou hast made Thyself known to all things that they might thereby proclaim Thy oneness and declare that there is no God but Thee. And hadst Thou not made Thyself known to anyone, could any soul have known Thee? Glory be unto Thee, glory be unto Thee!
And hadst Thou not recognized the hearts of the Primal Letters which came unto Thee with all they possessed melted away, without any mention remaining, and which appeared before Thee devoid of knowledge—who could have drawn nigh unto Thee through them or given thanks to Thee for knowledge of the Letters of the One proceeding from Thee? For verily Thou art One, not in number nor by number nor by anything known save by Thee.
And hadst Thou not established the path for them that love Thee and detailed the ways of detachment for them that are devoted to Thee, how could they that obey Thee worship Thee and find delight in what Thou hast taught them of the ways of Thy will? Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. All are from Thee, to Thee, by Thee, and unto Thee. There is no power nor strength except through Thee.
Thou hast ever called, in Thy most exalted heights, the lowest atom to the horizon of Thy praise, the heaven of Thy sanctification, the exaltation of Thy unity, the inaccessibility of Thy glorification, and the joy of Thy magnification. Who is like unto Thee in bounty despite Thy independence? Who is like unto Thee in mercy despite Thy self-sufficiency? Whose generosity equals Thy generosity, or whose nobility Thy nobility, or whose gift Thy gift, or whose kindness Thy kindness, or whose grace Thy grace, or whose pardon Thy pardon, or whose forbearance Thy forbearance, or whose compassion Thy compassion, or whose clemency after power Thy clemency, or whose forgiveness after might Thy forgiveness?
Nay, by Thy might! None can share with Thee in Thy names, Thy likenesses, Thy attributes, or Thy characteristics. All things besides Thee are as nothing before Thee except by Thy will. How could they be, when their very beings are dependent on what Thou lovest in Thy dominion? How could they be, when what Thou lovest not exists not in Thy mighty kingdom? Glorified art Thou above that! All else besides Thee was nothing before and shall be nothing after.
Absolute sovereignty belongeth to Thee alone, there is no God but Thee. Absolute majesty belongeth to Thee alone, there is no God but Thee. Absolute exaltation belongeth to Thee alone, there is no God but Thee. Absolute might belongeth to Thee alone, there is no God but Thee. Absolute grace belongeth to Thee alone, there is no God but Thee. Absolute perfection belongeth to Thee alone, there is no God but Thee. Absolute acceptance belongeth to Thee alone, there is no God but Thee.
Whomsoever Thou turnest Thy face toward, he is the beloved and cherished one; and whomsoever Thou turnest Thy countenance away from, he is the outcast and remote one. Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. All majesty is within Thy grasp and all glory is in the right hand of Thy dominion. Thou hast ever drawn them that love Thee through the holy breezes of Thy Lordship, such that nothing exists in Thy knowledge except that which Thou lovest. But woe unto him who is not drawn by the attractions of Thy nearness, nor detached unto Thee through the signs of Thy love, nor inspired by Thy holy conditions, nor ascendeth unto Thee through glimpses of intimacy with Thee, nor dwelleth near Thee through what lieth with Thee.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Thou art the King of the kingdom of the Hereafter and the First. All destinies are in Thy grasp and all keys are in the right hand of Thy will. Whomsoever Thou openest unto the doors of Thy mercy shall ever ascend unto Thee in the horizon of Thy care and rise unto Thee in the paths of Thy providence. Thou art the One Who hath ever been and will ever be in the kingdom of eternity and the heaven of independence.
Thou art the Builder after all things in the kingdom of might and the heights of power. Verily Thou createst all things from nothing, by Thyself and for Thyself, for Thou art [exalted] above any equal or peer, above any like or similitude, above any resemblance or attribute, above any associate or description.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Whenever I make mention of Thee my heart beareth witness that I must seek Thy forgiveness for having mentioned Thee, for what right hath the servant to make mention of One such as Thee, O my God without peer? And what right hath the poor one to praise One such as Thee, O my Lord without equal?
Glory be to Thee and exalted art Thou! Glory be to Thee and holy art Thou! Glory be to Thee in Thy oneness! Glory be to Thee in Thy power! Glory be to Thee in Thy wisdom! Glory be to Thee in Thy justice! Glory be to Thee in Thy holiness! Glory be to Thee in Thy greatness! Glory be to Thee in Thy might! Glory be to Thee in Thy mercy! Glory be to Thee in Thy grace! Glory be to Thee in Thy harmony! Glory be to Thee in Thy generosity! Glory be to Thee in Thy nobility! Glory be to Thee in Thy bestowal! Glory be to Thee in Thy tenderness! Glory be to Thee in Thy majesty! Glory be to Thee in Thy power! Glory be to Thee in Thy forming! Glory be to Thee in Thy grandeur! Glory be to Thee in Thy beauty! Glory be to Thee in Thy splendor! Forever do all prostrate before Thee and make mention of Thee and [worship] Thee.
Therefore, O my God, send down at this moment upon the hearts that have ascended unto Thee in Thy glorification, and the spirits that have turned unto Thee in Thy praise, and the souls that have been detached unto Thee in Thy unity, and the bodies that have risen unto Thee in Thy magnification, and the forms that have vanished in the realms of Thy might through Thy glorification, that which befitteth the loftiness of Thy grandeur and greatness, the sublimity of Thy independence and sovereignty, the elevation of Thy self-subsistence and awesomeness, the invincibility of Thine eternity and power, the joy of Thy self-subsistence and exaltation, and that of which Thou art worthy, which none besides Thee can comprehend.
O God, raise their stations to the highest possible degree in creation, and send down upon their stations in the Ridvan wherein they live and die not that which befitteth the loftiness of Thy grace and the sublimity of Thy generosity and the elevation of Thy nobility and the invincibility of Thy kindness and the exaltation of Thy beneficence. And assist, O God, those who have inherited from these through a victory from Thee and might from Thy presence.
And send down at this moment upon those who have shown pride before Thee that which will seize them and destroy them and annihilate them and remove them from the earth, and cause those who believe in Thee and Thy signs to inherit what they possess, through Thy power from which nothing can escape, and Thy might which nothing can frustrate, and Thy sovereignty which is triumphant over all things, and Thy glory which is invincible above all things.
By Thy grandeur, which is manifest above all things, and by Thy dominion, which encompasseth all things—for the exponents of Thy decree have ever existed and shall continue to exist by Thy leave in the kingdom of Thy might, determining what Thou hast determined for them, and the exemplars of Thy power in what hath been and shall be, administering in the kingdom of Thy earth and heaven that which Thou hast ordained for them through the operation of Thy power and the wonders of Thy wisdom and Thy glorification.
O God! Ordain for us from Thy presence every good thing encompassed by Thy knowledge, and preserve us, O God, through Thee and through all Thy names and attributes, and those who believe in Thee and Thy signs, from that which Thou lovest not. Verily, Thou hast power over all things. Through Thee we have gained insight, strength, exaltation, greatness, glory and victory, that we may uplift the tree of Thy oneness and annihilate all that lieth beneath its shade through Thy might and power. For this is naught but to solace the hearts of those who have melted in Thy path through what they have heard of Thy decree and destiny. Otherwise, we have no desire beyond what we have beseeched of Thee, nor is it meet for us at such time save to grieve in Thy path and weep for the people of Thy love.
We shall assuredly invoke blessings upon them with all wherewith Thou invokest blessings upon the people of Thy love—not through the utterance of our tongues but through the manifestation of our hands—and we shall curse those who believe not in Thee nor in Thy signs, not through the utterance of our tongues but through the manifestation of our own selves. For that, at such time, will profit us from Thee in the Mother Book according to what Thou hast decreed and ordained through Thy Will. And unto Thee belongeth the power to create whatsoever Thou hast created or wilt create.
There is no power nor strength except through Thee. Thou knowest what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and what lieth between them. Nothing escapeth Thee in the kingdoms of Command and Creation and whatsoever lieth beneath them. Verily Thou hast knowledge of all things and power over all things. Have mercy upon us, O God, through Thy mercy, for Thou art the Best of those who show mercy. And bestow Thy blessings, O God, upon the Primary Letters, nine before ten, in every time, and before time, and after time.

title: BB00060: Du’a’a’th-Thalith li’l-Avval
text:
Part 1: “Glorified art Thou, O my God, and all…”
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O my God, and all praise be unto Thee! There is none other God but Thee. Thou givest life and causest death, then causest death and givest life. Verily, Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not. In Thy right hand is all good, and in Thy grasp is all command. Thou createst what Thou willest, how Thou willest. None can resist Thy will, and none can thwart Thy purpose. Thou doest what Thou pleasest and ordainest what Thou desirest. Thou art not to be questioned about what Thou doest, while all besides Thee shall be questioned about all things, for all else is created by Thee and in Thy grasp, and none hath anything save by Thy leave, and nothing existeth save through Thy bounty.
How can I praise Thee, O my God, with this tongue before Thee, when verily I am powerless to praise Thee in the manner I should die in creating Thy praise, knowing that Thou hast not revealed that word except for what Thou didst intend therein of the praise of the Manifestation of Thy Divinity in the Point which Thou hast originated, and the Manifestation of Thy Divinity in the Letter Sin which Thou hast revealed unto it, then to manifest Thy knowledge in the Letter Mim which Thou hast made the manifestation of Thy knowledge in the kingdom of Thy heaven and earth, where nothing of Thy knowledge can set, neither in the heavens nor on earth nor what lieth between them. Whoso encompasseth the knowledge of Thy praise hath known all things, and whoso faileth to encompass the knowledge of the Manifestations of Thy praise knoweth nothing.
And unto Thee belong all conditions in every condition. If I knew Thee on that Day and praised Thee with true praise through the essence of my being and the reality of my identity and the essence of my self—that would be from Thee and unto Thee, Thy nearness from Thee, and returneth unto Thee. And verily I am assured of this while I live. But how can I praise Thee, O my God, after Thou hast taken me unto Thee, when on that Day my hearing heareth not the verses of Thy might from the Manifestation of Thy Countenance, nor doth my sight behold the glances of Thy face from the lights of Thy glory, nor doth my heart witness the place of Thy knowledge in the repository of Thy will? I have no way to praise Thee, O my God, except that Thou assist me with what Thou teachest me in every condition through the wonders of Thy Lordship, and attract me through the holy fragrances of Thy unity, and come between me and that which veils me from praising Thee through the manifestations of the glory of Thy oneness.
For whoso desireth to praise Thee as befitteth praising Thee must transcend all else in the exaltation of the Essence and unite Thee in that Most Exalted Station above all names and similitudes. Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee, the Lord of the worlds. Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee, the Mighty, the Beloved. Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee, the Overseer, the Self-Subsisting. Thine is the creation and the command. I am certain of this: that wert Thou to give me dominion over all that is in the heavens and earth and what lieth between them, I would not withhold anything from the Manifestation of the Point, nor the Letter Sin, nor the Letter Mim, for verily Thou hast ever been beyond the comprehension of all things, and whoso desireth to comprehend Thee shall never comprehend Thee except in the Point, the Manifestation of Thy revelation, or what Thou hast created from its light from the Letters of the Living with Thee.
Verily, were I to declare unto Thee, “Unto Thee belongeth the creation,” yet withhold from Thee whatsoever beareth the name of a thing, and deny to whom Thou purifiest on the Day of Resurrection—after the manner in which the Point hath already made manifest the clear and evident signs—how could I be true in my word? And if I follow not His command, how shall I confirm unto Thee that the Cause is Thine, that there, indeed, are the treasuries of Thy behest, and that every mention of praise proceedeth in like wise? For unto Thee belongeth whatsoever is in the highest heavens and the lowest earth, and whatsoever is in this world and in the world to come.
I seek refuge in Thee and in all Thy names and attributes, and in the holy Temples manifested in Thy First and Single Name, then in all the Manifestations of Thy names, lest I attribute unto Thee dominion and praise while denying these unto Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest on the Day of Resurrection, or unto any kingdom or thing that shall be gathered beneath the shadow of Thy praise, for such would be the utterance of one whose deeds belie his words. By Thy glory! I seek protection in Thee from praising Thee while perceiving among the manifestations of Thy praise any equal, likeness, or peer. If I be sincere in my praise of Thee, then glory be unto Thee!
Glory be unto Thee! Glory be unto Thee! I have known Thee inasmuch as Thou canst not be known except through Thyself, and I have praised Thee inasmuch as Thou canst not be praised except through Thyself, and I have sanctified Thee inasmuch as Thou canst not be sanctified except through Thyself, and I have become certain that there is no way for creation unto Thee except through the Manifestation of Thy revelation, for all that the sincere ones ascend thereby springeth from that Tree and returneth unto it, even though it be a Tree that hath been raised above its own identity wherein naught is seen except Thee, and it speaketh from Thy presence that which all Thy creation is powerless to utter.
Without doubt this is the Manifestation of Thy Self from the kingdom on high to the lowest atom. If I praise Thee, it is through what Thou hast taught me of Thy praise, else who is capable of praising Thee? I have thus come to know that when all things are called to declare that there is no God but God, this is from the sign which Thou hast deposited therein from Thyself. By Thy glory! I shall indeed reject all who love Him not, even were they the nearest of my near ones, and I shall accept all who love Him, even were they the remotest of my remote ones, for through Him Thy word “There is no God but Thee” hath been spread abroad. Were it not for Him, who would unite with Thee, or praise Thee, or sanctify Thee, or glorify Thee, or exalt Thee, or magnify Thee?
I beseech Thee, O my God, by that Tree which Thou hast raised in the heaven of Lordship, and watered with the water of the Alif of Oneness, and nurtured with the evidences of the glory of Thy Singleness, and made to be the station of Thy Self in creation and the manifestation of Thy power in invention, wherein Thou hast magnified and elevated and glorified and exalted it to a station known by none save Thee, that I shall, O my God, surely praise Thee by rejecting all that the Manifestation of Thy praise rejecteth—not merely by saying “Glory be to God above all they describe,” but with my heart and spirit and soul and body and possessions and all that pertaineth to His Cause. I praise Thee through my acknowledgment of the Manifestations of Thy praise, distinct from those who wish not to praise Thee even though their tongues may utter praise.
I testify that there is no God but Thee: whosoever hath known the Point, then the S and the M, and followed the ordinances which Thou hast sent down upon the Point, hath indeed praised Thee, and that one shall continue to praise Thee until the Day when that Point shall return as Thou pleaseth. Thus, if one praiseth Thee through it, one hath indeed praised Thee from before; otherwise one shall perish and all that one hath acquired shall be as though one had never praised Thee in any way, just as Thou didst cause to perish on that Day all who had praised Thee from the first day Thou didst send Muhammad—Thy blessings be upon Him and His family—unto the Day when Thou didst manifest Me. Whosoever hath glorified Thee through Me hath verily glorified Thee through Him aforetime.
And in the sight of God nothing is seen save this, my longing for the exaltation of Thy praise, my passion for the revelation of Thy sanctification, and my yearning for the elevation of Thy glorification. Such is the Most Exalted Height in all that hath been witnessed of Thy praise or shall be witnessed of Thy sanctification. Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. All have glorified Thee, yet all are veiled from the letters of Thy praise. Nay, the Tree of Negation and all within it were not content with their veiling and have grown proud against these letters, as Thou Thyself hast witnessed.
Indeed, they have committed with their hands, regarding a letter of Thy praise, that which no one possessed of a heart can comprehend. Their hearts are harder than stone. By Thy glory, I shall surely disavow such hearts and commune with Thee at that time, that Thou mayest raise up the Tree of Thy praise to its true exaltation from Thy presence and preserve it from that from which Thou hast purified it through Thy glory [which] Thou hast placed above all glory, and Thy majesty which Thou hast placed above all majesty, and Thy beauty which Thou hast placed above all beauty, and Thy grandeur which Thou hast placed above all grandeur, and Thy light which Thou hast placed above all light, and Thy mercy which Thou hast placed above all mercy, and Thy words which Thou hast placed above all words, and Thy perfections which Thou hast placed above all perfections, and Thy names which Thou hast placed above all names, and Thy might which Thou hast placed above all might, and Thy will which Thou hast placed above all will, and Thy knowledge which Thou hast placed above all power, and Thy utterance which Thou hast placed above all utterance, and Thy questions which Thou hast placed above all questions, and Thy nobility which Thou hast placed above all nobility, and Thy sovereignty by whose hands Thou hast subdued every sovereignty and placed it above all sovereignty, and by Thy kingdom with which Thou hast possessed every kingdom and placed it above all kingdom, and the exaltation which Thou hast placed above all exaltation and loftiness, and whatsoever Thou hast numbered of Thy most beautiful names which none save Thee can encompass—that Thou mayest preserve the letters of Thy praise from that which would grieve their hearts, their spirits, their souls and their bodies, in their sleep or their wakefulness, their beginning or their end, their outward or their inward state, or whatsoever pertaineth to their origin or their ultimate end.
For Thou, O my God, art the Upholder of all things through Thy power, the Strengthener of the letters of Thy praise through Thy might, the Preserver of these sacred temples through Thy sovereignty, and the Exalter of these essential manifestations through Thy self-subsistence. None besides Thee hath power over this, for Thou art the One with power over whatsoever Thou willest, hast ever been and wilt ever be, and art mighty over whatsoever Thou desirest at all times.
Glorified art Thou, O God! Even as Thou hast answered Thy praise which hath appeared from my limbs in like manner as my tongue hath spoken, I shall surely love Thy glorification likewise, then Thy oneness likewise, then Thy magnification likewise, then love for all Thy names and attributes in like manner.
For the Tree of the Point is one tree which Thou didst plant aforetime when Thou didst reveal unto it the Qur’an, and it was at that time alone with none beside it, and now when a thousand two hundred and seventy-five years shall have revolved, behold how that Tree hath grown mighty, and how its branches and leaves and fruits have filled the heavens and earth and all that lieth between them, and how the tree of negation that would not prostrate itself before it on the day of its manifestation hath been brought to naught beneath its shade.
Glorified art Thou! This is of Thy supreme handiwork, this is of Thy all-sufficient and perfect providence, how Thou didst nurture that Tree until it reached its full maturity and perfection. Then didst Thou take from it a pure essence which is the very essence of its origin when it was first planted, and upon it didst Thou send down the Bayan. Glorified art Thou! How great, how majestic, how beautiful, how mighty and how sanctified hast Thou made it in those numbered days, when Thou didst number its branches and leaves and fruits, and it ascended to a station no tree before it had attained, for before five years had passed, blood was shed in its path by souls the like of whom existed not on earth—without its permission, but through the attraction of their hearts, the detachment of their bodies, the certitude of their breasts, the loftiness of their examples, and the potency of their deeds.

title: BB00060: Du’a’a’th-Thalith li’l-Avval
section: Part 2: “Glorified art Thou! There is no God but…”
text:
Part 2: “Glorified art Thou! There is no God but…”
Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. How magnificent are Thy favors unto it, how glorious Thy bounties upon it, how great Thy manifestations within it and upon it, how mighty the lights of Thy wondrous oneness to its right and to its left, and how exalted it is in a might than which there is none mightier, wherein the letters of Thy unity and the manifestations of Thy sanctity were content that their spirits should ascend unto Thee to establish Thy remembrance and to make known to every soul that verily it is the truth from God, there is no doubt in it, a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
Glorified art Thou, O God! Thine is the creation and Thine the command, and there is no power except through Thee. If this be its station in its first five years, how shall it be when that Tree hath reached its full maturity and perfection in all that is within it and of it? Make it, O my God, wholly a blessed garden for Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest on the Day of Resurrection, for verily He is I and I am He. Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. There is no mention for me or for Him save through Thy mention of Thyself. Preserve, O my God, through that Tree, what lieth before it and behind it, to its right and to its left, above its head and beneath its feet, and whatsoever Thou hast caused to descend upon it from the heights of Thy bounty and the heaven of Thy grace, for before the tree of its own self was planted, that garden was from Thee, before its manifestation, that its heart might find rest therein.
O my God! Cause the Letters of the Living, before all other letters, to be present before it, that they may convey what they are commanded from the sources of Thy Command and the wellsprings of Thy creation, and that their hearts may be made firm in His Cause, and bring all who are upon the Tree of the Bayan into His presence with such submissiveness as Thou hast created naught above it of humility, with such lowliness as Thou hast created naught above it of abasement, and with such prostration upon the secret of their inmost beings, and with words of truth in His praise upon the manifestation of their essential realities. Destroy, O my God, by Thy power and might and grandeur and strength and sovereignty, the tree of negation until nothing returneth unto it therefrom, and preserve it, O my God, from that tree by all Thy protection, and bring it to naught in such wise that it shall find no existence at the dawning of Thy Lordship, with all its branches and leaves and fruits, that thereby the eyes of Thine enemy and of those who desire not to prostrate themselves before Him may be consoled, and create in all things a love for Him.
O God! Grant unto her mercy, modesty, awe, compassion, and honor in Thy presence. Make, O Lord, the entire tree to be hers, that there may be manifested from it the fruits which God hath created therein for him through whom God hath willed to reveal what He desireth. For, by Thy glory, I have not desired that there should be upon that tree any branch, leaf, or fruit that would not prostrate before Him on the day of His manifestation, nor glorify Thee in a manner befitting the loftiness of His revelation and the sublimity of His concealment. And if, O my God, I should witness any branch, leaf, or fruit that doth not prostrate before Him on the day of His manifestation, then sever it, O God, from that tree, for it is not of me, nor doth it return unto me.
Preserve, O God, for Thyself those who have believed in me in this creation, that they may believe in me in my return, that their faith may not perish, nor the knowledge of its possessor, for Thou hast power over all things. On that day, how many servants do I see who believed in Muhammad beforetime yet believe not in me on that day. There is no doubt that they believed not beforetime, but merely uttered words by which their lives were preserved and they attained their desires, yet they return not to Thy Cause. For at that time all negation will be transformed into affirmation, and darkness into light.
Cause Thou, O God, the earth and all who are upon it to witness none save those who have believed in Thee and in Thy signs and have followed the Letters of the First from Thy presence. Verily, Thou hast power over all things. Then turn unto him who is established upon the throne of his glory and settled upon the seat of his sovereignty. Look not upon him as being in clay, but rather in the exaltation of the Throne before God. He seeth whosoever appeareth before him and answereth everyone who greeteth him.
Say: May the most glorious, most resplendent Glory and the most impregnable, most luminous Light be upon thee, O Primal Tree, Most Exalted Seat, Garden of Refuge, Lote-Tree of the Uttermost Boundary, Supreme Horizon, Most Great Pavilion, and Most High Station at the distance of two bow-lengths or closer. I bear witness before God and those in His presence that through thee His greatest signs were sent down and His mightiest evidences were manifested, and all that was ordained in the Last and the First was created. How can I mention aught of thy praise or recite before thee aught of thy circumstances, or how can the knowledge of my heart encompass what hath befallen thee, whereby my spirit, my soul, and my destiny have melted away?
No command is there save from God, and no decree save in the hand of God. When I behold thy station with God, and how God hath set thee above all the Manifestations of His Names—so that none beginneth without thee, and naught returneth unto Him save through thee—and when I see how thou hast ascended, through that which thou hast borne in the path of God, unto the loftiest of stations, in the world to come and in this world, my soul is moved to desire that I might attain that which God hath ordained for thee, and that I might be brought down upon that wherewith thou hast triumphed. Yet this is a thing which none can reach save by My hand, except whomsoever God willeth; for all beseech of the bounty of God that He may ordain for them to be slain in His path, but none attaineth unto this save him for whom God hath so decreed from His presence, and upon whom He hath caused His decree to be executed by His irrevocable command. How exalted, then, is such honour in the sight of God, and how glorious such a bestowal in the Book of God!
Therefore grieve not for thy calamity, O Beloved of my heart, amid the depths of names and attributes; and how unassailable is thy affliction, O Purpose of my being, within the kingdoms of earth and heaven! It hath surpassed every calamity and risen above every woe, as though it had been lifted unto a station wherefrom all likenesses are cut off, and had ascended unto an horizon whereat the doors are shut. For this is a thing that entereth not into the heart of any one—that the King of creation should be dealt with even as thou hast been dealt with, O Light of Bahá. Yet since God hath made thee a Manifestation beyond compare, sanctified above resemblance, exalted beyond peer, inaccessible to companion, and raised above similitudes, it befitteth not one such as thou that thy calamity should have an equal, or thy affliction a likeness, or that what hath befallen thee should have a counterpart, or that what is decreed should have an equivalent.
It is, indeed, so magnified, so mighty, so purified, and so exalted, that every heart hath been confounded before it, even as it soared in its glorification; and every spirit hath been saddened thereby, even as it rose in its praise; and every soul hath humbled itself at its remembrance, despite the loftiness of its confession of unity; and from every eye tears have flowed, notwithstanding the greatness of what God hath ordained therein of magnifying Him.
O God! You are witness to what has been witnessed and You know what has been known. Therefore, O God, send down all Your most resplendent glory, Your most sublime majesty, Your most beautiful beauty, Your most magnificent grandeur, Your most brilliant light, Your most expansive mercy, Your most perfect words, Your most great names, Your most mighty power, Your most prevailing will, Your most penetrating knowledge, Your most far-reaching might, Your most pleasing utterance, Your most beloved and most impregnable questions, Your most noble honor, Your most enduring sovereignty, Your most glorious dominion, Your most exalted justice, and all that You have attributed to Yourself or love to attribute—for which there is no equal in Your knowledge—upon the Tree of the Bayan, its root, branch, twigs, fruits and leaves, in recompense for what has grieved it in Your path, or for any soul that has been slain for its sake seeking Your good-pleasure, or any heart that has been pierced in submission to its Educator. For verily, You are at all times engaged in a wondrous work, creating whatsoever You willest through Your command, and You are mighty and powerful.
O God! Exalt the station of Your glory and shower upon those hearts, spirits, souls and bodies the manifestations of Your will and the wonders of Your favoring grace. Gather together, O God, all that has been created through it under its shade on the Day when all things shall be brought before You on the Day of Resurrection, through Your power from which nothing can escape and Your might which nothing can frustrate. Create at all times, O God, through the sublimity of Your power and the exaltation of Your sovereignty, every good thing within Your knowledge for the spiritual Tree, its root, branch, twigs and fruits, and whatsoever pertains to its ultimate destiny and abode. Bring it and all that is within it and upon it into Your presence on the Day of Resurrection that it may bow down before Thee and worship Thee alone, apart from all things.
O my God, send down upon the Tree of Negation—its root, branch, boughs, leaves and fruits—the most severe of all chastisements, the most grievous of all vengeance, the greatest of all hardships, and whatsoever punishment Thou willest to visit upon those who worship Thee not, or to destroy those who bow not down before Thee. Send down that which riseth at the dawning of Thy wrath, that which emerges at the manifestation of Thy might, and that which appeareth at the revelation of Thy power upon those who have not raised up the tree of their existence before Thee, nor manifested that for which they were created through faith in Thee and Thy signs before Thy presence, and through following the Letters of the Unity from Thy presence. Verily, Thou art the most severe in punishment and the most grievous in chastisement.
Nay, by Thy might! There is no helper for him whom Thou forsakest, no glory for him whom Thou abasest, no perpetuity for him whom Thou causest to perish, no thing for him whom Thou destroyest, and no remembrance for him whom Thou bringest to naught. Such is the recompense of those who believe not in Me, nor in the signs of God which God hath sent down unto Me in the life to come and in this life. Whoso desireth God and that which is with Him, let him arise to fulfill what God hath established in the Bayan through His command concerning the conditions of His good-pleasure and the wonders of His beneficence. And whoso desireth not, let him destroy his own soul through his refusal to follow that which hath been sent down from his Lord. No punishment more severe than this existeth with God.
Such is God’s command, both before and after. God doeth what He willeth and ordaineth what He desireth. He shall not be asked of His doings, whilst all shall be asked of all things.

title: BB00168: Prayer and Ziyarat for Friday
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I bear witness unto Thee on this Friday, which Thou hast honored, magnified, glorified, sanctified, exalted, and ennobled, and which Thou hast clothed with the mantle of gathering after the six degrees in the temple of seven, and wherein Thou hast ordained the sources of creation through the outpourings of power. I bear witness, O my God, and so doth every created thing, that there is none other God but Thee, alone with none beside Thee. Thine is the Kingdom and the dominion, Thine the might and grandeur, Thine the power and divinity, Thine the strength and glory, Thine the sovereignty and the earthly realm. Thou givest life and causest death, then causest death and givest life. Verily, Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not, the Sovereign Who passeth not away, the Just Who wrongeth not, the Ruler Who changeth not, the Single One from Whose grasp nothing escapeth, whether in the heavens or on earth or between them. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
I bear witness concerning Him Whom Thou shalt manifest on the Day of Resurrection through Thy signs, that He is the Sign of Thine own Self, wherein naught is seen but Thee, and the Countenance of Thine Essence, which pointeth to none but Thee. Thou art the First in Him, and there is no first before Thee; Thou art the Last in Him, and there is no last after Thee; Thou art the Manifest in Him, and there is none manifest above Thee; and Thou art the Hidden in Him, and there is none hidden except Thee.
Do Thou then send down upon Him, O my God, from the most glorious of Thy glory, the most majestic of Thy majesty, the most beautiful of Thy beauty, the most mighty of Thy might, the most effulgent of Thy light, the most extensive of Thy mercy, the most perfect of Thy words, the greatest of Thy names, the most powerful of Thy sovereignty, the most effective of Thy will, the most penetrating of Thy knowledge, the most potent of Thy power, the most pleasing of Thy utterance, the most beloved and unapproachable of Thy causes, the most noble of Thy honor, the most enduring of Thy dominion, the most excellent of Thy kingdom, the most exalted of Thy loftiness, the most ancient of Thy bounty, the most wondrous of Thy signs, the most perfect of Thy conditions, the most manifest of Thy revelations, the most evident of Thy proofs, the most excellent of Thy grace, the most generous of Thy generosity, the most gentle of Thy tenderness, the most powerful of Thy words, the most elevated of Thy majesty, the most complete of Thy riches, the most unapproachable of Thy glory, the most joyous of Thy joy, the most exalted of Thy exaltation, the most attractive of Thy detachment, the most upright of Thy independence, and of all that Thou lovest that which hath no equal, no peer, no likeness, no associate, and no similitude. Hallowed be Thy names and exalted be Thy parables!
Take then, O my God, from all things that which befitteth Him on the day of His manifestation, from what reacheth Him after He knoweth His own Self until what is raised up by Thy command. This is what hath been brought forth from the beginning of Thy creation until that Day from all things, and this is what pointeth to Thee and beseemeth Thy remembrance. Cause all Thy creation, O my God, to know on the day of His manifestation that they should manifest that for which they were created and not be veiled from the glory for which they were originated. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
And do Thou send down, O my God, upon His father and His mother, and if Thou hast ordained for Him a brother or sister or what Thou hast loved for Him, or those who are related to Him among His loved ones who take shelter under the shadow of His authority, that which befitteth the loftiness of Thy holy glory and the sublimity of Thy mighty exaltation from all Thy bounty, then Thy grace, and from all Thy generosity, then Thy kindness, and from all Thy mercy, then Thy favor, and from all Thy gifts, then Thy might, and from all Thy tenderness, and by all that becometh Thee! O God, cause me to attain unto Him and unto all that is attributed unto Him by virtue of that which is related to what Thou hast loved or wilt love. Verily Thou hast encompassed all things with Thy knowledge. When thou art seated in such a lofty place on that day and desirest to remember God there, recite that prayer, then say:
O God! These are hearts that have glorified Thee, spirits that have sanctified Thee, souls that have proclaimed Thy unity, and bodies that have magnified Thee, and all things that have extolled Thy greatness. Send down upon them, in their beginning and their end, from all Thy bounty that which hath no equal, no likeness, no peer, no companion, and no similitude. For verily, they desired none but Thee in their beginning, and they desire none but Thee in their end. Therefore, O God, cause their eyes to be gladdened in the chambers of their paradise and the inner recesses of their gardens with what they love from the manifestations of Thy power and the conditions of Thy grandeur.
Verily, Thou art the Powerful, the Mighty, the Helper, the Self-Subsisting, the Subduer, the Almighty, the Manifest, the Self-Revealing, the All-Glorious, the Self-Sufficing. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
Then turn and say: All glory be unto God, exalted be His majesty, and unto the Letters of the Unity, and unto all the Letters of the Names that indicate God through might and glory, and through power and sublimity, upon you, O glorifying hearts, sanctified spirits, unifying souls, and magnifying bodies! Blessed and purified and exalted and elevated are ye by what hath been ordained in the Book through what hath been attributed unto you. In you hath been manifested in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and what lieth between them that there is no God but Him, the One, the Manifest.
How exalted is your station, your station with God! And what station can equal that which ye have gained through God’s bounty? How exalted is your glory, your glory! And what glory can compare with what ye have attained through God’s generosity? Unto you be the most resplendent glory of God, the most sublime majesty of God, the most beauteous beauty of God, the most supreme greatness of God, the most brilliant light of God, the most extensive mercy of God, the most perfect words of God, the greatest names of God, the most mighty power of God, the most penetrating knowledge of God, the most potent might of God, the most pleasing utterance of God, the most beloved causes of God, the most noble honor of God, the most enduring sovereignty of God, the most glorious dominion of God, the most elevated exaltation of God, and all that ye love for which there is no equal, no likeness, no similitude, no peer, and no comparison.
All this is with you in the chambers of your paradise and before you in the inner recesses of your gardens. Ye witness there naught but what ye love, and ye see there naught but what attracts you. This is from God’s bounty unto you. He is the Protector, the Self-Subsisting.
How many hearts have been consumed for your sake, how many spirits have melted in your path, how many eyes have shed tears in your calamities, how many pens have recorded your circumstances, how many places of command have been raised in your remembrance, and how many conditions of glory have been altered for your sake! Is there any heart that is not rent asunder at the mention of your tribulations? Is there any spirit that is not stilled at the hearing of your afflictions? Is there any soul that is not affected by what hath befallen you? Is there any body that hath not donned the garment of grief in your calamities?
Nay, by your glory! God doth ever remember you, and His angels pray for you, and every day ninety-five thousand angels descend upon you by number, and they go forth, by God your Lord’s leave, all circling around your heights and prostrating themselves before God in your presence. Ye shall see all this with your own eyes in your latter days, with these your eyes, after ye have beheld in these your stations of paradise with the eyes of your hearts that which none comprehendeth save God, your Lord. Therefore upon your first and your last, your outward and your inward, and those who seek shelter in your shade, and those who weep for your sorrows, and those who ascend unto your stations, and those who stand firm in the glory of your love, and those who spend what their hands possess in the path of your Word—upon all these be what behoveth God of bounty and loftiness, then of grace and exaltation. Verily He is possessed of great grace.
Glorified be God before your remembrance and at the time when ye make mention! Glorified be God after your remembrance and at the time when ye make mention of God! That is the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest, when ye shall be mentioned in the remembrance that is with God. And none hath aught except by God’s command. His is the greatness and grandeur in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them. There is no God but Him, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting.
Obligatory Prayer for Every Friday Night:
In the Name of God, the Most Overwhelming, the Most Overwhelming! Glory be to Thee, O God! Destroy Thou every possessor of the letter Alif who believeth not in Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest, the Manifestation of Thy Greatest Proof, by Thy Divinity which is indeed exalted above all things. Verily Thou art powerful over all things.
Glory be to Thee, O God! Destroy Thou every possessor of the letter Ba who believeth not in Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest, the Manifestation of Thy Greatest Proof, by Thy Glory which is indeed exalted above all things. Verily Thou art powerful over all things.
Glory be to Thee, O God! Destroy Thou every possessor of the letter Jim who believeth not in Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest, the Manifestation of Thy Greatest Proof, by Thy Might which is indeed exalted above all things. Verily Thou art powerful over all things.
Glory be to Thee, O God! Destroy Thou every possessor of the letter Dal who believeth not in Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest, the Manifestation of Thy Greatest Proof, by Thy Eternity which is indeed exalted above all things. Verily Thou art powerful over all things.
Glory be to Thee, O God! Destroy Thou every possessor of the letter Ha who believeth not in Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest, the Manifestation of Thy Greatest Proof, by Thy Guidance which is indeed exalted above all things. Verily Thou art powerful over all things.
Glory be to Thee, O God! Destroy Thou every possessor of the letter Vav who believeth not in Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest, the Manifestation of Thy Greatest Proof, by Thy Sovereignty which is indeed exalted above all things. Verily Thou art powerful over all things.
Glory be to Thee, O God! Destroy Thou every possessor of the letter Za who believeth not in Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest, the Manifestation of Thy Greatest Proof, by Thy Purity which is indeed exalted above all things. Verily Thou art powerful over all things.
Glory be to Thee, O God! Destroy Thou every possessor of the letter Ha who believeth not in Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest, the Manifestation of Thy Greatest Proof, by Thy Life which is indeed exalted above all things. Verily Thou art powerful over all things.
Glory be to Thee, O God! Destroy Thou every possessor of the letter Ta who believeth not in Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest, the Manifestation of Thy Greatest Proof, by Thy Purity which is indeed exalted above all things. Verily Thou art powerful over all things.

title: BB00083: Ziyarat for Friday and Thursday nights
text:
Part 1: “When you are in the presence…”
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
When you are in the presence of the Point of the Bayan or one of the Manifestations on a Thursday night or Friday, purify yourself from all that your heart abhors. For when a servant allows his nails, body hair, moustache hair, head hair, or facial hair to grow, and does not trim them when they become excessive—if he is able to trim them and maintain them well but does not do so—then that thing shall ask God to take vengeance upon its owner. This applies whether it pertains to the servant himself or to his nails, which should not exceed nineteen, and likewise to his ears and the exterior and interior of his body—anything that can be refined but is not. The same principle applies as mentioned at first.
If it is his custom to maintain part of his head, he must clean it with something that removes the particles that gather at the ends of the hair, like a comb or similar implement. Likewise with beard hair—he should maintain it as best he can, improving and beautifying it. If something is found at its roots that cannot be removed when washing, he should use a comb or something to refine it.
If this is the case for the physical body, how much more for the essential body! If upon that body there exists any love other than for the Six Manifestations, or if there remains any trace of the Letters of Negation, the body is not pure. The same applies to souls, spirits and hearts.
When the servant manifests from his first mention to his final appearance, then purifies his body and adorns what he wears of all things—even to the innermost garment—such that not even a mustard seed’s weight of oil stain remains, he must cleanse it of that. For God loves nothing in the Bayan as much as refinement, lightness, cleanliness and purity, so that whoever enters the Bayan may find delight in all possible aspects.
God has created Thursday night and Friday for His servants’ delight, relieving them during these hours from occupations that might burden them and veil them from their pleasures—each according to what they find delightful: those who glorify through their glorification, those who sanctify through their sanctification, those who unite through their unification, those who magnify through their magnification, those who eat through their eating, those who drink through their drinking, those who beautify through their beautification, those who take pleasure in what God has ordained for them, and those who refine through their refinement—each according to what brings them delight.
Indeed, God has guaranteed that whoever refrains from his work on Friday for the sake of refinement shall receive a thousandfold what he would have earned that day through his work. This is the day when God loves that people should arise and attend gatherings, honoring one another in their coming and going, and commemorating the tragedy than which God knows none greater, neither before nor after, for all tragedies before it have returned to it. And if there be tragedy in a future Manifestation, then all joy and sorrow of that day shall return to that Manifestation. Otherwise, before its appearance, all joy and all sorrow in that Bayan shall appear. Let them call to remembrance the Point and the Manifestations of the Living, and what befell Them and Their followers for love of Them; and let them entreat God for Their might and inviolability, Their succour and exaltation. Then let them implore God to send down every retribution upon those who acted with pride towards them and committed against them that which the pen cannot write, nor the ink record, nor the tablets enumerate. Let those who are able arise from their seats for this purpose and chant the verses of God in the beloved plaintive tone whereby souls, spirits, hearts and minds are attracted.
Or let them recite from the words of God or remember that which God hath revealed in the Bayan concerning Him Who shall be made manifest. Otherwise, after He manifesteth Himself, let them recite in His seat of glory and His house of unity that which delighteth His heart. And God loveth that on the eve and day of Friday ye should manifest His bounties unto yourselves according to your capacity, for each day correspondeth to one of the letters of the Seven Letters. On Friday is perfected the manifestation of the word of Unity in affirmation and the word of Divine proof in the Seven Letters, the essence of the Bayan.
Therefore hath God commanded in the Bayan that they should not wait regarding their children after eleven years have passed from their age, or fifteen years, or nineteen years—if unable at the first time, then the second, and if not, then the third. This is so that the conditions of limitation may be observed, otherwise whoso wisheth to seek the good-pleasure of the Beloved and is assured of what God hath promised to those who follow His command—that they shall be enriched through His bounty—will not wait beyond eleven, nay nine, nay nineteen, nay ten, nay nine of ten.
For all this is so that none who hath entered the Bayan should be diminished in any aspect of divine bounty. In every aspect that the servant witnesseth in God’s commands, as he observeth, let him know God’s purpose in that aspect. Then the one who knoweth God will look to the fruit of the commands and not be veiled by anything from what God desireth therein.
And verily the Seven Letters, until the final manifestation thereof, attendeth the places wherein mention is made of Its own Self and the tribulations of those martyred in Its path. No soul rejoiceth, nor is there anything in the Bayan that reacheth its ultimate perfection, except that the Seven Letters rejoiceth thereat and praiseth its Lord. And no soul in the Bayan grieveth, or is diminished in aught that preventeth it from attaining its perfection—even as seeing an unsharpened pen causeth grief, for its perfection in God’s sight is that it be sharpened—but that It witnesseth what It loveth to witness and rejoiceth thereat, for that thing in the Bayan hath entered Paradise.
And whoso desireth to gladden the Point of the Bayan should gladden It in Its latter manifestation, for that which hath been attributed to It of the joy and sorrow of those in the Bayan is like the sun attributing to itself the heat of the sun in mirrors, though it be from it, yet what reacheth these reacheth not the throne of the Point. It is an inner reality which none can comprehend save through Its manifestation, even as Muhammad, the Apostle of God, before. After His sun of manifestation had set, He was gladdened only by His Beloved in His kingdom, and He witnesseth those who followed His religion and beseecheth God for forgiveness and mercy for them, and He witnesseth those who entered not His religion or disobeyed His command.
Let him place himself before God and implore from his Lord what he deserves. No one knows his station, for he has set in the city and risen in the land of Fa. Before anyone knows himself, he knows all and bears witness to them, yet none knows him—neither his father, nor his mother, nor his brother, nor his sister, nor those related to him, nor those in his land. Even the divines in his land judge according to the religion prescribed for them, yet they know him not. Perhaps when they see him they will not bow before him, though night and day they prostrate to him. Thus are you […]
Let all of you deal kindly with all, and some of you with others, for they who manifest you see you and bear witness to you, though you know not and perceive not. And likewise should the Letters of the Living watch over the manifestations of the signs in your hearts, spirits, souls, bodies, and all that indicates God their Lord. For none but the Point knows himself, but all are in the dominion of his mother. Let all of you deal kindly with all, that none among the Letters of the Living be grieved through you. Let all of you deal kindly with all, that the Letters of the Living witness only what God has revealed in the Bayan from His presence, for on the Day of Resurrection you shall be questioned concerning this.
If you act according to what you have been commanded from God’s Book if you are able, and if not, grieve not to the extent of a mustard seed in the Bayan. For if what you love diminishes from you, God has angels who will complete from His Book what you love if you find no way to it. And God will grant you the reward of what you have loved from His presence—He is indeed the Generous, the Bountiful. When the servant is content […] when God knows that a soul is not capable of anything […] for this is the utmost that the servant loves to perform that deed, and harm not any soul, whether small or great, exalted or mighty or sublime, with that which whispers therein of what is not loved. For that will never harm the believer to any degree. Should anyone find this within himself, let him say:
It is as though nothing has occurred to his soul that would sadden him, and that is from the loftiness of the servant’s soul where he is not content that there should occur in his heart what God does not love in him.

title: BB00083: Ziyarat for Friday and Thursday nights
section: Part 2: “And for all who love aught…”
text:
Part 2: “And for all who love aught…”
And for all who love aught in the Bayan and are prevented from their love by what they are powerless over, God will multiply their reward from His bounty lest any soul in the paradise of the Bayan be saddened. He is indeed the Bestower, the Bountiful. There is no God but God, there is no God but He, the All-Bountiful, the All-Subtle.
When you present yourself before God, or have presented yourself, and have submitted to what was revealed before, then walk behind and sit in your place and recite what delights your heart—all that is to prepare you for the day of the manifestation of Him before whom you have presented yourself. Enter not into partnership with Him, nor rise against Him, but enter unto Him as you entered unto Him in His dust. Let him reckon according to the measure of his certitude, such that when the servant desires to know at the time he is taken how much of his Lord’s dominion his knowledge has encompassed—for that is among that for which the servant thanks his Beloved and praises Him for what He has bestowed from the treasuries of His bounty—and let him preserve what he reckons regarding what has been revealed, what is raised up, that his knowledge may encompass it, for He loves.
God hath ordained in the Bayan and pledged that He will not call anyone to account if they render account of what God their Lord hath bestowed upon them. If one is precise in accounting, not a grain’s weight escapeth His Pen, for this causeth souls to be exact and establisheth them, that they might learn the science of accounting. This is of God’s bounty unto whosoever entereth that Paradise until the Day of Reckoning, whether male or female. This is the first manifestation of Him Whom God shall make manifest. He exalteth what He willeth and abaseth what He desireth. None hath power to seize or to bestow except by His command. He doeth what He pleaseth and writeth what He willeth. He shall not be questioned about what He doeth, but all things shall be questioned.
When thou desirest to go forth, say: “Glory be unto Thee, O my God! There is none other God but Thee. Verily Thou art the First and before Thee there was naught, or from that First for which there is no beginning, which hath ended in Thy manifestation in the Bayan. Since before there were none save the Seven Letters who attained unto the truth, O my God, bless them with glory and power. And verily Thou art the Last and after Thee there is naught, for all that is possible of Thy manifestation after that Manifestation is in that Manifestation itself, and there was none after the Seven Letters who sought truth in that Manifestation from anyone. And verily Thou art the Outward and there is none besides Thee exalted and perceiving, and I witness none besides the Seven Letters in that Manifestation manifesting Thy exaltation above all that is exalted and perceiving. And verily Thou art the Inward and there is none besides Thee mighty and glorious, and I witness no manifestation of Thy might besides the Seven Letters in that Manifestation above all that is mighty and glorious.
For Thou hast judged those who entered not the Bayan as being without truth, and if Thou knewest truth from before, how couldst Thou judge […] in the Bayan contrary to what Thou didst reveal therein, even if in that Manifestation Thou hadst with Thee […] to reveal it.
Glory be unto Thee! There is none other God but Thee. Thou hast no beginning nor end. Thou wert eternally First before all things and Thou wilt eternally remain after all things. Creation and Command are Thine alone. There is none other God but Thee. In every Manifestation Thou dost raise up […] of Thy Will as Thou pleasest, through what Thou pleasest, when Thou pleasest, and Thou choosest for Him Letters of the Living as Thou willest, through what Thou willest, when Thou willest. I bear witness at this moment, and all things witness, that I have known no truth after the revelation of the Bayan except in it, and I behold no manifestation of Thy truth in another Manifestation, that Manifestation which none can repel from Thy presence. But before Thou didst manifest what Thou didst manifest, I knew not Thy good-pleasure save from the Seven Letters in the Bayan.
Glory be unto Thee! Verily Thou art the One worthy of worship in truth, and verily Thou art the Intended […]. I have worshipped none but Thee and I have recognized none besides Thee. My knowledge of Thee is not like the knowledge of those who all speak saying “We stand firm in Thy Manifestation.” Verily Thou art the Unseen that cannot be perceived and the Eternal that cannot be described. Yea, Thou art too glorious to be perceived and too exalted to be described. But I have worshipped none besides Thee, for Thou wert the Worshipped One before and after, and I have recognized none besides Thee, for Thou wert the Beloved in the glory of eternity. No soul can ever perceive the Essence of the Unseen through Thy manifestation, for He is He.
It is incumbent upon whoso hath recognized Thee to turn unto Thee, for there is no God to be worshipped besides Thee, and no Object of desire save Thee. Indeed, I am convinced that Thy Manifestation hath no beginning, and after it shall come Thy Manifestation in the other world—a hidden manifestation following this first creation. Yet throughout all this, nothing was witnessed besides Thee, nor any hidden essence save Thine own. How can any remembrance other than Thee occur to my heart? How can I succeed in unifying Thee, sanctifying Thee, glorifying Thee, and magnifying Thee? If I worship Thee with pure and sincere devotion, Thou alone art God. Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. All things stand firm by Thy command, and verily Thou art too exalted and glorious to be comprehended by any save Thyself or to be unified by aught except Thee. Yet to the extent possible in creation, I shall worship Thee, unify Thee, sanctify Thee, and magnify Thee.
No thing can be conceived above Thee, nor below Thee, nor before Thee, nor after Thee. Rather, should I ascend unto the limitless realms, that would be manifestation after manifestation, manifestation following manifestation, wherein nothing is seen in any manifestation except Thee alone, there is no God but Thee, just as nothing was seen in the manifestation before Thee, and before that, unto a mention that hath no beginning in Thy knowledge, except Thee alone, there is no God but Thee. None hath glorified Thee save Thyself, none hath sanctified Thee save Thyself, none hath unified Thee save Thyself, and none hath magnified Thee except Thyself. Yet all shall glorify Thee, all shall sanctify Thee, all shall unify Thee, all shall magnify Thee, all shall exalt Thee, all shall honor Thee, and all shall extol Thee to the extent possible within them in every manifestation, through that which Thou hast revealed unto them through them.
And though they be veiled in Thy later manifestation, yet they worship Thee in Thy first manifestation. But since Thou hast loved to be worshipped on that Day through the Bayan by what Thou hast revealed unto it, therefore Thou hast not decreed anything for those who worship Thee in the manifestation before Thee, just as Thou didst decree after Thy manifestation in the Furqan for those who […] O my God […] in every manifestation, for this is what […] Thou art the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful, the Almighty.
