title: BB00311: Ziyarat for the fifth to be martyred among the Letters of the Living
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O my God, my Lord, my Beloved and my Heart’s Desire! How can I begin to make mention of Thee and sing Thy praise, or ascend to the horizon of Thy glory and majesty, and bear witness before Thee to that whereunto Thou hast testified concerning Thine own Self, of the loftiness of Thy sanctity and the splendor of Thy light? Thou art He Who hast existed before all things, and Thou art He Who shall endure after the passing of all things. Verily Thou art He Who existeth with all things through Thine own Being, creating whatsoever Thou willest.
Thou hast ever been known through other than Thyself and wilt ever be described through none but Thee. I testify, and all that Thou hast created and wilt create testify, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone, with no partner. Thine is the creation and the command. Thou givest life and causest death, then causest death and givest life, and verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not. Within Thy grasp is the kingdom of all things. Thou createst what Thou willest, how Thou willest, by what means Thou willest, when Thou willest, and verily Thou art powerful over all things. Thou originatest what Thou desirest, how Thou desirest, by what means Thou desirest, when Thou desirest. Verily, Thou art the Swift, the Omnipotent, the Powerful.
Glory hath ever belonged to those who glorify, sanctify, magnify and extol Thee, and abasement to those who know Thee not and stand not for Thy rights. Thou didst not create the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them save in truth, that they who dwell in the kingdom of Thy earth and heaven might worship Thee, and that whatsoever existeth in the kingdom of Thy creation and majesty might prostrate before Thee.
Thou hast ever been alone in the heights of oneness, sanctified in the exaltation of Thy unity, inaccessible in Thine own sovereignty, and elevated in the sublimity of Thy holy dominion. How exalted is Thy remembrance, O my God, in the depths of names and attributes, and how hallowed is Thy praise and glorification, O my Beloved, in the kingdom of beginning and end! Thou hast ever been one God, single, individual, ever-living, self-subsisting. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast had no partner in dominion nor any helper in command. Thou hast ordained all things and ordained them in perfect order.
The sweet-scented breezes of Thy holy grace have ever descended upon the people of Thy realm, and the wondrous tokens of Thy creative handiwork have ever shone forth to those who dwell in the kingdom of Thy earth and heaven. I have witnessed, O my God, what none can witness in the path of Thy love, and this, O my God, is naught but from the loftiness of Thy power and the exaltation of Thy sovereignty, wherein that Most Great Branch of the Tree of Thy oneness was drawn, of His own will, unto Thee, and His mystery ascended unto Thy presence. Yea, by Thy might, He attained unto Thy meeting, and was exalted through the exaltation of Thy names, and was illumined by the revelation of Thy signs, and was made resplendent by the radiance of Thy similitudes.
This is Thy way for those who seek to know Thee, for Thou hast chosen for Him the most exalted chambers of Thy paradise and the most glorious pavilion at the summit of Thy creation. For what is with Thee, O my God, is better than what is in the hereafter and the former life, and what Thou bestowest upon the people of Thy love is that which none can attain save those for whom Thou hast ordained the highest stations in the hereafter and the former life.
Therefore, O God, send down all the good whereof Thou hast testified, and bear witness to that in every condition through the loftiness of Thy grace and the sublimity of Thy glory. Verily, Thou art the Munificent, the Generous. Then turn unto the Direction whereunto the near ones turn, and the Countenance before which the worlds bow down, and say: Verily, the Most Glorious Glory be upon him who glorifieth Glory through Glory, and the Most Exalted Exaltation be upon him who exalteth Exaltation through Exaltation, and indeed the Most Pleasing Good-Pleasure be upon him who raiseth Good-Pleasure through Good-Pleasure.
O Lord, how can I begin to make mention of Thy praise, or desire to speak of any of the wondrous manifestations of the glorious signs of Thy sacred majesty? For verily God hath ever remembered Thee, praised Thee, and drawn nigh unto Thee, revealing Himself to Thee, through Thee, and unto Thee. This hath no equal in all the kingdoms of earth and heaven, nor can any mention in the realm of names and attributes compare with it. Therefore will I beseech God on that Day when all shall be brought before Him, that He may grant me to attain unto Thy presence. God will surely unite me with Thee in the most exalted chambers of Paradise, for He hath ever been a Supreme Arbiter. Even thus doth God reward through Thee those who have martyred themselves in the path of His glory, for He hath ever been the All-Bountiful, the All-Powerful. Verily, we are God’s and unto Him shall we return. There is no power nor strength save in God, the Exalted, the Great.

title: BB00199: Ziyarat for the first and last to believe, on Friday
text:
The Visitation of the First and the Last unto the Presence of the One, the Incomparable—His Holiness ʿAlí-Muhammad, the Teacher
In the Name of God, the Most Inaccessible, the Most Holy.
I bear witness, O my God, on this Friday, unto the perfection of all things and that Thou art God, and that there is none other God but Thee, alone without partner, and that what Thou hast revealed in the Bayan is Thy proof unto Thy creation, and that those Seven Letters are Thy servant and Thy Gate, and that the Letters of the Living are Thy Names and Thy Proofs, and that whosoever hath believed in Thee and in Thy verses is a leaf from the tree of Thy love, and whosoever hath not believed in Thee nor in Thy verses is a leaf from the tree of fire. I seek refuge in Thee from it and from all that pertaineth unto it. Preserve me through Thy power, Thy might, Thy grandeur, Thy sovereignty, Thy dominion, Thy self-subsistence, Thy majesty, and Thy glory from all that is not of Thee.
I bear witness, and all things bear witness, that all things are Thy creation and within Thy grasp. Thine is the might and the majesty, Thine the greatness and the beauty, Thine the power and the independence, Thine the strength and the action, Thine the dominion and justice, Thine the similitude and the examples, Thine the mercy and bounty, Thine the glory and the exaltation, Thine the gift and the bestowal, Thine the might and the invincibility, Thine the victory and the triumph, Thine the power and the ascendancy, Thine the joy and the gladness, Thine the love and detachment, Thine the grandeur and the majesty, Thine the kingdom and the realm, Thine the glory and the might, Thine the power and the divinity, Thine the strength and the ruby, Thine the sovereignty and the human realm, Thine all that is seen and unseen from the highest heights to the lowliest atom.
I am assured that every object of worship besides Thee is null, all besides Thee perisheth and changeth, and every goal save Thee fadeth away. Wherefore, O my God, send down at this moment upon the first to believe in Thy Gate and upon the last to seek Thee through Thy verses, and upon all who were martyred between them among Thy Prophets, Thy chosen ones, Thy witnesses and Thy loved ones, from every most resplendent glory, from every most sublime majesty, from every most beauteous beauty, from every most magnificent grandeur, from every most brilliant light, from every most abundant mercy, from every most perfect word, from every most noble name, from every most mighty might, from every most efficacious will, from every most victorious knowledge, from every most powerful power, from every most pleasing utterance, from every most attractive love, from every most enduring sovereignty, from every most excellent exaltation, from every most elevated height, and from all that Thou lovest that hath no equal, no likeness, no peer, no similitude, no associate and no example.
Thou hast ever existed from all eternity, and wilt ever remain the Eternal, the Unique, without movement or transfer. Thou art the One Who existed before all things in independence, and Who bringeth all things into being through exaltation, and Who remaineth after the passing of all things in invincibility, Who existeth in the sublimity of holiness and majesty, and in the sovereignty of glory and beauty. All things forever bow down before Thee to the utmost of their capacity and seek Thy good-pleasure to the fullest extent of their station, for the promise of Thy Lord is too exalted to be likened unto aught else when it attaineth unto Thy love.
Yet I observe that if there be anyone from among the people of Thy wondrous creation who remaineth steadfast in his religion and boweth not down before Thee according to what Thou hast subsequently revealed of religions and sent down in the Bayan, but rather prostrateth himself before Thee according to what Thou didst create for him within his limitations and seeketh to draw nigh unto Thee through what Thou hast ordained for him in Thy religion—though this would not be, for one who hath not entered beneath the shadow of that Manifestation hath no worth—I would say this is one who prostrateth himself before Thee in this Revelation, for in every Revelation all the essences of Thy creation are Thy worshippers, Thy servants, Thy devoted ones, Thy channels, Thy faithful ones, and Thy visitors.
Thus it behooveth to be, else they enter not the arena of them that are nigh, and glorify Thee with the angels on high who praise Thee night and day and never cease. Then the veil is not lifted from the countenance of that soul’s heart; else, by Thy glory, he would become the most prostrating of them that prostrate when he knoweth Thee, and the most worshipful of them that worship when he findeth Thee. Is he distracted by aught wherein is not Thy love, or by aught that loveth not to prostrate before Thee? Glory be unto Thee! Were this so, that soul would not have prostrated in Adam’s religion. Rather, according to his knowledge doth he prostrate before Thee, except that veils have come between Thee and him. Indeed, he hath supposed Thy good-pleasure to lie in his standing still, and worship of Thee in his being veiled. Else, glory be unto Thee and exalted art Thou!
All shall worship Thee according to their capacity, all shall prostrate before Thee according to their capacity, all shall glorify Thee according to their capacity, all shall thank Thee according to their capacity, and all shall remember Thee according to their capacity.
Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee. I shall glorify Thee above all that contingent beings have glorified or shall glorify, and I shall sanctify Thee beyond all that existent things have sanctified or shall sanctify, and I shall exalt Thee above all that created things have called upon or shall call upon in unity, and I shall magnify Thee above all that atoms have magnified or shall magnify. Thou art the Most High and there is naught above Thee, Thou art the Most Exalted and there is naught beneath Thee. I shall testify that all besides Thee is created and within Thy grasp, and none hath anything save through Thy Will.
O God! Bestow all Thy goodness upon them that have entered the Bayan, and send down, O Lord, the hosts of Thy victory upon the letters of Thy Name, the Most Merciful. Seize, O God, by all Thy might and power, them that prostrate not before Thee and believe not in Thy signs. Verily, Thou art the Most Compelling of them that compel, the Most Powerful of them that are powerful, the Most Severe of them that are severe, the Most Forceful of them that are forceful, the Most Manifest of them that are manifest, the Most Invincible of them that are invincible, and the Most Sovereign of them that are sovereign.
O God! Do Thou establish the Tree of Thy affirmation and cause to perish whosoever entereth not beneath the Tree of Thy affirmation. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things. There is no power nor strength save in God, the Most High, the Most Great.
Verily the Glory is from the Glory of God, the Most Glorious, and Paradise is from the Majesty of God, the Most Majestic, and Beauty is from the Beauty of God, the Most Beautiful, and Grandeur is from the Grandeur of God, the Most Grand, and Light is from the Light of God, the Most Luminous, and Mercy is from the Mercy of God, the Most Merciful, and Words are from the Words of God, the Most Perfect, and Might is from the Might of God, the Most Mighty, and Names are from the Names of God, the Most Great, and Will is from the Will of God, the Most Decisive, and Knowledge is from the Knowledge of God, the Most Penetrating, and Power is from the Power of God, the Most Extensive, and Love is from the Love of God, the Most Loving, and Sovereignty is from the Sovereignty of God, the Most Enduring, and Dominion is from the Dominion of God, the Most Glorious, and Loftiness is from the Loftiness of God, the Most High, and all things are from the Essence of all things, the Most Exalted.
Upon Thee, O Thou Sublime and Impregnable Glory, and upon them that are beneath Thy shade! Then upon Thee, O Thou Sublime and Lofty Excellence, and upon them that are beneath Thy shade! Verily, the heavens and the earth and all that is between them grieve for your affliction and the affliction of them that are beneath your shade. How great, how majestic, how mighty, how luminous, and how glorious it is, that every possessor of glory weepeth over you both, and every possessor of loftiness grieveth before you both. And verily all that existeth besides God hath been created.
For God hath, through your light, created and through your remembrance, exalted that which beseemeth, from God and from those who dwell beneath your shadow, and from all who have believed in God and His signs, the loftiness of God’s bestowal upon you both and the sublimity of His gift unto you. God hath given you that which is envied by those who were before and those who shall come after, by those who are manifest and those who are hidden, and this because ye have detached yourselves unto God and have prostrated yourselves at the Gate in prostration before God, your Lord, the Lord of the heavens and of the earth and of whatsoever is between them. Ye have professed the unity of God, exalted be His glory, by your words, your hands, your souls and whatsoever is related unto you.
Such is the state of him who hath known God, then worshipped Him, who hath glorified God, then proclaimed His oneness. The angels of Paradise have ever descended from the most exalted heights unto your court, and through you have drawn nigh unto God, your Lord. Therefore, upon you, and upon you, O ye hearts that glorify, O ye sanctified spirits, O ye souls that are enthralled, O ye bodies that are purified, O ye faces that beam with light, until such time as God shall cause you to return unto the Manifestation of Him Whom God shall make manifest on the Day of Resurrection, when ye shall, on that Day, circle round about Him. There is no power nor strength except in God, the Most High, the Most Great.

title: BB00179: Ziyarat for the first to be martyred among the Letters of the Living
text:
In the Name of God, the All-Merciful, the Most Compassionate
O Lord! I beseech Thee by Thy Name—O God, O All-Merciful, O All-Compassionate, O Lord, O Sovereign, O All-Encompassing, O All-Powerful, O All-Knowing, O All-Glorified, O All-Wise, O Oft-Turning, O Maker, O Protector, O Succourer, O All-Bounteous, O Originator, O All-Hearing, O All-Mighty, O All-Wise, O One, O All-Forgiving, O Nigh, O Answerer, O Most Stern, O Most Swift, O All-Tender, O Forbearing, O All-Seeing, O All-Aware, O He, O Ever-Living, O Self-Subsisting, O Most High, O Most Great, O All-Sufficing, O All-Praised, O Bestower, O Witness, O Master, O Helper, O Reckoner, O Guarantor, O All-Pardoning, O …, O All-Thankful, O All-Knowing, O Subduer, O Able, O Intercessor, O Cleaver, O Creator, O Subtle, O Preserver, O Chastiser, O …, O Deliverer, O Most Strong, O Keeper, O Sought-For Help, O Prevailing, O All-Compelling, O Originator, O Most Exalted, O Refuge, O All-Determining, O …, O All-Forgiving, O King, O Truth, O Doer, O Recorder, O Light, O Guide, O Most Generous, O Opener, O …, O …, O Speaker, O Most Lofty, O All-Grateful, O Provider, O …, O Sovereign, O First, O Last, O Manifest, O Hidden, O King, O Most Holy, O Peace, O Faithful, O Guardian, O All-Mighty, O All-Subduing, O Possessor of Majesty, O Fashioner, O Supreme Ruler, O …, O All-Loving, O Most Exalted, O One, O Self-Sufficient, O God—to send down Thy blessings upon the Tree of Sinai and upon what Thou didst bring forth from the letters of His Self, the branches of His bounty, and the leaves of His exposition.
For Thou, O my God, hast ever been, and shalt forever remain, One Who bringeth forth wondrous breaths and calleth into being ever-new manifestations, distinguishing therewith the Dawning-Places of Thy Command and conferring thereby upon whomsoever Thou wilt among the Daysprings of Thy might.
Thou hast beheld the decree of a calamity—how great in the Bayan before Thee, and how momentous, long aforetime, in the Furqan before Thee! I, therefore, entreat Thee, O my God, by that sublime affliction—mighty, august, exalted and uplifted—whose burden ascended and was borne aloft, even unto the seat whereunto none hath been preferred, nor shall any be joined thereafter, save if Thou shouldst will it: send Thou down upon those hearts and spirits and souls and bodies that whereby Thy ipseity may glorify Thy Ipseity, Thy essence praise Thy Essence, Thy selfhood confess Thy Selfhood, and Thy identity magnify Thy Identity.
And upon such as knew not the right of those beloved Manifestations, from the billows of the Most High unto the lowest atom, and the purposed Dawning-Places, in the world to come and in this first life—send down what beseemeth the deserts of each in Thy sight. For Thou art the Possessor of dread chastisement against such as know Thee not, and the Ordainer of unerring retribution against those who love not them that have believed in Thee and in Thy signs.
Do Thou, then, O God, by Thy power, distinguish in truth between negation and affirmation; for Thou art, over whatsoever Thou willest, supremely potent, and unto whatsoever Thou desirest, all-subduing and most swift to accomplish.
Then turn thou toward Him Who is seated upon the throne of His majesty and established upon the couch of His exaltation, and say: Verily, the Most Glorious, the All-Glorious; the most exalted praise be upon thee—thou whom God singled out aforetime in the Furqan, and after that in the Bayan; He chose thee that thou mightest hearken, before all things, unto the signs of His sovereignty and the manifestations of His power—signs which those in the kingdom of the heavens and of the earth and what lieth between them have been powerless to comprehend, and which none in the realms of Command and Creation and what is below them can produce the like thereof. How exalted were Thy Names aforetime and hereafter! How have Thy manifestations been established in heaven and on earth!
I testify that through thee the true believers enter into the presence of God, both before and after; that those assured of the signs of God prostrate themselves in the heavens and on the earth; and that no worshipper in heaven or on earth but must needs confess, before Thee, Thy right over all things. For, next to the right of God, there hath never appeared, in the realm of origination, a right like unto thine. Through thee did God unlock whatsoever He unlocked; through thee did God bring into being whatsoever He brought into being; through thee did God send down whatsoever He sent down; through thee did God inaugurate whatsoever He inaugurated; and through thee did God ordain whatsoever He ordained. Blessed, then, is he who knoweth that his very self is thy self, and through thee turneth unto God, thy Lord—though thy calamity kindle fire within the hearts and melt the livers and the souls.
Yet that which God hath decreed for thee—of the loftiest heights of Guardianship and the most sublime …—He hath engraved upon thy heart, thy spirit, thy soul, and thy body: it exalteth the servant, even as it grieveth him. This exalteth—and this afflicteth—until the Day whereon God shall restore thee unto the first life and shall, from the treasuries of His command, vouchsafe thee what thou lovest and desirest. Ever have those under the Furqan been cast into mourning …; and those under the Bayan have let tears flow upon their cheeks because of Thy decree.
I bear God—and every soul—witness that martyrdom hath been ennobled through thee and uplifted by reason of thy acceptance thereof, for the exaltation of the oneness of thy Lord and the inviolability of the sanctity of thy Fashioner. Ever will God—glorified be His majesty—remember thee; nor will thy Lord, the All-Merciful, cease … For this is of those things for which there is no equal in origination nor likeness in invention.
Make mention, then, of those who were present with thee there, who are sustained before thee in the presence of God, thy Lord; and give them glad-tidings of what God hath bestowed upon them of His bounty, that they shall be returned—and He shall surely grant them that for which they supplicate of His grace; with Him they are neither … nor powerless. There is no power nor might save in God: His is the creation and the command, before and after; and unto Him do all return.
I therefore beseech Thee, O my God, by the Names which Thou didst aforetime send down upon Thy Beloved in the Qur’an, and didst single Him out therewith above all men in the Bayan, that with every Name Thou hast sent down Thou wouldst cause hosts of angels to descend—the most high, the celebrating, the cherubic, the sanctified, the unifiers, the magnifying, the exalting, the venerating, the honouring, and the ranged in ranks before Thy Beloved—first upon Him whom Thou didst adorn with it in His very self, and upon the branches, leaves, and fruits of the Tree of His Guardianship.
For Thou, O my God, art too exalted, too lofty, too mighty, too holy, and too resplendent for me to mention the Point within the Tree of Affirmation; for Thou hast made it the Tree Thou hast set up and appointed as Thy Paradise for the people of Thy knowledge. It is the mirror of Thy Self, wherein none is seen but Thee and aught beside Thee is but Thy creation.
I beseech Thee, O my God, by that whereby Thou hast distinguished Thy creatures—by negation and affirmation, by fire and by light—and hast made the first who bowed down before Thee to be the Tree of Affirmation; and Thou didst seize, from the first of all things, him who turned away from Thee, causing him to vanish in the nothingness of his own self before Thee: send Thou down every chastisement Thou hast originated upon the Tree of Negation, that unto it may revert what is its final home and destined end. And send Thou down all Thy mercies and Thy bounties and Thy grace and Thy blessings and Thy care and the manifestations of Thy sovereignty upon the Tree of Affirmation—its root and its branch, its boughs and its leaves and its fruits—until Thou makest me to witness, O my God, that from me Thou hast averted every seizure and vengeance meant for it, and upon whomsoever turneth toward me and is related unto me Thou hast poured Thy blessings and the forthshinings of Thy might. This is that which Thou lovest to behold; for I have no love but Thy love, no mention but Thy mention, no praise but Thy praise, no command but Thy command, no act but Thy act.
Thou hast ever decreed what Thou willedst, how Thou willedst, by what Thou willedst, when Thou willedst; and Thou wilt ever accomplish what Thou desirest, how Thou desirest, by what Thou desirest, when Thou desirest, for whom Thou desirest. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
Send down then, O God, upon the Tree of Negation what it deserveth at Thy taking; and upon the Tree of Affirmation what it deserveth, through Thy bounty and Thy grace—what beseemeth Thy mercy and the tenderness of Thy Lordship. Verily, Thou art the best of the merciful!
crumbs: BB00179: Ziyarat for the first to be martyred among the Letters of the Living

title: BB00133: Ziyarat for the first to believe, on Thursday night
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Inaccessible, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I testify unto Thee, as doth every created thing on this night—the night of Friday—whereon Thou beholdest him who calleth upon Thee in the Bayan, that there is none other God but Thee, alone, without partner, and that the Bayan is Thy proof wherein is detailed all things. Thou hast manifested Thy power therein such that were all who dwell on earth to gather together to produce a verse like unto Thy verses, they would be powerless. Therefore, glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee.
I further testify that the Seven Letters are with Thee and are Thy proof, that the Letters of the Living are Thy first Names, and that those who have believed in Thee in the Bayan are the evidences of Thy sovereignty, and all that is therein is from Thee, as Thou hast revealed in the Bayan that there is no God but Him, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the All-Compelling.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! How can I affirm anything of Thee when […] if there be nothing beside Thee? And though I know there is no creator besides Thee, no sustainer besides Thee, no life-giver besides Thee, no quickener besides Thee, and no resurrector besides Thee—Thou Who hast revealed Thyself to all things through all things that verily I am God, there is no God but Me, the Mighty, the Beloved.
Glorified art Thou! Send Thy blessings upon the Point of the Bayan, our Sovereign, our King, our Lord, our Beloved, and our Desire, in its beginning and its end, and upon the evidences of Thy Names in their beginning and their end, and upon the likeness of Thy Names in their beginning and their end, for Thy power extendeth over both, Thy sovereignty prevaileth over both, Thy Will is manifest in both, Thy Purpose is triumphant in both, Thy signs are resplendent in both, Thy words are perfected in both, and Thy revelations shine forth in both. Thine is the command and the creation, before and after. There is no God but Thee, the Self-Subsisting, the All-Compelling.
Send down, O my God, at this moment upon the Tree of the Bayan, its root, its branch, its twigs, its leaves, its fruits, and all that pertaineth unto it, that which beseemeth the loftiness of Thy generosity, the sublimity of Thy gift, the inaccessibility of Thy grace, the exaltation of Thy bounty, the excellence of […] and the manifestation from Thee, and the satisfaction of Thy bestowal. For verily Thou art powerful over all things, exalted above all things, inaccessible at the right hand of all things, elevated beyond the left hand of all things, and sovereign over every quarter of all things.
All shall glorify Thee according to their capacity, all shall sanctify Thee according to their capacity, all shall unite in Thy oneness according to their capacity, all shall magnify Thee according to their capacity, all shall exalt Thee according to their capacity, all shall venerate Thee according to their capacity, all shall extol Thy majesty according to their capacity, all shall honor Thee according to their capacity, all shall acclaim Thy sovereignty according to their capacity, and all shall prostrate before Thee according to their capacity, being assured that none of this can reach unto Thee in the sublimity of Thine exaltation and the supremacy of Thine inaccessibility, but rather reacheth unto the Manifestation of Thy Self, the Seven Letters, and those who point to Thee beneath His shadow from among the evidences of the sovereignty of Thy Self-Subsistence and the dwellers in the heaven of Thy sanctified might.
Thou art He Who existed before all things, Who brought all things into being, Who is above all things, Who is with all things, and Who subsisteth beyond all things. Send down, O my God, at this moment upon the Seven Letters, in their beginning and their end, and the manifestations of their self, and that which pointeth unto them, in their beginning and their end, from every help that helpeth them.
And grant unto it from all invincibility its most invincible, and from all sovereignty its most enduring, and from all loftiness its most elevated, and from all might its mightiest, and from all greatness its greatest, and from all grandeur its grandest, and from all joy its most joyous, and from all majesty its most majestic, and from all beauty its most beautiful, and from all light its most luminous, and from all sanctity its most sanctified, and from all mercy its most diffusive, and from all bounty its most resplendent, and from all grace its most gracious, and from all generosity its most generous, and from all munificence its most munificent, and from all names its greatest, and from all will its most decisive, and from all purpose its swiftest, and from all power its most powerful, and from all decree its most steadfast, and from all execution its most equitable, and from all glory its most beloved, and from all scripture its most splendid, and from all utterance its most pleasing, and from all judgment its most impregnable, and from all dominion its most independent, and from all might its most transcendent, and from all divinity its most concealed, and from all ruby its most treasured, and from all eternity its most ancient, and from all kingdom its most glorious, until Thou dost witness in the sanctuary of the first to believe in it what Thou witnesseth at that moment in the essence of the Seven’s elevation of gold, for the kingdom is Thine alone, there is no God but Thee, for whomsoever Thou willest, however Thou willest, through what Thou willest, and Thou bestowest upon whomsoever Thou willest, through what Thou willest, however Thou willest.
Therefore, O my God, manifest the sovereign power of Thy might throughout all created things, that they may raise up Thy house if one be able from above the water to cut diamond? Nay, rather like […] which is attributed to Thee, it behooveth […] upon this and according to the measure that Thou causest means to flow from the treasuries of Thy Command and sendest down destinies from the heaven of Thy might, and that Thou mayest raise up the houses wherein Thy Self hath been glorified to the highest possible degree in creation with Thee, for by Thy might, if […] according to the measure that the house of the first to believe in Thee and Thy signs is raised up of peerless ruby, were the suspended earth above the water to be filled until it reached the horizon of what is possible in elevation—for this is glory unto that thing, for it is attributed to that which is attributed to Thee, otherwise if it be not expended in Thy path and remaineth within its bounds, what difference is there between it and a stone with Thee?
Glorified art Thou, there is no God but Thee, Thou didst not create anything except for the Manifestations of Thyself and for those who draw nigh unto Thee in that Revelation than him upon whom […] Thy signs and upon whom Thy words were sent down, and those who are guides unto him, for they are guides unto Thee, and I beseech Thee for faith in Thee and in Thy signs in every Revelation, for what would benefit me and everything this and otherwise less than that I see from the day of Adam until now among the people which profiteth them not, nay rather I see them in the fire, so how would it benefit me were I to fill the pillars of my house with the red elixir, but on the Day of Resurrection Thou wilt not raise me first from the resting-place of a believer unless Thou rememberest me with a mention of Thy good-pleasure, nay by Thy might, though none may encompass the knowledge of my seat, yet on that Day Thou wilt raise me from the resting-place of one who believeth in Thee and nothing shall diminish from Thy grace towards me, and if Thou gatherest both for me it is better, for Thy treasuries are inexhaustible and Thy bounties are uncountable, if anyone through his knowledge be a guide unto Thy glory as though there were on that Day among those who believed in the Qur’an any glory, whether among their living or their dead, there was none but the All-Glorious.
Your Beloved Muhammad, Who possesses such glory, is more submissive than anyone possessing submission and more humble than anyone possessing humility. None owns this glory except Him. And despite His lofty glory before Thee, He is indeed humble and prostrate before Thee, submissive and low. Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. And if any believer in Muhammad experiences abasement, this brings grief to Thy Beloved if it relates to love for Him; otherwise such a one has turned away and will not return to Him. And likewise, O my God, in the Bayan, clothe every believer in Me with the garment of Thy glory if they believe in Him Whom Thou shall manifest on the Day of Resurrection through Thy verses. But clothe with the garment of Thy chastisement and vengeance, and place beneath His feet like dust, nay smaller than that, those who do not believe. Indeed, I am not pleased that such souls should enter My religion when they have not believed in My return.
Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. Glory belongs to Thee and to those who believe in Thee in that Manifestation through the Seven Letters and what Thou hast commanded in the Bayan. O God, bestow then all Thy blessings upon Him Whom Thou shall manifest, and upon His father, His mother, His brother, His sister, and those created through His grace, and those related to Him among His near kindred, and those who enter beneath the shadow of the sovereignty of His love—upon all things by which something is mentioned. Verily, Thou art the All-Bountiful, the All-Encompassing, the All-Surrounding.
Then turn to the Tree of Sin and say: May there shine from the horizon of Glory and rise from the horizon of Might and Beauty upon thee, O Most Luminous Leaf, the splendor, the fragrance, the pure Names, the Essence of symbols, the abstract Lights, and upon those who resemble thee in thy path from the beginning of Glory and Lights, and the possessors of ornament and adorning, that which extends to all things from God, the One, the All-Compelling, and that which the people of the Bayan draw from God, the One, the Manifest.
The glory from the Bayan be upon you, O sanctified hearts, holy spirits, glorified souls, adorned bodies, and forms that guide unto God, besides Whom there is no God. His are the most beautiful names, in both past and future. You are the highest example and the most beautiful names in your hearts. You shall not be guided except unto God your Lord. So glory be to God, your King, your Sovereign, your Lord and your God Who created you, sustained you, caused you to die, gave you life and will resurrect you. There is no God but Him. We and you are sincere unto Him, we and you are worshippers of Him, we and you are devoted to Him, we and you are thankful to Him, we and you are mindful of Him.
crumbs: BB00133: Ziyarat for the first to believe, on Thursday night

title: BB00338: Ziyarat for the fourth to be martyred among the Letters of the Living
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy!
Glorified art Thou, O Lord my God! Thou art the Creator of the heavens and the earth, the Knower of the unseen and the seen. Nothing escapes Thy knowledge, whether in the heavens or on the earth or in what lieth between them, and nothing can frustrate Thee in the kingdom of creation and command or in what lieth between them. Thou hast ever been one God, single, individual, self-subsistent, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, the All-Wise, the Just, the Holy, eternal, everlasting, self-sufficient. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast no partner in sovereignty nor any protector on earth save by Thy leave. All Thy creation hath ever worshipped Thee and all besides Thee bow down before Thee, yet Thou acceptest only from those who have recognized Thy truth and entered unto Thee through the gates of God from Thy presence.
For Thou hast ever been independent of all Thou hast created and exalted above all Thou dost create. Thou didst not create what is in […] before it or take comfort in what came after it, but rather didst create all things that all things might testify to Thy independence of all things and the sovereignty of Thy Lordship over all things, that all things might taste of Thy knowledge and drink of the cup of Thy creation, that all things might behold the lights of Thy countenance and witness the wonders of Thy might, that all things might reach the horizon of Thy glory and bounty.
Thou art the Being Who hath brought all things into being by Thy Will, and Thou art the Creator Who createth all things by Thy desire, and Thou art the Essence Who ordaineth all things by Thy power. Is there any heart that loveth Thee not and glorifieth Thee not? Is there any spirit that knoweth Thee not and sanctifieth Thee not? Is there any soul that boweth not before Thee and uniteth not with Thee? Is there any body that submitteth not to Thee and magnifieth Thee not? Nay, by Thy might! All glorify Thee though they know Thee not, and all follow Thy word though they witness not the manifestation of Thy Lordship. Were the veil to be lifted from the eyes of all Thy creation, then would all things prostrate themselves before Thy might and seek intercession with Thee apart from recognition of Thy Cause.
Glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou! […] the people of Thy Cause their just reward and cause those who have not […] to perish as they deserve. For Thou art the King of creation and the Sovereign of destiny. None can resist Thy command or reverse Thy decree. There is no power nor strength except through Thee. Thy mercy hath preceded Thy god-fearing servants and Thy vengeance is assured against Thy proud servants.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I have witnessed when I saw that Branch what causeth all hearts and spirits to melt and all souls and bodies to grieve. Send down upon him, O my God, from the treasuries of Thy wondrous grace that which befitteth the loftiness of Thy glory and praise. For what king, O my God, hath proudly opposed him in any matter save through the severity of Thy chastisement? Verily Thou art most severe in punishment and most terrible in retribution. Then turn unto him whom Thou didst desire to meet and appear before his sovereignty and say: May the ornament of names and the essence of similitudes and the pure expression of destiny and the camphor of fulfillment and the pristine resignation from God and all His names and similitudes, and from all who believe in Him among all His creation, be upon thee, O thou exalted Light and lofty Glory!
Great is thy affliction and exalted is thy calamity in the kingdom of earth and heaven. God shall surely take vengeance on those who have proudly opposed thee, and God shall surely reward those who have kept their covenant with thee in the Book of thy Lord, and God shall surely unite me with thee in the heights of glory and the summit of holiness from His presence. Verily He hath power over all things. The glory is in what thou hast attained and the honor in the Book of God is in what thou hast witnessed. This is what the ancients glory in in the path of God and what the latter ones boast of in the good-pleasure of God. We are all of God and unto God our Lord, the Merciful, do we return. There is no power nor strength except through God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting.
crumbs: BB00338: Ziyarat for the fourth to be martyred among the Letters of the Living

title: BB00103: Ziyarat for the martyrs
text:
Part 1: “Verily, all glory from God, Who is none…”
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Verily, all glory from God, Who is none other than He, be upon thy heart and the heart of what is within thy heart, upon thy spirit and the spirit of what is within thy spirit, upon thy soul and what is within thy soul, and upon thy body and what is within thy body. Then all loftiness from God be upon thy heart and the heart of what was created from the light of thy glorification, upon thy spirit and what was created from the spirit of thy praise, upon thy soul and what was created from the soul of thy unity, and upon thy body and what was created from the light of thy magnification.
Thou hast ascended and none above thee hath ascended as thou hast, and thou hast drawn nigh and none below thee hath drawn nigh as thou hast. All essences have glorified God through the pure essence of thy glorification, all realities have praised through the camphor of thy praise, all souls have unified through the substance of thy unification, and all beings have magnified through the abstraction of thy magnification. All glorify God through thee, all sanctify God through thee, all unify God through thee, and all magnify God through thee. So great was thy calamity that all calamities of all contingent beings were severed from association with it, and thy tribulation was exalted to such a station that all tribulations were separated from mention with it among all contingent beings.
By Thy might! There is nothing besides God except that it weepeth for thee, abideth beneath thy shadow, glorifieth God as thou hast glorified, sanctifieth God as thou hast sanctified, unifieth God as thou hast unified, and magnifieth God as thou hast magnified. Thou hast ever been and wilt ever be in the heights of holiness and majesty, and thou shalt ever be in the summit of sanctity and beauty. Thou art the Manifest through the manifestation of thy Lord and the Hidden through the concealment of thy Lord, the First where there is no first besides thee and the Last where there is no last other than thee. Thou hast ascended in creation to a horizon that none hath preceded thee to, and thou hast established thyself above the throne of thy might in the highest horizon of paradise where God knoweth naught higher than it.
I do verily cause Thee—and all things—to bear witness that He hath appeared as a Manifest One, manifesting His Manifestation; and that through the superabundance of His remembrance the essences of contingent beings have been made manifest, the intrinsic realities of substances sanctified, and the souls of immaterial beings brought into being; and that all things have been purified from the confines of mere allusion. How, then, shall I remember Thee, O Beloved of my heart, O King of my might and my decree, O Sovereign of my beginning and my end? For whatsoever is in existence hath been created by Thy light, and whatsoever is intended cometh into being through Thy Revelation. Thou art He Who hath ever been mighty, and all are made mighty through Thy might; nor is there aught abased in any station when Thou art present. And at the hour when Thy sovereignty was established above the dust, all worshipped God through Thee, and beheld in Thee naught save Him. Is there any exalted might that can equal this, or any splendid glory that can resemble it? All magnify God and exalt Thy greatness.
What fruit, O my God, could be compared with one such as Thee? And what jewel could be more exalted than the essence that hath no likeness to Thine? Therefore do I bear witness unto God, and unto all things, that God hath manifested Thee beyond all similitude, and hath bestowed upon Thee that which He hath bestowed upon none of His creatures—not the earth and whatsoever is upon it alone, but the Kingdom of Ridvan and all who dwell therein. No heart doth conceive the mention of grandeur or majesty but that it falleth, with all that is upon it, into remembrance of abasement before Thee, descending unto the dust of Thy presence with the utmost humility. By Thy truth!
In the Bayan naught hath diminished Thy worth by even the weight of a mustard seed; nay, Thou hast ascended with Thy whole being until Thou didst take possession of all things. Who is able to praise Thee, or encompass Thy knowledge? Verily Thou hast traversed the Path on that Day whose beginning hath no beginning and whose end hath no end—nearer than the mention of the kaf to the nun—and Thou didst stand firm in Thy love amid the abodes of sorrow, as though Thou wert a mountain in creation, which none of the forces of invention could move.
God hath never ceased to bless Thee, and God hath never ceased to gaze upon the dust of Thy resting-place, forasmuch as Thou didst proclaim the oneness of God, Thy Lord, unto all that could possibly exist, and Thou didst heed not the reproach of any reproacher in all creation. Thou didst separate those who worshipped not God, and didst consign them unto the Fire, though Thou Thyself didst not know Thy station; and Thou didst endure from every rending trial that which none could endure, for had they known Thy reality they would have prostrated themselves before Thee, and would not have raised their heads until death overtook them. How could they contend with Thee by idle imaginings? Nay, by Thy might!
The Paradise of Thy near ones is naught but the knowledge of Thy Self, their contentment in Thy Essence, their steadfastness in Thy love, and their glory in remembrance with Thee in Thy presence. And the Fire appointed for them that waxed arrogant against Thee is naught but that which they have themselves earned; for the punishment that overtakes them is the fruit thereof. For verily, when God—glorified be He—willeth to chastise a servant, He causeth his own disobedience and his veiling from the splendour of Him before Whom he prostrateth himself by night and by day, by His decree, to be the instrument thereof. And when God willeth to admit a soul into His good-pleasure, He inspireth him with guidance from His presence, and bestoweth upon him success in that which draweth him nigh unto Him—wherefrom branch forth all good; even as from the former branch forth all that is its contrary.
And I send blessings upon You and upon those who loved You and upon those who were with You and upon those […] in Your court, and upon those who raise me through Your afflictions and weep for You due to the sublimity of Your trials and tribulations and the exaltation of Your calamity and Your decree. And God shall surely reach unto all who were not for You but against You. And what they earned regarding You […] they had earned the like of it before regarding every believing man and believing woman, nay, regarding all things. Such ones shall never enter paradise, nor shall their fire ever be exchanged for light eternally. God shall surely magnify through You and reach unto his soul from whence he knows not.
Had he known himself, he would surely have accepted with his hands or fled to the mountains to dwell in […] for what his hands had earned, and he has no protector or helper. It is as if I witness the angels of the Throne and the Chair and the heavens and the supreme Paradise and the most glorious Ridvan circling around Your dust, taking the water of eyes from whoever manifests in Your love and presents it before God Your Lord. God looks upon whoever attains that station and inscribes His good pleasure upon him and singles him out for every grace possible in His creation. For no drop of water is more beloved to God than what flows in Your calamity and appears […] in the exaltation of Your tribulation.

title: BB00103: Ziyarat for the martyrs
section: Part 2: “I bear witness before God and all things…”
text:
Part 2: “I bear witness before God and all things…”
I bear witness before God and all things that I draw near to You and through You to God in Your station, though there be nothing lower in creation, yet that horizon has none higher. That dust has been adorned and magnified and sanctified and glorified and beautified and embellished and elevated by having borne You and those with You. I bear witness that Your spirit and the spirits of them who have detached themselves unto God in the most exalted horizon of the Ridvan—God doth regard them, and the angels shall enter upon them from every gate. Therein shall ye have all that your souls desire, and God shall increase it for you at all times through His grace. Verily, He is the All-Bountiful, the Most Generous.
Then pray two brief rak’ahs, more delicate than any leaf, for when that soul desired to ascend unto God, it was in a state of such weakness as had been decreed. When thou art startled, say: “Glory be unto Thee, O God! O my God! Thou art the First, and naught is before Thee. Thou art the Last, and naught is after Thee. Thou art the Manifest, and naught is above Thee. Thou art the Hidden, and naught is below Thee. Thou art the Almighty, and none is Thy peer. Thou hast risen above all heights and drawn nigh in utter remoteness. Thou hast caused all the spheres to move at the testimony of Thy Proof, and the Pens in the Most Exalted Paradise have fallen still at the manifestation of Thy countenance. Thou art exalted—there is naught above Thee; and Thou art near—there is naught below Thee. Thou seest and art not seen. Thou art at the highest horizon. Who can flee from Thy dominion? Thy might prevaileth over all created things. Who can escape Thy grasp? Thy power is manifest over all existing things.
Thou hast admitted to the Ridvan those who believe in Thy unity, having bestowed upon them glory and immortality. And Thou hast destroyed those who believe not in Thy unity and cast them into the fire for what their hands have wrought. Thy sign admits of no doubt. Who is mightier than Thee in punishment, and greater than Thee in prowess? Such is Thy punishment for him who believeth not in Thee, whom Thou cursest along with all things, even their own souls, by names before them until the Day of Resurrection. And who is greater than Thee in bounty and nearer than Thee in generosity, when Thou hast bestowed upon those who believe in Thy unity that which Thou sendest down upon them until the Day of Resurrection—of every splendor its most splendid, of every majesty its most majestic, of every beauty its most beautiful, of every grandeur its most grand, of every light its most luminous, of every mercy its most expansive, of every word its most perfect, of every name its most great, of every glory its most glorious, of every will its most compelling, of every knowledge its most penetrating, of every power its most extensive, of every utterance its most pleasing, of every matter its most beloved and most impregnable with Thee, of every nobility its most noble, of every sovereignty its most enduring, of every dominion its most magnificent, of every exaltation its most exalted, and of all that Thou hast loved or lovest what befitteth the loftiness of Thy generosity and the sublimity of Thy grace.
For whomsoever Thou hast remembered, all things remember him; and from whomsoever Thou hast exacted retribution, all things exact retribution from him. How exalted is the loftiness of Thy punishment and Thy chastisement! How supreme is the height of Thy vengeance and Thy might! How great is he whom Thou wouldst destroy for want of Thy love, for in every Manifestation, whoso harboureth in his heart aught but Thy love is veiled from Thy Manifestation and entereth into the fire of separation from Thee. But that is that negation which Thou hast annihilated, and its aspects are remembered in its shadow. Therefore, O God, cause the tree of Thy love to grow with all that is in it and upon it, for that in its station hath no equal, save when Thou purifiest the earth from it. Then shall the essence of fire be concealed in the souls of those in whom it existed before, and faith shall be made manifest, yet their hearts remain veiled such that they acknowledge not the Primal Letters and those who love Thee, for as Thou hast shown me, O my God! In the Most Great Name and the most noble symbols, none is known save the letters Ra and Sad.
Therefore, O Lord, shower Thy mercy upon these souls. And if in that Manifestation I should witness such souls, and it be ordained that all should enumerate this until the Day of Resurrection—after which my heart would not wish to bear witness—then let all things be content therewith when they desire to call upon Thee by Thy greatest names and Thy nearest symbols. O Lord, grant unto him who desires this but is unable to achieve it, a double reward if he be truthful in his words yet unable to attain it.
And upon him who enters the arena of the high and sanctified Cherubim who glorify and unite, and between what Thou hast graciously bestowed upon the successful ones, bestow that which Thy knowledge encompasses through Thy ordainment. Verily, Thou art powerful over whatsoever Thou willest. Thou hast ever been praised in what Thou hast done and doest, and just in what Thou hast decreed and decreest. Therefore, O Lord, judge now between me and those who worship Thee not through Thy power which prevaileth over all things, for Thou art the Best of judges. O Lord, through Thy might, preserve all Thy believing servants at all times, before all times and after all times.
O Great Name! Know thou the measure of these exalted words, for verily a single letter thereof equals not the kingdom of earth and all that is thereon. Thou hast indeed attained two victories, achieved two goodly things, and performed two migrations. Perhaps from thy Lord’s Book thou shalt receive two measures of Baha’u’llah’s justice and two portions of every good thing. Weep thou as much as thou art able, and cause to weep those who can weep, for God loveth to behold faces whose tears flow from their pain. And what deed could be more excellent than this in the sight of God and of those who are endowed with knowledge in the Book of God, did ye but know. No soul weepeth for God in the Manifestations of God’s Cause and the Exponents of God’s remembrance but that Paradise is assured for him, and the sea of fire is forbidden him, through God’s grace. Verily, He is the One, the Effulgent.

title: BB00071: Ziyarat for the Point and his Letters of the Living

Part 1: “When thou desirest to visit the Point or…”
In the name of God, the Most Inaccessible, the Most Holy
When thou desirest to visit the Point or one of the Letters of the Living, thou must refine thyself to the utmost degree of refinement such that if thou shouldst know there is even one superfluous hair upon thy body, it would be unfitting at that time. And thou must wear thy most pure garments, not the most splendid thereof, such that if thou wearest an old shirt that is pure, good, refined and clean to the extent that thou knowest not even a speck of dust the size of a mosquito’s wing is upon it; for if thou knowest of such, it would be unfitting. When thou findest thyself in that most glorious state and supreme refinement, place upon thy finger a ring of red carnelian, which is the sign upon that path before thy glorious Lord and the means of attaining unto God upon the throne of glorification.
Then pray two rak’ahs in […] and say in the first […] after the takbir that God may teach thee:
Then in the second rak’ah do as in the first, and at the point of glorification say three times:
Then with hands outstretched say:
In thy sitting position say:
Then if thy place be empty of anyone save those with whom God hath permitted thee to recline, prostrate thyself and say in thy prostration “I seek forgiveness of God, our Lord, the All-Merciful” seven times in the morning and the evening. Then be silent and walk with dignity and composure until thou seekest permission at the gate with this luminous method:
Glory be unto Thee, O God, my God! Thou hast ever been existent before all things, and a being with all things, and established above all things, and existing after all things. Nothing escapeth Thy knowledge whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them, and nothing in the kingdom of command or creation or below them can frustrate Thee. I testify before Thee and all things that Thou hast ever been and wilt ever be One God, Single, Alone, Self-Sufficient, Ever-Living, Self-Subsisting, All-Holy, Just, eternally holy and everlasting, self-subsisting. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast no partner in what Thou hast created, nor any helper in what Thou hast fashioned. All are within Thy grasp and in the right hand of Thy will. Thou givest permission to whom Thou pleasest, how Thou pleasest, for what Thou pleasest, and Thou deniest whom Thou pleasest, how Thou pleasest, for what Thou pleasest. Thou art not questioned about what Thou doest, but all shall be questioned about what they do.
Therefore it behooveth thee, if thou art possessed of knowledge and art able to read and art capable thereof, not to neglect purification and refinement, for these are among the attributes of man. And remember God with what floweth from thy tongue in a state of tranquility and complete turning to God. When thou reachest the gate before the hand of God, prostrate thyself and say:
For this sufficeth thee in place of all prayers. And thou shouldst speak these words standing after rising from thy prostration. Then present thyself before God and recite the verse of prayer. Then say:
This sufficeth thee as a grace from God and a bounty from His presence in His Book. Verily, He is the Self-Sufficient, the Beloved.

title: BB00071: Ziyarat for the Point and his Letters of the Living
text:
“O God, our Lord, the All-Merciful! God beareth witness that there is no God but Him, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting. His is the dominion and the kingdom, then the might and the power, then the strength and the sovereignty, then the force and authority. He giveth life and causeth death, then causeth death and giveth life, and verily He is the Ever-Living Who dieth not, and the King Who passeth not away, and the Just One Who wrongeth not, and the Sovereign Who changeth not, and the Single One from Whose grasp escapeth nothing whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them. He createth what He willeth by His command. Verily He is the All-Knowing, the Mighty, the Great.”


“O God, our Lord, the All-Merciful! Say: He is the One, the Single, the Eternal Being, the Everlasting Existence, the Self-Sufficient, the Divine Being sanctified and relied upon, Who begetteth not nor is begotten, and there is none like unto Him.”



“Glory be to God, the Lord of might and majesty! Glory be to God, the Lord of beauty and countenance! Glory be to God, the Lord of power and perfection!”



“Glory be unto Thee, O God! There is no God but Thee, and Thou hast no partner. Thine is the creation and the command, from before and after. Thou givest life and causeth death, then causeth death and givest life, and verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not. In Thy grasp is the kingdom of all things. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command. Verily Thou art powerful over all things. Grant us, O God, every good thing which Thy knowledge encompasseth.”



“God beareth witness that there is no God but Him, the Mighty, the Best Beloved. And I verily testify before God and all things that the Seven Letters are the Gate of God in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and what lieth between them, and we all believe in Him. Verily God will send His blessings upon the Letters of Unity according to what He hath ordained from His presence at all times, before time and after time. He is the Protector, the Best Beloved.”





“There is no God but God, the Ever-Living, the Ever-Living. There is no God but God, the Just, the Just. There is no God but God, the True, the True. There is no God but God, the Lord, the Lord. There is no God but God, the Single, the Single. God, God is my Lord and I associate none with Him.”



“Verily the Most Splendid Glory is from God, Who is none other than He, the Possessor of the Most Exalted Similitude. Upon thee, O Most Exalted Tree, in the hereafter and the former times.”

section: Part 2: “I beseech Thee by the Divine Point…”
text:
Part 2: “I beseech Thee by the Divine Point…”
I beseech Thee by the Divine Point and then by the Letters of the Living, that Thou send Thy blessings upon the Tree of Thy love and whatsoever is in it and upon it, and that Thou reckon without the Tree of Thy love and whatsoever is in it and upon it, for verily Thy knowledge is never absent from anything in the heavens or on the earth or whatsoever is between them, and nothing can frustrate Thee in the kingdom of command and creation and whatsoever is beneath them, and verily Thou art the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful, the Exalted.

title: BB00293: Ziyarat for the second to be martyred among the Letters of the Living
text:
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily Thou art the Creator of the heavens and the earth, the Knower of the unseen and the seen. Nothing in the heavens or on earth or between them escapes Thy knowledge, and nothing in the dominion of Command or Creation or whatsoever is beneath them can frustrate Thee. From time immemorial Thou hast been alone in Thy might and permanence, and Thou hast subdued Thy servants through death and extinction. Thou hast caused those whom Thou willest to ascend through martyrdom in Thy path to the summit of contentment, and elevated those for whom Thou hast ordained Thy meeting to the highest heaven of glory.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I bear witness, and all things bear witness, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone without partner. Thine is the sovereignty and Thine the praise. Thou givest life and causest death, then causest death and givest life, and verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not. Within Thy grasp is the dominion of all things, and in Thy right hand is the empire of all things. Thou createst what Thou willest, how Thou willest, by what Thou willest, and Thou originatest what Thou desirest, how Thou desirest, by what Thou desirest.
Thou hast ever been one God, Single, Unique, Eternal, Self-Subsisting, the Ever-Abiding, the Ever-Enduring, the Self-Dependent. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast no partner in what Thou hast created, nor any protector in what Thou hast fashioned. They glorify Thee in the kingdom of Thy earth and heaven, they praise Thee in the kingdom of Thy might and creation, they unite in Thy oneness in the kingdom of Thy wondrous works and glory, they magnify Thee in the kingdom of Thy sanctity and majesty, and they extol Thee in the kingdom of Thy exaltation and bounty.
Thou hast ever existed before all things and Thou wilt ever exist after all things. Thou hast subdued those in the kingdoms of earth and heaven through Thy sovereign might, and Thou hast dominated those in the kingdom of Command and Creation and whatsoever lieth between them through the authority of Thy omnipotence. Thou hast utterly annihilated the Tree of Negation with all that pertaineth unto it, and Thou hast caused the Tree of Affirmation to endure with all that pertaineth unto it. How great is Thy right, O my God, how mighty Thy station, O my Beloved, how exalted Thy sanctity, O my Lord, how invincible Thy power, O my King, how lofty the inaccessibility of Thy Lordship, O my Master and my Sovereign!
From all eternity Thou alone hast administered true justice and abandoned those who have not recognized Thy unity through what Thou hast ordained for the people of destiny. When wilt Thou be veiled that Thy loved ones should lose Thee, and when wilt Thou not be manifest through wondrous appearances that Thy friends may thereby be illumined? Thou art the Manifest One Who hast ever been above all things, and the Subduer Who wilt ever be above all things. My God beareth witness how that Branch from the branches of the tree of Thy love hath unified Thee through what Thou hast created in his essence of the truth of Thy unity, through his heart, spirit, soul, body and form.
Accept, O my God, this manifestation of Thy sanctification, and elevate, O my God, this for the exaltation of Thy unity, and make glorious, O my God, Thy paradise for those who […] upon his dust in detachment unto Thee and who have prostrated themselves before Thee through drawing nigh unto Thee. Verily Thou art powerful over whatsoever Thou willest and mighty, and exalted and swift in whatsoever Thou desirest. Then bear witness with the eye of thy heart that when thou hast recognized him unto whom thou hast desired to turn with all thy being, thou hast indeed recognized God thy Lord, for that which is manifest in him is none other than I. Know thou therefore the station of him whose presence thou hast desired.
I testify that if thou wert to witness before Him what God hath witnessed thereof, verily the Tree of the Branch hath been established in its essence, and whoso visiteth it hath visited the Primal Tree in its reality, and whoso visiteth it after recognizing what God hath ordained for it, it is as though he hath visited God in supreme glory. How great is this bounty in the Book, if thou be of them that perceive.
Then turn and say: Verily the Most Glorious Splendor, and the Most Exalted Majesty, and the Most Beauteous Beauty, and the Most Great Grandeur, and the Most Luminous Light, and all that God hath testified are His names and His attributes, be upon thee, O thou Most Excellent Excellence and […] Essence, who hath […] unto God thy Lord through the attraction of thy heart before all names, and hast ascended unto God thy Lord through what thou didst intend in what thou didst manifest of establishing His oneness by what thou didst witness in His path.
By My life, My heart was consumed when God decreed concerning thee and carried out His will regarding thee. But since this was from God’s bounty upon thee, whereby through that martyrdom thou didst attain the highest horizon of divine authority, My heart is at peace until God joineth Me with thee in the most exalted station, at the distance of two bow-lengths or nearer, in the Most Great Paradise and the Most Glorious Pavilion. Verily He is My Lord, the One with power over this in the Hereafter and in this world. We are God’s and unto God do we return. There is no power nor strength except through God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting.

title: BB00258: Ziyarat for the sixth to be martyred among the Letters of the Living
text:
In the name of God, the Most Inaccessible, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Thou art the Creator of the heavens and earth, the Knower of the unseen and the visible. From eternity Thou hast, through Thine Essence, been exalted above all contingent things, and wilt forever, through Thy dominion, be elevated above all created things. In every condition Thou hast, through Thy power, been supreme over all who dwell in the kingdoms of earth and heaven, and at all times Thou hast, through Thy majesty, held sway over all existence. In every circumstance wherein a thing is mentioned, Thou hast, through Thy Self-Sufficiency, been exalted above all that exists in the kingdom of names and attributes. Thou art the Most High, Whose glory and riches can never decline, and Thou art the Most Exalted, Whose might and permanence can never be altered. I testify, and all things testify, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, the Lord of might and majesty, of greatness and beauty, of power and independence, of sovereignty and bounty, of grandeur and perfection.
From eternity all things have glorified Thee, sanctified Thee, unified Thee, magnified Thee and extolled Thee. When wert Thou ever absent that nothing could behold Thee? When wert Thou ever hidden that nothing could witness Thee? Thou art the Manifest through Whose manifestation all are veiled, and Thou art the Hidden through Whose concealment all are made manifest.
Glorified art Thou, O Lord! Thou hast ever been one God, single, eternal, self-subsisting, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Thou hast taken neither consort nor offspring, and Thou hast created nothing except that Thou hast made it bear witness to Thy oneness and that Thou hast no partner in sovereignty nor any protector on earth save by Thy leave. Thou hast ordained all things by Thy power and fashioned all creation by Thy wisdom. Thou hast ever been exalted above all loftiness and glory, and wilt ever be transcendent above all elevation and deed.
How can I make mention of Thee, O my God and my Beloved, after Thou hast shown me that the paths of all contingent things, in their very essence, are cut off from knowing Thy reality, and the most profound realities, in their inmost being, are prevented from knowing Thy sanctity? Therefore, O Lord, send down upon this Fruit that hath sprouted from the Tree of Thy oneness the most excellent of all that Thou hast created or wilt create: the most resplendent of all Thy glory, the most sublime of all Thy majesty, the most beautiful of all Thy beauty, the most magnificent of all Thy grandeur, the most luminous of all Thy light, the most extensive of all Thy mercy, the most perfect of all Thy words, the most complete of all Thy perfections, the greatest of all Thy names, the most mighty of all Thy power, the most conclusive of all Thy will, the most penetrating of all Thy knowledge, the most far-reaching of all Thy might, the most pleasing of all Thy utterance, the most beloved and inaccessible of all Thy causes, the noblest of all Thy honor, the most enduring of all Thy dominion, the most glorious of all Thy sovereignty, the most exalted of all Thy transcendence, the most effulgent of all Thy radiance, the most ancient of all Thy favors, the most wondrous of all Thy signs, the most excellent of all Thy grace, the most elevated of all Thy gifts, the most generous of all Thy bounty, the nearest of all Thy vastness, the most uplifted of all Thy elevation, and the most impregnable of all Thy protection.
O Lord! Purify all the letters in it, upon it and before it. Send down upon it, O Lord, that which will cause it to ascend to the supreme horizon and attain the Most Glorious Summit, for unto Thee belong the Last and the First. Seize, O Lord, with all Thy might, those who recognize not His right in Thee and who bow not before His majesty, and send down upon him, by Thy Name, the severest of Thy chastisements and the swiftest of Thy seizures. Verily Thou art powerful, mighty and omnipotent. There is no power nor strength except through Thee, and verily Thou art witness over all things. Thou recompenseth every soul according to what it hath earned, and verily Thou art the observer of all things. Thine is the creation and the command, both before and after, and unto Thee is the final return.
Then turn unto Him Who is established upon the throne of His might and hath taken His seat upon the seat of His supreme power, and say: Verily We are the Most Glorious Beauty from God, the Most Beautiful Names, and whatsoever God hath attributed unto Himself in the hereafter and from eternity in His Most Exalted Remembrance. Upon thee, O Tree of Blessedness, Lote-Tree of the Furthermost Boundary, Garden of Refuge, Most Glorious Horizon and Most Exalted Station at the distance of two bow-lengths or closer! I testify that Thou hast manifested, through what Thou hast endured in Thy Lord’s path, His glorification, His praise, His oneness and His grandeur, according to what God hath created in Thee of the sublimity of His power and the exaltation of His might.
How transcendent is Thy right over all created things, and how magnificent is Thy station amidst the depths of Names and Attributes! Thou hast attained unto that which none comprehendeth save whom God willeth. May God unite me with Thee, then with him who hath believed in Him, in the most exalted horizon with Him, for verily He is the Lord of the hereafter and of the former days. God shall destroy all who bow down before God through Thee yet recognize not Thy right with Him, and who have shown pride against Thee to the extent of a mustard seed, through His power, might, strength, sovereignty and grandeur. Verily, He hath power over all things. We are God’s and unto Him shall we return. There is no power nor strength except through God, the Most High, the Most Great.
Praise be to God, before Whom prostrate themselves whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is on earth and whatsoever is between them. He hath taken unto Himself neither consort nor son, nor hath He any partner in sovereignty. He giveth life and causeth death, then causeth death and giveth life, and verily He is the Ever-Living Who dieth not. Within His grasp is the kingdom of all things. He createth what He pleaseth by His command. Therefore glorify ye Him, magnify ye Him, strengthen ye Him, sanctify ye Him, and extol ye Him with great exaltation, honor ye Him, exalt ye Him, and praise ye Him with supreme praise.
crumbs: BB00258: Ziyarat for the sixth to be martyred among the Letters of the Living

title: BB00329: Ziyarat for the third to be martyred among the Letters of the Living
text:
In the name of God, the Inaccessible, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I testify with the essence of my being, the purity of my reality, the abstraction of my soul, and the camphor of my identity that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thine is the power, might, grandeur and awe; Thine is sovereignty and love; Thine is dominion and exaltation; Thine are the names and similitudes; Thine are majesty and glory; Thine are creation and command over all that is seen and unseen in the highest heavens and lowest earth, and in the Hereafter and this world. Thou hast ever been sanctified in the uniqueness of Thy Being and wilt ever remain hallowed in the purity of Thy Essence.
Thou seest what is in the kingdom of Thy earth and heaven, and witnesseth what lies in the depths of Thy creation and invention. Thou hast ever bestowed upon the people of Thy Paradise the wondrous lights of Thy Lordship, and denied unto those in the fire what Thou hast ordained for the people of Thy cause, for Thou hast ever encompassed all things in Thy knowledge and ordained all things by Thy power. Thou drawest the people of Thy love unto the horizon of Thy good-pleasure through what Thou hast cast upon them of Thy likeness, and causeth the manifestations of Thy glory to ascend through what Thou hast created in them of Thy examples.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Thou hast ever been one God, single, unique, eternal, self-subsisting, living, all-compelling, wise, just and holy. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast no partner in sovereignty nor any protector in the earth save by Thy leave. Thou hast made Thyself known unto all things as God, there is no God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thine is the kingdom and the praise, Thou givest life and death, then causeth death and giveth life, and Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not. Within Thy grasp is the kingdom of all things. Thou createst by Thy command whatsoever Thou willest in every condition. Verily Thou art powerful over all things.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I have witnessed concerning that Branch from the Tree of Thy Oneness how He cast Himself in the paths of Thy love and drank the water of Thy good-pleasure in the way of Thy Cause. Therefore, O my God, send down upon Him every good thing encompassed by Thy knowledge, and upon those who know not His rights, who prostrate not themselves before Thee through Him, who believe not in Him in the path of Thy love, and who acknowledge not what Thou hast ordained for Him of Thy right, whatsoever they deserve by Thy reckoning. Verily Thou dost encompass all things.
Then turn unto Him Who is established upon the throne of His glory and seated upon the seat of His sovereignty, Who seeth all things in their appointed places and witnesseth the creation of all things in their hidden and manifest aspects. Say: Peace be upon Thee from God, exalted and mighty, and from the Letters that have preceded Thee in attaining unto God Thy Lord, and from those who have followed Thee from among the Letters of the First, then from all who have believed in God and His signs, whether male or female, and who have entered beneath the shade of the Tree of Affirmation, O Thou Beloved of my heart in the kingdom of earth and heaven!
Then upon Thee, O Essence of my being in the kingdom of glory and creation! Great indeed is Thy calamity and profound Thy tragedy. Were life in this first existence eternal, what Thou hast faced in Thy Lord’s path would be better with God. And were every soul to comprehend what is ordained for it—but by Thy right, I was not content to witness concerning Thee what I witness now. But now what God Thy Lord decreed hath been fulfilled through the attraction of Thy being and the abstraction of Thy reality. May God join Thee in the most exalted Companion and the most glorious Seat where no sorrow existeth. He is the Lord of the Hereafter and this world.
God shall take vengeance upon those who observed not God’s command concerning Thee and showed no shame before Thy countenance. He is most severe in might and punishment. And God shall reward those who are certain of Thy right and are guided by Thy guidance on the day of Thy return with the best of what God hath in the Book. Verily He is the…inaccessible…
