title: BB00225: Ziyaratu’l-Avval (in honor of Mulla Husayn)
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Praise be to God, beside Whom there is no other God, He Who hath ever been and shall everlastingly be. And verily all glory from God be upon the Primal Unity until all mention endeth and until all matters are transformed night after night.
And now, when thou desirest to pluck the virgin fruits from the gardens of Paradise and observe the effulgent lights of the Countenance of Unity, then purify thine inward and outward being. Dost thou know from what? From every mention that is not of Him Whom God shall make manifest on the Day of His Manifestation. For thou mayest perchance manifest and purify thine inward and outward being, yet in the sight of God be in the fire and pay no heed to it. Therefore sharpen thy vision and refine thy sight lest the Day of Resurrection come upon thee while thou art veiled. And before that, purify thine inward being from all who are not of the Bayan, for that is a hill which calleth unto that which is other than God, and thy outward being according to what hath been revealed therein by whatever means thou art able.
For in that Manifestation, God loveth naught as He loveth the manifestations of essence, grace, beauty and purity—not through washing in water, but through making it refined and more refined, then subtle and more subtle, if thou art able to find a way thereto. Otherwise, content thyself with thy recognition of God and His commandments, rather than with that to which thou findest no way. For God sufficeth thee above all things, while nothing sufficeth above God, thy Lord. And grieve not in the Bayan, for God desireth to behold thee in joy and gladness, in delight and exaltation, except in circumstances decreed in the Book. It is as though I behold Him Whom God shall make manifest, exalted be His mention, smiling in all His conditions when He beholdeth no grief that would grieve His heart, for that is the attribute of those who are tested and the way of those who are alone.
When thou hast done this, then glorify God once at the First Gate, twice at the Second Gate, thrice at the Third Gate, four times at the Fourth Gate, and five times at the Fifth Gate. There seek permission from God and all His creation, and enter in humility, pledging that shouldst thou attain unto Him on the Day of Resurrection, thou wilt act likewise with Him; otherwise it will profit thee not, for His Manifestation on the Day of Resurrection is mightier than His previous Manifestation. And look not upon earthly conditions save by God’s command alone, for perchance thou shalt find Him on the Day of Resurrection in exaltation, and perchance thou shalt find Him in abasement. Make not this thy proof, but make the Word of Him Whom God shall make manifest thy path. For verily I have counseled thee with that which shall deliver thee on the Great Day in the presence of God, if thou desirest to be among those who are delivered.
Then stand before the man and say: “God, there is no God but He, the Most Glorious, the Most Glorious. His is all that is in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them, and whatsoever is above the heights and below the depths. The All-Merciful is established upon the Throne. Before Him boweth down whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them, and every thing is brought low. And unto God belong the most beautiful names.
O Primal Point! How shall I make mention of Thee before God, Thy Lord, the Lord of the highest heavens and Thy Lord, the Lord of the lowest earths, and Thy Lord, the Lord of the Hereafter and of the former time, and Thy Lord, the Lord of Paradise, the Abode, and Thy Lord, the Lord of the mighty horizon, and Thy Lord, the Lord of the Lote-Tree beyond which there is no passing, and Thy Lord, the Lord of the most exalted pavilion, and Thy Lord, the Lord of the Most Glorious Books, and Thy Lord, the Lord of ʿor nearer,’ and Thy Lord Who created Thee, then established Himself upon the Throne, then drew nigh, and hath chosen Thee for Himself, then was well-pleased. O Thou Who art My Glory in the highest heavens! O Thou Who art My Good-Pleasure in the lowest earths! O Thou Who art My names in the first life! O My light in the highest horizon! O My glory at or nearer!
I have created thee and made thee a supreme sign, chosen thee and made thee the highest paradise. I bear witness to what those created before thee by thy most exalted command have witnessed, and I know what has been decreed for thee by all those of low degree. I bear witness to those who have fulfilled thy remembrance in the highest heights, then ascended with thee into the most glorious cloud. I shall not promise thee any reward less than what thou hast witnessed in the path of God through the greatest sign, for that is the ultimate end in the first life and the next creation.
Those who have veiled themselves from thee have no recourse like what they have earned in thy remembrance, though they were created to prostrate before thee in the Hereafter and in this world. I have not created the highest paradise for those who have recognized thee and then ascended by thy command to the Most Glorious Source except that I shall remember them through My greatest signs. This is what all things shall remember them by from this day until the Most Exalted Day—the day when God shall manifest the sign of His most exalted countenance.
He shall surely raise thee by His word from thy resting place with a mighty, most glorious life. Thou shalt witness what the dwellers of the heavens and earth and all between them remember through thy most exalted remembrance. Thou shalt surely answer those who remember thee with the most hidden call:

“Fear not, neither grieve, for I shall raise thee unto God if thou followest Me on the Day of Resurrection through what thou hast answered from God.”

Then be content and remember those who have been raised unto thee to God, the Possessor of most beautiful attributes. They have entered the highest paradise and settled upon silken carpets at or nearer, drinking from ruby cups wine that neither intoxicates nor clouds the mind, partaking of fresh meat and whatever their souls desire in the most glorious seats, elevated upon their thrones while angels stand before them to remind them of what was revealed in Our greatest verses.
They recline with their houris who were created from the light of their Lord upon the highest dune—their very hair remembering that there is no God but Him, the Most High, the Most Exalted. It is as though they were created from the spring of living rubies, all of them floating like mirrors wherein naught can be seen save the face of their Lord, the Mighty, the Most Glorious. Before them are most exalted open books which they gaze upon, rejoicing in what God hath sent down to them.
This is what God, thy Lord, hath granted thee in the greatest station and sent down to thee in the highest paradise. How dost thou see those who have veiled themselves from meeting thee in the most glorious pavilion? Glory be unto Thee, O God! Thou art my Lord and the Lord of all that is on high and every lowest atom. Thou hast caused me to reach the horizon of what is possible in Thy knowledge through Thy most exalted grace. I have seen those who veiled themselves from My remembrance in the blazing fire, and I witnessed the nearest hour, then possessed the kingdom of the Hereafter and this world through what Thou hast bestowed upon me from Thy most glorious bounty.
I am indeed the first to worship Thee upon the earth when Thou didst cause me to hear Thy greatest verses. I shall surely bear witness, and all things with me, that there is no God but Thee, Lord of the seen and unseen. By Thy command hast Thou originated me, and unto Thee is the return and the end. Nothing in paradise remindeth me save what was sent down upon it of Thy most glorious bounty:

“Fear not, neither grieve, for thou shalt see what thou lovest and then be content.”

Verily God, my Lord and thy Lord, heareth the secret and the whisper. There is no God but Him, the Most Glorious, the Most Glorious.
crumbs: BB00225: Ziyaratu'l-Avval (in honor of Mulla Husayn)

title: BB00207: Ziyaratu’l-Kull
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Just, the Most Just!
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! This is a night wherein Thou hast opened the gates of Thy grace, Thy bounty, Thy generosity, Thy kindness and Thy bestowals. Therefore I beseech Thee by Thyself—for nothing can equal Thy justice, none can be Thy peer, none can resemble Thee, none can be Thy companion, and nothing can be Thy likeness—and by Thy Glory, Thy Majesty, Thy Beauty, Thy Greatness, Thy Light, Thy Names, Thy Might, Thy Words, Thy Wisdom, Thy Knowledge, Thy Power, Thy Command, Thy Will, Thy Honor, Thy Sovereignty, Thy Dominion, Thy Loftiness, Thy Favor, Thy Grace, Thy Bounty, Thy Generosity, Thy Kindness, Thy Gift, Thy Benevolence, Thy Glory, Thy Transcendence, Thy Utterance, Thy Inaccessibility, Thy Greatness, Thy Independence, Thy Splendor, and Thy Lights, to send down upon Thy loved ones in the Bayan, from the first whom Thou hast witnessed unto the last, that which befitteth the sublimity of Thy holiness and the exaltation of Thy glory.
Raise up, O my God, those within it through Thy exaltation; make resplendent, O my God, those within it through Thy light; glorify, O my God, those within it through Thy majesty; beautify, O my God, those within it through Thy beauty; magnify, O my God, those within it through Thy greatness; illumine, O my God, those within it through Thy light; have mercy, O my God, upon those within it through Thy mercy; strengthen, O my God, those within it through Thy might; teach, O my God, those within it through Thy knowledge; make content, O my God, those within it through Thy good-pleasure; empower, O my God, those within it through Thy sovereignty; grant dominion, O my God, to those within it through Thy dominion; enrich, O my God, those within it through Thy riches; honor, O my God, those within it through Thy favors; make excellent, O my God, those within it through Thy benevolence; preserve, O my God, those within it through Thy names; aid, O my God, those within it through Thy example; manifest, O my God, those within it through Thy power; and bestow, O my God, upon those within it all Thy grace and wisdom, all Thy bounty and gift, for verily Thou hast encompassed all things with Thy knowledge.
And educate, O my God, all those within it to prostrate themselves before Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest and to find shelter beneath the shadow of Him Whom Thou shalt raise up on the Day of Resurrection through Thy signs which are Thy clear evidences. Verily, Thou hast power over all things.
O my God! Thou knowest all things and bearest witness unto all things. Unto Thee have been raised glorifying hearts, sanctified spirits, enraptured souls, and magnifying bodies from the First One, then from the numbers which Thou hast created through Thy power. Among them are a father and a brother who inscribe Thy verses before Thee. Therefore send down, O my God, upon them both and upon all who preceded them and followed them that which befitteth the sublimity of Thy sovereignty and the exaltation of Thy station. For whoso taketh pride in Thee, his pride shall not perish nor shall his glory fade. How generous art Thou unto Thy creation, for Thou hast raised unto Thyself one whom Thou didst create from clay and return unto clay, yet preserved his remembrance between these two states until the Hour shall arise, whereby he is remembered in Thy paradise and exalted in the midst of Thy gardens.
Therefore send down, O my God, upon their first and their last, their outward and their inward, from the signs of Thy sanctification, the manifestations of Thy glorification, the fragrances of Thy exaltation, the modes of Thy praise, and the expressions of Thy unity and oneness, that which shall fill Thy heavens and Thy earth and whatsoever lieth between them with the exaltation of Thy remembrance, the inaccessibility of Thy power, the transcendence of Thy Word, the majesty of Thy greatness, and the establishment of Thy Self-Subsistence, for naught in the heavens or on earth or between them escapeth Thy knowledge, nor is anything in the kingdom of Command or Creation or what lieth beneath them beyond Thy power, for verily Thou art All-Knowing, All-Powerful.
When thou findest thyself on such a night in the sacred garden and the precinct of intimacy, then purify thy physical form from whatsoever external impurity thy knowledge encompasseth, then don what God thy Lord hath bestowed upon thee from His grace, then walk until thou reachest the first gate. There say “O Thou Who art the Lord of sovereignty and kingdom” four times, then at the second gate “O Thou Who art the Lord of might and dominion” four times, then at the third gate “O Thou Who art the Lord of power and divinity” four times, then at the fourth gate “O Thou Who art the Lord of strength and the ruby” four times, then at the fifth gate “O Thou Who art the Lord of majesty and the human realm” three times, then enter with God’s leave in a spirit of joy and rapture.
When thou standest before God or before any of the Primary Unity, when thou desirest to make mention of the most exalted numbers, say “God beareth witness that there is no God but Him. His are the most beautiful names in the heavens and the earth and what lieth between them. There is no God but Him, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting.”
Then return until thou reachest the back of the shrine. There, if thou art in a spirit of joy and delight while standing, say what God hath commanded thee, otherwise be seated, for God loveth this for thee. Then say “Verily all glory from God be upon thee, O Glory of God”, then “All majesty be upon thee, O Majesty of God”, then “All beauty be upon thee, O Beauty of God”, then “All grandeur be upon thee, O Grandeur of God”, then “All light be upon thee, O Light of God”, then “All mercy be upon thee, O Mercy of God”, then “All names be upon thee, O Names of God”, then “All might be upon thee, O Might of God”, then “All will be upon thee, O Will of God”, then “All knowledge be upon thee, O Knowledge of God”, then “All power be upon thee, O Power of God”, then “All good-pleasure be upon thee, O Good-Pleasure of God”, then “All honor be upon thee, O Honor of God”, then “All dominion be upon thee, O Dominion of God”, then “All sovereignty be upon thee, O Sovereignty of God”, then “All loftiness be upon thee, O Loftiness of God”, then “All verses be upon thee, O Verses of God”, then “All words be upon thee, O Words of God”.
Thou hast ascended unto God thy Lord through that whereby God thy Creator hath caused thee to ascend. Bear thou witness that thou art in the supreme horizon of paradise and the most glorious station in the gardens. God hath created for thee that which will gladden thy heart and spirit, then thy soul and body, and God shall resurrect thee from a soul on the Day of Resurrection when He willeth through the word of Him Whom God shall make manifest, exalted be His mention. Hold fast unto Him if thou attainest His presence, for there is naught beyond God and naught after God, and after truth there is naught but falsehood, and after paradise naught but the fire, and after affirmation naught but negation, and after light naught but darkness, and after good-pleasure naught but less than good-pleasure.
This is what God hath revealed unto thee and unto every male and female who has entered into the Bayan before or will enter until the Day of Resurrection is conferred, through His bounty, unto all temples of existence, through His grace, unto all circles. His is the creation and the command, before and after. All are guided by the First Unity, and all shall be guided on the Day of Resurrection by the First Unity through Him Whom God shall make manifest.

title: BB00254: Du’a’ li’n-Nuri’l-Abyad
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy!
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the mightiest of Thy Names—and all Thy Names are mighty in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Names.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most resplendent of Thy Glory—and all Thy Glory is resplendent in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Glory.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most majestic of Thy Majesty—and all Thy Majesty is majestic in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Majesty.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most enduring of Thy Eternity—and all Thy Eternity is enduring in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Eternity.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most guiding of Thy Guidance—and all Thy Guidance is guiding in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Guidance.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most glorious of Thy Oneness—and all Thy Oneness is exalted in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Oneness.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most steadfast of Thy Creative Power—and all Thy Creative Power is steadfast in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Creative Power.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most enduring of Thy Life—and all Thy Life is enduring in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Life.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the purest of Thy Purity—and all Thy Purity is pure in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Purity.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the nearest of Thy Certitude—and all Thy Certitude is near in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Certitude.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most majestic of Thy Being—and all Thy Being is majestic in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Being.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most subtle of Thy Grace—and all Thy Grace is subtle in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Grace.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most glorious of Thy Dominion—and all Thy Dominion is glorious in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Dominion.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most luminous of Thy Light—and all Thy Light is luminous in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Light.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most enduring of Thy Sovereignty—and all Thy Sovereignty is enduring in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Sovereignty.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most exalted of Thy Loftiness—and all Thy Loftiness is exalted in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Loftiness.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most unapproachable of Thy Singleness—and all Thy Singleness is unapproachable in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Singleness.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most holy of Thy Self-Sufficiency—and all Thy Self-Sufficiency is holy in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Self-Sufficiency.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most self-subsisting of Thy Self-Subsistence—and all Thy Self-Subsistence is self-subsisting in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Self-Subsistence.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most expansive of Thy Mercy—and all Thy Mercy is expansive in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Mercy.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most exalted of Thy Praise—and all Thy Praise is exalted in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Praise.
Glory be to Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy most swift forgiveness—and all Thy forgiveness is swift with Thee—then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy forgiveness.
Glory be to Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy steadfastness in its independence—and all Thy steadfastness is established with Thee—then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy steadfastness.
Glory be to Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy creative power in its might—and all Thy creative power is mighty with Thee—then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy creative power.
Glory be to Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy power to multiply in its glory—and all Thy multiplying power is glorious with Thee—then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy multiplying power.
Glory be to Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by the radiance of the garments of Thy countenance in its brilliance—and all Thy radiance is brilliant with Thee—then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy radiance.
Glory be to Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy manifestation in its most manifest form—and all Thy manifestation is manifest with Thee—then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy manifestation.
Glory be to Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy wealth in its most abundant form—and all Thy wealth is abundant with Thee—then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy wealth.
O my Beloved! I glorify Thee above all that contingent things have glorified through their essence, and above all that existing things have sanctified through their reality, and above all that created things have unified through their substance, and above all that names and attributes have magnified through their abstraction, and above all that atoms have exalted through what Thou hast bestowed upon them.
Therefore, O God, send Thy blessings upon the Divine Point and upon the Letters of the Living, and bestow through that Most Exalted Similitude and Most Resplendent Garment upon me and upon all who have believed in God and His signs, in every condition whatsoever befitteth the loftiness of Thy bounty and Thy gift, and the glory of the detachment of Thy generosity and Thy favor. For nothing is hidden from Thy knowledge, whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them. Thou givest unto all things their due measure through the sublimity of Thy grace and the transcendence of Thy bestowals. Nothing in the heavens or on earth or between them can frustrate Thee. Verily, Thou hast power over all things.
And send Thy blessings, O God, upon Gabriel, the worker of Thy white light, in every condition, before every condition, and after every condition. Verily, Thou art the All-Bountiful, the All-Powerful, the All-Encompassing.

title: BB00227: Du’a’ li’n-Nuri’l-Ahmar
text:
In Thy Book, through every prayer that Thou hast fashioned or that hath been uttered about Thee, for all grace belongeth unto Thee, resideth in Thee, emanateth from Thee, and returneth unto Thee, and there is no power nor strength except through Thee, and unto Thee is the final return. This is a prayer to the crimson light whose bearer was Israfil, peace be upon him:
In the Name of God, the Exalted, the Most Holy
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most magnificent of Thy Divinity, though all Thy Divinity is magnificent with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Divinity.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most impregnable of Thy Loftiness, though all Thy Loftiness is impregnable with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Loftiness.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most glorious of Thy Might, though all Thy Might is glorious with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Might.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most enduring of Thy Eternity, though all Thy Eternity is enduring with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Eternity.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most guiding of Thy Guidance, though all Thy Guidance is guiding with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Guidance.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most resplendent of Thy Oneness, though all Thy Oneness is resplendent with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Oneness.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most pure of Thy Purity, though all Thy Purity is pure with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Purity.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most lasting of Thy Life, though all Thy Life is lasting with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Life.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most sanctified of Thy Sanctity, though all Thy Sanctity is sanctified with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Sanctity.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most steadfast of Thy Certitude, though all Thy Certitude is steadfast with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Certitude.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most cooling of Thy Camphor, though all Thy Camphor is cooling with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Camphor.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most subtle of Thy Grace, though all Thy Grace is subtle with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Grace.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most excellent of Thy Dominion, though all Thy Dominion is excellent with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Dominion.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most luminous of Thy Light, though all Thy Light is luminous with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Light.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most sovereign of Thy Sovereignty, though all Thy Sovereignty is sovereign with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Sovereignty.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most transcendent of Thy Transcendence, though all Thy Transcendence is transcendent with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Transcendence.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most singular of Thy Singleness, though all Thy Singleness is singular with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Singleness.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most hallowed of Thy Self-Subsistence, though all Thy Self-Subsistence is hallowed with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Self-Subsistence.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most enduring of Thy Everlastingness, though all Thy Everlastingness is enduring with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Everlastingness.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most embracing of Thy Mercy, though all Thy Mercy is embracing with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Mercy.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the most exalted of Thy Gratitude, though all Thy Gratitude is exalted with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Gratitude.
O God! I beseech Thee by the swiftest of Thy repentances, and all Thy repentances are swift with Thee and then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy repentances.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most steadfast of Thy steadfastness, and all Thy steadfastness is steadfast with Thee and then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy steadfastness.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most encompassing of Thy treasuries, and all Thy treasuries are encompassing with Thee and then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy treasuries.
O God! I beseech Thee by the mightiest of Thy offspring, and all Thy offspring are mighty with Thee and then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy offspring.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most luminous of Thy light, and all Thy light is luminous with Thee and then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy light.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most manifest of Thy manifestation, and all Thy manifestation is manifest with Thee and then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy manifestation.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most enriching of Thy riches, and all Thy riches are abundance with Thee and then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy riches.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thyself—there is none beside Thee equal, comparable, similar, like or resembling Thee—and by that which Thou hast loved for Thyself or lovest through the sublimity of Thy inaccessibility and the exaltation of Thy transcendence. For all things, O my God, bow down before Thy Countenance and are humble before Thine eyes. Thou art unique in Thy unity above all contingent beings, singular in the sovereignty of Thy eternity above all existing things, supreme in the dominion of Thy self-subsistence above all created things, and exalted in the inaccessible heights of Thine everlasting nature above all that is still or in motion. Thou art independent in the independence of Thy sanctity above all who dwell in the kingdoms of earth and heaven, sovereign in the sovereignty of Thy glory above all who inhabit the realms of names and attributes. Thou hast taken possession, through the dominion of Thy beloved nature, of all that Thou hast loved in the depths of names and attributes, and art magnificent in the majesty of Thy glory as the Object of all desire, above all that can be mentioned through similitude or allusion.
Thou art the Exalted One before Whose exaltation all bow down in humility, and the Attributed One before Whose transcendence all stand in reverence. All glorify Thee, proclaim Thy unity, magnify Thee and extol Thee according to their capacity. But perchance there may be directed toward Thee that which Thou hast foreordained of pure, crystalline, essential and abstract realities, and that by which Thou art remembered in the kingdom of names and attributes. There is no hour which Thou hast not made great, majestic, beautiful, mighty and illumined with the light that quivers from the Dayspring of morning and shines forth from the holy Star.
We shall assuredly cause to descend, O God, Thy light upon the Tree of Oneness and that which Thy knowledge hath encompassed therein, as befits the sublimity of Thy generosity, the exaltation of Thy grace, the elevation of Thy bounty, the inaccessibility of Thy tenderness and the independence of Thy loving-kindness; and upon all save the Tree of Thy love that which it deserves before Thy justice, the sovereignty of Thy omnipotence, Thy power, the dominion of Thy might, Thy glory and the court of Thy supreme grandeur. For Thy mercy transcends all mercy, Thy severity all severity, Thy might all might, Thy sovereignty all sovereignty, Thy grandeur all grandeur, and Thy power all power. Grant us, O God, that which we deserve, and pardon us, O God, through Thy grace and bounty for that which we deserve not before the independence of the sovereignty of Thy oneness and the majesty of the dominion of Thy eternity. Verily, Thou art the Self-Sufficient, the Most Exalted, the All-Forgiving, the Inaccessible, possessed of might and majesty.
Bless, O God, the bearer of Thy crimson light, Israfil, peace be upon him, morning and evening.

title: BB00181: Du’a’ li’n-Nuri’l-Akhdar
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
O God! I beseech Thee by the most enduring of Thine eternity, and all Thy eternity endureth with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thine eternity.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most resplendent of Thy glory, and all Thy glory is resplendent with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy glory.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most beautiful of Thy beauty, and all Thy beauty is beautiful with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy beauty.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most perpetual of Thy perpetuity, and all Thy perpetuity is perpetual with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy perpetuity.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most guiding of Thy guidance, and all Thy guidance is guiding with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy guidance.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most sovereign of Thy sovereignty, and all Thy sovereignty is sovereign with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy sovereignty.
O God! I beseech Thee by the purest of Thy purity, and all Thy purity is pure with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy purity.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy life, and all Thy life is eternal with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy life.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most sanctified of Thy sanctity, and all Thy sanctity is sanctified with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy sanctity.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most certain of Thy certitude, and all Thy certitude is certain with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy certitude.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most supreme of Thy supremacy, and all Thy supremacy is supreme with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy supremacy.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most gracious of Thy grace, and all Thy grace is gracious with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy grace.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most glorious of Thy dominion, and all Thy dominion is glorious with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy dominion.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most luminous of Thy light, and all Thy light is luminous with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy light.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most powerful of Thy power, and all Thy power is powerful with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy power.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most magnificent of Thy grandeur, and all Thy grandeur is magnificent with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy grandeur.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most singular of Thy oneness, and all Thy oneness is singular with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy oneness.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most impregnable of Thy self-subsistence, and all Thy self-subsistence is impregnable with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy self-subsistence.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most potent of Thy might, and all Thy might is potent with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy might.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most embracing of Thy mercy, and all Thy mercy is embracing with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy mercy.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most thankful of Thy thankfulness, and all Thy thankfulness is thankful with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy thankfulness.
O God! I beseech Thee by the swiftest of Thy forgiveness, and all Thy forgiveness is swift with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy forgiveness.
O God! I beseech Thee by the most steadfast of Thy steadfastness, and all Thy steadfastness is steadfast with Thee, then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy steadfastness.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Creative Power, the most manifest thereof, for all Thy creative power is manifest before Thee, and is set down in the Mother Book. O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Creative Power in its entirety.
O my God! I beseech Thee by the totality of Thy creative power. O my God! I beseech Thee by the most supreme manifestation of Thy originating power, for all Thy originating power abideth with Thee in the Mother Book. O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy originating power.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy most resplendent light, for all Thy light is radiant with Thee in the Mother Book. O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy light.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy most manifest revelation, for all Thy revelation is manifest with Thee in the Mother Book. O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy revelation.
O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy most abundant riches, for all Thy riches are abundant with Thee in the Mother Book. O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy riches.
O my God! I beseech Thee by that which Thou hast loved of all things, for all Thy love is beloved with Thee in the Mother Book. O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy love.
O my God! I beseech Thee by that which Thou lovest of all things, for all that Thou lovest is beloved with Thee in the Mother Book. O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy belovedness.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I and all things bear witness on this Night which Thou hast made magnificent, majestic, beauteous, mighty and holy, that there is no God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thine is the Kingdom and the Dominion, Thine the Glory and the Power, Thine the Might and the Divinity, Thine the Strength and Sovereignty, Thine the Rule and Creation. Thou givest life and causeth death, then causeth death and givest life. Verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not, the Sovereign Who passeth not away, the Just Who oppresseth not, the Potentate Who changeth not, the Single One from Whose grasp nothing escapeth, whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
I and all things bear witness, O my Beloved, that Thou hast ever been and wilt ever be before all things and after all things, existent after all things and fashioning above all things and being below all things. Thou hast ever been one God, Single, Unique, Eternal, Ever-Living, Self-Subsisting, Sovereign, Just, All-Glorious, Ever-Standing, All-Subduing, Holy, Everlasting, Self-Dependent. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, nor hath there been any partner with Thee in sovereignty. All are Thy servants and in Thy grasp, all glorify Thee with praise and all before the authority of Thy Will are prostrate, all testify to Thy oneness through Thy remembrance and all before the dominion of Thy Purpose are humble.
Thy Will hath ever been supreme above all contingent things, Thy Purpose manifest above all created things, Thy destiny dominant over all beings, Thy decree ruling over all in the kingdoms of earth and heaven, Thy leave exalted above all in the kingdom of names and attributes, Thy majesty unattainable above all atoms, and Thy Book elevated above all similitudes and allusions.
This is the Night, O my God, wherein Thou hast ordained the destinies of all things and will ordain from all things. Therefore, O my God, ordain in this Night, by Thy power which extendeth over all things and Thy knowledge which penetrateth the essence of all things, that which will exalt the Tree of Thy Unity and all beneath its shade, and will destroy all save the Tree of Thy Love and what lieth beneath its shadow, or will transform the fire into light in all things for which Thou hast ordained this. For this is the Night wherein Thy mercy hath encompassed all things and Thy bounty hath surrounded all things. Therefore, O my God, ordain for us through Thy grace and generosity, and what is best for us in Thy knowledge, that which befitteth the sublimity of Thy matchless gifts and the exaltation of Thy bounty and glory, for verily Thou art powerful over what Thou willest and mighty over […] Thou knowest what is best for us in our ultimate destiny and abode.
Therefore, O my God, ordain what befitteth Thy bounty, not what our souls deserve before Thy generosity. Verily, Thou art the Lord of righteousness and forgiveness, the Lord of grace and mercy, the Lord of bounty and bestowal, the Lord of honor and loving-kindness, the Lord of might and sovereignty. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command; verily, Thou hast power over all things. Thou ordainest from Thy presence as Thou pleasest by Thy command; verily, Thou hast encompassed all things with Thy knowledge. Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. Thou hast ever been independent of all things and self-subsisting.
O God! Send Thy blessings upon the bearer of Thy green light who standeth at the third pillar of Thy throne, through whom Thou takest the souls of Thy creation by Thy leave, that he may give them to drink from the wine of Thy oneness—he whom Thou hast named Azrael in Thy Book—with all the prayers Thou hast created or wilt create, for all bounty is Thine, from Thee, and through Thee, and sovereignty belongeth unto Thee. There is no power nor strength except through Thee, and unto Thee do all things return.

title: BB00212: Du’a’ li’n-Nuri’l-Asfar
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy!
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most magnificent of Thy Divinity, though all Thy Divinity is magnificent in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Divinity.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most inaccessible of Thy Transcendence, for all Thy Transcendence is inaccessible in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Transcendence.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most beautiful of Thy Beauty, for all Thy Beauty is beautiful in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Beauty.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most enduring of Thy Eternity, for all Thy Eternity is enduring in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Eternity.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most guiding of Thy Guidance, for all Thy Guidance is guiding in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Guidance.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most majestic of Thy Oneness, for all Thy Oneness is majestic in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Oneness.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the purest of Thy Purity, for all Thy Purity is pure in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Purity.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most passionate of Thy Love, for all Thy Love is passionate in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Love.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most sanctified of Thy Holiness, for all Thy Holiness is holy in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Holiness.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most just of Thy Certitude, for all Thy Certitude is just in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Certitude.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most luminous of Thy Radiance, for all Thy Radiance is luminous in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Radiance.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most gentle of Thy Grace, for all Thy Grace is gentle in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Grace.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most ancient of Thy Favors, for all Thy Favors are ancient in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Favors.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the nearest of Thy Help, for all Thy Help is near in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Help.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most hallowed of Thy Glorification, for all Thy Glorification is hallowed in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Glorification.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the mightiest of Thy Glory, for all Thy Glory is mighty in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Glory.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the nearest of Thy Creation, for all Thy Creation is near in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Creation.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most impregnable of Thy Self-Sufficiency, for all Thy Self-Sufficiency is impregnable in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Self-Sufficiency.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most powerful of Thy Power, for all Thy Power is powerful in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Power.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by the most extensive of Thy Mercy, for all Thy Mercy is extensive in Thy sight and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Mercy.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Thanksgiving, the most exalted thereof, for all Thy thanksgiving is exalted in Thy presence, and is recorded in the Mother Book. O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy Thanksgiving in its entirety.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by that which is most swift of all Thy forgiveness, for all Thy forgiveness is swift with Thee and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy forgiveness.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by that which is most praiseworthy of all Thy praise, for all Thy praise is exalted with Thee and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy praise.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by that which is most enduring of all Thy treasuries, for all Thy treasuries are enduring with Thee and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy treasuries.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by that which is most noble of all Thy creation, for all Thy creation is noble with Thee and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy creation.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by that which is most luminous of all Thy light, for all Thy light is luminous with Thee and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy light.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by that which is most manifest of all Thy manifestation, for all Thy manifestation is manifest with Thee and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy manifestation.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by that which is most forgiving of all Thy forgiveness, for all Thy forgiveness is forgiving with Thee and in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy forgiveness.
…I will glorify Thee above all that contingent beings have glorified by their own selves; and above all that created things have praised by their inmost reality; and above all that beings have affirmed Thy unity by their souls; and above all that names and attributes have magnified by their “I-ness”; and above all that atoms have exalted by their pristine simplicity; and above all that existences have sanctified by their camphor-sweetness; and above all that all things—whatsoever is within them and upon them—have honoured and made mighty.
Therefore do I beseech Thee, O my God, my Lord, my Beloved, my Possessor, and my Sovereign, that Thou mayest send blessings upon the Point of Divinity and the Letters of His Living, with every blessing Thou hast created or wilt create; and that Thou mayest bestow favour upon all who seek shelter beneath the shade of that Tree—befitting the sublimity of Thy exaltation and the loftiness of Thine unapproachableness. For from everlasting all atoms stand at the gate of Thy bounty, and all contingent beings prostrate themselves at the door of Thy generosity.
Sanctified is the essence of Thy being, by a camphor-sweetness, above that any of the contingent should know it; and exalted is Thy simple, uncompounded Self above that any contingent soul should comprehend it; and mighty is Thy essential soul above that any among created things should attain unto it; and sovereign is Thy immaterial dominion above that any who are in the kingdoms of earth and heaven should magnify it. Though all were to glorify Thee, and praise Thee, and proclaim Thine oneness, and magnify Thee according to the loftiness of the sovereignty of the might of Thy singleness and the unassailability of the holiness of Thy Self-Sufficiency, yet whatsoever appeareth from Thy creatures is as nothing before the majesty of the holiness of Thy unity and the gladness of the splendour of the countenance of the Sovereign of Thine essence.
Grant, then, O my God, unto me from Thy presence that which beseemeth the loftiness of Thy bounty and the sublimity of Thy favour. Verily Thou art the Protector, the Most Exalted. Nothing escapeth Thy knowledge, neither in the heavens nor on the earth nor whatsoever lieth between them; verily Thou art the All-Knowing, the Possessor of might and glory. Nor is aught beyond Thy power, neither in the realm of command nor of creation nor in whatsoever is beneath them; verily Thou art the Sovereign, the Almighty, the Possessor of sovereignty and power.
Glorified art Thou, O my Lord! Forgive me, and bestow upon me a mighty sovereignty such as Thou hast not bestowed upon any before, nor wilt ordain for any after—verily Thou art the Ever-Bestowing, the Inaccessible, the All-Powerful.

title: BB00417: Du’a’ li’sh-Shajarati’l-Ula va man i’sta’zalla fi zillih
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
O God, my Lord! Send Thy blessings upon the Tree of Thy Oneness, and cause to descend upon it, O my Lord, that which befitteth the loftiness of Thy bounty and the sovereignty of Thy mighty Self-Subsistence.
Do Thou, O my Lord, exalt me and it, and grant victory unto me and it, and inspire me and it, and clothe me and it with majesty, and adorn me and it with beauty, and magnify me and it, and illumine me and it, and have mercy upon me and it, and glorify me and it, and teach me and it, and enrich me and it, and content me and it, and preserve me and it, and manifest me and it, and grant dominion unto me and it, and answer me and it, by virtue of Thy most excellent Names and Thy most exalted Attributes, and through that which beseemeth the sublimity of Thy holy majesty in the most exalted heights and in the most lowly depths.
For Thou hast ever been, and wilt ever be, nigh in Thy nearness and transcendent in Thy loftiness. No thing can praise Thee as befitteth the reality of Thy Being, nor can any thing extol Thee as beseemeth the truth of Thy Self, nor can any thing unify Thee as befitteth the reality of Thy Nature, nor can any thing magnify Thee as beseemeth the truth of Thy Identity, nor can any thing glorify Thee as befitteth the sovereignty of Thy Lordship. Thou hast ever been independent of all else besides Thee and self-sufficient above all else except Thee. All worship Thee according to their capacity, and all prostrate themselves before Thee according to the limit of their power.
Send down then, O God, all Thy majesty and Thy beauty, Thy perfection and Thy greatness, Thy light and Thy mercy, Thy words and Thy names, Thy might and Thy will, Thy knowledge and Thy power, Thy speech and Thy dominion, Thy sovereignty and Thy bounty and Thy signs, and whatsoever Thy knowledge encompasseth of every good, upon the Reality of the Seven Letters, then upon the Letters of the Living, and upon all who seek shelter beneath the shade of that Treea€“until the Day when they shall discover it renewed through the effulgence of Thy light; and do Thou exalt it through the appearance of Thy wondrous novelty.
Send, then, Thy blessings, O God, upon the hearts of those who have ascended unto Thee, and upon their spirits, their souls, and their bodies, with all Thy bounty and Thy mercy, and all Thy grace and Thy munificence; for verily Thou art the King, the All-Bountiful, the Most Exalted, the Inaccessible. There is no power nor strength save in God, the Exalted, the Most Great.

title: BB00190: Du’a’ li-avvali man amana bi’llah va man qad sa’ida bihi ila’llah
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Inaccessible, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I bear Thee witness—yea, and all things bear Thee witness—that Thou art God: there is none other God but Thee, the One, the Single, the Self-Subsisting, the Peerless, the Living, the Ever-Abiding, the All-Relied-Upon; Thou begettest not, nor wast Thou begotten; for Thee there is no equal, no likeness, no peer, no mate, no exemplar. Thou hast been alone, by the loftiness of Thine eternal being, exalted above all things; by the sublimity of Thine Essence uplifted above the sublimity of all things; by the simple purity of Thy reality raised above all things; by the snow-white holiness of Thy abstraction sanctified above the height of all things; and by the sovereignty of Thy self-subsistence exalted above all things.
Thou art He beside Whom there hath been naught; Thou art the Maker at Whose degree there standeth naught. Thou art the Most High, Who by Thy Will hast called all things into being; the Most Exalted, Who by Thy Purpose hast brought forth all things; the Inaccessible, Who by Thy Decree hast originated all things. Hath any power apart from Thee, O my God? Hath any independence save through Thee? Is there for aught beside Thee a sign or proof of self-subsistence? Nay, by Thy might! All are upheld by Thee and by Thy power; and whatever is ascribed unto Thee they know only by themselves upon the earth. But should the relation unto Thee be severed from their souls, they possess nothing; and though they be not true in their claim to Thee, never dost Thou, O my God, confirm their claim unto Thyself.
Glorified art Thou above desiring that there be ascribed unto Thee one who worshippeth Thee not, boweth not down before Thee, confesseth not Thy oneness, submitteth not to the dominion of Thy unity, or humbleth not himself before the kingship of Thy sanctified oneness. Exalted art Thou above accepting the name of Islam—or those numbered therein—as related unto Thee after their hands have wrought what they have wrought; though by that attribution they bear the burden of their own deeds. Thou wilt assuredly set Thy seal upon their hands, take hold of them, and cause them to behold themselves and their works as are those who worship Thee not and claim no relation unto Thee.
Swift to seize and quick to requite is only he who feareth lest aught escape his dominion; and harsh in chastisement and destruction is only he who dreadeth loss within his kingdom. But, by Thy might! All are within Thy grasp; who hath power to flee Thy ruling sovereignty, which is lifted up above every atom? Who can turn aside from the ordinances of the King of Thy self-subsistence, which are unassailable above all possibilities?
Thou art the Most Lofty—no decline toucheth Thy glory and Thy height. Thou art the Most Exalted—no independence is save through Thy grandeur and Thy sublimity. Thou hast prevailed over all things until the might of every potentate is Thine; Thou hast towered above all things until the necks of every king are humbled by Thy power. Thou art the Subduer—before Thy Will all prostrate; Thou art the Manifest—beneath Thy Purpose all are humbled.
Hallowed be Thou, O my God! I have borne witness to what never was witnessed in the realm of origination before this, and I have numbered what no counting had encompassed in the world of invention. Can a heart that hath lived but a year… hearken, in the path of Thy guardianship, to the grief of a people?—how, then, to slay one whose testimony hath been that none in the heavens or on the earth or between them possess aught, while they—types and peers—stand cut off unto Thee, exalted in Thy presence, guarded with Thee, and rejoicing before Thee?
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Thou judgest over all things; Thou hast manifested Thy sovereignty above all things; Thou hast caused the measures of Thy decrees to run through all things; and the modes of Thy power are lifted above all things. Do Thou, then, judge, O my God, as Thou didst judge between fire and light; and make swift, O my God, what Thou didst ordain between negation and affirmation.
For I, O my God, beheld with mine eyes one who, ere this, drew nigh unto Thy Beloved; though in his lifetime he rendered not, in the path of that love, what befitteth the loftiness of His majesty and the sublimity of His exaltation. Yet, after he ascended, Thou didst raise his seat and didst expend, from what Thou hadst entrusted to His friends, in the path of His love, until—by Thy wealth—he was made independent of all … So high didst Thou exalt him that none may lay claim over him—not even a sovereign—though they possess what they possess; for over them, too, is Thy decree…
What is related unto Thee endureth—even unto the Day of Resurrection—by the mention of his exaltation and by what of Thy dominion Thou didst bestow upon him. O Thou whose relation is lofty and uplifted; whose will is over-ruling and unassailable! Exalt, O God, the seat of the first who bowed down before Thee at the Point—Thy servant made pure for Thy sake alone, who sought none but Thee, severed himself from all save Thee, and was veiled by naught of the manifestations of Thy kingdom—until he mounted above the ascent of the former generations and towered above the eminence of the latter times.
Send down then, O my God, upon the Tree of Oneness—and upon all who take shelter in its shade among former and latter, outward and inward—what beseemeth the height of Thy transcendence and the majesty of Thy power, until the hour Thou shalt restore me. And if aught be cut off from that Tree, then cut it off, at what Thou hast decreed of good, for Thou art swift to seize and strong to succour. Thy ordinances are exalted from resurrection to resurrection; Thy decrees are inaccessible from hour to hour. Thou alone encompassest the Hour—none knoweth it save Thee—and Thou art powerful to bring forth the Resurrection, whereunto none attaineth but Thee.
Cause Thou, then, to descend, in that moment, upon the first of the Letters of the Bayan—the proofs of Thy Name “In the Name of God, the Most Inaccessible, the Most Holy”—unto the last of the Letters of the Exalted Ones in Thy Book, what befitteth the loftiness of Thy majesty and the sublimity of Thy might. And send Thou down upon the nineteen gates of the fire—opened beneath the shade of the Letters of the First, “In the Name of God, the Most Inaccessible, the Most Holy”—and upon every letter that Thou didst reveal short of the Letters of the Exalted Ones, as Thou numberest, what beseemeth the height of Thy seizing, Thy might, Thy vengeance and Thy bounty. For Thy mercy hath been perfected and fulfilled towards the people of the Exalted Ones; and Thy vengeance hath appeared and been intensified upon the people of the fire.
For Thou, O my God, art the Creator of fire and light: Thou createdst not the fire for itself, save on account of its arrogance toward the dawning-places of Thy light—otherwise Thou hadst neither created it, nor sent down a single letter regarding it in the Bayan. Then, in that hour, shall I behold that whatsoever hath been decreed aforetime of the mention of the people of the fire is but for the exaltation, before Thee, of the mention of the people of light—even wert this but the remembrance vouchsafed them in the Book.
Exalted, then, O my God, is Thy proof over all possibilities! Magnified is Thy favour upon all created things! The people of the fire shall take possession of a scant portion of what Thou hast not made lawful for them, and Thou shalt seize them by their own hands whence they know not; while those in Paradise, by their attribution unto Thee, shall possess what Thou hast made lawful for them, without exhaustion and without end; and Thou shalt recompense them by their own hands, though they comprehend it not—for all things return unto man.
And that frame (of man) is never void of a twofold mention: either he is mentioned in negation—or …—or in affirmation. If he be mentioned in the former, he hath, in Thy sight, naught; he is mentioned only that Thou mayest therewith make mention of those in Thy Paradise. He is one of those whose name Thou lovest not to be named in the Book among the modes of the fire and its people. But if he be of the Letters of Affirmation, then is he of the angels of Ridvan; unto him belongeth every good by Thy bounty—and he is of the angels of the All-Merciful.
I therefore beseech Thee … to guard me from every fire and its people, and to provide for me of every Paradise and what Thou hast created therein; and to send down upon every heart that hath ascended unto Thee, upon every spirit that hath mounted up, upon every soul enraptured, and upon every body severed for Thy sake, what beseemeth the height of Thy glorification, the sublimity of Thy praise, the exaltation of Thy unity, and the inviolability of Thy magnification. None can compass this save Thee; verily, Thou hast ever been powerful over all things. There is no power nor strength save in Thee; and Thou art, in truth, the Lord of bounteous grace.

title: BB00024: Du’a’ li-Huruf-i-Bismi’llahi’r-Rahmani’r-Rahim
text:
Part 1: “Glorified art Thou, O my God! Thou art…”
In the name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Thou art the Creator of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, their Ordainer, their Fashioner, their Originator, and their Author. Thou hast ever been the One God, Single, Self-Subsistent, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Thou hast taken unto Thyself neither consort nor son, and Thou hast created all things through Thy power and established the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them through Thy might. Nothing escapeth the dominion of Thy oneness, nor is anything concealed from the sovereignty of Thy Self-Subsistence, nor doth anything in the kingdoms of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them elude Thy power.
Thou hast transcended all things through the essential nature of Thy Being, and hast exalted Thyself through the pure essence of Thy Reality above the height of all things. Thou hast risen through the abstraction of Thy Self above the loftiness of all things, and hast established Thyself through the essence of Thy Identity above the inaccessibility of all things. Thou art the Most High, and all besides Thee bow down before Thee in worship and glorification and praise and sanctification. Thou art the Most Exalted, and all beneath Thy gaze extol Thy majesty and greatness and might and oneness.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! There is no moment when any can be associated with the sovereignty of Thy holiness and the dominion of Thy singleness. How could I ever aspire to ascend unto the heaven of Thy sanctified glory or rise unto the clouds of Thy exalted names? Ever hath Thy Reality praised Thy Reality, and all else doth praise Thee within the bounds of Thy sovereign might. Forever dost Thou magnify Thy Self through Thy Self, and should any besides Thee magnify Thee, it is but within the confines of the geometry Thou hast established through the limitations of Thy creation and brought into being through the manifestations of Thy might.
O my God, by such likeness are all likenesses and similitudes made known; and by such balance, O my Lord, are all geometries and names weighed. Thou art the Most Exalted, and unto the height of Thy loftiness do all ascend and before Thee bow the knee. Thou art the All-Transcending, and unto the summit of Thy exaltation do all lift their gaze and, standing in Thy presence, glorify Thy Name.
What, then, is the splendor of Thy beauty, above every beauty in the realm of origination! How august Thy majesty, surpassing every majesty within the domain of invention! How ravishing the comeliness of Thy countenance, and how sublime the glances of the eyes turned toward Thy Face among the kings of earth and heaven! How immeasurable the elevation of the sanctity of Thy self-subsisting oneness amid the billows of names and attributes! How radiant the effulgences of Thy unity, with Thy peerlessness, upon the surging seas of glory and detachment!
From everlasting hast Thou stood, single and alone, upon the throne of Thine essential might—far above all that Thou hast, by Thy power, brought forth. And forever wilt Thou remain, invincible and exalted, beyond all over whom Thou hast, by Thy sovereignty, conferred dominion. Every thing deriveth a sign of Thy glory; yet none among Thy creatures can hymn Thy praise as becometh the sublimity of Thy praise—though all things yearn to celebrate Thee according to the loftiness of Thy glorification. None can worthily laud Thee, for the eminence of Thy thanksgiving is unapproachable—albeit all things long to extol Thee, whilst Thy praise remaineth beyond their reach. None can truly unify Thee, for the dominion of Thy peerless oneness is self-sufficient—though all things yearn to acknowledge Thee, even as Thou hast affirmed Thine Essence by the altitude of Thine eternity.
None among Thy servants can magnify Thee as is meet, for the ascendant might of Thy majestic grandeur is insurmountable, yet all that dwell from the highest height unto the primal atom fain would exalt Thee according to the excellence of Thy majesty, the sublimity of Thy singleness, the loftiness of Thy self-subsistence, and the holiness of Thy radiant sanctity.
Thou art the Being who by Thy Will hast given being to all things; the Essence who by Thy purpose hast brought all things into being; the Light who by Thy power hast decreed all things; the All-Knowing who by Thy lordly knowledge hast numbered all things; the Fashioner who by the wondrous artistry of Thy gracious lordship hast formed all things. How resplendent is Thy glory, O my God, in the depths of might and detachment, and how sublime is Thy majesty, O my Beloved, in the kingdom of might and inaccessibility. How beauteous is the beauty of Thy holy Countenance in its bounty within the holy realms of might and majesty, and how delicate are the wondrous manifestations of the favors of Thy grandeur in the ultimate essences of might and joy.
I have ever glorified Thee through the essence of my being, certain that this befitteth not the majesty of Thy holy praise, and bearing witness that this befitteth not the loftiness of Thy holy sanctification. And in like manner do I praise Thee, O my Beloved, and proclaim Thy unity, O my Desire, and magnify Thee, O Thou to Whom I shall return and in Whom I find my resting-place. Thou hast ever clothed me in every vesture of Thy might, wherein Thou didst cause whomsoever Thou wouldst to hearken a hundredfold times; and all this within the Kingdom of the might of the sanctity of Thy loving care. And Thou ceaselessly settest in motion the ordinances of Thy subsistence, as Thou dost will. I know of naught that grieveth my knowledge before the Sovereign of Thy holy oneness. There ceaselessly rain down from the heaven of the bounty of Thy Lordship the rains of Thy wondrous mercy, and there unceasingly descend from the heaven of Thy holy love the outpourings of the wondrous effects of the manifestation of Thy power.
Can any whom Thou art his God be grieved by aught? Glory be unto Thee! Glory be unto Thee! Can any whom Thou art his Lord […] from his knowledge of aught? Glory be unto Thee! Glory be unto Thee! Can any whom Thou art his Creator be rendered powerless by aught? Glory be unto Thee! Glory be unto Thee! Can any whom Thou art his Possessor have his dominion diminished by aught? Glory be unto Thee! Glory be unto Thee! Can any whom Thou art his Sovereign be associated with aught? Glory be unto Thee! Glory be unto Thee!
Through my recognition of Thy oneness shall I glory over all who dwell in the kingdom of Thy earth and the heaven of Thy Lordship, and through my acknowledgment of Thy oneness shall I rise above all the inhabitants of Thy realm. Is there any glory, O my God, save in submission to Thy oneness, and is there any exaltation, O my God, save in prostration before the Sovereign of Thy might? Nay, by Thy might! Through my humility before Thee shall I be raised above all who are exalted, and through my submissiveness before Thy eyes shall I ascend above all who are high.
Thine is the decree in its essence, and the praise in its purity, and the beginning in its pristine nature. Thou dost ever […] the people of Thy love with the holy fragrances of Thy attraction, and Thou causest to ascend whom Thou willest through what Thou bestowest upon them of the wondrous manifestations of Thy power to the horizon of the atmosphere of Thy love. Thou art He through connection with Whom none can be brought low, and through separation from Whose exalted sovereignty none can find independence.
Therefore unto Thee, O my God, […] all from the highest heights of the essence of my being to the lowest depths of the clay of my reality, for I witness as absolute truth and observe as the very essence of certainty that the clay which Thou hast attributed to Thyself in Thy Book causeth the necks of all who are mighty to bow down before it and the mightiest of the mighty to circle round it. The body which beforetime bore witness to all Thy tribulations—how do all the great ones among the mighty prostrate themselves before it and all the exalted ones among the wealthy humble themselves before it! If this be the effect of clay’s connection to Thee and the fruit of the body that was martyred in Thy path […] how much more so for him whom Thou hast chosen for the loftiness of Thy sanctification and […] for the exaltation of Thy glorification, whom Thou hast singled out for the elevation of Thy unity and preferred above all things for the inaccessibility of Thy magnification.
Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee, without my looking to aught else or […] […] in aught save Thy unity. Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee, without my heart finding rest in aught else or my being finding stability in any but Thee. Glory be unto Thee, O God, through Thy remembrance of me.
I shall verily glory over all who are in the Kingdom of Names and Attributes, and through My remembrance of Thee shall I triumph over all who are in the kingdoms of earth and heaven. And in that time, O my God, shall I soar in the atmosphere of Thy divine Unity, and wing my flight in the heights of Thy sovereignty, and praise Thee for what Thou art in the horizon of Thy dominion and kingdom. For he who seeketh Thee in the heights of Thy names, or desireth to tread the paths of Thy glory and transcendence, would not wish to descend from the heaven of Thy names to […] Thy creation or to be like Thy servants, for there all names are cut off and all likenesses are forbidden.
And I love Thy manifestation at the Point which Thou hast established in the Bayan through Thy creative power. Through Thee shall I behold Thee, and testify before Thee to that which Thou hast caused me to witness concerning Thyself, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone, without partner. Thine is the creation and the command, and Thine are might and transcendence, and Thine are power and exaltation, and Thine are joy and gladness, and Thine are grandeur and majesty, and Thine are sovereignty and splendor, and Thine are might and radiance, and Thine are the names and whatsoever Thou hast loved in Thy knowledge of the unseen realms of divine good-pleasure and the manifold wonders of Thy decree.
And I love to acknowledge the right of […] before Thee in the depths of Thy names, and to behold above the heads of all the manifestations of Thy likenesses, inasmuch as He hath preceded all Thy names through what Thou hast cast upon Him of Thy majesty and the sublimity of Thy transcendence.
And I shall say: O Thou Who art the Most Exalted above all that is exalted, O Thou Who art the Most Glorious above all possessed of glory, O Thou Who art the Most Holy above all possessed of transcendence, O Thou Who art the Most Elevated above all possessed of elevation, O Thou Who art the Most Great above all possessed of greatness! Is there any manifestation other than Thee, O my God, whereby I might be guided to Thee? Is there any remembrance besides Thee, O my Beloved, whereby I might remember Thee? Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. Thou art the First before all things, and the Last after all things, and the Outward above all things, and the Inward beneath all things, and the Omnipotent over all things.
Exalted is Thy Being above description through similitudes of glory and majesty, and sanctified is Thy Essence from praise through manifestations of glory and beauty. Thou hast ever been one God, Single, Eternal, Independent, Ever-Living, Self-Subsisting. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, nor hath Thy Being been joined with aught that Thou hast created or determined or fashioned or limited or numbered. The wonders of the signs of Thy power have ever shone forth upon the people of Thy dominion, and the evidences of Thy divine Unity have ever been raised up among those who dwell in the kingdom of Thy earth and heaven.
How shall I beseech Thee, O my God, by the Name which Thou hast made to precede all Thy names, and through which Thou hast brought into being what was and what will be until the end of Thy creation’s term, and through which Thou hast manifested those who dwell in the kingdom of Thy creation and Thy command! Verily Thou art He Who hath ever been and will ever be […] to Him through it from before when there was no beginning to when Thou didst manifest, and no limit to when Thou shalt manifest. Thine is the might and power, O Thou Who art possessed of strength and might! And Thine are grandeur and exaltation, O Thou Who art possessed of sovereignty and transcendence! And Thine are awe and detachment, O Thou Who art possessed of joy and gladness! And Thine are majesty and glory, O Thou Who art possessed of countenance and magnificence! And Thine are creation and command in the kingdom of origination, O Thou Who art possessed of ascents and attributes! And Thine are dominion and kingdom, O Thou Who art possessed of bounties!
O Ever-Bountiful One! The Sovereign of Thy hallowed munificence hath ever showered the rain of Thy lordly majesty from the heaven of Thy holy oneness upon those who dwell in the kingdom of Thy earth and the heaven of Thy loving-kindness. And forever shall the dawning-places of the command of the kingdom of the wondrous innovation of Thy lordship manifest that which Thou hast ordained in the kingdom of the might of Thy dominion through the marvelous handiwork of Thy transcendent unity. How exalted is Thy sublimity in the depths of names and similitudes, and how resplendent is Thy loftiness in the kingdom of might and majesty! Were the ocean to become ink for that which Thou art worthy of praise and glorification, it would be exhausted ere a single letter of the laudations of Thy supreme might or the glorification of Thy most great sanctity could be revealed.

title: BB00024: Du’a’ li-Huruf-i-Bismi’llahi’r-Rahmani’r-Rahim
section: Part 2: “And likewise, O my God, were I…”
text:
Part 2: “And likewise, O my God, were I…”
And likewise, O my God, were I to desire to mention before Thee the letter M, or to raise it towards Thee, or to cause it to ascend unto Thy presence—for Thy knowledge hath ever penetrated all things, Thy power hath encompassed all things, Thy might hath prevailed over all things, and there existeth nothing in earth nor in heaven nor in what lieth between them save through Thy Will which Thou hast made to triumph over all things, and Thy Purpose which Thou hast caused to appear above all things, and Thy Power which Thou hast made to tower above all things, and Thy Decree which Thou hast made to transcend all things, and Thy Permission which Thou hast elevated above all things, and that which Thou hast exalted above all that Thou hast exalted, and that which Thou hast inscribed for the One Who is raised above all that is in earth and heaven and what lieth between them.
For these are the manifestations of Thy Cause ere the dawning-places of Thy names appear or the daysprings of Thy creation emerge from the horizon of the Unseen. For the first of Thy names in eternity consisteth of seven hidden letters, and the last symbol in the number of Him Who is Implored for Help is Thy Most Great Name inscribed, and between them are those for which there is no equal in the Book and which none can reckon save Thee, O Lord of Lords, Sovereign of Destiny, King of Fulfillment, Monarch of Glory, Master of Light, and Possessor of all things.
For verily, O my God, through this Thou hast created the essential gems, the adorned ornaments, and the hidden treasures which Thou hast created by Thy command, and through these beloved temples, praised dawning-places, and described rising-points, that they who dwell in the kingdom of Thy earth and heaven might glorify Thee. For this is the element of the water of the divine cloud wherein two latter letters are heard from the first letter, and what Thou lovest from the Primal Point is the mention of Thy Self, Thy Self:

“Verily I am God, there is no God but Me, the Lord of the Hereafter and the Former times.”

Yea, I bear witness unto that which Thou hast caused me to witness and made me to hear, that this is the fire through which Thou hast created all lights, and the ornament with which Thou hast adorned all ornaments, and the gems through which Thou hast magnified all the gems of names.
I beseech Thee therefore, O my God, to grant that I may attain unto that Fire on the Day of Resurrection at the first moment of its appearance and elevation, that I may hear from Thee that which Thou didst cause me to hear at that time in Thy Book, that Thou mayest transform the fire into light for me inasmuch as I will prostrate myself before Thee at the Gate on that Day at the manifestation of Thy Will and the dawning of Thy Purpose. For whoso entereth that Fire—the kindled Fire of God which flameth in the hearts—then if […] from him what is his and upon him, otherwise what he hath acquired will profit him not even if he should ascend to the highest horizon.
Therefore, by Thy glory, O my God, I seek refuge in Thee through the name of Thy Divinity and Thy Lordship and Thy Mercy, that Thou mayest protect me on the Day of Resurrection and attract me through the attraction of the unseen realm of Thy Lordship to acknowledge Thy truth at the appearance of Thy Messengers and Thy Books. For on that Day the servant was sitting in his self-existence when someone came to him with a book perchance […] Let him not turn to one who has come, nor copy that Book to act according to what is in it, for then he would be veiled from meeting God inasmuch as he turns not unto Him.
For this is the Book of God from Him Whom God shall make manifest, and these are the messengers of God from Him, even as Thou didst cause me to witness, O my God, on that Day of Resurrection when Thy messengers delivered Thy verses unto every soul, yet none were conscious of them save the God-fearing among Thy servants, after Thy proof had been perfected through but a single one of Thy verses. For Thou hast created within every soul the essence of understanding whereby it comprehendeth that through which its religion is established. And there is no doubt that Thou hast proven to all who believe in Thee that the Qur’an is from Thee, a proof unto every soul, as all on earth are powerless to produce its like.
Then Thou didst send down the like thereof in the Bayan, and Thy messengers delivered the same, yet none became conscious of it even to say to himself: “If I believe in God and His verses, since all else is powerless to produce its like, how then can I remain patient regarding these verses, when every soul is incapable of producing their like?
