title: BB00058: Ziyarat li-Avvali man aman
text:
Part 1: “Glorified art Thou, O my God! I bear…”
In the name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy!
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I bear witness, and all things bear witness, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone, without peer. Thine is the dominion and the kingdom, Thine the might and the power, Thine the strength and the divinity, Thine the force and sovereignty, Thine the rule and the human realm. Thou givest life and causest death, then causest death and givest life. Verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not, the King Who passeth not away, the Just Who deviateth not, the Sovereign Who changeth not, the Single One from Whose grasp nothing escapeth, whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them. Thou art, verily, powerful over all things.
I testify, and all things testify, on this Most Great and Supreme Day, this Most Exalted and Impregnable Cause, this Most Lofty and Elevated Station, this Most Enduring Might, and this Most Noble and Gracious Glory, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, Lord of the kingdom and the realm, Possessor of might and power, of strength and sovereignty, of force and dominion, of invincibility and exaltation, of elevation and detachment, of majesty and grandeur, of greatness and beauty, of perfection and completeness, of power and action, of mercy and bounty, of awe and justice, of grandeur and pride, of sovereignty and radiance, of power and authority, and of all parables and similitudes.
Thou hast ever existed before all things without design or likeness, and wilt ever exist after all things without manner or transition. Thou hast ever been one God, Single, Eternal, Self-Subsisting, Ever-Living, Self-Sustaining. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast had no partner in sovereignty, nor any protector out of weakness. All creation is within Thy grasp; the dwellers of Thy earth and heaven stand in awe of Thy greatness, and all things worship Thee according to their understanding.
I testify that on that Day Thou wilt accept the praise of none, nor their turning toward Thee, except those who have believed in Thee and in Thy signs in the Bayan and what was sent down from Thee in the Book. I praise Thee for this lofty and impregnable glory and this exalted and elevated might, whereby all worship Thee, yet Thou acceptest none save me and those who follow me. All prostrate themselves before Thee, yet Thou hast loved this station from none save me and those who affirm my truth.
Glorified be Thy justice, O my God, whereby all are veiled while I and those who follow me delight in Thy good-pleasure, are thankful for Thy recognition, and prostrate ourselves before Thee at the gate Thou hast opened. And all do yearn for this; yet what […], when I found them abiding by the dictates of their own loves? Nevertheless Thou hast lavished upon us Thy supreme bounties and Thy most exalted [favors], in that Thou hast made every thing to taste the sweetness of knowing Thee—on such a plane that, were it given the choice of the dominion of the whole earth, it would assuredly choose the delight of Thy knowledge rather than possess that dominion. And all make this claim.
Yet will I praise Thee that all are slumbering while we are beholding and standing, as though they had no vital spirit to delight in that gnosis or to glory in that exposition. As for me—through the loftiness of my love therein and the exaltation of my spirit herein—my heart is not content that [anyone] should gain access thereto, nor [find] a path to it other than myself, O Lord of lords.
How then could [anyone] look upon the very Essence of the supernal treasuries? Let them strive that they may not look upon what none save I have beheld. Have thy knowledge and verses ever equaled all the treasures of earth? Nay, by Thy glory! I would not take a single letter in exchange for the kingdom of earth and all that is therein, nor do I wish to know myself except through knowing that Thou hast made this a glory, as Thou hast loved it, and a power, as Thou hast unified it. How has a particle of clay attained to a station Thou hast made Thine own self, and Thou hast removed all distinction between it and Thyself, as though it were Thee?
Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee. I shall surely glory in this on that Day which Thou hast magnified, honored, sanctified, exalted, beautified, glorified, elevated, fortified, empowered, perpetuated, established, and made illustrious, according to what Thou lovest to witness in me and in all things. And I shall praise Thee for bestowing the sovereignty of Thy oneness with praise that […] Thy praise from anything, and praise that filleth all the heavens with Thy grace, and all the earth with Thy bounty, and whatsoever is between them with Thy mercy. And I shall thank Thee for this […] with gratitude […] from before and none shall thank Thee hereafter with thanksgiving that filleth the essence of all things with mention of Thy glorification, and the reality of all things with mention of Thy praise, and the identity of all things with mention of Thy unity, and the being of all things with mention of Thy magnification, whereby nothing is seen in itself nor in anything except Thee, manifest and hidden, standing and compelling, powerful and impregnable, exalted and transcendent, supreme and all-encompassing.
Glory be unto Thee! How lofty is the elevation of Thy supreme gifts and how resplendent the ascension of Thy greatest bestowals, whereby Thou hast favored me with guidance and faith, and blessed me with exaltation and expression! I beseech Thee by Him through Whom Thou hast guided me and removed from me what Thou didst make grievous unto me, and opened unto me the gates of Thy bounty and Thy gift unto me, that Thou send blessings upon the Essence of the Seven Letters, then the Letters of the Living, through dominion and the kingdom, then through might and power, then through strength and divinity, then through force and the ruby, then sovereignty and the human realm, then through glory and majesty, then through countenance and beauty, then through presence and perfection, then through power and deed, then through sovereignty and independence, then through similitude and parables, then through loftiness and elevation, then through authority and invincibility, then through grandeur and bounty, then through whatsoever beseemeth Thee of similitude, names, geometry, radiance, might, and splendor.
For all this proceedeth from none but Thee, and none deserveth it on that Day save that Tree unto which Thou hast revealed these things and cast therein the likeness of Thyself, whereupon it reciteth Thy verses from Thy presence like unto an ocean surging in Thy love and good-pleasure […] in the limitless ocean in praise of Thy Essence and Thy glory.
I shall surely praise Thee for what Thou hast shown me at that time with mine own eyes concerning what Thou hast bestowed upon me of nineteen rings, and Thou dost witness in my hands. I shall surely testify concerning each one a mention from Thee according to the letters of “In the Name of God, the Most Impregnable, the Most Holy, the One” whereby Thou didst begin the creation of all things and unto which Thou didst cause all things to return. O God! Multiply that Oneness until it filleth Thy heaven and Thy earth, until there remaineth not a single human soul except that it turneth unto Thee through that Face and returneth unto Thee through that Oneness, for the decree of all things returneth unto that Temple, the Temple of humanity and the Divine Countenance and the Eternal Face and the Impenetrable Garment and the Unique Splendor.
Should any soul possess whatsoever is upon the whole earth—through Thee and Thy signs, then through the Point of the Bayan and the Letters of the Living—and should it love the Manifestations of Thy Names and Thy Likenesses, and those among Thy creatures who obey Thee, then whatsoever is upon the earth, in its entirety, is within Thy Paradise; and if it possess not the highest measure [of love], then according to the measure of what it doth possess shall it abide in Thy Paradise, whether they be of the highest ruby or the lowest clay.
Therefore I praise Thee and bear witness that I am at this moment in the most exalted [station] and the most glorious recognition of Thee, and the loftiest of Thy seats, and the most impregnable of Thy mysteries, and the most mighty of Thy thrones in the sacred heights of Thy presence. Thou hast created therein the most excellent things and provided for me according to Thy decree. By Thy power Thou hast inscribed therein the mention of Thy Most Exalted Name […] Then the third and […] the all-embracing and the attentive ear, then the fourth and its consummate wisdom and abundant grace, then in the fifth peace be upon […] paradise and hell. Glory be unto Thee! All this is Thine, from Thee, through Thee, and unto Thee.
There is none other God but Thee. O God! Reward him who hath written this in the Ridvan by Thy leave upon that crimson silk—for each letter reward him as befitteth the sublimity of Thy generosity and the exaltation of Thy grace […] of Thy bounty, for verily Thou art the Knower of all atoms and the Powerful over all possibilities, the Exalted above all who dwell in the kingdoms of earth and heaven, the Inaccessible above all contingent things, and the Most High above all atoms. Creation is Thy creation and command is from Thee and unto Thee alone. There is none other God but Thee.
Therefore, O God, send Thy blessings upon the Tree that Thou wilt manifest on the Day of Resurrection through Thy power, and wilt strengthen through Thy might, and wilt cause to reign through Thy sovereignty, and wilt exalt through Thy loftiness, and wilt manifest through Thy manifestation, and wilt endow with whatsoever Thou hast loved for it through the dominion of Thy oneness, and upon the heaven from which […] hath descended and the earth that hath borne it […] and the first relation that is attributed to it, and the first […] that is drawn unto it, and the first knowledge that is devoted unto it—from all Thy glory its most glorious, and from all Thy majesty its most majestic, and from all Thy beauty its most beautiful, and from all Thy grandeur its most grand, and from all Thy light its most luminous, and from all Thy mercy its most extensive, and from all Thy words its most perfect, and from all Thy names its most great, and from all Thy might its most mighty, and from all Thy will its most potent, and from all Thy knowledge its most penetrating, and from all Thy power its most dominant, and from all Thy utterance its most pleasing, and from all Thy sovereignty its most enduring, and from all Thy dominion its most excellent, and from all Thy exaltation its most exalted, and from all Thy signs its most wondrous, and from all that Thou hast loved or wilt love in the kingdom of Thy heaven and earth that which hath no equal, no peer, no likeness, no associate, and no similitude.
And preserve it from the beginning of its manifestation from between its hands and from behind it and from its right and its left and from above its head and beneath its feet and from every direction that extends toward it and from all that Thou hast given it and that is attributed to it, by that whereby Thou didst preserve the Bayan with Thee and didst send down the Book upon it, and by the right of that divine Tree, do Thou assist that lordly Tree, and by the right of its Letters of the Living, do Thou assist those Names, and by the right of its similitudes, do Thou verily succour those likenesses. And by the right of that which shineth forth from its words, do Thou exalt that which dawneth from those words; for every former Manifestation hath faded before that wherewith Thou dost reveal Thyself thereafter. And, verily, I have loved naught but what Thou hast loved. There is no doubt that Thou hast desired for Thy loved ones naught but the eternal abode and everlasting glory which hath ever been and shall ever be exalted beyond reach.

title: BB00058: Ziyarat li-Avvali man aman
section: Part 2: “I beseech Thee by her parents to bestow…”
text:
Part 2: “I beseech Thee by her parents to bestow…”
I beseech Thee by her parents to bestow upon the parents of that Tree what beseemeth the loftiness of Thy generosity and the sublimity of Thy grace. And by her siblings, bestow upon the siblings of that Tree what beseemeth the heights of Thy transcendence and the summit of Thy inaccessibility. And by her hidden names, bestow upon those concealed names what beseemeth the exaltation of Thy sovereignty and the effulgence of Thy light and the transcendent joy of Thy divine unity. And upon all who believe in Him, whether male or female, and all things that enter His dominion, bestow upon those who have believed in her and entered beneath the shadow of her sovereignty what beseemeth the glory of Thy splendor and the eminence of Thy exaltation. For verily nothing in the heavens or earth escapeth Thy knowledge, and nothing in the kingdoms of command or creation can frustrate Thee. Shower upon the Primary Letters and all that relateth unto them at all times the tokens of Thy bounty and the wonders of Thy generosity. For Thou art the King, the All-Bestowing, the Inaccessible, the Mighty, the Most Exalted.
And if thou findest thyself on such a day near the Tree of Sin or any of the Letters of the Living, then don thou the most glorious raiment that God hath given thee and enter, by God’s leave, into the precincts of His Cause. Then proclaim before God, if thou canst attain His presence, or before the Letters of the Living, if thou attainest their presence: “We are the Most Glorious Splendor, the Most Sublime Majesty, the Most Beauteous Beauty, the Most Great Grandeur, the Most Luminous Light, the All-embracing Mercy, and the […] on high; and the Most Great Names; and the [mightiest …]; and the Irresistible Will; the Most Penetrating Knowledge; the Outstretched Power; the Most Acceptable Good-Pleasure; the Most Pre-eminent Love; nay, the Most Firm, the Most High; the Ever-abiding Sovereignty; the Noble Dominion; the [lofty …]; and the Most Ancient, Towering Bounty—be upon thee, O Tree of Glory, Lamp of Splendour, Countenance hallowed by Radiance, Orientation suffused with Praise, and Beingness deserving all greatness and primacy—from God, beside Whom there is none other God, Who hath ever been and shall forever be.
How should I not make mention of thee, when it behoveth that whatsoever is upon the earth be arrayed before thee, even as thou, with every thing, standest before God? I behold naught in the heavens, on the earth, or between them but that it hath been created through thee, provided through thee, slain through thee, quickened through thee, and raised up through thee.
And notwithstanding all this, thou—upon the height of thy seat—art the very Alif without the Ba’; and the seat of […] hath made thee […] for all things, upon a Mount that knoweth no seat of might and no effulgence. With every soul, from Adam until that Hour, is it so, that they may turn by thee unto […] and attain by thee unto His presence. Thus hath He singled thee out for […] and veiled it from all else, for that, with Him, is more precious than aught besides.
And though all should abandon obedience unto thee and refrain from prostration before the Sultan of thy might, yet, by Thy glory, I will verily glory upon my seat atop that Mount, that I do salute thee, and make thee hear the mention of my love before Thee, and […] with me upon […] in the path of Thy affection and Thy love. Nay, by Thy might! Thou wert never abased; for every honour is honour through Thy might, and every exaltation exalted by Thy majesty. Thou wert never alone, for every remembrance is multiplied through Thy multiplication. Thou wert never vanquished, for all victory is triumphant through Thy triumph. Thou wert never a stranger, for all intimacy finds comfort in Thy companionship. Thou wert never without sovereignty, for all dominion takes pride in Thy dominion. Thou art the Exalted One, and all are exalted through Thy exaltation. Thou art the Most High, and all are elevated through Thy inaccessibility.
Essences were made non-existent that they might prostrate before Thee to God, yet they knew Thee not. Tongues were severed that they might stammer Thy remembrance and the loftiness of Thy glory, yet they speak in denial of Thee. Hands were cut off for the exaltation of Thy grace and the sublimity of […] among those who dwell in Thy shadow, yet they order Thy death and that which befitteth not Thy holy exaltation.
Therefore do I complain unto God of what hath befallen me and Thee, and through Thy remembrance on that most exalted Day shall I glory over all else, for none seeth what I see in Thee of Thy right over all things and the loftiness of Thy station with God, Thy Lord, in that Thou didst follow the Truth when Thou found it and didst verify the verses of God when Thou heard them. Nay, by Thy glory! Even wert Thou at that time beneath the dust of Thy body, yet the exaltation of Thy station in the essences of souls and horizons is so inaccessible that all things recognize Thee and every soul draweth nigh unto God through Thee, for all advance toward God through the first to believe in their Prophet, even though in that Day they know Thee not and witness not Thy station with God, Thy Lord.
Yet sufficient is God’s testimony concerning Thee before every soul, for if all things were to testify to something, unless that testimony be true, God would testify to it through something as He willeth, according to His Will […] I bear witness that Thou hast ascended with all that Thou art unto God, the Glorious, the Mighty, and hast mounted with all that is within and upon Thee unto Thy Creator Who created Thee. The Letters of the Living, all of them, bear witness through Thy soul, and all that God hath unified in the Bayan hath been quickened through Thy guidance. Who then can fail to thank Thee as is Thy due and to turn through Thee to God, Thy Lord?
Had Thou not opened the gate of the Bayan, who could turn to God and who could know Him? I bear witness that all good hath been quickened through Thee and realized from Thee and returneth unto Thee, while Thou returnest unto God, bearing witness to His supreme unity, submitting before the Sovereign of His unity, humbling Thyself before the King of His glory, raising through Thee unto Thee, and speaking through Thy grace before Thee, whence there is no return save from Thee. This is a glory wherein all created things take pride in their deeds and acts […]
O God, have mercy upon all Thy creation, for verily Thou hast ordained those graves only for glory on that Day, and Thou hast commanded attendance at those [places] only for the presence of Thy creation before the Manifestations of Thy might. Therefore I beseech Thee, O my God, by the truth of that which in Thy knowledge […] that when one appears before that Letter, his essence and all he has acquired shall be annihilated though he perceives it not. For by Thy glory, from the beginning of my Manifestation I recognized all who believed in Thee and in Thy verses aforetime in the Furqan, and I found none who was conscious of Thy Manifestation save whom Thou didst will, lest any soul’s essence be annihilated or any deed be rendered void. Yet I have witnessed—and there is no strength except through Thee—that Thou hast ordained what causes the possessors of crafts to receive the elixir of faith from every being, and Thou hast commanded concerning the accidental parts as Thou hast commanded. Therefore O God, take not from the Bayan except that Thou makest them all possessed of the elixir, receptive to the day of Thy Manifestation and prostrate before […] in the day of Thy concealment, for verily Thou art powerful over that.
Then turn to the branches of that Tree and say: Verily We are the Most Glorious Beauty from God, the Lord of the Hereafter and the Former times. Upon you be what […] the holy branches and the transcendent leaves and the exalted fruits […] the sun and the stars in their rising places illumined […] he who is guided is guided and […] he who is not guided is not guided. And upon you from your Lord is what befits the loftiness of His bounty and the sublimity of His holiness, for all that descends from the heights of His glory ever descends upon you […] that you may attain unto […] and thereby those who ascend to God your Lord ascend through you, and through you descends who descends and […] ascends who ascends. There is no power save in God, no grandeur save in God, no sovereignty save in God’s hand, no might save in His grasp, and no invincibility save in God’s Self. And from Him upon you is what befits the loftiness of His remembrance of you at morn and eve, then in every condition and before every condition, and that whereby He remembers Himself with the remembrance of might and majesty.
Then turn to God’s martyrs in the Holy Land and say: Verily the Supreme Example and the Most Glorious Geometry from God, the Lord of the greatest signs and the mightiest evidences and the most exalted manifestations and the most beautiful names and the most sublime examples, be upon you, O leaves of the Tree of the Bayan! How exalted is your station, your station! How sweet is your state, your state! How lofty is your rank, your rank! How glorious is your seat, your seat! How great is your detachment, your detachment unto God your Lord Who created you and provided for you and […] and raised you from the resting-places of your hearts by God’s blessings upon you and upon them who believed in Him!
By the life of Him Who made you the names of His Self on the day of His Manifestation and the proofs of His unity’s sovereignty on the day of His dawning, you have attained a triumph the ancients envy and achieved a grace the manifest and hidden ones desire! Upon your great ones be God’s grandeur at its greatest, upon your mighty ones be God’s might at its mightiest, upon your wealthy ones be God’s riches at their richest, upon your powerful ones be God’s power at its most powerful, upon your manifest ones be God’s manifestation at its most manifest, upon your hidden ones be God’s concealment at its most concealed, and upon your first and last, your high and low, what God has ordained for you of the sublimity of transcendence and the exaltation of elevation and […] detachment and elevation.
Opening and the prevention of power, and there is no doubt […] or do not comprehend this how […] upon you all who have followed the Bayan and […] […] like […] every soul. And when you have comprehended from the light of martyrdom and the exaltation of guardianship—and this is that in which the mighty ones take pride and by which the boastful ones boast. And there is no might and no power except through God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting. And there is no glory and no invincibility and no sovereignty and no loftiness and no grandeur and no power and no majesty except through God, the Mighty, the Holy.

title: BB00255: Ziyarat li-Avvali man aman
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I testify before Thee on this day, the Day of Friday, and before all things, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone without partner. Thine is the dominion and the kingdom, Thine the might and the power, Thine the strength and the sovereignty, Thine the force and authority. Thou givest life and causest death, then causest death and givest life. Verily, Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not, the Single One Who passeth not away, the King Who perisheth not, the Sovereign Who changeth not. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
Then turn to the Sun and say: May the Most Glorious Glory and the Most Exalted Sublimity from Thy Lord, the God of all things, be upon thee, O thou Rising Sun, Eternal Sign, Divine Countenance, Most Holy Face, and Garment of Unity! I testify before thee and all things that there is no God but Him, my Lord and thy Lord. He hath ever been One God, Single, Alone, Self-Subsisting. He hath no partner in sovereignty, nor any protector in the earth save by His leave. He hath ordained the creation of all things by His power and hath fashioned the essence of all things by His will.
I shall testify before thee from this moment until the Day of Resurrection, that thou mayest bear witness before God concerning that which I have testified to thee, for that is the Day of Judgment and Decree. God, thy Lord, shall judge between His servants and shall recompense every soul according to what it hath earned, by His creation. Nothing escapeth His knowledge, whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them, and nothing in the kingdom of command or creation or what lieth beneath them can frustrate Him. Verily, He is powerful over all things.
Then turn to [Him Who is] established upon His throne and settled upon His seat and say: Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Verily Thou art Peace, and from Thee cometh peace, and unto Thee returneth peace, and Thou art the Creator of peace. Thou hast ever been exalted in Thine Essence above the most sublime essences of all contingent beings reaching toward the horizon of Thy majesty’s glory, and Thou wilt ever be sanctified in Thine Entity at a height which no being can attain through the manifestation of its essential reality. I beseech Thee, O my God, in this hour on Friday, before Thy Beloved, Thy Friend, Thy Chosen One, Thy Intimate One, and Thy Trusted One, by that which Thou hast revealed unto Him, that Thou wilt bless the Tree of Affirmation, its root, branch, twigs, leaves and fruits with every blessing Thou hast created or wilt create, with every mercy Thou hast spread or wilt spread, with every gift Thou hast bestowed or wilt bestow upon anyone, with every honor Thou hast conferred or wilt confer upon anyone, and with every bounty Thou hast sent down by Thy command or wilt send down. For every good by which something is remembered descendeth from the heaven of Thy glory’s clouds, and whatsoever is below that is created by Thy justice.
I testify before Thee, O my God, that the Tree of Thy Unity hath ever been unapproachable, exalted, transcendent, holy, magnificent, glorious, mighty, sovereign, and ruling. It hath been elevated above every elevation through its indication of Thee, and raised above every height through its confronting Thy Will, for Thou hast tested all Thy creation in Thy unity through the manifestation of Him Whom Thou hast established in the station of Thy uniqueness and upon Whom Thou hast sent down the signs of Thy grandeur. For whosoever hath truly believed in Thy servant in Thy unity, then he hath no will save the Will underlying the Will of Thy uniqueness, no desire save its desire, no power save its power, no decree save its decree, no term save its term, no permission save its permission, and no book besides His Books.
And if there be in any soul aught beside His Will, such would not be among the proofs of Thy unity nor among the manifestations of Thy sanctity, but rather a sign of the fire and within it, for Thou hast not created any fire more intense than separation from Thee, and Thou hast not decreed anything Thou lovest not to be mentioned more remote than that which would indicate will besides Thy Will. By Thy glory, I shall surely flee from such a state unto Thee, and shall turn through Thee to Thee, that I may not indicate anything except Thee, for that is the ultimate ascent of the servant unto Thee, and the final height to which the servant can rise unto Thee.
Therefore, O my God, cause at that time the entire tree and whatsoever shall be its return and abode to be according to what Thou lovest and art pleased with, for whosoever departeth from beneath its shade entereth into the shadow of the fire, as there is naught between negation and affirmation, and whosoever is therein is either in Thy fire or in Thy paradise—around these two do all contingent beings revolve and all created things circle. Therefore, O my God, protect me from all fire and grant me paradise and whatsoever Thou hast created therein, for I know of no fire more intense than remoteness from Thee, and no paradise more exalted than nearness unto Thee. Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. Below that fire is the limit of existence, and below that paradise is the paradise of existence.
I verily seek Thy forgiveness for all that Thou lovest not, and I beseech Thee for all that Thou lovest to send down upon that Most Exalted Branch and the Most Impregnable, Most Glorious Exemplar, and upon whosoever followeth His path among the former and latter ones, the outer and inner ones, until the Day wherein Thou shalt judge, for that is the Day of Judgment. Grant me, O my God, on that Day complete certitude, for I have already witnessed therein from before, when naught remained save Thee. Therefore, O my God, on that Day encompass all who have believed in Thee and in Thy signs, for Thou art the Lord of all worlds. He is God. And unto God belongeth all command before and after, and verily unto God shall all return.

title: BB00053: Ziyarat
text:
Part 1: “Glorified art Thou, O my God! I possess…”
In the Name of God, the Most Inaccessible, the Most Holy!
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I possess not a heart wherewith to remember Thee, nor a soul to praise Thee, nor a spirit to sanctify Thee, nor a being to unite with Thee. All of me hath melted away through what Thou hast decreed. Thine is the command and the creation in what Thou hast decreed and wilt decree. From time immemorial Thou hast been one God, single, unique, eternal, self-subsisting. Thou hast taken neither consort nor offspring, nor hath Thine Essence been joined with aught that Thou hast created out of nothing through Thy creation.
Glorified and exalted art Thou! Thou dost ever cause to die and give life, and verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not, the Single One from Whose grasp nothing can escape, whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them. Thou hast distinguished Thyself through might and immortality, and hast exalted Thyself through grandeur and glory. Thou hast existed before all things without mention of anything, and Thou wilt continue to exist after all things without the presence of anything.
Glorified art Thou beyond being known by any of Thy creatures, or being unified by any of Thy servants, or being praised by any dwellers of Thy earth and heaven, or being acknowledged as one by aught that Thou hast numbered in the kingdom of Thy creation. Thou art the Exalted above all things and the Most Exalted above all things. Thou hast ever been praised in Thy decrees and thanked in all Thy glorification, for nothing can frustrate Thee in the heavens or on the earth, nor can anything escape Thy knowledge in the kingdoms of command and creation.
That Thou shouldst carry out a decree for the people of Thy love is not due to any impotence on Thy part, nor is Thy respite to Thine enemy due to any restraint. Rather, it hath ever been and will ever be Thy way to raise Thy loved ones to the horizon of what is possible in creation and to abase Thine enemies to what is possible in invention. Thou proceedest through the dominion of Thy decree after Thy power over all else, and Thou sendest down from the treasuries of Thy Command after Thy ability over all else.
Glorified and exalted art Thou! I shall remember Thee according to what Thou hast decreed for me, and I shall weep over that, and I shall mention unto Thee that which Thou indeed knowest. Glorified and exalted art Thou! These are hearts that have praised none but Thee, and these are spirits that have glorified none but Thee, and these are souls that have united with none but Thee, and these are bodies that have worshipped none but Thee.
Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. How can I remember Thee in Thy presence or complain to Thee of my sorrow and grief? Glorified art Thou, O Thou Who ordaineth what He pleaseth and doeth what He willeth! I beseech Thee to send down upon those who have ascended unto Thee the measures of Thy glory and the dawning-places of Thy majesty, for through them hast Thou created that and wilt create and create again.
Glorified art Thou! Verily Thy might is more elevated and Thy power, O Mighty One, is greater than that I should ask Thee to destroy those who have grown proud before Thee and worshipped other than Thee, for Thou art more severe in might and greater in power. Nothing can escape Thy grasp and nothing can frustrate Thee.
I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thyself—for nothing with Thee is greater than Thee, nor more mighty, nor more exalted, nor more glorious—to punish those who have slain Thy proofs, grown proud before Thy loved ones, and worshipped other than Thee, with every chastisement Thou art capable of in creation, and to seize them and what their right hands possess with what Thy knowledge encompasseth of the measures of Thy seizure and the occurrences of Thy severity. For there is no glory for whom Thou hast forsaken, and nothing for whom Thou hast annihilated, and no life for whom Thou hast tormented, and nothing for who hath worshipped other than Thee and been deluded by what Thou hast given him.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Send down that which befitteth the loftiness of Thy grasp, the sublimity of Thy might, and the elevation of Thy power upon those who have waxed proud against the Manifestations of Thy Countenance and have slain those who worship none but Thee. For Thou didst speak—and Thy word is the truth in the Qur’an—“whoso killeth a soul, it shall be as if he had killed all mankind.” Thou, O my God, dost number what their hands have wrought. Such was the decree of one of those who believed in Thee; how much more so with those by whom and for whom Thou didst create the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them, and didst ordain their authority over all things, and didst send down the Bayan in exaltation of their mention and elevation of their glory. Unto Thee all things return, and there is no power except through Thee.
I make mention of Thee at this moment with what Thou lovest to be mentioned, that Thou mayest send down upon the Manifestations of Thy obedience and the Dawning-places of Thy glory what Thou hast recorded in the Mother Book of all prayers—the most magnificent thereof—and of all salutations—the most noble thereof that Thou hast created. And do Thou, O God, manifest the measures of Thy glory and send down upon them from the angels on high what is decreed by Thee, for verily Thou art the One Who hath power over whatsoever Thou willest and art mighty over whatsoever Thou desirest. Thy Will is supreme in all that Thou hast willed or wilt will, and Thy Purpose prevaileth in all that Thou hast purposed or wilt purpose.
Send down, O my God, from the heights of Thy bounty and the elevation of Thy glory, upon the Letters of the First, that which befitteth the sublimity of Thy grandeur and the inaccessibility of Thy oneness. Then upon those who have sought shelter beneath the shadow of those possessed of Thy authority, from the gems of verses and the ornaments of clear proofs, that which Thou alone art worthy of, for none is worthy of that which Thou art worthy of, and that which others are worthy of—Thou art far exalted above being mentioned thereby.
O God! Send Thy blessings upon Muhammad and the Manifestations of His Self, and the Gates of Thy Countenance, and upon those who have believed in Thee and in Thy signs, according to what Thou hast numbered in Thy knowledge, for there is no escape for Thy creation and no limit to what returneth of the wonders of the Cause unto Thee. Send down, O my God, upon those holy spirits, those sanctified souls, and those impregnable bodies, that which befitteth the loftiness of Thy glory and the elevation of Thy majesty. And ordain, O my God, for those who were against them and acted wrongfully towards them that which Thou art worthy of, for Thou art the Most Great among the mighty in the realm of grandeur and glory, and the Most Severe of avengers in the station of chastisement and retribution.
Curse, O God, whosoever hath cut from the tree of Thy love whether root, branch, or twig, with every curse encompassed by Thy knowledge. For Thou art the Almighty from Whose grasp nothing escapeth, and the All-Compelling from Whose will nothing can withhold. I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thy Name through which the Dawning-places of Thy unity are established and there is negated from Thee whatsoever Thou lovest not in the kingdom of Thy sanctity—the Name which Thou hast placed after the letter B before all Thy names, and through which Thou hast created all things, sustained them, caused them to die, given them life, and raised them up—to send blessings upon those who have believed in Thee and in Thy signs, who have ascended to the horizon of Thy good-pleasure, who have detached themselves unto the horizon of Thy grandeur, who have risen to the court of Thy glory, and have drunk from the cup of Thy mercy that which befitteth the loftiness of Thy grace and the power of Thy might. For Thy giving hath no equal, and what Thou hast ordained in the Mother Book for those who have ascended unto Thee hath no limit.
Thou dost ever reveal unto those whom Thou hast caused to dwell in Thy paradise and hast raised to the horizon of Thy glory that which befitteth the loftiness of Thy Countenance. Glorified art Thou, O my God! How can I mention that which my heart hath witnessed? This is beyond my capacity and the capacity of any of Thy creatures. The heavens are well-nigh cleft asunder and the earth rent asunder.
Glory be unto Thee! Glory be unto Thee! How great is such a calamity in the kingdom of Thy creation, and how grievous is such an affliction in the realm of Thy heaven and earth! Glory be unto Thee, O God! How canst Thou decree for those hidden gems and treasured essences that which Thou hast decreed, while I am powerless even to witness it? Glory be unto Thee! Glory be unto Thee! I shall entrust my affair unto Thee and rely upon Thee in all my concerns. I shall beseech of Thee that which Thou lovest and with which Thou art well-pleased, from the most exalted horizon to the lowest depths. I shall remember Thee, O my God, with a grief before Thee that hath no beginning, and my sorrow in Thy path shall never cease, nor shall my lamentations about the measures of Thy power be cut short.
I beseech Thee, O Lord my God, by that which Thou lovest to be beseeched by, to raise me up unto Thee in a manner that Thou lovest and approvest, and to unite me with those who have attained unto Thy good-pleasure in this earthly life, who have ascended unto Thee and have attained Thy presence. For that which is with Thee, O my God, is better than that which is with men, and what Thou hast ordained in the hereafter for Thy God-fearing servants is better than what Thou hast decreed in the first life.
I beseech Thee, O Lord my God, my Beloved, my Creator, and my Desired One, to send Thy blessings at this moment upon Muhammad, then upon the Manifestations of Thy Self, then upon those who have followed what they followed of Thy unity, Thy sanctity, Thy oneness, and Thy glorification, and what Thou hast ordained at this noon-tide hour for the dwellers of Thy kingdom that befitteth the sublimity of Thy grace, O Thou Who art the Lord of mercy and bounty, and that which is worthy of the court of Thy generosity, O Thou Who art the Lord of munificence and favor!
Glory be unto Thee! Glory be unto Thee! Thou art He Who begetteth not, nor wast begotten, and there is none like unto Thee, nor equal unto Thee, nor comparable unto Thee, nor peer unto Thee. Thou hast ever been supreme over all Thy servants and manifest above all that Thou hast created in the kingdom of Thy earth and heaven. I beseech Thee, O God, by that which is befitting to be beseeched by, to ordain at this moment from Thy presence that which is best for the people of Thy love, for Thou art the Sovereign of this world and the next, the Originator of their cause, the One Who causeth their means to flow, and the Mover of their destinies. Unto Thee do all return, and before Thee all are brought.
I beseech Thee, O God, by the grief which I have witnessed like unto which no grief hath been witnessed for the Manifestations of Thy countenance, to send Thy blessings upon them at this moment with all Thy glory, and to send down upon them from the most exalted horizon that which befitteth the sublimity of Thy bestowal. For verily, I have known and do know that this is not from Thee; rather, Thou hast ever done what Thou willest as Thou willest, and ordained what Thou desirest as Thou desirest. There is no power nor strength except through Thee, and unto Thee do we return.
And when thou desirest to enter that sacred land, purify thyself and make wholesome what is with thee to the best of thy ability. Know thou that there is the most exalted horizon of the Throne and the ultimate summit of Paradise, and that God doth ever behold thee, and the Manifestations of His Self do ever illumine thee.
When thou hast performed such ablutions as thou art able, lie down for a while until thy strength returneth unto thee. Then arise and pray two rak’ahs in thy house, then walk in silence until thou reachest the first gate.
There stand and say: “Glory be unto Thee, O God! Verily, Thou art the Originator of the heavens and the earth, the Knower of the unseen and the seen. Nothing of Thy knowledge can be known, neither in the heavens nor on the earth, and nothing can frustrate Thee, neither in the kingdom of Command nor of Creation. Thou hast ever existed before all things through the existence of Thy Essence, and wilt ever exist after all things through the existence of Thine own Self. Creation is Thy creation and Command is from Thee, and no one hath aught save that which Thou hast ordained.
“I beseech Thee, O my God, by that Most Exalted Seat which Thou hast favored through those Manifestations of Thy Beauty and Repositories of Thy Glory who dwell therein, that Thou grant me leave to enter unto Thee through Thee and to witness before Thee that for which Thou hast created me. For Thou hast not created anything except that it may testify to Thy unity and reject those who deny Thy oneness.
“I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thy generosity and grace, to permit me to enter the sanctuary of Thy grandeur and to abide before the sovereignty of Thy Self-Sufficiency, that I may praise Thee as befitteth the majesty of Thy glory and the exaltation of Thy greatness, for none but Thee can do this. Verily, I see no limit to my heart nor to what Thou hast given me that I should present myself before Thee without Thy leave, or claim for myself any station through my own merit. Glory be to Thee! Exalted art Thou! Thou art too high and glorious for any created thing to fulfill what is due unto Thee, or to enter the sanctuary of Thy glory through its own merit rather than through Thy grace and favor.

title: BB00053: Ziyarat
text: “Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I have no remembrance save through Thy remembrance of me, and no permission save what Thou hast permitted me in the Mother Book. I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thyself, to send down upon me from the Most Exalted Horizon that which will purify me when I stand before Thy glory and prepare me for the meeting with Thy countenance. Glory be unto Thee! Thou hast not created me save for this, nor provided for me save for that. Unto Thee be praise, true praise, for having granted me leave to that Most Exalted Seat and honored me with that Most Glorious Horizon. There is no power save in God, the Lord of the Hereafter and the Former Times.”

title: BB00053: Ziyarat
section: Part 2: “Enter thou, therefore, and glorify God within thyself…”
text:
Part 2: “Enter thou, therefore, and glorify God within thyself…”
Enter thou, therefore, and glorify God within thyself without uttering with thy tongue. And if thou art unable to recite that prayer, then recite the Surih of Unity three times. Then walk as thou art able until thou reachest the second door.
There pause and say:

“There is no God but God, and God is Most Great. Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no power save in God. He is my Lord and no one is partner unto Him in anything.”

Then enter and prostrate thyself there until thou reachest the door of the sanctuary.
There prostrate thyself before God and say: “God beareth witness that there is no God but Him. His are the creation and the command. He giveth life and causeth death, then causeth death and giveth life, and He is the Ever-Living Who dieth not. Within His grasp is the dominion of all things. He createth what He pleaseth by His command. He is, verily, powerful over all things.
“O God! Thou art the Lord of Glory and the Creator of Glory and the Bestower of Glory and the Ordainer of Glory and the Fashioner of Glory. Thine are the most beautiful names and the most exalted similitudes, and all that is seen and unseen, from the highest height to the lowest depth. I bear witness, and all things bear witness, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone with no partner, and that Muhammad—Thy blessings be upon him and upon the Manifestations of his self—was Thy servant and Thy Messenger whom Thou didst choose for Thy Cause and select for Thy Message and single out for what lieth with Thee, and upon whom Thou didst send down Thy verses and through whom Thou didst magnify Thy clear proofs and through whom Thou didst manifest all that Thou hadst created by Thy command.
“I beseech Thee, O my God, at this moment to send blessings upon him with every glory wherewith Thou hast glorified, and every majesty wherewith Thou hast exalted, and every beauty wherewith Thou hast beautified, and every grandeur wherewith Thou hast magnified, and every light wherewith Thou hast illumined, and every mercy wherewith Thou hast spread abroad, and every word which Thou hast sent down, and every might wherewith Thou hast strengthened, and every will hast Thou confirmed, and every knowledge hast Thou executed, and every power hast Thou decreed, and every exaltation hast Thou elevated, and every sovereignty hast Thou perpetuated, and every dominion hast Thou glorified, and every bounty hast Thou enumerated, for none possesseth any of these save Thee, and none hath power over these except Thee. Thou art the Ever-Existing, Who hath never ceased to be and will never cease to be, and the Creator of all things at all times as Thou willest.

“I beseech Thee, O my God, by every name wherewith Thou hast named Thyself, and by every attribute which Thou hast mentioned in Thy Book, to send down upon the heart of Muhammad, and the spirit of Muhammad, and the soul of Muhammad, and the body of Muhammad that which befitteth the loftiness of Thy bestowal and the sublimity of Thine exaltation. And do Thou specifically favor, O my God, the manifestations of His Self and those who have drunk the water of His love and have been given to drink the pure water of His authority. Verily, Thou art the Munificent, the Inaccessible, and verily, Thou art the All-Bountiful, the Most Generous.”

Then enter and witness with the eye of thy heart that thou art turned towards God and art present before His eyes, and that He, verily, nurtureth thee, heareth what thou sayest and witnesseth what thou earnest, and He is with thee to turn thee as He willeth and to inspire thee in the places of His Command as He desireth. Verily, He is powerful over all things.
Then walk and say in thy walking “Allahu Akbar” seven times, and when thou reachest the gate of the sanctuary, stand there and enter not except thou waitest there seven days, for there it behooveth thee to enter and say: “O my God! Thou art the Possessor of all things and none besides Thee possesseth anything. I seek Thy leave by Thy grace, and by all that Thou hast loved of Thy near angels and Thy commissioned Prophets and Thy pure ones who stand in ranks and Thy God-fearing servants, that I may enter before Thy Beloved, Whom Thou hast chosen for Thyself and selected for Thy Remembrance and chosen for Thy Successor, and has linked His obedience to Thy obedience and His authority to Thy authority, for verily Thou art not associated with the mention of anything, and nothing comprehendeth Thee, neither in the heavens nor on earth nor what lieth between them, and Thou art the King, the Quickener, the Supreme, the Transcendent.”
Then turn towards Him Who is established upon the throne of His might and is seated upon the seat of His sovereignty, and say five times:

“There is no God but Thee, alone, alone, none is worshipped but Him, making our worship pure for Him, though the unbelievers be averse.”

Then say: “The most exalted glory and the most sublime praise from the King of creation and the Ordainer of all things be upon thee, O Essence of the Qur’an and Beauty of expression, O Thou Whom God hath distinguished with that wherewith He hath distinguished none other of His servants, for He hath manifested Himself through Thee to Thyself before all things, and made Thee know His Self, and made Thee witness His oneness before all things. Then through Thee hath He created all things, and through Thee hath He provided sustenance for all things, and through Thee hath He caused all things to die, and through Thee hath He given life to all things, and through Thee will He resurrect all things.
“I bear witness that Thou hast ascended unto God and hast been raised up unto Thy Lord, and all who lived in Thy days and ascended with Thee unto God, Thy Lord, are among those who shall inherit Paradise, wherein they shall abide forever, provided with what God hath given them of His grace, and wherein they shall have what they desire. May my soul and all that my Lord’s knowledge encompasseth be a sacrifice unto Thee! How can I make mention of Thee or praise Thee, when all that is seen and unseen is but a trace created through Thee and a form brought into being through Thee?
“Exalted is Thy remembrance above being conjoined with the remembrance of the foremost of them that make mention; and uplifted is Thy glory beyond being matched by the glory of the chiefs among men of thought. I bear witness that though Thou wert slain, yet Thou art alive with God. Through that which God hath created from the excellence of Thy life, the hearts of the sincere are quickened, and thereby they recognize the unity of God, Thy Lord, and glorify Him day and night without cease.
“How great is Thy right, how exalted is that which befitteth the wondrous nature of Thy station, the loftiness of Thy rank, and the sublimity of Thy manifestations! Thou didst detach Thyself from all things for the sake of God, Thy Lord, ascending to such heights as none before Thee attained nor any shall reach after Thee. Exalted is that which Thou hast attained, and blessed is that which Thou hast witnessed.
“I testify that Thou and those who ascended with Thee are in the most exalted horizon above the Throne and in the most glorious heights of the heaven of the Divine Seat. There they glorify God with the praise of their Lord and celebrate His unity. I bear witness before God, before Thyself, before the Manifestations of Thy countenance, and before all that God hath willed, that Thou didst call unto God, didst deliver that which was entrusted to Thee from the Book of God, and didst attain unto that which God, Thy Lord, had promised Thee from the most exalted martyrdom and the most sublime station of divine authority. None after Thee can reach Thy station. Nay, by Thy glory! All who are martyred shall be martyred through Thy martyrdom, and all who ascend shall ascend after the ascension of Thy glory.
“I testify that Thy calamity is the greatest of all calamities in creation, and Thy tribulation is more exalted than any tribulation in existence. Cursed be the people who knew not Thy right, who prostrated not themselves before the loftiness of Thy station, and who turned not through Thee to God, Thy Lord. These are they who are quit of God’s religion, and I am quit of them and of that whereunto their affair shall return in their place of return and abode. They worshipped not God for even the twinkling of an eye in creation, nor did they recognize His unity in the least degree in existence. They have naught from God, and they shall receive the recompense of that which their hands have wrought—the most severe fire and the most grievous punishment.
“Glory be unto Thee, O God! My Lord, multiply upon them that which they deserve, send down upon them that of which they are fearful, seize them as Thou didst seize those before them, and chastise them in the lowest depths of the fire for that which their hands have earned, for they have attributed themselves to Thy friend while slaying that whereby religion is established, without recognizing Him. O God! Double the punishment and torment upon those who have slain a soul without cause. Verily Thou art possessed of mighty vengeance and severe chastisement. How can any of Thy loved ones observe even an atom of the affairs of Thy justice, and how much more Thy vengeance! O God! Destroy those who were proud before Thee and slew him against whom Thou hadst witnessed naught save His love for Thee and Thy unity, who earned naught in Thy path save Thy good-pleasure and Thy sanctification, and who desired naught save the exaltation of Thy remembrance and Thy glorification.
“I therefore commit unto Thee, O my God, the judgment of these infidels who prostrated not themselves before Thee and worshipped Thee not in the least. Verily Thou art most severe in might and in punishment. How can I send greetings unto Thee, O Beloved of my heart, after having heard what befell Thee, whereby the heavens are well-nigh rent asunder, the earth cleft, and the mountains crumble to dust? Unto God do I complain, and unto Thee is the return. God shall unite me and those who believe in Him with Thee in the seat which He hath ordained for Thee and to which He hath brought Thee. Would that I had been with Thee that I might have ransomed myself for Thee, and that I might attain that which Thou didst attain through the mercy of my Lord!
“I bear witness that the angels of the heavens, the Throne, and the Divine Seat are, at all times, prostrate before the seat of Thy glory, that the hearts of the sincere are, in every state, enraptured with Thy love, and that the hearts of the mystics are directed towards the seat of Thy Divine Unity! Blessed is he who attaineth unto Thy presence, after God Himself hath testified to his presence before Him. How great a bounty is this in all existence, and how mighty a glory is this in all utterance!
“I testify that Thou hast ever been, and wilt ever be, alive with the life of Thy Lord, glorifying Him, praising Him, proclaiming His unity and magnifying Him, until the day when God shall return Thee to the primal life. Verily He alone was […] and unto […] I praise Thee, yet knowing that all praise before Thy reality is veiled, I fall short in utterance and find enlightenment in what God hath revealed concerning Thee. Were there naught else but this, all who dwell in the kingdoms of the heavens and earth and what lieth between them would bow down before it.
“I beseech Thee, by the loftiness of Thy grace and the sublimity of Thy mercy, to remember me before God, Thy Lord, and to remember those who are martyrs from Thy presence, then those who were martyred in the path of Thy love, who gave up their souls in ardent devotion to Thy Cause, who ascended unto God through their detachment in Thy love, and who attained what is with God through their attraction to obedience unto Thee. Nothing existeth save that it hath been realized through the manifestation of obedience unto Thee, and nothing existeth save that it hath withered away through the manifestation of Thy Will.

“I bear witness before God and those near unto Him that God shall seek vengeance for Thee as He pleaseth, through what He pleaseth, for unto Him belong all conditions both before and after, and unto Him belong all the seats of command in the heavens and earth which none comprehendeth save Him, and there is no command except from Him, and no glory except in His good-pleasure, and no abasement save for those upon whom God hath sent down His wrath. […] Indeed He is most severe in punishment and most mighty in retribution, most swift in power and most near in command concerning whatsoever He willeth and ordaineth. Verily, He hath power over all things.”

Then present thyself before the Manifestations […] from God through what God hath mentioned before or will reveal hereafter, then before those who have ascended unto God from among the embodiments of the Qur’an and the essences of the Bayan, and bear witness unto them through the mystery of the Bayan according to what God hath ordained for them in the Book.
Were the ocean to become ink wherewith to reckon the grace of but one of these near ones and pure souls, it would be exhausted ere that remembrance from God could be counted. If at that time thou art able to remember the Manifestations of His Remembrance with such remembrance, then remember them; otherwise, wait until God bringeth His Command.
And if thou art unable to enter that holy land, then visit the Proofs of God in thy home on Friday, according to what God hath revealed in the Book, for that is better in His sight than what people know. Verily we are God’s, and unto Him shall we return. There is no power nor strength except through God, the Most High, the Most Great.

title: BB00201: Du’ayi Sahar likulli laylin min shahri’llah
text:
In the name of God, the Most Inaccessible, the Most Holy!
O Thou Who accepteth whom the Point of the Bayan accepteth, and Who rejecteth whom the Point of the Bayan rejecteth, and Who regardeth that which the Point of the Bayan regardeth, and Who turneth not unto him unto whom the Point of the Bayan turneth not, and Who loveth whom the Point of the Bayan loveth, and Who loveth not whom the Point of the Bayan loveth not, and Who pardoneth him whom the Point of the Bayan pardoneth, and Who pardoneth not him whom the Point of the Bayan pardoneth not, and Who forgiveth him whom the Point of the Bayan forgiveth, and Who forgiveth not him whom the Point of the Bayan forgiveth not! I beseech Thee by Thy glory and by that which Thy knowledge encompasseth of its most glorious expression, to cause all Thy glory to descend upon the letter of the Point and upon whosoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the Knower of all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy majesty, by its most sublime expression which Thy knowledge encompasseth, to cause all Thy majesty to descend upon the letter Sin and upon whosoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the Knower of all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by Thy beauty and by that which Thy knowledge encompasseth of all Thy beauty, to cause all Thy beauty to descend upon the letter Mim and upon whosoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the Knower of all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy grandeur and by that which Thy knowledge encompasseth of its most magnificent expression, to cause all Thy grandeur to descend upon the letter Lam and upon whosoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the Knower of all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy mercy and by that which Thy knowledge encompasseth of its most extensive expression, to cause all Thy mercy to descend upon the letter Lam and upon whosoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the Knower of all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy words, by their most perfect expression with Thee and by that which Thy knowledge encompasseth, to cause all Thy words to descend upon the letter Ha and upon whosoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the Knower of all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy perfections and by that which Thy knowledge encompasseth of their most perfect expression, to cause all Thy perfections to descend upon the letter Alif and upon whosoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the Knower of all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy names and by that which Thy knowledge encompasseth of their most great expression, to cause all Thy names to descend upon the letter Lam and upon whosoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the Knower of all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy might and by that which Thy knowledge encompasseth of its mightiest expression, to cause all Thy might to descend upon the letter Alif and upon whosoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the Knower of all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy will and by that which Thy knowledge encompasseth of its most conclusive expression, to cause all Thy will to descend upon the letter Mim and upon whosoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the Knower of all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy knowledge and by that which Thy knowledge encompasseth of its most penetrating expression, to cause all Thy knowledge to descend upon the letter Nun and upon whosoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the Knower of all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy power and by that which Thy knowledge encompasseth of its most potent expression, to cause all Thy power to descend upon the letter ʿAyn and upon whosoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the Knower of all things.
O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy words and all that Thy knowledge encompasseth, from the most pleasing thereof, that Thou wouldst cause all Thy words to descend upon the letter Alif, and upon whomsoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the All-Knowing.
O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy favors and all that Thy knowledge encompasseth, from the most ancient thereof, that Thou wouldst cause all Thy favors to descend upon the letter Lam, and upon whomsoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the All-Knowing.
O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy sovereignty and all that Thy knowledge encompasseth, from the most enduring thereof, that Thou wouldst cause all Thy sovereignty to descend upon the letter Alif, and upon whomsoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the All-Knowing.
O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy dominion and all that Thy knowledge encompasseth, from the most glorious thereof, that Thou wouldst cause all Thy dominion to descend upon the letter Qaf, and upon whomsoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the All-Knowing.
O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy loftiness and all that Thy knowledge encompasseth, from the most exalted thereof, that Thou wouldst cause all Thy loftiness to descend upon the letter Dal, and upon whomsoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. Verily, Thou art the All-Knowing.
O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy signs, by the most wondrous thereof in Thy sight, that Thou wouldst cause all Thy signs at this moment to descend upon the letter Sin, and upon whomsoever seeketh shelter beneath its shade. For none, O my God, can comprehend Thy names, and were I to attempt to mention, O my God, the conditions of Thy Lordship, the oceans of the heavens and earth and all that lieth between them would be exhausted ere their mention.
Cause me then, O God, through these nine gates before the ten, to enter Thy paradise, and shield me, O God, by Thy grace and the holy dominion of Thy Lordship, from the gates of fire in its shadow. For there is no power nor strength save in Thee. In Thee have I sought refuge, protection, and reliance, and from Thee do I seek aid and illumination.
Do Thou ordain for me, O Lord, every good thing Thou hast created or wilt create, and shield me from whatever evil Thou abhorrest from among the things Thou hast caused or wilt cause to exist. In truth Thy knowledge embraceth all things. Praised be Thou, verily no God is there but Thee, and nothing whatsoever in the heavens or on the earth and all that is between them can ever thwart Thy Purpose. Indeed potent art Thou over all things.
Far be it from the sublimity of Thy Being, O my God, that anyone seek Thy loving-kindness or favor. Far be it from Thy transcendent glory that anyone entreat Thee for the evidences of Thy bestowals and tender mercy. Too high art Thou for any soul to beseech the revelation of Thy gracious providence and loving care, and too sanctified is Thy glory for anyone to beg of Thee the outpourings of Thy blessings and of Thy heavenly bounty and grace. Throughout Thy kingdom of heaven and earth, which is endowed with manifold bounties, Thou art immeasurably glorified above aught whereunto any identity could be ascribed.
All that I beg of Thee, O my God, is to enable me, ere my soul departeth from my body, to attain Thy good-pleasure, even were it granted to me for a moment tinier than the infinitesimal fraction of a mustard seed. For if it departeth while Thou art pleased with me, then I shall be free from every concern or anxiety; but if it abandoneth me while Thou art displeased with me, then, even had I wrought every good deed, none would be of any avail, and had I earned every honor and glory, none would serve to exalt me.
I earnestly beseech Thee then, O my God, to graciously bestow Thy good-pleasure upon me when Thou dost cause me to ascend unto Thee and make me appear before Thy holy presence, inasmuch as Thou hast, from everlasting, been the God of immense bounty unto the people of Thy realm, and the Lord of most excellent gifts to all that dwell in the exalted heaven of Thine omnipotence.
Grant me, O God, that which diminisheth Thee not in aught, nor profiteth Thee in aught, yet which benefiteth me before Thee shouldst Thou bestow Thy good-pleasure upon me, and harmeth me in Thy presence shouldst Thou withhold from me Thy good-pleasure. Make known unto me, O God, in every circumstance the seats of Thy command, and make me content with whatsoever Thou hast ordained for me.
Make me a dawning-place of Thy bounty and remember me when none of Thy creatures remember me, and behold me with Thy loving gaze when none of Thy servants behold me. Verily, Thou art the All-Seeing.
crumbs: BB00201: Du'ayi Sahar likulli laylin min shahri'llah

title: BB00086: Li-avvali man sa’ida ilayh (Mulla Husayn)
text:
Part 1: “This is a prayer and visitation…”
This is a prayer and visitation for the first to respond to his Lord, for the manifestations of His Self, and for the martyrs in His path.
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O God! I and all things bear witness that verily Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone, without peer. Thine is the Kingdom and the Dominion, and Thine the Glory and the Might, and Thine the Power and the Divinity, and Thine the Strength and the Ruby. Thou givest life and causest death, then causest death and givest life, and verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not. Within Thy grasp is the kingdom of all things. Thou createst whatsoever Thou willest by Thy command. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
Glorified art Thou, O God! I and all things bear witness that Thou hast ever been One God, Single, Alone, Eternal, Self-Subsisting, the All-Wise, the Just, the Holy, the Everlasting, the Eternal, the Self-Dependent. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast had no partner in sovereignty, nor any protector in all the earth save by Thy leave. Thou didst ordain the creation of all things and fashion them according to Thy Will, and Thou didst determine the measures of all things by Thy leave and decree them by Thy ordering.
Therefore, O my God, send down at this moment from every glory with which Thou hast encompassed all knowledge, and from all majesty, beauty, grandeur, light, mercy, might, word, power, strength and loftiness upon the Tree which Thou hast established from nothing by Thy Will, and raised above all Thy creation, for it responded to Thee in the primal atom by Thy Will. Therefore, O my God, at this moment shower upon it all Thy blessings, and send down upon it Thy manifestations, and ordain for it in the Kingdom of the hereafter and the present all Thy attributes, for this is an Essential Reality, a Pure Essence, an Abstract Spirit, and a Camphorated Soul, a pristine Being, which hath no will save the essence of Thy Will, and no desire save the essence of Thy Desire. How exalted is such a station in creation, whereby Thou hast made its will the essence of Thy Will and its desire the essence of Thy Desire, and through it Thou didst begin all Thy creation and through it Thou wilt return it—a true promise upon Thee, before and after. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
Therefore, O my God, bless the Letters of its Self who have prostrated themselves before Thee through it and have made their will its will in acknowledging Thy unity and in their certitude of Thy oneness, and bless those who follow its path and ascend through its will from among all souls who have turned to Thee and presented themselves before Thee. And especially bless at this moment, on the night of Friday, those who have martyred themselves in the path of Thy Cause and have ascended unto Thee through the glory of Thy grandeur, and have risen up before Thee in the stations of the glory of Thy Lordship, and have detached themselves from all things through their supplication to the Sovereign of Thy Oneness and their attainment unto the King of Thy Unity. How exalted is what Thou hast ordained for them, while they all seek it from Thee night and day yet its means are not provided to them, and they ask Thee about it in every condition yet its fulfillment is not granted to them.
Therefore, I praise Thee, O my God, on their behalf with the most exalted praise, for Thou hast answered their prayers and brought them to their ultimate desire, and I thank Thee, O my God, from their presence for having favored them with this gift and bestowed upon them this station. O my God! How lofty is it before Thee and how mighty in Thy Book! I bear witness that this is a calamity that has become universal and mighty and elevated and advanced beyond all calamities, for it has been cut off unto Thee and has prostrated itself before Thee and has shown humility before Thine eyes and has submitted before Thy hands and has surrendered to Thy Cause through that Simple Essence and Abstract Contingent Being, whereby if Thou accepteth not, none besides it would be accepted, and if Thou art not pleased, none besides it would be pleased.
Therefore, O God, ordain the reward of all who are martyred in Thy path and believe in Thee and in Thy words, unto that Camphor-Tree of the divine Being; for whatsoever they attain of good is but through the overflow of Thy bounty, and whatsoever they acquire of evil is only by the decree of Thy justice. Thus dost Thou create what Thou willest and exalt whom Thou desirest, whereof none other besides Thee hath power. Therefore, O my God, at this time do Thou chastise all Thine enemies, and the enemies of Thy Beloved, and the enemies of the Manifestations of Thyself, and the enemies of those who claim relationship to Thee. For by Thy might! I shall forever disavow all who show enmity toward those who claim relationship to Thee—how much more those whom Thou hast made Manifestations of Thyself!
Therefore, O my God, on this night send down Thy vengeance upon those who have worshipped other than Thee and who have, without any right granted by Thee, waxed proud before the Manifestations of Thy Cause. Seize them, O my God, through Thy might with a mighty seizure, for verily Thou art the All-Powerful, the Almighty. Chastise them, O my God, through Thy power with a great chastisement, for verily Thou art most severe in punishment and in retribution.
O my God! Send down Thy blessings upon the hearts that have grieved in Thy path, and upon the bodies that have endured patiently for Thy good-pleasure, and upon the souls that have yearned for Thee in their love for Thee, and upon the hearts that have ascended unto Thee through their devotion to Thee—blessings that have no equal in Thy knowledge and no likeness in Thy Book, blessings that fill Thy heaven and Thy earth and all things that have been created through Thy will. There is no God but Thee, alone with no partner, and verily he who is martyred in Thy path is a branch of the Tree which hath seven letters with Thee, and verily he who turneth unto him and believeth in him ascendeth to the highest horizon of spiritual realities. And verily whosoever hath not tasted what he hath tasted in Thy path—the acknowledgment of Thy oneness and the certitude of Thy justice and self-subsistence—hath been created from fire and unto it shall return.
Ordain, O my God, on this night which Thou hast magnified in the month which Thou hast associated with Thyself, that which is best in Thy sight for those who have believed in Thee and in Thy signs, and that which befitteth Thy justice for those who believe not in Thee nor in Thy signs. For verily Thou art most bountiful of the bountiful to those who serve Thee, and most severe of the avengers against those who veil themselves from Thee.
Unto Thee do I entrust my affairs and the affairs of those who seek Thee. Thou art sufficient unto me, O my God, to protect me from all things, while nothing sufficeth to protect from Thee. Through Thee have I become independent of all Thy creation, through Thee have I become independent of all Thy servants. Upon Thee have I relied in my coming and going, unto Thee have I turned in my worldly affairs and in my life to come.
Therefore, O my God, send down now upon my father in the most exalted horizon of Paradise that which will gladden his heart through Thy bounty, and upon those who dwell in my house that which will gladden their hearts through Thy grace, and upon those who are related to me that which will gladden their hearts through the sublimity of Thy loving-kindness and care, and upon those who purely seek me in the path of Thy love that which will gladden their hearts through the excellence of Thy bounty and mercy. For verily Thy mercy hath preceded all atoms and Thy grace hath encompassed all created things. Thou recompensest every soul according to what it hath earned. Thou art too exalted to be questioned and too glorious to be called to account.
Can there be for creation any god besides Thee, or for aught else any lord except Thee, who might deliver whom He willeth from the fire of His justice and cause whom He willeth to enter the paradise of His grace? Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. I have worshipped none but Thee, nor shall I worship any but Thee. There is no command save from Thee, no bounty save from Thy presence; no might nor power except through Thee, and unto Thee is the return.
Then turn to the Tree of Sin and say: Verily the Most Glorious Glory and Most Exalted Praise from God, Lord of the last and the first, be upon you, O Tree of Blessedness, Paradise of Refuge, the Most Remote Temple, the Greatest Sign, the Most Supreme Countenance, the Most Beautiful Face, and Station of “two bow-lengths or closer.” How can I mention You, O my Beloved, now that God has shown me the loftiness of Your station and the exaltation of Your remembrance? And how can I not mention You when You have manifested Yourself through the most perfect expressions of servitude and the most sublime and glorious manifestations of limitation?
