title: BB00086: Li-avvali man sa’ida ilayh (Mulla Husayn)
section: Part 2: “I bear witness before God and all things…”
text:
Part 2: “I bear witness before God and all things…”
I bear witness before God and all things that Your tribulation has been magnificent, majestic, momentous, and elevated, surpassing all that was decreed for those who came before. To God do we complain of what befell You from those who claim they worship God, yet who inflicted upon You and upon those who turned to God what God had never ordained for anyone before. I bear witness that although You were martyred in God’s path, through You and through what You guided all unto, the hearts of those who glorify God are alive, and the spirits of those who praise God, and the souls of those who proclaim God’s unity, and the bodies of those who magnify God.
How exalted is Your station with God and how elevated is Your rank in God’s Book! I beseech God to inflict the severest punishment upon those who acted proudly against You and transgressed against You, for He is most severe in might and in retribution. May God bestow favor upon those who were guided by Your guidance, and may He grant, through His grace and mercy, His good pleasure to those who are pleased with Your good pleasure, as befits His supreme generosity and bounty, for He is the Munificent, the Inaccessible.
Then turn to the Branches of that Letter and say: The most exalted essence of the abstracted hearts, the most splendid ornament of eternal adornments, the most impregnable manifestations of holy oneness, and the most elevated conditions of lordly glory be upon you, O Branches of the Divine Tree and Fruits of the Tree of Oneness! How exalted is your mention, your mention! How lofty is your station, your station! How sublime is your rank, your rank! How glorious is your elevation, your elevation! How excellent is your ascension, your ascension! How sweet is your detachment, your detachment! For you have detached yourselves wholly unto God your Lord and have veiled yourselves from all else through your ascension unto God your Creator.
Though you were slain in God’s path, God ceaselessly remembers you, all the angels of the heavens praise you, and the maidens of Paradise in their very essence grieve for your sake. Were I to praise the loftiness of your station, none could enumerate it save God Who created you and manifested Himself to you through your own selves. And were I to mention your tribulations, they have risen above all tribulations and transcended all calamities. Is there any essence that has not grieved for you, or any being that has not yearned for you, or any substance that has not cursed those who slew you, or any ethereal spirit that has not blessed those who blessed you?
Upon you be from your Lord that which satisfies your hearts, spirits, souls and bodies, now in the chambers of your Paradise, the seats of your immortality, the pavilions of your glory, and the innermost sanctuaries of your majesty. May God join with you those who follow your path, and may God rend asunder those who acted proudly against you and transgressed against you, for He is the Subduer over whatsoever He wishes and the Powerful over whatsoever He desires. And I shall continue to remember you until my spirit is severed from my heart. The sweetness of your remembrance shall never depart from My Being, nor shall I cease to extol you even as God hath extolled you. He, verily, is the best Protector and Helper.
Then turn unto those who have been martyred in the path of God and say: The most exalted words revealed in the Book of God, the most sublime bounties from God, the most elevated attainments in the good-pleasure of God, the most impregnable strongholds in the dominion of God, and the most glorious creation by the command of God be upon you, O manifestations of God’s mystery, daysprings of God’s Cause, rising-places of God’s countenance, settings of God’s presence, and signs of the kingdom of God’s command!
I testify that ye have ascended unto that which was loved by the first and the last, and have risen unto that which shall be attained by the manifest and the hidden. Would that I were among those for whom God hath ordained what He hath ordained for you, for ye have attained the portion of your existence and have drunk from the cup of the bounty of your Beloved, whereby ye have demonstrated in yourselves the loftiness of God’s Cause and the sublimity of God’s station in your countenance.
Through you the realities of love and detachment have become manifest in the kingdom of souls and horizons, and the essences of awe and reverence have been realized in the kingdom of earth and heaven. Upon each one of you, therefore, be from God, your Lord, that which befitteth the loftiness of His bestowal and the sublimity of His giving.
And verily the most ornate adornment, the most pure essence, the most glorious glory, the most sublime praise, and that which will satisfy your hearts in the hereafter and the former life from the Book of God be upon your first and your last, your outer and your inner being, and upon all that pertaineth to you in your journeying and your abiding.
By the likes of you should the ascending ones ascend, the aspiring ones aspire, the exalted ones be exalted, the elevated ones be elevated, and those who seek precedence seek precedence. Nay, by the glory of your Revealer, naught shall diminish from you.
How many souls have been seized upon the carpet of their glory, yet at that moment had no mention or name; but ye, though ye were seized like the most exalted one on earth upon his throne of glory, who would remember you, or present himself before your seats, or send greetings upon you from your Lord, or offer prayers upon you from your Revealer, or thank you for the exaltation of God’s Cause from your Educator?
Verily, the being that hath not glorified God in His path, even if it possessed existence, would be better in the sight of its Lord had it not existed; and the essence that is not detached unto God, even if it possessed a spirit, would be better in the sight of its Lord had it not existed. For clay returneth to its extinction and is not remembered, and that which God remembereth not endureth not.
Ye have attained unto this and have comprehended it. Therefore, upon you be the most glorious Glory of God, the most sublime Majesty of God, the most beauteous Beauty of God, the most magnificent Grandeur of God, the most luminous Light of God, the most extensive Mercy of God, the most perfect Words of God, the most great Names of God, the most mighty Might of God, the most penetrating Knowledge of God, the most potent Power of God, the most able Ability of God, the most pleasing Good-pleasure of God, the most enduring Authority of God, the most excellent Dominion of God, the most exalted Sublimity of God, the most ancient Favor of God, the most generous Signs of God, and the most bountiful Grace of God.
None shall approach Your sacred threshold, for You have offered up Your souls in the path of Your Lord. Nay, by the glory of Him Who created you and ordained for you this exalted station and lofty rank! All love you for the sake of God, and all pray for you seeking God’s good pleasure. I testify before God and all things that you abide in the pavilions of Ridvan with your Lord in joy, and in the inmost sanctuaries of holiness and grandeur you receive sustenance from God, your Lord. There is no lofty and impregnable grace, nor towering and sublime bounty, but that it descends upon your threshold and appears before you. This is from what God has initiated regarding you through His praise of you. And whomsoever God initiates with a mention from His presence, all shall initiate; and upon whomsoever God bestows mention in His Cause, if it be not altered from His presence, then all shall make mention.
Say: Verily, the Glory is the most pure Embellishment and the most excellent Essence from God—exalted and glorified be His mention—and from the Manifestations of His Cause, and the examples of His names, and the evidence of the kingdom of His majesty. Upon you, O sanctified essence, illumined reality, beloved soul, and content being, who has soared unto God and attained unto the heights of what God has ordained for those who ascend unto Him and are elevated through Him! Blessed be your seat with God, for you have attained, and exalted be what you have achieved from the Book of God. This is from God’s grace upon you and upon your father and upon your mother and upon your brother, wherein you are mentioned with the mention of God—he whom God mentions thereby, all shall mention him, and he whom God raises to the highest horizon through His grace, all shall be annihilated before Him.

title: BB00275: Ziyarat for the last [to believe]
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Visitation for the last [to ascend], upon him be the Glory of God, the Sovereign, the Subduer
Praise be to God, besides Whom there is no other god, the Most Constraining, the Most Constraining! And verily all glory be from God upon His Most Luminous, Most Luminous Light! And then, when thou hast attained unto that which God hath ordained for thee through the recognition of that Most Great, Most Great, Most Great Name, and that Most Mighty, Most Mighty, Most Mighty Remembrance, and that Most Exalted, Most Exalted, Most Exalted Glory, and that Most Splendid, Most Splendid, Most Splendid Praise, then purify thy inner and outer being from all that thou hast witnessed in the Bayan regarding the commandments of thy Lord. Then when thou standest at the First Gate, glorify God nineteen times, then at the Second Gate eighteen times, then at the Third Gate seventeen times, then at the Fourth Gate sixteen times, then at the Fifth Gate fifteen times. There say:
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I and all things testify that Thou art God, that there is no God but Thee, alone with no partner, and I bear witness that the Point of the Bayan is the Manifestation of Thy Self, Who hath revealed what Thou didst desire of Thy religion through what Thou didst send down of Thy verses. Verily, I testify, and all things with me, that my very being hath borne witness to that which it hath witnessed, and my reality likewise, and my self likewise, and my identity likewise. I turn unto Thee through the First Vahid, then through all Thy Most Beautiful Names and Thy Most Exalted Examples in their essence, beseeching from Thy grace, knocking at the door of Thy bounty, that Thou mayest cause me to enter the sanctuary of Thy Name ʿthe Other’ from the First Vahid, which Thou hast established through the Word of the Point of the Bayan, through that in which he believed and unto which he turned in what was ordained in existence.
Then let me seek permission from all Thy names and the exponents of Thy sovereignty. Sufficient is it that Thou hast permitted me to attain Thy presence before Thy Name and hast impelled me through what Thou hast commanded me to cast myself before the sign of Thy countenance. Praise be unto Thee for knowledge of Him, and glory be unto Thee for having caused me to know His exaltation, the sublimity of His glory, the elevation of His radiance, the inviolability of His good-pleasure, the joy of His delight and His names. Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee! Glory be unto Thee! Verily, I am of those who seek permission.
Then prostrate thyself and kiss whatever thou canst reach. And if the essences of the cherubim have multiplied at that Gate and the drops of the water of love have surged at that Path, then sufficient for thee is one mention. When thou hast entered, stand at the threshold and say “God is Most Manifest” nineteen times. Then say:
Verily, of the Glory of God, He is the Most Glorious; and of the Majesty of God, He is the Most Majestic; and of the Beauty of God, He is the Most Beautiful; and of the Grandeur of God, He is the Most Grand; and of the Light of God, He is the Most Luminous; and of the Mercy of God, He is the Most All-Encompassing; and of the Names of God, He is the Most Great; and of the Might of God, He is the Most Mighty; and of the Will of God, He is the Most Decisive; and of the Knowledge of God, He is the Most Penetrating; and of the Power of God, He is the Most Powerful; and of the Word of God, He is the Most Pleasing; and of the Causes of God, He is the Most Beloved and Most Invincible; and of the Honor of God, He is the Most Honorable; and of the Sovereignty of God, He is the Most Spiritual; and of the Dominion of God, He is the Most Glorious; and of the Exaltation of God, He is the Most Exalted; and of the Favors of God, He is the Most Ancient; and of the Signs of God, He is the Most Wondrous; and of the Grace of God, He is the Most Gracious; and of the Generosity of God, He is the Most Generous; and of the Bestowals of God, He is the Most Felicitous; and of the Manifestations of God, He is the Most Manifest; and of the Revelations of God, He is the Most Evident; and of the Proofs of God, He is the Most Steadfast; and of the Clear Signs of God, He is the Most Elevated.
Upon thee and upon the Letters that have preceded thee and upon those who have followed thee—all guides unto God thy Lord, witnesses in God thy Creator, prostrate before God through thy Countenance, servants of God through thy Beauty, and preservers of the Cause of God through thy guidance. I bear witness before God and all things that thou hast glorified God thy Lord as befitteth what God hath created within thee, and thou hast praised God thy Creator as befitteth what God hath revealed unto thee through thee, and thou hast unified God thy Revealer as befitteth what He hath ordained within thee, and thou hast magnified God Who praiseth thee as befitteth what He hath encompassed through His knowledge within thee, and thou hast exalted the Cause of God as much as thou wast able. Thus hast thou ascended, and there is none like thee ascending in creation, and thou hast drawn nigh, and there is none like thee in drawing nigh.
By My glory! Thy nearness shall not turn Me away from Thy loftiness, nor shall Thy loftiness veil Me from Thy nearness. Thy seat is in the highest chambers of paradise. Verily Thou beholdest those who dwell in the kingdom of the heavens and of the earth and that which lieth between them, and bearest witness unto those whom God hath created in the kingdom of His command and of His creation and all that is beneath them. Thou hast ever gazed upon Me and sacrificed thyself for Me, and sought forgiveness from God, thy Lord, for those who are detached from all else save Him. This is a fruit in the Book of God for him who perceiveth it. No justice can compare with this, and this is a gift from God whereto nothing can be likened. Verily Thou, and numbers, and the First One, and all that God, exalted be His glory, hath reckoned, God hath made but as a seal upon the hand of Him Whom God shall make manifest, exalted be His mention. He turneth it as He pleaseth, by whatsoever He pleaseth, for whatsoever He pleaseth. He is, in truth, the Help in Peril, the Most High, the Most Glorious.
It sufficeth Thee in the kingdom of the heavens and of the earth and whatsoever lieth between them when He willeth to descend upon Thy court and to exalt Thy station through His holy sovereignty, or to mention Thee with praise from His presence, for God hath made no other bounty like unto this, nor any exaltation comparable to this. This is what God, Thy Lord, hath promised Thee in Thy beginning and in Thine end, and hath sent down upon Thee in Thy beginning what Thou seest in Thine end. He is, in truth, the One, the Manifest. Therefore make mention from there, in Thy presence, of the names of God and His loved ones, servants who have inherited that which was created in paradise, who have found solace in what was originated in the Bayan, and who have delighted in that which their hearts, their spirits, their souls and their bodies desired in the highest chambers of paradise, through what they hope for from God’s grace and bounty. He is, verily, the Help in Peril, the All-Bountiful.

title: BB00246: Ziyarat for the letters of unity, on Friday
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy!
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I and all things bear witness on this night which Thou hast magnified, honored, sanctified and exalted, and upon which Thou hast bestowed Thy remembrance, and wherein Thou didst send down Thy mercy and didst open the gates of Thy forgiveness, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thine is the kingdom and the heavenly dominion, Thine the might and the divine power, Thine the strength and the celestial gems, Thine the sovereignty and the earthly realm, Thine the glory and the majesty, Thine the countenance and the beauty, Thine the presence and the perfection, Thine the mercy and bounty, Thine the authority and sublimity, Thine the grandeur and the invincibility, Thine the power and the exaltation, Thine the greatness and the favors, Thine the proofs and the examples, Thine the joy and the gladness, Thine the grandeur and the detachment from all that Thou hast created or wilt create.
Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee. Thine is all that is in the heights unto the uttermost reaches of the depths. All things glorify Thee in the truth of Thy unity, all things prostrate before Thee in the truth of Thy light-giving power, all things sanctify Thee in the truth of Thy manifestation, all things testify to Thy oneness in the truth of Thy singleness, all things magnify Thee in the truth of Thine eternity, all things love to meet Thee in the truth of Thy lovingness, all things are severed unto the places of knowing Thee through the signs of Thy sovereignty. I and all things bear witness that Thou givest life and causeth death, then causeth death and givest life, and that Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not, the Sovereign Who passeth not away, the Just Who wrongeth not, the King Who changeth not, the One from Whose grasp nothing escapeth, whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
O my God! Do Thou send down in this mighty night during Thy days, which Thou hast attributed to Thyself and honored in Thy presence, upon the hearts of them that glorify Thee, and their spirits, their souls and their bodies, and all that hath ascended unto Thee and all that liveth before Thee, from all Thy glory its most glorious, from all Thy majesty its most majestic, from all Thy beauty its most beautiful, from all Thy grandeur its most grand, from all Thy light its most luminous, from all Thy mercy its most extensive, from all Thy words their most perfect, from all Thy names their most great, from all Thy might its most mighty, from all Thy will its most conclusive, from all Thy knowledge its most penetrating, from all Thy power its most enduring, from all Thy utterance its most pleasing, from all Thy causes those most beloved by Thee and most unapproachable before Thee, from all Thy honor its most honorable, from all Thy dominion its most lasting, from all Thy kingdom its most excellent, from all Thy loftiness its most elevated, from all Thy bestowals its most ancient, and from all that Thou hast loved or wilt love that which hath no equal, no peer, no likeness, no companion and no similitude, for Thou art our God and the God of all things, our Originator and the Originator of all things, our Creator and the Creator of all things, our Ordainer and the Ordainer of all things, our Fashioner and the Fashioner of all things.
Do Thou therefore preserve us, O my God, through Thy might and power and glory and greatness and sovereignty and dominion and self-subsistence, from that which grieveth us, and show us that whereby our hearts and our spirits and our souls and our bodies may find tranquility, through Thy grace, then Thy generosity, then Thy tender mercy, then Thy kindness, then Thy mercy, then Thy gift, then Thy beneficence. For verily Thou art the Knower of all things, and the Powerful over all things, and the Almighty above all things, and the Invincible over all things. Thou hast not created any grief for anyone except that Thou hast created with it some gladness.
I testify to my joy after having recognized my own self through recognition of Thee and having recited Thy verses through Thy clear proofs. And if I experienced sorrow in Thy path, yet have I witnessed joy in Thy path. Therefore praise be unto Thee, O my God, for all that Thou hast ordained and decreed, and thanks be unto Thee, O my Lord, for what Thou hast sent down and executed.
Thou art the One Worshipped alone, there is no God but Thee. Thou art the One Intended alone, there is no God but Thee. Thou art the One Prostrated to alone, there is no God but Thee. Thou art the One Praised alone, there is no God but Thee. Thou art the One Existing alone, there is no God but Thee. Thou seest but art not seen, and verily Thou art in the Most Exalted Horizon, the Cleaver of the grain and the date-stone. Unto Thee belongeth whatsoever is in the heights and whatsoever is in the lowest depths. Therefore, O my God, send down at this moment upon everyone whose essence hath ascended unto Thee through their relationship to me, or whose being hath remained in Thy good-pleasure through their connection to all, Thy forgiveness, Thy good-pleasure, Thy grace, Thy favor, Thy generosity and Thy glory. Verily, Thou art possessed of great bounty.
Then turn and say, when thou art like on such a night in the presence of the Letters of the One or the Guides of God’s Cause, and say: From the splendor of God, His most splendid; from the majesty of God, His most majestic; from the beauty of God, His most beautiful; from the grandeur of God, His most grand; from the light of God, His most luminous; from the mercy of God, His most extensive; from the words of God, His most perfect; from the signs of God, His most mighty; from the names of God, His most great; from the Will of God, His most decisive; from the knowledge of God, His most penetrating; from the power of God, His most powerful; from the utterance of God, His most pleasing; from the questions of God, His most beloved and most impregnable; from the nobility of God, His most noble; from the sovereignty of God, His most enduring; from the dominion of God, His most glorious; from the exaltation of God, His most exalted; and from all the names of God and His attributes, upon you be that which befitteth God, exalted be His glory, and that which He deserveth through the Manifestations of His Cause and His power.
I testify that through you have appeared the essences of glorification, and have been exalted the realities of sanctification, and have been established the spirits of unity, and have been settled the identities of magnification, and have been elevated the manifestations of grandeur unto God Who created you, sustained you, caused you to die, gave you life, and raised you from the resting-places of your hearts. God hath never ceased to send down upon you from all His bounty and grace, and from all His generosity and favor. The rememberers shall remember you and all the God-fearing shall weep for you. You are the first and the last, you are the outer and the inner, you are the most elevated and most exalted, you are the most impregnable and most mighty.
Blessed be the day when He Whom God shall make manifest, exalted be His mention, shall honor your land with His footsteps when He willeth, and your resting-places with the radiance of His lights, and your essences with the signs of His glory. That is a day which none can avert from God; all shall be presented before God their Lord. God hath not created any bounty greater for you than His mention of you through His good-pleasure, and God hath not created any fire more remote than the absence of the mention of His good-pleasure by anyone, for in the shadow of this is inscribed every good, and in the shadow of this is that which God loveth not to mention. Therefore seek assistance through the name of your Lord, the Most Merciful, from that which ye love not to know, or to comprehend in knowledge, or to hear, or to see, or to witness, or to speak, or to write, for God will surely protect you through His command, as He hath power over all things.
crumbs: BB00246: Ziyarat for the letters of unity, on Friday

title: BB00169: Du’a’ li’lladhina ’araju
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Thou hast ever been the Creator of all things, the Provider of all things, the Giver of life and the Ordainer of death unto all things, the Beloved of all that have loved Thee. Thou hast ever been one, single, peerless, self-subsisting, eternal, living, all-sustaining, just, and sovereign. Thou hast taken unto Thyself neither consort nor child, nor hast Thou any partner in Thy dominion, nor any protector upon earth save by Thy leave. By Thy power didst Thou bring into being the creation of all things, and by Thy might didst Thou ordain each one according to Thy decree. By Thy Will didst Thou fashion the form of all that hath been created, and by that same Will didst Thou give unto each its image and proportion.
O Thou Whose dominion is exalted above the kingdoms of all possible beings, Whose Will shineth resplendent above the existence of all created things, Whose Decree holdeth sway over whatsoever is in the heavens and on the earth, and Whose command is uplifted above all that hath come to be or shall be! O Thou Whose permission none can attain save by Thy bounty, and Whose knowledge encompasseth all things, bearing witness unto Thy creatures, and Whose might doeth whatsoever Thou willest by a word of Thine!
I beseech Thee, before the breaking of dawn in that month which Thou hast ascribed unto Thyself, clothed with the vesture of Thy might, and adorned with the raiment of Thy grace—wherein Thou didst send down the tokens of Thy Revelation and ordain in one of its nights the measures of Thine invention—that Thou wouldst cause to descend upon the hearts that have ascended unto Thee the mysteries befitting the loftiness of Thy praise; upon the spirits that have winged their flight to Thy presence the adorations consonant with the sublimity of Thy glory; upon the souls that have melted in the path of Thy love the recognitions meet for the majesty of Thy unity; and upon the bodies that have turned wholly unto Thee, inwardly and outwardly, the exultations worthy of the greatness of Thy magnification.
Send down, then, upon those hallowed temples and exalted dawning-places that which shall gladden their eyes in the highest of the gardens of Ria¸van and the brightest of the seats of Paradise. For we have ever been the objects of Thy … bounty, and the recipients of Thy … favor, and the trophies Thou bestowest upon those who have acknowledged Thy unity are the evidences of Thy mercy, while the mention of whatsoever pertaineth unto Thee is exalted above all that can be mentioned. Blessed, then, is the dust that is content with Thy good-pleasure and is ennobled by ascription unto Thee through Thy permanence.
Therefore, I entreat Thee, O my God, by Thyself—for beside Thee there is none to ask—by Him who hath known Thee, that Thou wouldst send down what Thou lovest upon all who have ascended unto Thee through the Bayan from the first moment of its descent until the hour when the verses of Thy Manifestation shall appear; upon those who have sorrowed in Thy path; upon those who have striven, bearing Thy tokens in the path of Thy love and guidance.
How numerous the souls raised to life who were exposed to dire humiliation in Thy Path for exalting Thy Word and for glorifying Thy divine Unity! How profuse the blood that hath been shed for the sake of Thy Faith to vindicate the authenticity of Thy divine Mission and to celebrate Thy praise! How vast the possessions that were wrongfully seized in the Path of Thy love in order to affirm the loftiness of Thy sanctity and to extol Thy glorious Name! How many the feet that have trodden upon the dust in order to magnify Thy holy Word and to extol Thy glory! How innumerable the voices that were raised in lamentation, the hearts that were struck with terror, the grievous woes that none other than Thee can reckon, and the adversities and afflictions that remain inscrutable to anyone except Thyself; all this to establish, O my God, the loftiness of Thy sanctity and to demonstrate the transcendent character of Thy glory.
These decrees were ordained by Thee so that all created things might bear witness that they have been brought into being for the sake of naught else but Thee. Thou hast withheld from them the things that bring tranquillity to their hearts, that they might know of a certainty that whatever is associated with Thy holy Being is far superior to and exalted above aught else that would satisfy them; inasmuch as Thine indomitable power pervadeth all things, and nothing can ever frustrate it. Indeed Thou hast caused these momentous happenings to come to pass that those who are endued with perception may readily recognize that they were ordained by Thee to demonstrate the loftiness of Thy divine Unity and to affirm the exaltation of Thy sanctity….
For if Thou wert pleased, O my Lord, to cause Thy decree to descend even upon him who was the most beloved of Thy creation and the nearest of the former saints unto Thy presence, it would be but for the uplifting of the Tree of Thy Oneness, the elevation of the canopy of Thy Eternity, the exaltation of the standard of Thy Singleness, and the appearance of the fruits of Thy Self-subsisting Being. How then could that loftiness, that glory and majesty, be unbefitting unto any other in Thy sight?
Thine are, O my Lord, the essential decrees of existence in the purity of their simplicity and the calamities of detachment in the fragrance of their camphor-like whiteness—each bereft of independent being save in so far as it proveth Thy sanctity, and each devoid of self-identity save as it testifieth to the exaltation of Thy unity. For had these not appeared, all would have returned to dust and clay; whence then could aught yield fruit or make mention of Thee in the realms Thou hast created? How could any soul remember Thee with the glances of Thy sanctified Lordship, or cause Thy Name to descend amid the names of the manifestations of Thy might?
Glorified art Thou! Even as Solomon whom Thou didst cause to possess the dominion of the earth—he had no remembrance save Thy remembrance of him; so likewise, whosoever is made to reign over men without Thy sanction shall have no portion but Thy curse pronounced aforetime in Thy Book. Naught remaineth of either save Thy praise and Thy thanksgiving, wherein are all the delights of Paradise; for no garden is higher than that, nor fragrance more beauteous than its perfume. In Thy chastisement is naught but justice, and in Thy pardon naught but mercy; there is no torment greater than remoteness from Thee, nor felicity sweeter than nearness unto Thy favor.
I therefore beseech Thee, O my God, to ordain for whosoever hath believed in the Bayan Thy good-pleasure; for if Thou shouldst sustain Thy servant throughout his life with the tender flesh of birds, yet when his soul is taken from his body he would find no delight therein. And if Thou shouldst allot unto him the leaves of trees to eat, yet when his spirit departeth he would find no pain therein. For what availeth aught save Thy good-pleasure, and what harmeth aught save Thy wrath and rejection?
Have mercy, then, O my God, upon all who have embraced the Bayan, for those who are deprived thereof abide in the fire and have no station before Thee. Bestow, moreover, upon the dwellers of that Paradise such bounty that their gaze shall not be drawn to aught that perisheth or changeth, but rather to that which abideth with Thee—that is, the relation of the servant to Thy good-pleasure and his steadfastness in the path of Thy love and meeting. There is no power nor might save in Thee, O Lord of might and glory, of majesty and beauty, of authority and perfection, of sovereignty and exaltation, of mercy and bounty, of dominion and justice, of tenderness and grace, of similitude and exemplarity!
Thou beholdest, O my God, all things testifying unto Thee that beside Thee there was no being endowed with mention save through Thy remembrance of it, nor any existence possessed of reality save through Thy causing it to exist by Thy will. No glory is there save in Thy good-pleasure, no beauty save in Thy meeting. Therefore do I entreat Thee, O my Beloved, Who hast ever been and wilt ever remain, to make mention of me before Thy presence with a remembrance none knoweth save Thee; for none comprehendeth the stations of Thy remembrance but Thee Thyself. Whoso remembereth Thee through the Point of the Bayan, that one hath indeed remembered Thee; whoso hath borne witness unto that Reality, that one hath verily borne witness unto Thee; whoso hath been well-pleasing unto Thee, that one art Thou pleased withal; and whoso hast been deprived of Thy leave, him hast Thou debarred by Thine own decree.
For verily, O my God, by Thy Essence Thou art united with naught; by Thy Being Thou art comprehended by naught; by Thy sanctity Thou art glorified by naught; by Thy simplicity Thou art thanked by naught; by Thy Self Thou art known by naught—for all besides Thee are veiled in the garb of limitation in the realm of origination, whereas Thou art exalted above all mention in the sublimity of invention and the majesty of restraint.
Nay rather, whatsoever Thy Manifestation doeth, that hast Thou done; whatsoever Thy Manifestation commandeth, that hast Thou commanded. Verily, they are one reality—if it dawn, it hath no beginning; if it set, it hath no equal. It is one essence that abideth in the firmament of glory, without peer or likeness. Its similitude before Thee is as the sun—Thou hast created it for the manifestation of Thy splendour.
Glorified art Thou above all that have known Thee! I beg forgiveness of Thee for all with which I have praised Thee, and turn repentant unto Thee for all wherewith I have magnified Thee, for whatsoever is mine is unworthy to be ascribed unto Thee. Pardon me, O my God, through Thy bounty, Thy grace, Thy generosity, Thy tenderness, Thy mercy, Thy compassion, and Thy munificence; for whatsoever is attributed unto Thee—were it but a single atom—would transcend all being by reason of its association with Thee.
And I bear witness, O my God, and all things bear witness, that there is no power nor strength save in Thee, the Almighty, the All-Compelling, the Ever-Abiding.

title: BB00109: Du’ayi Laylatu aula min Shahri’llah
text:
Part 1: “Glorified art Thou, O my God! This…”
In the name of God, the Most Invincible, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O my God! This is a night which Thou hast magnified, honored, exalted, adorned and sanctified by associating it with Thyself. Thou hast caused to appear therein a sign that proclaimeth it to be a wondrous night of a wondrous month, which Thou hast favored, honored, exalted, magnified, illumined, elevated and loved. Therein do those who call upon Thee and glorify Thee in the watches of the night and the hours of the day, and Thou hast given leave to the angels to raise unto Thee the voices of Thy believing servants, Thy assured ones, Thy chosen ones, Thy beloved ones and those who are detached from all else save Thee.
How exalted, O my God, is Thy gift to those who call upon Thee! How invincible, O my Beloved, is Thy bounty to those who are devoted to Thee! Unto Thee boweth down in worship whatsoever is in the heavens and on the earth and all that lieth between them, and unto Thee glorifieth whatsoever is in the kingdom of command and creation and all that is beneath them. I testify and am assured that Thou canst never be attributed with any trait of Thy creation or any characteristic of Thy servants. When I describe Thee, O my God, as the Most Merciful in the realms of pardon and forgiveness, that attribute falls short of the mercy Thou hast created in the essence of Thy creation, for the mercy attributed to Thee hath no equal. And when I remember Thee, O my God, as the Most Severe in the realms of chastisement and tribulation, that too falls short of how I have described Thee, for it cannot be compared to the severity of Thy creation.
And if I say, O my God, that Thou art the Most Generous of the generous, or the Nearest of the near, or the Most Hearing of those who hear, or the Most Seeing of those who see, or the Swiftest in reckoning, or the Most Truthful of those who speak—all of these cut off what is beneath Thee from being associated with Thee. Thy names have ever been exalted above all names, and Thy attributes have ever been elevated above all similitudes and attributes.
Exalted is Thy Being, O my God, above the mention of similitudes and allusions, or description through geometry and attributes. For all names are but signs of the sovereignty of Thy Self-Subsistence, yet Thou art free from them, transcendent above them, manifesting them through their own essence. Even were I to describe Thee through the highest essences of geometry and attributes, these would be but signs of the Sovereign of Thy Holiness and Glory, yet they would still be cut off from attaining unto Thy presence, Thy exaltation, Thy might, and the meeting with Thee.
O Thou Who existed before all things in independence, and through Whose manifestation all things came to be, and Who remaineth after all things in unattainability, and Who art with all things in exaltation! Thou seest all Thy creation and hearest those who call upon Thee on this most exalted night, each according to their own essence and how Thou hast manifested Thyself unto them. They turn toward Thee and worship Thee, yet exalted is Thy Being above accepting praise from one who knoweth not the Manifestation of Thy Countenance, or answering the prayer of one who is not assured of the Image of Thy Presence, for none can ascend unto Thee save through Him.
How many are Thy servants, O my God, who call upon Thee with humility, supplication, submissiveness and detachment, yet their prayers rise not beyond their own ears. Though Thou punish them not, Thou answereth them not, for they have heard Thy verses from Thy Manifestation and witnessed the wonders of Thy words from Thy Presence, yet they are veiled by that which profiteth them not with Thee. Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee! How many are the pens of those who call upon Thee, worship Thee, glorify Thee, bow before Thee, magnify Thee and are devoted to Thee in such wise that were I now to […]
Glorified art Thou! Glorified art Thou by the supreme exaltation of Thy power and transcendence! Thou hast created naught except that it may know Thy oneness, yet how can all things recognize Thy unity when they know not the Dawning-Place of Thy oneness, nor recognize the Dayspring of Thy sanctity, nor comprehend the Source of Thy glorification? Can they, O my God, offer any praise before Thee, or possess any worth in Thy presence? Nay, by Thy glory! Verily, by Thy might, I shall glorify Thee with certitude that there is no God but Thee, and I shall praise Thee with sincerity that there is no God but Thee, and I shall proclaim Thy unity in prostration before Thee that there is no God but Thee, and I shall magnify Thee in humble submission that there is no God but Thee, being certain of the manifestations of Thy Cause and beholding the Daysprings of Thy glory. For Thou art the Manifest, and none is manifest besides Thee; Thou art the Subduer, and none subdues besides Thee; Thou art the Exalted, and none is exalted besides Thee; Thou art the Inaccessible, and none is inaccessible besides Thee.
Glorified art Thou above whatsoever may glorify Thee or hath glorified Thee! Glorified art Thou above that any should praise Thee or hath praised Thee! Glorified art Thou above that any should proclaim Thy unity or hath proclaimed Thy unity! Glorified art Thou above that any should magnify Thee or hath magnified Thee! The sweet-scented breezes of the sanctity of Thy sovereign Lordship have ever drawn the hearts of Thy loved ones to the source of the glory of Thy countenance, and the rays of the light of Thy beauty ever shine upon those who glorify Thee, drawing them to the atmosphere of Thy bounty and grace.
O my God! No mercy hath been joined with Thy mercy through which I might seek intercession with Thee, no bounty with Thy bounty through which I might beseech Thee, no generosity with Thy generosity through which I might make my petition to Thee, no grace with Thy grace through which I might seek refuge with Thee, and no forgiveness with Thy forgiveness through which I might implore Thy aid. Thou seest what creation deserveth of poverty and evanescence, and Thou witnessest what it meriteth of glory and perpetuity. Thy mercy hath perfected all created things, and Thy proof hath reached all beings. The effulgence that shineth from Thy words hath dominated all who dwell in the kingdom of names and attributes.
Therefore, O my God, I beseech Thee by those who know Thee and worship Thee, by those who glorify Thee and bear witness to Thee, and by those who magnify Thee and call upon Thee, that Thou make me one of those upon whom Thou hast gazed at the dawning of this Night, and whose mention and praise Thou hast loved to hear, and upon whom Thou hast bestowed Thy grace and bounty, and whose name Thou hast loved to remember among the manifestations of Thy glory and sovereignty, and for whom Thou hast ordained from Thy grace and bounty that whereby he may be independent of all else besides Thee.
O my God! If I ask Thee about Thy glory, verily Thou art more exalted than that! If I ask Thee about Thy majesty, verily Thou art greater than that! If I ask Thee about Thy beauty, verily Thou art more inaccessible than that! If I ask Thee about Thy grandeur, verily Thou art more elevated than that! If I ask Thee about Thy light, verily Thou art more powerful than that! Yea, O my God, I ask Thee by Thyself, for there is no glory equal to Thy justice, no majesty comparable to Thee, no beauty similar to Thee, no grandeur like unto Thee, and no light resembling Thee. Nothing in the heavens or on the earth or between them can be hidden from Thy knowledge, and nothing in the kingdom of command or creation or below them can frustrate Thee.

title: BB00109: Du’ayi Laylatu aula min Shahri’llah
section: Part 2: “Therefore, O God, send down upon the hearts…”
text:
Part 2: “Therefore, O God, send down upon the hearts…”
Therefore, O God, send down upon the hearts that have ascended unto Thee that which beseemeth the loftiness of Thy glorification, and upon the spirits that have turned unto Thee that which beseemeth the sublimity of Thy praise, and upon the souls that have risen unto Thee that which beseemeth the inaccessibility of Thy unity, and upon those that became seized with rapture in Thy path and ascended unto the Most Exalted Horizon … that which befitteth the exaltation of Thy glorification, and that Thou mayest send down upon … from the Tree of Thy unity that which befitteth the sublimity of Thy grace, Thy bounty, Thy generosity and Thy favor, and that Thou mayest manifest that whereby Thou hast willed to make manifest Thy religion, and that Thou mayest aid that whereby Thou hast willed to manifest and …, and that Thou mayest seize through Thy might that which Thou hast ordained to seize for the exaltation of Thy sanctification, and that Thou mayest destroy whom Thou hast willed to destroy for the exaltation of Thy glorification, and that Thou mayest abase whom Thou hast willed to abase for the invincibility of Thy glorification, and that Thou mayest forsake whom Thou hast willed to forsake for the jubilation of the light of Thy sanctification, and that Thou mayest remove from the earth whom Thou hast willed to remove for the sovereignty of Thy divine dominion and oneness.
For I, O my God, by Thy glory, seek Thy protection from all the fire, and I beseech Thee of Thy grace concerning what Thou hast ordained in all of Paradise. For Thy retribution shall never cease from this through what … hath earned and its people, and Thy mercy shall never cease from this through what itself and those within it have prostrated. Thou art He Who hath subdued through the sovereignty of Thy dominion all created things, until Thou didst possess the sovereigns through the sovereignty of Thy dominion with power and independence. And Thou art He Who hath shown Thy might through the holy kingdom … above all contingent things, until Thou didst subject every possessor of sovereignty through Thy glory and grandeur and the kingdom of Thy mighty dominion with divinity and invincibility.
O my God, Thou beholdest the stations of those who call upon Thee and hast power over the exaltation of their souls and their stations. Therefore, O God, hasten in this through that which Thy Being deserveth, not through what the souls of Thy loved ones deserve, for through Thy desert every possessor of right receiveth his right and every possessor of love beholdeth what he loveth. Therefore I beseech Thee, O God, by the merit of Thy Lordship and the independence of Thy divine dominion, that Thou mayest utterly annihilate the tree of negation and send down upon it Thy retribution in every condition, and that Thou mayest preserve the tree of Thy oneness and send down upon it that which befitteth the sublimity of Thy gracious favor and the exaltation of Thy sovereignty. For were the veil to be lifted from the insight of those in the fire, they would desire naught save what Thou hast ordained for them, and were it lifted from the insight of those in Paradise, they would desire naught save what Thou hast ordained for them. This hath never ceased … and perisheth, and this shall never cease to endure and be exalted. This is from the command of God; verily He hath power over all things.
And bless, O God, the Point of the Bayan and whatsoever is related unto it, and exalt it, O my God, through Thine exaltation, and magnify it, O my God, through Thy grandeur, and glorify it, O my God, through Thy glory, and strengthen it, O my God, through Thy might, and empower it, O my God, through Thy sovereignty, and grant unto it that which will gladden its heart and beyond what will please it and beyond what it desireth from the treasuries of the wonders of Thy divine dominion and the repositories of the mystery of Thy holiness, for there is no equal to Thy bounty.
And ordain, O God, for the letters of its self, eighteen before ten, whatsoever Thou hast ordained for it of every good thing which Thy knowledge hath encompassed, and upon all the manifestations of its names and the dawning-places of its likenesses, and upon those who have sought shelter in its shade from among the first and the last, the outward and the inward. For there was not at that time upon the earth any who would worship Thee in truth except these, nor prostrate before Thee in truth except these, nor glorify Thee in truth except these, nor praise Thee in truth except these, nor testify to Thy unity in truth except these, nor … in truth except these! By Thy might, these are none other than these! None recite Thy Book except these, none seek Thy good-pleasure except these, none succeed to Thy justice except these, none […] Thy presence except these, none raise Thy remembrance except these, none make manifest Thy Cause except these, none aid Thy Faith except these, none establish Thy Word except these.
O God, at this time, through Thy grace, grant that which will cause this Tree to reach its loftiest heights and attain its uttermost ascendancy, and to witness what Thou hast ordained in its glory and to testify to what Thou hast decreed for its exaltation. And cause its eyes to be gladdened by what Thou hast ordained for it from the treasuries of Thy bestowals and the heights of Thy gifts, for all things besides Thee are poor before Thee and unto Thee, and whatsoever is other than Thee are Thy creatures and Thy servants before Thee. Grant unto me, O my God, and unto them that love me and them that are under my authority, whether of the past or yet to come until the Day of Resurrection, that which beseemeth the ascendancy of the sovereignty of Thy Self-Subsistence, and the inaccessibility of the kingdom of Thy Divine Unity, and the joy of the carpet of the glory of Thy Oneness. For Thy gifts have no equal, neither before nor after, and Thy bounties have no likeness, neither in the kingdom of command nor of creation.
Verily Thou art the All-Bountiful, the All-Knowing. Verily Thou art the Munificent, the Near One. Verily Thou art the Invincible, the All-Seeing. Verily Thou art the Bestower, the Most Generous. Verily Thou art the All-Merciful, the Most Kind. There is no power nor strength except through Thee, and Thou hast encompassed all things with Thy knowledge.

title: BB00080: Ziyarat for the first to believe, on the Day of ’Arafa
text:
Part 1: “First Visitation…”
First Visitation
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy!
God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him. His are the most excellent names. All that are in the heavens and on the earth and whatsoever lieth between them sing His praise. There is none other God but Him, the Sovereign, the Self-Subsisting.
And verily the Glory from God was upon the Throne of Reality in the Qur’an, wherein all who are in the heavens and who are on the earth and whatsoever lieth between them were illumined by the light of His Being. And among His effulgences is the knowledge of that Day which He hath mentioned as the Day of Arafat. Knowest thou what Arafat is? It is he whom every soul had known aforetime in the Qur’an as the One Who declareth: “There is no God but I, the Mighty, the Well-Beloved.”
Behold then all who profess the religion of Muhammad—verily each one knoweth Him, after the words “There is no God but God,” as “Muhammad is the Apostle of God” from time immemorial. And no soul knew Him save for the Day when God would raise Him from His resting-place, that all things might know Him. Hast thou known Him, or hath anyone? This is a fruit that hath grown from the Tree of Knowledge, among whose attributes is the recognition of that Day.
Look from the beginning that hath no beginning, and trace all this back to the Day of Muhammad. Then behold what was manifested through Muhammad: Among the signs of His Revelation was the Sacred House, around which seventy thousand souls would circumambulate in those days. And among the signs of His Revelation was His sacred resting-place—behold how many of God’s creatures ascend thereto and serve there in humility.
And among the signs of His Revelation were Ali, then Fatimih, then Hasan, then Husayn, then Ali son of Husayn, then Muhammad son of Ali, then Ja’far son of Muhammad, then Musa son of Ja’far, then Ali son of Musa, then Muhammad son of Ali, then Ali son of Muhammad, then Hasan son of ʿAli, then the Proof, then the Manifestations of the letter Ha’. How exalted were these stations raised for the revelation of His Self, and how many servants ascend hoping for His grace and bounty!
And among the signs of His Revelation is Prayer—can anyone count the number who pray? And among the signs of His Revelation is Alms—can anyone count those who give alms? And among the signs of His Revelation is Fasting—can anyone count those who fast? And among the signs of His Revelation is the Fifth—can anyone count those who give it? And among the signs of His Revelation is the Qur’an—can anyone count those who recite it? And among the signs of His Revelation is all that God hath revealed from the beginning to the end of religion, concerning every male and female and what they possess. Thou canst not count them even for that day, how much less from the day of His Manifestation until now!
All this is that thou mayest know that He was the Revealer of all things, and He revealed Himself to that creation only through what was uttered in truth from the tongue of His Reality:
This is His creation—behold but one sign among the signs of His creation which thou canst not enumerate, how much less the Manifestations of His command and His prohibition! All this is that thou mayest know Him as the Throne of Reality and know God thy Lord, and that thou mayest not associate anything with Him.
Behold then the first day when God brought him into His presence and he prostrated himself before the throne of the Point of the Bayan, for verily the Qur’an and all that is therein was created for the Bayan and all that is therein, and verily the Bayan and all that is therein was created for Him Whom God shall make manifest, exalted be His mention, and what God shall reveal unto Him. Then all before exists for what comes after, and thou shalt find no limit to the love of God as thou findest no beginning for it, for through it the beginning is created and through it the return is brought forth. Exalted be God above what those who remember mention.
When he appeared before the Point of the Bayan, it was to make known to creation that “I am He Who hath created that creation for My recognition.” All who professed the religion of Islam were thus addressed: “Ye were all created for My recognition, therefore know Me, for I am the first who hath recognized God, my Lord, in the Bayan. Worship God and associate naught with Him.” None followed his word, none recognized him save I. His manifestation ended, it came to pass and was ordained. For when all were intent upon extinguishing the light of God and quenching the fire of God, the love of his being would not consent that he remain patient in God after seeing that all in the heavens and earth and what lieth between them was in His grasp like a ring, in actual reality deserving thereof, not in mere verbal or intellectual forms.
He submitted himself wholly unto God, for after the Point of the Bayan he saw nothing in creation more precious before God than the Point of the Furqan. Therefore did he turn wholly unto Him, that it might be established in the kingdoms of the heavens and earth and what lieth between them that the Point of the Furqan, despite her exaltation, submitted to the Point of the Bayan, that perchance someone might perceive this and worship God, his Lord, with pure sincerity, until there came to pass that which made the heavens nearly to be cleft asunder and the earth to be split and the mountains to fall.
Behold then how the essences of all glorified beings turn unto Him, and the realities of all sanctified ones are drawn to Him, and the souls of all unified ones take refuge in His shadow, and the beings of all proud ones prostrate before God through Him. How can I say to whom I speak, for whom I speak, who can comprehend all things to fulfill them on that Day when no one was present before the throne of His bodily sovereignty? By Him Who splitteth the seed and createth the soul, if anyone should take one step toward Him, its weight would be greater before God than all who have followed their Lord’s religion from the beginning that hath no beginning to the end that hath no end. For all that was created for the recognition of that Most Luminous Light and Most Manifest Radiance, yet the people know Him from behind veils and perceive Him not as manifest and visible.
By Him Who created Paradise and formed the soul, all who circumambulate the House on such a day, even seventy thousand souls, and all who visit the Martyr’s Tomb on that day, whose numbers none can reckon—neither of these shall weigh before God as much as a gnat’s wing. But should one take a step toward that One, it would be greater than the creation of the heavens and earth and what lieth between them. Therefore watch ye for the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest, for the Tree of the Bayan was planted only that ye might recognize Me, and verily I am the first to prostrate before God and believe in His Self. Therefore waste not your recognition, for verily the Bayan, for all its loftiness, believeth in Him Whom God shall make manifest, and He indeed is worthy to be the Throne of Truth, though He is I and I am He.
But when the Tree of the Bayan reached the summit of its exaltation, its Point prostrated itself before God, its Lord, in the temple of Him Whom God shall make manifest, that ye might magnify God as His Self deserveth. Ye were created by the Point of the Bayan, and when that Point submitted itself to Him Whom God shall make manifest, and was exalted through His exaltation, and was made manifest through the manifestation of His might, and was glorified through the glory of His oneness, and was beautified through the beauty of His singleness, and was magnified through the greatness of His eternality, and was empowered through the sovereignty of His everlastingness—what station remaineth for those created by it to say “why” or “wherefore”?
O all things in the Bayan! Know ye your limits, for if the Point of the Bayan believeth in Him Whom God shall make manifest before all things—and I verily glory in this above all who are in the kingdoms of the heavens and earth and whatsoever is between them—for there is no glory save in the knowledge of God, and no joy save in the unity of God. Be not veiled from God after His manifestation, for all that the Bayan achieved is like a ring upon My fingers, and I am like a ring upon the fingers of Him Whom God shall make manifest, even as ye have seen how all that the Qur’an achieved was, in the estimation of its Point, but as a ring when He first believed in the Bayan. Were it not so, how could He have transformed those within Islam through the verses of His Lord, and summoned all unto the path of their Creator? He is indeed the Manifestation of His Cause in relation to the Point of the Bayan, and He appeared unto those within the Furqan only for His latter day. But who knew Him, and who fulfilled His command, and who attained the fruit of Islam’s planting at its source?
Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no God but God, and God is Most Great! None knew Him save Me, and none knew Me save Him, to such extent that in that Day all who are in Islam are mentioned through His manifestation, yet all are veiled from His remembrance and all are far removed from their stations. Otherwise it would have been meet that when the verses of God were revealed, all who are in Islam should have recognized Him as the One Who had revealed that religion unto them and created that creation by His command, that they might know Him on the day of His manifestation and not associate anyone with Him. But none knew Him save God Who created Him, and whosoever knoweth Him thereafter, knoweth Him through what God hath caused him to know through the Point of the Bayan. Therefore do I address all who follow His religion, saying through the shortest Surih that was revealed aforetime concerning His own Self:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
Say: O ye unbelievers! I worship not that which ye worship, nor will ye worship that which I worship. And I will not worship that which ye have been wont to worship, nor will ye worship that which I worship. To you be your way, and to me mine.
Knowest thou what He saith? He addresseth all who are in Islam, saying:
It is as though on the Day of My Return I shall address those who are in the Bayan in like manner. Be ye watchful of yourselves, for the Cause of God shall come unto you in truth, yet ye remain veiled from the presence of God.
Know thou that on that Day none shall be known except God, none shall be worshipped save Him, none shall be described but He, none shall be loved but Him, and none shall be sought except Him. However, not according to how thou hast known God before, for if Muhammad were to accept from thee, He would accept from those who came before, since the Known is one Sun, though Its thrones are made manifest in every Revelation upon whatsoever throne It willeth. Otherwise, it is but one Sun, though It may be manifested unto infinity through infinity—It is one Sun.
crumbs: BB00080: Ziyarat for the first to believe, on the Day of 'Arafa

title: BB00080: Ziyarat for the first to believe, on the Day of ’Arafa
text:
“I was a Hidden Treasure and wished to be known, so I created creation that I might be known.”














“I follow none save Him Whom God hath caused to descend with the Bayan. Unto you your religion, and ye have naught, for I have ordained your religion for you, and I have submitted myself to God and worship God, my Lord. Yea, my religion is the Bayan, and unto you what ye possess. Be ye patient, then bear witness, for it shall profit you not the weight of a grain of mustard seed. God sufficeth me; in Him do I place my trust, and in God let them that trust put their trust.”
crumbs: BB00080: Ziyarat for the first to believe, on the Day of 'Arafa

title: BB00080: Ziyarat for the first to believe, on the Day of ’Arafa
section: Part 2: “Your God is One God. There is no…”
text:
Part 2: “Your God is One God. There is no…”
Say: Your God is One God. There is no God but He, the Mighty, the Best Beloved. He it is Who hath sent forth the Messengers from His presence, that ye should worship none but God, for all Temples speak of God and through Him. And He it is Who hath sent down the Books from His presence, that ye should associate naught with God, your Lord, and that ye should be assured of the signs of God.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I testify that none hath known Thee through the knowledge of Thy Self which Thou seest and I see, since none hath known Thee save him whom Thou hast caused to know Thee through me. All who knew Thee before imagine they excel in knowing Thee. Yet in this my station I make mention of Him in such wise that were I above the earth in such manner that all were within my grasp, I would ascend unto Him and alight at His dwelling, and would manifest the fruit of what I had formerly planted of His religion through what the Manifestation of Thy Self knew in that Revelation before all souls. But Thou beholdest my position and art witness that my knowledge hath not changed whether I be in the highest heights or below that.
Therefore, O my God, send down upon him from all things that which beseemeth the loftiness of Thy grace and the sublimity of Thy bounty, and upon those who have ascended unto Thee—they who are near unto Thee, where each one was, in the manifestations of the Throne of Truth, a throne for It, since it beseemeth not the Point of the Bayan that any should ascend unto It save him who was the Manifestation of Its throne in Its previous manifestations.
O God! On that day, shower down upon those impregnable temples the knowledge of what Thou art in Thy transcendent exaltation, Thy supreme ascendancy, Thy lofty elevation, Thy matchless immunity, Thy glorious joy, Thy triumphant victory, and Thy compelling power, that their eyes may be gladdened in the chambers of their gardens by beholding the glory of their souls and Thy vengeance upon those who know them not and uphold not their rights. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things. Then, when thou art blessed to present thyself before God, thy Lord, on the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest, exalted be His mention, know that the Command is His Command. Look thou to none save Him and His Command, for all who are in the heavens and on earth and whatsoever lieth between them stand ready at His Command. We see not God’s Command as limited, for from the beginning that hath no beginning His Command hath been manifest in the temples of His Revelation, and unto the end that hath no end His Command shall be manifest in the temples of His Concealment. The temples are but thrones for the Primal Reality, and what is manifest in the temples is but one Manifestation and one Concealment.
Say: There is no God but God; all are His servants and all stand ready at His Command. Yet look not to that Temple, for it is the Temple of the Throne of Reality from aforetime, nor to Him Whom God shall make manifest, exalted be His mention, for He is that same Temple, since the thrones are like unto what is manifest in them—were it to differ, the manifestation of the Unseen Unity would not appear. What We have taught thee concerning the previous Manifestations, wherein each Manifestation after a previous Manifestation was in His grasp—thus hath God created this creation that perchance in each wondrous Manifestation they might be able to believe. When thou attainest unto that Most Great Remembrance, that Most Luminous Light, that Most Manifest Radiance, that Most Precious Essence, and that Most Pure Leaf, then purify thy inner being from all that God loveth not and thy outer being from all that God loveth not, according to what God hath sent down from His presence.
Then seek permission from God and all His guides and from whomsoever believeth in God and His signs, for all stand ready at God’s Command. Then say: Peace be upon Thee, O Essence of Eternity in the exaltation of Glory! Peace be upon Thee, O Camphor of Pre-existence in the ascendancy of Beauty! Peace be upon Thee, O Pure Essence of Bounty in the immunity of Perfection! Peace be upon Thee, O Essence of Mystery in the exaltation of Most Holy Action! Peace be upon Thee, O Pure Embodiment of Command at the ultimate pinnacle of might and justice! Thou didst make Thyself known at the Point of the Furqan that Thou wert, in the eternity of eternities, the Guide unto God, Thy Lord, that there is no God but He, the One, the All-Compelling.
Then thou didst draw forth from the Ocean of the Furqan and, through God, didst enter into the Sea of the Bayan, adducing proof concerning thy Lord that there is none other God but Him, the One, the Manifest. Upon thee be from the splendor of God its most splendid, from the majesty of God its most majestic, from the beauty of God its most beautiful, from the grandeur of God its most grand, from the light of God its most luminous, from the loftiness of God its most lofty, from the might of God its mightiest, from the holiness of God its most holy, from the power of God its most powerful, from the strength of God its strongest, from the good-pleasure of God its most pleasing, from the sovereignty of God its most enduring, from the dominion of God its most glorious, from the bounty of God its most ancient, from the riches of God its most steadfast, from the generosity of God its nearest, and from the glory of God its most exalted.
How lofty is thy loftiness, for thou hast been raised up and there is none like unto thee in elevation! Then thou didst seek the good-pleasure of God, thy Lord, in the Bayan, that thou mightest announce unto all who dwell in the kingdom of the heavens and of the earth and whatsoever lieth between them that authority and creation belong to God—there is none other God but Him, the One, the All-Compelling.
May God reward thee through the Bayan and through all that are therein with the best reward granted to the first believer in the Tree of Truth. Then thy manifestation in the First Unity is like unto that wherewith God hath favored thee, then thy former manifestations in the Temples of Truth. How exalted is your loftiness, again your loftiness! How glorious your glory, again your glory! How impregnable your strength, again your strength! How elevated your elevation, again your elevation! How firm your independence, again your independence! Through you hath God drawn nigh unto the creation of the Bayan, and through you will God cause the creation of the Bayan to return unto Him Whom God shall make manifest, exalted be His mention. If thou and thy manifestations and thy former Temples of manifestation had desired naught but God, therefore hath God caused them to attain unto what they desired of His knowledge. And those beneath thee and those that are under thy shadow, inasmuch as they desired the things of dominion, each according to his desire hath taken possession through the grace of his Lord. But ye have attained unto that which all desire but cannot reach.
When I behold the loftiness of what thou hast attained, my soul envieth thee, but when I behold the lowliness of what thou hast suffered, I weep for thee. When will my heart, my spirit, my soul, or the essence of my being find rest in thee? Unto God do I complain, and in His grasp lieth the kingdom of the most high unto the lowest atom. This sufficeth me and sufficeth thee, for He is the Powerful, the Compelling, the Manifest, the Mighty, the Exalted, the Inaccessible. Nothing whatsoever in the heavens or in the earth or in what lieth between them can frustrate Him. He will assuredly aid thee and those who are under thy shadow to attain an exaltation possible in creation and realizable in invention.
But all that was naught in the sight of God, in His essential being, save for those who recognize the Manifestation of His Self on the Day of Resurrection. For on that Day they shall witness the exaltation of thy station and the stations of the exponents of thy cause, and all shall ascend. Yet this shall profit neither thee nor them except before the appearance of the Resurrection and the dawning of the Sun of Truth, whereby those of faith are strengthened and those of certitude take pride. For verily the Cause of God, at the time of the Manifestation of His Self, doeth whatsoever He willeth by His command. He shall not be asked of His doings, while all else shall be questioned. I beseech God that He may honor me with His presence and make me and thee and those beneath thy shadow to be the names of His might on the day of His Manifestation. Verily He, exalted and mighty is He, answereth whom He willeth and raiseth up whom He desireth from among those who call upon His Most Beautiful Names. He is truly the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.
By thy life! My heart is not content that I should make mention of one who knoweth thee not, or standeth not up for thy rights, or causeth thee grief in any way. God shall suffice to deal with them, for God is the All-Compelling, the Severe. No fire is more intense for them than their being veiled from meeting thee, though they were created that on the day of thy manifestation they might believe in thee and in him whom thou callest all unto.
Verily what God hath foreordained for thee and for the exponents of thy cause and the names of those near thee and those who love that exalted remembrance of thee—that is the bounty from His presence, for He is possessed of great favor. For all good, after God hath recognized a soul’s acknowledgment of thy right and its independence beneath the shade of meeting thee, is established in its recognition of thee. And all that is less than good for those who know thee not is established with God, for thou hast made the first element of religion to be the knowledge of God, and this appeareth only through knowing thee, just as God hath made in every dispensation the first element of religion to be knowledge of Him, then knowledge of the Manifestation of His Self, then knowledge of Him through creation through His word from the Manifestation of His Self, from conditions which none can reckon save God. Upon this were all created and concerning this shall all be questioned.
Were I to make mention of thy merit, no heart could bear to hear it. But according to the capacity of hearts, spirits, souls and bodies to know and recognize—this sufficeth now before thee. Verily a drop of water flowing from a spring within thee is more beloved to God than the deeds of all upon earth, for thereby doth God love to be pleased, and without it God loveth not to be pleased. Blessed then are they who attain unto this bounty, which no bounty equalleth save that of those who weep for the Point. And all this is in His grasp at the appearance of the Truth—whoso grieveth for His grief or rejoiceth at His joy is better than the worship of all that is on earth in its entirety, for thus doth God love to be worshipped, not according to what His servants love. Therefore recognize Him Whom God shall make manifest, then be ye certain of His Cause. Say: should ye recognize Him, then remember what befell the First Vahid, then grieve ye all. And remember the Latter as ye remember the Former nineteen times, then from the essence of your beings grieve ye, then weep ye.
crumbs: BB00080: Ziyarat for the first to believe, on the Day of 'Arafa

title: BB00478: Ziyarat for the last [to believe]
text:
Visitation for the last [to ascend]
Then recite what hath been sent down by God in His remembrance, for verily He is the Remembrance, the Manifest, the Inaccessible, the Exalted, the Great.
May there be upon thee from the Glory of God its most glorious, and from the Majesty of God its most majestic, and from the Beauty of God its most beautiful, and from the Grandeur of God its most grand, and from the Light of God its most luminous, and from the Mercy of God its most expansive, and from the Words of God their most perfect, and from the Names of God their most great, and from the Might of God its mightiest, and from the Will of God its most conclusive, and from the Knowledge of God its most penetrating, and from the Power of God its most potent, and from the Utterance of God its most pleasing, and from the Honor of God its most honorable, and from the Sovereignty of God its most enduring, and from the Dominion of God its most glorious, and from the Loftiness of God its most elevated, and from the Favor of God its most ancient, and from every good thing that hath no equal, no peer, no associate, no likeness, and no similitude, unto thee, through thee, from thee, towards thee, and upon thee.
How great is thy right in creation and how manifest thy station in invention! Ever doth the ocean of omnipotence surge with thy conquering power, and the sea of almightiness boil with thy overwhelming might. God shall take vengeance on those who know thee not, and God shall aid those who uphold thy right. Nothing whatsoever in the heavens or on earth or in all that lieth between them can be hidden from His knowledge, nor can anything in the kingdom of command or creation or whatsoever lieth beneath them render Him powerless. He createth what He willeth through His command; verily He hath power over all things.
And thou shalt mention all the primary names, then the names which have been established under the shadow of thy self, according to what thou hast heard before from the Book of God and what thou hearest at that time from the Tongue of God, for this is a bounty that nothing in the heavens or on earth or in all that lieth between them can equal. Thus doth God bestow His favor upon thee and upon whomsoever He willeth among His creation. Verily, He is the Possessor of great bounty.
The verses which were revealed on the Day of ʿArafat
