title: BB00215: Ziyarat for the middle night of the month of God
text:
This is a blessed visitation for the night of the mid-month of God unto the Primal Tree and pardon for it and for those who seek shelter in its shade, then mention for Him Whom God shall make manifest:
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy! Glory be unto Thee, O my God! This is a night which Thou hast magnified and exalted and adorned and distinguished and honored through that which Thou hast ordained for it and sent down upon it. Therefore, O my God, bless on this night Thy Tree of Love and every root that hath sprung from that Root, and every branch that hath grown from that Branch, and every twig that hath stemmed from those Twigs, and every leaf that hath resembled those Leaves, and every fruit that hath taken form from those Fruits, from the first moment when Thou didst plant those Trees in the heart of the sign of Thy love, which if Thou shouldst cause to ascend unto the ultimate height of its ascension in the dawning-place of Thy grace and the exaltation of Thy bounty, verily the dwellers of the heaven of Thy dominion would be illumined by the glances of Thy near benevolence, and the essences of the manifestations of Thy oneness would be elevated through the revelations of the wondrous sovereign of Thy Lordship.
Send down, therefore, O my God, upon that Tree in this hour of this night every splendor which Thou hast numbered in Thy knowledge, and every majesty which Thy knowledge hath encompassed, and every beauty wherewith Thou hast adorned Thy Book, and every grandeur which Thou hast numbered by Thy knowledge, and every light which Thou hast ordained by Thy power, and every mercy which Thou hast spread through the munificence of Thy bounty, and every word which hath been sent down from the clouds of the inaccessibility of Thy glory, every name which hath indicated Thee and become established in Thee and goeth not forth from Thee unto aught else, and every might which Thou hast strengthened, and every will which Thou hast embraced, and every knowledge which Thou hast caused to penetrate, and every power which Thou hast manifested, and every utterance which Thou hast loved, and every word wherewith Thou hast been well-pleased, and every sovereignty which Thou hast perpetuated, and every dominion which Thou hast glorified, and every exaltation which Thou hast raised up, and every good which Thy knowledge hath encompassed from before and after, for none can reckon the conditions of Thy Lordship save Thee, and none can comprehend the manifestations of Thy sovereignty save Thee.
Thou art He Who existed before all things, and the Creator of all things, and the Being after all things. Thou hast ever been one God, Single, Eternal, Self-Subsistent, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Thou hast taken unto Thyself neither consort nor son, and nothing is hidden from Thy knowledge, neither in the heavens nor on the earth nor between them, and nothing can frustrate Thee, neither in the kingdom of earth nor of creation nor what lieth beneath them. Verily, Thou art the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.
Then turn and say: Verily, the Most Holy, Most Resplendent Glory and the Most Impregnable, Most Exalted Grandeur from God, the Lord of the Hereafter and of the former time, be upon thee, O Divine Tree, and Simple Essence, and Pure Camphor, and Eternal Branch, and Camphoric Leaf, and Intended Fruit, so long as the spheres of names revolve in the heaven of the cloud-white realm around the zone of oneness, and the winds of love blow from the holy and glorious horizon of the King of might and eternity. Beyond that is a limit in the Book of God. Exalted is Thine essence above that which is limited by creation should ascend unto Thee, and sanctified is Thy reality that what is determined in invention should rise unto Thee. Therefore upon Thee, never-ceasing and never-ending, be all glory and majesty, all beauty and radiance, all perfection and exaltation, all independence and grandeur, all bounty and praise. Though Thou in Thine essence hast ever been transcendent above that which hath sprung through guidance and been realized through resources, for He ever remembereth Thee, and whom God remembereth, every mention is with Him and in His grasp, and upon whom God bestoweth His blessings, every soul is before Him and in the right hand of His will.
Therefore bear witness, O my Beloved, before God, mighty and glorious, that I have testified that there is no God but Him, alone, there is no God but Him. His is the dominion and the kingdom, power and divinity are His, grandeur and the ruby are His! He giveth life and causeth death; then He causeth death and giveth life. He is the Living One Who dieth not. Within His grasp is the dominion of all things. He createth what He willeth through His command; verily, He hath power over all things.
And further, the Point of the Bayan, represented by the Seven Letters, was before and shall be after, and thou and the Letters of the Living who follow thee are the Names nearest unto Him and the most perfect Symbols in reference to Him. Then whosoever believeth as do believe the leaves of the Tree of Affirmation, these shall abide in the Paradise of eternity, and before God shall they ever be engaged in glorification. And whosoever believeth not in that which is from God, such are created of fire and in it shall they be tormented through God’s justice.
I bear thee witness that I shall love all who love thee and shall be quit of all who love thee not. Thus hath God, my Lord, inspired me on the Day of Resurrection beneath the shadow of the Tree of thy love and certitude in that which God hath ordained for thee and for the sincerity of thy dust. He is the Mighty, the Best-Beloved.
Then turn and say: God hath ever blessed you, O ye sacred Branches, and peace be upon you, O ye shining Stars! Blessed are ye and that which God hath ordained in you of the loftiness of His Cause and the exaltation of His remembrance. He is the All-Compelling, the Self-Subsisting.
Then turn and say: The transcendent, inaccessible and mighty glory and the lofty, sublime and exalted splendor be upon you, O ye sacred spirits, perfected hearts, sanctified souls and purified bodies! Your essential realities, your very beings, your inner selves and your identities have been made good and pure through your turning to God your Lord, your ascension and your rising unto God your Creator. Blessed are ye and that which God hath ordained for you of the exaltation of His remembrance and the sublimity of His praise. He is the All-Compelling, the Best-Beloved.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy signs, the most mighty thereof; by Thy glory, the most glorious thereof; by Thy majesty, the most august thereof; by Thy beauty, the most fair thereof; by Thy light, the most luminous thereof; by Thy greatness, the most mighty thereof; by Thy mercy, the most all-embracing thereof; by Thy names, the greatest thereof; by Thy might, the most puissant thereof; by Thy strength, the strongest thereof; by Thy knowledge, the most penetrating thereof; by Thy power, the most potent thereof; by Thy word, the most pleasing unto Thee thereof; by Thy manifestations, the most manifest thereof; by Thy attributes, the most unassailable thereof; by Thy sovereignty, the most enduring thereof; by Thy dominion, the most splendid thereof; by Thy loftiness, the most sublime thereof; and by Thy words, the most attractive in Thy presence, the most guarded with Thee, the most precious in the Mother Book before Thee, and the nearest in the Concourse on high through Thee.
For between Thee and all beside Thee there hath been nothing save that which hath trembled forth from the horizon of the Word of the Dayspring of Thine own Self, and shone from the heaven of the might of Thy Lordship and Thy bounty. Nothing hath been ascribed unto Thee save Thy signs and Thy words; and all that lieth between them—whether of the exalted heights or the lowest depths—is but within their compass.
Send down, then, O my God, at that time, blessings upon Him Whom Thou shalt cause to appear on the Day of Resurrection with clear and manifest signs. Strengthen Him through Thy might; invest Him with Thy sovereignty; uplift Him by Thy exaltation; grant Him victory through Thy power; make Him manifest through Thy Self-Subsisting Being; establish for Him the whole of the earth through Thy strength; and show Him, by Thy all-compelling dominion, that whereunto none can stretch forth his hands, and which lieth beneath His feet. Verily Thou art able to do whatsoever Thou willest, and powerful to accomplish whatsoever Thou desirest.
And send down, O my God, all Thy bounty and Thy munificence upon the heaven of His might and the earth of His love, and upon whatsoever is remembered by His remembrance in the heights of the holiness of His majesty; and upon whatsoever is ascribed unto Him of the affairs of the might of Thy Lordship; and upon him whose very being Thou hast created from the light of His being; and upon all who shall believe in Him and glorify Thee before His presence, by reason of the loftiness of the sovereignty of His Self-Subsisting Being—whether of the former or the latter, the manifest or the hidden—whatsoever Thy knowledge hath encompassed. For nothing escapeth Thy knowledge, neither in the heavens nor on the earth nor whatsoever lieth between them; and Thou art, verily, the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful, the All-Potent.

title: BB00322: Letter to an unnamed recipient re Mulla Husayn
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
When thou desirest to enter that hallowed land, purify thyself, and render goodly whatsoever thou possessest to the utmost of thy ability. Know thou that here is the loftiest horizon of the Throne and the uttermost pinnacle of Paradise, and that God hath ever watched over thee, unto the words:
“And say: O God! Thou art the Possessor of all things, and none beside Thee possesseth aught. I beseech, first, Thy bounty, then the grace of all whom Thou hast loved—of Thine angels nigh unto Thee, Thy Envoys sent forth, Thy chosen, purified ones, and Thy righteous servants—that I may enter before Thy Beloved, whom Thou hast chosen for Thyself, elected for Thy remembrance, singled out for Thy revelation, and linked obedience unto Him with obedience unto Thee,” unto the words:
“My father be a ransom for Thee, and all that the knowledge of my Lord encompasseth! How can I make mention of Thee or praise Thee? For whatsoever we behold and whatsoever we behold not is but an effect created through Thee, a form brought into being by Thee. Exalted is Thy remembrance above being conjoined with the remembrance of any of the rememberers, and uplifted is Thy glory above being matched by the glory of any of the thinkers. I bear witness that though Thou wast slain, yet surely Thou livest with God; and through what God hath brought forth from the overflow of Thy life, the hearts of the monotheists do live, and thereby they confess the oneness of Thy Lord and glorify Him, by night and by day, without cease.
How mighty is Thy right! How befitting the wonder of Thy station, the loftiness of Thy rank, and the sublimity of Thy manifestations! Thou hast severed Thyself unto God with all Thou didst possess, unto a height of exaltation which none hath preceded nor shall attain. Exalted is that which Thou hast achieved, and blessed that which Thou hast witnessed. I testify that Thou, and they who ascended with Thee, abide in the Most Exalted Horizon of the Throne and the most glorious pinnacle of the heaven of the Seat. There do they glorify God with the praise of their Lord, and through His remembrance do they profess His unity. Verily I shall testify, before God and before Thyself and the manifestations of Thy Countenance, and whatsoever God hath willed, that Thou didst summon unto God and didst deliver that with which Thou wast charged from the Book of God, and didst attain that which God, Thy Lord, had promised Thee—namely, the most exalted height of martyrdom and the loftiest summit of sainthood.
Who, after Thee, can reach unto Thee? Nay, by Thy glory! All who are martyred are martyred by virtue of Thy martyrdom, and all who ascend do so after the ascension of Thy glory. I testify that Thy calamity is too great to be conjoined with any calamity in creation, and Thy tribulation too high to be equalled by any tribulation in the realm of invention. Curse of God be upon a people who knew not Thy right, who bowed not down before the loftiness of Thy station, and who, through Thee, turned not to God, Thy Lord,” unto the words:

“And how can I send peace upon Thee, O Beloved of my heart, after what mine ears have heard of that which befell Thee? Nigh would the heavens be rent asunder, the earth be cloven, and the mountains fall down in fragments. Unto God do I complain, and unto Thee do I return. God shall assuredly unite me—and them that believe in Him—with the goal He ordained for Thee and whereunto He conveyed Thee. Would that I had been with Thee, that I might have sacrificed my life for Thine!”

And in the Most Sublime, Most Holy Tablets there are recorded many descriptions of His stations and attributes—among them His Supreme Utterance:

“The Name Ha—upon him be His most glorious Baha! He attained unto this supreme martyrdom ere his outward martyrdom; for in no wise had he any will, desire, or thought of his own. All these degrees he sacrificed for the Friend; thereafter he attained outward martyrdom, offering his very life in the path of the True Beloved.”

And likewise His Supreme Utterance:

“I bear witness that, in the Manifestation of the Point of the Bayan—exalted be His grandeur—He decreed that the first who believed was Muhammad, the Messenger of God. Doth it befit anyone to object, saying, This one is Persian whereas that one was Arab,’ or, This one was named Husayn whereas that one was named Muhammad’? Nay, by His exalted, all-glorious Self! The man of insight looketh not unto limitations and names; rather he looketh unto that whereon Muhammad stood—the Cause of God. Likewise he looketh upon Husayn according to that whereon he stood of the Cause of God, the All-Powerful, the Most Exalted, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.”

title: BB00129: Li-Akhiri’l-Mu’min
text:
In the name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy!
Verily I am God, there is no God but Me. I have created all things by My command, and all else besides Me is My creation. Say: O My creation! Worship ye Me! Verily I have existed from time immemorial, before and after all things, and no state existeth but that I have a proof thereof among My creation. Could there be any state conceived in My mind without My having created beings to worship Me and without My having established My proof over them? Glory be to God beyond all that! All things are created by My command, and verily My command existed before all things, after them, above all things and beneath them. Through it We create whatsoever We will—will ye not then behold?
I have created what I have created in such wise that none besides Me can comprehend it. How then can ye hope to understand the extent of the worlds set forth in the Book until the time of Adam? Until this moment, what ye would enumerate hath been ordained. Creation reached its culmination at the appearance of Muhammad, the Apostle of God, and We sent down the Furqan (Qur’an) unto him that ye might be assured of the signs of God, that the fruits of your faith might be manifested on the Day of My Manifestation. How is it then that ye comprehend not?
I have manifested the Gate through the revelation of My Self on the Day of Resurrection, that We might recompense those who believed in the Qur’an and cast into the fire those who believed not therein. Behold ye therefore! And from the first day of the Resurrection until now, ye behold those numbered by the letters Ra and Sad, and besides them those who are sincere in their faith. These are the best of those who have worshipped God according to the Qur’an, while those besides them were far removed from Our signs. We bear witness to no faith in them, nor will We recompense them with aught. Thus shall those who are veiled from Our signs enter the fire.
Your religion and all that is established therein existed only through My verses aforetime in the Furqan. How is it then that on this day ye have neither heard nor perceived, yet remain steadfast in your religion? Will your steadfastness profit you save in the fire? Verily when We say “Be!” and it is, your souls shall perish and your deeds shall be effaced. Can ye find any mention before God or any deed of those who entered not Islam? Your souls are like unto them, yet ye understand not. Ye prostrate yourselves before Me night and day, yet ye are not among those who act truly. If ye have prostrated before Me, how is it that when ye hear My verses ye prostrate not? If ye worship Me, how is it that ye believe not in Him unto whom We have given verses and clear proofs from Our presence?
I bear witness concerning what the Qur’an hath brought forth until now of those who believed in Me and were sincere—these are they who have met their Lord and are assured of His signs. I have witnessed no fruit like the mention of Mine own Name, the Mighty, the Wise. I have witnessed what I have made manifest of that might and wisdom from first to last and all between, whereby the heavens are nearly rent asunder, the earth cleft open, and the mountains fall down in ruins.
They have entered their chambers in paradise, but the fire shall torment you for what your hands have wrought, and the angels shall take vengeance upon you, yet ye perceive it not. I revealed not the Qur’an nor commanded Islam save for this day, and verily We were witnesses that the highest fruits of the verses have ascended to such a station that those in the heavens cannot but weep thereat—even all those in the worlds who worship God and magnify Him.
After he had ascended unto God his Lord, with a countenance wherein naught could be seen save the face of God, it was fulfilled according to the number We had sent down aforetime in the Furqan, but with authority. Thus did We cause him to ascend to a horizon that none had ever attained, after which the Tablet is powerless to reckon, the Pen to write, or the ink to flow concerning that which was decreed for him.
And verily beyond that in creation none can ascend unto God at that most exalted horizon of the Ridvan—We were witnesses to this. And after he had ascended until what was inscribed, We were witnesses. The angels of heaven were astounded by him, such that the sincere servants of God should be wholly detached unto Him.
I Myself prayed for him as none had ever prayed, and in My prayer I said:

“Verily I am God, there is no God but I, the Most Evident, the Most Evident, the Lord of all worlds,”

according to the number I had testified. Would God pray for anyone? Yes, for one whom creation did not pray for yet who was among those certain in their love for God. And thus do We bestow Our grace upon whomsoever We will, and We were witnesses.
All things glorify God through him while you turn toward Him day and night, yet you neither know nor perceive. You shall be torn utterly asunder in the fire, and God will seize you with a mighty seizure. We have power over all things.
I have raised up his remembrance thereby and erased mention of those who showed pride against him through their own works, for We have ever been supreme over creation. O people of faith in the Qur’an! How often have you recited mention of what was decreed concerning those who were martyrs after Muhammad the Messenger of God, wishing you could be one of them—praying, fasting, performing pilgrimage, giving alms and reforming yourselves day and night that you might draw nigh unto God and earn what the Pen is ashamed to write!
What ails you that you do not understand? You commemorate the afflictions of those who were martyrs before and spend your wealth in their cause, leaving your homes to go to them. Yet when they returned to their former life, you earned in their right what We witnessed. How can you be patient when they have turned to God? God’s proof, at its appearance, completed His argument against all who are on earth.
These shall enter the Ridvan through God’s verses, while those shall be punished in the fire for not believing God’s verses. These are the highest fruits of the Furqan, while those are the severest fruits of the fire wherein you shall be tormented though you perceive it not.
We prayed for them and commanded the angels of the heavens and earth and what lies between them to descend upon them, and they were humble before them. We punished those others and all associated with them, and We shall punish whoever loves them or mentions their names without cursing them. At that time they shall curse themselves by their former names.
And let them not curse them, for at that moment they are cursing themselves by their own names as before, and they are indeed worse than these others. Verily the punishment of God in the hereafter is more severe than what was ordained in the first life. Therefore await ye the Manifestation of God, for ye shall indeed be tried. Remember what We have revealed in the Book, and invoke blessings upon those who were martyred in the path of God, and curse those who have unjustly acquired that which burns the hearts of all peoples.
But on the Day of Truth ye shall follow all that was revealed in the Bayan, yet shall ye be veiled from its fruits just as ye were veiled from these ones. Verily Islam circles round about them while ye commit against them that which causes tears to flow down the faces of the God-fearing. Soon shall ye exalt their stations, and ye shall all enter therein, and shall pride yourselves in prostrating at their doors, and ye shall be rewarded when ye are sincere.
This is among that which changeth not with God and altereth not in any way. But that which existeth with that Temple and that which changeth is attributed unto Us, wherefore We indeed do weep. Were ye not to grieve on account of My Self, it would be better for you than acquiring all good things.
And those whom ye do not recognize as being guided—they do not act thus, even though they are veiled from that which they have been commanded. But they will not flee this religion of theirs, and that which they do not wish—that they should grieve on account of My Self—shall profit them. But that which ye worship by night and by day, while ye were not sincere, shall not profit you, and what ye commit against those who are more precious in God’s sight than all creation shall harm you.
See then how God will destroy you thereby, though ye claimed to be workers for God’s sake. Those who killed the Imams of the Faith spoke words like unto your words, and upon you shall be ordained in the Book of God that which is more severe than what was ordained for them. Ye shall not flee from God and His names in any way, though ye worship by His names night and day.
Therefore weep for them insofar as ye are able, when it becomes grievous upon your hearts, spirits, souls and bodies, or else grieve in your hearts, for We shall record, on account of this love of yours, the reward thereof in God’s Book if ye are sincere in this.
I send greetings upon thee, O thou purified body, and upon those who have been tried as thou wert tried in My good-pleasure. I shall bestow upon you from the treasuries of My Cause that wherewith ye shall be well-pleased, and even more than that wherewith ye shall be well-pleased. And verily what I have bestowed upon you is above that wherewith your hearts would be content, for were ye to hear the like of this from God, how it would attract your hearts, spirits, souls and bodies, and ye would be content that your spirits be severed from you by reason of what ye find of the love of God within you—this is above that wherewith your souls would be content.
Therefore grieve not in your stations, for We shall indeed take vengeance. Be patient in God, for We were patient. Thus doth God cause you to enter Paradise through His grace, and causeth those who know you not to enter the Fire by reason of what their hands have wrought. Thus doth God requite the veiled ones and show favor unto the sincere ones who have answered God’s call in what they asked of His grace. Verily He is the All-Bountiful, the Exalted.
Before Him prostrate all who are in the heavens and who are on the earth and what lieth between them. Verily He is the Mighty, the Impregnable, the Exalted. And unto God glorify all who are in the heavens and on the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and verily He is the Mighty, the Powerful, the Strong. And unto God boweth down in worship whosoever is in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and verily He is the All-Compelling, the One possessed of terrible might. And verily He is the Subduer, possessed of supreme ascendancy. And verily He is the Almighty Who shall assuredly take vengeance upon those who believe not in God and His signs, and who have caused even an atom’s weight of sorrow unto them that have believed in God and His signs. Verily He was ever possessed of immense power. O all things! Ye shall surely weep for Him Who had no peer or likeness on earth, and ye shall grieve for Him and be among those who sorrow in the days of God.

title: BB00164: Li-Harfi’l-Avval
text:
In the Name of God, the First, the First
Verily I am God; there is no God but I. I shall bestow My blessings upon all My guides from the beginning that hath no beginning unto the end that hath no end. I am the Best of those who bless, and I am indeed cognizant of all worlds.
Say: My guides in every Dispensation enter into the subsequent Dispensation, and they are they who know Me. My guides in the Gospel are they who recognized Muhammad, My Messenger, and believed in Him. My guides in the Furqan are they who recognized the Point of the Bayan and believed in Him. And My guides in the Bayan are they who recognize Him Whom God shall make manifest and believe in Him. Ye shall behold all things unto the end that hath no beginning even as the beginning that hath no beginning—know ye this and be ye assured.
I have created the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them for My names, and ye all, with one accord, do call upon Me through them. My names have ever been Mine, and all do turn unto Me through them. My attributes shall ever be Mine, and all shall turn unto Me through them. I created this creation from the beginning that hath no beginning so that every soul might recognize My Self through the Self of the Point of the Bayan, that ye might outwardly perceive Me through My names and inwardly turn unto Me through My attributes.
Ye have indeed witnessed how the people of the Furqan dealt with My guides, whose very beings were mirrors of My names, and ye all do call upon Me through them. Were they to know what they have wrought against those in whose right they have transgressed, they would not circumambulate around themselves nor around the House which We commanded you to circumambulate. For the House of My names in the heavens and earth and whatsoever is between them—how can ye all circumambulate around it within the limits of your physical frames? Even so do ye circumambulate around the names of God within the limits of your hearts.
Verily, the first of My names that hath indicated that there is no God but I, the Guardian, the Self-Subsisting, was the first to believe in the Point of the Bayan. Behold how ye have dealt with him after ye claimed to turn unto Me through him. I shall bestow My blessings upon thee, that this First Name may behold—never-ceasing and never-ending—through all My names and attributes that which My knowledge hath encompassed. Then upon all My names after that Name who shall, on the Day of Resurrection, guide others unto Him Whom God shall make manifest.
Through My glory, behold My most glorious glory upon thee among the glorious ones; through My majesty, behold My most majestic majesty upon thee among the majestic ones; through My beauty, behold My most beauteous beauty upon thee among the beautiful ones; through My grandeur, behold My most grand grandeur upon thee among the grand ones; through My light, behold My most luminous light upon thee among the luminous ones; through My mercy, behold My most merciful mercy upon thee among the merciful ones; through My perfection, behold My most perfect perfection upon thee among the perfect ones; through My completeness, behold My most complete completeness upon thee among the complete ones; through My greatness, behold My greatest greatness upon thee among the great ones; through My might, behold My mightiest might upon thee among the mighty ones; through My power, behold My most powerful power upon thee among the powerful ones; through My good-pleasure, behold My most pleasing good-pleasure upon thee among the well-pleased ones; through My love, behold My most loving love upon thee among the loving ones; through My nobility, behold My most noble nobility upon thee among the noble ones; through My sovereignty, behold My most sovereign sovereignty upon thee among the sovereign ones; through My dominion, behold My most dominant dominion upon thee among the dominant ones; and verily from My loftiness upon thee, My loftiness shall be observed, the most exalted among the exalted ones; and verily from My generosity upon thee, My generosity shall be observed, the most bountiful among the bountiful ones; and verily from all My names and My likenesses upon thee is that which beseemeth God, thy Lord, in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them among all the worlds.
Thou hast known God, thy Lord, before all worlds, and thou hast declared with thy tongue that there is none other God but God among all worlds, and thou hast manifested through thy word the Word that there is none other God but God among all worlds, until thou didst comprehend in the Revelation of God all that can be comprehended through Him—verily He is the Best of comprehenders. Thou hast taken possession of every good thing through what thou hast understood from God, the Most High, the Most Great. God will assuredly send down upon thee in Paradise that which shall satisfy thy soul, and beyond what shall satisfy—verily He is the Best of satisfiers.
And one of the Letters of the Primary Living One, the Letter of thy self, shall remember thee at the time when these verses are being written down from God, the Lord of all worlds, and thou shalt say:

“God, my Lord, hath guided me through thee, for thou art the First of the first ones; and God, my Lord, hath honored me through thee, for thou art the Most Honored of the honored ones; and God hath elevated me through thee, for thou art the Most Exalted of the exalted ones; and God, my Lord, hath ennobled me through thee, for thou art the Most Noble of the noble ones; and God, my Lord, hath taught me through thee, for thou art the Most Learned of the learned ones.”

All that thou hast comprehended, and all who are in the Bayan, is because thou didst believe in God, thy Lord, before the believers, and didst prostrate thyself before God, thy Lord, before those who prostrate, and didst glorify God, thy Lord, before those who glorify, and didst sanctify God, thy Lord, before those who sanctify, and didst magnify God, thy Lord, before those who magnify, and didst praise God, thy Lord, before those who praise, and didst exalt God, thy Lord, before those who exalt.
How many sovereigns shall come in the Bayan who shall rule through thy guidance, and how many angels shall come in the Bayan who shall possess through thy guidance, and how many learned ones shall come in the Bayan who shall learn through thy guidance, and how many judges shall come in the Bayan who shall judge through thy guidance, and how many distinguished ones shall come in the Bayan who shall be distinguished through thy guidance.
And from God, my Lord, then from all His names upon thee, then upon the First Bahi, then the numbers of those who ascend around thee unto God, their Lord, in every glory which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Most Glorious, the All-Glorious; and from every majesty which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Most Majestic of the majestic ones; and from every beauty which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Most Beautiful of the beautiful ones; and from every grandeur which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Most Grand of the grand ones; and from every light which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Most Luminous of the luminous ones; and from every mercy which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Most Merciful of the merciful ones; and from every perfection which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Most Perfect of the perfect ones; and from every greatness which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Greatest of the great ones.
And from every might which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Mightiest of the mighty ones; and from every power which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Most Powerful of the powerful ones; and from every good-pleasure which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Most Pleasing of the pleasing ones; and from every love which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Most Loving of the loving ones; and from every honor which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Most Honored of the honored ones; and from every dominion which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Most Sovereign of the sovereign ones; and from every kingdom which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Most Royal of the royal ones; and from every loftiness which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—verily He is the Most Exalted of the exalted ones; and from every bounty which God, my Lord, hath created or shall create—He, verily, is the Most Generous of the generous.
Remember all the signs of the Illumined Name before thee, for verily I am with God, remembering all who remember. I shall remember thee and them, though We are all deprived. Say: Verily that Name was created in Paradise that thou mightest love God, its Lord. Then say: O God! There is no God but Thee. Thou hast created me, sustained me, favored me, given me life, and made me foremost among worshippers. By Thy might! I have witnessed naught from Thee save all good, for Thou art the most excellent of the excellent ones. I have not witnessed grief to the measure of a mustard seed. Thou hast caused me to ascend unto Thee and enter the most exalted Paradise, wherein we have been blessed.
Let those who love Us in the Ridvan bear witness, for We are well-pleased with Thee. And let those who know Thee not bear witness in the fire, while We in the pavilions of Ridvan laugh at them. And verily, whoso hath been mentioned in his creation from the Letters of Abha—that is from Thee, for Thou art the most remembering of those who remember. Therefore, O God, remember him from Thy presence as a recompense for his remembrance of Me, for Thou art the best of those who remember. Let the First Letter see. Say: From thy Lord—whosoever remembereth Me once, God will remember him a thousand times, as a bounty from His presence. Verily, He is the best of those who remember.
And whosoever sendeth blessings upon Me once, God will send blessings upon him five hundred thousand times. Verily, He is the best of those who send blessings. And whosoever visiteth Me, I shall visit him on the Day of Resurrection before my Lord, for God hath granted Me from His presence a most great station among the worlds. Say to those who are in the Bayan: I shall surely know who entereth therein if ye help Me and if ye love Me.

title: BB00166: Ziyarat for Hadrat-i-Quddus
text:
In the Name of the Most High, the Most Great, the Most Exalted
O Pure and Most Luminous Essence, Who rose and shone forth, then gleamed and flashed, then dawned and resounded, then illumined and ascended from the lights of the holy splendor near the garment of the countenance of the One, the Single, the Unique, the Eternal, and Muhammad, peace be upon Him and His family, His servant, the first number in the world of eternity, and the Manifestations of His Beloved’s Self, the essential sustainers in the everlasting realm.
Upon thee, O Light of Glory, Remembrance of Creation, Mystery of Destiny, Guide of Implementation, Camphor of Praise, Mount Sinai, and Appearance of the Crimson Pillar, by the essence of my heart and by what God, my Lord, loves.
Then upon thee, O Point of the Gates, Reality of the Book, Word of the Bestower, Sign of the Oft-Returning, Center of the Circle of the Poles, the Countenance veiled in the House of Response, and the Universal Trial for the perfection of causes, by my pure being and by what God, my Master, loves.
Then upon thee, O Thou Who proves the Essence by the Essence for the Essence, and the Beauty of Attributes in all manifestations, conditions, signs and evidences, by the light of my essence and by what God, my Sovereign, loves.
Then upon thee, O Bearer of Succor, the One humbled before the Help in Peril, transformed by life, penetrating through gentleness, and drawing near through supplication at the time of calling for help to God, the Help in Peril, by the glory of my soul and by what God, my King, loves.
Then upon thee, O Blazing Lamp, Stirrer of Joy, Ocean surging with waves, Heaven adorned with constellations, Light shining at the time of ascension, Tumultuous Light in the pitch darkness of commotion, and Straightener of crookedness in the station of agitation, by the camphor of my being and by what God, my Beloved, loves.
Then upon thee, O Radiant Star, Swimming Planet, Successful Light, Sincere Servant, Manifest Glory, Refreshing Wind, and Pure Righteous One, by the essence of my element and by what God, my Intended One, loves.
Then upon thee, O Lofty Throne, Firm Spirit, Diffusing Light, Towering Mountain, Flowing Earth, Blowing Trump, and Crying Servant, by my father and what lies within my Lord’s knowledge.
Then upon thee, O Essence of the Heart, Progress of Creation, Quickener of Lands, Inspirer of Truth, Guide of Servants, Elucidator of Guidance, and the One exalted above opposites, by my father and what lies within my Lord’s knowledge.
Then upon thee, O Thou in Whom I seek refuge and to Whom I flee, from Whose decree there is no escape, for neither I nor anyone has any deviation from Thee, and Thou art the refuge for all who seek protection in Thy presence and then take shelter in Thy court, by my father and what lies within my Lord’s knowledge.
Upon thee, O Inscribed Book, Famous Delicate Symbol, Frequented House, Camphor Leaf, Hidden Secret, and Manifest Light, by my father and what lies within my Lord’s knowledge.
Then upon thee, O Adorned Ornament, Ultimate Symbol, Final Mystery in the pole of the circle of the center, Embellished Glory, Adorned Radiance, Most Beautiful Ornaments, and Essential Jewel, by my father and what lies within my Lord’s knowledge.
Then upon thee, O Light of Holiness, Spirit of Fellowship, Mystery of the All-Holy, King of Paradise, Sovereign of Heaven, and Warbling Peacock in the essences of the ocean, from Whose dominion no decree of the most precious souls can flee, and compared to Whom in His heart the finest horseman is but of the nature of darkness, a dry stone, a blazing meteor, and a pitch-dark night, by my father and what lies within my Lord’s knowledge.
Then upon Thee, O Provider of sustenance by God’s leave, and Ruler over all flocks, and Nurturer of nestlings, and Quencher of all who thirst, and Bestower of raiment upon mankind, and the Smiling, the Cheerful One, by my soul and all within my Lord’s knowledge!
Then upon Thee, O Master of refuge, and the Powerful to deliver, and Witness to absorption, and Ruler over young camels, and Judge between people and the recoilers, and the Living Spirit in bodies, by my soul and all within my Lord’s knowledge!
Then upon Thee, O Best of substitutes, and Master of gardens, and the Bountiful Sovereign, and Remover of diseases, and Witness to all red and white, for I testify that Thy word is effective and Thy decree decisive, by my soul and all within my Lord’s knowledge!
Then upon Thee, O Light of the earth, and the All-encompassing Knowledge, and the Extended Justice, and the Straight Line, and the Central Point, and the Outspread Sustenance, and the Secret Path on the Day of Equity, by my soul and all within my Lord’s knowledge!
Then upon Thee, O Preserved Tablet, and the Protected Book, and the Observed Letter, and the Seer of glances, and the Hearer of utterances, and the Distributor of portions, and the Witness to the spoken word, by my soul and all within my Lord’s knowledge!
Then upon Thee, O All-Gathering Name, and the Fourth Symbol, and the Decisive Judgment, and the Rising Sun, and the Protective Veil, and the Seeing, Hearing One, and the Brilliant, Radiant Light, by my soul and all within my Lord’s knowledge! O Thou Who hast witnessed and bestowed abundantly, and shown compassion and permitted, and carried and delivered, and spoken and poured forth, and saw and completed, and heard and found pleasing, and beheld and rejected not, by my soul and all within my Lord’s knowledge!
Then upon Thee, O Thou Just and Mighty Sovereign, and the Kind King, and the Compassionate Monarch, and the Surging, Overflowing, Protected Ocean, Refuge of the weak, Support of the distressed, and the Upright, Inclined Alif, by my soul and all within my Lord’s knowledge!
Then upon Thee, O True Reality, and the Precise Absolute Mystery, and the Deep Surging Ocean, and the Brilliant Firm Pillar, and the Elevated Ancient House, and the Delicate Shining Light, and the Compassionate Gleaming Glory, by my soul and all within my Lord’s knowledge!
Then upon Thee, O King of the Kingdom, and Sovereign of sovereigns, and the Merciful to the possessed, and the Ordainer of ways of conduct, and the Established Pole in the depths of the spheres, and the Witness to the perceiving wayfarer—Thou art He Whom perception cannot perceive, by my soul and all within my Lord’s knowledge!
Then upon Thee, O Oceans of majesty, and Mine of grandeur, and Sovereign of bounties, and the Powerful over deeds, and the Exalted in impossibilities, and the Condescending in annihilation, and the Witness to the end, by my soul and all within my Lord’s knowledge! I testify that Thou art the Most Ancient Light, and the Greatest Name, and the Delicate Symbol, and the Most Noble Sign, and the Most Perfect Remembrance, and the Most Decisive Radiance, and the Most Upright Glory, by my soul and all within my Lord’s knowledge!
Then upon Thee, O Tree of the Bayan, and Mystery of the Qur’an, and Glory of Paradise, and Unseen of contingent being, and Manifestness of creation, and Appearance of the All-Merciful, by my soul and all within my Lord’s knowledge!
Then upon Thee, O Mystery of transcendence, and Symbol of exaltation, and the Effective in nearness, through Whom the valley bestows without Thee the mention of effacement and the mystery of consciousness without the remembrance of trees, no hearing of vain decree, by my soul and all within my Lord’s knowledge!
Then upon Thee, O Light of the Divine Identity, and Garment of the Countenance of Oneness, and Mystery of Eternality, and the Divine Grandeur, and the Glory of the Divine Essence, and the Sublimity of the Realm of Might, and […] praise be upon my father and what is in my Lord’s knowledge!
Then upon you be the letter “la” and the word “illa” and the mystery of “la” and “la illa,” for through you has shone forth what has illumined, and through you is cast the majesty of my father and what is in my Lord’s knowledge.
Then upon you, O Remembrance of the Most High, Praise of the Manifest, Glory of the Hidden, Splendor of the Concealed, the Faithful Name, the Pure Light, and the Fresh Book! I bear witness before God and what is in His knowledge that there is no God but Him, alone with no partner. His is the Kingdom and Command, there is no God but Him, the Great, the Exalted.
And I bear witness to Muhammad, peace be upon him and his family and upon their followers, and to the Manifestations of His Self, as He Himself has testified to them in His knowledge, and none can comprehend their knowledge save Him. There is no God but Him, the Mighty, the Sublime, the Gracious.
And I bear witness to all that God’s knowledge encompasses, as He numbers it and as He loves and is pleased with. And I bear witness before You of the greatest causes and the mightiest outcomes, that every essential attribute, abstract description, manifest remembrance, and camphor mystery of the exaltation of God’s Cause in You and before You is pure falsehood.
Thus do I seek Your forgiveness as You love and are pleased with, and I turn to You in repentance as You reckon. For my very existence in Your dominion is pure sin, so how much more when sin acquires another sin? Therefore grant me, O Sovereign of my heart, Sultan of my being, Master of my secret and my public self, what proceeds from Your generosity and grace, for the cause of Your gifts and bounties is Your munificence and nothing else. Bestow Your grace upon me, for verily You are the Generous, the Sublime, the All-Giving.

title: BB00509: Ziyarat for the first [to believe]
text:
If, on that Day, thou shouldst find thyself in the presence of Him Whom God shall make manifest, that alone would suffice thee, before God, for every remembrance and praise. But if thou art in the darkest night, then, first of all, be not veiled by the outward conjunctions of this world, nor face them with either acceptance or aversion. For the honour of God cometh only by a command from His presence, and the abasement which descendeth from Him cometh only by a prohibition from Him. Thus, if God desireth to exalt a soul by His remembrance of it and His good-pleasure with it, He exalteth it; and if He desireth to abase a people in like manner, then, when God maketh mention of them without the right that is meet, He abaseth them.
Worldly conjunctions and outward circumstances are, at every moment, renewed—whether in the Manifestations of Truth or in those beneath them. Consider the appearance of the Messenger of God: God hath rehearsed to all religions the tale of abasement, and how often honour and humiliation were exchanged among the communities. If such things were among the measures by which the servant should accept or by which he should be veiled, how then wouldst thou regard these peoples? Perchance, in every day, He exalteth servants whose number none can reckon save God, and in like manner He abaseth others. If, then, thou desirest to make such outward conditions the balance of His religion, how shalt thou ever know God and Him Whom He shall make manifest?
All this is that, on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, thou mayest not infer, from royal and worldly conjunctions, the abasement of any who have not believed in Him, nor the honour of any who have believed in Him. For the might of God is His command unto whomsoever He willeth, and the measure of abasement is His prohibition concerning whomsoever He willeth. This is the beginning and the end of the matter for such as dwell upon the pinnacle of the names and attributes. Otherwise, the True One exalteth and abaseth, and others likewise; yet such states can never serve as conclusive proofs whereby any soul may rightfully infer the truth. Say: All glory lieth in the Cause of Him Whom God shall make manifest, for whomsoever He commandeth; and all abasement belongeth unto whomsoever He forbiddeth. This is the testimony whereunto the people of knowledge hold fast, and whatsoever is beside this, God hath not loved as yet.
There is, in very truth, no doubt that the entire matter is in the hand of God, and that no soul hath any motion or stillness save through God, exalted be His glory. All honour, moreover, consisteth in faith in God, and this is naught but true faith in Him Whom God shall make manifest. For, on the Day of His manifestation, there shall remain upon the earth no truth save such as have believed in Him. Whoso believeth in Him, God will exalt and honour; God will succour him, assist him, and cause him to be made manifest upon the earth, for the confirmations of God shall descend upon him and be cut off from all else. And though there should appear a division in the outward means, this is not outside the realm of glory; for glory resideth in the Cause of God, whether or not its means appear in the earthly kingdom at every moment.
Consider, for example, that had all who were upon the earth believed in the Messenger of God at the first dawning of His Revelation, this would have been in conformity with what befitteth the following of His command. But when the Most Exalted One was denied, this wrought no diminution in the bounty of the glory of God; it was rather the result of the veiling of the people and of the means. All that is with God—were He to unveil it—none among His servants, who are all within His grasp, could endure it. There is no affair but by the leave of God. Unto Him belong creation and command, in the beginning and in the end. There is no God but He, the Mighty, the Well-Beloved.
Then, if thou shouldst find thyself in one of the foremost seats, say: Verily, the Glory is from God, then from all His Names, then from everyone who hath believed in God and in His signs—upon thee be that glory, O thou who art well-pleasing and well-pleased, O exalted, impregnable Word—at every moment, and before time and after time. And when thou desirest to stand before the body of one of thy near kindred, then remember God, in that place, by means of that Word, nineteen times; for with every letter thereof will God send down upon him that whereby his eye shall be cheered. Verily, He hath encompassed all things in His knowledge.
There is no God but God, one God; and we all are, in very truth, His sincere servants.

title: BB00389: Ziyarat for the last [to believe]
text:
The Glory from God be upon thee, O Essence of Glory; and the Majesty be upon thee, O Essence of Majesty; and the Beauty be upon thee, O Essence of Beauty; and the Grandeur be upon thee, O Essence of Grandeur; and the Light be upon thee, O Essence of Light; and the Mercy be upon thee, O Essence of Mercy; and the Words be upon thee, O Essence of the Words; and the Names be upon thee, O Essence of the Names; and the Might be upon thee, O Essence of Might; and the Knowledge be upon thee, O Essence of Knowledge; and the Strength be upon thee, O Essence of Strength; and the Power be upon thee, O Essence of Power; and the Utterance be upon thee, O Essence of Utterance—and the good-pleasure; and the Love be upon thee, O Essence of Love—and the exaltation; and the Honor be upon thee, O Essence of Honor, in this world and in the world to come; and the Sovereignty be upon thee, O Essence of Sovereignty, in the Kingdom of the Most High, unto the first atom; and the Dominion be upon thee, O Essence of Dominion, in the Most Great Horizon; and the Loftiness be upon thee, O Essence of Loftiness, in every mighty verse.
Therefore do I bear witness that there is none other God but He. His are the most beauteous names. All that are in the heavens and on the earth and whatsoever lieth between them glorify Him; and all that dwell in the kingdoms of command and creation and whatsoever is beneath them bow down before Him. There is none other God but He, the Mighty, the Well-Beloved.
And I testify that all the essences of whatsoever appeared through Muhammad, the Messenger of God—of realities and inner beings, of souls and selves, of guardianship, of prayer, of alms, of pilgrimage, of fasting, and of whatsoever was revealed in the Book—have returned unto thee in their glory and their inmost substance, according to the knowledge of the Inmost of the Inmost, from God, the Manifest of the Manifest.
How exalted is thy loftiness and thy unapproachableness! How resplendent thy sublimity and thy joy! How great thy lowliness before God, and how near thy awe before God! All are worshippers of God by virtue of thy countenance, and all are prostrate before God through thy direction.
And those who have wrought against thee what they have wrought have not worshipped God for the twinkling of an eye, nor have they affirmed His unity even less than that. What their hands have earned—God hath created no fire more grievous than this, wherewith they shall take vengeance upon their own selves against their own selves, whence they perceive not. Therefore do they curse their own selves by names that were revealed before, yet they know not; for thou art the Known One in the heavens and on the earth, and the Described One among all realities. There is nothing that glorifieth God but it descendeth unto thy threshold; nothing that affirmeth His oneness but it standeth before the court of thy might; nothing that magnifieth God but it is uplifted by the loftiness of thy Cause.
And verily thou art the last letter of the Letters of the One; thou shalt assuredly believe in Him Whom God shall make manifest. He hath mentioned thee by these words in the manifestation that preceded thee, and hath raised thee by those manifestations above all that are. He it is unto Whom all the Bayan returneth, and from Whose presence God bringeth into being whatsoever He willeth in the realm of existence. Through Him doth He hold back the heaven lest it fall upon the earth, and through Him doth everything subsist.
No servant that hath worshipped God throughout all worlds, and yet hath not believed in Him, hath truly worshipped God for the twinkling of an eye. And no servant that hath been veiled from God throughout all worlds, yet hath believed in Him, is as though he had been veiled in any world. But God hath refused to admit into the paradise of His recognition any save the guides of His Names and the likenesses thereof. Though all who are in the Bayan should be prostrate before God by Him, and worshippers of God by His Face, yet none shall attain unto His love and recognition save the purified—those who behold in Him naught but God, and who are assured of meeting Him.
Otherwise, every soul would fain enter His paradise; for God hath created all things for that end. Yet because of the veils men set between themselves and Him, they are unable thereafter. Mighty is His glory and exalted His loftiness! He desireth that there be no soul upon earth save that it believe in Him and in His verses, and prostrate itself at His Gate—for the first that believed in Him are the essences in the Bayan and the immaterial ones in the Bayan. Upon Him, and upon all who follow the guidance He hath bestowed, be every bounty from God in the Most High Horizon—then in the world to come and in this world—aye, even in the nearness of nearnesses.
His visitation—what tongue can number? God alone can reckon it. And He loveth and is well-pleased: upon him be the glory of God.

title: BB00663: Ziyarat for ‘the second to believe’ on ’Id al-Fitr
text:
The glory, the Most Exalted Glory, and the majesty, the Most Splendid Majesty, and the beauty, the Most Beauteous Beauty, and greatness, the Most Great Greatness; and the light, the Most Luminous Light; and the mercy, all-embracing, through the Most Lofty Words and the Most Great Names; and might, the Most Mighty Might; and the Will, enduring; and knowledge, most penetrating; and power, far-reaching; and good-pleasure, well-pleasing; and love, most august, most steadfast, most sublime; and sovereignty, everlasting; and dominion, decreeing; and exaltation, resplendent; and favor, primal, towering—be upon Thee, O Tree of Glory, O Light of Splendor, O Countenance sanctified through radiance, O Direction robed in praise, O Being worthy of all greatness and grandeur, from God, besides Whom there is none other God, Who hath ever been and will ever remain.
How shall I make mention of Thee on that Day, when it behoveth that whatsoever is on earth should stand before Thee, whilst Thou wast, with all things, in the presence of God? I behold nothing in the heavens and the earth, and all that lieth between them, but hath been created through Thee, and sustained through Thee, and quickened through Thee, and raised up through Thee. And yet, notwithstanding this, Thou art exalted upon Thy seat, a very thousand—without equal; whilst the seat of him whom God hath made a gate unto all things is set above a mountain, without seat, without glory, without radiance.
Every soul, from Adam until that time, shall surely turn unto God through Thee, and shall call upon Him by Thy name, each according to the measure of his recognition of his Lord; and he shall veil himself from Thee, inasmuch as that is dearer unto him than all things beside. And though all should forsake Thee—turning away from Thy obedience and from prostration before the Sovereign of Thy might—yet, by Thy might, I would glory upon my seat upon that mountain, in that I render Thee greeting; that I hearken to Thee recounting the tale of my love in Thy presence; that I cause my tears to flow upon my cheek in the path of Thy affection and Thy love.
Nay, by Thy might! I have not been abased, for all honor is made honorable through Thy honor. I have not been solitary, for all multitude is multiplied through Thy multitude. I have not been overcome, for all victory is victorious through Thy victory. I have not been a stranger, for all companionship is made companionable through Thy companionship. Nor have I been without sovereignty, for all sovereignty glorieth in Thy sovereignty. Thou art the Most High, and through Thy loftiness all are uplifted; Thou art the Inaccessible, and through Thy unapproachableness all are exalted.
Beings have been brought to naught, that they might bow down through Thee unto God—yet they knew Thee not. Tongues have been loosed, that they might stammer forth Thy remembrance and the loftiness of Thy glory—yet in denial of Thee they speak. Hands have been severed, that they might write the sublimity of Thy bounty and the exaltation of Thy power concerning him that dwelleth in Thy shadow—yet they command his death, and that which beseemeth not the height of Thy holiness. Unto God do I complain of that which hath befallen me and Thee. On that Most Great Day I shall assuredly glory over all beneath me, for none beholdeth what I behold in Thee—Thy right over all things, and Thy lofty rank in the presence of God, Thy Lord.
I followed the truth when I found it, and I believed the verses of God when I heard them. Nay, by Thy might! Though Thou shouldst then be beneath the dust of Thy body, yet the loftiness of Thy power within the realities of souls and the horizons of existence would remain so unassailable that every thing would recognize Thee, and every soul would draw nigh unto God by Thee, as they turn unto their Lord. Were it not for those who first believed among them, they would not recognize Thee, nor bear witness unto Thy station in the presence of God, Thy Lord. Yet sufficient is the testimony God hath borne unto Thee before every spirit; for if all things were to bear witness unto all things, and there were no true testimony save that God hath testified unto that thing as He willeth, by whatsoever He willeth—then, though none should testify, and God should testify, that testimony would suffice that thing; and all things would bear witness unto it, when they came to know the testimony of their Lord concerning it.
I bear witness that Thou hast ascended, with Thy whole being, unto God, glorious and mighty, and hast risen with what was and what shall be unto Thy Creator Who created Thee. I bear witness that the Letters of the Living, every one of them, are of Thy very self; that what God hath made one in the Bayan hath been melted by Thy guidance. Who, then, can refrain from thanking Thee, according to Thy right, or from turning unto God, his Lord, through Thee? Hadst Thou not opened the gate of the Bayan, who would have turned unto God, and who would have known Him?
I testify that every good wherewith the name of good is remembered hath been tasted through Thee, confirmed from Thee, and returneth unto Thee—whilst Thou returnest unto God, bearing witness unto His oneness; abasing Thyself before the Sovereign of His unity; humbled before the King of the might of His singleness; raised up through Thee unto Thee; made to speak, by Thy bounty, in Thy presence, where no one hath any recourse save from Thee. This is an honor whereof all contingent beings glory, in the station of their deeds and their words, and in the end whereunto their affairs return, and their abode and resting-place.
No doubt will God return Thee unto the Point of the Bayan at its latter end, and will adorn Thee with a multiplication of Thy self, until beneath Thy shadow kings most mighty, and learned men preservers, and sages subtle, shall all draw nigh unto God by Thee, and turn unto Thee through Thee—though they recognized Thee not on the day of Thy manifestation, nor bore witness to Thy power. God will try every one who hath professed faith in the Bayan by Thy appearance, on the day when God shall make manifest, time after time, the very soul of the Point of the Bayan in its latter end. On that day shalt thou see how they that professed the Bayan will descend to the court of Thy dust, and will prostrate themselves before Thy greatness. Yet from the first day of Thy manifestation their presence at Thy dust will profit them not, as it profited those who attained unto my dust and thy dust and the dust of the martyrs after my manifestation. God will try every one who hath professed the Bayan by this.
Be Thou compassionate, O my God, unto all Thy creatures; for Thou hast ordained those graves for naught but the glory of that Day, and hast commanded men to gather at those watering-places for no purpose save that Thy servants might stand in attendance before the Manifestations of Thy might. I beseech Thee, O my God, by that Name than which, in Thy knowledge, there is none more exalted, that Thou cast not forth from the Bayan—nor bar from presence before that Letter—any one whose very being is consumed, and who is heedless of what he hath gained. For by Thy might, from the first moment of mine appearing I have known all who have believed in Thee and in Thy signs in the Furqan; yet have I found none to be truly conscious of Thine advent save whom Thou hast willed—souls like pearls of being—such that no soul is wronged, nor any deed rendered vain.
But Thou hast made firm that which I have borne witness unto; and there is no power save through Thee. Through Thee have I accomplished what the masters of crafts accomplish by a single elixir, until I have taken the elixir of faith from every soul, and have commanded the contingent parts according to Thy command. Therefore will I take naught from the Bayan except that Thou make every soul endowed with this elixir capable for the Day of Thine appearing, and of prostration before Thy Gate in the Day of Thy concealment; for verily Thou art over all things potent and powerful.
Then turn thou unto three branches of the Tree, and say: The glory, the Most Exalted Glory, from God, the Lord of the hereafter and the former world, be upon you, O sanctified branches, O inaccessible leaves, O uplifted fruits, so long as the sun shineth and the stars in their dawning-places are illumined. Through you is guided whoso is guided, and through you is led astray whoso is led astray. Upon you from your Lord shall descend that which befitteth the loftiness of His bounty and the sublimity of His holiness. Whatsoever descendeth from the height of His glory shall assuredly descend upon you; and ye shall be exalted above those beneath you; and through you shall they ascend unto God, your Lord. By you descendeth he that descendeth, and by you ascendeth he that ascendeth. There is no might save in God, no greatness save in God, no sovereignty save by the hand of God, no power save within the grasp of God, no protection save in the very Self of God.
Then turn thou unto the martyrs of God in the Holy Land, and say: The Most Exalted Pattern and the Most Beauteous Order, from God, the Possessor of the Most Great signs and the Most Mighty proofs, and the utmost manifestations, and the Most Beautiful Names, and the Loftiest similitudes—be upon you, O leaves of the Tree of the Bayan! How high is your station, how lofty your condition, how exalted your rank, how mighty your seat, how great your severance unto your Lord Who created you, sustained you, caused you to die, and raised you up from the couches of your hearts! May God bless you, on the part of him who believed in Him.
By the life of Him Who made you, on the day of His manifestation, the names of His own Self and the guides unto the sovereignty of His unity on the day of His rising—ye have attained a triumph that vexeth the first and the last, and have obtained a grace coveted by the outward and the inward. Upon your greatness be the greatness of God, and upon your might be the might of God, and upon your riches be the riches of God, and upon your strength be the strength of God, and upon your manifestation be the manifestation of God, and upon your inwardness be the inwardness of God—upon your first and your last, above you and beneath you—whatsoever God hath ordained for you of loftiness and unapproachableness, sublimity and exaltation, severance and opening, dominion and power.
No doubt, could ye but apprehend this, all who have professed the Bayan would hasten to greet you. Yet ye must needs be taken, even as every soul is taken. When ye have attained unto the light of martyrdom and the height of guardianship, this shall be that wherewith the mighty are made mighty and the proud do glory. There is no power nor strength save in God, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting; and there is no glory, nor protection, nor sovereignty, nor exaltation, nor greatness, nor power, nor awe, save with God, the Mighty, the Most Holy.

title: BB00508: Ziyarat for the ten letters
text:
Verily, the glory (Bahá) is from God, and then from every soul that hath believed in God and in His signs. Upon you, O ye ten Letters, and upon all who have ascended unto God together with you, whether of the former or of the latter generations, whether of the seen or of the unseen, be the glory of God.
Unceasingly hath God caused to descend upon you, from every splendour, its most splendid; and from every majesty, its most majestic; and from every beauty, its most beauteous; and from every greatness, its most great; and from every light, its most luminous; and from every mercy, its most expansive; and from all words, their most perfect; and from all Names, their mightiest; and from every might, its mightiest; and from every will, its most effectual; and from every knowledge, its most penetrating; and from every power, its most potent; and from every utterance, that which is most acceptable; and from every supplication, that which is most beloved; and from every sovereignty, its most enduring; and from every glory, its most glorious; and from every exaltation, its most exalted.
That which ye have borne in the path of God is better for you, in the sight of God and of those who know you, than were the dominion of the earth and whatsoever is upon it—yea, and the dominion of such as possess it. For after your passing to your winding-sheets there descended not upon them the succouring hosts of the glorifiers, the sanctifiers, the cherubim, the rank-and-file of the near ones.
But now do they verily descend upon your courts and call down blessings upon you at your tombs; and ye shall return, on the Day of Resurrection, whensoever God, your Lord, shall will, and ye shall assuredly inherit the earth and whoso is upon it whenso God, its Fashioner, shall desire. And ye—ye are, in the loftiness of Paradise, before your Lord, exhilarated with joy; and in the heaven of holiness, before God, do ye celebrate His praise.
What ye have with your Lord, in His knowledge, is greater than that which ye have acquired; for when ye behold, in the life to come, that which ye beheld in the former life, then shall it be manifest. And for such as wrought that deed against you there shall be, as their recompense, no fire more burning than the very work they have accomplished; and what they shall witness after their death shall be naught but the fruit of that same act.
Blessed are ye, and blessed is that which ye have earned in the path of God in every condition. The eyes of them that love you, at what hath befallen you, are as an ocean ever-flowing; and the hearts of your well-wishers, at what ye have endured in the path of God, are as leaves of the olive-tree, all consumed. And naught hath God created in Paradise, as a joy and a delight, to surpass the burning of those hearts in your afflictions and the outpouring of those oceans of blood in your calamity.
Ever do your hearts glorify God in the highest Paradise; your spirits, in the holiness of God, are in the cloud of sanctity; your souls confess the oneness of God upon the pinnacle of nearness and intimacy; and your bodies magnify God in the furthermost pavilion of holiness. How exalted is your tribulation in the realm of origination! For it hath no equal; from the “first” which hath no beginning down to that very hour, and from that same hour onward unto the “last” which hath no end.
And there is no soul that maketh mention of your calamity, and letteth the tears flow down upon his cheeks by reason of the loftiness of your affliction, but that God forgiveth him all that His knowledge embraceth: He, verily, is the Lord of surpassing bounty, the Most Generous. And there is no soul that cometh on pilgrimage unto your exalted ranks, and acknowledgeth your right, and then calleth down blessings upon you, but that God shall, of a certainty, gather him and me together in the highest Paradise. He, verily, is the Lord of surpassing bounty, the All-Glorious, the Most Great.
