title: BB00095: Du’a’ li-Man Yuzhiruhu’llah
text:
A Prayer for Him Whom God shall make manifest
In the Name of God, the Most Inaccessible, the Most Holy
Glory be unto Thee, O God! Thou art God and there is no God but Thee, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, the Lord of all things. Thou hast ever been one God, Single, Individual, Self-Subsisting, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Eternal, the Everlasting. Thou hast taken unto Thyself neither consort nor son, and Thou hast no partner in sovereignty, nor any protector on earth except by Thy leave. Before Thee bow down in worship all who are in the heavens and on earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and before Thee prostrate themselves all who dwell in the kingdoms of Command and Creation and all below them. None possesseth anything except by Thy leave, and none hath aught save what Thou hast ordained by Thy command.
Unto Thee belongeth the most resplendent Glory above all glory, and the most exalted Grandeur above all grandeur, and the most excellent Good-Pleasure above all good-pleasure, and the most effulgent Light above all light, and the most beautiful Names above all names, and the most supreme Greatness above all greatness, and the most mighty Proofs above all proofs. Were I to attempt to mention any of the wondrous manifestations of Thy sovereignty, the oceans of creation and invention would be exhausted before I could mention aught thereof.
Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee. Thou hast ever been the Sustainer of every soul and the Knower of all things, powerful over whatsoever Thou willest and mighty over whatsoever Thou desirest. Nothing escapeth Thy knowledge, whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them, and nothing can frustrate Thee, whether in the kingdom of Command or of Creation or whatsoever lieth below them.
Thou hast created me and made me to know Thyself, then Thou didst send down unto me Thy verses. By Thy glory, I testify before Thee and all things that I have made all words attributed to me into a single Book of nineteen gates, and I have made all of it, from its beginning to its end, its outward and its inward aspects, its exalted and its lowly elements, its hidden and its manifest meanings, as a delightful garden for the Day when Thou shalt return me to earthly life, for that is the mention of Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest on the Day of Resurrection by Thy power, that He may recompense from Thy presence those who have followed the Bayan.
O God! Send down upon the Point of the Bayan in that existence, then in the next existence on the day of His return, and upon those who have recognized His truth and have prostrated themselves before Thee through Him, that which befitteth the loftiness of Thy exaltation, the sublimity of Thy transcendence, the majesty of Thy power, the extensiveness of Thy bounty and favors, the joy of Thy self-subsistence, and the manifestations of Thy signs. For Thou, O my God, art the independent Sovereign of all things and the Ordainer of all things in the heights of the throne of glory. Thou hast created nothing save for Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest on the Day of Resurrection with clear signs, even as Thou didst make me manifest through their appearance from His presence before His rising with clear signs at which all in the kingdoms of earth and heaven were powerless, and before whose greatness all in the kingdom of names and attributes have prostrated themselves.
I beseech Thee, O God, by that Single Temple for Whom and through Whom Thou didst create the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, Whom Thou hast distinguished with the Living Letters before all names, and Whose names Thou hast made Thy names and Thy names His names, since naught can be seen in Him save Thee. I beseech Thee, O God, by all His names from the beginning of numbers to the mention of eternity where no name for them exists in Thy Book, and from the beginning of eternity to Thy Name the Most Often Invoked.
And what You have enumerated for Him of conditions, similitudes, manifestations and attributes, as there is no limit to these with You, nor any measure in the Mother Book. For all that flows from that Most Great Sea—the sea of Your love—and that Mighty Deep—the deep of Your oneness—has neither bound nor number, nor end nor count. It is as though the regions of the seas of His love encompass all who dwell in the kingdoms of heaven and earth and what lies between them, from infinity to infinity, and the rain from the quaking heaven falls upon all who dwell in the kingdom of names and attributes, calling with the Most Exalted Call that this has neither beginning nor end.
Blessed art Thou, O my God, in Thy wondrous handiwork! Exalted art Thou, O my God, in Thy mighty creation! Sanctified art Thou, O my God, in Thy impregnable glory! Glorified art Thou, O my God, in Thy sublime inaccessibility! Honored art Thou, O my God, in Thy gentle joy!
For all similitudes bow down before the countenance of Thy Divinity, and all names emerge not from the horizon of the Unseen save after the name of Thy Identity. Exalted are Thy most beautiful names and magnified are Thy supreme examples in the kingdoms of the hereafter and of the first!
I beseech Thee therefore, O my God, by how Thou hast made Thyself known to all things through the name of Thy Divinity, and hast caused all things to witness the names of Thy Identity, and what Thou hast ordained thereafter in their manifestation. For I, O my God, do at this time turn unto Thee through that divine Countenance, that eternal Face, that sign of oneness, that essence of singleness, that camphor of everlastingness, that pristine sanctity, that essential love, that pure glorification, that personal purpose, that praiseworthy presence, that universal divinity, and through the letters that attend before all Thy names—which are undoubtedly eight before ten, for thus hast Thou manifested from before—and through all Thy names wherein that Point is related to Itself and is revealed through what It casts forth of Its signs.
For all names belong to Thee alone, no partner hast Thou. Thine is the dominion and the kingdom, Thine the might and the power, Thine the strength and the divinity, Thine the grandeur and sovereignty, Thine the rule in the manifestations of creation and of the unseen.
Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, the King, the Sovereign, the Mighty, the Beloved. Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, the Eternal, the Just, the Sovereign, the Self-Subsisting. Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, the Single, the One, the Sovereign, the All-Glorious. Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, the Judge, the Most High, the Sovereign, the Most Holy. Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, the Emperor, the Most Great, the Most High, the Most Holy.
All faces have prostrated themselves before the majesty of Thy countenance, all voices have been hushed before the dawning-place of Thy will, and all within the kingdoms of the heavens and earth and what lies between them have melted away before Thy power.
Thou art He Who hath possessed all kings through Thy power and hath taken possession of all sovereigns through Thy might, and hast ordered whatsoever is in the kingdoms of the heavens and earth and what lies between them through Thy wisdom. Thou art not to be questioned about what Thou doest. Thou decreest what Thou pleasest, how Thou pleasest, through what Thou pleasest, for what Thou pleasest, and Thou doest what Thou willest, how Thou willest, through what Thou willest, for what Thou willest.
All glory be unto him who hath believed in Thee and hath confirmed […] from Thee, and there is no mention with God for whosoever saith concerning Thy deed or what appeareth from Thee “why” or “wherefore,” for his mention is joined with the mention of remoteness and extinction in the presence of Thy power’s manifestation and the exalted exaltation of the rapturous severance of them that love Thee.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Thy proof hath ever been conclusive over all atoms, Thy Will dominant over all contingent beings, Thy Purpose exalted above all that dwelleth in the kingdoms of earth and heaven, and Thy Power supreme over all that abideth in the realms of names and attributes. Thou art the Most High, to Whose loftiness no baseness can be compared, and the Most Exalted, Whose mention can never equal the mention of Thine elevation.
Therefore, I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thy Godhead, Thy Lordship, Thy mercy, Thy oneness, Thy singleness, Thy self-subsistence, Thy might, Thy sovereignty, Thy power, Thy love, Thy strength, Thy divinity, Thy greatness, Thy holiness, Thy dominion, Thy sanctity, Thy countenance, Thy luminosity, Thy face, and Thy grandeur, that Thou wilt forgive, through Thine exalted independence of all things, them that are in the Bayan, and accept the Book of the Vahid and all therein, causing it to ascend unto Thee as Thou pleasest through Thy grace, for this is the utmost that a servant can attain before Thee.
Otherwise, nothing in creation befitteth Thee, and nothing in invention deserveth Thy Being, for everything that is mentioned is but a created thing before Thee, which Thou hast created from nothing by Thy Will and brought into being from naught by Thy Purpose.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! If Thou sayest “I have forgiven the Bayan and all therein,” then it will soar in Thy forgiveness and good-pleasure. And if Thou sayest “Nay,” then I am he who clingeth to the hem of Thy bounty, who imploreth Thee by Thyself, who persistently beseecheth Thee by the right of Thy Lordship. For verily Thou art independent of all that is in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them. The obedience of them that obey Thee profiteth Thee not, nor doth the remoteness of those who are far from the good-pleasure of Thy Self-Subsistence diminish aught from the treasuries of Thy grandeur.
Therefore I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thine independence of all things, to accept the Bayan and all therein. For I have named all that hath appeared from me by that name and made all of it as one Book, a leaf from among the leaves of Thy gardens. Accept it, O my Beloved, for that would be a manifestation of Thy grace and mercy; and if Thou rejectest it, O my Beloved, that would be a manifestation of Thy justice and the independence of Thy Lordship. Thou hast ever been beloved in all Thy doings. By Thy glory! If Thou forgivest the Bayan and all therein, it diminisheth not Thy dominion in any way, and if Thou acceptest not the Bayan and all therein, it addeth not to Thy dominion in any way. Rather, if Thou acceptest it, those perfected hearts will enter beneath the shade of Thy love, and if Thou rejectest it, it will vanish as though it had never been mentioned before.
I beseech Thee, O my God and my Beloved, O my Lord and my Purpose, O my King and my Witness, that Thou wilt not deal with it except through Thy grace, nor look upon it except through Thy bounty and favor, nor reckon with it and those therein except through Thy generosity and kindness. For the servant’s gaze hath ever been and will ever be fixed upon his Master and Lord, and the refuge of the needy one in every condition is his King and the Ultimate Goal of his desire.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! May Thou send down upon Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest on the Day of Resurrection the most resplendent of all Thy glory, the most sublime of all Thy majesty, and of all Thy beauty, the most beauteous; of all Thy grandeur, the most grand; of all Thy light, the most luminous; of all Thy mercy, the most expansive; of all Thy words, the most perfect; of all Thy perfections, the most complete; of all Thy names, the most great; of all Thy glory, the most glorious; of all Thy will, the most resolute; of all Thy knowledge, the most penetrating; of all Thy power, the most mighty; of all Thy utterance, the most pleasing; of all Thy causes, the most beloved; of all Thy honor, the most honorable; of all Thy sovereignty, the most enduring; of all Thy dominion, the most exalted; of all Thy favors, the most elevated; of all Thy signs, the most wondrous; of all Thy might, the most impregnable; and of all things Thou lovest, that which hath no equal, no peer, no likeness, no partner, and no similitude in Thy knowledge.
Preserve it, O my God, within the shelter of Thy Lordship, the sanctuary of Thy Oneness, the protection of Thy glory, the pavilion of Thy grandeur, and the holy mysteries of Thy exaltation from those who recognize not its right and prostrate not themselves before it on the day of its manifestation, by Thy power that hath held the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them, and by Thy might whereby Thou hast prevailed over whatsoever Thou willest, and by Thy glory whereby Thou hast exalted Thyself above all things, and by Thy dominion whereby Thou hast ascended above all things, and by Thy grandeur whereby Thou hast magnified Thyself above all things in Thy sovereignty whereby Thou hast possessed all things, and by the King of Thy uniqueness whereby Thou hast ordained the measures of all things.
For verily it is, O my God, the essence of what Thou hast taken from the Bayan, the pure extract of what Thou hast chosen from the Furqan, the ornament wherewith Thou hast adorned the evidences, and the Manifestation of Thy Lordship which Thou hast bestowed upon the Manifestation of Thy name, the All-Merciful. Send down, O my God, Thy blessings upon its letters, and upon whosoever hath believed in it, whether male or female, and hath prostrated before Thee in recognition of the loftiness of Thy glory, the sublimity of Thy exaltation, the inviolability of Thy independence, and the joy of Thine inaccessibility.
Grant me, O my God, and all who are in the Bayan, to attain unto His presence, and make, O my God, the fruit of all that Thou hast ordained to be realized on the day of meeting Him, and make, O my God, my best days to be the days of meeting Him, and my best hours those hours wherein Thou bringest me into His presence and enablest me to prostrate before Him, and to receive that which appeareth from the horizon of His bounty or is concealed in the treasuries of His glory. For verily He is the Temple of Thy Divinity in the kingdom of Thy heaven and Thy earth, through Whom all that hath beginning began and unto Whom all that returneth doth return, through Whom the Day of Resurrection is established, through Whom Thou gatherest whomsoever Thou willest, through Whom Thou resurrected whomsoever Thou willest, through Whom Thou spreadest abroad whomsoever Thou willest, and through Whom Thou presentest whatsoever Thou willest.
I beseech Thee, O my God, by the hours of His life from beginning to end, and by what Thou hast witnessed of the subtle signs of His belovedness and the wondrous manifestations of His praised nature, that Thou shouldst bless at that time His father and His mother, and those whom Thou hast joined with Him in His household, and those whom Thou hast honored through their relationship to Him among His near kindred, and those who follow His good-pleasure and strive in the presence of His sovereignty when He permitteth them through Thy creation and the wondrous artistry of Thy inaccessibility.
O my God! Through Him exalt what Thou hast magnified for the people of the Bayan, and send down through Him what hath been asked for by those who have believed in the Bayan. For there is no glory for anyone except in obedience to Him, and no abasement for anyone except in failing to follow His will. Should the lowliest of creation prostrate before Him and follow Him, he would be the most exalted in the sight of God; and should the most exalted of creation neither prostrate before Him nor follow His command, he would be the most abased, for there is no honor for anything except through its relation to Him. How many are the servants, O my God, who supplicate night and day for His day, yet when Thou dost manifest Him, they remain veiled by that which they possess of that which is as nothing. Therefore, O my God, send down Thy mercy upon these souls that they may not be veiled by anything from their Lord, and that their deeds may not be rendered vain by their being deprived of the meeting with their Beloved. Verily, Thou hast power over all things. Thou guidest whom Thou pleasest by Thy command, and Thy mercy hath preceded Thy God-fearing servants.

title: BB00231: Du’a’al-Avval fi Ardi’l’A’la, lil-Murtada
text:
Thou art sufficient unto me. In Thee do I place my trust, and in Thee let Thy believing servants place their trust. There is no power nor strength save in God, the Most High, the Most Great.
Prayer of the Dawning-Place in the Land of the Most High by Murtada
In the Name of God, the Most Impregnable, the Most Holy!
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I testify, and all things testify, that Thou art God and there is no God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thine is the kingdom and the dominion, Thine the might and the power, Thine the strength and the divinity, Thine the force and sovereignty, Thine the grandeur and the glory, Thine the countenance and the beauty, Thine the face and the perfection, Thine the greatness and independence, Thine the loftiness and majesty, Thine the greatness and pride, Thine the proofs and examples, Thine the power and deeds, Thine the might and exaltation, Thine the force and elevation, Thine the joy and gladness, Thine the authority and detachment from all Thy servants, and Thine is whatsoever Thou hast loved or lovest of what Thou hast created or wilt create. All belongeth unto Thee alone. There is no God but Thee. Thou hast ever given life and caused death, then caused death and given life, and verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not, the King Who passeth not away, the Just Who wrongeth not, the Sovereign Who changeth not, the One from Whose grasp nothing escapeth, whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
Hallowed be Thy name, O my God, and exalted be Thy similitudes, O my Beloved! Thou hast ever been one God, Single, Eternal, Self-Subsisting, Living, Self-Sufficient, Wise, Just, Holy, Transcendent, Inaccessible, Exalted, Trusted, Everlasting, Eternal. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, nor hath there been any partner in what Thou hast created, nor any protector in what Thou hast fashioned. Thou hast established all things by Thy Will and ordained the creation of all things by Thy Purpose. All must worship Thee in the heights of Thy Oneness, all must prostrate themselves before Thee in the summit of Thy Unity, all must testify to Thy Oneness in the inaccessibility of Thy Singleness, all must magnify Thee in the exaltation of Thy divine verses, and all must glorify Thee for what Thou art in the kingdom of Thy bountiful might.
Thou wert before all things, Thou art after all things, Thou art above all things, Thou art the Fashioner of all things, and Thou art distinguished by the essence of Thy Being above all things. The attributes are confounded in Thee, and the essences of all beings are manifest in the wonders of Thy handiwork. Thou art He Who hath no equal, no peer, no likeness, no companion, no similitude, and Thou art He Who begetteth not, nor wast Thou begotten, Who cannot be limited or described by any similitude.
Therefore, O God, send Thy blessings upon the Tree of Thy love—its root, its branch, its twigs, its leaves, and its fruits—through the glory of Thy most glorious Beauty, through Thy most sublime Majesty, through Thy most beauteous Beauty, through Thy most mighty Greatness, through Thy most luminous Light, through Thy most vast Mercy, through Thy most perfect Words, through Thy most great Names, through Thy most mighty Power, through Thy most efficacious Will, through Thy most penetrating Knowledge, through Thy most extensive Power, through Thy most pleasing Word, through Thy most beloved and impregnable Causes, through Thy most noble Honor, through Thy most enduring Sovereignty, through Thy most glorious Dominion, through Thy most exalted Loftiness, and through what Thou art of Thy grace, Thy generosity, Thy bounty, and Thy kindness.
For all are Thy servants and in Thy grasp. The dwellers of Thy heaven and earth glorify Thee, and those in the kingdom of Thy Command and Creation prostrate themselves before Thee. Who is able to worship Thee as befitteth Thy worship, or to know Thee as befitteth Thy knowledge? Verily, what Thou createst by Thy Command, Thou bringest forth from nothing by Thy power and sustainest without means by Thy strength. I testify, and all things testify, that all are Thy servants, Thy worshippers, Thy supplicants, Thy rememberers, Thy thankful ones, Thy submissive ones, and Thy humble ones, for Thou hast created them, sustained them, caused them to die, given them life, and ordained for them their paths, according to what is possible for them within the bounds of Thy power. Otherwise, how could that which Thou dost merit manifest itself in creation, and how could it be realized in invention? This is that which no heart hath encompassed in knowledge from the beginning of thought, nor can the essence of those possessed of insight and vision bear witness unto it.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Thy power hath risen to such heights that all things fall short of attaining unto it. Thy grandeur hath been exalted to such a degree that all existence is bewildered before it. Thy sovereignty hath been elevated to such heights that all affairs submit to Thy will. Thy will hath prevailed over whatsoever Thou hast desired with such supremacy that all Thy creation must needs bow before it, through what Thou hast ordained therein of the expressions of Thy Command and the wonders of Thy wisdom.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I shall glorify Thee above all that the glorifiers have glorified, sanctify Thee beyond all that the sanctifiers have sanctified, unite Thee beyond all that the uniters have united, and magnify Thee beyond all that the magnifiers have magnified, and exalt Thee beyond all that the exalters have exalted. For the highest that my heart can comprehend is but a creation with Thee—how then can I know Thee through it? And the utmost that my being can witness is but a trace of what Thou hast established out of nothing by Thy power—how then can I draw evidence thereby unto Thee?
Glorified art Thou! There is no knowledge save for him who knoweth Thee and serveth Thee and feareth Thy justice and hopeth for Thy grace and is exalted through the exaltation of Thy Cause. For there is no glory except in Thy love and good-pleasure and obedience and fear of Thee, and in detachment unto Thee and abiding beneath the shade of Thy gracious favors and the expressions of Thy Command.
Praise be to Thee, O my God, for that Thou hast made me to know Thine own Self, and hast given me to drink from the rivers of Thy paradise through Thy signs, Thy words, Thine attributes, and Thy manifestations. Thine is the Most Exalted Loftiness, according to that which Thou dost deserve, and Thine is the Most Glorious Sublimity, according to that which Thou lovest to bear witness unto Thy creation. By Thy might! All Thy creatures are, in Thy sight, even as the day whereon Thou didst create them; their existence addeth nothing unto Thy dominion, neither doth their absence diminish aught from Thy dominion. Nay, honour belongeth to Thy loved ones through that they have proclaimed Thy unity, have known Thee, have obeyed Thee, and have hoped in Thee.
Therefore do I cause Thee—and all Thy creatures—to bear witness that every object of worship beside Thee is in the Fire. In truth none is worthy of worship save Thee alone; there is none other God but Thee. I have not worshipped Thee with the worship that is Thy due, nor known Thee with the knowledge that is Thy due, nor remembered Thee with the remembrance befitting Thy Self-Subsisting Being, nor praised Thee with the praise worthy of Thy singleness, nor thanked Thee with the thanksgiving due unto Thy Self-Sufficiency. All is from Thee, and by Thee, and unto Thee. Thou alone art God; there is none other God but Thee.
Thou hast made Thyself known through the revelation of that which Thou hast ascribed unto Thine own Self; and thus have those who seek to know been enabled to know, in their firstness and their lastness, their outwardness and their inwardness, their loftiness and their sublimity, their exaltation and their unapproachableness. And those who are veiled have remained veiled in that which they are, after that Thy proof hath been made complete against them, and Thy favours and Thy bounties have been perfected within them and for them. Glorified art Thou and exalted above all! Glorified art Thou and sanctified beyond all! Glorified art Thou and magnified above all! Glorified art Thou and praised above all!
All Thy servants are in Thy grasp, that they may know Thee according to the station wherein Thou hast revealed Thyself unto them, and may prostrate themselves before Thee for that which Thou hast bestowed, through what Thou hast made known of Thy religion. Yet all are in a veil save such as have known Thee and believed in Thy signs; for in this lieth the spirit of true reality, and herein is the loftiness of recognition.
Glorified art Thou: there is none other God but Thee. From everlasting Thou dost uplift whom Thou willest by Thy exaltation, and enrich whom Thou willest by Thy bounty, and aid whom Thou willest by Thy might, and send down the wondrous traces of Thy mercy upon the denizens of the heaven of Thy obedience. Thine is the glory, O Possessor of munificence, and Thine is the praise, O Possessor of justice. Thou givest life and Thou causest death; then Thou causest death and Thou givest life; and Thou art the Living Who dieth not. Within Thy grasp is the dominion of all things; Thou createst whatsoever Thou willest by Thy command. Verily Thou hast ever been powerful over all things.

title: BB00259: Du’a’ath-Thani fi Ardi’l’A’la li-Karbala’I Mustafa Quli
text:
The Second Prayer in the Most Exalted Land—Al-Karbala’i Mustafa Quli
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I testify, and all things testify, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thine is the dominion of the earth and heavens, Thine is might and power divine, Thine is strength and glory sublime, Thine is force and dominion in time, Thine is sovereignty o’er all that doth shine, Thine is majesty and grandeur combined, Thine is beauty and perfection designed, Thine is glory and excellence defined, Thine is independence and dominion sublime, Thine is majesty and exaltation divine, Thine is power none can confine, Thine is joy and delight that doth shine, Thine is greatness and pride none can define, Thine are the names and attributes divine.
Thou hast ever been One God, Single, Eternal, Self-Subsisting, All-Wise, All-Just, Most Holy. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, no partner hast Thou in creation, no helper in Thy handiwork. Thou didst create all things by Thy power and fashion all things by Thy will. Thou dost ever give life and death, then death and life, and verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not, the Sovereign Who passeth not away, the Just Who wrongeth not, the King Who changeth not, the Single One from Whose grasp nothing escapeth, whether in the heavens or on earth or between them. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command; verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
Sanctified are Thy likenesses and exalted are Thy attributes. Thou hast ever been triumphant above all contingent things, manifest above all existing things, unapproachable above all created things, elevated above all essences, transcendent above all who dwell in the kingdoms of earth and heaven. All are Thy servants and within Thy grasp. The dwellers of Thy heaven and earth worship Thee, and they who abide in the kingdom of Thy Command and creation sanctify Thee. Thou hast ever been supreme over all things and powerful over all things. There is nothing that doth not glorify Thy praise, sanctify Thy remembrance, magnify Thy praise, worship Thee as befitteth Thy glory, and detach itself unto Thee as befitteth Thy justice.
Thou didst create all things from nothing by Thy power, and provided for all in the kingdom of command and creation by Thy will. Thou didst cause to die whom Thou didst will among Thy creation by Thy might, and didst give life to whom Thou didst desire among the dwellers of Thy heaven and earth by Thy mercy and the sublimity of Thy grandeur. Thou art the One Who existed before all things, Who will exist after all things, Who brought all things into being, Who will remain after all things, Who causes all things to pass away.
Exalted is the Manifestation of Thy Cause, sanctified is the likeness of Thy sovereign justice, and glorified are the Manifestations of the might of Thy holy dominion above the ability of all contingent things to praise Thee as Thou art, or all existing things to sanctify Thee as Thou deservest. Thou hast ever created from nothing by Thy power and decreed what Thou didst love by the sovereignty of Thy Lordship. All Thy servants, worshippers, suppliants, and celebrants are ever enchanted by the holy fragrances of Thy might that glorify Thee, and illumined by the manifestations of Thy majestic glory that proclaim Thy oneness.
Thou art He Who hath taken neither consort nor son, and Thy Being hath never been joined with any manifestation of Thy creation. Thou didst bring into being all that Thou didst create by Thy will, originate all that Thou didst originate by Thy desire, generate all that Thou didst generate by Thy power, and invent all that Thou didst invent by Thy purpose. Thou art He Who sent forth the Messengers to manifest Thy power and revealed the Books to exalt Thy sovereignty, and created what Thou didst will of the varieties of Thy creation by the wondrous might of Thy oneness.
How near art Thou to Thy creation, how generous art Thou to Thy servants, how exalted art Thou above the dwellers of Thy heaven and earth, how established art Thou above all who dwell in the kingdom of Thy command and creation! Thou didst hold back the heavens from falling upon the earth by Thy power, and didst hold the earth above the water by Thy grandeur. Thine is the most sublime elevation above all who possess elevation and exaltation, and Thine is the most glorious ascendancy above all who possess ascendancy. The splendours of Thy wondrous gifts have ever descended upon those who love Thee, and the manifestations of Thy Cause upon those who are sanctified by Thee. Glorified art Thou above all that hath glorified Thee or shall ever glorify Thee, and exalted art Thou above all that hath sanctified Thee or shall ever sanctify Thee. Thou hast established all the paths Thou hast established for the recognition of Thy Self-Subsistence, and Thou hast originated all the wonders Thou hast created for the manifestation of Thy Divine Unity.
I beseech Thee, O my God, to send down upon the guides to Thy Self, the manifestations of Thy Cause, the repositories of Thy creation, and the treasuries of Thy words, that which beseemeth Thy grace and Thy bounty, Thy generosity and Thy glory, Thy favor and Thy beneficence, Thy munificence and Thy sovereignty, Thy bestowal and Thy majesty. For verily Thou art powerful over what Thou willest and mighty over what Thou desirest. Thou createst what Thou pleaseth and ordainest what Thou wishest. None hath any power save through Thee alone. There is no God but Thee. Glory be to Thee, I have ever been of those who remember Thee.
I testify before Thee, O my God, concerning that which was asked of the Point of the Furqan and His living Letters, that on the Day of Resurrection the Command is Thine alone. There is no God but Thee, and verily all, whether of the past or of the future, shall be brought before Thee, and that which draweth them nigh unto Thee is their acknowledgment of Thy oneness without hesitation at Thy saying “Am I not your Lord?” And verily that which appeared aforetime from the chosen ones of Thy Self was because they were the thrones of Thy Cause, and therefore Thou didst grant unto each what Thou didst grant, and that Day was none other than the Day of Presentation. Glory be to Thee, there is no God but Thee. Glory be to Thee, I have ever been of those who remember Thee.
I bear witness that whosoever looketh upon the essence of the acknowledgment of the manifestation of Thy creation, which is the ultimate essence of knowledge and deed, shall testify that those who responded to Thee in Thy previous Manifestation, since there are no limits to the conditions of Thy creation that anyone can define, and this in Thy Book none can witness except the one inspired, and whatsoever hath been mentioned attributed to the Manifestations of Thy Cause of old […]

title: BB00253: Du’a’ath-Thalith fi Ardi’l’A’la li-Karbala’I Fath-’Ali
text:
The third prayer in the Land of the Most High for Karbila’i Fath-ʿAli
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I bear witness unto Thee, and unto all things, that Thou art God; there is none other God but Thee. Thine are creation and command, from before and from after.
From everlasting Thou hast been God—One, Single, Self-Subsisting, Unique, Living, Ever-Abiding, the Ruler, the Just, the Holy. Thou hast taken unto Thyself neither consort nor child; Thou hast had no partner in what Thou hast created, nor any helper in what Thou hast wrought. Thou hast created all things by Thy power, in due measure, and hast fashioned the creation of all things by Thy will, with perfect form. Thou art He before Whom all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth and whatsoever lieth between them prostrate themselves; and all who are in the realms of command and creation and whatsoever is beneath them are humble and submissive.
From everlasting Thou hast been God—One, Single, Self-Subsisting, Unique, Living, Ever-Abiding. Thou hast taken unto Thyself neither consort nor child; Thou hast had no partner in what Thou hast created, nor any helper in what Thou hast wrought. Thou didst rear up the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them out of nothing, by Thy command; then didst Thou create the creation of all things through Thy power, and didst provide sustenance for the creation of all things through Thy will. Thou didst cause all things to die through the sovereignty of the might of Thy oneness, and didst quicken all things through the abodes of the might of Thy Self-Sufficiency.
Thou art the One Who existed before all things and Thou art the Creator of all things. Glorified and exalted art Thou! Glorified and manifest art Thou! Glorified and beauteous art Thou! Glorified and illumined art Thou! Glorified and merciful art Thou! Glorified and compassionate art Thou! Glorified and perfect art Thou! Glorified and mighty art Thou! Glorified and wise art Thou! Glorified and well-pleased art Thou! Glorified and sovereign art Thou! Glorified and dominant art Thou! Glorified and manifest art Thou! Glorified and hidden art Thou! Glorified and holy art Thou!
There hath ever been nothing like unto Thee, nor any equal, nor any likeness, nor any companion, nor any similitude. I shall sanctify Thee above all that hath sanctified Thee or shall sanctify Thee, and I shall glorify Thee above all that hath glorified Thee or shall glorify Thee, and I shall testify to Thy oneness with all that hath testified or shall testify to Thy oneness, and I shall magnify Thee above all that hath magnified or shall magnify Thee, and I shall exalt Thee above all that hath exalted or shall exalt Thee.
Thou hast created all things from nothing that they might worship Thee, prostrate themselves before Thee, magnify Thee, exalt Thee and sanctify Thee. Thou hast made Thyself known in every Revelation through what Thou hast manifested of Thy Self. Thus have the recognizers in every Revelation recognized through what Thou hast caused them to know through Thy signs, and the veiled have been veiled through what Thou hast completed as Thy proof against them. Thereby hath been realized in the kingdom of command and creation the existence of negation and affirmation, and what Thou hast ordained of heaven and hell.
Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee, the One, the Almighty. Thy bounties have ever shone upon the dwellers of Thy kingdom, and Thy gifts have ever been bestowed upon those in the kingdom of command and creation. By Thy grace Thou dost provide for whomsoever Thou willest, and by Thy generosity Thou dost cause to enter Paradise whomsoever Thou desirest, and by Thy favor Thou dost ordain whatsoever Thou willest from Thy presence.
Thine is the most exalted loftiness, O my God, above all loftiness and exaltation, and Thine is the most resplendent sublimity, O my Beloved, above all sublimity and glory. Thou hast described Thyself, and verily Thou art above what the describers say. Thine is the kingdom and the dominion, Thine the might and the power, Thine the strength and the divinity, Thine the force and the essence, Thine the sovereignty and human nature, Thine the might and the majesty, Thine the dominion and perfection, Thine the power and action, Thine the countenance and beauty, Thine the similitude and example, Thine the grandeur and pride, Thine the power and ascendancy, Thine the joy and gladness, Thine the greatness and independence.
The dwellers of Thy kingdom have ever been and shall ever be Thy servants and worshippers, and all within the kingdom of Thy command and creation shall forever remain Thy possessions and remembrancers. Is there anything, O my God, that doth not prostrate itself before Thee through its essence, its identity, its self, its being, its beginning, its end, its outward aspect, its inward reality, its height, its depth, and in all that pertains to its final state and abode? Glorified and exalted art Thou at every good thing that prostrateth itself before Thee through what Thou hast ordained.
In all his deeds he worshipeth Thee through what Thou hast brought into being, for the contingent realm hath ever circled and will continue to circle round Thy Will, and in all conditions the one drawn unto Thee experienceth the power of Thy sovereignty. Unto Thee, O my God, ascendeth the work of all who dwell in the kingdom of creation and command, and before Thee bow down the essences of all who inhabit the kingdom of heaven and earth. Thou beholdest the dwellers of Thy heaven and earth, and observest the essences of Thy creation and what their hands have wrought. When one is purified solely for Thee—there is no God but Thee—or is sanctified from all else beside Thee, then dost Thou remember him as befitteth Thy grace, according to what the contingent beings deserve before Thy presence. Otherwise, none in the kingdom of Thy command and creation can comprehend what Thou art, much less find Thee.
Glorified and exalted art Thou! We have ever worshipped none but Thee, sought none except Thee, desired naught besides Thee, and mentioned none but Thee alone—there is no God but Thee. For all else besides Thee, unto whatever heights they may ascend, the limits of their essence returneth only to a collection of constraints, and their realities are bound to orbital geometries, their essences having been kneaded with the waters of allusions through what their hands have wrought.
Thou art far above whatsoever the contingent beings have described Thee with or shall describe Thee, and Thou art sanctified beyond all that created things have mentioned of Thee or shall mention. When I ascend to Thy remembrance, I must needs sanctify Thee from my remembrance, and when I rise to praise Thee, I am bound to exalt Thee above my praise. If this be true of the highest station to which the name of existence can be attributed, how much more so of that which befitteth not Thy holy majesty nor is worthy of Thy glorious court!
Glorified and exalted art Thou! All Thy servants are in Thy grasp. Through following Thee, the monotheists have entered the pavilions of Thy good-pleasure, while the veiled ones are concealed through what their hands have wrought, according to what Thou hast promised them of Thy might. Glorified and exalted, hallowed and sanctified art Thou! I have never awaited aught from Thee save that Thou hast perfected the creation of all things by Thy command and completed Thy favors and bounties upon the dwellers of Thy earth and heaven.
Praise be unto Thee, O my God, with praise befitting Thy right over Thy creation, and glory be unto Thee, O my Beloved, according to how Thou hast described Thyself. Glorified and exalted art Thou! Thou givest life and causest death, then causest death and givest life. Verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not, the King Who passeth not away, the Just Who wrongeth not, the Sovereign Who changeth not, and the Single One from Whose grasp nothing escapeth, whether in the heavens or on earth or between them. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.

title: BB00271: on the Hadith of ‘the Land of Paradise’
text:
In the name of God, the Most Great, the Most Great
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I bear witness, and all things bear witness, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone without peer. Thine is the kingdom and the dominion, Thine the might and the omnipotence, Thine the power and divinity, Thine the strength and glory, Thine the sovereignty and the earthly realm, Thine the majesty and grandeur, Thine the countenance and beauty, Thine the face and perfection, Thine the similitudes and parables, Thine the stations and magnificence, Thine the glory and invincibility, Thine the power and exaltation, Thine the greatness and independence, Thine the grandeur and sublimity, Thine the joy and gladness, Thine the sovereignty and might, and Thine whatsoever Thou hast loved or wilt love in the kingdom of Thy Cause and creation.
Thou hast ever been one God, single, eternal, self-subsisting, ever-living, all-compelling, sovereign, all-subduing, holy, everlasting, inaccessible, exalted, supreme, possessing, glorious, powerful. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, nor hath there been any partner in what Thou hast created, nor any protector in what Thou hast fashioned. By Thy wisdom hast Thou ordered the kingdom of Thy heaven and earth, and by Thy will hast Thou perfected the affairs of all in the kingdom of Thy Cause and creation.
Thou hast ever been supreme above all contingent things, manifest above all existing things, inaccessible above all created things, exalted above all atoms, transcendent above all in the kingdoms of earth and heaven, sovereign above all in the kingdom of names and attributes, and powerful above all in creation. Sanctified are all Thy names, and exalted are all Thy parables. Thou hast made Thyself known to all things while nothing knoweth Thee, and Thou art hidden from all things while nothing findeth Thee. Thou art the Manifest above all things, and the Hidden beneath all things, the First before all things, and the Last after all things.
All glorify Thee, all sanctify Thee, all magnify Thee, all extol Thee, all proclaim Thy greatness, all prostrate before Thee, all are detached unto Thee, all are guided to Thee, all are victorious through Thee, all bow down before Thee, all turn their faces toward Thee. Thou hast ever been forgiving through bounty and grace, and compelling through might and justice. Thy giving is grace from Thy bounty, and Thy withholding is justice.
O God! Do Thou enrich all Thy creation from Thy presence, and send down upon all Thy evidence the dawning-places of Thy grace. Inspire all with Thy remembrance and gratitude, with the victory of Thy chosen ones and martyrs, with tranquility in Thy remembrance, with assurance in Thy grace, with fear of Thee and longing for Thee.
Glorified and exalted art Thou! Thou art He Who hath apportioned among Thy servants the measures to which they are proceeding, and granted to each one that which causeth his tongue to speak Thy praise and createth in him longing for Thy meeting and nearness. Praise be unto Thee, O my God, praise that filleth Thy heaven with the manifestation of Thy glory and Thy earth with the dawning of Thy holiness, and what lieth between them with the exaltation of Thy Cause and the invincibility of Thy remembrance.
Glorified, glorified art Thou! Thou hast favored none except through Thy knowledge, Thy love, Thy meeting, Thy affection and Thy good-pleasure. Do Thou send down upon the land wherein Thou hast caused Thy chosen ones to enter Thy paradise the highest of what may be in its surroundings that may cause their hearts to be firmly established in Thy religion, strengthen them through Thy power against those beneath them among Thy creation, purify them through Thy manifestation from all besides Thee among Thy servants. Send down the blessings of heaven upon them through Thy grace, bring forth for them the blessings of earth through Thy bounty, preserve them from before them and behind them, from their right and their left, from above their heads and beneath their feet […] enrich them through Thy riches, glorify them through Thy glory, assist them through Thy help, support them through Thy signs, and nurture them through Thy words.
Glorified and exalted art Thou! Thou art He Whose mercy hath encompassed all contingent things and Whose gifts surround every atom of existence. O my God! Shower upon Thy servants from the treasuries of Thy grace that which shall content them, and from the wonders of Thy bounty that which shall give them peace, and cause them to appear on earth through Thy manifestation and strengthen them on earth through Thy power. Glorified and exalted art Thou! Thou art He Who causeth every soul to move according to what it hath earned. Thou admittest whom Thou willest into Thy love and good-pleasure, which is the highest of Thy heavens and Thy paradise, and Thou deniest whom Thou willest from recognizing Thy Proof and His good-pleasure—that is the fire which Thou hast promised to the sinning among Thy servants.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! By Thy might, I seek refuge with Thee in this life from that fire, for whoso entereth therein entereth after his death. And I beseech Thee for that paradise, for whoso entereth into the love of Thy Proof and His recognition shall enter therein after his death. Glorified and exalted art Thou! All worship Thee—some behold this with their eyes while others worship unknowingly. The heavens worship Thee through their steadfastness, the celestial spheres through their motion, the sun through its radiance, the moon through its light, the stars through their rising and setting, the earth through its stability, the mountains through their elevation, the seas through their waves, the trees through their fruits, and all things through that which proclaimeth their highest glory before Thee—such is their worship of Thee before Thine eyes.
Glorified and exalted art Thou! Thou hast said—and Thy word is the truth—“there is nothing that doth not glorify His praise.” Yea, by Thy might, there is nothing that doth not glorify Thee from the beginning that hath no beginning unto the end that hath no end. Thou hast sent down Thy most beautiful names in Thy Words and Tablets, and bestowed them upon whom Thou willest among Thy creation as a mark of honor from Thee and a bounty from Thy presence, from Thy gifts.
O God! Send down upon all Thy guides, those who were and those who will be, that which shall show them the good of their world and their hereafter. Verily, Thou givest life and causeth death, then causeth death and givest life, and verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not, and the King Who passeth not away, and the Just Who wrongeth not, and the Sovereign Who changeth not, and the Single One from Whose grasp escapeth nothing whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command. Verily, Thou art powerful over what Thou willest.

title: The Bab—Prayers (1848-1850)
text: Volume 023-023. Contains 113 writings.

title: BB00349: Ziyarat li-Hurufi’l-’isma
text:
In the Name of God, the All-Bestowing, the Most Gentle.
I call God—and all whom His knowledge encompasseth—to witness that there is no God but He, the Ever-Abiding, the Most Holy, the Most Exalted. Again I call Him to witness over all that He hath originated and shall yet originate, according to His good-pleasure and His will: verily, there is no God but He, the All-High, the All-Great.
Every simple essence that hath emerged from the court of the nearness of the Sovereign of Eternity, and every pure camphor of splendor that hath shone from the presence of the King—first remembered—together with His manifestations at the wellsprings of causes, and with what revealed itself by its very self in the blackest night—be upon Thee, O Beloved, O Lord of the All-Exalted, the Most High! And upon Thee, O Dreaded One, O utmost object of my desire in the world to come and in this first life!
No doubt remaineth that Thy knowledge embraceth all things, Thy power prevaileth over all things, Thy will subdueth all things, Thy purpose is executed ere all things, Thy sovereignty is manifest above all things, Thy words are perfected after all things, and Thy manifestations stand firm with all things. And yet—according to what God, thy Lord, hath taught me—how shall I make mention of Thy praises, or cling to the fringes of Thy bounties and Thy gifts? For whatsoever the servant mentioneth is referred back unto himself, returned to his own limit, banished within the confines of his bounds, and cut off from the station of nearness and presence.
Nay, by Thy might! I have not truly made mention of Thee aforetime, neither have I a portion in Thy nearness. Had I known the path, I would have been the first of them that remember. I sought not the dawning of Thy Being, nor do I seek it; and had I known the proof, I would have been the first to hasten unto Thee, to gaze upon Thee, to find repose with Thee, and to delight in Thy companionship. But now—how can I attain thereto, when the heights of denial are barred from every quarter, and the utmost summit of exaltation is veiled from every gaze?
Glorified be God, thy Lord! The very grandeur hath bowed before the majesty of the sovereignty of Thy might, and assuredly it faileth to discharge Thy due. Sanctified are all manifestations, in the secrets of their hearts, through turning unto Thy Countenance; yet, of a certainty, they tremble and are afraid before the sovereignty of Thy justice and the evidences of Thy dominion.
Glorified be God, and praise be unto Him, for He hath numbered me among those who grasp the cord of His guardianship, and among the assured in what God hath decreed for Thee of His mighty decree and His bounteous gifts. By Thy glory and Thy majesty! Were it not that Thou hast forbidden Thy lovers to despair of Thy mercy and to lose hope in the portals of Thy loving-care, then, in view of the limits of my soul and the faults of my being, I would have been the first of the despairing and the last of the despondent. But since, through Thy grace, Thou hast made that attribute unlawful to the people of Thy love, and hast forbidden it to the people of Thy allegiance, I have burned in the fire of remembering myself, yet remained hopeful of Thy favor and Thy mention. I have marked the sighs of my soul whenever it is conjoined with aught save the effulgence of Thy might; yet I have not despaired of the path of Thy care, nor of the springs of Thy mercy.
By Thy might! My rebellion is not like the rebellion of Thy servants; for I knew the Lord of the servants, then set myself against Him by the rising of opposites and rivals. What sin, then, is greater than that I should remember myself before Thee? What fault more grievous than that my existence should subsist in Thy presence? Nay, by Thy glory! The servant’s mention of his Lord is a sin not matched by all sins; a blemish not equaled by all blemishes; a grief not balanced by all griefs. I call God to witness—He is the Truth, the Knower of things unseen.
Had my disobedience been like that of the people of splendors, my occupation that of the folk of allusions, my deeds those performed by souls immersed in the billows of limitations—then had I been free and at rest over against the City of Thy might, for such things are as nothing that Thou shouldst question me thereon or take me to task for them; and they are forgiven their people when they turn unto Thee and repent thereof. But how shall I fare, when every time I ascend, seeking to unify God by His own remembrance, I behold my soul and its remembrance? Each time I would be lifted up to drink from the cup of God’s love, I perceive the love of myself for itself.
Unto Thee, then, is the flight, O King, O All-Subduing! Unto Thee is the refuge, O Sovereign, O All-Bestowing! I flee unto Thee with my whole being, my oneness, and the quintessence of my praise. Had not the knowledge of Thy Lord encompassed my confession of His oneness, it had been better for me; for before I affirmed His unity I bore but a single fault, whereas after my confession it is as though I bore every fault and acquired every sin: my mention of His mention is a sin; my mention of myself is a sin; the coupling of the two is a sin; their separation a sin; their union a sin; the gaze at this a sin, and the gaze at that a sin. These are seven gates whose fires are kindled on every side, whose columns are filled with sighs from every corner.
There is no escape save that I alight in Thy court; no refuge save that I cling to Thy threshold. For with Thee there is no mention save His mention, no splendor save His splendor, no praise save His praise, no exaltation save His exaltation, no nearness save His nearness, no manifestation save His manifestation, no concealment save His concealment. Therefore hath God commanded all to return unto Him, to repair unto Thee, to acknowledge Thy guardianship, to arise in obedience unto Thee, to hold fast to the cord of Thy protection, and to behold the lights of the effulgence of Thy Countenance.
Here am I, casting before Thee the very being of my identity and its essence. Do with it what beseemeth the sovereignty of Thy mercy and accordeth with the majesty and beauty of the King of Thy tenderness, Thy kindness, Thy loving care, Thy generosity, Thy favor, and Thy bounties. For whatever I mention is a sin after a sin; whenever I seek forgiveness, it is a fault after a fault; whenever I repent unto God, it is disobedience upon disobedience—such is all that proceedeth from the servant.
Deal, then, with me—and with whomsoever hath turned unto me—even as God hath dealt with Thee; He made Thee the guardian of His own Self in the kingdom of His Command and His creation; He entrusted to Thee the affairs of His dominion; He vouchsafed Thee what describers cannot describe, what the severed cannot attain, what the counters cannot reckon, what the knowers cannot know.
Verily, we are God’s, and unto Him shall we return. In Thee have I put my trust; unto our Lord do we turn in longing. He sufficeth us—there is no God but He. Unto Him do we commit our affairs, and upon Him do we rely in all that He hath decreed for us. And upon God, then, let the believers rely. Glorified be God, the Lord of the heavens, the Lord of all the worlds.

title: BB00386: Du’a’-i-Salavat-i-Muhammad
text:
In the Name of God, the Exalted, the Inaccessible
O God! Thou art the Creator of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them. Thou didst create Muhammad—Thy blessings be upon him—by Thy command, and didst choose him for Thy covenant, and didst select him for Thy remembrance, and didst single him out for Thy providence, and didst place him above all Thy Prophets and Messengers, and didst establish him upon the station of the sovereignty of Thy oneness in the kingdom of Thy earth and the heaven of Thy lordship, that he might convey unto all things that Thou art God, that there is no God but Thee, and that all else besides Thee is Thy creation and within Thy grasp. Thou hast ever been one God, single, unique, self-subsisting, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, nor hast Thou chosen for Thyself any geometry or number.
O God! Send blessings upon Muhammad with all Thy glory, for he hath borne Thy revelation, and delivered Thy messages, and recited Thy verses, and exalted Thy majesty, and warned of Thy might and power, and given glad tidings of what lieth with Thee of the manifestations of Thy divinity, and the revelations of Thy sovereignty, and the signs of Thy kingdom, and the stations of Thy self-subsistence, where there is no end to the appearance of Thy creation nor to the principles of Thy invention. Therefore, O God, send blessings upon Muhammad superior to what Thou hast bestowed upon any of Thy creation, and upon him what Thou hast specially conferred upon any of Thy servants, and more exalted than what Thou hast graciously bestowed upon any of Thy chosen ones, and more glorious than what Thou hast honored any of Thy sincere ones—blessings that have no equal in Thy knowledge, no likeness in Thy Book, no peer in Thy kingdom, and no companion among the manifestations of Thy creation.
Blessings whereby the heart of Thy Beloved may find contentment in Thee and in all things, and the spirit of Thy Prophet may find repose from Thee and from all things, and the soul of Thy Messenger may find freedom from Thee and from all things, and the body of Thy Guest may find wonder from Thee and from all things. For were he to know that there existed in Thy knowledge even an atom that did not acknowledge Thy oneness, and his prophethood, and the authority of the Imams after him, and the pillars of the House from him, his heart would not rest nor would he be truly content with Thy creation, as his contentment with Thee in every condition is with him.
Therefore, O God, cool his eyes through his contentment with all that Thou hast created and brought into being and dost create or originate, for none possesseth this save Thee, and none hath power over this besides Thee. I beseech Thee, O my God and my Lord, by Muhammad, Thy servant and Thy Prophet and Thy Messenger with Thee, to purify all things, that there may not exist in the knowledge of Thy Beloved aught that he would dislike, by purifying the earth and all that is thereon, that all may worship Thee on the basis that there is no God but Thee, and that Muhammad is Thy Messenger and Thy Beloved, and that the Imams after him are Thy witnesses, and that the pillars of the House are the manifestations of Thy Self. For this cannot be except through Thy grace and mercy. Therefore, O God, accomplish through Thy mercy what I have asked of Thee, for Thou art the Lord of all worlds.

title: BB00404: Du’a’-i-Salavat-i-’Ali, Amiru’l-Mu’minin
text:
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Thou art the Originator of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them. Thou hast ever been supreme over all things, manifest above all things, standing over all things, powerful over all things, and all-compelling over all things.
I beseech Thee by that wherewith Thou hast glorified Thyself, and praised Thine Essence, and promised through Thine Own Being, and magnified through Thine Identity, and exalted through the sovereignty of Thine Own Self-Sufficiency, that Thou wilt send Thy blessings upon Thy Friend, whom Thou hast made a proof unto Thy creation and a conclusive Word after Thy Beloved One, whom Thou didst raise up to manifest Thy religion and exalt Thy Word, and in whom Thou hast deposited the knowledge of what was and what will be until the end of Thy creation, and whose obedience Thou hast made incumbent upon all things, and whose love Thou hast ordained for all things.
Send down Thy blessings, O my God, upon him through every name by which Thou art remembered, and every attribute by which Thou art described, and through all glory, majesty, beauty, grandeur, light, mercy, sublimity, might, perfection, loftiness, will, purpose, power, decree, permission, destiny, scripture, knowledge, ability, word, love, honor, sovereignty, dominion, exaltation, grace, beneficence, tenderness, bounty, generosity, elevation, sanctity and transcendence. For verily, after Thy Beloved One, he called unto Thy religion, and Thy Beloved One established the covenant of his love in the hearts of Thy creation, and he raised up Thy Words and was wholly devoted unto Thee.
Therefore, as Thou hast made him a prince in the kingdom of names and attributes, and a luminary in the kingdom of earth and heavens, send down upon him, O my God, the most excellent blessings Thou hast ever sent down upon any of the successors of Thy Beloved One and Messenger, for none but Thee hath power over this. And make him wholly pleased with Thee, for he is not content save when there remaineth naught in his knowledge except the acknowledgment that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, and that Muhammad is Thy Beloved One and Thy Messenger, and that he is Thy Friend and the Successor of Thy Messenger, and the acknowledgment of what Thou hast ordained regarding the authority of the Imams after him and the Pillars of the House after them.
Therefore deal with him, O my God, through Thy mercy and grace, in such wise as shall make him pleased with Thee and with all Thy creation. For his pleasure with Thee hath no description nor similitude, but his pleasure with Thy creation can only be when Thou dost purify the earth and all who dwell therein. Make it so, O my God, and make him a door to the knowledge of Thy Beloved One, for Thou hast guaranteed his triumph and that all successors shall be gathered beneath his shadow. Deal thus, O my God, through Thy mercy, for verily Thou hast power over this and createst what Thou willest through Thy command, and Thou art the Lord of all the worlds.

title: BB00380: Du’a’-i-Salavat-i-Fatimih
text:
Glorified art Thou, O God! Thou art the Creator of the heavens and earth, the Ordainer of command and creation. There hath never been for Thee any likeness, equal, peer, partner or comparison. Far be it that the highest essences of contingent beings should ascend to the atmosphere of Thy holy air, or that the supreme realities of created things should soar to the horizon of Thy glory, or that the most exalted summits of existence should rise up before Thee, or that the most precious substances Thou hast created in the kingdoms of earth and heaven should descend into Thy presence.
I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thy Name through which Thou didst create Muhammad, Thy Beloved One, and by Thy Name through which Thou didst create Ali, Thy Friend, and by Thy Name through which Thou didst create Fatimih, the Luminous Leaf from the Tree of Thy Prophethood and the Celestial Fruit from the Tree of Thy Providence—she whom Thou didst ennoble, beautify, exalt, honor and place above all the women of the world, whom Thou didst magnify and illumine with Thy light—to send upon her such prayers as would satisfy her heart concerning the sovereignty of Thy oneness, her spirit concerning her father, the Sign of Thy dominion, her soul concerning Ali, Thy Friend, whom Thou didst join with her, and the Imams who came after him, and her body concerning the radiance of the First Pillar, the loftiness of the Second Pillar, the splendor of the Third Pillar, and the names of the Fourth Pillar, for none but Thee possesseth this power and none but Thee is able to accomplish this.
And do Thou, O my God, satisfy her heart with Thee, her spirit with Thy Prophet, her soul with the Imams who came after Thy Prophet, and her body with the shining lights of the pillars of Thy House. Comfort her eyes by purifying the earth and all that is thereon, that there might remain in her knowledge naught but the letters of the most high, that her ears might hear naught but Thy verses, that her eyes might behold naught but Thy words, that her heart might witness naught but the garments of Thy countenance, that her tongue might speak naught but Thy praise and the King of the holy realm of Thy oneness, that naught might dwell in her breast save love for Thee and loyalty to Thee, naught in her liver save Thy spirit and the sweet fragrance of the court of Thy holy oneness, and naught in the essence of her being save that which delighteth her through the manifestations of Thy holy favor and the dawning-places of the sun of Thy exaltation. For were there to remain in her heart aversion to anything which she did not rid herself of, she would not be free for Thy worship. And this is something which none knoweth save Thee, and none but Thee hath power over this.
Therefore, O my God, deal with her and send prayers upon her as Thou didst send prayers upon her father and bestow distinction upon him whom Thou didst join with her. For this is easier with Thee than to say “Be!” and it is. And send down, O my God, that which is best with Thee upon her and upon her father and upon him whom Thou didst join with her, and send prayers upon the Imams who came after her and upon the shining Pillars who came after the Imams. For Thou art the Creator of all things, there is no God but Thee. Thou knowest all things and hast power over all things. Nothing escapeth Thee and nothing is beyond Thy grasp. Glorified art Thou, there is no God but Thee, and Thou art the Lord of all the worlds.

title: BB00452: Du’a’-i-Salavat-i-Hasan
text:
Glory be to Thee, O my God! Thou art my Beloved in the kingdom of command and creation, and my Goal in all the manifestations of creation and command. I have worshipped none but Thee, desired none except Thee, prostrated before none save Thee, and will prostrate before none other than Thee.
I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thy Name through which Thou didst create Thy beloved one and Thy trusted one and the purified leaf from the tree of Thy beloved one, to send Thy blessings upon Hasan, son of Ali, Thy proof, as Thou didst send blessings upon Muhammad and Ali and Fatimah. For Thou hast distinguished him with that which Thou hast not distinguished anyone else in all the worlds, and preferred them with that which Thou hast not preferred anyone like them in all the worlds.
Therefore, O my God, send down, as befitteth the majesty of Thy holy might and the splendor of Thy glorious bounty, upon Thy Most Glorious Beauty, Thy Most Exalted Grandeur, Thy Most Beautiful Beauty, Thy Greatest Name, Thy Most Luminous Light, Thy Perfect Mercy, Thy All-Encompassing Exaltation, and whatsoever Thou hast named Thyself with and revealed in Thy Book of Thy most beautiful names which none can enumerate save Thee, and Thy most exalted similitudes which none can comprehend except Thee, to send upon him the most excellent of Thy blessings and to cause to descend upon him the most attractive of Thy manifestations and to ordain for him the best of Thy names and attributes. For verily he is under Thine eyes and Thy protection and Thy safeguarding and Thy sufficiency.
Therefore, O God, make his heart well-pleased with Thee, and his spirit with Thy beloved one, and his soul with his father and mother and his self, and his body with the places of Thy intimacy and the pillars of Thy house and the sites of Thy bounty and the settings of Thy generosity. And cause his eyes, O my God, to be gladdened with what Thou lovest and art pleased with in the hereafter and in this world, such that there be not in his knowledge that which he abhorreth concerning it, and purify the earth and all that is thereon through Thy grace and Thy mercy that Thou mayest be well-pleased with all things.
For verily his pleasure in Thee cannot be turned back, but his pleasure in all Thy creation existeth not save that there be not in his knowledge except those who acknowledge Thy oneness and believe in Thy Prophet and confess the guardianship of the successors of Thy beloved one and bear witness to the truth of the pillars of His house according to what Thou hast ordained in the knowledge of the unseen with Thee.
Therefore, O God, do with him as befitteth the majesty of his holiness, and accomplish through him, O God, what the court of Thy glory deserveth, for verily Thou art the Lord of all the worlds.

title: BB00395: Du’a’-i-Salavat-i-Husayn
text:
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Thou art the Light of the heavens and the earth and all that lieth between them. From time immemorial Thou hast been one God, single, unique, eternal, self-subsisting, ever-living. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and verily all that existeth in the kingdom of earth and heaven lieth within Thy grasp and right hand. Thou createst what Thou willest, and providest for whom Thou desirest, causeth to die and giveth life, and unto Thee shall all creation return.
I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thy Name through which Thou didst create Muhammad, Thy Beloved, and by Thy Name through which Thou didst create Ali, Thy Friend, and by Thy Name through which Thou didst create Fatima, the fruit of the tree of Thy love, and by Thy Name through which Thou didst create Hasan and made him a proof unto Thy creation, and by Thy Name through which Thou didst create Husayn—Thy blessings be upon them all, now and before and after—and made him a proof from Thee unto Thy creation, that Thou mayest send upon him the most excellent blessings Thou hast ever bestowed upon any of Thy loved ones, and the most noble favors Thou hast ever conferred upon any of Thy chosen ones.
Ordain for him, O my God, from Thy glory its most glorious, from Thy majesty its most majestic, from Thy beauty its most beautiful, from Thy grandeur its most grand, from Thy light its most luminous, from Thy mercy its most expansive, from Thy words their most perfect, from Thy perfection its most perfect, from Thy names their greatest, from Thy might its mightiest, from Thy will its most decisive, from Thy purpose its swiftest, from Thy power its most powerful, from Thy decree its most just, from Thy providence its nearest, from Thy permission its most elevated, from Thy cause its most subtle, from Thy Book its most excellent, from Thy knowledge its most penetrating, from Thy power its most far-reaching, from Thy word its most pleasing, from Thy questions their most beloved, from Thy honor its most honorable, from Thy sovereignty its most enduring, from Thy dominion its most glorious, from Thy tenderness its most tender, from Thy exaltation its most exalted, from Thy bounty its most ancient, from Thy signs their most wondrous.
And from all things that which hath no equal as recompense for his martyrdom in Thy path, his satisfaction with what lieth with Thee, his detachment unto Thee, his desire for the exaltation of Thy oneness and the establishment of Thy sanctity. Make content, O my God, his heart with Thee, his spirit with Thy Prophet, his soul with his mother and brother, and his body with the pillars of Thy House. Purify, O my God, all that lieth within his knowledge that there remain naught save love for him, and cause him then to descend into the highest chambers of Thy paradise and the most glorious degrees of Thy presence, whereby his eyes may be solaced. And since this day is a day of festival, I love not to mention aught save the letters of the most high. Verily Thou art most bountiful in grace and mercy toward him who fulfilleth his covenant, and most severe in might and power toward others besides him. Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee. There is no power nor strength except through Thee. Verily Thou art the Lord of all worlds.

title: BB00453: Du’a’-i-Salavat-i-’Ali Ibn-i-Husayn
text:
Glorified art Thou, O my God! How can I soar into the atmosphere of Thy holy air, or ascend to the carpet of intimacy with Thee, or stand in the heaven of Thy divine essence, or dwell in the atmosphere of Thy mighty realm, or rise to the horizon of Thy generosity, when I know of Thy oneness and singleness and self-subsistence and eternity and everlastingness and permanence and holiness and sanctity and belovedness and purposefulness and worthiness of worship and desirability and visibility and eagerness and knowability and describability? For none of these befits the servant before the Sovereign of Thine eternity, nor is proper for the one lorded over when faced with the dawning lights of Thy lordship.
Therefore, O my God, send Thy blessings upon Thy friend and son of Thy friends, ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, Thy proof unto Thy creation and Thy sign in the kingdom of Thy earth and heaven, the light of Thy countenance in the manifestations of Thy creation and the garment of Thy face in the inner realities of Thy invention, and the expression of the sovereignty of Thy oneness in the kingdom of Thy sanctity and majesty. For verily Thou, O my God, hast ever distinguished the people of Thy Cause with wondrous conditions and bestowed upon the people of Thy love sublime and glorious favors.
Therefore, O my God, send upon him the most excellent blessings Thou hast ever sent upon any of Thy friends, and the most resplendent that Thou hast ever caused to descend upon any of Thy loved ones. And make content, O my God, his heart with Thee, and his spirit with Thy Prophet, and his soul with the Imams who came before him and after him, and his body with the pillars of the veils of Thy holy might and the suns of the glory of Thy exaltation and the sanctified Manifestations that prove Thy oneness and the shining stars in the kingdom of Thy sovereignty—such that his knowledge encompasses nothing except what He loves, being certain of Thy oneness, believing in Thy self-subsistence, acknowledging the prophethood of Thy Beloved, confirming the authority of Thy friends, and awaiting the manifestations of Thy gates. For none but Thee can do this, and Thy command is closer than saying to a thing “Be” and it is.
Therefore, O my God, send down upon him that which will bring comfort to his eyes before God and the Imams from his lineage. For Thou knowest what is in the heavens and what is on earth, and Thou hast power over all things, and Thou art the Lord of all the worlds.

title: BB00449: Du’a’-i-Salavat-i-Baqir
text:
Prayer of Muhammad ibn ʿAli, peace be upon him
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Thou art the Originator of the heavens and earth, possessed of might and splendor, of majesty and radiance, of grandeur and glory, of loftiness and names, of dominion and attributes. Through Thy camphor-like essence Thou hast sanctified Thyself above the recognition of all created things, and through Thine own Being Thou hast exalted Thyself above the praise of all existences. Through the glory of Thy holy Personality, Thou art beyond what any bird of the hearts can attain in the kingdom of names and attributes. Through the sublimity of Thy Self-Subsistence, Thou art exalted in such grandeur that the hands of the essences among the possessors of abstraction in the kingdom of earth and heavens cannot reach Thee. Thou art safeguarded in such an impregnable manifestation that none among all beings can know Thee.
I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thy splendor which is more splendorous than all splendor, and Thy majesty which is more majestic than all majesty, and Thy beauty which is more beautiful than all beauty, and Thy grandeur which is greater than all grandeur, and by Thy light which is more luminous than all light, and by Thy mercy which hath encompassed all atoms, and by Thy perfection which is more perfect than all perfection in the kingdom of earth and heavens, to send Thy blessings upon Muhammad ibn ʿAli, Thy Proof and son of Thy Proof, with the most excellent blessings Thou hast ever sent upon any of Thy chosen ones or bestowed upon any of Thy sincere ones. And cause, O my God, his heart to be well-pleased with Thee, his spirit with Thy Prophet, his soul with his chosen forefathers and then with the Imams after him, the pure ones, and his body with the pillars of Thy Sacred House, for verily none but Thee possesseth this, nor can any besides Thee accomplish it.
Make his eyes, O my God, to be gladdened by there being naught in his knowledge that he would dislike, that all things may bear witness to that for which Thou didst create them—the testimony that there is no God but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God and that the Imams are the Proofs of God and that the Gates of the House are the Manifestations of God’s Mystery. For this is that for which Thou hast created, sustained, caused to die and given life to all things. There is no power nor strength except through Thee. Through Thee have I become independent of all else but Thee, and have hoped for Thy grace and beneficence, being certain that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, the Lord of all worlds.

title: BB00427: Du’a’-i-Salavat-i-Sadiq
text:
The Prayer of Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Thou art the Originator of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them, Who maketh the angels messengers having wings, two, three and four, Who increaseth in creation what He pleaseth. Nothing can frustrate Thee, neither in the heavens nor on earth. Nothing escapeth Thy knowledge, neither in the kingdom of command nor creation.
I bear witness unto Thee, O my God, with that wherewith Thou hast testified concerning Thyself, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee. Thou hast ever been, existing before all things, and Thou wilt ever be, existing after all things. None knoweth Thee save Thyself, none can describe Thee save Thyself, and none can worship Thee as befitteth Thy worship save Thyself.
Thou art the Subduer Who cannot be subdued, the Manifest Who cannot be manifested, the Dominator Who cannot be prevented, the Inaccessible from Whose grasp nothing can escape, and the Ever-Standing Whom nothing can rival.
I beseech Thee by the greatest of all Thy names, by the nearest of all Thy symbols, by the most manifest of all Thy revelations, by the most attractive of all Thy effulgences, by the most exalted of all Thy attributes, by the most perfect of all Thy words, by the most wondrous of all Thy signs, by the most elevated of all Thy stations, by the most radiant of all Thy tokens, and by the most resplendent of all Thy evidences, that Thou send Thy blessings upon Ja’far ibn Muhammad, Thy Proof and son of Thy Proof, whom Thou hast made a sign of the sovereignty of Thy oneness, a focal point for the King of Thy eternality, a sacred tree for the exaltation of Thy self-subsistence, a sanctified leaf for the establishment of Thy unity, and an originated sign for the elevation of the wondrous lights of the garments of Thy countenance.
Send down upon him, O Lord, all Thy sweet fragrances, and cause me, O Lord, to receive from all Thy creation Thy remembrance and praise. Grant, O Lord, that his body be well-pleased with Thee with true pleasure and above it, and Thyself with Thy Prophet with true pleasure and above pleasure, and his spirit with the Imams after Thy Beloved and his self, and the Imams after him, and his heart with the pillars of Thy House. For I have besought Thee, O my God, concerning seven whom Thou hast designated for the manifestation of the descent of Thy mercy upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad unto Thee in the world of Thy testimony, for the Command with Thee is one.
Comfort his eyes, O Lord, with that which was not in his knowledge besides what he loveth not, for Thou hast power over this and none other than Thee, and Thou createst all things by Thy command.
