And without doubt this was not made manifest save that ye should believe in Muhammad the Messenger of God and then in that which he reciteth from God, that ye might be assured.
Behold then the verse wherein God hath mentioned: “In what revelation, after God and His signs, will they then believe?” [Q77:50]. For that is in the element of air through Muhammad and His words, then in the element of water through the first who believed in Him and then His words, then in the element of earth through the last who shall guide unto God and seek tidings of God’s pleasure. And upon this hath been revealed: “O ye who believe! Put not yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger” [Q49:1]. And the intent in the name of God is not the name of the Messenger, for He Who is made manifest through the manifestation of Divinity is He Who reciteth unto thee from God His verses, and that is the highest that can possibly appear in creation from God, mighty and glorious, inasmuch as that which God attributeth unto Himself is like unto the House which He hath attributed unto Himself.
Otherwise, the Essence of the Eternal, glorified and exalted be His mention, can never be seen nor described nor comprehended nor pointed to nor spoken of in the dual. And whatsoever is mentioned or described as the Sun of Reality by the ignorant concerning the Will—whose inner aspect is mentioned in relation to the mention of Divinity and whose outer aspect in relation to the mention of servitude and messengership, or whatsoever is mentioned of the names of goodliness and the states of belovedness—call thou this to mind, for that is indeed the Great Day.

title: BB00506: Answer to Mirza Ahmad-i-Azghandi
section: Part 5: “And I testify concerning the Word of God…”
text:
Part 5: “And I testify concerning the Word of God…”
And I testify concerning the Word of God: “Taste ye the penalty of burning” (Qur’an 8:50), for that is the outer aspect, while its inner aspect is the nectar for those who believe in God and His signs. Behold then how thou seest the veils of the people, for that is what thou hast witnessed in the traditions in the interpretation of: “One liable to punishment did ask for a punishment about to befall the unbelievers, the which none can repel, from Allah, Lord of the Ways of Ascent” (Qur’an 70:1-3). For it hath been interpreted as the Proof, and there is none who can repel it from those who believe not in Him. Though they should spend all that is on earth, they would find no one to repel it. For God, mighty and glorified, hath said: “Knowest thou not that Allah hath power over all things in heaven and earth? And besides Allah ye have neither patron nor helper” (Qur’an 2:107). That is, for Muhammad aforetime, then for the Essence of the Seven Letters in that Manifestation, then for Him Whom God shall make manifest in the latter Resurrection.
Then call to mind truth after truth in the Living Letters in both the Furqan and the Bayan, both of which are one, then among the witnesses of the Bayan that they should believe in Him Whom God shall make manifest with truth after truths according to the nearness of their hearts. For on the Day of His appearance none shall have any excellence save through belief in Him, nor any knowledge save through knowledge of Him. Wash then from the tablet of all things their thingness save through Him, for that is the certain truth.
Then I testify on the night of the third of the third ten of the greatest month, where He saith: Did the people think that they would be left alone on saying “We believe,” and that they would not be tested? Behold, the word of God is certain beyond doubt, and all who lay claim to faith must needs be refined and tested until their truthfulness is distinguished from their falsehood. I have set apart all people by the word “There is no God but God,” and I have sent unto one, so seek ye Him, for He is more precious than red sulphur. Red sulphur cannot save thee, but this One can save thee. Seek ye Him from him whom ye knew aforetime, for he was aforetime the gate of bounty for whosoever desired to receive from God, exalted and glorified be He, through the Manifestation of His own Self. But I will expound that testing for thee that thou mayest see with thine own eyes, for the plan of God is above every plan, and were it not for the grace of God and His mercy, none among you would ever be purified.
Therefore, observe those who have said “There is no God but God,” for these are the first whom We have tested by declaring that there is no God but Me, and We have distinguished the truthful from the rest. He who spoke that word aforetime spoke it only according to that which God had revealed in the Qur’an, and the authority of the Qur’an was not established save through the inability of all upon earth to produce its like, and Muhammad proved the authority of the Qur’an and its supremacy over all miracles, so that none should depart on the day of testing. And a period of one thousand two hundred and seventy years was decreed for it. When God desireth to test His creatures and to witness who will testify to the truth and who will not, then He revealeth that verse even as it was revealed aforetime in the Qur’an. This is the straight path of the beginning.
Observe now who saith “There is no God but God” and who passeth over this straight path after God hath made known unto all who believed in the Qur’an that its like cannot appear from among the creatures, and all have testified to this from after Muhammad until now, that no signs come from anyone thereafter. God hath seized them by that from which they have no escape, that they might be certain that those words are from God. This is a universal grace to close the doors of remoteness and veiling from every soul, that perchance thereby on the Day of Resurrection they may be saved. But when those words were revealed, thou seest that none believed in them with certainty that they were from God, the Lord of the worlds.
And verily that which thou hast validated of that word through thy knowledge in the pillar of glorification at the time of reckoning—if We wished We would not accept it from thee, for thou hast known from behind the veils and hast validated that word through thy principles which are in thy hand. And verily this according to thy principles is not valid, since from that pillar it is not meet that such a word should appear, for if it were meet, it should appear from the pillar of Unity which is above that pillar. And shouldst thou elevate thy principles, verily that is not meet save for the Tree of Reality, the Primal Point, and below it creation is brought into being by its word. And verily thy knowledge in the validation of that word was not through a primal reality. And if thou hast seen that thou hast spoken truly, it is for the sake of thy companions that their feet may not slip upon the Bridge on the Day of Resurrection.
Otherwise, verily that word is not meet save from God, glorified and exalted be He, for if it were possible for another after the cessation of revelation, the witnesses of God would not weep after Muhammad, nor would they supplicate for the Day of the appearance of the Truth, which is the appearance of the Will that speaketh from God with that which rendereth powerless all that is upon the earth.
Therefore thou seest that all who say “There is no god but God”—their source was naught but the word of Muhammad, and his word is established as being from God only through the verses which God sent down upon him, wherein all that is upon the earth is rendered powerless. Therefore behold—this is the first principle of the religion of creation. We have tried them with that word on the Day of Resurrection, and that which was established aforetime shall be established on that Day. Nay, the Cause of God is more manifest, for He Who was sent aforetime was sent at the age of forty, and his tongue was Arabic, and those verses were revealed unto him in twenty-three years according to what thou seest in the Furqan at that time.
But through that Tree, perchance He reciteth the like thereof when He willeth in two days and two nights. And thou hast witnessed that He was a Persian and recited not those verses save when four and twenty years had passed over Him, after God had given Him of the prayers and tablets and the true spiritual forms that which none can enumerate save God.
Observe how in every Manifestation the Reality Which God manifesteth among the people is by that which was the greatest example among them. On the day of Moses, when the superiority of the people lay in the science of talismans, God revealed His Prophet with that which was mightiest, that none might have any argument concerning His Cause. Then in the manifestation of Jesus, when the superiority of the people lay in the science of bodily healing, God sent forth Jesus with that power, that none might tarry in acknowledging Him. Then in the manifestation of Muhammad, when the superiority of creation lay in the science of eloquence in speech, even so did God send Him forth that none might be able to tarry in recognizing Him.
And in thy time, when the superiority of the people lieth in the knowledge of God and the mysteries of Reality and Divine Unity, therefore hath God manifested Him Whom He desired to manifest in that station, that none might be able to tarry in recognizing Him. Observe in the tradition of the Tablet of Fatimah, for therein is mentioned concerning Him the perfection of Moses and the glory of Jesus and the patience of Job. This is a word according to the measure of creation’s capacity; otherwise, naught is attributed to the Tree of Reality save the perfection of God and His glory and His patience.
And dost thou know what is the patience of God? It is My patience with that creation, and it is the severest vengeance from God. Observe in the visitation of the Proof where it saith: “And thy wrestling-places are in God the essence of God’s vengeance,” and there is naught more grievous for creation than this, if they but knew.
Behold how God hath manifested the summit of perfection, yet all are in veils. If thou wouldst desire to recite even one verse, thou couldst not do so, and like unto thee is all that is upon the earth. And this is because it pertaineth to the station of God—He associateth none with Him. Then concerning supplications, if thou didst desire them, thou couldst not accomplish it, and if thou couldst accomplish it, thou must needs take the forms from the words of thy Imams, and thou wilt find no path thereto.
Verily, the first is water that changeth not, and verily this is milk whose taste hath not altered. Then observe the sermons and visitations, for they are wine delightsome to the drinkers. Then observe the forms of knowledge, for they are purified honey for the God-fearing.
And that which God hath promised thee, and all of those rivers in Paradise—God intended not by Paradise save the Primal Reality, nor by those rivers aught else but that which floweth from that Reality like unto oceans. And this is the meaning of the saying of your Imams that our enemies in Our manifestation shall eat that which I am ashamed to mention, for they enter not into Paradise to partake of its sustenance, and whilst they remain in the Fire they are sustained by that which is therein. And had this been before the Manifestation, it would have been the sustenance of Paradise, but after the Manifestation it is transformed.
And if thou desirest, look upon the people of Jesus before God manifested Muhammad—whatsoever they recited of the Gospel and the words of Jesus, they were sustained by the sustenance of Paradise. But when God sent forth Muhammad, the sustenance of Paradise was transformed to that which is beneath it. Therefore it was not lawful for anyone, so perceive thou and arise from thy slumber, and let them arise from their slumber whom ye see desiring God as their Lord.
For that which thou hast beheld in the Tradition—“People are asleep, and when they die they awaken”—those are the stages of the Day of Resurrection, as hath been recited in the Prayer of Adiliyyah from death unto resurrection, which are eleven stages, whereof the Persian children say that the root of religion is five and its branch is six. That is thy temple in the Most Great Name, whose outward form is Ha and whose inward reality is Waw. And We have sent unto thee that thou mayest give thanks unto God thy Lord thereby, through that which We have sent unto thee from the temples of the First Unity.
And though all those stages are established with the discerning ones at the time of the Manifestation, yet since the people are among the remote ones, I shall place each one in a cycle that perchance thereby one of the Muslims may be delivered. But nay, by God thy Lord, He is independent of all the worlds.
By my life, I have found none who speaketh the truth “There is no god but God” in such wise as would establish that Word in his religion aforetime, inasmuch as all that they have comprehended and grasped of that Word is from their own knowledge which is in their possession. But verily the matter is as I have informed thee and the mystery is that which I have brought thee. And methinks I behold all who are in the Bayan in the last height of its manifestation—all of them are slumbering.
Until God shall raise up him whom God will manifest, exalted be His command! Then those who believe in Him know not anything until they turn with the sun till it reacheth the midst of its decline. Then perchance they may comprehend something and behold God their Lord and associate naught with Him. God hath created for them no paradise greater than this, whether they find their Beloved alone, alone, or find before Him all that is on the earth. For His likeness, glorified be His mention, is like unto the sun—were there to confront it mirrors without number, all of them would reflect the radiance of the sun within their bounds, and if none should confront it, the sun would rise and set, and the veil would be for the mirrors.
And verily I have not fallen short in my counsel to those creatures and in my guidance for their turning unto God their Lord and their faith in God their Creator, that they may believe in Him on the Day of His Manifestation—all that is on the earth. This would gladden my being, when all have attained unto the summit of their existence and have reached the dawning-place of their Beloved and have comprehended that which is possible in the realm of possibility from the manifestation of their Desired One. Otherwise my heart is grieved that I have nurtured all things for this purpose—how then should anyone be veiled therefrom? I have called upon God and I call upon Him—verily He is nigh, responsive.
Then observe the testing of God for whoso uttereth that Word—how far do they depart from that which God thy Lord loveth! Yea, and God, inasmuch as He desireth to deal with them through grace and spreadeth not the wings of justice, whosoever may be saved on the Day of Resurrection, even though it be through love as of a mother for her child—since the essence of religion is the love of God, and when this is not of the attributes of love of God, He saveth whomsoever possesseth it, but that is through grace, not through justice. Whoso looketh upon that Tree with other than the eye of God shall not merit the decree of salvation. And God shall cause all to ascend until they behold with that eye their Lord God in the horizon of the beginning and then in the summit of the return.

title: BB00506: Answer to Mirza Ahmad-i-Azghandi
section: Part 6: “And were I to wish to mention…”
text:
Part 6: “And were I to wish to mention…”
And were I to wish to mention the testing of those creatures in all the circumstances of their religion and their world, the Tablets of possibility and of existence would not suffice, inasmuch as if the testing of creatures in the essence of essences be such as this, how shall it be for those who are under the shadow of that Word? Observe how many acknowledge that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, and there is no doubt that none hath been nearer to God than Muhammad, then than the Letters of the Living. Then observe those who recognize them after they have been known by proof to be the first of creation and those from whom hath been taken and upon whom hath been bestowed the pre-eternal before all things. But inasmuch as the knowledge of creatures is mere words, not reality, therefore it beareth no fruit for them. Otherwise, whosoever possesseth the eye of insight and heareth the verses of God from their Tree shall be assured of the appearance of his Lord and the presence of Muhammad and the Manifestations of His Self and the Gates of His glory and all the Prophets and the truthful ones and the martyrs and the believers.
And likewise, whosoever may be in their shadow shall be in the shadows of the Fire. By Him Who cleft the grain and created the soul! If God had created in the first that hath no first anything of good, He would have gathered it into the first of them that believed in God, inasmuch as he is the essence of all good. And this is the meaning of the word of God: “Your creation and your resurrection are but as a single soul,” and the meaning of the saying: “As for the Prophets, I am they, and as for the Successors, my brother Ali is they.”
And if God created anything devoid of good in any world of the worlds of Command and Creation, He would send it forth in the first of them that said not “Yea” unto “Am I not your Lord?” Then hath He divided the source of that good until it cannot be numbered, and likewise its shadow, until it reacheth beneath the dust. Behold then the word of God: “We have gathered you and the ancients,” for this is a word of truth wherein is no doubt, inasmuch as all things have been created for God, and needs must return to none save God.
When God desired aught of a soul and it knew Him, that soul hath manifested what God desired of all things, and verily all are charged with the like thereof. But inasmuch as they manifested it not, the command of God is established in that thing. Otherwise, on the day when the first of them that believed desired the Truth, all were charged with the like thereof, but inasmuch as they turned not and were veiled, the Holy Spirit hath taken, in the gardens of infancy from the orchards of the Garden of Eternity, the first-fruits thereof and their manifestation and their inner essence and their secret and their witnessing.
And if each should take according to his like, then should they take, inasmuch as the like thereof is as mirrors—if all the mirrors were alike, there would be manifested in them the image of the sun. Then should the name of humanity be applied to all of them, and all things be gathered according to the appearance of their differentiation. But inasmuch as they turned not, they gathered all in one soul.
Marvel not at this, but look upon the manifestation of Jesus, for He, peace be upon Him, trained all creation for the manifestation of Muhammad, and promised them what mentioneth the name of Ahmad in the Book. And all, by night and by day, awaited His manifestation and besought their attainment unto His person. And when God manifested Him, then in five years or more naught was gathered save in Ali. And although it behooved on that day that all things be gathered unto God, yet inasmuch as they were veiled, each from that for which they were created—the meeting with God—the bounty of all things was taken by Ali, and the fruit of the creation of all things was manifested in Ali, peace be upon Him.
And on that day all the Names of God were He, inasmuch as He had taken His rest in the shadow of God until God should differentiate Him. And on that day thou seest His multiplication where it cannot be numbered.
And likewise they of the Bayan, if they would recognize Him Whom God shall make manifest, that they might be delivered, inasmuch as they were not created—God hath revealed in the Book:

“God created not anything save that it should believe in Him Whom He shall make manifest on the Day of Resurrection.”

By the Truth! O all things, ye shall be certain of that for which ye were created.
That verse is the fruit of the creation of all things, inasmuch as it taketh from one and fulfilleth unto one. Methinks I can behold the day of His manifestation when all people shall arise in His name. And by night and day for His appearance they shall supplicate. But when God manifesteth Him, lo, none shall believe in Him save the sincere. By Him Who cleaveth the grain and createth the soul, were every soul to believe in Him when He saith “Verily I am God, there is no God but Me, and whatsoever is beneath Me is My creation; O all things, worship ye Me!” then would it be meet that every soul should say “Yea” and prostrate themselves before God while they are assured.
And should any be veiled from Him, that is from after their own selves. And whoso comprehendeth this, that is all things, let them first recognize Him Who believeth in Him, then shall ye recognize Him. Verily we are all believers in Him.
Behold, all who were created awaited Muhammad from the Gospel, and He came and there passed over Him one thousand two hundred and seventy years, yet they unto this time are waiting. Then bear witness to this, then say: “Glorified be God above that which they know not!”
Then likewise bear witness on the day when God—exalted be His mention—shall manifest Him, for He shall assuredly come with the truth. But they who await Him and by night and day arise in His name shall disbelieve in God Who created them and sustained them and caused them to die and gave them life and shall raise them up, yet they perceive not.
The example of all who are veiled from the Manifestation of that One is that each seeth within himself that he is for God, but God beareth witness that he is naught but for that which is beneath God, save those who were assured in God and His signs. These are they who have believed in Me and in whatsoever God hath sent down unto Me from the verses, and they in meeting their Lord on the Day of Resurrection are assured.
Therefore behold the trial of all who have said “Muhammad is the Messenger of God” and their tribulation on the Day of Resurrection. For that which maketh the Prophet a Prophet—which is the signs of God—God hath manifested in the beginning of the matter, yet none have been fulfilled thereby save the learned.
Then look upon those who have claimed love for the Imams and loyalty to them, or love for the Gates of Guidance and knowledge of them, for all have been tried and tested. Were I not loath to make mention of excellence, I would say: “And there will swoon all who are in the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, save whom Allah willeth”—and dost thou know what Allah willeth? That is the Word of God: “Everything will perish save His countenance”—and dost thou know what the countenance is? Those are they who have believed in God and His signs, and who have followed the messages of those who have delivered unto them from God their Lord whatsoever hath been sent down unto them of the verses. Verily, those are they who, in the shadow of the letters of the countenance, shall be saved.
And the condition of all creation is like unto the Day of Resurrection, save that on that Day their trials shall be made manifest. Otherwise, the station of creation in every matter before God is like unto that. And how oft have I seen in the traditions accounts of trials, which the learned of thy time have related, until it was said: “None shall remain save us and our followers”—yet none payeth heed to this, and each regardeth himself as the very essence of the followers.
And verily I have endured patiently in the Cause of God, for I shall assuredly take from above the earth the number of the companions of destiny, and I have endured with what none knoweth save God. Thus when they have been taken from the sieve, I have heard their names ere the decline. This is the meaning of the saying of Ali:

“And surely the remaining ones who have preceded shall be cut short”

- and so forth.
Then His saying: “Your lowest shall become your highest, and your highest your lowest”—behold above the earth the people of His truth are confined to Islam, and Islam is confined to a portion of the fifths, and little in other lands. And the portion of Islam—its greatest city according to outward appearance is the land of Sad, where in every chamber one crieth out: “Verily I am the mujtahid in the religion of Islam!” And God hath made their highest—whom thou knowest outwardly—that which God loveth not to mention, for sufficient unto them is what they have earned before God, and unto God their Lord shall they all return.
And verily their lowest in outward appearance—he who worketh with wheat—hath said “Yea!” and believed in God, the Most High, the Most Exalted. And for this reason hath he become higher than whosoever is upon that earth, even though he knoweth not a single Arabic word. And those who are followed in learning and piety from the beginning of their lives to the end thereof have given false judgment concerning God their Lord, notwithstanding that they glorify God by night and day, yet they believe not, inasmuch as they are in themselves the letters of negation, though they perceive it not.
This is the meaning of the saying of Ali: “Your lowest shall become your highest, and your highest your lowest.” Whosoever upon that earth is lowest of them all according to outward appearance, on the Day of Resurrection shall be saved and shall don the garment of glory and exaltation before God and before those possessed of knowledge of Him. And whosoever upon that earth is above them all—God loveth not to mention him because he hath not believed in God his Lord, notwithstanding that he attributeth himself to God by a name which hath no reality for him, and he is not of the truthful.
If the Cause of God were in a land which had no reality to attribute itself to God, and ye had among you its like according to Islam in such a condition, how then could it be in other lands? And that which thou hast seen in the tradition—that one shall come forth from that land and two from this land, to the end of the tradition—naught but this hath been with God in truth. Otherwise, how shall each be faithful to his covenant with God? Verily, the essence of the Word today is the Day of Resurrection, and all have been gathered and shall be gathered according to what they have earned.
I have mentioned the trials of the people in the fundamentals of their religion—how then shall I mention their branches? This is but a branch, provided their fundamentals be established for them. And how shall I mention what is in their religion whereby they transgress the bounds of God? Verily, they have no mention. And those who derive poetry from poetry—this is the measure of their trial, inasmuch as they have entered into the religion of Islam by virtue of the Furqan after being assured that it was naught but from God, and they behold the like of that proof yet believe not in God nor are assured that it is from God. They extract from what is therein yet perceive not, and I think not that they shall perceive. Shall those who believed not in Muhammad until that time perceive these? But God loveth that they should perceive, that they may be saved thereby on the Day of Resurrection. And this is of the grace of God upon mankind, but they give not thanks.
And this is what I have seen—that the appearance of the Proof is the Lesser Resurrection. And according to the saying of the people, I shall be patient until the day of fifty thousand years, that God may judge between His servants in truth. Verily, He is the Best of Judges.

title: BB00052: Li-’Aliyyi’l-A’la
text:
Part 1: “All praise be unto Thee, O my God!…”
In the name of God, the Most Exalted, the Most Holy
All praise be unto Thee, O my God! I testify, as doth every created thing, that Thou art God, that there is none other God but Thee, alone, without peer or partner. Thine is the creation and the command, both before and after. Thou givest life and death, then causeth death and giveth life. Verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not, the Sovereign Whose dominion passeth not away, the Ruler Whose authority changeth not, the Just Who wrong not, the One from Whose grasp nothing escapeth, whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them. Thou createst whatsoever Thou willest by Thy command. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
I further testify, as doth all creation, that Thou hast ever existed before all things, subsisting with all things, enduring after all things, and transcending all things. Thou hast distinguished Thyself through might and majesty, and exalted Thyself through grandeur and independence. Thou hast ever been the One God, Single, Eternal, Self-Subsisting, All-Wise, Just, Holy, Everlasting, Self-Dependent. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son.
All contingent beings glorify Thee in their essence, all realities sanctify Thee in their identity, all created things unite in testifying to Thy oneness in their inmost truth, and all dwellers in the kingdoms of earth and heaven magnify Thee in their pure being. Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. Thou hast ever been supreme over all contingent beings, manifest above all created things, transcendent over all existence, elevated above all who dwell in the kingdoms of earth and heaven, inaccessible above all who inhabit the realms of origin and end, sovereign over every atom, and dominant over all who dwell in the kingdoms of names and attributes.
Thine is the kingdom and the dominion, then the might and the omnipotence, then the power and divinity, then strength and glory, then sovereignty and human nature, then honor and majesty, then the countenance and beauty, then the visage and perfection, then authority and justice, then mercy and grace, then likeness and similitude, then reality and deeds, then glory and inaccessibility, then power and transcendence, then joy and gladness, then awe and detachment, then the visible and invisible from the highest heaven to the lowliest atom—that which hath no equal, no likeness, no peer, no associate, and no similitude, for nothing in Thy creation befitteth such attributes.
Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. I have ever been among those who glorify Thee. Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. I have ever been among those who sanctify Thee. Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. I have ever been among those who proclaim Thy unity. Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. I have ever been among those who magnify Thee. Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. I have ever been among those who exalt Thee. There is no god but Thee and nothing belongeth to anyone except by Thy command, before and after. There is no God but Thee, the Most Great, the Most High.
I further testify before Thee that Thy Manifestation in creation hath neither beginning nor end that I might remember Thee thereby. In every Manifestation, Thou acceptest not from the Manifestations of Thy creation that which Thou didst reveal unto them aforetime, from the days of Adam until now. Such hath been Thy way in every Manifestation, for the Sun of Thy Revelation is one, though it rise infinitely unto infinity—it is but one fruit, though its rising in each Manifestation be according to what Thou hast ordained for it.
Thus do I testify that it is a mirror that speaketh naught except of Thee and guideth to none save Thee, and that indeed it is the One made manifest from a beginning that hath no beginning in every Dispensation, through that which Thou hast named and bestowed upon it of signs and evidences, until Thou didst bring the Dispensations to an end through the Manifestation of Thy Beloved One aforetime, and didst send down the Furqan unto Him, and didst nurture creation for the Manifestation of Thyself on the Day of Resurrection, when none was manifest from Thee except the Primal Point, since all that appeareth in every Manifestation deriveth its existence through Him alone, as all that was raised up in Islam was through none other than the Manifestation of Thy Beloved One aforetime—Thy blessings be upon Him and upon the Exponents of His Revelation and upon those who followed His Cause.
And Thy Manifestation after that Manifestation was not like His Manifestation after Thy Manifestation in the Gospel, for verily Thou didst create all things for the Day of Resurrection, the Day of meeting with Thee, wherein Thou didst send down aforetime unto Thy Beloved One—Thy blessings be upon Him and upon the Guides to Thy Self—“God is He Who raised up the heavens without pillars as ye see them. Then mounted He the Throne, and compelled the sun and the moon to serve. Each runneth unto an appointed term. He ordereth all things. He maketh clear His revelations, that ye may be convinced of meeting with your Lord.” And there is no doubt that Thou, O my God, in Thine Essence, canst never be seen or comprehended, but rather Thou hast made meeting with the Manifestation of Thy Self to be meeting with Thee, and for this purpose hast Thou created all things, for every Manifestation of Thine aforetime was intended for Thy Manifestation to come, since what Thou didst intend in that Manifestation was for the Day of Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest like unto that Manifestation on the Day of Resurrection through Thy signs.
Therefore, O my God, do Thou preserve all who have believed in Thee and then in Thy signs until the Day of Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest, for on that Day all who dwell on earth in their entirety claim in their religion a connection to Him through the previous Manifestations, yet all are veiled from Him Who hath appeared unto them through their own selves and hath ordained their destinies, save Thy servants upon whom Thou hast bestowed Thy guidance and assured Thy good-pleasure through their recognition of Thy Self and Thy signs.
I will assuredly bear witness unto Thee, by that which hath been mentioned in the Book of Thy Most Exalted, Most High Name, and by Thy most glorious, most beauteous remembrance, that when he turned his gaze unto the Source of the proof, Thou didst bestow upon him Thy favor through that which Thou hast revealed in the Revelation, even as Thou hast said—and Thy word is the truth—:
For after thy appearance, whosoever had believed in thee and in thy signs was commanded that he should believe in the manifestation of thy Cause and in its tokens—for thy Cause in that Revelation is more wondrous, and thy proof mightier. For the verses were revealed unto Thy Beloved after forty years; and though a thousand two hundred and seventy years have since elapsed, no one hath produced a single verse. Yet Thou didst reveal unto the Manifestation of Thy Cause after he had attained the age of four and twenty; and none can produce a verse by that which Thou didst reveal unto him, until the Day whereon Thou wilt manifest him whom Thou shalt make manifest.
Moreover, that which Thou didst reveal with Thy Beloved in three and twenty years, Thou didst reveal unto him in five days and nights, when Thou didst permit him to recite from Thee. Glorified art Thou! How lofty is Thy proof above all Thy creatures, though all are veiled from Thy Cause save those whom Thou hast singled out for the knowledge of Thee! For in Islam, whether in the whole or in the part, nothing hath been established save by that which Thou didst reveal unto him of Thy greatest proof—those verses wherewith Thou didst graciously favor him—for Thou didst not argue in the Qur’an by aught beside this.
Therefore do I bear witness unto Thee that Thy proof hath been made complete upon all contingent beings; and that what befell those who awaited Thy Beloved, and were promised concerning him, hath now befallen those who, in their religion, refer their affairs unto Thy Book—yet, heedless, veil themselves therefrom. Thou wilt assuredly contend with every one that hath believed in it: “Recite this, and then this.” If he should say, “The former was sent down from God,” how can he then endure in regard to this? And if he should say, “This is not like that,” his speech shall not, in the sight of God, be accounted true; for even so did they speak aforetime, yet they found naught of that which they said. Thus doth God establish the truth through His verses, and blot out the works of the veiled.
O God! Do Thou guide all who love me to Thy religion, for the Cause from Thee is equal: if the lowliest of creation were to believe in Thy proof and Thy verses, they would become the highest, and the most distant would become the nearest, while below this is to be veiled. O God! Do Thou preserve all Thy creation lest they be veiled from Thy Manifestation, that Thou mayest erase their essence and deeds while they perceive not. For all think they act for God, but Thou bearest witness only to those who believe in Thee and Thy verses, for besides them none work for Thee, nor will their earnings profit them.
I bear witness that one step in Thy path is better than all who have performed pilgrimage to Thy House, for none ascendeth to Thy House save by Thy leave. And at the time of the appearance of Thy Self, Thou art indeed more exalted and glorious than that any who would ascend could reach Thee, or that Thy devoted ones could attain unto Thee. For all who exceeded any of Thy Beloved’s successors, this was because Thy Beloved made him the manifestation of His Self, and likewise what was revealed at Thy Messenger’s tomb was because Thou didst make him Thy Prophet. Yet all who gained this are tested on that Day by the manifestation of Thy Self, for had they truly acted before, how could they be veiled on that Day?
Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee! How lofty is the elevation of Thy Word, how resplendent the sublimity of Thy evidence, which none can know save Thee! Thou beholdest the beginning of proof and arguest with that which Thou didst argue in the Revelation, after Thou didst manifest Thy love in such wise that all could recognize it. For all hopes cannot be likened to speech, and whoso hath recited Thy verses before will surely believe in Thy verses afterward. Thou hast made manifest the proof in such wise that all possessed of utterance can recognize it, such that were a child to recite from this or that and be asked “What dost thou recite?” he would say “The Book of God.”
Glorified art Thou! How great is Thy proof over all Thy creation, and how veiling are the veils of them that are veiled, who return not to that which the nature of a child would judge! Glory be to Thee! Thine is the grace upon whom Thou hast bestowed guidance, and from Thee is justice for whom Thou hast veiled from what Thou didst promise in the Hereafter and the former times.
Then will I yet bear witness unto Thee that, in that year, I did send down unto that Name five Tablets; and if they should not reach him, this verily is of the measures of Thy wisdom and the ordinances of Thy preserving care. Do Thou, O God, inspire each one with that whereby he may safeguard his own soul; for I have loved not, nor do I love, for any that have believed in Thee and in Thy signs, save this. Make Thou manifest, O God, this unto all Thy confessors of Thy unity, howsoever Thou willest and wheresoever Thou willest; for Thou art the Powerful, the All-Sufficient, the Overpowering, the Manifest, the Exalted, the Inaccessible.
And as to what hath been mentioned in his question concerning Thee, and Thy withholding him from ascent—no doubt is there that this proceedeth from the workmanship of Thy wisdom and the wondrousness of Thy mercy. Inspire him, O God, to return unto the House of Thy love, if he be able thereto; and if not, verily Thou hast permitted unto all Thy creatures that for which they were created, and hast made my station—despite the loftiness of its glory—such that, were all to desire to attain it, they could attain it; so that none might have any plea, saying: “I was unable to reach that for which I was created.”
Yet Thou hast made his station upon a height whereunto none of Thy creatures can ascend; and this hath not been, save through the wideness of Thy bounty unto them that know Thee, and the all-encompassingness of Thy bestowal upon them that glorify Thee.
But Thou, O my God, bearest witness that I have not wished for anyone to be saddened in my path, and therefore I have descended from the third lofty station of Thy proof. The matter is in Thy hands—O God, grant him what is best for him in his return and resting place. Verily Thou hast power over all things.
That which was taken with passionate love from the hair of the one created from that Nun belongs to him and none other has right to it. And what was mentioned of the pleasure of his love is what Thou bestowed upon those near ones from glory that all Thy chosen ones asked of Thee, which Thou granted only to the sincere. Thou wilt surely grant him this and ordain for him what Thou hast decreed herein, for by Thy word Thou createst what Thou willest and by Thy leave Thou manifestest what Thou desirest.
O God! Ordain for him what Thou hast decreed in that Most Exalted Height and Most Glorious Splendor, for the love of his heart speaks of his pleasure in obeying Thy paths of love and exalting Thy unity and Thy Word. O God! Preserve him that he may aid Thy Faith, for that day is nearer to Thee than this, and Thou art the Reckoner of all things.
What has been mentioned of that which has passed is what God decreed and then fulfilled. But the doors of God’s grace are open and response is assured for whoever calls upon God, for in every matter God aids His creation with what He sends down from His presence. In every Manifestation, the essence of creation is only for those who believe in Thee and Thy signs, for without them their existence profits not. And if there be profit in their existence, Thou must surely make them among those who turn to Thee.
Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. O God! Guide by Thy grace all who are on earth until there remains not in Thy knowledge that which Thou lovest not. Verily Thou art the Self-Sufficient, the Powerful.
What has been mentioned of the manifestation of Thy wondrous words is for those who believe not in Thy proof through His signs, else they would not be veiled by anything. For the people have only words whose meaning they comprehend not, and thus they were veiled on the day of Thy manifestation by what Thou hadst sent down before in the Qur’an, wherein Thou intended and mentioned naught but the remembrance of the Manifestation of Thy Self, through whom all remember.
And if any man should enter Thy Faith by virtue of that wherewith Thou hast set forth Thy proof in Thy Book, naught would arise within his heart save Thy good-pleasure; for whatsoever cometh to pass is for an appointed term. Yet the people will not reflect upon the proof of their religion—neither aforetime nor hereafter. Thy testimony hath been completed upon them, whether they be aware or remain unaware. And Thou, verily, art independent of all Thy creatures. Rather, he that believeth in Thee, by his own self is delivered from the fire; and he that veileth himself, by his own self entereth therein. And Thou hast of old revealed in the Furqan:

title: BB00052: Li-’Aliyyi’l-A’la
text:
“Will it not suffice them that We have sent down unto thee the Book to be recited unto them? Verily in it is mercy and a reminder unto a people who believe.”



















“We have guided him unto the way, whether he be thankful or unthankful.”

title: BB00052: Li-’Aliyyi’l-A’la
section: Part 2: “And as to that which hath been mentioned…”
text:
Part 2: “And as to that which hath been mentioned…”
And as to that which hath been mentioned touching Thy exalted decrees—glorified, glorified art Thou above permitting, for Thine loved ones, aught other than that which Thou hast chosen for Thine elect, and selected for Thy favored ones. Thy wont hath ever been bounty and bestowal, the uplifting of the Cause and the loosening of bonds. Were it to be according to Thy justice, none would be found worthy of Thy decree. Yet hast Thou ordained the measures of all things by Thy wisdom, in such wise that, were all Thy creatures to ponder thereon, they would surely behold the mystery of its beginning and its end.
Wherefore, O my God, bestow upon me and upon them that love Thee that which Thou dost send down upon Thy chosen ones, and preserve me, O my Lord, from aught whereby anyone might be grieved in Thy path, for such is Thy decree for those who have believed in Thee and Thy signs. Glory be unto Thee! How exalted is Thy power in creating certitude in the heart through such an impregnable Book, wherein the measure of all decrees is naught but Thy command, and which regardeth not the essence of things except as Thou dost ordain.
Indeed, it hath been mentioned that wert Thou to create the number of all things from among those who believe not in Thee, it would not cause any soul to waver who is steadfast in Thy love and allegiance. Yea, by Thy glory! This is the height of certitude for those who know Thee, and the station of knowledge and wisdom for those who gaze upon the dawning-places of Thy signs and evidences. Nothing in all creation could be more precious than this, for were one to possess all things but lack this, it would profit him not, while after attaining this, nothing could diminish its excellence.
As for what hath been mentioned concerning the followers of the Letters of the Living, this is due to what Thou hast ordained therein regarding the Manifestation of Thyself. While the Sun of Thy Revelation shineth, Thou art indeed too glorious and exalted to permit anyone save through It. Verily do I call Thee to witness that Thy decree concerning the Letter Ya’ hath been fulfilled. Blessed is he who attaineth their days through Thy bounty; and whoso attaineth them not hath no path save unto their stations.
And Thy decree regarding the Ha’—each, according to what Thou hast ordained and irrevocably decreed—pointeth unto Thee and summoneth all unto Thee. Blessed, then, is he who meeteth them in the days of their manifestation, ere their appointed terms are sent down upon them from their Lord, or the measured decrees of destiny from their Fashioner.
I bear witness that after them, all who follow Thee are like unto them, having been guided by Thy guidance through them, while none can ascend to Thy names and attributes save Thee alone, there is no God but Thee. After the mention of the special one hath been cut off, countless are they who exemplify that First Unity. Those Letters have presented themselves before Thee through the attraction of their hearts, and were there any upon earth closer to Thee than they, they would surely bear witness to Thy signs apart from them.
Verily, true glory consisteth in the knowledge of Thee, and not in that wherewith all Thy creatures seek to glory; for the first of religion is the recognition of Thee. Thou hast, moreover, bestowed Thy grace upon those Manifestations, granting them the knowledge of Thee before all Thy servants, and Thou didst apprise that Name at the dawning of Thy Revelation. Yet, inasmuch as its faith was not made manifest, Thou didst admit it among those Letters; and should it manifest faith, it would be accounted as one of them. For glory is in the knowledge of Thee and in following Thy signs.
And after that One, there is no doubt that He is mentioned in the second One; for, once thou hadst recognized Him, the book of His faith was come. He is a Name among Thy Names, and a Manifestation of glory among Thy Manifestations. Such a Revelation is even as that of Thy Beloved: the first to turn unto Him aforetime is the very one that turneth unto Him in a later Manifestation thereafter. For the “latter” is none other than Thy Revelation in the “former,” and the “inward” is none other than Thy hiddenness within the “outward.”
And as to that which hath been decreed concerning the span of his life—were it Thy pleasure to cause him to appear at the age of thirty, there is no way for him save this; and should it be otherwise, it would proceed even as it proceeded for Thy Beloved of old, and even before that. Glory be to Thee! There is none other God but Thee. All is from Thee, and by Thee, and then from Thee and unto Thee alone. There is none other God but Thee.
How many a servant hath visited the grave of Thy chosen one, ʿAli, and yet, in His Revelation, knew Him not; and until this day I have not heard of any that hath visited him—inasmuch as that people gaze only upon the loftiness of His Manifestation. Were they to ponder the ways of His Cause, they would surely recognize His Revelation in its latterness, and would not veil themselves from Him by aught—neither in its firstness nor in its latterness. Wherefore do Thou, O God, inspire all who desire His good-pleasure with those eight Letters, ere Thou reveal them unto them in that Manifestation; for what Thou didst formerly enjoin was but the preparation of mankind for that Day. How then shall I mention what hath been ordained by Thee for such as have none above the Cause like unto them? For from the first of the Manifestation until this day Thou hast taken the jewels of the earth, that the number of the chiefs might be made complete—three hundred and thirteen souls—drawn from among them whose clay Thou hast fashioned from the clay of Thy love, and who have been attracted unto Thee.
Blessed, then, is he that turneth unto Thee and preserveth the mention of his name until the Day of Resurrection in Thy Book—before Thee, and then before them that have known Thee. This, verily, is the great bounty; for all men toil and act for Thy sake, perchance Thou mayest accept their works. Yet the acceptance of the deeds of Thy creatures can appear only in the signs that proceed from Thy Proof. How, then, have all who labor for Thee been veiled, deeming that they labor for God, while in Thy sight they are far beneath Him? Even though all returneth unto Thee.
Do Thou, therefore, O God, raise up all mankind from their slumber; for Thy mercy hath encompassed them, and all are Thy servants and in Thy grasp. We beseech Thee, of Thy bounty, for the best thereof, and of Thy generosity, for the choicest thereof: bestow upon us Thy good-pleasure, and accept our deeds from the first that hath no first—inasmuch as we have labored for Thee until this day—by uttering but “Yea.” For beneath all things such as this hath not appeared in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and Thou art, indeed, the Most Bountiful, the Most Great.
And as to what hath been mentioned in the Books of old concerning that which Thou didst command to be purchased thereafter according to Thy good-pleasure—He loveth naught save what Thou hast loved; and, beyond doubt, the nearer unto Thee, the nearer. Thou art the All-Encompassing over all. And what hath been mentioned of him who was tried in Thy path is, in Thy sight, greater than that deed, and mightier than that goodly act in Thy presence. I testify before Thee that even the weight of a mote expended in that way is greater with Thee than the spending of all that is upon the earth, were it to be laid at its stations.
Bestow, then, O God, upon him the grace to return unto his home, that the eyes of my mother may be consoled thereby; verily Thou art powerful over all things. (Concerning the matter of Muhammad ʿAli.) And whoso hath desired this hath trafficked with God, his Lord. His footsteps are dearer unto God than that he should perform pilgrimage two thousand and one times; for whoso quickeneth a soul, it is as though he had quickened all mankind. Do Thou, therefore, send down upon him the recompense of that from all that hath no equal with Thee in Thy knowledge—having neither peer, nor like, nor counterpart, nor semblance, nor associate. And establish, O God, his heart in Thy love and in the knowledge of Thee; for he is, beyond doubt, of the names of Thy might. When he heard of the Manifestation of Thy Cause, he severed himself and hastened unto the Manifestation of Thy Self from the land wherein he dwelt—whether it were two years, or more, or less. Do Thou, then, pour upon him all Thy bounty and mercy, all Thy munificence, generosity, and gifts; for Thou art, verily, the Ever-Bestowing, the Most Generous.
And what hath been mentioned of Thy presence before the veiled Word—when he did desire it, there was written for him even as there was written of old in the Qur’an for the third Word, which did answer its Lord among the Letters of the Living out of its hiddenness. And though there be upon the earth, apart from it, a resting-place, it would assuredly answer God of itself. I had loved that it might be nearer unto me; yet since it answered not, it was not made manifest unto him. I testify before Thee that none is nearer unto me than my mother in Thy sight; and from the beginning of my life until the last that Thou hast ordained for me, I have desired her good-pleasure.
Do Thou, therefore, O God, be well-pleased with her who did rear him in his childhood; for Thou hast bestowed upon her a favor whereat the former and the latter will envy. Thou hast already declared that the Manifestation of that Most Exalted Name—were he not to behold upon himself a veil that hindereth him—would return unto her, bring her peace from Him Who reared him, and gladden her with the tidings of the grace God hath bestowed upon her and upon her kindred. This is an honor unmatched by any comparison, and an elevation unto which no likeness may be found; and this is my good-pleasure in every affair.
Mayest Thou, O God, cause the means thereof to run their course; and mayest Thou gladden her eyes with that which Thou lovest and approvest, in her first and in her last. Remove, then, from us all her sorrow, through that One whom He that reared him knoweth, and through the assurance she hath of the loftiness of His Cause and the splendor of His glory which God hath revealed unto Him. Verily Thou art powerful over all things.
And mayest Thou inspire, O God, that Name, that he may accomplish the manifestations of Thy wondrous creations, and whatsoever Thy decrees desire—though thereby he be made to grieve. For I will cause them to appear, by Thine leave, in gratitude for Thy bounties from her, and for the perfecting of Thy favor in her presence. For, apart from it, were all that are on the earth to be gathered together to alter a single letter, they would not be able; nor could they add aught thereto—save as Thou willest, or for whomsoever Thou willest, in Thy Manifestation. This is of that wherewith Thou hast bestowed favor upon her. Verily Thou art the Possessor of great bounty, that she may be well-pleased with the Manifestation of her Lord, and be of the thankful.
And as to what hath been mentioned concerning the appearance of deliverance: Thou hast, O my God, manifested—through the appearance of a Proof—what all that are on the earth have been powerless to produce. For, short of that station, from after Muhammad until this day, in his community, hidden and manifest, it hath profited them nothing. Nay, deliverance is that which Thou hast manifested from One whose wisdom none hath encompassed, from One with all-encompassing wisdom; Signs before which all the worlds have been brought low—Signs whereby He establisheth what He willeth and doeth what He pleaseth. He is not asked of that which He doeth, and none shall question Thy judgment.
Inspire, then, O God, all Thy creatures to recognize the worth of these days; for if they set, they shall behold them only from Him whom Thou wilt make manifest. And the creatures shall be in the deepest night, even as they were after Muhammad, until Thou dost bestow upon them the appearance of Thy Self on the Day of Resurrection; for then shall all be gathered in the day.
And as to what hath been mentioned concerning the other: I testify unto Thee that this was not by leave from me. Nay, I commanded all to follow Thy ordinances from aforetime, until they might compass with knowledge the stations of Thy Cause. For then—if he behold not for himself aught that maketh him sorrow—he is by a leave from Thee; otherwise, Thy self-sufficiency is manifest and Thy independence resplendent; for glory is in the knowledge of Thee and in following Thee.
And though the sustenances wherewith Thou providest Thine loved ones in the Revelation of Thy wondrous creation be gentler and sweeter than what Thou didst formerly send down—yet if none be saddened thereby, and naught injure him, still Thy decrees of old abide firm. Exalt, then, O God, Thy word, that all may draw their sustenance from the first-fruits of the gardens of Thy Paradise.
And I will seek provision meet for the babe in his mother’s womb, if he find unto that a path; and do Thou, O God, convey unto him, from his hidden place, all this. For if he return to his land, he will surely relate it to such as are seen in him to possess certitude in God and His Signs—provided he be not grieved thereby in Thy path; for Thou hast not been pleased that any should sorrow in Thy way. Rather hast Thou loved that Thy good-pleasure should be made manifest through the honoring of Thine loved ones, the exaltation of Thy sincere ones, and the inviolability of Thine saints.
And preserve, O God, all who have believed in Thee and then in Thy Signs, from before them and from behind them, from their right and from their left, from above their heads and beneath their feet—by Thy guardianship, Thy protection, Thy preservation, Thy stronghold, and Thy care. Verily Thou upholdest the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them by Thy power, and preservest all things by Thy might. No command is save from Thee, no bounty save from Thy presence, no glory save in Thy good-pleasure, no loftiness save in the knowledge of Thee and in Thy splendor. There is no power except from Thee.
Send blessings, O God, upon the Primal Point, and upon the Letters of the Primal, and upon all who resemble those Letters, to such a number as Thou dost reckon—according to what befitteth the exaltation of Thy bounty, the loftiness of Thy favor, the elevation of Thy munificence, the inviolability of Thy tenderness, and the self-subsistence of Thy lordship. Verily Thou hast encompassed all things; Thou art powerful over all things; Thou art independent of all things; and Thou art knowing of all things.
And inspire him, O God, that he may send forth a prayer such as this unto the possessors of Thy love, that he may show them the good that is therein—lest any be veiled from Thy Manifestation on the Day of Resurrection. And all were assured of Thy Signs.

title: BB00351: Da’irat’il-Hirz
text:
In the Name of God, the Exalted, the Mighty
Praise be to Him Who created all things according to the form of His love and made known to all His sovereign signs, that none might be veiled from the countenance of their Beloved, nor anything be distant from the station of nearness to its Goal. Glorified and exalted is He! His essential camphor-like nature is too great to be known through description or majesty, and His essential cypress-like being is too holy to be described through manifestations of power before the appearance of all things and after their concealment. There is no God but He, the King, the Manifest, the Resplendent, the Sovereign, the Powerful, the Subduer, Who has ordained the measures of all things under the shadow of His command, and made the essences of all things between the Kaf and the Nun through the revolution of the Vav by the appearance of the Ha’ in the degree of concealment.
This is the handiwork of God whereby He creates what He creates and originates whatever He originates. He has ever been unknown through His creation and indescribable through His servants. He brings forth what He wishes through His Will without any prior origination, and does what He desires through His Purpose without any previous mention in His kingdom. For glorified is He! At every instant He is engaged in a wondrous creation. Before all things He has sent forth a sign of His oneness and a manifestation from the countenance of His eternality to all things, that all might know what God, glorified be He, has intended for His creation. His Messenger has conveyed this and those who were witnesses after him have testified to it, and those who came after them act according to their command.
Furthermore, whosoever God enables to act according to what has been written and to comprehend what has been revealed, let him act as commanded. That is, he should keep with him for nineteen complete days, without separation, the circle whose pillars have been described and whose signs have been perfected, beginning from the night of the fifth of the first ten days of each month and ending on the twenty-fourth day of that month. After the obligatory prayers he should recite these seven Names—Living, One, Self-Subsisting, Almighty, Creator, Luminous, Subduer—nineteen times. When he has finished reciting these seven invocations, let him recite this prayer. Before he completes his practice, God will set right what he desires through His grace and fulfill it through His favor. Verily He is the Powerful, the All-Sufficient, the Guardian, Whom nothing in the heavens or earth can frustrate, nor can any matter in the kingdom of creation prove too great for Him. His command is but to say to a thing “Be!” and it is.
This is the prayer:
In the Name of God, the Exalted, the Great! O Lord! I beseech Thee by every Name which is Thine in Thy knowledge, that Thou send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and those whom Thou hast created from the overflowing light of the family of Muhammad. Grant me, through the sovereignty of Thy singleness and bestow upon me, through the dominion of Thy eternality, mercy from Thy presence regarding what Thou knowest of my inner state and witnessest of my outer condition. For none besides Thee knows what is desired, and none other than Thee has power to fulfill my request save Thee alone.
Therefore I beseech Thee by the light of Thy exalted and sublime countenance and the splendor of Thy exalted and mighty presence, that Thou say to what I have desired in the path of Thy love, “Be!” and it is. Indeed God has said to all who ask, “Be!” and it is. That is God’s command, nearer than all things. To Him belongs whatsoever is in the heavens and on earth. He does what He wishes by His command, and He truly has power over all things. He bestows favor upon whom He wishes without desert and grants bounty to whom He desires from His presence without any path of certitude. This is from God’s grace upon all things. He is possessed of mighty grace. Glorified be God, Lord of the heavens and earth, Lord of all the worlds! Indeed peace from God be upon His sincere servants. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.
Answer to the question of Shaykh Nasir al-Din al-Karbala’i, year 1264.

title: BB00108
text:
Part 1: “Ye believe and are certain in the Unity…”
…Ye believe and are certain in the Unity, and God hath singled out the Point of the Bayan with His verses and then this science, which is the greatest proof from God, a knowledge for all the worlds, would ye but reflect upon it. All are powerless before the first, and none have encompassed knowledge of the second save after what We have revealed in the Book, and ye shall act according to what God hath taught you thereafter.
When the years of your children reach the number of eleven, ye shall teach them this science as a bounty from God, that they may be grateful. And ye shall write the temple of Unity and preserve it as ye desire. All of these are eleven units from the Names which ye write in nineteen temples, and whatsoever ye desire to add. And be ye certain that all began from the first temple and unto it shall all return.
(in tabular form) 1—Wahid—Mahbub—Bidavi—Jazal—Ilah—Majid—Hish—Basit—Vazi’—Muluk—Haqq—29—36—48—60—220—84—96—108
2—Halik—Qavi—Din—Hasib—Basit—Vali—Masik—Hamid—Hafif—Fanis—Kharif
3—Madil—ʿAqd—Vazi’—Mukabbir—Huda—Madaf—Munif—Hariz—Mubir—Farah—Shaydur
4—Baqi—Kabir—Fazi’—Ni’am—ʿIlm—Qasab—Qarfasam—Farah—Musavvir—Farif—Katib
5—ʿAlim
6—Qayus
7—Sarif
8—Raydur
9—Mubir
10—Qasman
11—Raziq
12—Musavvir
13—Rayfu’
14—Nasran
15—Katab
16—Hatm
17—Sayravi
18—Rashad
19—Fatil
And God preserveth those who are in the Bayan from differing in a matter, for God loveth not differences.
Know with certainty that the differences in each Manifestation are like the differences in that Manifestation, such as the differences between Moses and Jesus in their Manifestation, and this is what the people truly read in their religion. And perhaps the differences are parts of the Manifestation, just as Moses was divided into seventy-two sects, and Jesus likewise, and the community of Muhammad similarly, and verily each one of them was true in their manifestation.
In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful
Blessed is He Who sendeth down, upon whomsoever He willeth, the Spirit of the Cause. Be at ease, and fear not: verily God, thy Lord, is Forgiving, Grateful; and there is none other God but He. He hath caused the Book to descend by His command, that men may learn the ordinance of their Lord, the All-Merciful, in every inscribed letter; and We, in truth, bestow the wondrous judgment upon whomsoever We will of Our servants, according to a measure ordained.
Convey, O thou exalted man, the Message in every condition; for, this day, all shall be brought to appear before the mention of the Name of thy Lord. Whoso followeth Our verses, and striveth on the Day of the First—these have We confirmed—such are they that shall attain. But as for those who followed the command of God, yet went not forth from their dwellings for the sake of the covenant of God’s Remembrance, their works shall not profit them, and they are in manifest error. Sufficient is this Book as a proof for him who desireth to believe in the signs of God and be of them that bow down. And say: Praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds.
The Messenger of God—may the blessings of God be upon Him and His kindred—hath said: “We have not worshipped Thee with the worship Thou dost deserve, nor have we known Thee with the knowledge Thou dost merit.” And his descendant, ʿAli ibn al-Husayn—peace be upon them both—hath said in the Dawn Supplication (in the portion wherein he maketh mention of the summary concerning the return): “O my God! By Thy might and Thy majesty and by Thy greatness: were I, from the day Thou didst originate me, to worship Thee from the beginning of time with a worship enduring through the everlastingness of Thy lordship—were every hair, in every blink of the eye, to offer Thee, unto eternity, the praise of all created things and their gratitude altogether—yet should I be found wanting in the discharge of thanksgiving for the hidden blessing of but one of Thy favors unto me.”
And he saith, in substance: “And were I to crush the mines of the world’s iron with my body, and to till its earth with the lids of mine eyes; and were I to weep, for fear of Thee, tears abundant as the heavens and the earth—supplication and blood—this would still be little beside the great right Thou hast over me.” And he addeth: “And were it that Thou, O my God, shouldst punish me thereafter with the punishment of all created things together, and shouldst increase the fire behind me and within my body, and shouldst fill the layers of Gehenna because of me, that in the fire there might be one tormented other than myself, and that there be no fuel for Hell but me—this would yet be, by Thy justice toward me, but little compared with the abundance of what Thy pardoning-kindness hath made incumbent.”
And ʿAli—peace be upon him—hath said (ascribed here as the “Pillar”): “I have not worshipped Thee for fear of Thy fire, nor for longing after Thy paradise; rather did I find Thee worthy of worship, and therefore worshipped Thee.” Such is the station of his servitude—may the blessings of God rest upon him. Nay, the very secret of the Cause is that every hair of their bodies, in all states, voiced the like.
And the Proof, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, the Lord of the Age—peace be upon them both—hath said in the Friday supplication (some words here being uncertain):
And thus is the station of contentment unto God, the One, the Single. And he saith (in meaning):
Glory be to Thee, O my God! There is no knowledge save Thee—Thou alone, without partner. Thou, O my God, knowest our evil deeds—none but Thee. I seek forgiveness for all that which Thou lovest not; and I call upon Thee in every state with the tongue of Thy inspiration, as Thou willest. And Thou art the Self-Sufficient, peerless beyond compare.

title: BB00108
text:
“O my God, my Master and my Lord! By Thy greatness and Thy majesty: Thou art the Intended One, and Thou art the Worshipped—none beside Thee, O my God. The paths of severance have caused me to utter … and in the ways of inviolability … signs … Glory be to Thee, O my God: Thy Manifestation is more manifest than all things, that I should point to aught beside Thee; and Thy love is sweeter than all knowing, that I should stand in need of knowing other than Thee. Glory be to Thee, O my God: I have believed in Thee as Thou art—Thou art; and I repent of myself and of all that is before the worlds, as Thou art—Thou art. I have fled, O my God, with my whole being unto Thee, and cast … unto Thee. I possess nothing before Thee: if Thou punish me with all Thy power, Thou art most just in judgment; and if Thou ennoble me with all good, Thou art the Lord of bounty and bestowal; and verily Thou art independent of all the worlds.”



“O my Master: thus have I reached Thee; and I found only, in knowledge, severance from all beside Thee. I sought Thy love, and found it only by effacing all that is other than Thee. I sought obedience unto Thee, and found it only in the love of Thy loved ones.”

title: BB00108
section: Part 2: “There is no God but Thee. Glorified be…”
text:
Part 2: “There is no God but Thee. Glorified be…”
There is no God but Thee. Glorified be Thou above the descriptions of them that liken Thee unto created things—exalted, exceeding high.
…words… from the beginning… of the jurists… in the Rida’i Visitation, upon him and his seven fathers and his four sons be the prayers of God:

“O Sovereign Bestower! I am the fugitive, with my whole being—my oneness and the very essence of my praise—hastening unto Thee. Had not Thy Lord encompassed my unity, it would have been better for me; for, before I affirmed His oneness, I bore but a single fault; but after I affirmed His oneness, it is as though I had committed every fault—since His very remembrance is a sin… and I have acquired every guilt; and my remembrance of myself—of the remembrancers—is a sin… amidst seven… whose groaning… Therefore there is no escape save… and today is the first… for, within Thee, there remaineth not… its pillars… in Thy annihilation. Nor is there any flight but that I take refuge in Thy court. There is no remembrance save His remembrance; no glory save His glory; no praise save His praise; no loftiness save His loftiness; no nearness save His nearness; no manifestness save His manifestness; no hiddenness save His hiddenness. Therefore hath God commanded all to return unto Thee, to come before Thee, to confess Thy guardianship, to arise in obedience unto Thee, to cleave to the cord of Thine infallibility, and to gaze upon the lights of the effulgence of Thy Countenance—O my Master—and the mercy of God and His blessings…”

…sin and conjunction… sin… and grace between them, and union between them… and the gaze… from…? (Signature of Haji Rafi’ …) to this… sin… from its extremities and …? …sin… sin—then those refused…? …the last of the supplications: “Ya Hu.”
Glorified art Thou, O my Beloved! I knew not that I was heedless, and that all beside me was mad—how is it that I behold some who neglect Thy remembrance and take delight in other than Thee, and build up the world though they know it shall pass away? Some worship Thee for what Thou givest them; some ask Thee for the needs they desire; some abandon the world and sever themselves from its pleasures, yet forsake Thy good-pleasure in the world to come; some obey Thee out of fear; some worship Thee out of love; some affirm Thy unity because Thy oneness is nobler than all things; and some remember Thee because Thy remembrance is more manifest than every remembrance.
Yet when I look closely upon their souls and lift the veil from their deeds, I see them as associators in Thy sight, far removed from Thy nearness—for even the greatest of them is he who loveth Thy remembrance because it is clearer than all things… whereas He Himself is like unto nothing, and in truth he worshippeth but himself, granting it its portion, and making… for his need… a resting-place… Glory be to Thee! Is one like Thee to be sought for…? How far astray are men: they ask their own selves and forget Thy greatness… They ask of Thee their wants, though they know that all beside Thee is naught in Thy presence… and that what is not turned toward Thee, and what asketh Thee for that which perisheth in a few brief days—how can it befit the world without end in its totality…?
Glory be to Thee, glory be to Thee! By Thy might… I know not by what path I should remember Thee, nor by what proof I should keep silence before Thy Countenance… I stand before Thee and say what Thou hast taught me: “I commit my affair unto God; verily God seeth His servants.” …It was sent down upon me upon that mountain… wrote the truth… Thou knowest them better than I. Grant, O God, unto each of the seven… what they desire in… for Thou art the Munificent, and…
The difference is the measure of two letters—how then beyond that? Yet We have sent down at the beginnings of the differences words firm and clear, whereby shall the veiled be raised up—and also the people of unveiling and discovery shall see all these as from a single Tree: at its summit it calleth out, from God its Lord, “Verily there is no God but I, the All-Glorious, the Most Glorious!” and at its lowest degree it crieth of itself, “Verily I am the least of every small thing!” and between the two its degrees are beyond counting—each by the command of God; and all, by His command, make mention.
Then, then… the tahlilat of the first of every month and its last. It behoveth not him that is able to read to abandon them; and whoso reciteth, God shall bestow upon him, for every letter ghayn, two-and-fifty degrees in Ridvan:
“There is no God but God”—as many as all that He hath created and will create. “There is no God but God”—as many as all that He hath brought forth and will bring forth. “There is no God but God”—as many as all that He hath originated and will originate. “There is no God but God”—as many as all that He hath ordained and will ordain. “There is no God but God”—as many as all that He hath been and will be. “There is no God but God”—as many as all that He hath decreed and will decree. “There is no God but God”—as many as all that He hath … and will … “There is no God but God”—as many as all that He hath willed and will will; “There is no God but God”—as many as all that hath gone forth and will go forth; “There is no God but God”—as many as all that He hath determined and will determine; “There is no God but God”—as many as all that He hath formed and will form; “There is no God but God”—as many as all that He hath verified and will verify; “There is no God but God”—as many as all that He hath found and will find; “There is no God but God”—from the first that hath no first, as many as every number; “There is no God but God”—unto the last that hath no last, as many as every sun of truth that hath risen or shall rise.
In the Name of God, the Most Unassailable, the Most Holy.
God hath borne witness that there is none other God but He. His are creation and command: He giveth life and causeth death, causeth death and giveth life; and He is the Living Who dieth not. In His grasp is the dominion of all things. He createth what He willeth by His command; verily He is powerful over all things.
Then bear thou witness that there is none other God but He, the All-Watchful, the Self-Subsisting; and that He is the True One Who standeth—He in whom all are promised. So give thanks unto your Lord, the All-Merciful, at every moment—before every moment and after every moment.
…Write not part of the Tablet… a remembrance from God, the Most High… thereby… it shall not be manifested by God on the Day of Resurrection—then shall ye remember… God… Mighty… Most Exalted… Strong… Sovereign… King… All-Watchful…

title: BB00672: Letter to Muhammad Karim Khan Kirmani
text:
In the Name of God, the Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner, the All-Subduing, the All-Powerful
Praise be to God, Who hath revealed Himself unto the realm of possibility through the radiance of the lights of His Countenance, which hath dawned from the horizon of His creative Will—that Will which He brought forth for its own sake, by its own Self…
And naught is beheld in any thing save the signs of the effulgences of His Manifestation; indeed, He hath filled the inmost reality of every thing with the vesture of His majesty…
Then came the truth, and the Cause of God was made manifest, and the Day is God’s Day, grievous for the disbelievers. Verily, this is the Hour which hath appeared, and the moon is cleft asunder, and the signs have been sent down; yet the deniers have said: ʿThis is but a persistent sorcery’…
Say: Taste ye the chastisement for your idolatry! This is the Tree of Zaqqum…
We have, indeed, threatened the sinful one with a sore punishment, with scorching blast, and boiling water, and a fire of blazing hell. The threatened doom hath been fulfilled. Taste it, O thou that wast called mighty and noble!…
The word “athim” (“sinful”) hath been repeatedly revealed in the Glorious Qur’an. In the Surih of Baqarah He saith: “And God loveth not every obstinate unbelieving sinner”—that is, God loveth not the wrongdoer who persisteth in unbelief. And in the Surih of Nisa’ He saith: “Verily God loveth not him who is treacherous and sinful”—that is, God loveth not the sinner who is a traitor.
And in the Surih of Shu’ara’ He saith:

“Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every lying sinner”

—that is, would ye that I acquaint you upon whom the demons descend? They descend upon those people who are fabricators of lies and steeped in sin.
And in the Surih of Dukhan there have likewise been sent down verses to which reference hath already been made. And in the Surih of Jathiyah He saith:

“Woe betide every lying sinner, who heareth the signs of God recited unto him, yet persisteth in arrogance as though he had not heard them. Announce thou unto him a grievous punishment. And when he learneth aught of Our signs, he maketh a mockery thereof. These are they for whom there is a humiliating chastisement.”
crumbs: BB00672: Letter to Muhammad Karim Khan Kirmani

title: BB00657: Tafsir-i Kun wa Yakun
text:
Part 1: “Praise be to God, the Originator of origination…”
In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Most Compassionate
Praise be to God, the Originator of origination, the Producer of invention, the Creator of whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is on earth—He beside Whom there is no God. No description of His creation taketh hold upon Him, nor doth any attribute of His servants ascend unto Him.
