title: BB00690
text:
All men have proceeded from God and unto Him shall all return. All shall appear before Him for judgment. He is the Lord of the Day of Resurrection, of Regeneration and of Reckoning, and His revealed Word is the Balance.
True death is realized when a person dieth to himself at the time of His Revelation in such wise that he seeketh naught except Him.
True resurrection from the sepulchers means to be quickened in conformity with His Will, through the power of His utterance.
Paradise is attainment of His good-pleasure and everlasting hellfire His judgment through justice.
The Day He revealeth Himself is Resurrection Day which shall last as long as He ordaineth.
Everything belongeth unto Him and is fashioned by Him. All besides Him are His creatures….

title: BB00059
text:
Part 1: “Verily, O my God, Thou didst rear me…”
Verily, O my God, Thou didst rear me among the non-Arabs and nurture me like unto the unlettered ones for the day when, shouldst Thou desire that I manifest Thy signs, none would fabricate lies against me and all would submit to Thy signs. Thou hast indeed ordained obedience to the true divines for this my day, lest anyone should deny me in anything, for I call the people to Thy Book, the Qur’an, unto which falsehood approacheth not from before it nor from behind it.
And whoso desireth to believe in me needeth no proof, as though I were one of their divines whom Thou hast made their rejection to be Thy rejection and their obedience Thy obedience. But since Thou knowest that pure truth will not be accepted save by a few, Thou hast sent down unto me Thy verses in such wise that were all to gather together to produce the like of a single verse, they would neither be able nor capable, lest anyone should think of me other than the truth. And Thou hast filled my heart with verses of intimate communion with Thee in such wise that none of the believers can surpass me, nor can any of the truthful ones withstand me.
And Thou hast expanded my breast with the subtleties of knowledge and the realities of what is known in such wise that none among all the people can surpass me, as though all Thy signs encompassed me from every direction, such that none around me can do aught but deny Thy signs and be numbered among the idolaters. And Thou hast made my hand a power of truth whereby I write whatsoever I will by Thy leave without thought, and Thou hast established in my heart such strength that I have called all unto Thee and feared no one.
And today, O my God, Thou knowest my station, and I do complain unto Thee of my tribulations, for they have debased what Thou hast exalted and exalted what Thou hast abased in Thy Book, and they have grown proud against Thy servants who have no portion in my judgment save helplessness, until the oppressor hath oppressed, and the reviler hath reviled, and the denier hath denied, and he hath verified what was false, and praised what was reprehensible, and exalted that which hath no standing among the people.
Alas, alas, O my God! Verily the divines pass judgment against anyone with a judgment that none can reject through Thy judgment. What is decreed is accomplished, and there is no power save in God.
And verily, O my God, through the workings of Thy wisdom, Thou hast made my proof in Thy religion like unto the proof of the verses of Muhammad, the Apostle of God, may God’s blessings be upon Him and His family, lest anyone should doubt my truth, and should all who are on earth desire to believe, they would have no proof before Thee. And were naught else to exist alongside it, nothing would diminish from Thy proof, for Thou hast made the proof a sign that transcendeth all signs, with which no token can compare, from which no evidence can be separated, and wherein the deeds of the idolaters cannot be conceived. And by it are all Thy servants tested and Thy loved ones proved, until there hath issued forth from Thy presence that wherein is naught of Thy wrath, and that which is wholly Thine alone, no partner hast Thou. None hath any proof against Thee, for Thy proof hath reached all hands, and even if Thou didst make the entire proof of Thy beloved Muhammad, the Apostle of God, may God’s blessings be upon Him and His family, to be the Surih of Kawthar, none would have the right to utter a word concerning it, and it is incumbent upon all to believe in it.
After Thou hast ordained for those verses a limit, Thou dost send down in every circumstance whatsoever Thou willest, as Thou willest, through what Thou willest, when Thou willest. None can repel Thy command, none can reverse Thy words, and no proof before Thee and before the believers among Thy servants is greater than Thy verses, for the spirit of divine lordship and the mystery of eternality, which is Thy love for me, is made manifest.
Concerning her in Thy verses, which are a proof for those of Thy servants who are nigh unto Thee. Thou hast made the outward meaning of Thy verses a proof for the idolaters, that they might witness their own powerlessness to produce the like thereof throughout all ages and the eternity of manifestations. Thus was Thy proof made complete against all mankind, that he who perisheth might perish with clear evidence, and he who liveth might live with clear evidence, and that none might say “Had God made His verses known to me, I would have been among the believers.”
O my God! I bear witness that on the day when Thou didst complete Thy proof concerning my own self, Thou didst complete it for all through a scroll of Thy intimate communion, lest anyone should fabricate falsehood. Verily Thou didst choose the pure ones of creation and made them beforehand from among the followers of Muhammad and Kazim, Thy two servants who fulfilled Thy covenant and were faithful to Thy decree, and were among those possessed of certitude. All know that when a youth from their community debates with any of the great scholars, he prevails over him and renders him utterly confounded, such that he cannot answer him, when he follows the truth and is among the truthful ones.
Thou knowest that when their days were ended, the necks of their great ones were raised up to assume their station, by reason of its loftiness, majesty, grandeur and beauty, until Thou didst manifest Thy servant wherein none had discerned their cause, and Thou didst send it down upon one of Thy unlettered servants of whom none suspected knowledge. Therefore didst Thou conceal my name, and had none ever appeared, I would not have manifested it, for Thou knowest therein what none save Thee can know, until what was to appear appeared and what was to be achieved was achieved. At the time of manifestation, it was raised to such a station as to reach the East and West of the earth, such that I myself heard some Bedouins speaking of it in the Sacred Mosque.
Thou knowest, O my God, that on the first day I did not think anyone would see my scroll with patience concerning my right, or would say “nay,” for the gates of knowledge and the keys of truth were stored and unveiled in my words. I attributed my writings to Thy Living Proof lest anyone should magnify himself or lie, though all good descended from Him and upon Him does one rely. Had the Messengers attributed to me, the people would not have believed, for none of the learned ones came with such, and it is a station of Thy good proofs and great in the eyes of the people.
O my God! When Thou didst desire to try Thy servants, Thou didst send down trials and made the companions of Thy trial to be oppressed, until the oppressor oppressed and the liar lied, and the fabricators found comfort in their knowledge. Thou didst know their station and didst reveal the inner states of Thy servants who believed and conveyed and migrated by what they did and wrote and took. Verily Thou knowest all things and nothing is hidden from Thee. Thereby didst Thou try all from the first day until none remained in that land save one or two or three, moving with the shadow, fearful and apprehensive.
Glorified art Thou! Glorified art Thou! How mighty is Thy proof, how generous Thy gift, and how great Thy trial! I seek refuge in Thee and hold fast to Thy cord. There is no power nor strength save in Thee. I thank Thee for what Thou willest when Thou willest, and I praise Thee for what Thou pleasest. None can resist Thy command or reverse Thy decree. Thou hast tried all in such wise that none hath any proof against Thee, and Thou hast made Thy mighty Cause so humble that every soul among Thy servants can recognize it and draw nigh unto it. But since they were veiled from Thy countenance, Thy angels intervened between them such that they were unable to draw nigh. Glorified art Thou! Glorified art Thou! This is naught but Thy trial.
Thou causest whom Thou willest to go astray, and guidest whom Thou willest. Verily, those who lead themselves astray through their own doings have no refuge, and they have no guide. And those who are certain of Thy judgment shall never be led astray. And here am I, O my God, seeking Thy forgiveness for what my hands have wrought. Thou knowest that I have not drawn near to this Cause except out of fear of Thee alone—there is no God but Thee. From the days when Thou didst not manifest Thy Covenant, no one belied me. And now Thou hearest what Thou hearest concerning me, and seest what Thou seest regarding my judgment. I have placed my trust in Thee and committed my affairs unto Thee.
The calumniators have transgressed against me just as the ancients transgressed against those who were nigh unto Thee. One says this, then that, and I, by Thy glory, am ashamed before Thee to let flow from my pen what they fabricate and know. I complain unto Thee of my anguish and grief, and all that they utter against me without right. I see it as similar to what the Christians say concerning Thee. None of them can harm me save as Thou willest, but since Thou didst nurture me aforetime with sweet words, my heart is grieved by what I now hear from the calumniators—those about whom people say what they say. I praise Thee and thank Thee that to this day no one has overcome me through truth, but through falsehood beyond what Thy Book can enumerate and Thy knowledge encompass.
Thou knowest that to him who claimed the station of Kazim (peace be upon him), I initiated the Book that he might be reminded or fear. I wrote to him certain verses, and he was unable to reply to me with the like of my writing, for it is a proof against all. Had he been able, he would have sent it by now. Thereafter he transgressed in ways Thou knowest better than I. And as for him who took a book wrongfully—Thou knowest, O my God, that I asked of them a single utterance like unto my verses, but they were unable to produce it. Had they been able, I have no doubt they would have sent it. Thereafter they committed sins against Thee and worshipped Satan unawares. People imagine that producing an utterance like unto the verses is an easy matter, but nay! Thou knowest, O my God, that this was made Thy proof in the Qur’an, and Muhammad Thy Messenger (Thy blessings be upon him and his family) used it as an argument against the people, and it is a proof from Thee until the Day of Resurrection.
Thou dost witness, O my God, that after these mighty signs and supreme proofs, I have made no claim before Thee save what Thou hast established through truth. Dost Thou not know that if I had made a false claim, Thy glory would not have been content except to destroy me instantly or invalidate my proof by causing someone to produce the like of my Book—which I revealed in fourteen thousand verses, each one of which suffices for all who are in the heavens and on earth? I am certain in my love for Thee and Thy love for me that hadst Thou wished to invalidate this Cause, Thou wouldst have inspired one of Thy creatures to recite verses like mine, thereby nullifying my proof, and I would have remained silent. But now, knowing Thy good-pleasure, I commune with Thee: How hast Thou honored me, O my God, with this supreme proof, yet Thou dost not send down another sign to reassure the hearts of the fearful and oppressed? And how is it that the servant whom Thou hast raised to the station of greatness does not manifest all the qualities of that station, lest anyone be able to attribute any inadequacy to him?
Glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou, O my God! I am assured that naught can frustrate Thy power. Perchance Thou hast willed thereby to try all mankind; for wert Thou to vouchsafe unto me a proof like unto the rod of Moses, not a soul would depart from Thy decree. But now Thou hast honored me with that which is greater, and those in whose hearts is perversity turn away from Thy path.
Perchance Thou didst desire to make manifest on the Day of Resurrection, among Thy near ones from among Thy servants, when Thou permittest their signs to appear before Thee, so that Thy Living Proof might glory in the Book of His servant before all people.
And perchance Thou didst desire to elevate my station through trials, as hath been Thy practice with those near ones who came before. And if Thou hadst honored me with a physical sign by which all hearts would be subdued, I would not have experienced sorrow in Thy path, and thereby would not have attained the stations Thou hast promised to the patient ones. And as the life of this world passeth away, He hath chosen for me the eternal life and its stations, wherefore the people’s causing me grief in Thy days grieveth me not.

title: BB00059
section: Part 2: “And perchance through these verses Thou didst desire…”
text:
Part 2: “And perchance through these verses Thou didst desire…”
And perchance through these verses Thou didst desire to establish the authority of the Qur’an among all, that those who doubt the right of the Imams of justice might believe.
And perchance through these verses Thou didst desire to nullify the deeds of the people of the towns and those around them from among the Arabs who believe in Muhammad, Thy Messenger, peace be upon him and his family, and in his Book, yet who deny the names of the Imams of justice and their traditions, and to test them that they might either believe as do the believers or deny Thy favors.
And verily, if Thou hadst manifested other than these verses, they would not have believed, even as they believed not before in the miracles of the Imams of justice. But today they have no escape when they read the Book of Justice except to believe in it or to deny the Qur’an that came before, for there is not in it a single letter without connection, nor contrary to the rules of the people, and through it God nullifieth the deeds of all the idolaters.
And perchance I am not worthy that Thou shouldst honor me with another sign, but far be it to harbor such thoughts about Thee, for Thou hast honored me with the most mighty of all Thy signs, and he who is worthy of such a great bounty is worthy of all Thy manifestations and signs.
And verily, O my God, Thou hast not established with Thee any sign of justice other than this proof, and physical signs have no station with Thee, for therein both those near ones and the transgressors participate. But in Thy Word none can fabricate, for from the first day of Adam all have fabricated concerning all signs, yet none among the fabricators hath produced a book from Thee that would render all on earth unable to produce its like.
Glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou! Far be it from me to harbor thoughts of any deficiency in Thee. Rather, Thou hast made the Proof a sign that transcendeth every sign, from which none can escape. And verily, if Thou shouldst open unto me the gate of knowledge of the unseen or control over things, all would harbor doubts about Thee and would confuse the deeds of the fabricators with those of the near ones, and none among the possessors of understanding would be able to attain certainty of Thy truth, for such manifestations appear among the Christians and the idolatrous peoples.
But with this station none hath come save Muhammad, the Messenger of God. Nay, by Thy might, none can say aught concerning Thy proof, for those who say there is no connection between the verses and that they were revealed contrary to the rules of the people might look to the Commentary on the Surih of Joseph. Yea, verily they know not how to write the forms of that which hath been revealed, and thereby do all differ concerning it, and I have changed it. But concerning the Book of Justice, none can say aught about it save a contentious fabricator and liar.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! How perfect is Thy proof, how great is Thy favor, how mighty are Thy blessings, and how exalted art Thou! By Thy might, if anyone should read the Book of Justice and not believe in the Book of Thy servant, he is more astray than any beast before Me, and I am ashamed to call him bestial, for even beasts remember their Lord, while he who denies perceives nothing.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I know not Thy purpose regarding me, nor the manifestation of Thy signs within my soul, but I know that Thou didst desire to demonstrate to all that today there is a Hidden Proof for mankind, and none among those idolatrous peoples can deny it, for He Who brought these mighty signs was His servant and friend. All believe in Him while unseen and await His days, and support His servant that he might cause the religion of God’s Messenger—peace be upon him and his family—to triumph over all and nullify the deeds of the transgressors.
By Thy might and majesty, if people knew what their support of Thy Faith entailed, none would turn away but would aid Thy Cause until all religion belonged to Thee alone, without partner.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I thought in that station that Thou hadst manifested nothing from me save that Proof and those signs of love, lest anyone say this is the work of Satan or grieve me with evil words.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I complain of my sorrow to Thee that if this Cause should abrogate any decree without the authority of the Qur’an and Traditions, its Bearer must produce a proof. But now I make myself like any of the divines who look to the traditions and convey all ordinances to the people. The difference between me and them is that they acquire their knowledge from men and are licensed by some scholars to issue rulings, while I have studied under none—rather God was my teacher and His verses and communes my license. This is indeed possible, as God revealed in the Qur’an before: “Fear God,” and I did fear God my Lord, and thereby did God teach me all things.
Can one who stands upon a clear proof from Thee be like one who has no proof save the desires of the transgressors? I take refuge in Thee, O my God! Thou knowest that though they issue Thy rulings by permission of certain scholars and their license, most of the Muslim divines and accomplished mujtahids whom none would deny except those who wish to disbelieve in Thee have followed me.
I complain to Thee, O my God, that had the divines not turned away from my judgment, none would have been wronged. And now the sin of all rests upon them though they perceive it not. Thou knowest the divines imagine this Cause is like that of Ahmad before Kazim—peace be upon them—and therefore they follow me not and think wrongly of me. Far be it that I should think thus of that Cause! This is a Cause that breaks the back of all and nullifies the deeds of all who turn away. It has a proof like unto the pillar of prophethood—were all to gather to nullify the Truth they would fail. Indeed, those who look to the word of reality know that all the proofs of the three pillars are manifested in this Cause—nay, in but one verse from its Bearer’s verses.
Glory be unto Thee! How mighty is Thy proof in my hands, how great Thy power within my soul, how sweet Thy remembrance in my heart, how lofty Thy strength in my being! Through myself alone hast Thou manifested my Cause and sent messengers bearing glad tidings and warnings according to the ordinances of the Qur’an without changing a letter, and Thou hast brought low the station of the oppressors until the Day of Resurrection, with an irrefutable proof that none among Thy creation can escape, and I have endured all manner of tribulation with contentment and patience, fearing none in the path that leads to Thy presence.
I know not, O my God, whether I am beguiled by Thy proof or whether all men are as dead ones who perceive not that one among the Jews believed in Musa ibn Ja’far, Thy proof, when he witnessed his patience. All people know my station and observe my patience, yet they perceive not and find no way unto Thee.
By Thy might! My breast is constricted by that which, were it to settle upon the Throne, would cause it to quake; were it to rest upon the Chair, would cause it to break; were it to descend upon the heaven, would cause it to split asunder; were it to fall upon the earth, would cause it to cleave in twain; were it to touch the mountains, would cause them to crumble; were it to be recited upon the sea, would cause it to surge; were it to be inscribed upon the Tablet, would cause it to darken; were it to be mentioned by the Pen, would cause it to split; were it to draw nigh unto fire, would cause it to be extinguished; were it to be raised unto the trees, would cause them to wither and their branches to become as dry wood; were it to be read unto hearts, would cause them to tremble and fall down; were it to be mentioned unto minds, would cause them to be seized with fear; were it to be recited unto souls, would cause them to be humbled; were it to appear unto bodies, would cause them to shudder; were it to be recorded by pens, verily eyes would overflow with tears.
O my God! Is there anyone encompassed by Thy knowledge who, upon reading this my epistle, would cry out as do those who cherish hope? Is there anyone who would enumerate Thy Book who, upon hearing this prayer, would weep for me as do those who are drowned? Is there anyone among Thy servants upon whom that Book would descend who would feel his skin crawl, who would arise to aid me and guard his tongue lest he stir up sedition around me, and who would exalt the religion of God as do these transgressors? Is there anyone among Thy creation who, upon writing these intimate prayers, would be moved in his heart and would beseech God by the sanctity of the Imams of justice for my deliverance?
O my God! Thou knowest my station and my solitude, and here am I, before Thee, calling upon Thy believing servants—those who are alive and those who shall yet live by Thy leave—to help Thy religion and not destroy themselves, to have mercy upon my soul and not draw near to sedition, nor assist in sin and transgression. If they can follow God’s decree, let them believe; if not, let them remain silent until God makes His signs manifest and guides them aright.
O God! I beseech Thee by the right of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad to bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and to have mercy upon the weak souls whom Satan touches every moment, with all Thy mercy and Thy signs. Guard them from the evil of the wicked among the jinn and men, and deposit in their hearts and in all my verses and prayers that Name of Thine which Thou didst entrust to Azrael, peace be upon him, whereby souls are forcefully affected. Verily, Thou art the Bestower, the All-Praised.
O God! Let them read that blessed verse from the sacred Tree, that their souls may be preserved from the evil of the transgressors. Lord! I ask of Thee a spiritual, radiant, brilliant, and everlasting support that would strengthen my essential and accidental powers, then my angelic and animal powers, then my universal and particular powers, until thereby I and my servants might overcome every overwhelming soul, such that the sign of their subtle essences would contract with such force as to cause their powers to fall, leaving no living thing in existence but that the fire of my conquest would consume its back. O Powerful One! O Mighty One! O Severe One! O Thou Who art possessed of overwhelming strength and kingly power! O Subduer, O All-Subduing! I beseech Thee by that which Thou hast entrusted to ʿIzra’il of Thy subduing Names—whereby souls are overpowered beneath his sway—that Thou wilt, at this very hour, deposit within me this secret, that through it I may render every hardness pliant and humble every stubborn resister, through Thy might, O Thou Possessor of Strength, the All-Strong, and through Thy power, O Thou Who holdest sway over both dominions.
Verily Thou art God, the Lord of the worlds. There is no strength nor power except through Thee. Thou art God, my Protector, Who hath ever been and will ever be. Verily Thou art my Protector and Thou art the Ever-Abiding. In Thee have I placed my trust, and in Thy protection have I taken refuge. Through Thy will have I sought assistance, to Thy glory have I held fast, and upon Thee have I relied. I say: whatsoever God willeth shall come to pass. There is no strength nor power except through God, the Most High, the Most Great. Glory be to Thee, Lord of Might, above what they describe. And praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds.

title: BB00296
text:
In the Name of God, the All-Illumined, the All-Originating, the Transcendent, the All-Glorious.
Unto God belongeth the splendor of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a splendour tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the radiance of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a radiance tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the exaltation of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with an exaltation tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the effulgence of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with an effulgence tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the bounty of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a bounty tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the beauty of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a beauty and a majesty tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the majesty of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a majesty and a beauty tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the effectual working of Truth in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a working tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the unassailable might of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a might, exalted, tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the liberal bestowal of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a bounty, exalted, tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the whole of mercy, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been endowed with a mercy tremendous.
Unto God belongeth honour in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with an honour tremendous.
Unto God belongeth all might in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a might tremendous.
Unto God belongeth all power, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been endowed with a power tremendous.
Unto God belongeth all sovereignty, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been endowed with a sovereignty tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the Exposition of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with an exposition tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the good-pleasure (ridwan) of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a good-pleasure tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the forgiveness of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a forgiveness tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the Criterion (furqan) of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a criterion tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the Qur’an of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a Recitation tremendous.
Unto God belong the signs of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with signs tremendous.
Unto God belong the words of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with words tremendous.
Unto God belong the manifestations of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a manifestation tremendous.
Unto God belong the modes and dispositions of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a mode tremendous.
Unto God belong the tokens and evidences of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with evidences tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the ruby treasure of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a ruby treasure tremendous.
Unto God belong the inmost essences and jewels of the entire Cause, in the Kingdom of command and creation, for every soul according to what it can bear; and God hath ever been endowed with a sovereignty tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the realm of Divinity (lahut) of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a Divinity tremendous. Unto God belongeth the realm of Might (jabarut) of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a Might tremendous. Unto God belongeth the Kingdom (malakut) of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been endowed with a Kingdom tremendous.
In the Name of God, the All-Glorious, the All-Transcending, the All-Majestic, the All-Near.
Unto God appertaineth the whole of the Cause, in the beginning and in the end. He createth whatsoever He willeth through His command, “Be”, and it is. He it is Who hath created you according to that which hath been sent down in the Book from His presence, and He, verily, is all-knowing, all-wise.
Unto God prostrateth himself whosoever is in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever encompassed all things. Unto God belong the East and the West and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever encompassed all things. Unto God belong the lines and courses of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been possessed of a comely, beauteous tracing. Unto God belongeth the splendour of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been possessed of splendour and radiance. Unto God belongeth the majesty of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, majestic, majestic. Unto God belongeth the beauty of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, beautiful, beautiful. Unto God belongeth all greatness in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been possessed of greatness and exalted might tremendous.
Unto God appertaineth the whole of the Cause, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been one God, single, alone, peerless, living, self-subsisting, everlasting, all-holy, all-sanctified, One to be feared, One well-beloved, the Goal of all, the Object of all desire, the Praised, the Thanked, the Worshipped, the Seen, the Remembered, the Known.
His is the creation and the command, in the beginning and in the end, and unto Him shall all return.
Say: All are unto Him devoutly obedient. Say: All are unto Him worshippers. Say: All are unto Him prostrate. Say: All are unto Him patient and steadfast. Say: All are unto Him humble and submissive.
Say: Verily, in God I am, over you, a reckoner and a witness. Say: Verily, in God I am, over you, a guardian and a protector. Say: Verily, in God I am, over you, a watcher, potent. Say: Verily, in God I am, over you, mighty, all-glorious. Say: Verily, in God I am, over you, a subduer, manifest. Say: Verily, in God I am, over you, one standing, standing (ever-watchful, unsleeping). Say: Verily, in God I am, over you, exalted, impregnable.
Say: I have put my whole trust in God, my Lord, in the beginning and in the end, and sufficient is God as a Guardian.
Say: I have put my whole trust in God, the Living One, Who createth whatsoever He willeth through His command, “Be”, and it is.
And say: Praise be to God, before Whom prostrate themselves whosoever are in the heavens and whosoever are on the earth and whatsoever lieth between them. Then glorify Him, and hallow Him, and magnify Him, and exalt Him with a mighty exaltation.
Unto God belongeth the realm of Divinity (lahut) of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in truth, powerful, powerful. Unto God belongeth the realm of Might (jabarut) of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in truth, majestic, majestic. Unto God belongeth the Kingdom (malakut) of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in truth, radiant, radiant. Unto God belongeth the ruby treasure of God in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in truth, tremendous, tremendous. Unto God belongeth the realm of the visible world (nasut) of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in truth, beautiful, beautiful.
Say: Verily, I shall assuredly draw all things unto Myself through God, for God, the Lord of all the worlds. Say: Verily, I shall assuredly make all things subservient through God, for God, the Lord of all the worlds. Say: Verily, I shall assuredly gain dominion over all things through God, for God, the Lord of all the worlds. Say: Verily, I shall assuredly prevail over all things through God, for God, the Lord of all the worlds. Say: Verily, I shall assuredly lay hold of all things through God, for God, the Lord of all the worlds. Say: Verily, I shall assuredly seek to guide all things aright through God, for God, the Lord of all the worlds.
Say: Verily, I shall assuredly seek victory, through God, over all things, at every time, before time and after time.

title: BB00310
text:
In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
In the name of God, the Most Inaccessible, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O Lord! Verily, Thou art the Creator of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, the Knower of the unseen and the visible. Not a thing escapeth Thy knowledge, whether in the heavens or on earth or whatsoever lieth between them, and nothing can frustrate Thee in the kingdom of Command or Creation or in aught else besides these. Thou hast distinguished Thyself above all things, and through Thy loftiness Thou hast transcended the elevation of all things, and through Thy grandeur Thou hast risen above the exaltation of all things.
Thou art the Ever-Existing through the reality of Thine essence, and Thou art the Creator of all things through Thine eternal being, and Thou art the One Who remaineth after all things through Thy pristine essence. None of Thy servants shall ever know Thee, nor shall any dweller of Thy earth and heaven describe Thee as befitteth the sublimity of Thy glory and the exaltation of Thy sovereignty. Thou hast ever been one God, single, unique, ever-living, self-subsisting, eternal, everlasting. Thou dost send down in every condition from Thy presence upon the heaven of Thy might, and Thou dost favor the people of Thy kingdom with the wondrous holy gifts of Thy sovereign grace, as Thou willest, through the signs of Thy creative Lordship.
Therefore, O my God, I beseech Thee to send Thy blessings upon Muhammad and the Manifestations of His countenance, such as Thou hast ordained in the Book through the names of Thy Lordship, and to shower upon the Tree of Thy love the wondrous effects of Thy holy grace as befitteth the loftiness and exaltation of Thy bestowing holiness in the kingdom of glory and majesty. For verily Thou, O my God, hast ever known every soul’s position of recognition of Thee in its journey and abode, and Thou dost send down upon whomsoever Thou willest the wondrous expressions of Thy favors in their journey and dwelling place.
Thou art He Who hath created this creation for naught else save to worship Thee, to glorify Thee, to sanctify Thee, and to follow that which hath been sent down from Thee from the places of Thy holy eternity and the wonders of Thy glorious oneness. How then can I thank Thee, O Lord my God, when my thanksgiving to Thee merits yet further thanks? And how can I praise Thee, O my Lord, when my praise of Thee necessitates yet further praise as befitteth the sublimity of Thy holy majesty and the exaltation of Thy glorious might?
Thou art He before Whom prostrate all who are in the kingdoms of Thy earth and Thy heaven, yet all this, O my God, is only to the measure of what Thou hast created in the realm of creation, not according to what Thy Self deserveth. Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thou givest life and causeth death, then causeth death and givest life, and verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not. In Thy grasp is the kingdom of all things. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
There is no glory save in believing in Thee and following the ways of Thy good-pleasure, and there is nothing for those who do not arise for the stations of Thy Cause regarding Thy trusted ones. Therefore, O God, inspire all Thy servants with the path of Thy good-pleasure, and cause all Thy servants, O Lord, to know the wondrous signs of Thy creation. Send down, O God, upon all who have believed in Thee and Thy signs, every good thing which Thy knowledge hath encompassed and which Thou hast sent down in the Tablet. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
That which descendeth from Thee unto all things hath ever been in equal measure, for Thy independence from all things—to this all do testify—and the dependence of all things in their essence upon Thee—this all do affirm. Therefore I beseech Thee, O Lord my God, at this moment to sever every soul from that which veils it from Thee in Thy presence, and to grant every soul that which draweth it nigh unto Thee, and to send down upon him who hath turned to Thee that which is best for him in his return and his resting place. Guard him in the pathways of Thy love from that which Thou wouldst not wish to befall Thy loved ones, and cause him to return unto him from whom he departed with Thy leave, in accordance with what Thou dost desire.
And if Thou hast ordained for him, O my God, to present himself before one who seeketh to discover the features of that station, let him not utter that which would sadden any soul, but rather speak that which would bring tranquility to every soul, for this is what hath been sent down in the Book and what Thou hast commanded in the verses to all Thy servants. Through Thy grace and mercy, O Lord, do Thou calm all the hearts of Thy loved ones in such wise as to gladden their hearts, their spirits, their souls and their bodies, through Thy bounty and favor, then through Thy grace and generosity. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things. Thy mercy hath preceded Thy believing servants, therefore cause all Thy believing servants, O Lord, to enter into the depths of the ocean of Thy love.

title: BB00653
text:
Praise be unto God, Who hath borne witness unto His own Self, through His own Self, that verily He is God, there is none other God but Him, alone and peerless, without associate. From everlasting Thou wast, with none beside Thee, and unto everlasting Thou shalt remain, abiding as Thou hast ever been. No thing hath ever been, in any condition or degree, that could attain unto Thy station; for Thy very Essence is the eternal Essence, whose Being hath, by its very subsistence, severed material realities from the realm of true recognition; and Thy Being is the ancient Being, whose foundation hath, by its own ordinance, sundered essential realities from the domain of utterance. Glory be unto Thee, O my God! When I say, “Thou art Thou,” Thou dost confute me, in that very moment, by Thine own Self; and when I behold all created things, they proclaim that God is exalted above being described by His creation or characterized by His servants. And when I fall silent before the Court of the holiness of Thy Self-Subsisting Oneness, my inmost soul rebuketh me, saying: God hath not created aught in vain or in idle sport. Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I behold no path, nor do I find in remembrance any guiding proof.
Thou, O my Lord, art my secret and my open being, and Thou bearest witness to that which my hands have wrought before the Court of the abyss of Thy Selfhood. Should I say, “Blessed am I,” Thy justice and Thy decree would be my deliverance; and should I say, “Woe unto me,” Thy dealing with the erring among Thy servants would encompass me. By Thy might and Thy majesty, O Thou Who art God and none else beside Thee, I know full well that Thou art nearer unto me than all things, and more merciful and more bountiful toward me than every possessor of bounty; for Thou didst create me when I was not even mentioned, and didst nurture me through Thy grace after Thou hadst chosen—yea, chosen—deeds that are praiseworthy. Ever hath beneficence been Thy wont, and munificence Thy way. If Thou chastisest me, it is but through Thy mercy toward Thy righteous servants; and if Thou bestowest, it is through Thy generosity and Thy care, without any cause on my part.
Unto Thee be praise, O my God, for the right of Thine eternal Being, in all that hath befallen me at Thy hands—praise radiant, resplendent, sanctified, exalted above the bounds of all besides Thee, standing alone beyond the praise of Thy servants and beyond all that can enter the loftiest reaches of their thought; praise that surpasseth all things through Thy grace and bounty, and perfecteth Thy favors unto me in this world and in the world to come, by the fullness of Thy bestowal.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Thou knowest my station in that land, and Thou bearest witness to that which Thou didst will for me in the presence of Thy all-embracing mercy.
And now, behold me bearing witness unto Thine own Self that Thou art God, there is none other God but Thee, the Mighty, the All-Bountiful; and I bear witness unto Muhammad, Thy Beloved—may the blessings of God be upon Him and upon His kindred—to that which Thou didst ordain for Him in Thy hidden knowledge, such as none among Thy creatures can encompass. Verily Thou art the Mighty, the Bestower. And I bear witness unto the successors of Muhammad, Thy Beloved—upon them be Thy blessings—to that which Thou didst reveal concerning them, when Thou didst say—and Thy word is the truth—“Honored servants; they speak not till He hath spoken, and they act by His command.” I bear witness unto every truth, O my God, to that whereunto Thou Thyself hast borne witness; and unto every falsehood, to that which Thou desirest Thy creation to witness concerning it. Thou knowest all things, and nothing escapeth Thy knowledge, neither in the heavens nor on the earth. Verily Thou art the Mighty, the Wise.
O my God! Exalted is Thy bounty above afflicting Thy servants in this earthly life without raising them to higher degrees in the life to come. Thou knowest full well that when Thou dost take unto Thyself the souls of certain of Thy servants, the hearts of some among Thy creatures are saddened. Send down, then, upon such a one the word of patience and resignation to Thy decree; and send down upon those whom Thou hast taken unto Thyself, in the sacred land, the word of mercy and those wondrous breaths and ever-new bounties which none can fathom save Thyself, through Thy grace and Thy generosity, O Lord of lords. Thou art the Protector of the faithful and the Successor of the godly; perfect, then, Thy favor upon us, pour forth Thy blessings upon us, and admit us among the righteous of Thy loved ones.
For Thou art independent of the rule of all things, and nothing in the heavens or on the earth can magnify itself before Thee. Verily Thou art the Powerful, the Mighty.
O God! If the heart of any of Thy servants hath been saddened by the taking unto Thee of one near unto him, I beseech Thee, by Thy grace, to cause Thy mercy to descend upon that soul in every condition, and to still the heart of the bereaved through Thy promise and Thy good-pleasure. For souls find no peace in any state save in meeting Thee, nor do we attain unto the utmost limit of contentment except through Thy loving favor. Fulfill, O God, that which Thou hast promised unto the believers among those who have answered Thy call; forgive me, and my parents, and all who have followed Thy command, feared Thy justice, and found assurance in Thy grace.
Verily Thou art God, the Generous, the All-Bountiful, the Single, the One, from Whose knowledge nothing in the heavens or on the earth can ever be hidden, and over all things Thou art powerful.
Glory be unto God, the Lord of the Throne, exalted above all that they ascribe unto Him; and peace be upon the Messengers; and praise be unto God, the Lord of all the worlds.

title: BB00323
text:
Praise be to God Who hath created the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them in truth; and His command is nearer than that He should say unto it, “Be”, and it is.
Unto God belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them. Say: All shall return unto Him.
Unto God belongeth the splendour of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, all-glorious, all-glorious.
Unto God belongeth the radiance of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, all-illuminating, all-illuminating.
Unto God belongeth the effulgence of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, all-luminous, all-luminous.
Unto God belongeth the majesty of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, majestic, majestic.
Unto God belongeth the beauty of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, beautiful, beautiful.
Unto God belongeth all greatness in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, most great, most great.
Unto God belongeth all glory and loftiness in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, all-great, all-great.
Unto God belongeth all might in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, mighty, mighty.
Unto God belongeth all power in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, powerful, powerful.
Unto God belongeth all wisdom in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, wise, wise.
And unto God it pertaineth that, in every domain and in each house, there be of times and seasons a place wherein the verses of God are inscribed, that men may dwell therein and that mercy may be shown unto the people, that haply God may exalt the station of him (who thus serveth); for He hath ever been forbearing, all-forbearing.
Unto God belongeth the knowledge of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, all-knowing, all-knowing.
Unto God belongeth the judgement of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, One Whose judgement is nigh at hand.
Unto God belongeth the light of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, the Possessor of a light all-luminous.
Unto God belongeth all power in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, all-powerful, all-powerful.
Unto God belongeth the word of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, the Possessor of a word acceptable and well-pleasing.
Unto God belong the entreaties and supplications of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, the Well-Beloved, the Well-Beloved.
Unto God belongeth the honour of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, the Possessor of an honour tremendous.
Unto God belongeth all sovereignty in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, a Sovereign, Most Great.
Unto God belongeth the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, the Possessor of a dominion tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the Kingdom (malakút) of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, a King, Most Bountiful.
Unto God belongeth the exaltation of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, the Most High, the Most High.
Unto God belong the signs of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, manifest, all-glorious.
Unto God belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, a Keeper, a Keeper.
Unto God belongeth all mercy in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, merciful, merciful.
Unto God belongeth all forgiveness in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, all-forgiving, all-bountiful.
Unto God belong the wondrous realities of the entire Cause, in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, the Possessor of a Cause all-glorious.

title: BB00361
text:
He is the Most Great, the Most Ancient, the Most Generous
God testifieth that there is none other God but Him. His is the Kingdom and the Dominion, then the Might and the Omnipotence, then the Power and the Divine Realm, then the Strength and the Ruby, then the Sovereignty and the Human Kingdom. He causeth to live and to die, then causeth to die and to live. Verily He is the Ever-Living Who dieth not, and the King Who passeth not away, and the Just Who oppresseth not, and the Sovereign Who changeth not, and the Single One from Whose grasp nothing escapeth, whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them. He createth what He willeth by His command. He is, verily, powerful over all things.
To continue: O Sayyah of Truth—upon thee be the Kingdom Absolute—and upon whomsoever He hath sheltered within His precinct through His word of truth, “As is meet, seek thou after Me.” He hath spoken in thy regard that He hath entered thy precinct, forasmuch as thou didst abide in His service. That which I inscribed at the head of My Book—by a secret for this measure and no more—hath descended for all the God-fearing. Thy letter hath come down; I have discerned thy purpose and laid it before thy Lord and Mine—the Lord of all the worlds. God hath sent down unto thee clear verses wherein abideth every bounty existent. Recite them, and recite what therein was revealed for the Name of God, the August—ninety-two—in the Land of Ba’; bear witness thereto, and be among the thankful.
Then—by thy Lord’s right—whensoever thou enterest the Most Exalted Paradise and the Most Glorious Garden, magnify, with My tongue, in that supremely lofty court: “O my God, let Thy Lordship flow upon my tongue!” Look thou not save upon the frames of those intended ones and the decayed bones, for they received upon their lines the Names of God made manifest in those hallowed temples, inasmuch as from God, their Lord, they arose—openly, visibly—and unveiled their Lord, fearing not the reproach of any reproacher in the paths of their Creator. Grieve thou not for their outward thrones: such were but accidents of the arena. Yet the matter that hath withered remaineth in those proofs until the Day when God shall appear in the world of the Cloud once again.
Magnify, then, over them—and increase thy praise—at every time, before time, and after time; for they, verily, are the first and the most ancient; they, verily, are the victors and the triumphant; they, verily, are the living—nourished with their Lord by whatsoever they desire. I have dispatched two Leaves from the Leaves of Fa’—may my spirit be a ransom unto him—and one Leaf remaineth; even now have I sent it to thy presence, for I was commanded to do so, and summoned thereto in my supplication. Magnify, then, over it—at every time, before time, and after time; and magnify over the Name of God, the Most High, the Most Exalted; depart not therefrom save by His leave. And praise be to God, the Lord of all the worlds.
The constraint is exceeding great—marvellous indeed! O King, O Bearer of Glad-Tidings: he is the most safeguarded, the most ennobled, in his perusal of the Sayyah of Truth; and the friend of the Friend of God, unbounded—he is the Most Exalted, the Most Exalted! A beloved beyond every love be upon thee from thy Lord—the inmost heart, the solace of their eyes—upon him be every protection! He hath set out, at the command of the Presence of the Beloved—exalted be His love, magnified His affection—hoping that a meeting may come to pass. Deliver Duldul unto them, for it is beloved of the Presence of the Beloved.
Say: He—verily—is God; there is no God but He, the Mighty, the Well-Beloved. Hasten thou unto Us, if there be a wondrous matter which the believers await. I have, before this, sent unto thee a Book, together with what God hath sent down upon thee. Take fast hold thereof, and be among the thankful. And praise be to God, the Lord of all the worlds.

title: BB00429
text:
Say: God is my Lord. He createth what He willeth by His command, “Be”, and it is.
Unto Him belongeth the wondrous origination of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and He is the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, the Exalted.
He it is Who hath created the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them by His command; verily, He is the Strong, the All-Powerful.
His is the creation and the command, in the beginning and in the end; and He is the Creator, the Inaccessible.
Verily, all prostrate themselves before Him. Verily, all worship Him. Verily, all are unto Him devoutly obedient. Verily, all labour in His path. Verily, all fall down in adoration before Him. Verily, all are before Him humble and submissive.
Unto God belongeth the whole of mercy in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and then, beyond them, in all the worlds; such is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them—the Lord of all worlds.
Unto God belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been powerful over all things.
Such is the Ordainer and Originator of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been, of all things, all-knowing.
Unto God belong the oceans of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been the Sustainer of all things.
Unto God belongeth the realm of might (jabarut) of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been the Sustainer of all things.
Unto God appertain the fourfold seals of the Lord—say: of them shall all be questioned.
Unto God belong the keys of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been All-Bounteous, All-Knowing.
Unto God belong the treasuries and clasps (maqalid) of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been, over all things, a Guardian.
Unto God belong the measures of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been, of all things, fully aware.
Unto God belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been mighty, all-wise.
Unto God belongeth the splendour of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, all-glorious, all-glorious.
Unto God belongeth the majesty of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, beautiful, beautiful.
Unto God belongeth all greatness in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, most great, most great.
Unto God belongeth the light of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, all-luminous, all-luminous.
Unto God belongeth the whole of mercy in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, merciful, merciful.
Unto God belongeth the radiance of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, all-illuminating, all-illuminating.
Unto God belong the Most Excellent Names in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, the Possessor of a Name most glorious.
Unto God belong the loftiest similitudes in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and He is the Possessor of an Exalted Similitude.
Unto God belongeth all might and honour in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, mighty, mighty.
Unto God appertaineth the whole of the Cause, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a Cause tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the knowledge of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been, of all things, all-knowing.
Unto God belongeth the whole of power in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, all-powerful, all-powerful.
Unto God belongeth the utterance of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is, in very truth, well-pleased, well-pleased.
Unto God belong the entreaties and the honour, in the beginning and in the end, and God is, in very truth, the Well-Beloved, the All-Glorious.
Unto God belongeth sovereignty and exaltation, in the beginning and in the end, and God is, in very truth, an Ancient Sovereign.
Unto God belongeth dominion and bounty, in the beginning and in the end, and God is, in very truth, the Munificent, the Most Generous.

title: BB00456
text:
He is the Truth! There is no God but Him and all bow down before Him.
O Name of God, the Most Generous! Upon thee be the Glory of God, the Ancient King. After greetings, 9 parts have been sent with Al-Azim, 4. Let the haykals be written from these or in the manner of the connected haykal, for it has the strongest effect therein. You desire not what has already been revealed to you before, for it is indeed an ancient and true Book. And glorify all the people of guidance together.
And verily what ought to be manifested is that which is manifest above all things, and hidden beneath all things, and first before all things, and last on the right of all things, and dominant on the left of all things, according to what is in the traditions concerning the age of thirty. And verily from the first descent of the water of His being until the time He spoke the number of Ta and Kaf, and We have not made thee aware of it, and from an ancient living soul the letter of peace, and it has been fulfilled according to what the pure Family of God have informed after peace, the cycle of fire. Let them speak to those who believed before all worlds and to those around him at the time when “He answers the distressed when they call upon Him.” So answer him who calls you from around the shrine, and be not content until a thousand after peace is completed. That is to be calculated from the first water of His being, and if calculated from the first manifestation of His body, subtract nine months and nine days.
So watch for what the witnesses of God have informed you beforehand, for when the month of Mim first rises, peace will be completed in the matter of calculation that you outwardly reckon, while inwardly it has been fulfilled, and in the inmost inward it has been fulfilled around, then the number of the name Muhammad. So watch your days and be victorious through God, your Lord, for those in whose hearts is the power of exposition, these are they who have power over all things by God’s leave—He Who created all things by His command. Nothing in the heavens or on earth or between them can frustrate Him. Verily, He has power over all things.

title: BB00557
text:
He is the Almighty, the Ever-Abiding, the Most Exalted
From Shiraz my mother—may she be illumined—sendeth word: May my soul be a ransom for thee! From the hour of sunset, honored with the bounty of Presence, until now—which is the afternoon of Thursday, the twenty-eighth of the blessed month of Sha’ban—praise and thanksgiving be to God, all that God ordained for me hath passed in goodly wise.
At all times the sorrow that hath been is but the sorrow and longing for the Presence. And though I am far removed from attaining the honour of that Presence, yet, for divers reasons—inasmuch as my nearness would give rise to afflictions—I am well-pleased, for my own self, with whatsoever He willeth: resignation to the decree of God and submission to His command. Only, as to drawing nigh unto the Presence, let nothing occur that would become a cause of grief.
I render thanks. Be in no wise saddened; for the road is far and false reports are many. Let no perturbation arise, for—praise be to God—there is well-being in every state. In any case, let whatsoever is needful be appointed and obtained; and let the omissions from the effusions of the Presence be made good through remembrance—especially on behalf of the honoured grandmother—may God, exalted be He, protect her. At all times, should there be any instruction, let it be signified, that it may be obeyed.
In Yazd, kindly have regard to Sayyid 228.

title: BB00595
text: Say: O God! Thou art the Creator of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them. Thou givest innate nature unto whomsoever Thou willest and takest it away from whomsoever Thou willest. Thou exaltest whomsoever Thou willest and abasest whomsoever Thou willest. Thou raisest up whomsoever Thou willest and bringest low whomsoever Thou willest. Thou grantest victory unto whomsoever Thou willest and causest to fail whomsoever Thou willest. Thou enrichest whomsoever Thou willest and makest poor whomsoever Thou willest. Within Thy grasp is the kingdom of all things. Thou createst whatsoever Thou willest, how Thou willest, by what means Thou willest, and for what purpose Thou willest. Verily, Thou art powerful over whatsoever Thou willest, O Best of Protectors. In our own house, the sister of Aqa Mir-Siyyid.

title: BB00619
text:
He is God; glorified is the splendor of His light.
O thou who art the chosen one among women!
The verses in this Tablet are revealed for the one who hath believed in the signs of her Lord and is reckoned among such as are wholly devoted unto Him. Bear thou witness that verily no God is there but Him, Who is both my Lord and thine, and that no other God besides Him existeth. He is the Bountiful, the Almighty.
Yield thee thanks unto God, for He hath graciously aided thee in this Day, revealed for thee the clear verses of this Tablet, and hath numbered thee among such women as have believed in the signs of God, have taken Him as their guardian and are of the grateful. Verily God shall soon reward thee and those who have believed in His signs with an excellent reward from His presence. Assuredly no God is there other than Him, the All-Possessing, the Most Generous. The revelations of His bounty pervade all created things; He is the Merciful, the Compassionate.

title: BB00632
text: God, there is no God but Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting. Neither slumber nor sleep overtaketh Him. His is whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is on earth and whatsoever is between them.

title: BB00676: Inscription on the Bab’s signet ring
text: Glorified be God besides Whom there is no God, and verily this is a path from His presence upon which all must pass.

title: BB00635: Seal of the Bab
text: God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, the Mighty, the Best-Beloved.

title: BB00649: Seal of the Bab
text: Verily I am the Proof of God and His Light.

title: BB00622
text:
In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful.
He is God, the Most Great, the Most Exalted. God is Most Great. He is the Most Inaccessible, the Most Holy, the Most High.
Say, God is the Lord and all are worshippers unto Him. Say, God is the True One and all pay homage unto Him. This is God, your Lord, and unto Him shall ye return. Is there any doubt concerning God? He hath created you and all things. The Lord of all worlds is He.

title: BB00626
text: O Name of Nobility and Exaltedness! Convey My greetings unto those in the House of Truth and be watchful over their affairs, lest grief be witnessed by any one among those possessed of My love. And make mention, in the Book of thy Lord, of all the believing men and believing women.

title: BB00674
text: Write thou the first verse on the Day of Thursday upon green silk, together with ten exalted invocations, and keep it with thee. Then write thou the second verse on the Day of Tuesday, and wash it with water, and drink it, for love of Him. Verily God—were He to will—would, through this, grant thee thine asking. He is, in truth, the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.

title: BB00675
text:
Upon the Best of all His creatures next I called—Muḥammad—He Who swept misguidance far away;
By Light of hallowed Majesty and grace, the shadows fled, and darkness passed away.

title: BB00294
text:
In the Name of God, the Most Great, the Most Great
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I testify, and all things testify, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone, with no partner. Thine is the kingdom and the heavenly dominion, Thine the might and the divine power, Thine the strength and sovereignty, Thine the force and grandeur, Thine the dominion and the realm of man, Thine the glory and majesty, Thine the countenance and beauty, Thine the direction and perfection, Thine the likeness and similitudes, Thine the stations and reverence, Thine the greatness and independence, Thine the grandeur and exaltation, Thine the glory and invincibility, Thine the power and ascendancy, Thine the joy and gladness, Thine the sovereignty and might, and Thine is whatsoever Thou hast loved or wilt love in the kingdom of Thy Cause and creation.
Thou hast ever been one God, single, eternal, self-subsisting, living, enduring, sovereign, all-pervading, holy, everlasting, forever, inaccessible, possessing, ruling, manifest, powerful. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast no partner in what Thou hast created, nor any helper in what Thou hast fashioned. Thou hast created the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them through Thy wisdom, and hast perfected the creation of all things through Thy Lordship.
Thou art the First, O my God, before all things, and there was nothing before Thee. Thou art the Last, O my God, after all things, and there shall be nothing after Thee. Thou art the Manifest, O my Beloved, above all things, and there is nothing above Thee. Thou art the Hidden, O my Desired One, beneath all things, and there is nothing beneath Thee.
Sanctified are all Thy names and exalted are all Thy examples. Thou hast ever been sanctified beyond all names and wilt ever be pure from all similitudes. How near art Thou to Thy loved ones and how gracious unto Thy beloved ones!
I beseech Thee by Thy Most Beautiful Names—O Beauty, O Most Beautiful, O All-Beautiful, O Beauteous One, O Embellisher, O Adorner, O Gracious, O Most Gracious, O Most Lovely, O Hussein, O Most Excellent, O Beneficent, O Most Beneficent, O Source of Beauty, O Twin Beauty, O He Who Acquireth Beauty, O He Who Assumeth Beauty, O He Who Shareth Beauty, O He Who Approveth Beauty—that Thou wilt send Thy blessings upon the Primal Point and then upon Him Who lived in eternity, from the beginning that hath no beginning in every Manifestation unto the end that hath no end in every concealment.
I testify, and all things testify, that the Manifestation of Thy Beauty, from the beginning when Thou didst make Thyself known to all created things, hath known Thee through Thy causing him to know Thee, and hath shown patience in Thy path upon the summits of mountains, and hath wearied himself in seeking Thy good-pleasure upon the paths of love and acceptance. Therefore, O God, inspire him with all good from Thy presence, preserve him, O God, from aught else but good through Thy power, and assist him, O God, to convey Thy Books unto Thy creation and to preserve Thy words in Thy lands, that they may glory in knowing Thee among the creatures of the first and the last, and may praise Thee in the precincts of his love in Thy most glorious Paradise among those who praise Thee, and may laugh at those whom Thou hast caused to enter the fire for lack of knowledge of Thee.
For on the Day of Resurrection Thou hast promised to make all Thy creation know the guides of Thy Cause in the paradise of Thy love, and Thou hast distinguished between the creation of all things where Thy guides shall see […] From those who believe not in the Cause and who convey what they possess to every person of authority and fame, for Thy Book is Thy proof unto Thy creation. It descendeth not upon a believer but that it causeth him to speak forth Thy praise and thanksgiving, nor upon an unbeliever but that it consumeth him with the fire of Thy justice and equity.
O God! Do Thou guide all Thy creation through Thy bounty, and deliver them all, O Lord, from the fire of being deprived of Thy knowledge, and cause them all to enter, O God, the paradise of Thy love and good-pleasure. For Thou hast ever been independent of the glorification of all created things and the sanctification of all existing things, self-sufficient above the exaltation of all beings and the elevation of all atoms. All are poor before Thy praise and glory and sanctification and glorification. And all this becometh Thee through Thy grace, wherein Thou hast accepted from those whom Thou didst create from nothing Thy unity and Thy sanctification. Otherwise, how could that which appeareth from Thy creation be worthy of Thy eternal Countenance and Thy everlasting Face? Glory be unto Thee! Glory be unto Thee! Verily Thou art the Single One, the Sanctified, the Beloved, the Eternal, the Holy, the Dreaded, Who was before all things. That which Thou willest not shall never be, and there is no power nor strength except through Thee. Verily Thou art the Most High, the Most Great.

title: BB00468: Tawqi’ Khitab bih ahl-i-bait dar Shiraz
text:
He is the Most Glorious
God testifieth that there is no God but He, the Mighty, the Well-Beloved.
The letter of Siyyid dated 662 from Rashid Lutf has not arrived that would reveal the reason for his movement. Verily it was for the purpose of trade. He will soon return.
Thereafter the word of truth was fulfilled—“Verily, We were recording that which ye were doing”—and another dispensation and the worlds of Return were made manifest. In consideration of safeguarding a certain ruling, no [change] was enacted—for He is the Most Pure.
Wearing silk and the use of gold and silver are permitted; congregational prayer is not incumbent.
As to the recitation of the hidden verse that was asked about: it is obligatory to purify the “earth of souls”—that is, that they neither hear, nor behold, nor utter, nor write aught save the words of the ʿIlliyyin. And even as the earth of the Book of God was filled with justice and equity, so must the earth of souls likewise be.
Whatsoever is put to use should bear the letters of His Name—the Name of God—pronounced upon it; for example, let it be said “Ya Qadir,” or “Ya Latif,” or “Ya Malik,” over the pen or whatever is employed; then may it be used.
We have no contention with the people, albeit their cry “Haste! Haste!” hath filled the world; yet they are not sincere—we have tried them.
At present, nothing is more meet in Our sight than that We leave them to recite the Prayer of the Covenant, the Tablet of the Testament, and the Supplication of Nudbah, while themselves remaining veiled from its Lord.
Aqa Mirza Aqa Mulla ʿAli-Rida came to the Land of Hayy.
Whenever the Sayyid, by His power, shall transmute his fire into light, the Sayyid of 1280 and the Sayyid of 92 shall be gathered in human form. Even the wolf of the age possessed a measure of wolfishness—this was the origin of this journey.
The righteous and the unrighteous are all distinguished in the Return.
I desire not that this be written for any save the people of truth; otherwise, let a sign be shown. Send it to the mulla and the sayyid.
As for the mistress/mother, let the guardian act with piety; let them change “water” into “air,” that they may find some ease. God willing, the end of all their kindred shall be good.
