title: BB00299
text:
In the Name of God, the All-Thankful, the Pre-Existent, the All-Bountiful, the All-Glorious
Unto God belongeth all splendor (Baha); and verily through God do we array ourselves with splendor at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth all glory; and verily through God do we exalt ourselves in glory at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth all beauty; and verily through God do we bedeck ourselves with beauty at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth all grandeur; and verily through God do we magnify ourselves in grandeur at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth all light; and verily through God do we seek illumination at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth all mercy; and verily through God do we show forth tenderness and compassion at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belong all words; and verily through God do we seek perfection, that we may be made complete, at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth all perfection; and verily through God do we strive to attain unto fullness and completeness at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belong all Names; and verily through God do we become exalted and ennobled by the sanctified Names at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth all might and honour; and verily through God do we seek to be strengthened and honoured at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth the whole of the Will in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God, in very truth, embraceth all things in His knowledge.
Unto God belongeth all knowledge; and verily through God do we strive to acquire understanding at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth all power; and verily through God do we seek to be empowered at every time, before time and after time.
And verily through God do we seek to be well-pleasing (unto Him) at every time, before time and after time; and verily shall we respond to God and to His Messenger and to those who, from His presence, are witnesses, and unto whom they stand assured.
Unto God belongeth all honour and high rank; and verily through God do we seek exaltation and true distinction at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth all sovereignty; and verily through God do we seek to possess whatsoever He willeth for us at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth all dominion; and verily through God do we make all that we desire subservient unto His purpose at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth all loftiness and elevation; and verily through God do we seek to be uplifted at every time, before time and after time.
And verily through God do we rehearse the verses of God at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belong all signs; and verily through God do we seek support and confirmation at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth all bounty and favour; and verily through God do we render thanks at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth the whole of the Cause; and verily through God do we seek to submit ourselves to His command and bidding at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth all liberality and generosity; and verily through God do we seek to be generous, at every time, before time and after time; and verily through God do we seek to be bountiful and noble at every time, before time and after time; and verily through God do we seek to receive from Him gracious gifts at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth all grace and favour; and verily through God do we seek to obtain His grace at every time, before time and after time.
Unto God belongeth all victory; and verily through God do we seek succour and triumph at every time, before time and after time.
And as to silver and gold: when, according to your scale, they have reached the measure of six thousand and five mithqals, then, if one-sixth thereof be set apart for God, let God take it from you, and concerning all else thereof shall they be questioned.
Unto God belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and verily, through God, at every time were we truly independent and free of all save Him.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Thou art, in truth, the Lord of all the worlds.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the All-Merciful, the Compassionate.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the Knower of the unseen and the seen, the King, the True One, the Most High, the Exalted.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the King, the All-Holy, the Source of Peace, the Faithful, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Subduer, the All-Glorious, the Inaccessible.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner. Thine are the most excellent Names in the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and Thou, verily, art the Mighty, the Wise.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the Ordainer, the Originator of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, the King, the Incomparable, the All-Subtle. God hath prescribed unto men the remembrance of the Mystery; say: of it shall all be questioned.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the All-Subtle, the All-Informed.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the Most High, the All-Exalted, the Almighty.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the King, the Sovereign, the Manifest, the All-Glorious, the All-Majestic, the All-Glorified, the Well-Beloved, the All-Transcending, the Most Exalted.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the Beloved, the One, the Single, the Peerless, the Self-Sufficient, the Beauteous, the Near-at-Hand.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the King, the Powerful, the Self-Subsisting, the Subduer, the All-Knowing, the Manifest, the Hidden, the All-Resplendent, the Ordainer, the Bountiful, the Ruler, the Judge, the Answerer of prayer.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the King, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Inaccessible.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the Most High, the All-Exalted, the Most Great.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the most Hearing of them that hear.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the most Seeing of them that behold.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the swiftest of those who reckon.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the most Powerful of them that are powerful.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the best of guardians.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the most Merciful of them that show mercy.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the most Bountiful of them that are bountiful.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the nearest of them that are near.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the most Generous of them that are generous.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the most Wise of them that judge.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the most Excellent of them that are excellent.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the greatest of those who bestow gifts.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the best of them that decide between men.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the best of them that forgive.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the best of them that gather together.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the best of them that bring victory.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Thee alone do we worship; unto Thee alone do we bow down; unto Thee alone do we stand in devout humility; unto Thee alone do we show reverence; unto Thee alone do we submit; in Thee alone do we place our hope; Thee alone do we glorify; Thee alone do we hallow; Thee alone do we declare One; Thee alone do we magnify; from Thee alone do we seek aid.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily, Thou art the best of inheritors.

title: BB00394
text:
In the Name of God, the All-Powerful, the All-Holy, the Inaccessible.
Glorified be He Who hath created the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them by His command—“Be,” and it is.
Glorified be He Whom all that are in the heavens and all that are on the earth and whatsoever lieth between them glorify, according to that which He hath ordained by His command; and all prostrate themselves before Him.
Glorified be He in Whose grasp is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and by His leave do all act.
Glorified be He Who hath established Himself upon the Throne, Who knoweth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is on the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and Who ordaineth the creation of all things, as He willeth, by His command, according to a measured decree.
Glorified be He in Whose grasp is the realm of omnipotent dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and unto Him shall all return.
Glorified be He for Whose sake act all that are in the heavens and on the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and unto Him shall all turn again.
Glorified be He Whose is the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and before Him do all stand.
Glorified be He Whose is the primal origination of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and before Him do all bow down.
Glorified be He Whose is the judgment of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and unto Him shall all be raised up.
Glorified be He Whose is the justice of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and by His command do all judge.
Glorified be He Whose is the bounty of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and of His bounty do all ask.
Glorified be He Whose is the light of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and by His light are all illumined.
Glorified be He Whose are the keys of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them: He expendeth as He willeth through His bounty; and all remember Him.
Glorified be He Whose are the measures of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and all praise Him.
Glorified be He Whose are the keys of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and all give thanks unto Him.
Glorified be He Whose is the grandeur in the kingdom of command and creation and whatsoever lieth between them; and all stand in awe before Him.
Glorified be He Whose is the might in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and all humble themselves before Him.
Glorified be He Whose is all power in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and all magnify Him.
Glorified be He, for Whose Name no name of any thing shall be mentioned—neither from before nor from after, neither in the heavens nor on the earth nor in whatsoever lieth between them; and all things have ever acted by His command, and unto this bear witness.
Glorified be He Who hath sent down the Bayan upon all that are in the heavens and on the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, according to that which He hath decreed for them—that they may proclaim the oneness of God and then worship Him.
Glorified be He Who hath brought into being the Point in its entirety, and hath created therein what He hath created in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, that its people may say: God is our Lord, the Well-Beloved of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them; and that all may be assured of what hath been sent down from God.
Glorified be He Who hath commanded in the Book that with every soul, whether male or female, there be a thousand verses of the verses of God, from what hath been revealed in the Point and the Letters; and that all, at every time, may acknowledge Muhammad, the Apostle of God, and those who are witnesses after Him, and those who have believed in God and His verses—all are submissive unto Him.

title: BB00405
text:
In the Name of God, the Subduer of all things, the All-Attracting, the All-Glorious, the All-Powerful.
Unto God appertaineth the whole of the Cause, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a Cause tremendous.
Unto God belong the subtleties of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a tenderness tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the light of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a light tremendous.
Unto God belongeth all power, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a power tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the purity of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a purity tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the dust of the first and of the last, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a dust tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the Point in its entirety, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a Point tremendous.
Unto God appertaineth the whole of the Cause, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a Cause tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the grace of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a grace tremendous.
Say: God is my Lord, and He, verily, is my Sufficiency; He will assuredly aid me, by His command, at all times, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a Cause tremendous.
Unto God belong the subtleties of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a tenderness tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the singleness of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a oneness tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the Alif in its entirety, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of an Alif tremendous.
Say: God is the Creator of all things, through His command, “Be”, and it is.
Unto God belongeth the Standard of might, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a standard tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the splendour of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a splendour tremendous.
Unto God belong the Most Excellent Names, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a Name tremendous.
Unto God belongeth guardianship in its fulness, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a guardianship tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the Ba’ in its entirety, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a Ba’ tremendous.
Unto God appertaineth the Cause, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a Cause tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the Standard of greatness in its entirety, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a standard tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the bounty of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a bounty tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the certitude of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a certitude tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a Kingdom (malakút) tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the Jim in its entirety, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a Jim tremendous.
Unto God appertaineth the whole of the Cause, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a Cause tremendous.
Unto God belong the subtleties of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a tenderness tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the perpetuity of judgement, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a lasting judgement tremendous.
Unto God appertaineth the whole of the Cause, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a Cause tremendous.
Unto God it pertaineth that, from every soul, there be nineteen days wherein it serveth the Point and acteth by Her leave; and God hath ever been the Possessor of a grace tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the Standard of power, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a standard tremendous.
Say: God is my Lord, in the beginning and in the end; in Him have I put my trust, and sufficient is God as a Sovereign, tremendous.
Unto God belongeth the Standard of sovereignty, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a standard tremendous.
Unto God belongeth guidance in its fulness, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a guidance tremendous.
Unto God appertaineth the whole of the Cause, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a Cause tremendous.
Unto God belongeth guardianship in its fulness, in the beginning and in the end, and God hath ever been the Possessor of a guardianship tremendous.

title: BB00097
text:
Part 1: “Glorified art Thou, O my God! I testify…”
In the Name of God, the Most Vast, the Most Holy
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I testify by all things unto Thee that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thine is the Kingdom and the Dominion, then the Might and the Omnipotence, then the Power and the Divine Realm, then the Strength and the Sapphire, then the Sovereignty and the Human Realm, then the Glory and the Majesty, then the Countenance and the Perfection, then the Face and the Beauty, then the Grandeur and the Independence, then the Pride and the Sublimity, then the Mercy and the Grace, then the Authority and the Justice, then the Similitude and the Examples, then the Power and the Deeds, then the Loftiness and the Exaltation, then the Joy and the Gladness, then the Might and the Invincibility, then the Love and the Detachment.
Then by all that is seen and unseen from the highest heights to the primal atom, I testify with certainty that Thou hast been independent of all contingent beings and self-sufficient above all existing things. All are created through knowledge of Thee and are remembered through faith in what Thou hast revealed unto Thy Proof. Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not, the Sovereign Who passeth not away, the Just Who wrongeth not, the King Who changeth not, the Single One from Whose grasp nothing escapeth. Thou givest life and causest death, and causest death and givest life. Verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not, and the King from Whose grasp escapeth nothing, whether in the heavens or on earth or between them. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
Moreover, I testify that creation is Thy creation and command is from Thee and unto Thee, alone with no God but Thee. Thou hast created no glory save in knowing Thee and following Thy commandments. Thou hast ever been and wilt ever be. Thou savest from the fire whom Thou willest and causest to enter therein whom Thou willest. For in each of Thy Manifestations, when Thou makest Thyself known through Thy signs, all Thy creation become veiled. Thy servants, even should they worship Thee, would be veiled, and those who prostrate themselves before Thee, even should they prostrate, would not be veiled. Rather, they have worshipped Thee based on imagination and prostrated themselves without knowledge.
Glorified art Thou, there is no God but Thee. By Thy might, knowledge of Thy Self-Manifestation is dearer to me than all else. Without this nothing profiteth me, and this without all else profiteth me. Thus do I testify that in each of Thy Manifestations, when Thou hast perfected the Manifestations of those whom Thou hast nurtured through Thy commands and prohibitions, that Thou mightest purify them in Thy revelation after that Manifestation, if they were truthful in Thy previous Manifestation, then they would be detached unto Thee and not be veiled by anything before Thee.
Indeed, O my God, from the first moment Thou didst manifest me, all who followed me through what Thou gavest me of Thy signs—there is no doubt they are among those possessed of knowledge and wisdom with Thee—have entered knowingly into Thy good-pleasure and are not veiled by anything from Thy glory. And beyond that, until Thou takest me up unto Thee, Thy manifestations are shining upon him. Should he become veiled by anything, he hath fallen into unconsciousness and what he hath gained will not profit him. Thou hast said—and Thy word regarding Thy manifestation on the Day of Resurrection is true—“All who are in the heavens and earth and what lieth between them shall swoon away, save those whom God willeth.” Therefore, O God, make those whom Thou hast mentioned in the Book among those whom Thou hast willed, lest the fruit of their existence be lost on the Day of Thy Manifestation. For all act for Thee that Thou might accept from them, but they pay no heed that Thy acceptance will only be manifested through what is revealed from Thee in verses that have rendered the learned impotent.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! The people have heard all that is in the Furqan and the traditions of Thy Proofs from before, yet they have not understood their meaning nor paid attention to Thy purpose therein, such as when Thou didst reveal in the Qur’an the mention of the Day of Resurrection and the Day of Judgment, yet when Thou didst reveal these, Thou didst intend naught save the time of Thine Own manifestation in the revelation of Thy wondrous creation, though Thy chosen ones had interpreted both as the appearance of Thy proof. The people, however, having believed in illusory matters devoid of reality, failed to serve Thee, for they hearkened not unto Thy proofs and comprehended only what their minds could grasp. They claim to possess in this regard tradition or necessity, failing to understand that these two can only be established after the Manifestation of God, Whose prophethood—upon which all religion depends—Thou didst establish through Thy verses, though these two claims are rejected by Thee unless they accord with Thy purpose in the Book and the good-pleasure of Thy proofs in what they have uttered from Thee.
All peoples possess similar claims from their prophets, yet these shall profit them nothing with Thee. Their consensus, which is their greatest proof, was initially nullified by lacking even seven souls. How then could their greatest proof be nullified by lacking seven souls, when at that time these seven were considered by them to be possessed of wisdom and faith? Yet on that first day, they spoke of them as mentioned in the Furqan: “Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?” Such is the limitation of creation, in that they pay no heed to the origin of their religion and that whereby their ordinances are established.
By Thy glory! The truly learned are they who know Thee and verify Thy verses, whether they know all things or know nothing of all things. In every Dispensation, those who came before are tested, and nothing shall profit them save following Thy guidance and believing in Thy Manifestation, for there is none manifest but Thee, and none hidden save Thee. If the appearance of Thy Beloved were inferior to Thine Own, how couldst Thou have elevated the appearance of Jesus through His Manifestation?
I bear witness, by Thy glory, that Thou art the First and there is nothing before Thee, Thou art the Last and there is nothing after Thee, Thou art the Manifest and there is nothing above Thee, and Thou art the Hidden and there is nothing beyond Thee. Thy decrees are inscrutable and transcendent, and Thy beginnings are exalted and unique.
O God! Send down upon him who hath manifested Thy verses in his First Book all Thy grace and mercy, for were it not for Thy bestowal of all Thy grace and mercy upon him, nothing would suffice him, though after this nothing shall diminish from his grace. And concerning what hath been mentioned before Thee regarding the Bayan, do Thou cause him, O God, through Thy grace and mercy, to be sustained by the virgin cities of Thy paradise and to delight in the melodies of the birds and the warbling of the doves in the gardens of Thy oneness. This is Thy grace unto whom Thou pleasest and Thy bounty unto whom Thou willest.
Do Thou inspire him, O God, to observe Thy bounds as established before, lest he be saddened in Thy path. And concerning what hath been revealed from Thee regarding the loftiness of Thy grace and the sublimity of Thy bounty—yea, by Thy glory, were it not for Thy desired grace, who would be worthy of Thy bounty? Thou hast indeed carried all the destinies of that Manifestation upon spirit and fragrance, glory and exposition, lest anyone find within himself aught that might weigh heavily upon him, for Thy independence from all things is indubitable and the need of all things for Thee is irrefutable. Wert Thou to desire justice, who could establish Thy right? Rather, Thou hast ever spread mercy and grace over all Thy servants, for Thy chosen ones therein and Thy loved ones in its invisible and visible realms, for besides them, through their grace, do they enter Paradise and recite the Bayan […]
Verily, what he hath desired of Thy grace, there is no doubt that whoso is in Thy love, he hath ever been and shall ever be in Thy paradise—none can remove him therefrom. This is what Thou hast sealed for him and ordained for him as a bounty from Thee and a gift from Thy presence. Therefore, O my God, do Thou answer his prayer that he may witness the fulfillment of all his needs in this life, if Thy decrees have ordained it thus, and if not, then in Thy worlds which Thou hast destined, until there remaineth with him nothing that he loveth save that he findeth Thy criterion. Thou art the One Who hath power over whatsoever Thou pleaseth and might over whatsoever Thou willeth. Do Thou preserve him, O my God, through Thy might and power and strength and grandeur and majesty, for verily his survival is most beloved unto me, for were there not such souls as these, wherefrom would the earth be weighted with Thy unity and through it flow the rivers of Thy sanctification?

title: BB00097
section: Part 2: “Glorified art Thou! There is no God but…”
text:
Part 2: “Glorified art Thou! There is no God but…”
Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee! Indeed he hath desired of Thy Most Great Glad-Tidings and Thy Supreme Gift. What glad-tidings could be greater than Thy remembrance of him, and what gift more exalted than Thy good-pleasure with him, whereby he shall endure unto the Day of Resurrection in the Book? Do Thou, O my God, create him with the character of the most exalted ones, and of them that glorify, and of the spiritual ones who stand in ranks. Separate between him and those who believe not in Thy signs, and unite him with those who have believed in Thy signs. Verily, the companions of Thy good-pleasure are like unto the morning stars in their radiance. Should anyone in that day desire to distinguish between their sandals and those beneath them, verily he would be able to do so, for all that he desireth lieth within the shadow of Thy Word and what Thou hast established after Thy exposition.
O my God! Separate not between him and the people of Thy Ridvan, for these are they who have recognized Thee and followed Thy signs, and besides them I love not to make mention of any. Do Thou preserve, O my God, him and the people of Thy love from that which Thou lovest not, for verily Thou art the best of doers. And if he desireth to have his name mentioned in the paths, then separate not, O my God, between him and it, and do Thou cause him to know his station with Thee and his rank before Thee, lest he witness that which would sadden him in Thy presence. For verily Thou hast loved him and loved those who love him for Thy sake. How great is his station and the station of those like him in their faith in Thee and then in Thy signs!
As for what he hath mentioned in his letter regarding intercession for his father and mother and family and those who have aided him in his cause—verily Thou art more worthy and more glorious than to turn away anyone from Thy door or to withhold from any soul Thy forgiveness and good-pleasure. However, O my God, I would love to teach him that which would benefit him in intercession and bear fruit for its people.
For whoso was in a Manifestation before Thee, if he was veiled by anything, then the intercession of his brother or of one who would intercede for him would benefit him. But since the essence of His Cause hath been established for him, all the measures of Thy forgiveness and all the gates of Thy good-pleasure are accepted for him in their entirety.
But as for one who hath been veiled from the Manifestation of Thy creation by responding to Thy call with “Yea,” how can Thy forgiveness reach him when he hath no essence capable of bearing Thy forgiveness? And whoso hath heard but estimated that which hath come between him and his response hath entered the fire and is deserving according to the measure of his separation.
But after he hath responded, it is as though he had responded to Thee from the beginning that hath no beginning to the end that hath no end. For whoso respondeth to Thee in Him Whom Thou shalt manifest, verily he hath responded to Thee in all the worlds; and whoso respondeth not to Thee in Him, even if he responded to Thee in all the worlds, it would profit him not. For He is the Manifestation of Thy Self—how then could one who responded to Thee before not respond to Thee afterwards? Verily, the manifestation of Thy Cause in the Hereafter is greater and more exalted than the manifestation of Thy Cause in the first life.
And I testify unto Thee that Paradise in that life is to know Thee and to love Thee, then to follow what hath been sent down from Thy presence, for Thy verses have been magnified above all who dwell in the kingdoms of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them. After one entereth therein, he shall not be veiled by aught from the seats of Thy command and Thy prohibition. Then shall the intercession of whomsoever intercedeth be accepted therein. But for him who hath no ruling, how can this be applicable to him?
Nay, by Thy glory, I shall surely love whomsoever is from Thee, that I may forgive all things and cause all things to enter Paradise, for I desire naught save what Thou hast forgiven, and I love naught save what Thou hast caused to enter. But Thy forgiveness descendeth not save upon him who knoweth Thee and followeth Thy command, nor doth any enter Thy Paradise save he who loveth Thee and followeth what hath been ordained from Thy presence. For what Thou hast promised in the Hereafter shall be made manifest unto its people according to what they have tasted in that existence.
Thus, were all upon the earth to answer Thy call at the time of His manifestation, they would all enter Thy Paradise and the garden of Thy forgiveness. But none attaineth unto this save he who truly believeth in Him, even though Thou hast commanded all to this and permitted all to that. And likewise in Thy manifestation in the Bayan, and likewise in Thy manifestation to Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest through the signs of Thy power and the words of Thy glory.
Otherwise, were the veil to be lifted, all would worship Thee and prostrate themselves before Thee according to what Thou lovest and art pleased with. But when they are veiled without right, they worship Thee and prostrate themselves before Thee through the manifestation of Him Who preceded Thee; yet it is not for Thee but for other than Thee—and if it be for Thee it returneth unto Thee. For from the days of Adam until now, there is none save that he hath a path from his Prophet who was in his time the Truth, if he altereth it not. But how can this benefit him?
Therefore, O my God, do Thou have mercy upon all Thy creation and send forth from Thy presence one who shall cause them to enter the Paradise of Thy forgiveness and the heaven of Thy good-pleasure. For verily, I see not the people possessed of knowledge; rather I see them as the embryo in its mother’s womb, finding it difficult to emerge, and seeing itself as though God had created no world for it save that wherein it dwelleth, and God had created no sustenance sweeter than that which nourisheth it. Yet God bringeth it forth without its consent, and day by day it witnesseth the bounty of its Lord and the generosity of its Creator.
Therefore, O my God, show grace unto all Thy creation, for they are Thy servants and within Thy grasp. They reckon they do good while in Thy sight they do not good, after Thou hadst taught them the ways of knowing Thee. But they have become veiled thereby, though they have seen Thy chosen ones among Thy creation following Thy good-pleasure and detaching themselves from all else in such wise as none hath preceded them. Yet they pay no heed.
And I see not, O my God, for all who are on earth any bounty from Thy presence and generosity from Thy side greater and mightier than that Thou shouldst send forth from Thy presence one who shall cause them to enter into Thy Faith. For by Thy glory, I have loved none save Thee and desired naught besides Thee. Verily Thou sufficest me against all things, and nothing sufficeth against Thee, neither in the heavens nor on earth nor whatsoever lieth between them. Thou art indeed the Encompasser of all things.
And verily he who hath desired of Thy grace and communed with Thee in his book before Thee—no doubt Thou art the Knower of all things and the Powerful over all things. Thou causest the measures to flow through their means, and he knoweth Thee not who desireth them without their means, though Thou art indeed powerful and mighty over all things. Thou createst the means through their cause and createst the cause through no cause of itself.
But Thou hast ordained measures for all things which appear only through the operation of their causes. Therefore, O my God, set in motion for him who hath beseeched Thee in his book all the causes of Thy bounty, both in his beginning and his end. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things. And inspire him, O my God, as he reciteth that verse, with that which will gladden his heart, for in every letter thereof is that which Thou hast created of Thy spirit which must needs attach itself to him who readeth it, for Thou art indeed near and ready to answer. Say: God hath manifested above every manifestation, and none in the heavens or on the earth or in what lieth between them can withhold himself from the sovereign power of His manifestation. Verily, His was a manifestation manifest and manifest-making. And cause him, O my God, to know the places where the Command falleth upon him, for Thou art the best Ordainer and Decreer, and Thou art, verily, the Preserver of all things.

title: BB00276: Letter to Mulla Nawruz ’Ali
text:
To Mulla Naw-ruz-ʿAli:
In the Name of the Most Great, the Most Great. Glorified be He Whom all that are in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them do praise, say: All bow down before Him in adoration. Praise be to God, Whom all that are in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them do glorify, say: All stand humbly before Him. To God belongeth all that is in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them, say: All abide by His command. To God belongeth the dominion of the heavens and of the earth and of whatsoever is between them. He createth what He willeth through His command, verily He is the Strong, the Powerful.
Say: God is the Creator of all things. All that are in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them glorify Him, say: All are His servants and all bow down before Him. Say: O God! Thou art the Light of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them. Thou givest light unto whom Thou willest, and withdrawest light from whom Thou willest. Thou exaltest whom Thou willest and abaseth whom Thou willest. Thou strengthenest whom Thou willest and humblest whom Thou willest. Thou aidest whom Thou willest and forsaketh whom Thou willest. Thou enrichest whom Thou willest and makest poor whom Thou willest. Within Thy grasp is the kingdom of all things. Thou createst what Thou willest, how Thou willest, by what Thou willest, for what Thou willest. Verily, Thou hast power over all things.
Say: God is the Most Exalted above all who are exalted. None in the heavens or the earth or whatsoever is between them can withstand the supreme exaltation of His exaltedness. Verily, He is the Most High, the Most Exalted, the Supreme.
O Day of Naw-Ruz! We have created thee aforetime and made thee a festival for all the worlds. We promised to gather thee on the Day of Resurrection and present thee before Us in human form, and verily We are faithful to Our promise. This is a day which God hath magnified from the beginning that hath no beginning, and all magnify it as God hath magnified it. And this is a day which God will continue to magnify until the end that hath no end, and all shall magnify it as God doth magnify it. This is the Day of God, the Dominant, the Self-Subsisting. And verily its night is the Night of God, the Mighty, the Beloved.
O all things! Magnify ye God on that night and its day and in all the joy ye manifest. We have enabled thee aforetime to present thyself before God by night and by day—this is of God’s grace unto thee from before, and this indeed is the great bounty. Shouldst thou glory in this over all who are in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them, thou art indeed among those who are worthy. And all the sorrow that hath been endured in God’s path aforetime—how they were veiled from God their Lord—shall deliver them from the fire of their veiling, for We are indeed bountiful.
Thou hast been presented before God thy Lord once, then again, then yet again, and then after yet again—all this was what God had promised that thou wouldst be presented before Him on that Day, and God will present thee again hereafter, for He is indeed the All-Preserving, the Powerful. We have shown favor unto thee and sent thee with this Book unto those who desire to be guided. Let no sorrow be witnessed; deliver this unto all whom thou findest a way to reach. For this is indeed a Book which, when it descendeth upon a believer, becometh light upon light and grace upon grace, and he will be assured by it and will stand firm in the Cause of his Lord like unto a mighty mountain. And if it descendeth upon one who is not a believer but desireth to be guided, God will guide him thereby; and if he does not wish to be guided, God will punish him for what God has established as proofs of truth in that Book for all the worlds.
We do not wish you to grieve about this on the path, and We shall surely answer concerning what you have borne of God’s proofs from the Holy Land. By God, exalt your Lord before them all. Everyone who calls unto God your Lord is in truth, if he is not veiled from anything by the limits of the Bayan.
Say: O all things, assist the religion of God according to your capacity. Recite what We have revealed of the Prayer of Clay in the sanctuary which you entered aforetime, for We did enter there. Bring the clay in such a manner as to fashion seals in a style without equal, and carry them with you, for We have so commanded. Guard the words of God as your own eyes, and give not a word to anyone unless you command that they preserve it or its like among those who preserve the words of your Lord, for one letter thereof is better in the sight of God than all that is in the last and first life. If you wish to attain the presence of one who attains the House of God from before, then attain it and convey to him the like of what you have borne of the Book of God, for this is indeed the great bounty.
Say: Aid God through the Most Great Name according to your power, and know the value of the days of God, for the sun has never risen upon their like. If you wish to join two souls in marriage, none can prevent you from this as a bounty from God upon you and upon them both. God has nurtured you in them both before the creation of the heavens and earth and what lies between them, for He is the Best of Judges. However, be vigilant lest it become a veil to the manifestation of God’s Cause, for this is most great in the sight of God in a mighty Book.

title: BB00357: Tawqi’a Tahrim Sharb-i-Dukhkhan (in honor of Shaykh ’Ali)
text:
He is the Most High, the Most Great, the Wondrous
Glorified be He Who knoweth what is in the heavens and what is on earth. There is no God but Him, the Mighty, the Wise.
He is the One Who createth what He willeth by His command. Those who have disbelieved in God and His signs—these are they who are the lost. And those who have believed in God and His signs and followed the light that guideth mankind unto a straight path—these are they who are guided by the Book of God and these are they who shall inherit the gardens of eternity, for which there is no equal in thy Lord’s Book. Therein hath been prepared by thy Lord’s leave all that their souls desire, and the remembrance of God therein is greater than what men ask for.
And if today the veil were lifted from their eyes, they would surely witness that the remembrance of God among them is dearer to them than their own selves, and it is greater in God’s Book than what men do. These are clear signs for those who believe in them. And for those who disbelieve in God’s signs there is a grievous punishment.
It hath been forbidden in the Book for people to smoke tobacco and drink wine, and God hath not placed any healing in them. Those who prescribe them for some people have ruled by the judgment of the Evil One. These people drink naught but the boiling water of hell, did they but perceive it.
Say: O people, fear God and deny not Him Who guideth you to a straight path. The pillars of religion are raised forever, and it is the Sacred House, if ye but knew it.
He is the One by Whose light ye were guided before, and about Whom ye shall be questioned on the Day of Resurrection. Today no deed of any of you shall be accepted unless ye believe in the remembrance of your Lord’s name and act with justice. Say: Fear ye God on the day when ye shall be resurrected, then shall ye be gathered unto God. On that day ye shall stand before God, then shall ye be brought before Him. On that day thy Lord God shall judge between people with truth according to what their hands have earned, and thy Lord God is not heedless of what the workers do.
He is the One Who knoweth the unseen of the heavens and earth, and guideth whom He willeth, and none go astray save the heedless people. Those who fabricate lies about thy Lord God, then follow their own desires against those who believe in God and His signs—these shall not prosper. They enjoy but a brief pleasure in this worldly life, and when they die they shall be tormented in the fire and shall not be helped.
Those who judge without the judgment detailed in the Book aforetime and who oppress those who are weak in the earth without right—these shall not prosper. Say: Power belongeth unto God and might is in His hand. He doeth what He willeth and He is the Prevailer over His creation. He judgeth between them with justice and He is most severe in punishing the oppressors and most stern in retribution.
My Lord, judge between me and the people with truth, and pour forth upon me patience, and draw me unto Thee, and join me with those who are nigh unto Thee. And should anyone become aware of these verses, let him strive in God’s path with truth, and let no one cause him fear, nor let the blame of any blamer turn him aside, and let him work for naught but God and be among the witnesses in God’s religion.
Should all people gather together to produce the like of these verses, they would never be able, even if they were helpers one to another. This is a perfect proof from God’s Book for all on earth, and God sufficeth as a witness over the worlds.

title: BB00662: Javab-i-’Alim-i-Rashti
text:
In the Name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate
Praise be to God, the Lord of all worlds; and may blessings be upon the One, the Primal, at all times.
To continue: It is no secret to any soul who believeth in God, in His Book, in His Messenger, in the Imams of guidance and the Manifestations of His Cause, that in this day there is no matter more momentous than the knowledge of the Fountain-Head of religion. Wherefore he hath deemed it incumbent upon himself to apprise all of that which he hath himself expounded, that he may not fall under the shadow of the well-known tradition, and that the concise may be made plain by the detailed.
That Cause which, in the year sixty, was made manifest—and upon the tongues of all is mentioned by the name of the Bab—was of the stages of the Promised One in Whom all the sects of Islam have believed and Whose advent they have expected. The proof that hath assured his own heart, and is sufficient for whomsoever God willeth, is the appearance of the verses which he hath witnessed—verses issuing from that Origin in a manner innate to His nature: for, if a soul but request of Him, in the span of five hours a thousand verses, after this fashion, would proceed from that Source. Though other modes and signs, beyond all count and number, have likewise appeared—inasmuch as, within five hours, a thousand supplications were heard to be revealed—this he did not himself behold; yet of the verses he witnessed with his very eyes that in their recitation there was, and is, no pause nor premeditation whatsoever.
This may be verified in divers ways. One is this: From the descent of the Qur’an until the year wherein one thousand two hundred and seventy years elapsed, had it been possible to produce a single verse of the verses of God by human power, it would assuredly have been produced. That it was not—while now the appearance thereof is beheld—leaveth no doubt that it is “from God”, for the incapacity of all is manifest. He himself hath witnessed to the number of one hundred thousand verses; and though all mankind, within the bounds wherein they stand, advance their claims, none hath been seen to bring the like. Is it that they are able yet refrain? Nay, for had it been in their power, long since would they have done so.
It is evident to the people of the world, who, with great toil attain unto the utmost limit of skill, that if they read a single Arabic line, they can indeed compose one; beyond that they can but reflect and falter. And if anyone hath perused the commentaries and compositions ascribed to them against this Cause, he is thereby permitted to render the judgment that is meet; otherwise, he denieth his very sense. All these allusions are but to show the path; else, by the proof of wisdom, if a man desire to know, there is no thing but it pointeth to His knowledge; and He is exalted above being known by aught save Himself—rather, all else is known by Him.
He is, moreover, uplifted above that mention of the True One should be made in that station, for every reality is by Him made real. Its likeness is the sun: wert thou to imagine it to rise and set times without number, there would yet be but one sun. And this is that which, in every Dispensation, shone forth under the Name of the Manifest, and in that Dispensation was the Manifest; until, in the former Manifestation, it was the Muhammadan Reality—blessings of God be upon it and upon the Manifestations of its Cause.
This is the mystery of that tradition transmitted from the Imams—peace be upon them—that at the time of the Advent He will make mention of Adam unto the Seal, after this wise: “Whoso desireth to behold Him, let him look upon me,” for in truth His Reality is that Reality and none other. This is pure Reality, not metaphor nor hyperbole.
That which hath occasioned the veiling of the whole community is the very power of the Cause that is among men: for today, whatsoever occurreth in Islam occurreth under the name of the Manifestation of the Messenger of God—peace be upon Him—whether in the horizons or within souls. For every soul who, between himself and God, determineth to act, whatever verse pointeth him unto God is a verse wherein the Theophany of the Messenger of God is made manifest. Likewise, in the horizons, the Manifestations wherein naught is seen but God—such as the Imams of guidance and the Gates—are verses in which the Primal Reality shineth forth within them. Nay rather, whatsoever in Islam hath appeared until this day hath been through that Manifestation.
And this Manifestation in this era is, openly, the appearance of the Messenger of God: lesser in relation to the cycle that followeth, and greater in relation to the cycle that preceded. What hath veiled the believers therefrom is but their own surmise: they have striven, yet not testified for God, and this is pure fancy. For whatsoever the Muslims hold today of religious ordinances, of degrees of knowledge, of certitude in the Guardianship of the Imams and the Prophethood of the Messenger, of what God sent down in the Qur’an, and of belief in the Day of Resurrection and in the raising, assembling, presentation and meeting with Him, in Paradise and Hell, and other matters mentioned—all return to the authority of the verses, which are the source of every proof. For the prophethood of the Messenger is established thereby and not otherwise; and the ordinances of religion, in fundamentals and branches, are established by the word of the Messenger—peace be upon Him.
As to what is cited in the tokens of appearance, the traditions agreed upon by all are not, one and all, certain in origin; and if they conflict with the Book, they are not to be acted upon. How, then, could the very proof by which prophethood was first established be set aside, and reliance placed upon traditions whose issuance is unproven or whose intended meaning, after establishment, is not made plain by the Speaker?
In sum: It is far from the discerning soul that, by matters which, in manifold degrees, lead back to the Source, he should be veiled from the primal proof. For what we, this despised band, now affirm—we have never heard from any Messenger or Imam a decisive exposition of what is meant by “return” (raj’at), or by “Resurrection” and its concerns; and if one holdeth a belief therein, it is in things he himself hath conceived. Indeed, concerning a single subsidiary question certainty is not attained—how then should it appear in the principal stations?
What we possess is but words we have seen; yet today these do not withstand that proof whereby religion itself is established. For example: among the signs of the Advent is that the sun should rise from the West. If this be as we understand it, then from the days of Adam to the Seal it hath not occurred. How, then, could it not occur for one like unto the Messenger of God in the very hour of His manifestation? While reason pronounceth its impossibility, and will so pronounce though a thousand thousand advents occur—the sun of the heaven shall not be changed. And so in other signs the intellect, by first principles, knoweth that such things are of another import—when, that is, one desireth to understand the traditions. Otherwise, where the manifest proof and the conclusive argument—the verses of God—are present, what need to be veiled by such matters?
That which hath brought perplexity to the bewildered is the failure to adduce any proof other than the verses. Yet in this station it is evident to the discerning soul that, if the Manifestation be established, the authority of the Proof and its bounds sufficeth—according to the explicit word of the noble verse:

“Is it not enough for them that We have sent down unto thee the Book which is recited unto them? Verily in this is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.”

It is manifest that God, in the Qur’an, in establishing the truth of the Messenger of God, advanced no plea but the verses. It is as though whatsoever is narrated elsewhere hath no place of mention before God—or rather, the most exalted is established, and mention of the lesser is not made.
To summarize: In the Qur’an today, the plea adduced for the proof of prophethood is the verses alone. In the matter of proof they differ not, before the discerning, whether the whole Qur’an or the Surih of Tawhid be cited. As for those who cavil at the niceties of Arab eloquence, grammar and morphology: let them refer to themselves, and they will find their answer. Such objections would hold only were the verses of God revealed in accordance with what the people already possess; whereas all that the people have, they have taken from it. After the establishment of the proof, these become no locus of doubt or dispute. For had aught contrary to what now appeareth been revealed in the Qur’an, who would have been permitted to argue by anything other than what was sent down?
Far be it from God! Nay, this is the strongest proof of the proof: how could one who knoweth these rules utter words of such a kind unless from before Him? By the sanctified Essence of God! His Cause is, for him who pondereth with fairness, more wondrous even than the Cause of the Messenger of God. For the acquisition of these sciences is for the sake of understanding the Qur’an; how then should He Who is their Fountain be encompassed by them? And yet it is seen how those perfected therein have believed—inasmuch as they beheld their own impotence before the verses.
Naught is beheld, among those who have heard and pondered, but the like of the adversaries’ verses that were heard and pondered in the dawn of Islam. How many of the community of Jesus awaited the advent of Ahmad—blessings and peace be upon Him and His kindred!—and when He appeared, it became clear how many were guided. Today the very same affliction hath encompassed all, and all are veiled—though, in their fancy, they act “for God”, in truth it is “besides God”. For there is no soul who, between himself and God, knoweth the creation aright, willeth to attest the truth, and yet, in a station he comprehendeth not, attaineth certainty in the proof thereof—according to the word of God: “And they rejected it, though their souls were convinced thereof, out of injustice.” For that very Soul Who “ordereth the affair, and setteth forth the signs, that haply ye may be assured of meeting your Lord”—the “meeting” intended is this very Manifestation, wherein naught is seen but God, for His verses bear witness to His truth.
Ask whom thou wilt: “Whose word is the Qur’an?” He will say: “The word of God.” Look then upon these verses; if thou findest a difference, remain veiled; otherwise, know of a certainty that it is that same Origin of the Word. For “speech” is not an attribute of the Essence, but of the Will—therefore it appeareth from It.
Consider the Tablet of Fatimah, until He saith: “And He shall perfect that through God: Muhammad, a mercy to all the worlds—upon Him be the perfection of Moses, and the splendor of Jesus, and the patience of Job. My friends in His days shall be abased; their heads shall be borne as are borne the heads of the Turks and Daylamites; they shall be slain and burned, and shall be in fear …”—that thou mayest know what, in the former Manifestation, was sent down. Were it of the sort all could grasp, God would not have revealed thus in the dawn of Islam in the Tablet of Fatimah, nor would our lord Sadiq—in the prayer of Nudbih—have spoken after this manner. Nay, the Cause is even as it appeared at the rise of Islam, and the word of the Messenger of God must be fulfilled: “Islam shall return estranged as it began; blessed are the strangers!”
Gaze upon the Advent of the Messenger of God in the very midst of effulgence, and upon what then befell. Marvel not, then, at what hath come to pass at the appearing of thy Beloved; for “the truth turneth with the True One”—Paradise is with Him and Hell is with Him; it moveth as the shadow moveth with the sun, and pastureth wheresoever He gazeth. Look, perchance thou mayest derive the honor of existence; for if thou art guided, it is for thine own self, and if thou remain veiled, thou wilt be thyself the fire of thine own veil. “God guideth whom He willeth unto the straight Path.”

title: BB00289: Prayer for Friday
text:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate
God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, and the angels and they who are endowed with knowledge, standing firm on justice, proclaim that there is none other God but Him, the Almighty, the All-Wise. Thy letter hath reached that Mountain, and I bear witness to that which God in His knowledge hath testified, that there is none other God but Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Most Exalted, the Most Great, the Lord of Glory and Bounty.
God, exalted be His mention, hath said:

“God hath made the Ka’bah, the Sacred House, a standard for mankind, and the Sacred Month, and the offerings and the garlands. This is that ye may know that God knoweth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, and that God hath knowledge of all things.”

I bear witness before God on this Friday upon the Mighty Mountain that God hath encompassed all things in His knowledge. O Lord! Bear Thou witness to that which I have witnessed, and sufficient art Thou as a witness unto me. Know thou that God hath said:

“We will show them Our signs in the horizons and in themselves until it becomes clear to them that this is the Truth. Is it not sufficient that thy Lord is witness over all things?”

Then He, exalted be His mention, saith: “When he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley in the blessed spot, from the Tree: ʿO Moses! Verily, I am God, the Lord of the Worlds.”’ Say: Yea, by my Lord, this is the certain Truth. Therefore glorify the name of thy Lord, the Most Great.
Open thine eyes, for all are this day in a stupor. For whom shall I speak, concerning whose command shall I speak, wherefore and whereby? None shall deny save him upon whom thy Lord’s mighty grasp shall fall. Verily, He it is Who beginneth and repeateth, and He is the All-Forgiving, the All-Loving, the Lord of the Glorious Throne.
He hath said concerning that which He willeth: “Verily, I am the Essence whereupon no name nor thing can fall, and I am the Gate of Remission, and there is no strength nor power save in God, the Most High, the Most Great.” But out of mercy unto thee, I shall inform thee as one well-informed. Verily, that matter is the very Reality concerning which Kumayl inquired of ʿAli—peace be upon him: For in the first year there appeared the unveiling of the Splendors of Majesty without allusion; in the second, the second; in the third, the third; in the fourth, the fourth; and in the fifth, a Light shone forth from the Dawn of Pre-Eternity upon the forms of Divine Unity, revealing its traces.
Yet it is a test for you, and a fleeting provision for a time appointed. Extinguish, then, the lamp, for the Sun of Reality hath reached the point of its zenith. Say: Glorified be the Lord of the angels and of the Spirit! Thus was a wall set between them wherein is a gate—its inner side containeth mercy, and its outer side, facing them, torment. And as to the Surah of Unity—its secret is one thousand and two and two hundred and one—Lord! Consider the number of His saying “with a wall” (bi-sur), for it is fifteen; and “God” (Allah) is sixty-five; and “Lord” (Rabb) is in the number of tarab—which itself alludeth to the Surah of Unity. And unto this point referreth that which hath been sent down.
For in the Du’aʾ al-ʿAsharat after the ranks of the tens, there are seventeen levels; and each one is a unity among the manifestations of Divine Oneness. Fourteen of these are the Imams of the unseen and of the seen. And His saying—peace be upon Him—“O God! Deal with me as Thou art worthy” is equal to sixty-five, while “Āmin, Āmin” is he who fulfilled his covenant—peace be upon them both and upon their Imams until the Day of Resurrection. The seventeenth is the Surah of Unity.
And the proof of this lieth in the Book of God: for the verse of tahlil—“There is no God but God”—hath been revealed in the Qur’an but thirty-four times, even as the Imam declared in his supplication on the Day of ʿArafah. Refer to it, read it, and in the end say: God! There is no God but He; take thou Him as thy Guardian.
Before the “stroke” is the letter Qaf—By the glorious Qur’an!—and after it is Nun—By the Pen and what they inscribe! And if thou add six to it—counting what hath come from the presence of God—thou shalt behold the House of Unity itself, and the Word of God shall be made manifest: Blessed be the Name of thy Lord, the Lord of Glory and of Bounty!
Then recite the Prayer of Qaf, for it pertaineth to His station. Verily the Resurrection hath come to pass, and that Day with thy Lord is as fifty thousand years. Then read the Prayer of Light and pause at “the All-Compelling”, then the Dawn Prayer and pause at “the Everlasting Sovereign”—1150 aspirations—and add to it one. Know thou through the all-embracing Form which is the very truth of certitude in the knowledge of certitude, and reckon from alif to nun in the abjad—there wilt thou see the number 400, and verily He is the Knower of all things hidden. Then thy Lord arose in Ahmad, and her Lord thereafter, and thy Lord in this.
Then read the Sermon of the Gulf and pause at His words “that thou mayest behold Him Who conversed with Moses from the Tree, manifest, unveiled, and described.” Then read the Sermon of Ghadir and of Friday at the explanation of the striking, then read the Prayer of Adilih at His words “verily death is truth” etc., for the Reality is in His exalted words “Ha Mim Ayn Sin Qaf [=278]. Remember thy Lord, the Merciful, in the number of the renowned year, and the All-Wise in that which is concealed. Dwell in the land of ya and thou shalt find Him, for He is the Truth and He is the Sanctuary.”
Guard thou the mystery of God, for it was made manifest in the year sixty. Put thy trust in God, turn away from the ignorant ones, and say: Praise be to God, the Lord of all worlds.

title: BB00094: Kitabu’l-’Ulama II
text:
Part 1: “Glorified be He before Whom all within…”
In the name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy
Glorified be He before Whom all within the heavens and earth fall prostrate, and we are all prostrators before Him. Glorified be He Whom all within the heavens and earth and whatsoever lieth between them praise, and we are all devoutly obedient unto Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him. He giveth life and causeth death, then causeth death and giveth life, and verily He is the Ever-Living Who dieth not. Within His grasp lieth the dominion of all things. He createth what He willeth through His command “Be!” and it is. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, the Almighty, the Self-Subsisting, and that this is the true Promised One of Whom ye were foretold.
And further: There is no doubt that we and you seek after truth, yet we have found no path thereto save through those signs of God which render impotent all the learned. This is what establisheth our religion from aforetime, and according to what hath been established between us and you, if discourse be not equitable with what God hath revealed in the Book, then whoso desireth to take a path unto God shall not act upon it.
We have indeed heard what was decreed concerning the appearance of Muhammad, peace be upon Him and His family. There is no doubt that the appearance of the Mahdi is identical with the appearance of Muhammad in the eyes of those who look unto the Point of the Cause. Nay, it is identical with all whom God hath sent as Prophets, for all are created by God’s command. This is the Origin of the Cause, which hath no beginning, unto the End that hath no end, and all stand firm through it. The similitude of this is as the sun: all souls are as mirrors which, when facing it, find within themselves the sun’s reflection as it appeareth unto them according to their capacity from their Lord. Thus all proceed from the sun. And all who are sent forth are none other than what hath been sent. This is God’s command—a single creation through which all are created, all are sustained, all die, and all live.
In every Revelation He raiseth up what He willeth and abaseth what He desireth. He desireth naught save what God, His Lord, desireth, and willeth naught save what God, thy Lord, hath willed in the Book. Thus doth God detail His signs that ye may understand and believe. This is the meaning of the tradition which ye all remember:
Thus shall ye behold all, for each hath begun from that Tree and unto it shall return. This is God’s command by which all stand firm.
The people are as dead, knowing not, thinking they are in God’s religion while they have departed from it just as they entered it, yet they perceive not. Had they known Him, none who remained from Adam’s religion and before Adam unto that which hath no beginning would have been veiled from Him, for such a one would surely turn unto God, his Lord. But having been veiled, he was not in that day among the believers.
Similarly, whoso was patient during the Dispensation of the Qur’an yet believed not in God and His signs deemed himself to be acting in God’s good pleasure, yet his knowledge encompassed not that whereof God had testified. Thus in that day are all tried. No soul acteth save that it desireth to act for God, yet God beareth witness concerning it only through those who believe in Him. Thus in that day do they abide in God’s good pleasure.
And He Whom God shall make manifest at the age of thirty, after a thousand years have passed—it cannot be less than this, nor is what hath been decreed what ye imagine. He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden. This is the Sun of the Divine Will—whenever it riseth or setteth by God’s leave, it is but one Sun. Be not veiled by the proofs whereby ye strive, for this is established by the word of him whom God made a witness unto the Messenger after Him, for he confirmeth what God bestowed upon him of prophethood and the Book through what was revealed unto him of signs which ye now behold.
Therefore, lighten from yourselves what ye love in God’s religion, for God is indeed independent of what ye do. Were ye to spend all that is on earth, ye could neither add nor subtract a single letter from the religion. But God doeth what He willeth. Know ye the value of your days, for when the sun setteth ye shall find no path unto it until the Day of Resurrection, and ye shall be in night.
Follow ye all that which ye attribute to the Truth, for it hath been fulfilled through the Word of God. Such was the beginning of the Cause—how then do ye not fear? There is no way for you to believe in the Qur’an except that ye believe in the Bayan, and it is the same whether ye believe or believe not. Would any among you be content to say at this time “I follow the religion of Jesus”? If not, then how can ye be content to follow that which ye now follow? That which Jesus—peace be upon Him—revealed of religion was from God; this became the religion of Muhammad in His Manifestation, and this became the religion of your Qa’im in His Manifestation. God desireth to lighten your religion for you, that ye may give thanks unto God in the days of your Lord and be among those who are certain in the religion of God.
The relief that hath come to you is that which God hath bestowed, in that He hath manifested a Servant and given Him clear proofs from His presence, even as He gave unto Muhammad aforetime. No other proof is needed on that Day, and this sufficeth the believers, even as was revealed aforetime in a mighty Book:
If relief consisted in sovereignty and power, or knowledge of the Qur’an and various branches of learning, then from the time of the Apostle of God until today, all these have been possessed by the believers, both Sunni and Shi’ih. Nay, relief is that God should raise up a Proof and give Him such evidence that all are powerless before it, even as He gave to Muhammad, the Apostle of God, and today the Qur’an is His proof and none other in the eyes of all the community. Why do ye veil yourselves with matters of knowledge, or practice, or sovereignty, or glory, when there is no doubt that day and night ye act according to what ye believe to be truth, yet have caused the matter to become doubtful to your own selves, just as at the time of the Manifestation of the Truth, the previous community remained veiled by this same doubt, and while thinking they remained faithful to God, they remained in the fire?
And now when relief is manifest, why should it be that in Islam today two sovereigns rule in the name of Islam in Turkey and Persia, and countless divines give rulings in this name, yet remain veiled from Him in whom Islam is confirmed, while His proof is manifest? He hath designated nothing as proof save verses, and if anyone today were to reflect, he would know that this hath been and is the greatest of miracles, though all were heedless of what they saw in the Qur’an: “Say: ʿIf mankind and the jinn were to combine…”’ They marveled at this. Indeed, had any other than God revealed it, it would have been impossible, for from the Mission until the beginning of this Manifestation, one thousand two hundred and sixty years passed and none came forth to produce the like of the Qur’an. And now that One hath come, there is no doubt that He is from God.
It is evident that were He not from God, it would have been necessary for God, the Powerful, the All-Knowing, the All-Seeing, to repel Him by whatever means, even as He saith in His glorious utterance:
Or else He would have raised up a proof from Himself who would produce better than it or the like thereof. And since during these five years respite hath been granted from the Lord, the Powerful, the truth of this Cause hath been established, even as by this same proof the prophethood of the Prophet is now established, and not by aught else such as successive transmission and the like, for successive transmission benefiteth not the deniers, such as the People of the Book.

title: BB00094: Kitabu’l-’Ulama II
text:
“When the Qa’im appeareth by His Lord’s leave, then from Adam unto Muhammad ye shall behold all that ye love to see in a Prophet whom ye follow.”









“Is it not enough for them that We have sent down unto thee the Book which is recited unto them? Verily, in this is a mercy and a reminder for people who believe.”





“And if he had fabricated against Us some statements, We would assuredly have seized him by the right hand, and would assuredly have cut his life-vein.”

title: BB00094: Kitabu’l-’Ulama II
section: Part 2: “From the beginning of the Manifestation until now…”
text:
Part 2: “From the beginning of the Manifestation until now…”
From the beginning of the Manifestation until now, day by day it hath spread and become more widely known, and in no wise hath any deficiency appeared therein, nor shall it appear, for “God will perfect His light, though the polytheists be averse.” And whatever objection is raised against this will likewise be raised against the prophethood of the Prophet. Therefore, ye must needs either accept this Cause or renounce your religion and deny the authority of the Qur’an. And if anyone could write, He would reveal in His presence, night and day, within four days, that which was revealed in twenty-four years, and there is no doubt that this is the Expected One whose name is the Truth, for none other than Him has been or is capable of revealing the verses of God.
Thus in every Dispensation He appears with a name, and this is none other than Muhammad, the Messenger of God, Who has appeared on the Day of Resurrection through the Manifestation of God. From the beginning of the Qur’an to its end there is no mention more great than this, and His meeting is the meeting with God, for meeting the Ancient Essence is impossible. Whatever is mentioned in the Qur’an about meeting God refers to meeting that Reality, which God has attributed to meeting with Himself as an honor, just as He has called the Ka’bah His House. He is the Expected One Who will renew the ordinances and traditions, and He is the One of Whom the blessed Sadiq—peace be upon Him—said that three hundred and thirteen people will become unbelievers and will flee, then return after the Cause becomes most difficult.
Why have they not pondered this, and how their deeds performed day and night, supposedly for God’s sake, will suddenly become void? Just as the appearance of His Holiness was considered the lesser resurrection, from its magnitude and the thunderstruck state of all who are in the heavens and earth and what lies between them, it became manifest how all descended to the realm of unbelief. Why do they not reflect upon the traditions?
Have they not seen the tradition of Azerbaijan in the thirteenth volume of Biharu’l-Anvar:

“Azerbaijan is inevitable for us. Nothing can withstand it. When this happens, remain in your homes and stay where we stay. When one moves, hasten to him even if you must crawl. It is as though I see him between the Corner and the Station, while people are pledging allegiance to him, and he accepts from them only that he shall rule among them with new laws.”

(narrated in meaning)
Likewise in the mentioned book are traditions regarding the imprisonment of the Master of this Cause, and also the tradition of Mufaddal who asked how the beginning of this Cause and its first appearance would be. He replied that He will appear in a state of confusion until His Cause becomes manifest and His mention is exalted among the people. Then He will be called by name, lineage, and title among the people, by hearing which the proof will be complete for all the world. And likewise the tradition:

“When our Qa’im rises in Khurasan… and when our Qa’im rises in Gilan…”

And likewise the passing of signs they foretold, such as the splitting of the Euphrates, the collapse of the wall of Kufih, the killing of the people of Egypt by their leader, the locusts, the two plagues, the Dajjal, the black standards from Khurasan, the killing of the Pure Soul—may my spirit and all within my Lord’s knowledge be sacrificed for him—and the killing of the Hasani, the eclipse of the sun and moon, and thus occurred the signs which the noble Prince—may my spirit and all within my Lord’s knowledge be sacrificed for him—mentions in his collection:
O my sons, when the Turks surge forth, then await The guardianship of a Mahdi who shall arise and do justice And the kingdom of earth from the House of Hashim shall be humbled And one of them who takes pleasure and jests shall receive allegiance A youth among youths with no judgment Neither serious nor reasonable Then shall arise from among you the True Qa’im Who shall give you truth and act with truth Named after God’s Prophet, my soul his ransom So fail him not, O my sons, and make haste!
O sanctified ones, be fair to yourselves and your followers, fear the Day when leg shall be wrapped around leg, [Q68:42] and the Day when the keepers of Hell shall ask: “Did there not come to you a warner?” And they shall say: “Yes indeed! A warner came to us, but we rejected him and said: ʿGod has not sent down anything—you are only in great error.”’
Consider and observe how if someone among you claims “I saw the Promised One in a dream last night,” how much respect you accord that person. If they say “I saw him standing in such-and-such place,” you make it a shrine and show reverence. Yet I know not what has transpired that now, with such clear proofs and speaking evidences, you do not even consider the possibility that this could be the Awaited One himself (may my spirit and all within God’s knowledge be sacrificed for him). Not only do you fail to obey, but see how you treat that noble one and his companions—he himself imprisoned while his followers are all scattered.
The traditions of the Family of the Prophet have been fulfilled completely, including where they said that when He appears, the clergy of my community will wage war against Him, inflicting upon Him the same persecution inflicted upon the Messenger of God, because they interpret God’s word according to their false beliefs and fight against Him, joining the ranks of sun-worshippers and moon-worshippers.
My dear one, beware lest you be among those to whom this tradition applies. Be not proud of your knowledge nor confident in your deeds. Many a deed thought to be for God’s pleasure was not, and many an act believed to be truth was falsehood. Yes, if one realizes while acting that it is against God’s pleasure, no truth is wronged. But at that very moment the proof had been completed against him, “and they rejected them, though their souls were convinced thereof.” This applied to him, but being proud of his own truth, he was destroyed without realizing it. Just as there were believers in God’s Messenger in Islam who became proofs against other believers, though this time God has manifested differently such that every person of keen insight everywhere has become a Babi.
Indeed, we have seen in the writings that if there were other than the 313 chiefs, they would gather. Now all believers in the Qur’an await the Mahdi of the family of Muhammad (peace be upon him), with none of them imagining they would fail to believe in him, just as the believers in the Spirit of God (Jesus) who awaited Ahmad the Messenger of God could not imagine he would come and they would not believe, yet this is what happened and is evident. There is no doubt this is the Promised Manifestation mentioned in countless traditions, to the point where they said “until one who splits a hair into two strands emerges, until none remain except us and our followers”—and all has appeared. Had they followed truth, all the benefits they perceived in this world would have been theirs until now and nothing would have been lost to them. Just as if the Sultan of Islam had aided truth and all the believers, all they had intended and sought in this world would have multiplied until now.
Even now the past can be compensated and tested—if it does not multiply they can return, and their religious law would not be invalidated. Now each looks out of fear for their position until it reached where it has reached, such that the pen is ashamed to mention it. Yet at the appearance all the Family of the Prophet and those of pure faith returned, and all that was seen in traditions about them has appeared, as the discerning one understands.
But even today what was lost can be rectified, for with the Lord of Command there is nothing but one pardon—by this they are pardoned until the Day of Resurrection. From the Source of Command there is but one punishment—by this they are deprived of every good until the Day of Resurrection.
