Despair not of God’s mercy, but enter with those who enter and be among the believers. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.

title: BB00460: Tawbat-namih (authenticity disputed)
text:
(A facsimile of the handwriting of His Holiness the Primal Point, addressed to Nasir al-Din Shah during the period of his heir-apparency in Tabriz, wherein a written reply was set forth to the divines:)
May my spirit be sacrificed for Thee! Praise be to God, as befitteth Him and as He deserveth, for He hath made His grace and mercy in all conditions to encompass all His servants. So praise be unto Him, again praise be unto Him, that He hath made one such as Your Highness to be the fountainhead of His grace and mercy, that through the manifestation of His kindness, forgiveness is granted to His servants, wrongdoers are sheltered, and mercy is shown to supplicants.
I bear witness before God and those in His presence that this weak servant hath no purpose contrary to the good-pleasure of the Lord of the World and those who possess His authority. Although my very existence is absolute sin, yet since my heart is steadfast in the unity of God, exalted be His remembrance, in the prophethood of His Messenger, and in the authority of those who possess His authority, and my tongue confesseth all that hath been revealed from God, I have hope in His mercy and have never desired aught contrary to His good-pleasure. And if words have flowed from my pen contrary to His good-pleasure, my intent was not disobedience, and in all conditions I seek His forgiveness and repent before Him.
This servant hath no knowledge whatsoever that would warrant any claim. I seek forgiveness from God, my Lord, and turn unto Him from any suggestion that any Cause be attributed to me. Certain prayers and words that have flowed from my tongue do not indicate any Cause, and whoever claims specific deputyship of the Proof of God, peace be upon Him, is a false pretender. This servant hath made no such claim, nor any other claim. I beseech the favors of His Imperial Majesty and Your Highness that you would honor this supplicant with your royal favors and benevolence, your grace and mercy. Peace be upon you.
(The originals of these two epistles, together with a number of other official communications which are herein included, were—after the deposition of Muhammad-ʿAli Shah, when the organs of government passed into the hands of the nationalists—photographed by one of the historical researchers and made public.)

title: BB00165: Sharh-i-Du’a’-i-Sabah I
text:
Part 1: “Praise be to God, Who, by His command…”
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate
Praise be to God, Who, by His command and out of no thing, hath brought into being the atoms of all that exist, that the tongues of all possible beings might attest to that whereunto God hath borne witness unto Himself by Himself, in the ranks of Command and of Creation; that every limit might recognize the effulgences of the station of the Divine Theophanies in the tokens of the Names and Attributes before the dawning of the Presence of the Divine Essence.
And praise be to God, Who hath devised all inventions in the station wherein the ultimate ends of Command and the seals of consummation are revealed, in accordance with what He hath willed in the mystery of essential realities, in the mention of identities, in the ordinance of beings, and in the decree concerning the souls—yea, and what God hath willed beyond these stations, in the indications of Lahut and the degrees of Jabarut and the signs of Mulk and Malakut, and the finalities of Command in the manifestations of Nasut—to the end that all may learn the rulings of all things from their beginnings unto their endings, and thereafter whatsoever God hath willed beyond such allusions, of infinity upon infinity, and of what no one’s knowledge can encompass save God. Verily, there is none other God but He, the All-Glorious, the Most Exalted.
O God, I call Thee to witness, in this day of Friday, by that wherewith Thou dost bear witness unto Thyself in every affair, that Thou art God, the One, the Single. Thou hast ever been—there was naught with Thee—and Thou shalt forever be even as Thou hast been. Nothing that pertaineth to Thy degree hath been commemorated in any matter; for Thy essential identity is cut off from the station of comprehension, and Thy ipseity severeth beings from the station of exposition. Never hath any save Thee known Thy Essence, nor is it possible, in the realm of Thy origination, that aught attain thereto; for in the primal eternity Thou wast the Describer of Thyself and the Unifier of Thine Essence in every affair, without change and without decay.
Thou art the Self-Subsisting One Whom eyes perceive not; to Thee the highest-flying birds of hearts and thoughts may never ascend. Glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou! If I say, “Thine Essence pointeth to Thy Essence,” and “Thy beingness maketh known Thy beingness,” and “Thine essential oneness uniteth Thine essential oneness,” I do but testify to the signs of Thy invention, the manifestations of Thy devising, and the tokens of Thy origination. And if I say, “Thou art Thou,” the similitude speaketh, in the station of origination, of majesty—yet Thou, O my God, art exalted above being known by similitudes or described by the verses of magnificence. And if I say, “Thou art He,” the Oneness denoteth the very essence of Thy Will, and Lordship the beingness of Thy Purpose; and even as they are, they signify only severance and bespeak but interdiction. Glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou! I perceive no path, nor find I any mention that might serve as proof.
Wherefore, having borne witness to the stations of my impotence, and having returned, after my ascent unto Thee, with the empty palm of my poverty and despairing of my nearness, I commune with Thee in this tongue, invoking Muhammad and His Trustees—peace be upon them—that the remembrance of them may still my heart, and that my secret and my open parts may find repose in confessing their right.
I entreat Thee, O my God, by that wherewith Thou art invested of majesty and Lahut, of power and Jabarut, that Thou wouldst send Thy blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad by Thy wondrous manifestations and Thy ancient signs, and by whatsoever Thou art bringing forth in every affair—whereof none hath knowledge save Thee. Verily, Thou art God, the All-Glorious, the Bestower.
And now, in this my station, I bear witness that there is no God but Thee, alone, without partner—by that wherewith Thou dost bear witness unto Thyself and Thy very Essence acknowledgeth Thy right—even though I am unable to comprehend its ruling or to taste the sweetness of its knowledge. Glory be to Thee! By Thee have I known Thee; by Thyself have I confessed Thy unity; by Thy summons hath my soul ascended unto the court of Thy holiness and the sanctuary of Thy might; and but for Thee I had been as naught, unable to know how Thou art.
Glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou! By Thy might and Thy majesty, I bear witness for myself only to sin; and I know that whatsoever sin acquiseth is, before Thee, but sin. How then shall my soul find rest, after my knowledge of my transgressions? By Thy might! Wert Thou to chastise me with the eternity of everlastingness, by the permanence of Thine Essence, with all Thy vengeance and Thy might; wert Thou to make whatsoever Thy knowledge encompasseth within space a fire, and then to enlarge my body until none should fill this earth save I alone—by Thy glory, Thou wouldst still be praised in Thy deed and obeyed in the sovereignty of Thy majesty. And I, for my part, should be but deserving thereby of the recompense of my deeds before Thee.
How then shall the decree be, whether Thou judgest by justice or callest through bounty? This is a matter under which the heavens and the earth would well-nigh be weighed down! Glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou! By Thy might, there is no refuge for me but unto Thee; no salvation for any soul save through Thy grace; nor can any intercede with Thee except by Thy leave.
Sanctified art Thou and exalted! If I mention Thee as Thou hast described Thyself, Thy justice and Thy beginningless decree make me to fear; and if I fall silent before the city of Thy all-bountiful mercy, the manner of Thy dealing with the believers among Thy servants and the sinners among Thy creatures maketh me yearn. Glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou! Thou art the One, the Self-Subsisting: Thou doest continually what Thou willest, as Thou wilt. None can turn back Thy command, nor can any reverse Thy words. Verily, Thou art God, the All-Glorious, the Bestower.
And I bear witness that Muhammad—peace be upon Him—is Thy servant, whom Thou didst choose, in the broad expanse of pre-eternity, above all that Thou hast brought forth and devised; for in His station He desired none but Thee and the path of Thy love. Thou didst make Him, in every degree, the locus of Thy power and Thy might in decree and judgment, in origination and fulfilment, for Thou wert ever knowing the ordinance of all things in the heavens and on the earth.
I therefore beseech Thee, O my God, to cause to descend upon Him, in this very hour, Thy wondrous bounties and Thy ancient signs, and whatsoever Thou dost merit at the time of bestowal. Verily, Thou art the All-Glorious, the Most Exalted.
And I bear witness, before Thee, concerning His Trustees—may Thy blessings rest upon them—that they are the pillars of Thy unity, the tokens of Thy sanctity, the manifestations of Thy oneness, and the effulgences of Thy mercy; the sites of Thy command, such as Thou Thyself hast testified for them in the knowledge of the unseen. Thou hast made them the station of Thy Self in all the worlds, and hast ascribed whatsoever is ascribed unto them unto Thy presence, that none may doubt in any matter regarding their majesty, but that all may confess their virtue, even as Thou didst ordain for them in Thy knowledge. Verily, Thou art the Lord of mighty favour.
And I bear witness, O my God, unto my own self, to the supreme affliction and the grievous trespasses which Thy knowledge hath encompassed and Thy Book reckoneth. Nay, I know that my very existence is sin itself—how then when I acquire sin upon sin? Wherefore I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thy bounty, to vouchsafe unto me perfect severance unto the pinnacle of Thy holiness, and entrance upon the carpet of Thy might, that I may find no sweetness but in nearness unto Thee, nor recognize any affair save Thy oneness; that I may be conjoined with the mine of grandeur, the mystery of identity, the token of oneness, and the light of self-subsistence which Thou hast ordained for all possible things in the realm of Thy invention and the theatre of Thy devising—so that, in every affair, I may act according to that whereunto Thou callest me in secret and lovest for me in the open. Verily, Thou art the Lord of pardon and bounty; naught in heaven or on earth overburdeneth Thee. Thou, indeed, art the All-Glorious, the All-Forgiving.
And I entreat Thee, O my God, in this very hour of this festival-day, to forgive me and those who have followed Thy command and have not shown enmity toward me before the dawning of the splendour of Thy Presence; and judge between me and those who have borne witness against me and disputed my right, according to what is meet for Thee and within Thy power. Verily, Thou art God, from Whose knowledge nothing in the heavens or on the earth is concealed; and Thou art the All-Glorious, the Most Exalted.

title: BB00165: Sharh-i-Du’a’-i-Sabah I
section: Part 2: “Before the august threshold—may God preserve…”
text:
Part 2: “Before the august threshold—may God preserve…”
Before the august threshold—may God preserve it through His love and through his fair deeds until the Day of Return—this is a clarification of what was asked of me concerning the meaning of his word, peace be upon him, in the Du’a’ al-Sabah: “O Thou Who hast made Thyself known by Thyself.” Behold, I now set the Pen in motion to manifest what God hath deposited in the frame of being, bringing it forth to open view, that the lights which God created in the realities of possibility, in the rank of man, may be beheld.
Know that the knowledge of the Essence of the Eternal—glorified be He—is impossible for contingent being; for, as He is, there was none with Him to unite Him, and naught is mentioned in any rank until it be known. All allusions from all souls revert to the station of His origination, speak of the degree of His devising, and point—by the closing of the way and the forbidding of proof—away from knowledge of the manifestations of His theophanies; for knowledge is a branch of conjunction.
Access unto the station of finding in the world of vision is by the self-disclosure of God unto each thing according to its measure, in the degrees of Command and the consummations of the Seal. And since God knew that within the realm of the contingent the comprehension of the inmost reality of His Essence is impossible, He originated signs for the appearance of the knowledge of Him in the horizons and within the souls, and He made the recognition of those signs to be naught but those very signs themselves; for true knowledge is not attained save by the thing itself. He who would know the colour red—were he to know it by the colour white—would not have truly known it; the reality of a thing is not known but by itself.
Thus the Imam said: “Know God by God.” And Ali, peace be upon him, declared: “O Thou Who hast made Thyself known by Thyself.” And Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon him, in his supplication for Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, saith: “By Thee have I known Thee; Thou hast guided me unto Thee and summoned me unto Thee; and but for Thee I had not known what Thou art.” This is the loftiest of the degrees of knowledge attainable by contingent being and the portion of existent things, above which, in the realm of possibility, there lieth no higher station.
In the subtlety of His workmanship and the greatness of His grace, God hath placed the signs of His knowledge within the realities of souls and horizons, as He hath indicated in His mighty Book: “We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves, until it become manifest unto them that He is the Truth.” Were the splendours of Majesty and the allusions to be unveiled from the court of the sanctity of the token of the Essence, they would perceive the station which God hath deposited within their realities; to this pointeth the saying of al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, in al-Misbah: “Servitude is a jewel whose essence is Lordship; that which is hidden in Lordship is attained in servitude, and that which is lost in servitude is found in Lordship.”
God, exalted be He, hath said: “We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it become manifest unto them that He is the Truth,” that is: He is found in thine absence and thy presence. When thou turnest unto God, the veils, allusions, degrees, and signs are lifted, and thou knowest the indication of His self-manifestations—Essence by Essence. Even as the Word “There is none other God but God” pointeth to the oneness of God—albeit it is created within God’s kingdom—so too is the token of thy very reality an indication of God, though created; the pre-eternal mystery lieth hidden in thy rank, the divine light in thy beingness, and the self-subsisting splendour in thine essential identity. Thereby dost thou confess His unity and know Him; and no soul within possibility can tread the path of knowledge save by the knowledge of that station and the movement through those degrees deposited within souls and horizons.
In this station have the feet of the wise slipped; for they have supposed, in the ranks of their unities and the tokens of their abstractions, that they have attained unto the pure Essence. This, in the creed of the People of Infallibility—peace be upon them—is unbelief. They adduce, as proof, the saying of al-Husayn, peace be upon him, on the Day of ʿArafah:

“Hath aught other than Thee any manifestation not Thine, that it should be the one to manifest Thee? When wast Thou absent that Thou shouldst need a proof to guide unto Thee? When wert Thou distant that the traces should be those that lead to Thee? Blind be the eye that beholdeth Thee not while Thou art ever watching over it! Ruined the bargain of the servant who appointed for himself no share of Thy love!”

Assuredly they have not grasped the true intent, nor gazed upon the station of origination with the light of the heart. By my spirit—and by all who dwell in the kingdoms of Command and Creation—he meant naught thereby but the vision of His self-manifestation—exalted be His remembrance—the station wherein He revealed Himself to him by Himself; not the vision of the Essence nor arrival thereunto, for that is impossible within the realm of possibility. Doth not the Greatest Master—may the blessings of God be upon Him and His House—confess: “We have not known Thee as is Thy due, nor worshipped Thee as is Thy due”?
The very saying of al-Husayn, upon which the philosophers have relied, and the Qur’anic verses and the words of them of insight—these are plain to whoso considereth the traces and looketh upon the utterances of the people of exposition. Among them are the explicit words of ʿAli, peace be upon him, in the Khutbah al-Tatanjiyyah: “I beheld God and Paradise with the eye of vision,” and in another place: “I worship not a Lord whom I do not see.” None can doubt that his—may my spirit be a ransom for him and for them that abide in the kingdom of names and attributes—intent was the rank of the theophany, that God revealed Himself unto him thereby in the stations which God had decreed for him. This is witnessed at thy sublime threshold when the veils are rent from before the heart.
By the knowledge of this station all contradictions among certain men of learning and contention are lifted, when the servant beholdeth the lights of majesty in the realities of origin and return. If thou hast comprehended this exposition, know then that this noble clause hath a meaning which none knoweth save God and whomsoever He willeth; it speaketh of the station of its Speaker and pointeth to the exaltation of the degree of His identity. None among existent things hath apprehended its meaning as He—may my spirit be a sacrifice unto Him—intended; for He standeth at the station of true unity, in the rank of the pliant alif, after Muhammad, the Messenger of God—may God bless Him and His family—at the station of the Point. None encompasseth the knowledge of this save whom God willeth. All that we have made known unto thee in these allusions is but a mode of the inner meanings of that noble clause.
As for the outward path, it is manifest at thy presence; for “whoso knoweth his self knoweth his Lord.” Even as the self is not known by aught else, so is the decree in the knowledge of the Essence and in the appearance of the stations of manifestation within the kingdom of names and attributes.
And here I stay the Pen from its course; for the oceans of possibility suffice not to convey the meanings of that noble clause. I beg God’s forgiveness, out of His bounty—and from the keen-sighted observer I beg pardon for what hath flowed from my Pen. My very existence is sin—how then when I add sin unto sin? Glorified be God, the Lord of the Throne, above that which they ascribe unto Him! And I verily say as God hath sent down in the Qur’an:

“Peace be upon the Messengers; and praise be to God, the Lord of all worlds.”

title: BB00061: Sharh-i-Du’a’-i-Sabah II
text:
Part 1: “Praise be to God Who brought into being…”
In the Name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate
Praise be to God Who brought into being whatsoever is in the heavens and on earth by His command, and Who judges between all with justice on the Day when all shall be gathered unto God. And praise be to God Who originated all created things from nothing and without any prior model, and Who invented all inventions in forms of His choosing without any precedent, such that the realities of essential beings cry out in praise of Him Who manifested Himself to the Divine Will at the moment of their existence, and the essences of abstract beings are stirred by the glory of Him Who distinguished the Divine Purpose after their acceptance, until all bore witness in the station of recognition of the Pure Essence and the Pristine Source to that which He testified of His own Self by His own Self, and described thereafter to His servants that there is no God but Him, alone with no partner, in the eternity of eternities, and that He was the Living, the Self-Subsisting before the appearance in existence of the decree of creation, and that He shall remain as He is after the passing of all things without any attribute of transition.
Glorified and exalted is He! He has transcended in the loftiness of His Being above all height, and is sanctified in the holiness of His Essence above all elevation. Whosoever claims to understand His unity as He has unified His Essence has claimed the station of the impossible and has associated partners in the station of his own self through severance. And whosoever claims to know His Being has veiled himself from the station of the manifestation of His presence, for his self-existence severs essential realities from the station of knowledge, and his individuality blocks material things from the station of expression.
There is no way to know Him except through what He has revealed to creation through creation, by extending to them from nothing according to their capacity to receive, and rewarding them according to His all-encompassing knowledge of them. Verily, there is no God but He, the Mighty, the Exalted.
And believe thou, with thy whole heart, in the station of the First Effulgence of the Absolute Outpouring—Muhammad, may the blessings of God rest upon Him and upon His kindred—His servant, Whom He drew forth for Himself from the vast expanse of pre-eternity, and chose from the loftiest heights of creation for His love, and accepted from the sublime realm of origination for His knowledge, and elected from the hidden mystery of invention for His sovereignty; in such wise that He established no distinction between Him and His Manifestation, save only the reality of servitude. And He made Him, by reason of the exaltedness of His own station and His sanctity above association with created things, to be the seat of His creative power, that He might render unto every possessor of a right his due, by His command. Wherefore may God’s blessings be upon Him, so long as the birds of the unseen do warble, and the dove of the concourse of Names doth coo, and the peacock of the kingdom of Attributes doth spread his plumes—yea, beyond all that none can comprehend save God alone. Verily He is the Mighty, the Most Exalted.
And be thou assured of the station of the Manifestations of that Absolute Outpouring—whatsoever God hath ordained for them in the knowledge of the Most Holy—for He hath made them the successors of His Apostle, the pillars of His unity, the trustees of His Revelation, His chosen ones among His servants, the interpreters of His signs, and the exponents of His Names and His Attributes. Send down, O God, Thy blessings upon them, according to the glory, the dominion, the power, and the divinity which are Thine, and according to that bestowal which Thy worthiness requireth. Verily Thou art God, the Most Generous, the Bestower.
And acknowledge thou, in the stations wherein the traces of that Absolute Outpouring appear, what God hath willed for them in the realm of Names and Attributes; inasmuch as God hath appointed them, in the station of bounty, to be single signs, and, in the station of justice, to be manifestations of oneness—so that He hath linked … their obedience with obedience unto His friends, and their recognition with recognition of His chosen ones, and their disobedience with disobedience unto His trusted ones. And raise thou no distinction between them and their Imams, within the sanctuary of the heart, save only the rank of bringing into being within the degrees of their acceptance; for they point in no matter save through them, nor speak in any station save on their behalf. Wherefore may God’s blessings be upon them, so long as the light of the morn of pre-eternity shineth upon the entire temple of contingent existence. There is none other God but Him, the Generous, the Bountiful.
And now, after I had, through constraint, set foot in the land of Tabriz—by reason of the irrevocable decree pronounced by the Sovereign Judge, the Chosen One—there was asked of the Siyyid Abu’l-Hasan, son of the honored Siyyid Ali Zunuzi (may God forgive them both, encompassed as they are by His all-embracing knowledge), that I should expound the mystery of the Morning Prayer transmitted from Ali. I answered him with such reply as befitted, according to what I then knew of him as one of the people of love. And now, in the midst of the mountains, I have not fulfilled what I promised, by bringing forth into open view that which God had veiled within the realm of being. No power and no might is there save in God, the Exalted, the All-Bountiful.
Know that were the seas of the heavens and earth to become ink, they would be exhausted before the meanings of a single letter of that prayer could be fully revealed, even if one were to quote God’s words “though We brought the like thereof in aid.” There is no doubt that the measure of every person’s words corresponds to their station. Just as no one knows his station except God and His Messenger, as declared by God’s Messenger, the same applies to this prayer. No one has access to its understanding, for it speaks of the stations of expression of the Bayan, the meanings, the Gates, and the Imamate. One may say none knows it as it truly is except Him, for He is the Mighty, the Exalted.
There is no doubt that when its Speaker was in the station of “We are He and He is We,” the same applies to its manifestation in this prayer, as though He Himself were speaking these very words before the Qur’an. This is by God’s command—He teaches it to whomsoever He wishes among His servants, for He is the Generous, the Bestower.
Likewise is the judgment regarding the station which al-Sadiq described in the tradition of excellence as the House of Light and the Garments of Manifestation, saying “Neither is it Him nor other than Him.” Understand what We have made known to you, for that is the spirit in the prayer—thy Lord bestows His mercy on whom He pleases, and God is the Lord of great bounty.
As for Him to Whom I referred regarding His words—may my spirit and all in the kingdoms of command and creation be sacrificed for Him—He is in the station of limitation and the judgment of servitude. Otherwise, He is more sublime and greater than to be indicated by any near reference or proven by any distant proof. For its Speaker has described Himself in His words saying:
There is no power nor strength except through God, the Most High, the Great.
Even so doth the ordinance proceed in the Manifestation of God within the Prayer; and He possesseth a station upon which no name, no sign, no allusion, no form of worship can fall, nor can any comprehend how this may be, save God, His Lord. Verily He is the All-Powerful, the All-Glorious. I have apprehended, therefore, a glimmer of the majesty of the ancient Word of thy Lord. Know thou that every letter thereof hath seven stations—those stations which the Imam, in the realm of recognition, enjoined upon Jabir, when He said (exalted be His remembrance) unto the end of the tradition. And for each of these stations there are the four worlds, which in certain places are expressed as: the Lahut, which is the rank of the heart, and the first atom; the Jabarut, which is the station of the intellect, and the second; the Mulk, which is the station of the soul and the third scene, and the Word of tahlil; and the Malakut, which is the station of the Proof and the fourth scene, and the Word of takbir.
And all the takbir—yea, the whole of the takbir—doth run through these degrees. Each grade of these grades moveth within the chain of the eight, established among the people of truth; and when thou multipliest these numbers by themselves, there becometh for every letter two hundred and twenty-eight meanings—according to a decree that proceedeth beneath that all-embracing rule from which none among them that are endued with understanding can find escape, save by turning aside therefrom.
And as for me, were I to set forth, in recounting these grades, that which pertaineth to the first letter, none could bear it save whom God willeth. It is not for any soul to speak thereof apart from the Truth; for the proof and the argument are in my hand, clear as this sun in the midst of heaven. And if any one should transfer the names of a rank and its meanings into another rank, he would have committed associating partners in his station; for the least of association, as the Imam hath said, is that thou call a pebble a date-stone, and a date-stone a pebble—then dost thou persist therein. For this cause hath the recognition of those numbered grades, and their flowing beneath the divine rule, been made difficult unto hearts; though they move by the indication of the four and the three paths—paths which are the proof of wisdom, and fair admonition, and disputation in the manner that is best.
And were these seven to be struck within the number, there would appear for every letter of this Prayer one thousand five hundred and sixty-seven universal meanings—such as the Imam intended when He expounded it; nay rather, within the realm of possibility, whatever meaning may be possible for this Prayer, He intended it at the moment of its bringing into being. For nothing, in any condition, escapeth His knowledge; and the whole of existence, and its loftiness … through origination, is before Him as a shadow. I seek forgiveness of God for delimiting by “the many”; and by my life! were it not for my fear of the frailty of hearts and the remoteness of souls, I would not mention, in describing the words of thy Lord, that Master at Whose feet my spirit—and all who are in the kingdom of command and creation—would be a ransom.
Whenever bodies shudder at the hearing of them—hast thou not beheld thy Lord, how He lengtheneth the shadow? Had He so willed, He would have made it still; then did We make the sun to be a guide thereunto. Know thou, then, and ponder, O man of understanding; otherwise submit, that thou mayest be of them that have prospered.
And He—exalted be His remembrance—hath said: “O my God! O Thou Who hast caused the tongue of morning to speak with an utterance that ….” And that Spirit—may my life be offered up for His sake—intended, in this station of supplication, the turning of the face unto the pure Essence, unto Whom none is like, Who is joined with no thing, and Whom no thing can know as is His due; for “vision apprehendeth Him not, but He apprehendeth vision; and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.”
In the station of prayer, it is necessary to know five stations: the description, the described, then the description, that by which description occurs, and that to which description tends. These are five gates, the first of which cannot be known except through the last. In the terminology of the people of definition, these are the station of the Point, the soft Alif, then the extended one, then the letters, then the Word, which is the station of the ranks of the divine unity of the believers, as explained by the Shaykh, may God’s mercy be upon him, in the commentary on the Benefits.
It behooves the supplicant to behold none but the countenance of his Lord at the time of prayer, for if he finds himself or his desire while turning to his Lord, he has associated partners with his Master and has not truly turned in the station of prayer. This is the doctrine of the Christians, about whom God has said regarding their belief: “The Christians say: He is the third of three,” etc. Therefore, be conscious of God and flee unto His presence from the mention of anything other than His Essence in the station of His worship. This is difficult for the sincere ones except for whom God wills, for He is the Generous, the Bestower.
For this reason, God does not accept the prayers of most supplicants, nor are they answered, because they call upon what they do not know. When anyone calls upon God in this way, God answers immediately, for turning to God in true unity is greater than what the servant asks of his Lord. Prayer in that station is itself the answer, and therefore God has said: “Call upon Me; I will answer you.” There is no doubt that God’s promise is fulfilled.
When you have understood the laws of prayer, then be certain that everything in its rank glorifies its Lord, as the Qur’an has pronounced: “There is nothing that doth not celebrate His praise.” Reason indicates that the fruit of existence is the praise of the Worshipped One and nothing else. Therefore, the tongue of morning unfolds at every moment with praise of its Creator, and what is meant by morning is His station—may my spirit be His sacrifice—for the light of dawn has been realized from the light of the sun, and it is the light of the Eternal Dawn which has shed its effects upon the temples of all. And there is, in this respect, an obligation to acquaint thyself with the realities of those allusions, lest, when confronted with the forms of abstruse questions, the union of essences be imagined; for in that station it is known that the learned stand distinguished from the rest of the kindreds of men.

title: BB00061: Sharh-i-Du’a’-i-Sabah II
text: “I am the Meaning upon which no name or likeness falls, and I am the Gate of His Line.”

title: BB00061: Sharh-i-Du’a’-i-Sabah II
section: Part 2: “Know thou that the Point of Existence…”
text:
Part 2: “Know thou that the Point of Existence…”
Know thou that the Point of Existence, which is the station of the Absolute Effulgence and the rank of the radiant, unified Primal Will in the Muhammadan Presence, hath caused the sun of creation to dawn, O Identity, and the moon of origination through oneness. Then after the station of the Point is the station of the Hidden Alif, which is the station of the First Effulgence’s manifestation, expressed as the rank of Will, and the investiture of light in the house of outward Guardianship appearing in the form of abstraction, whereof it was said:

“Its outward aspect cannot be described and its inner reality is an impenetrable mystery that cannot be grasped.”

Then after the station of the Hidden Alif is the rank of the Soft Alif, which is the station of Destiny and contingent geometry, expressed as the station of Beauty. Then the station of the Unjoined Alif is the rank of Decree, Implementation and Origination. Then the station of the Joined Alif is the station of the Qa’im, which is the rank of Permission. Then the station of the Letters, which is the station of the Eight Imams and is the rank of Term. Then the station of the Word, which is the station of Fatima. These are the seven ranks through which nothing in contingent existence can come to be except through them, as is clearly stated in the tradition of al-Sadiq, who said, exalted be His remembrance:

“Nothing existeth in earth or heaven save through seven: through Will, Purpose, Decree, Destiny, Permission, Term and Book. Whoso claimeth one of these to be lacking hath indeed disbelieved.”

These indicated ranks are the manifestations of the Imams of Justice in the unseen realm, and when the lights descend to the realm of witnessing, they are sacred temples in this world. The name “Morning” in the primary reality applieth to them and none else. When the Cause descendeth to the realm of limitations, it hath been realized from the light of the Sun, and none uttereth God’s praise except that the name “Morning” truly applieth to him. The praise of all things is according to their rank, for things differ in their manifestations of orientation, since the “Morning” spoken of by the Chiefs is pure essence compared to the praise uttered by the Nobles, which is but a shadow and accident, even if appearing in similar and identical form.
Know thou this hidden secret, for through it hearts and minds are illumined and souls emerge from the darkness of reflections into the effulgence of the suns. Were one not to know this wisdom, they could not distinguish between deeds, movements, glances and words, for two words may be similar in outward form while none knoweth the difference between them save God. Thus thou mayest see the letter Alif from one of the Nobles and the letter Alif from one of the Chiefs, perceiving no outward difference between them, yet in God’s knowledge the latter dominateth over the Alif of the Noble who standeth in fear before Him.
This is the wisdom of the glorification of essences in the kingdom of names and attributes, which none comprehendeth save whom God willeth, for He is the Guardian in beginning and return. In the station of mentioning utterance, the servant must know its ranks, for utterance is the manifestation of potentiality into actual existence. It hath ranks: The utterance of the heart is will and its manifestations; the utterance of the tongue is exposition and what is realized thereby; the utterance of the pen is the flow of what God hath ordained for it; and the utterance of the tablet is the acceptance of forms and figures—each having its own aspect and utterance that none knoweth save Him.
The intended meaning of “exhalation” in His words—may my spirit be sacrificed for Him—is in language the meaning of breathing and exhaling, and in that station it indicateth all that is attributed to Him of manifestations, conditions, endpoints, indications, stations, signs, verses and what resembleth His wisdom in wisdom among the inscribed figures. Indeed the people of inner vision recognize in that pronoun the name of theophany in the form of the Manifestation, which is the indication in that word.
He returns in both stations to a single station—a clear proof of the connection between the high and the low according to the path of truth, for the effect must necessarily reflect the attributes of its cause. Even though the rank of manifestation appears through connection, the effect does not indicate the station of its cause. And it transcends the station of relating the manifestations of the Countenance of the Divine Unity, for that is the mystery of contingency in the realm of exposition. No one can distinguish the station of the reality of creation except as God wills, for He is the Exalted Protector.
Similarly, you understand all the words of this prayer just as was distilled in those words. But since today all people have been tested by the deaf, dumb, overwhelming trial which the Imam mentioned in his words, saying gloriously that they did not perceive the clear verses in the station of exposition, nor did they follow their own desires in what they inclined toward from limited reflections. Their hearts were not at peace with the flowing verses from the ranks of nature and the prayers speaking of nearness to the presence of the Manifestation of Truth.
Yet al-Sadiq said in al-Misbah:

“When knowledge is realized in the breast it fears, when fear is confirmed it flees, when it flees it is saved. When the light of certainty shines in the heart it witnesses grace, when grace is established in vision it hopes, when it finds the sweetness of hope it seeks, when it succeeds in seeking it finds. When the radiance of knowledge is unveiled in the inner heart, the wind of love stirs; when the wind of love stirs it finds intimacy in the presence of the Beloved and prefers the Beloved over all else, implementing His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, choosing them over everything else. When [one reaches] the Beloved while fulfilling His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, one attains the spirit of communion and nearness.”

The parable of these three principles is like the Sacred Precinct, the Mosque, and the Ka’bah. Whoever enters the Sacred Precinct is safe from creation; whoever enters the Mosque, their limbs are protected from being used in disobedience; whoever enters the Ka’bah, their heart is protected from being occupied with other than God. This is only due to their distance from observing the lights of Divine Unity.
And this hath come to pass only because of their remoteness from beholding the lights of oneness; otherwise they would have chosen, for their own selves, naught save that which God—glorified be He—hath caused to flow forth from the outpouring of His power, and hath chosen after His own Self. And this is the grace of God: He bestoweth it upon whom He willeth of His servants; and He is the Mighty, the Wise. And if thou dost gaze upon the mystery of the worlds, thou shalt behold, in this world, none other but Him.
Even as al-Baqir hath spoken, as is mentioned in al-Ikmal:

“God created a thousand thousand worlds, and a thousand thousand Adams; ye are in the last of those worlds, and those two Adams…”

For the temple of oneness hath not appeared save in this human form—according as the saying of Ali hath indicated, as mentioned in al-Azr … and al-Qadr—its purport being that the human form is the greatest proof of God unto His creation; it is the Book which God hath written with His own Hand; it is the temple He hath reared by His wisdom; it is the gathering-place of the forms of the two worlds; it is the abridgment of the Preserved Tablet; it is the witness over every absent one and the proof against every present one; it is the Straight Path; it is the Path stretched out between Paradise and fire—so runneth the tradition.
And wert thou to look with the eye of inner discernment, thou wouldst behold the ordinances of this “Anza’i” form in these verses, as the sun in the midst of heaven. He—exalted be His remembrance—hath said in the Surih of …: “God hath sent down…”—the tradition—“a Book, mutually resembling…”; and then His saying in the Surih of Bani Isra’il …
… “We have written in the Psalms, after the Remembrance, that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants.” And the Imam hath said in his commentary: “As for the Remembrance with God, and ʿMy righteous servants,’ they are the Qa’im and his companions—may God hasten their deliverance.” And God hath warned His servants, in the station of turning away, by His saying—exalted be His remembrance—“Whoso turneth away from My Remembrance, his shall be a straitened life.” And this is the ruling of inner realities in the verses, according to the pattern whereby the tidings have descended from the Suns of greatness and the mysteries—an admonition to such as possess insight.
Thus spake the Lord of the prostrate ones: “Dost thou know what recognition is?” He said, “No.” He—may my spirit be a sacrifice for Him—said: “Recognition of the Bayan first; and recognition of the Bayan first; and recognition of the meanings second; and recognition of the Gates third; and recognition of the Imam fourth; and recognition of the Pillars fifth; and recognition of the Deputies sixth; and recognition of the Nobles seventh.”
And al-Baqir hath said—according to that which is related in al-Kafi concerning His saying, exalted be His remembrance, “Nay! I swear by the retreating stars, that run and hide”—“The Imam withdraweth in the year two hundred and sixty, then appeareth like a meteor in the darkness. If thou dost attain unto his time, thine eyes shall be refreshed.” And al-Baqir said: “I seem to behold a people who have arisen in the East, seeking the truth, but it is not given unto them; then they seek it again, but it is not given unto them; and when they see this, they lay their swords upon their shoulders, and what they asked is granted them, yet they accept it not, until they rise up; and they will not offer it save unto your master.
Their slain are martyrs.” And our Master ʿAli said: “When the thousands are arrayed and the ranks set in order, and the ram meeteth the letters, then shall the latter arise, and the avenger shall cry out, and the unbeliever shall perish. Then shall the promised Qa’im arise, the fashioned Imam, to whom belong honor and bounty. He is thy son, O Husayn—none like unto him shall appear. He shall appear between the two supports, at the summit of his advance; he shall prevail over both realms, and shall leave none upon the earth … Blessed is he who attaineth unto his time, reacheth his appointed hour, and witnesseth the days foretold in the tradition.
Consider what has been recited to you from God’s verses and be among the learners, as Ali said: “People are of three kinds: the divine scholar, the learner on the path of salvation, and followers of every crier, swaying with every wind, not illumined by the light of knowledge nor taking refuge in a firm support.” That he may witness with certainty what al-Sadiq said: “You shall surely be confounded with confusion, and scattered with scattering, and whipped with the whip of destiny until your lowest becomes your highest and your highest becomes your lowest. And those who gave to drink though they fell short shall give drink, and those who took the lead though they preceded shall be cut off. By my life, our Cause in that time is clearer than this sun at its zenith.”
Therefore you must discipline yourself. Al-Sadiq said:

“You are not what you made yourself to be, nor did one like you form you. The nobility of the servant is through fear of God and knowledge, and it is not attained through the means by which all students today seek it. Rather, fear God and He will teach you what you desire.”

And the Commander of the Faithful said:

“Knowledge is not in heaven that it should descend upon you, nor in the earth that it should ascend unto you. Rather it is hidden within you, created in your hearts. Adopt the character of the spiritual ones, that it may be manifested to you.”

And if you stand firm in God’s covenant by arising upon the carpet of His Cause, you will be of me; otherwise God will execute His judgment upon you and distance you between the two Easts—and evil is that companion.
I have abbreviated the answer regarding the meaning of the prayer; indeed I have not interpreted a single letter of it, though I am able to do so in a way none other than myself can encompass in knowledge. What has come to you suffices. Seek forgiveness of God your Lord and be among the thankful.
And I say what God, exalted be His mention, has said: Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the Messengers. And praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds.

title: BB00208: Li-Validay man yaktub bayna yadi’llah
text:
In the name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy!
Glorified art Thou, O my God! I and all created things bear witness that Thou art God, that there is no God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thine is the kingdom and the dominion, Thine the might and the omnipotence, Thine the power and divinity, Thine the strength and glory, Thine the sovereignty and the earthly realm, Thine the majesty and grandeur, Thine the countenance and beauty, Thine the direction and perfection, Thine the mercy and bounty, Thine the authority and justice, Thine the likeness and paragon, Thine the stations and glory, Thine the greatness and independence, Thine the power and sublimity, Thine the might and inapproachability, Thine the force and exaltation, Thine the joy and gladness, Thine the likeness and paragon, Thine the sovereignty and dominion.
Thou hast ever been one God, single, eternal, self-subsisting, ever-living, self-sustaining, sovereign, all-encompassing, holy. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast no partner in what Thou hast created, nor any protector in what Thou hast fashioned. Thou hast created all things by Thy power and ordained them by Thine ordinance, and Thou hast formed all things by Thy will and fashioned them by Thy forming. Thou dost ever give life and cause death, then cause death and give life. Verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not, the Sovereign Who passeth not away, the Just Who wrongeth not, the King Who changeth not, the Single One Who escapeth not from anything, whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things.
Glorified art Thou, O my God! Sanctified be Thy names and exalted be Thy parables. Thou hast ever been unique in might and grandeur, and singular in countenance and beauty. How lofty is Thy station and how resplendent Thy summit! Thou hast created all things by Thy power, sustained all things by Thy mercy, perpetuated all things by Thy might, encompassed all things by Thy sovereignty, and remembered whom Thou willest of Thy creation through the sovereign craft of Thy Lordship. I shall not sanctify Thee save by what sanctifieth Thee, nor glorify Thee save by what glorifieth Thee, nor unite Thee, nor magnify Thee, nor exalt Thee, nor sovereign Thee save by what becometh the loftiness of Thy Being and the sublimity of Thy glory.
Glorified and exalted art Thou! Sanctified be Thy names and exalted be Thy parables. All worship Thee according to Thy true unity, all sanctify Thee according to Thy true eternality, all remember Thee according to the truth of Thy sovereign self-subsistence. Thou hast breathed the spirit of Thy command into the temples of Thy creation, whereupon all have ascended, through what they have known of Thy remembrance, unto what Thou hast of Thy grace. Glorified and exalted art Thou! All these are manifestations of Thy power from Thy Will and revelations of Thy might from Thy Purpose. Thou art the One existing before all things, Thou art the Maker of all things, Thou art the Being above all things, Thou art the Essence after all things, Thou art the Creator in the heights of all things. Voices are humbled before the sovereignty of Thy might, and faces prostrate at the appearance of Thy countenance. Thou art He Who hath caused all things to worship Thee, and all are Thy worshippers. Thou art He Who hath caused all things to prostrate to Thee, and all are prostrate before Thee, [though?] these befit not Thy exalted Being and Thy transcendent Self.
When I behold, O my God, Thy manifestation aforetime in the Furqan, had Thy Beloved not mentioned aught save what was revealed unto him—“Verily I am God, there is no God but Me, therefore worship Me”—then nothing else would have been mentioned. How could anything be created, neither His Self Who is the First of Thy creation, nor those beneath His Self who are witnesses by His command, nor any aspect of His religion, nor any element of His Cause? Thus all are effaced before Thy good-pleasure and overwhelmed before Thy decree in that thing. I know not, O my God, whether its descent from its heights and its mention of all things is more precious to Thee than the creation of all things, or whether that thing remained unmentioned, steadfast in the remembrance of Thy Self and speaking in praise of Thy Being. Glorified and exalted art Thou! I seek Thy forgiveness for every descent of the Will from that station wherein something mentioned His Self, Who is the First of Thy creation, and I turn in repentance unto Thee from…
…hath ever been and shall ever be worthy to remember Thee through Thy remembrance of Thyself, even were nothing created, no Prophet, no Successor, no Proof, no Path and no Guide. But since Thou hast named Thyself the All-Forgiving, It descended from Its heights to call upon Thee in Its lowliness and to populate the kingdoms of Thy heaven and earth with the emanations of Its Self, for Its essence, as Thou didst create it, indicateth none but Thee and mentioneth none but Thee. And whatever is mentioned of Thy Messenger, or the witnesses of Thy Messenger, or the gates of Thy glory, or the paths of Thy religion, or the manifestations of Thy love, or that which Thou lovest not—all of this is within Thy dominion and Thou rulest over it by Thy leave, exalting the conditions of Thy unity and bestowing favor upon the dawning-places of Thy will. It is all the same to It whether It speaketh from Thy presence or speaketh from clay, the lowest of Thy creation. Glorified and exalted art Thou!
Therefore, O God, send down upon the parents of him who standeth before Thee and writeth Thy verses by night and by day that which will satisfy them concerning their child on the Day of Resurrection in Thy presence, and comfort their eyes through what Thou hast caused to reach from what Thou didst create through them unto the source of Thy good-pleasure and Thy remembrance. For all, O my God, exchange Thee for clay and return to clay. How blessed is he whose remembrance endureth between the two clays and who pleaseth Thee between the two inanimate states. By Thy might, I seek protection with Thee and with all Thy names from anyone acquiring between the two clays that which Thou lovest not, for without doubt all return to that just as all began from this, and there remaineth not in this world the mention of Thy good-pleasure concerning it, and beneath it and beneath that world what Thou hast charged anyone with, for Thou art too exalted and glorious to command Thy creation with what they cannot comprehend or to burden them with what they cannot encompass.
Without doubt Thou hast ordained for every soul after its death in Thy paradise that which none of Thy creation can comprehend, and if it be not a believer, then in Thy fire with that which none of Thy creation can comprehend. But Thou hast made the pivot of what comes after death the conditions before it in that world. Glorified art Thou, there is no God but Thee! Send down upon all who have believed in Thee and will believe what befitteth Thee through Thy grace and bounty. Verily Thou art the All-Bestowing, the Subtle, and verily Thou art the Generous, the Bountiful.
