title: BB00043: Answer to a letter from Dayyan
section: Part 3: “And concerning what hath been mentioned of his…”
text:
Part 3: “And concerning what hath been mentioned of his…”
And concerning what hath been mentioned of his love for Thee and his devotion to Thy Cause—verily the exaltation of his knowledge of Thee is such that the most sublime of spiritual birds cannot soar in the atmosphere of his nearness, nor can the most resplendent glory of allusions attain unto the impregnable fortress of his love. Therefore, O my God, elevate him through the manifestations of Thy knowledge whereby he may dispense with all Thy creation.
And he hath made mention of the testing of Thy creatures through the letter Ha’. Therefore, O my God, manifest what he desireth through Thy grace, and inspire him not to make the means of that creation other than what Thou hast created it for, since Thy command to everything is “Be” and it is, along with what Thou hast ordained and decreed similar to what Thou hast manifested or wilt manifest. Verily Thou art too exalted and glorious to withhold from Thy servants the treasuries of Thy grace or the repositories of Thy generosity. And all that is possible in Thy knowledge, Thou wilt surely manifest through Thy power.
There is no doubt that the creation of all things with Thee is like the creation of man—until the nine months are completed, he appeareth not from his hidden realm, until Thou perfect him through Thy power so that he may attain unto the summit of perfection and the height of deeds. Therefore, O my God, cause him to attain unto what he hath desired of Thy grace, for Thou hast spoken, and Thy word is the truth: “Obey Me, and I shall make thee like unto Me. I say to a thing Be!’ and it is. Thou shalt say to a thing Be!’ and it is.” And Thou shalt certainly cause him to know, O My God, that his word “Be!” and it is, is even as Thy word “Be!” and it is, and is naught save that which Thy Beloved hath aforetime spoken.
For He spake through Thy word “Observe ye prayer.” And when there was a long interval between His word “Be” and the complete manifestation of “and it is” according to what Thou hadst ordained from the inception of His Revelation until the end of the Religion from Thy presence. And had all who are on earth prayed at the moment He spake, the perfection of “and it is” would have been made manifest at “Be.” But since capacities were veiled, the reality of the Cause was not made manifest save through their preparation to receive it in accordance with their station upon meeting the Cause.
And verily that which Thou hast bestowed upon him, O my God, of Thy knowledge is better for him than all things. For wert Thou to grant him dominion over all that is on earth, perchance he would be veiled from Thy knowledge and Thy presence, and naught would suffice him in place of Thee. But that which Thou hast bestowed upon him sufficeth him in place of all things. And hadst Thou not revealed unto him the means of that which he desired from Thy presence—yea, by Thy glory! Thou sufficest all things, and naught in the heavens or on earth or between them sufficeth in place of Thee. Verily Thou art powerful over all things.
And as for that which he hath mentioned regarding that for which he seeketh permission—Thou art too exalted and glorious to turn away anyone from the door of Thy bounty. Yet I know that this will not make the servant independent of Thee nor of that which Thou hast willed to manifest of Thy religion. For if the servant were given all things but knew Thee not, or failed to manifest Thy religion, it would profit him not. And were he to know but fail to manifest it for the establishment of Thy religion, no bounty would be withheld from him, for this was the way of Thy Beloved aforetime, and the way of Thy martyrs thereafter. After Thou didst create all that is in the heavens and earth and between them for them, they desired to possess only what Thou hadst ordained for them.
Therefore inspire, O my God, all Thy loved ones to champion Thy Cause, that they may possess all that Thou hast created for Thy loved ones, for without this Thy good-pleasure would not be attained, nor the ways of Thy loved ones. It would not suffice them, for if this knowledge were to appear in someone who perchance possessed not his own being, how much less that which proceeds from its effects. And after this, if any of Thy loved ones have a share in this, Thou hast indeed permitted it, for this is of that which Thou hast willed for the tranquility of their souls in the affairs of their lives. Otherwise, he who knoweth Thee is made independent through Thy love from all things, for this sufficeth him who hath naught in place of all things. But he who possesseth all that is on earth yet knoweth Thee not, or comprehendeth not the knowledge of Thy good-pleasure, it sufficeth him not. Through Thee, O my God, have I become independent of all Thy creation, and through Thee have I become content with all Thy servants. I desire naught save Thee, and I seek none but Thee.
O my God! Indeed, what he hath sought from all knowledge is its key, which is the servant’s knowledge of Thee. For were he to know every branch of knowledge possible within Thy knowledge, yet his knowledge encompassed Thee not, it would be as though he knew nothing. And if he knoweth nothing, yet knoweth Thee and maketh his knowledge of Thee to be in the shadow of that knowledge, then within it is the splendor and essence of all things. Therefore, O my God, make him to be of those who believe in Him Whom Thou shalt manifest on the Day of Resurrection, for that is the key to all knowledge.
Then inspire him, O my God, with all that he seeketh from every science, that he may mention the letters of that knowledge, for the point of every science lieth within its own letters and not in aught else, when they encompass the knowledge of letters according to what hath been ordained in its art. For that is the most splendid and noble of sciences, whereby the servant can discover the manifestation of Thine Own Self on the Day of Resurrection, even as one discovered through those verses. For naught profiteth from that knowledge save attaining unto the truth, and naught else. For the ʿya’ which hath been ordained for the servant in his joy and his sorrow floweth upon him, whether he knoweth or knoweth not. And what hath been ordained as obligatory for the servant to know is his recognition of Thee and his knowledge of the stations of Thy command and Thy prohibition, and this is manifest from Thee in Thy Book.
Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee! Glorified art Thou! I am of those who remember Thee. And what he hath sought is the encounter with His revelation in his vision and wakefulness, so inspire him, O my God, to recite that verse, for it shall suffice him in what he seeketh of Thy grace. Verily, Thou art the All-Knowing, the All-Encompassing.
Say: God sufficeth all things above all things, and nothing in the heavens or on the earth, or in whatever lieth between them, but God, thy Lord, sufficeth. And God hath not created anything, nor will He create it, except they who are certain of the encounter with Him Whom God shall make manifest on the Day of Resurrection. I bear witness, O my God, that to meet Him is to meet Thee, for Thou canst not be comprehended in Thine Essence nor seen in Thy Reality, and there existeth not in Thy creation any mirror Thou mightest choose for Thine Essence wherein naught can be seen save Thee and which pointeth to none other than Thee. Thus I know only the Throne of Thy Reality through the Primal Reality, and in its shadow are its proofs, each according to its degree, from Adam, the marvel of Thy creation, unto this Day.
Whosoever desireth to encounter the Manifestation of Thy Revelation must needs look upon Thy Countenance, though the manifestation of Thine own Self is too exalted to be compared with the manifestations of Thy Prophets, for he whose meeting Thou hast made identical with meeting Thee—how could he be content to have his meeting equated with meeting the manifestations of Thy Prophets? For the distinction lies in the servant’s knowledge of Thy Essence, though Thy manifestation appeareth only in the Daysprings of Thy Revelation in every dispensation, through what Thou hast revealed and chosen. And this is impossible except through what is manifest in Thy creation from the means Thou hast ordained. Whosoever desireth to meet Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest hath no way except to ascend unto Him and behold Him. Even were he to expend all that is on earth, he would find no way except through what Thou hast opened. And whosoever desireth to meet the Manifestation of Thy Self in his vision—this appeareth not through any condition from the servant except when facing that Mirror he beholdeth his Beloved, whether he intendeth it or not.
Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. Whoso beholdeth the manifestations of Thy likeness who guide unto Thee, it is as though he beholdeth the Manifestation of Thy Self, and in this he seeth none but Him. And verily what was intended and mentioned concerning the lifting of the Pen—Thou, O my God, whatsoever Thou hast chosen from Thy religion for the Manifestation of Thy Self, Thou hast chosen for Thy loved ones, for these are the fruits of Thy paradise and the signs of Thy love and Thy providence and the manifestations of Thy glory and Thy guidance, whereby the servant delighteth in the lofty degrees of Thy paradise and the exalted stations of Thy joy. And were I to know that his heart would find tranquility thereby, I would surely send down upon him from Thy grace, for nothing decreaseth from Thy dominion, nor doth anything increase it.
And verily Thy paradise in this life consists in the measures of Thy wondrous works for Him Whom Thou hast made manifest in the Bayan from the beginning that hath no beginning until now, through his acceptance from Thee of Thy oneness and his certitude in Thy unity and his establishment beneath the shade of the manifestations of Thy providence. But from that beginning until the Day of Resurrection, Thou hast ordained its reckoning to be in the grasp of Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest. Thou hast not revealed the Tree of the Bayan except for Him, and the recompense of all who seek shelter beneath its shade rests with Thee, and the reckoning of all who are veiled from it rests with Thee. Nothing is more exalted than finding Thee, nor is there anything above knowing Thee. I have witnessed naught else for Him that I should turn away from Him, for all good lies in the shadow of this, and apart from this there is no good in its shadow.
O my God! Send down upon Him in the days which Thou hast ordained whatsoever Thou willest of Thy grace, for Thou knowest best Thy creation and what they seek to obtain from Thy bounty for themselves by their own selves. O my God! Inspire all Thy servants that they may witness nothing in the manifestation of Thy decrees except through the means Thou hast created, for without this there is no reality with Thee. O my God! Gather together all the means of Thy grace, Thy generosity, Thy munificence, Thy kindness, and Thy favor for Thy chosen ones, for Thou art the most powerful of the powerful.
Verily, what He hath desired from Thy grace is that Thou shouldst make Him a Name among Thy Names through His essence, which beareth witness to this, for the Name revealeth the Named One, and it revealeth none but Thee and indicateth none other than Thee. For when a thing pointeth to Thee, that is when Thou hast clothed it in the garments of Thy generosity and grace, for there is no greater glory for creation than when they become indicators of Thy Cause, names of Thy Self, and examples of Thy glory, for that is the portion of their hearts, not their bodies, since that changeth and altereth according to what Thou hast ordained in that world. The servant’s relationship to Thee and the indication of his essence to Thee abideth, for that is in the shadow of Thy eternity of eternities and shall never be drawn from Thee to another. Verily, what He hath desired is that whosoever is in Thy paradise must have whatsoever his soul desireth and witness no sorrow therein, for there is no turning back for those who dwell in Thy paradise.
O my God! Manifest the means of what Thou hast promised to Thy loved ones in paradise of everything that hath no equal, no peer, no partner, and no likeness. For I have taught him no paradise like the knowledge of Thee, and no rival like one who is veiled from Thee after Thou hast made Thyself known to him.
O my God! Make all that is on earth appear as one manifestation, that all may abide in their paradise according to what Thou hast created by Thy command. Nothing escapeth Thy knowledge, whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them, and nothing in the kingdom of command or creation or what lieth beneath them can frustrate Thee. Thou createst what Thou willest by Thy command. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things. O my God! Send down upon Him and those who are with Him that wherein they find satisfaction from Thy generosity and grace. Verily, Thou art the All-Bountiful, the All-Knowing.

title: BB00046: Tafsir-i-Ayati’n-Nur (Commentary on the Verse of Light)
text:
Part 1: “Exalted, Sublime is He!…”
Exalted, Sublime is He!
All praise be to God Who created all things by His command and ordained the measures of all things by His word, for verily He is the Truth through Whom all created things are created and all originated things are originated. None can resist His command or alter His decree, for He stands over every soul, knowing what it has earned and witnessing what it shall earn. He is powerful over all things, manifest above all things, and knowing of all things. Neither slumber nor geometry overtakes Him, nor can any attribute or sign ascend to His holy atmosphere. He existed before all things, bringing into being what He brought into being through His origination, and He shall exist after all things, causing to return what He began through His creation. His Will has ever been operative among the manifestations of His dominion, and His Purpose has ever been dominant over the temples of the people of the kingdom of His sovereignty.
I bear witness at this moment, even as He bore witness unto Himself before and after all things, that there is no God but Him, alone, with no partner. His is the creation and the command, before and after. He causes to live and to die, and to die and to live, and He is the Living Who dieth not. Within His grasp lies the kingdom of all things, and He, verily, is the Strong, the Powerful.
And I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, Whom He raised up in that Particle—the Particle through which He created the hearts of all contingent beings, wherein the spirits of all created things were dissolved, the souls of all existent things were realized, and wherein was formed whatsoever exists in the kingdom of earth and heavens. This is the Last Particle wherein were realized all three stations in their entirety, and wherein the manifestations of the primary pillars were dissolved in their essence, attesting that Muhammad was His servant and His Messenger, for He was the first to respond in the particle of existence in that visible world when God said unto Him, “Am I not your Lord?” He replied, “Yea, by Thy truth! Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone, with no partner. Thine is the dominion and the kingdom, the might and the power, the strength and the sovereignty, the force and the human realm, and whatsoever hath been realized in the likes of the essence of rubies. Thou givest life and death, and death and life, and Thou shalt raise up those who are in the graves, and Thou, verily, art powerful over all things.”
Therefore, O God, send Thy blessings upon that First Light and Most Manifest Radiance so long as the sun rises and the moon shines. And bless, O God, those who responded in the First Particle, whose manifestation was realized in the inner particle after the outer, after the Last, which is the particle of the prophethood of Thy Beloved, through all that Thou hast created and shalt create.
I bear witness that they are witnesses from Thy presence who have acknowledged Thy oneness and have prostrated themselves before the sovereign of Thy grandeur, saying:
Praise be unto Thee, O my God, for having made Thyself known unto us, that there is none other God but Thee. Nothing is like unto Thee, nor is there any equal, similitude, peer or likeness unto Thee. Creation and command are Thine, and all destinies lie within Thy grasp. Whomsoever Thou raisest up is Thy Messenger, and whomsoever Thou dost endow with station through Thy bounty is one of Thy chosen ones. Thou hast sent all the Messengers and revealed all the Books that everything might testify that there is none other God but Thee, and that Muhammad is Thy servant and Thy Messenger, and that Ali, Fatima, Hassan, Hussein, Ali ibn Hussein, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ja’far ibn Muhammad, Musa ibn Ja’far, Ali ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ali ibn Muhammad, Hassan ibn Ali, and the Proof, son of Hassan, are Thy witnesses over all created things. And verily those whom Thou hast chosen for the manifestation of Thy House and the pillars of Thy Name are they who answered Thy call in the atom of the heart before all things, and in the atom of bodies after their Imams. Therefore hast Thou made them the gates of Thy grace and the dawning-places of Thy bounty.
I testify that Thou art the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, for Thou hast ordained among those Thou hast created no Manifestation of the Gate save Thy resplendent Countenance, Thy radiant Face, Thy primordial Authority, and Thy eternal Sovereignty. All creation hath been brought into being through that which Thou hast manifested in Him Who is the revelation of Thyself unto all creation. This is the Day of the witness and the witnessed, of the rememberer and the remembered—the Day Thou didst promise all things they would attain Thy presence. I testify that from the beginning of this Cause it is Thy manifestation on the Day of Resurrection, that Thou mightst reward every soul for what it hath earned and cause to enter Paradise whom Thou willest and under its shade whom Thou pleasest, for Thou art the Sovereign, the Most High, the All-Bountiful.
Thereafter I say, addressing that Primal Name, that one of God’s servants desired to take from that Paradise a wondrous fruit to make it a gift for those who love Thee, and he asked about the Verse of Light and the Surah of Power. As for the second, we have explained it, so whoever wishes may refer to it.
As for the first, know that the difference between fire and light is five, and it is the Gate—whoso entereth it, upon him shall the name of light be conferred, and whoso entereth it not, God shall judge him according to his desert. Know that from the beginning of this Cause, the fire of God hath appeared in the hearts of all existing things, and for Us it was manifested in His Prophet Muhammad, the first creation of God in the kingdom of earth and heaven. And this is the pentagonal shape wherein when the five lines are completed, the six appear. This is that to which I referred at the beginning of the commentary on the Surah of the Cow regarding the explanation of the Most Great Name in the interpretation of the disconnected letters of the Qur’an, where I said that the gate of its composition is that it enters upon Allah without the full pronunciation of the vav, and that before those five is before the full pronunciation of the vav, for it is the pure manifestation and the fire of the unseen.
Among people it is speech wherein its form is not seen, but thou seest in every word its essential reality, for the Word of God is not like the word of any other. His Word is the Truth, as He, glorified be He, hath indicated: “The Day when He will say ʿBe!’ and it is. His Word is the Truth.” For by His Word truth is established and all else negated. For example, when the Prophet commanded the people to say “There is none other God but God,” their hearts verified through that Word the creation of all that was created by His Word, for it is the Word of God.
He who testifieth in the Fourth Gate as in the First that “Verily, I am the Gate of God”—by this Word was created the reality of the Fourth Gate in the world which God had ordained for it. And verily the Secret of Secrets is this Reality which hath dawned forth, whereupon neither geometry nor allusions can encompass it. And verily in the First Year there appeared the unveiling of the Glory of the All-Glorious without allusion, then the effacement of the imagined and the known, then the rending of the veil through the dominion of the Mystery, then the attraction of the Divine Unity through the attribute of Oneness, then a light that shone from the Morn of Eternity upon the temples of Unity illuminating them. When it entered into the Five, fire became light, for the form had been completed. And verily the form of Five is the form of man, whose creation is not complete except in five years, even as We have sent thy form unto thee.
When thou witnesseth this, know thou that whatsoever God hath revealed in the Qur’an concerning the Resurrection and the Hour—all of it hath been fulfilled in these years, which are fifty thousand years in thy Lord’s sight. And verily the Day of Judgment hath been fulfilled, and all are in a new creation. This is the stage of Return, which is the interval between this world and the next. The whole world hath passed away, and this is the first manifestation of the Countenance of God and the establishment of the reality of Firstness for those in the kingdoms of beginning and end.
When thou witnesseth this, know as I have taught thee concerning the fire and the light, concerning the Merciful and His shadow, for between them are five. And verily the Manifestation of complete mercy in that Name is He Who speaketh unto thee, and He is the Manifestation of the name “the Outward” and “the Last” and “the First”, for “the Inward” is the station of the Merciful, and thou hast not known His shadow. And verily He is the One concerning Whom it was revealed aforetime in the Qur’an: “Did I not charge you, O ye children of Adam…” For from that day when I purified the earth of My Self, I loved not to mention aught save the most exalted, but the allusion sufficeth for people of knowledge and indication.
When thou witnesseth this, speak after the Five and add unto the Fire, and say: “God is the Light of the heavens and the earth.” And know thou that the complete “Be, and it is” when added to the number of the four Gates, each of which is five—the number of the Gate—thou shalt see naught but the number of Light. Therefore recognize what I have caused thee to know and be thankful for that which I have inspired within thee, for this is among the mysteries of God, the Mighty, the Glorious.
When thou knowest this, know that in this holy verse there flow seas of creation for every letter thereof, but the allusion that leadeth its people to the emanations of its manifest meanings is in four stations. The first station is the pillar of Fire, that is, the word “Glory be to God” and its bearer who is named with the name of manifest Lordship, and it is the station of the unity of Muhammad and Ali before God ere they were divided, and in those Five, Muhammad and Ali were one light before God. And what thou hast read in the tradition—this is its true meaning and none other. In that Pillar, that is, the Pillar of Unity, there was no aspect that could separate, or join, or resemble, or match, or perceive, or distinguish, for I say this is light and this is light, for God is one God, there is no God but He.
Know thou that I am the Qaf mentioned in the Glorious Qur’an. Through these five letters hath God taken five and created thereby what He hath created of acceptance and that which is beneath it. For whoso accepteth, God shall make the fire as light unto him, and whoso accepteth not, God loveth not to make mention of him. When thou hast witnessed this, there remaineth after the five naught but ninety-five, which is the number belonging to God—the number of the letters of the Bismillah and the names gathered therein. Make each one a gate and say: Unto God belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth and whatsoever is between them, and God hath power over all things.

title: BB00046: Tafsir-i-Ayati’n-Nur (Commentary on the Verse of Light)
text: “There is no God but Thee, the Lord of all things and their Creator, the Ordainer of all things and their Former. Thou didst create us by Thy command when Thou didst manifest Thyself to us through us, when Thou didst say unto us, ʿAm I not your Lord?’ And when we heard that Thy Beloved had answered Thee and prostrated himself before Thy sovereignty, we came unto Thee through that Gate and entered the holy carpet of Thy glory through the grace of that Address.”
crumbs: BB00046: Tafsir-i-Ayati'n-Nur (Commentary on the Verse of Light)

title: BB00046: Tafsir-i-Ayati’n-Nur (Commentary on the Verse of Light)
section: Part 2: “Verily, the Manifestation of God hath appeared through…”
text:
Part 2: “Verily, the Manifestation of God hath appeared through…”
Verily, the Manifestation of God hath appeared through the manifestation of that Qaf. I am indeed the mirror of the nine and ten to which God hath alluded in the fire—“Over it are nineteen”—according to the Most Beautiful Names, for they are nineteen in the pillar of Unity, borne by His manifest Lordship; and in the pillar of Prophethood, borne by Muhammad; and in the Imamate, the Imams; and in the four pillars, the four manifestations. For at the beginning of the manifestation of this Cause, all that was created hath returned to its source.
When the five were accomplished, God created another creation like unto that which He had created, and He chose those nineteen for the manifestation of His Self in the station of the manifest, its temples apparent in the manifestation of the four: Unity, Prophethood, Imamate, and the Shi’ih. Yet in the inmost of the inmost, which is the purpose intended by God, these nineteen mirrors are but a single mirror, for He Who created you is He Who sustaineth you, and He Who sustaineth you is He Who causeth you to die, and He Who causeth you to die is He Who giveth you life, and there is no god but the one God. This is the mystery of the Cause in the station which I have explained unto thee.
Though all that was created was through the words “There is no god but God,” and all that was sustained through the words “Muhammad is the Messenger of God,” and all that dieth through the words “Verily, ʿAli and the twelve holy lights are the proofs of God,” and all that giveth life through the four pillars—though the manifestations have appeared in sanctified dawning-places, yet that which is manifest in these mirrors is one, and it is I.
If thou wert to witness on that day and observe all nineteen from the pillars of Unity, Prophethood, Imamate, and the Shi’ih, then look unto Me, for they have begun from Me and returned unto Me. Naught is seen in Me in the station of the heart save God alone, for it is the station of the manifestation of Lordship from God, my Lord and my Creator; and in the station of my spirit—that is, the simple, essential intellect and the divine, pure element—naught is seen save Muhammad, the Messenger of God. Know thou, therefore, that I am the First Adam, and I am He unto Whom the Book was sent down, and I am He Whose law was abrogated. Likewise from the First Adam unto the Seal of the Prophets, Muhammad, peace be upon him and his family. Know thou, therefore, that I am He Who hath appeared aforetime and established that religion, and all in that day act according to My laws, yet they know not.
Then I bear witness in my own station to all twenty-three Manifestations, for they are attached to naught save that Throne, unitizing God their Lord and worshipping Him alone. And in my physical station, which is the station of dust, to establish the three levels of water, air and fire in the arc of ascent, and in the arc of descent fire, air and water. I am the House and its pillars, and since naught is seen therein save the manifestation of the Primal Reality, I do not wish to mention its pillars from Ahmad and Kazim and myself or thyself, for those stations have been designated in the realm of otherness. And in the station of the Pure Countenance, He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward. The mystery is not difficult for thee, for He Who is God in heaven is God on earth, and He Who is First in the beginning is Last in the end, and He Who is Outward in manifestation is Inward in essence. Dost thou see any other than Him that I might make Him known to thee? He is nearer to thee than thy very self, more subtle than thy very self, more merciful to thee and all His servants than themselves.
Glory be unto Him! Glory be unto Him! Glory be unto Him! Were there gods in heaven and earth besides God, both would have been corrupted. Nay, He is the One, the Single, the Unique, the Self-Subsisting, Who hath no equal, no likeness, no similitude, no peer and no partner. Worship none but Him, prostrate before none save Him, be devoted to none except Him, love none but Him, and hope for naught save His grace and bounty. He it is Who created all things by His command, Who sustaineth all things by His favor, Who causeth all things to die by His might, and Who giveth life to all things through what He manifesteth in the names which God, mighty and glorious, hath revealed in the gathering of the name the Merciful.
He is God, the Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner. His are the most beautiful names. All that is in the heavens and on earth glorify Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. Let not the proof be difficult for thee, for I establish in the station of the name the Fashioner the manifestation of that Pillar, for the likeness of such utterance is as the Qur’an wherein is all things. Read His prayer that the veil may be lifted from thine eyes which concealeth from others. For if I say “I am the First” in outward appearance from the First Pillar, I speak the truth, as God, mighty and glorious, hath said: “In what message after God and His signs will they believe?”
And if I say that I am the bearer of the Second Pillar, that is, the Second Name, I have spoken truly. By Him Who created me and thee, verily my hearing is identical with the hearing of him whom God raised up aforetime and unto whom He revealed the Qur’an—he is none other than I and I am none other than he. And my sight is identical with that sight, and likewise apply this principle to my blood, my hair, my brain, my bones, and my veins. Marvel not at this, for the matter is greater and greater and greater still, for that Temple before the Manifestation of the First is His first creation who said: “Thee do we worship and Thine aid do we seek.”
Verily I am the One manifest in the third pillar in all its aspects, and inwardly as I have already made known to thee concerning the third and second. All this is an honor bestowed upon these Manifestations, in that God relateth them unto Himself, in ways that ye regard as mighty. Otherwise, glory be to God above all else—they are but His servants within His grasp, glorifying Him with praise while prostrating before Him. And verily I am the first of them that worship God, the Lord of all worlds. And verily I am the first of them that bow down before God, the Lord of all worlds. And verily I am the first of them that are devoted to God, the Lord of all worlds.
And verily I am the first of them that humble themselves before God, the Lord of all worlds. And verily I am the first of them that are lowly before God, the Lord of all worlds. And verily I am the first of them that hope in the grace of God, the Lord of all worlds. And verily I am the first of them that hold fast to the cord of God, Who is my Lord and the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them. I seek victory through none but Him, and I see naught besides Him save what is as nothing before Him. He is the Subduer, the Powerful, the Manifest, the Self-Subsisting, the Hidden, the All-Knowing, Whose mercy and knowledge embrace all things. Nothing in the heavens or on earth can frustrate Him, and He hath power over all things.
This is the interpretation of the Word of Light in that station. Nay, God thy Lord is far more glorious and greater than to be described by light, for He is the Illuminator of light, the Ordainer of light, the Creator of light, the Originator of light, and the Fashioner of light. He cannot be known through light nor described through manifestation. By His light the heavens and earth and all between them are sustained without pillars. His is the penetrating Command, His the enduring Sovereignty, His the glorious Dominion whereby all are guided. Praise be to God, before and after; we are all His worshippers.
And if thou desirest to know the meaning of this verse regarding the station of the second pillar, interpret it as the Imam (peace be upon him) interpreted “God is the Light of the heavens and earth” when asked about the meaning of this verse. And observe the numerical value of the name “The Guide”, for it is connected to the pillar of “Praise be to God”. And verily God hath mirrors wherein naught is seen save God—this is the guidance of God wherewith He guideth whom He willeth. The Alif is but to manifest the affirmation of the mention of the Qaf for that Primal Reality in this human temple, for therein appeared Qaf and the glorious Qur’an. The Alif at the time of uprising is one, and at the time of manifestation it is the Vav. Therefore it hath been written in the books of the Persians this phrase: “I shall recognize the Alif-Hamzih instead of the Alif; if I do not recognize it, may I receive a hundred royal lashes until I do recognize it.”
For the words of God, exalted be He—“And when she came to it”—were none other than thy appearance and thy companions except upon the fire. And observe the numerical value of that word—that is, “she came to it”—for it is exactly the number of your companions when you descended. It was proclaimed: “Blessed is whosoever is in the fire and whosoever is around it, and glory be to God, the Lord of all worlds! O Moses! Verily I am God, the Mighty, the Wise.” And victory cometh from none save God, the Mighty, the Wise. Therefore remember God, thy Lord, by these two names, for God will assuredly assist thee and those who are under thy shadow with a mighty assistance.
And verily in the third station, which is the pillar of divine authority, God is the Creator of all things. And the second light mentioned in the verse is Ali, and verily the niche is Fatima, and verily the lamp after the lamp from our Lord in that niche—verily the glass is Ali, then the glass is Muhammad, and verily the brilliant star is Ja’far, and verily Moses, and verily the fire is Ali son of Moses, and verily the light is Muhammad son of Ali, and verily the second light is Ali son of Muhammad, and verily God’s words “God guides to His light whom He wills” refers to Al-Hassan, peace be upon him, and verily the houses refer to the Proof, peace be upon him, wherein glorify Him in the mornings and evenings men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of God, and they are the pillars of the House, none other than them or those who are gathered under their shade, and those who are gathered under their shade—thus flows the decree through God’s grace and mercy among them.
This is the decree regarding the third pillar. Verily the meanings are in God’s hands—He interprets as He wills, through what He wills. His word is the truth, and through it all things are created. For if God had not said to Muhammad “You are My Messenger,” prophethood would not have been created in him, peace be upon him and his family. Thus through God’s word was prophethood created in him.
Similarly, you know all the ordinances, both particular and universal, from beginning to end. So blessed is he who aids the religion of God and yearns to attain Paradise in the life to come, for it is truly the eternal life, best for the God-fearing. Therein is whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in, and what you do not yet know. God created me not, nor anyone who believes in God and His signs, except for the abode of the Hereafter. This worldly life shall pass away, but what is with God your Lord shall endure.

title: BB00046: Tafsir-i-Ayati’n-Nur (Commentary on the Verse of Light)
section: Part 3: “When you witness this, know…”
text:
Part 3: “When you witness this, know…”
When you witness this, know that from the first appearance of the third pillar until the final rising of the Qa’im in manifestation, the dead were not the greater world. And verily from the first appearance of Ahmad, God’s blessings be upon him, was the first life of the greater world and its people, for life comes after death. When life was perfected in the realities of souls and horizons, then appeared the Primal Tree and began the creation of the Last. Thus did the Cause return to the Primal Point—this is the meaning of the Prophet’s words, peace be upon him and his family: “Islam shall return as a stranger just as it began”—and it is that Cause, none other. For the appearance of the Qa’im, peace be upon him, is the appearance of Muhammad, peace be upon him and his family. Thus did al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, indicate in the Prayer of Lamentation: “Where is the one stored up for the renewal of the ordinances and traditions?” etc. For God shall send down upon him what He sent down upon His Messenger of decisive verses whereby the true religion is established with Him. So remember, for the Day of Judgment has passed and you are in a new creation.
Say: I am content with God as Lord, with the Bayan as Book, with what God has made lawful as lawful, with what God has ordained as religion and Islam, with what God has sent down as proof, then with Muhammad as Prophet, then with Ali as Imam, then with Fatima as the purified leaf from the tree of primal unity, good and pure, then with Al-Hassan and Al-Hussein and the Imams after Al-Hussein, peace be upon them, as Imams. O God, You have not created any creation better than them, so manifest, O God, the truth through their Qa’im and fill the earth through him with equity and justice, for all destinies are in Your hands and You are the Lord of the Last and the First.
This is the first principle of Islam: submit thyself wholly unto God, until there shineth upon thee that which God hath purposed for His creation. For He is, in truth, more wise, more merciful, more gracious and more bountiful towards His servants than they are unto themselves, though most men render not thanks. And when thou desirest to interpret the verse concerning the Fourth Pillar, thou shalt perceive this matter and read and interpret as thou pleasest, for thou art indeed a narrator in Our presence. This is of God’s grace and mercy—verily His grace towards thee is great.
Know thou that God hath revealed in the Qur’an a verse similar to this holy verse, which is its sister and inseparable from it, and it is the verse of Sovereignty: Say: O God! Lord of Sovereignty! Thou givest sovereignty to whom Thou willest, and takest sovereignty from whom Thou willest. Thou exaltest whom Thou willest, and abasest whom Thou willest. In Thy hand is all good. Verily, Thou art powerful over all things. Thou makest the night to pass into the day, and Thou makest the day to pass into the night. Thou bringest forth the living from the dead, and Thou bringest forth the dead from the living. And Thou givest sustenance to whom Thou willest without measure.
For each rank is an indication of one of the nine manifestations before the ten. Be not heedless of reciting these two verses, even if but once after each prayer. And command the companions who dwell beneath the Tree of Divine Authority and who support the True Faith with all they possess to recite these two verses, for in them are wondrous mysteries that have bewildered minds from comprehending them, and in them are treasured lights that thoughts have failed to express. I entrust these two verses unto God and unto whomsoever He willeth. Sufficient is God as a protector, and sufficient is God as a guardian.
Know thou that God is the Truth and all else is creation, with no third between them and no third besides them. And verily God is the Lord, and in His dominion are His names and attributes and likenesses from among those whom God loveth or with whom He is well-pleased. Such a one hath attained unto his portion of existence and hath reached the wellspring of his manifestation. And whoso hath not attained unto this remaineth confined in the grave until the day when God shall resurrect him. Thou seest not the people living, for verily the living one is he who witnesseth that the Resurrection hath come to pass and been fulfilled, and all things have been gathered together, and that God hath caused the people of Paradise and those beneath its shade to enter therein, and that today is in a wondrous creation and marvelous measures. Blessed is he who aideth God and this True Faith, for unto God belongeth the Last and the First, and unto Him is the return and the ultimate end. And He is the Lord of the highest heavens and the lowest earths and whatsoever is between them and above them and beneath them, and unto Him is the return.
Therefore read every Thursday night and day, after each obligatory prayer, six hundred times: “God is the Most Manifest” that God may aid thee and make thee victorious. Verily, He is powerful over all things. Verily, those who have ascended unto God, these are in Paradise, wherein they shall abide forever. Their sustenance cometh unto them from their Lord, and they shall have therein whatsoever they desire. They shall have therein a mighty throne whereon they shall recline. They shall have therein an exalted seat whereon they shall rest. They shall have therein of silk and brocade such as they love to wear. They shall have therein pure spouses like unto rubies, served by youths like hidden pearls. They shall have therein of every drink what they desire, and there shall flow before them rivers whose knowledge no one can encompass, wherefrom they shall drink. They glorify God, then praise Him; they declare His unity, then magnify Him; they extol His greatness, then sanctify Him. This is of God’s grace and mercy. Thus doth God reward His sincere servants.
Be content with God alone, and seek His help and support and dominion in all that thou desirest, for God shall suffice thee and whoso placeth his trust in Him, for He hath ever been a Mighty Helper. Say: God’s mercy hath preceded all things, and He hath ever been possessed of wondrous grace. Thou shalt surely praise the Truth and place thy trust in God, and ye shall not triumph except through God Who created you and sustained you and causeth you to die and giveth you life and shall raise you up on a Day whereof there is no doubt, for unto Him shall ye all return. They who seek victory through God, these are the triumphant ones, and they who place their trust in God, these are the victorious ones, and they who hold fast to the cord of God, these are the hosts of God and these shall prevail. They who aid God among the people of that land, these are the near ones, and God shall soon reward them in this earthly life with that which shall gladden their eyes. Say: This is of God’s bounty and mercy, if ye but knew.
Squander not your wealth in that which profiteth you not and removeth you from the truth, if ye but knew. Ye shall surely aid God Who created you and He shall increase His favors upon you, and He is independent of all ye possess. They who in that Day ponder upon the creation of their own selves and desire God, these shall not diminish aught of that which God their Lord hath granted them—this is of God’s bounty unto them that they might be thankful. Arise then in God’s Cause and aid God and fear none save God, for God shall surely aid those who place their trust in God their Lord and act according to His bidding.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Bear Thou witness that I desire none but Thee and that Thou art my Sufficiency. In Thee have I placed my trust, and in Thee let Thy trusting servants place their trust. Aid, O my God, them that aid the True Faith, and grant them victory in the land through what Thou createst anew at every moment by a wondrous command. Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Bear Thou witness that I have conveyed from Thee that which was entrusted to me from a mighty Book. Diminish not aught of what God hath bestowed upon you of His bounty and mercy, and aid ye God that ye may attain unto that which ye love.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Thou art the Protector of them that believe and of them that place their trust in their Lord. Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Thou art the Creator of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, the Lord of all worlds. Thou judgest between Thy servants in that which they know this Day. Aid, O my God, them that glorify Thee by night and by day and are assured of Thy Command.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! We, all Thy servants, beseech Thee of Thy bounty to aid us with a mighty triumph and to cause them that place their trust in Thee to prevail in the earth and all that is thereon, them that remember Thee though they know it not. Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Purify the earth and all that dwell thereon that none may remain save they who follow the True Faith from Thy presence and are among them that bow down in worship. The Kingdom is God’s—He bestoweth it upon whomsoever He willeth among His servants, and He is the Praiseworthy Protector.
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Grant us what Thou hast ordained for us from Thy presence, for Thou art the Lord of all worlds. Glory be unto Thee, O my God! We all are supplicants of Thy bounty and unto Thee do we all return. Send down, O my God, Thy mercy upon them that raise aloft the Word of Faith and strive in Thy path by night and by day, desiring none but Thee and victorious through Thy command. Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Thou art the Protector of them that believe and them that show forth righteousness. Send down upon them from the treasuries of Thy mercy that which shall enrich them through Thy bounty and make firm their feet upon the path of a mighty truth. Thou ordainest the creation of all things according to a preserved measure.
Glory be unto Thee, O God! Unto Thee shall we commit ourselves and all that Thou hast given us to possess, for Thou art our Lord, in Thee do we place our trust, and Thou art the best of helpers. Do Thou ordain, O God, for those who commit their affairs unto Thee that which is best for them in this world and the world to come. Verily Thou art the Guardian of the believers. And he who writeth this letter doth surely send greetings unto thee and unto the companions of Ridvan, for ye are indeed the triumphant ones. Blessed are ye and that which God hath ordained in the Mother Book for those who seek after God and the true Faith on a momentous day, the day when mankind shall stand before the Lord of the worlds. Say at all times, before all times and after all times: There is no power nor strength except in God, the Most High, the Most Great. Ye shall surely come to know His message after a time. Be patient, for the end belongeth to the God-fearing. Say: Glory be to God, the Lord of all worlds. And verily His peace be upon His believing servants. And praise be to God, the Lord of all worlds.

title: BB00044: Kitabu’l-Ba’th
text:
Part 1: “At the head of this Tablet these words…”
At the head of this Tablet these words and phrases are inscribed individually: There is no God but God. Glory be to God. The Fire of God. The creation of humanity. Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Ali and the Imams and the Holy Leaf are God’s proofs. Praise be to God. There is no God but God. The gates of guidance, these are the deputies of God. God is Most Great. Sustenance. Death. Life. Ruby. Emerald. Sapphire.
In the Name of God, the Most Unapproachable, the Most Holy.
God testifieth that there is none other God but Him. His is the creation and the command. He giveth life and causeth death, then causeth death and giveth life, and verily He is the Ever-Living Who dieth not. Within His grasp lieth the kingdom of all things. He createth what He willeth by His command. He, verily, is powerful over all things.
God testifieth that there is none other God but Me, the Mighty, the Best-Beloved. God testifieth that there is none other God but God. Say: All, by night and by day, are His worshippers. Say: Glory be unto Thee! There is none other God but Thee. Thou art, verily, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, Lord of all things, Lord of all the worlds.
Say: Verily, at this moment, all proclaim that there is none other God but He in Whom the Babis have believed. Say: God is living, and whatsoever is beside God is less than this—do ye not see? Say: God is justice, and whatsoever is beside God is less than this—do ye not fear? Say: God is truth, and whatsoever is beside God is creation—do ye not recognize His unity? Say: God is Lord, and whatsoever is beside God is from Him—do ye not reflect? Say: God is singular, and whatsoever is beside God is less than one—do ye not remember?
O Ali! We have verily created thee and sustained thee and caused thee to die and brought thee to life and raised thee from the resting place of thy heart. Thou wert aforetime an angel in the Book of God who breatheth the spirit of life after death into Our believing servants. And when We raised thee from the resting place of thy heart after We had taken thee, and returned thee unto Us after We had sent thee down—this is from God’s grace upon thee—that thou shouldst render thanks unto God, thy Lord, with great thanksgiving, and that thou shouldst aid God, thy Lord, at this moment with great aid, and that thou shouldst breathe the spirit of life into Our servants who hope to attain Our presence morning and evening.
Say: Verily God breatheth into His servants the spirit of exposition, whereupon all the dead are quickened from the resting places of their hearts unto life. O thou King! Bear thou witness that there is none other God but Him, the Supreme, the Self-Subsisting. His are the most excellent names, from before and after. All who are in the heavens and on earth and between them glorify Him. There is none other God but Him, the Mighty, the Best-Beloved.
Bear thou witness that My Manifestation is the Manifestation of God on the Day of Resurrection. I have taken all spirits from all things, even from the Angel of Death after We commanded him to take the spirit of every possessor of spirit. Then We took him himself, and We were witnesses that no possessor of spirit remained in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and what lieth between them. And when We asked “Whose is the Kingdom this Day?”, there was no possessor of spirit to answer God, thy Lord. Then We were the ones who answered God, Who taketh every possessor of spirit and then giveth life as He willeth by His command. Verily, He is the Strong, the Powerful.
When We had taken the spirit of all things, We then tarried for a time beyond reckoning, when neither age nor eternity, neither above nor below, could be spoken of. Then did We create Muhammad and those who bore witness after Him, then the Gates of Guidance, then the angels who glorify and stand in ranks, then the exalted and manifest ones, then the hidden and unified ones, then those who stand and supplicate. And what thou hast witnessed before concerning the mention of a thousand thousand ages is for Our eternal servants, and less than that for those bound by time. Exalted is God, thy Lord, above being described by limit or limitlessness, for both are limits in the Book of God—do ye not perceive? Say: Verily I am not mentioned by any name, and all the names of thy Lord are but names of him who causeth thee to speak from God, wherein naught is seen but God—do ye not perceive? And verily all the angels of God are manifestations of God’s Command, working by day and by night through His leave—do ye not observe?
O Ali! From the beginning of this Cause is the Day of Resurrection, and Paradise from all eternity is for those who are certain of meeting God. No higher paradise existeth in contingent being than that God should openly speak to His servants as He spoke inwardly to Muhammad aforetime—this is of God’s grace unto those who are certain of His signs. How should I make Myself known to thee through aught besides Me when all besides God was created for Me—do ye not perceive?
If thou desirest to be certain of this, recite the Book of God that came before, for all say “This is from God, there is no doubt therein” and all in that day believe in it. Then observe what We have sent down unto thee and say: “What God willeth!” There is no book except from God—who besides God could reveal a single verse, when all are powerless before it? This is a proof unto all who dwell in the kingdoms of the heavens and earth and what lieth between them until the Day when He Whom God shall make manifest shall appear—on that Day shall all be brought before God their Lord. Say: Verily He is in that time I Myself, and I am in that Day He Himself. Though the sun should rise countless times, it is but one sun—do ye not reflect? And though it should set, it is but one sun—do ye not remember?
O Ali! We have appointed the alembic and retort from the beginning of this Cause among Our servants that We might extract the elixiric components from the hearts of those who desire naught but God and are thankful unto Him. Yet We appointed not the alembic and retort save that We sent down death upon all people—and this they recite at all times when they mention that death is truth. After this was perfected the number of the One before the Ten, and lo, the human form appeared in wondrous creation—its outward aspect is a gate, and it is the letter Ha followed by the full Vav in a mighty book, and its inward aspect is Vav followed by the full Ha in an impregnable book.
In the form of man hath been created that subtle essence which is the Most Great Name. Whoso possesseth it shall be manifested before all the worlds. This is the Most Exalted Name—none in all the worlds can fathom its mystery. This is the Most Impregnable Name—none in all the worlds can resist what God hath ordained for him beneath its shadow. Through it are they glorified, through it are they beautified, through it are they magnified, through it are they illumined, through it are they perfected, through it are they exalted, through it do they gain mastery, through it do they gain dominion, through it do they gain sovereignty, through it do they find all that they love, through it do they behold all that they desire in the path of God.
And all that God hath created in the kingdoms of heaven and earth and what lieth between them is contained within this temple—the temple of man. Will ye not then be thankful? This is the temple of the Point, from which all things were brought into being for the manifestation of God unto it, and unto which all shall return. These are the signs of God, the fruits of that Garden. Will ye not then delight therein? This is that proof which, were God to cast it upon the fire, would transform it into light. Will ye not then be thankful? Through it doth God establish what He willeth and erase what He pleaseth, even as was established aforetime in the Book. With God there existeth no proof equal unto this for those who believe in God and His signs.
This is the proof through which were created the Prophet and those who bore witness after Him, then the gates of guidance, then those drawn nigh from among Our God-fearing servants. From the beginning of this Cause it is the Paradise of eternity for those who attain unto the presence of God, and verily it is the fire of God for those who are remote from His signs. Yet should they enter in at the gate in prostration unto God, then will God transform their fire into His light, whereupon God will multiply for them the number of the gate, and then shall all attain unto the presence of God.
Say: The years of the letter Ha [five, =1265] have passed, and ye are now being gathered in the letter Vav [six]. This is what ye and all non-Arabs read, and those possessed of knowledge remember from the first death until the resurrection. We took in the first year those who say “There is no God but He, and we are His servants.” Then after that, those who seek shade beneath what God revealed aforetime: “There is no God but I; therefore fear ye Me.” Then in the third, when it was said unto them “There is no God but God,” they fell down in prostration. Then in the fourth, those who say “Glory be unto Thee, O God! Verily Thou art our Lord. Thou hast created us and sustained us and caused us to die and brought us to life, and we have no God save Thee. Thy mercy embraceth all that is in the heavens and the earth and what lieth between them. Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thou; verily Thou art the Lord of all worlds.” Then in the fifth, those who remember what God revealed aforetime: “There is no God but He in Whom the God-fearing believe.”
These are the components of the elixir from those who believed in the Qur’an, and those beneath them are but dross, unworthy of mention save in terms of their extinction. Verily they shall return unto God, then in another creation shall they be resurrected. And all that thou hast witnessed from the beginning of this Cause until this day is the fruit of the creation of that religion and of all that was created aforetime, when the Day of Resurrection is made manifest in the sight of God.
Therefore grieve thou for all mankind, for they prostrate themselves before God by night and by day, yet their prostrations are vain, and they utter in their prayers that which they do not mean. They remain veiled from Him Who created them, sustained them, caused them to die and brought them back to life, and in His presence they believe not. Were they not dead they would arise, even if but a little. Therefore, breathe into their hearts the spirit of knowledge, that perchance they may arise from their slumber.
This indeed is the fruit that the creation of the Qur’an hath yielded in Our sight, and thus must We needs create a new creation. All are in a wondrous creation. Since men have failed to know God, We speak in terms of what they await and in which they firmly believe. They supplicate by night and by day for the day of His manifestation, while each morning they read what they are commanded to read.
O my God! Number me among those who have attained martyrdom in His presence, in ranks like solid walls, as Thou didst mention aforetime. Say: Praise be to God that none heedeth what he readeth, and all move according to their own desires, save those who have detached themselves unto God and who aid His religion.

title: BB00044: Kitabu’l-Ba’th
section: Part 2: “These are they who, on that Day, truly…”
text:
Part 2: “These are they who, on that Day, truly…”
These are they who, on that Day, truly worship God upon the earth, and these are they who, through God their Lord, have ascendancy over the earth and all who dwell therein. Look not upon those who prostrate themselves by night and by day, claiming they are God-fearing. We hear their words “Thee do we worship” but We answer them not in what they say, for We had revealed that verse unto Muhammad, the Apostle of God, beforetime, and all read according to what was previously ordained.
He hath returned to the primal life, as have all who believed in God and His signs, while all who are dead wander in the desires of their vain imaginings. Say: That whereby religion was established aforetime existeth with you today. It is now established, whether before God my Lord and before those who have believed in God and His signs they be God-fearing or not.
If ye do good, ye prepare it for your own souls; otherwise ye shall die and shall not return. How many servants in former times possessed the East and West of the earth, yet today who among all the peoples remembereth them? Ye too shall die, then perish, then find in the fire what ye cannot remember.
Therefore have mercy upon yourselves and attain unto what escapeth you, and let each one of you, whether male or female, be as though ye possessed God’s Cause from Him, however ye may administer or reform it. This is the state of one who feareth God in His religion and desireth the abode of the Hereafter, which is true life with God, while they regard not this present life.
By the life of Him Whom God shall make manifest! If on that Day one who hath never worshipped God in this world should believe, it would be as though he had worshipped God throughout all the worlds of Command and Creation, and thereby all would ascend to the highest degrees of grace. And should anyone who hath worshipped God from the beginning of this world until now reflect, even to the measure of nine times nineteen mustard seeds, then all he hath gained would descend as though he had never worshipped God in any way.
Similarly shall you be tested concerning Him Whom God shall make manifest. Those who believe in Him are those who have believed in Me, and they are the triumphant ones. And whoso believes not in Him at the time of His manifestation has not in truth believed in God his Lord, and thus shall all people be tested on the day of His manifestation.
On that day all who are in the heavens and on the earth and whatever lies between them shall be struck unconscious by His Cause, save those whom God willeth. These are they who have truly recognized God their Lord and are well-assured of His signs.
There exists naught in the heaven above you nor in the earth beneath you save that which exists in the heaven of your hearts and the earth of your bodies and whatsoever lies between them. Therefore imagine not that which you cannot comprehend.
Say: My Revelation is the Revelation of God. None can dwell in that paradise except His most excellent Names, and these are they who are dominant over the earth and all who dwell thereon. Say: Everyone who believes in Me—is he not named after Me? Will ye not reflect how We began this creation with the Letters of the One, whereupon all who are guided in God’s Book are guided by them? We have multiplied that Unity even as ye behold this day, and We shall continue to multiply that Unity until the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest, until there remains not a single soul on earth who has not believed in the Bayan. This is God’s command, and He has power over all things.
Say: O people! Ye are, of your own selves, the angels of victory. If ye assist God, ye shall indeed be assisted. Imagine not that which ye cannot understand. And should anyone dispute with Me concerning how one who was born aforetime and more than a thousand years have passed can now appear in the form of one who is thirty years of age, say: Indeed, this is from God’s command. How can ye be certain that Muhammad’s body ascended to heaven and entered every station and departed from every station, while His seat remained empty of His body, and all creation witnessed His presence in His Own sphere while He was in His sphere of exaltation? Similarly do ye speak concerning Me. This is one of God’s mysteries which ye cannot comprehend. We are indeed the First and the Last, and We are indeed the Outward and the Inward. Neither sleep nor geometry takes hold of Us as it does you or those above you. Therefore believe in God Who created all things, then trust in God, the Ever-Living, Who causes you to turn about by night and by day.
Make not difficult for yourselves the religion of your Lord, for God wishes not to grieve the heart of even an ant that crawls in one of the houses of His dominion. This is God’s mercy—will ye not be thankful? Yet despite this mercy, were God to create an angel who would cause all those on earth to receive one message, His dominion would not be diminished. Verily He is the All-Subduing, the Possessor of mighty strength.
All who believed in the Qur’an aforetime say “Thee do we worship and Thine aid do we seek,” yet behold what their hands have wrought. God will seize them for what their hands have earned. Verily God shall seize them for what their hands have wrought. Verily He is possessed of a mighty grasp. By the life of Him Whom God shall make manifest, were no one to grieve Me on the Day of Resurrection, I would cause all things to enter into My mercy through My word Be! and it is.’ For were I to utter this, all would rejoice until the Day of Resurrection. But I shall assuredly lay hold upon the people for not having believed in My presence on the Day of My Manifestation, and I shall surely prevail over them for not having believed in My signs, though night and day they say We are assured of God and His signs.’
Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Create then servants through Thy might who shall prevail over the earth and all that are thereon, that they may purify the whole earth from the letters of negation and cause every soul to enter into the letters of affirmation, even though they know not that this is better for them with their Lord. Verily Thou hast power over all things. And create, O my God, servants from the light of Thy dominion who shall lay hold upon the earth and all that are thereon, that they may banish from it whoso believeth not in Thee and Thy signs, and may fill it from end to end with such as have believed in Thee and then in Thy signs. Verily Thou knowest what is in the heavens and what is on earth and what lieth between them. Nothing can frustrate Thee, whether in the kingdom of command or creation or what lieth beneath them. Thou createst what Thou willest as Thou willest. Verily Thou art the All-Powerful, the Almighty, the Omnipotent.
Say: God at this time loveth that all His servants should be unto one another manifestations of His mercy, that none should grieve another while remaining joyous in their inmost hearts. And it behooveth them, if they are able, to prevail and to triumph; otherwise to be patient and remain silent, for this profiteth them not at this time until God grant them relief and assist them through the angels of the heavens and the earth and all that lieth between them, as He willeth through His command. Verily He is possessed of mighty vision.
Say: The religion at this time, so long as the Point shineth among you, is that ye should unite with God to the extent of your powers. Then what We have ordained of three hundred and several words—for all this is the number of all things—will ye not then be thankful? Whoso in the first year believeth in God and is among the unitarians, it behooveth him to negate by his hands the number of negation and affirm by his strength the number of affirmation. Then in the second year the second, then in the third year the third, then in the fourth year the fourth, then in the fifth year the fifth. This is from God’s command if they be among those who profess the unity of God in His religion.
Say: God will not burden you save according to your capacity. I desire not to cause grief to anyone in the Bayan. Rather, We desire for those who have believed in God and His signs, whether male or female, that they should live in God’s dominion while giving thanks night and day. However, We find at this time nothing sweeter than to cast out negation as We are able and establish affirmation as We are empowered. The fire of negation hath indeed been extinguished in your saying “There is no god but He”—will ye not then give thanks? See how God hath made the letters of negation like unto a day when they shall not be mentioned on earth. And its pillars are five, and shouldst thou comprehend the second among them, it shall surely consume them through the breathing of the spirit therein, for that is more grievous in the sight of God than if they deny it, and likewise are all who are mortal.
We do not wish to mention aught save the letters of the exalted ones, else We would acquaint thee with their abodes in the fire. Make mention, therefore, of the former ones, then draw from them evidence regarding the latter ones. Say: The resting place wherein rivers flow hath returned to earthly life, and on that day it is with those who are witnesses from God. Of no profit unto men is that which they earn concerning them. Strive ye until ye are assured that He and your own selves are as dust before God, and ye shall find naught with God save that ye return unto God and then become certain of His signs.
How many are they who were given the Book aforetime and until now await the appearance of Muhammad, whom they find mentioned in their Books! He came with the truth, His resurrection was fulfilled, and every soul was rewarded according to its deserts—yet they still wait. Similarly are they who in this day show patience in the Cause of God—nay, more severe than these, for they had believed in the Book aforetime and now interpret the verses of the Bayan, yet they remember not.
Present ye the Khums and deliver unto its people that from which they are veiled. The resurrection hath come to pass, and that which ye await hath been fulfilled in His manifestation, though ye be far removed from His signs. Thus hath the breath of life been breathed after death, that perchance the people may arise from their graves. Guard thyself with utmost vigilance, and speak not of God, nor utter aught save from the Bayan and such verses as move thee and all people.
And if thou don the garment of the third letter, God will protect thee thereby, though they who have believed in God and His signs and possess the Temples are preserved by God’s leave. Weep thou now, day and night, for those who await Him, imploring. And when He desired to send His Messenger unto them with tidings, then by what their hands had wrought, they were content to don the garment of the third letter. Such is the state of men before God. God will soon seize them for what their hands have earned. Verily, His grasp is nigh.
But make no mention in the land of Fa save of him who was a believer in God and His signs from among the letters, lest there arise thereby a sedition causing grief to them that grieve in God. Make mention of Our noble remembrance, the merchant there, for he is one who aforetime believed in God and His signs and was among the God-fearing. Receive from him and take from him the Book, for he receiveth from those who know the places of the House and who in this day are God-fearing. Deliver the Tablets unto all who have believed in God and His signs when thou findest them among the assured ones.

title: BB00044: Kitabu’l-Ba’th
section: Part 3: “This is the mending of what is torn…”
text:
Part 3: “This is the mending of what is torn…”
This is the mending of what is torn—thou wilt find their sleep beneath their heads. God will send down unto all His servants detailed Tablets wherein is every good thing measured out. For every term there is a Book, and when its term cometh, all rejoice. And if thou art able to enter the Holy Land, enter therein, give greetings unto its people, and recite unto them the Book of thy Lord. Otherwise, proceed whither thou art commanded and return unto God, for that is the mighty triumph.
I bear witness that there is none other God but Him, Who is independent of all who have believed and all who have failed to acknowledge the words of their Lord. Indeed, those who have acknowledged the words of God—these are they who shall triumph.
This is the law of the Alif in the thousand, therefore gather ye beneath its shade, then multiply. Thereafter shall the permanence be intensified, then shall appear the Alif, then shall dawn the letters of Him whom all shall meet their Lord with certitude. Though all this is with all things, before all things, after all things, to the right of all things, and to the left of all things, yet His manifestation is according to the measure of nineteen units that revolve until it becomes manifest to all the worlds.
We have divided the year into nineteen portions and made each one a unity, thus all this is the number of all things. We have ordained for you in the Bayan the measures of all things in this. Thus is established the Primal Word “There is none other God but Him,” and by it is established all that they profess. That is the day wherein ye shall manifest all that ye are empowered with of might and ordainment, then of knowledge and governance, that this may be revealed and by its revelation all shall be made manifest.
Say: O people! Verily deliverance lies not in wealth nor in exaltation as ye imagine. How many kings have been raised up in the religion of Islam who to this day await it and supplicate for it! Rather, deliverance is what God hath bestowed upon a servant as a proof whereby He establisheth what He willeth, and before which all the worlds are powerless—even as He bestowed upon Muhammad aforetime and established thereby the religion of Islam. And now on this day God hath bestowed upon Me this—that whereby the affairs of the first and the last, the outward and the inward, the mighty and the glorious, the greatest and the most great shall be set aright.
And when thou enterest the blessed spot on the right of the Mount of Faith, remember there the sincere servants of God. Then remember there him who hath presented himself from the land of Qaf, for he is Muhammad-before-Husayn in a beloved and mighty Book, then Muhammad-before-ʿAli in a beloved and mighty Book. Say: They who have detached themselves unto God—these are the inheritors. And recite unto the First Name the verse of the Qur’an “The punishment of those who wage war against God…” that they may rise up in the religion of God. Say: Concerning this was this verse revealed aforetime. Blessed are they who manifest themselves through God their Lord.
Say: Verily the Last is the First, and the Manifest is the Hidden. Is there any creator besides God who createth you, sustaineth you, causeth you to die, giveth you life, or helpeth you? Glory be to God! Rejoice then in the life wherein ye shall be rewarded in paradise.
Remember Our name the All-Giving in a mighty, inscribed Book. Say: Write books from one whose name is not known in the Book to those who will benefit thereby if they come to know of it; otherwise be silent and trust in God, the Ever-Living Who dieth not. And say to him whose name is numbered by the name of thy Lord there: Command the people of guidance to present themselves there, then arise for the religion of God. And say: O Abu-ʿAli! From the day thou presented thyself there, We knew not that what thou desired in the path of God would benefit. Therefore preserve thyself and then those who are guided, and be of them that ponder. And if thou knowest that a word from thee, or mention of a Book wherein is remembered the Manifestation, or the return of Muhammad, or the Day of Resurrection, or aught whereby the hearts of them that behold are transformed—then aid thou God’s Cause on that day in the religion of truth, for this shall profit the God-fearing. At that time, righteous deeds shall not profit except those who aid in God’s path.
We have indeed sent down to thee aforetime numbered Books, and now a white, inscribed Tablet, whose single letter none in the heavens and earth and all between them can equal. Through it are gladdened the hearts of the sincere, though all are before God, in every time, before time and after time. This is what thou hast heard from him who came in the name of Ahmad before. Therefore call ye upon God lest ye be among the first at the time of the Manifestation, for verily ye are of the assured ones.
Say: Praise be to God Who hath favored me with His remembrance and made me to be of the sincere ones. By the life of Him Whom God shall make manifest! Nothing shall profit mankind on that Day save their following God and aiding the Cause of Truth. This shall profit God’s sincere servants.
Take a piece of paper and divide it in half, and send the half to Me. Then purchase another piece and convey all this to one of those who are assured of God and His signs. And let this be conveyed in the Land of Kaf if there be found there one of the gilders, otherwise in the Land of Sad to him who is called Muhammad-before-Husayn, that he may bring one of the gilders to gild each tablet according to the Book, one by one. Then let him who writes inscribe in each house “Allahu Akbar” to fill the number of pages of each thing from the first multiplication. For this is a great victory from God. And if there be none there, then bring Our gracious remembrance to the Land of Fa that someone may gild it, if there appear not thereby what would grieve the God-fearing.
Otherwise approach not there, and command this in every land where it appears, and place it in a binding and bring it if thou art able. Otherwise let it remain with one who watches over His Cause until We give permission regarding it. For this is of God’s grace upon the Letters of the Unity, that their outward manifestation in the earth may give thanks and then arise by God’s command. And if it appear in two volumes, the thinner is preferable with thy Lord, for God is indeed most subtle. But according to what that paper was, let not its state be altered, for in this is a beautiful glory of might. But let the gilders watch over the Unity in Unity with gold water without other, that it change not from beauty of appearance at the Greatest Scene.
For they who are subtle in their craft, these are they who shall attain. But let not the work of gilding appear like those who gild in the Land of Fa, for these are they who are most precise. And perchance what is precise in the Land of Sad equals this, and it is a subtle deed which appeareth in the form of a rustling breeze.
And when thou art in the presence of the All-Bountiful, remember Him with gracious remembrance from thy Lord, and say:

“We have sent down unto thee the Book aforetime; therefore recite the Book of thy Lord morning and evening, and remember those who are there among them who have believed in God and His signs, for these are they who shall triumph.”

And whoso is unable to recognize the oneness of God through that which appeareth in the horizons, let him recognize His oneness through the Haykals, and whoso is unable to do this, let him recognize the oneness of God his Lord through the degrees We have sent down in the Book, and let him not turn aside from excellence of vision when in the presence of the Most Great Scene. Verily God is content with those who, in their joy, seek to unify Him. He who hath the power to observe the first cannot defer to the second, and he who hath the power to observe the second cannot defer to the third. And how can one who doth not observe the third, though professing God’s unity with his tongue after having recognized the Letters of Negation and borne witness to the truth of the Letters of Affirmation, be accounted among the believers?
And when thou reachest the Land of Nun, remember His sincere servants. Then return by way of the sea and remember on thy path the sleeping servants of God.
